post_title: Fewer New Year’s Day Births Recorded in 2025
post_content:
n

South Africa’s public health facilities recorded 1,448 births on New Year’s Day 2025, a decline from the 1,703 births reported on the same day last year, the Department of Health announced.

nnnn

In its statement, the department highlighted a significant drop in the number of teen mothers, from 190 in 2024 to just over 80 in 2025. The department emphasized the need for continued societal efforts to address teenage pregnancy.

nnnn

“Teenage pregnancy often results in irregular school attendance, poor academic performance, and school dropout, especially for mothers who lack family support to care for their babies,” the department noted.

nnnn

The government is working with the Departments of Social Development and Basic Education to support mothers through existing programs, ensuring their babies not only survive but thrive.

nnnn

Provincial Breakdown of Births

nnnn

Gauteng recorded the highest number of births, with 387, followed by Eastern Cape (219) and Limpopo (191).

nnnn

Birth Statistics by Province

nnnnnnnn

The department reaffirmed its commitment to reducing teenage pregnancy and supporting mothers through collaborative efforts with various societal and governmental organizations.

post_title: Foreign Nationals Arrested in Mpumalanga with Explosives
post_content:
n

Two foreign nationals, aged 33 and 39, were arrested in Mpumalanga on Sunday after being found in possession of explosives and other suspicious items, police confirmed.

nnnn

Provincial police spokesperson Brigadier Donald Mdhluli said the arrests were the result of efforts by the Combat and Proactive Unit under Operation Vala Umgodi, targeting illegal mining and other crimes in the province.

nnnn

“The suspects were apprehended on the R38 Road near Consort Mine in Barberton. Police conducting vehicle checkpoints stopped a black BMW 1 Series with two occupants. During the search, explosives, jackhammers, water boots, and R10,000 in cash were discovered,” Mdhluli said.

nnnn

The suspects reportedly failed to provide a valid explanation for possessing the items, leading to their arrest.

nnnn

Pending Cases

nnnn

One of the suspects was found to be out on bail for a separate case involving the illegal possession of a firearm. He is scheduled to appear in court on January 30, 2025, for that matter.

nnnn

Both suspects will appear at the Barberton Magistrate’s Court on 07 January in connection with the explosives case.

nnnn

Commendation for Police Efforts

nnnn

The provincial acting police commissioner, Major General Zeph Mkhwanazi, commended the officers involved for their dedication to combating illegal mining and related activities.

nnnn

“This arrest is a testament to the hard work and vigilance of our members in ensuring the safety of the community,” said Mkhwanazi.

post_content:
n

Police are investigating the fatal shooting of Kosabo Thugwana (45), a member of the Ndzundza-Fene Traditional Council, whose body was discovered in his Toyota Fortuner in KwaMhlanga on January 5.

nnnn

Provincial police spokesperson, Brigadier Donald Mdhluli, confirmed that Thugwana had suffered multiple gunshot wounds and was declared dead at the scene by paramedics.

“Officers recovered several cartridges from the scene. While no arrests have been made, the South African Police Service (SAPS) assures the public that all efforts are being made to bring those responsible to justice. The motive for the shooting is still unknown,” Mdhluli stated.

post_title: Court to Rule on Urgency of Publishing Matric Results Case
post_content:
n

The Gauteng High Court in Pretoria has reserved its decision on whether it will hear an urgent application regarding the publication of the 2024 matric results. A ruling on the matter is expected.

nnnn

The urgent application was brought by the Information Regulator (IR), seeking to prevent the Department of Basic Education (DBE) from publicly releasing matric results. The IR argues that such publication violates matriculants' right to privacy.

nnnn

The DBE and AfriForum opposed the application, asserting that releasing the results does not prejudice the public and that the urgency of the matter is self-made. Matric results are set to be announced by Minister of Basic Education Siviwe Gwarube on 13 January.

nnnn

Background on the Debate

nnnn

In 2022, AfriForum and other parties successfully challenged a similar attempt to block the publication of matric results. The court ruled then that releasing results with examination numbers instead of names adequately protects students' privacy and serves the public interest.

nnnn

AfriForum legal counsel Advocate Quintus Pelser SC highlighted that since 2022, matric results have been published without student names and without any public backlash.

nnnn

However, the IR’s legal counsel, Advocate Kennedy Tsatsawane SC, argued that the matter became urgent after the DBE announced its intention to defy the IR’s enforcement notice against publication.

nnnn

Current Proceedings

nnnn

Judge Ronèl Tolmay questioned both the urgency of the application and the potential prejudice caused by publishing or withholding the results.

nnnn

The court noted that the broader issue of whether matric results should be published will be addressed later this year. For now, the urgent application seeks to clarify whether the results may be released via newspapers and public platforms next week.

nnnn

The DBE maintains that it is bound by the 2022 court order requiring the publication of results and thus cannot comply with the IR’s directive.

nnnn

The court's decision on urgency is eagerly awaited as it will determine whether the matter proceeds immediately.

n

post_title: Van Reenen’s Pass Crash: Minibus Blamed as Death Toll Rises to 17
post_content:
n

Preliminary investigations into the deadly crash at Van Reenen’s Pass on January 6 have revealed that the minibus involved lost control and veered into the path of an oncoming truck. The horrific accident claimed 17 lives, leaving only one survivor—a baby girl—who is currently receiving medical care in hospital.

nnnn

Details of the Crash

nnnn

The collision occurred amid heavy rainfall, and investigators are considering several contributing factors, including speed, vehicle defects, and possible recklessness on the part of the minibus driver.

nnnn

The truck driver, a Zimbabwean national, reportedly contacted his employer before fleeing the scene. Authorities are working to locate him.

nnnn

Investigative Efforts

nnnn

A detailed report from Ndabezinhle Sibiya, spokesperson for MEC for Transport and Human Settlements, confirmed the casualty numbers and outlined the investigation process.

nnnn

A technical team comprising the Department of Transport, Road Traffic Inspectorate, South African National Road Agency, and South African Police Service (SAPS) met under the leadership of Major General Gonya, the Cluster Commander of Thukela District, to initiate a thorough probe into the crash.

nnnn

Support for the Survivor

nnnn

MEC for Transport and Human Settlements, Siboniso Duma, has requested the Head of the Department and the investigation team to visit the baby girl in hospital, calling her “the brave little girl.”

nnnn

The investigation continues as authorities seek to determine the exact cause of the tragedy and ensure accountability.

Four talented individuals from Breyten have returned with bronze medals after representing Mpumalanga in the U15 basketball division during the summer schools sport competition held in Tshwane in December.

Andiswa Motha, Lethu Mlambo, and Junior Mkasi showcased impressive skills on the court, while Phumlani Ndlovu contributed as the team’s assistant coach.

Their combined efforts led Mpumalanga to a well-deserved third-place finish in the fiercely contested tournament, which attracts young athletes from across the country vying for top honors.

The achievement highlights the growing talent in Breyten and Mpumalanga, with the young stars serving as an inspiration for aspiring athletes in their community.

post_title: Teen Allegedly Assaulted by Seven Men in Bambamatches
post_content:
n

A 17-year-old girl was allegedly assaulted by seven men on 03 January in the Bambamatches area, according to police reports.

nnnn

The incident occurred when the owner of a local salon left the victim alone to retrieve food from his nearby home. During his absence, a group of men reportedly entered the premises and forced the teenager into a nearby room.

nnnn

“The victim stated that the men confined her and subjected her to an ordeal throughout the night,” said police spokesperson Jabu Ndubane. “She reported that a passerby assisted her the following morning by unlocking the door. By then, the suspects had fled the scene.”

nnnn

Authorities have arrested one of the suspects, a 20-year-old foreign national, who appeared in the Bushbuckridge Magistrate’s Court on 07 January. He remains in custody.

nnnn

Ndubane added that investigations have revealed the suspect's status as a Mozambican national. Officials are working with the Department of Home Affairs, and additional charges related to immigration violations may be brought against him.

nnnn

A manhunt is underway for the six remaining suspects. Police have urged community members to provide any information that could assist in the investigation.

post_title: Ramaphosa Calls for Inclusivity at ANC’s 113th Anniversary Celebration
post_content:
n

President Cyril Ramaphosa emphasized the importance of inclusivity and non-racialism during a cake-cutting ceremony at the Athlone Civic Centre, part of the ANC’s 113th-anniversary celebrations.

nnnn

Speaking to attendees, Ramaphosa highlighted the absence of coloured community members at the event, despite their significant presence in the Athlone area.

nnnn

“The ANC has always been a party that advocates for non-racialism,” said Ramaphosa. “Non-racialism means that white South Africans, Black South Africans, South Africans who are coloured, and those who are Indian must feel at home within the ANC.”

nnnn

Reflecting on the gathering, he noted, “I looked at all of us and realized that we are in Athlone, where many coloured people reside, yet many of them are not here.”

nnnn

Ramaphosa urged the ANC to strengthen efforts to engage all communities and make them feel part of the organization. “We must reach out to other national groups and ensure they feel at home within the ANC,” he said.

nnnn

He concluded by encouraging attendees to actively promote inclusivity and diversity within the party, ensuring that the ANC remains a space for all South Africans.

post_title: Ex-Cop, Accomplice Arrested for Pension Fraud
post_content:
n

A former police officer, aged 46, and an accomplice, aged 37, were arrested on January 6, 2025, for allegedly defrauding a 71-year-old woman of her pension money at Dayizenza Complex in Masoyi.

nnnn

On January 3, the victim was reportedly approached by two women while attempting to withdraw money from an ATM. The suspects claimed the ATM had no network and advised her to try a nearby supermarket. Upon arrival, the victim discovered her bank card had been swapped.

nnnn

The victim later reported the incident to the Hazyview offices, learning that R1,700 had already been withdrawn from her account. Police traced and apprehended the suspects, charging them with fraud.

nnnn

Both appeared in the Kabokweni Magistrate’s Court on January 8, 2025. Former Constable Thembi Aretha Mhlanga (47) was granted bail of R1,000, while her co-accused, Sarel Sithole (37), was denied bail due to pending cases and remanded in custody.

nnnn

Their next court appearance is set for January 15, 2025, at the Masoyi Periodical Court.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner Major General (Dr.) Zeph Mkhwanazi commended the investigative team for their swift action and warned against breaking the law, regardless of social standing. He also urged the public to remain vigilant and cautious of scams targeting vulnerable individuals.

post_title: Polo Driver Killed in N4 Collision
post_content:
n

A Volkswagen Polo driver was declared dead after a collision with a minibus taxi towing a heavily loaded trailer on the N4 between Rivulets and the Sudwala turn-off on January 9.

nnnn

A mother and her young child, passengers in the Polo, sustained injuries and were transported to a nearby medical facility for treatment.

nnnn

The crash caused significant traffic disruption, with the eastbound lane completely blocked and the westbound lane partially obstructed.

nnnn

According to the Department of Community Safety, Security and Liaison’s spokesperson, Moeti Mmusi, the heavily loaded trailer likely contributed to the accident.

nnnn

“Preliminary investigations suggest that the trailer may have pushed the taxi down a steep descent, leading the driver to lose control,” said Mmusi.

nnnn

The out-of-control taxi then collided with the Polo. The Mozambican taxi was reportedly en route back to Mozambique.

nnnn

Mmusi emphasized the importance of reducing speed and avoiding overloading, noting these as leading causes of road fatalities.

nnnn

The department’s accident experts are conducting further investigations into the incident.

nnnn

post_title: Court Limits Mbombela Fire Vehicle Use
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga High Court has ruled that the City of Mbombela (CoM) Fire, Rescue, and Emergency Services can use its attached firefighting vehicles exclusively for emergencies.

nnnn

This decision, delivered on Tuesday, keeps all seven vehicles under judicial attachment. They cannot be sold or disposed of but may be deployed for emergency services. The CoM retains the option to apply for rescission of the order, which would be reviewed later.

nnnn

The vehicles—three fire engines, three water tankers, and a grader—were seized by service provider Tunica Trading 104 on December 9. This action followed the CoM’s failure to pay nearly R7 million for services rendered over a year ago.

nnnn

Although the vehicles remain at the Mbombela Fire Station, their legal possession has been transferred to the Sheriff of the Court. If the outstanding debt remains unpaid, the next step would be to auction the vehicles.

nnnn

The CoM’s urgent rescission application on December 24 was denied and struck off the roll.

nnnn

Advocate Ali Milazi, representing Tunica Trading 104, highlighted the municipality’s obligation to settle its debt. “The Sheriff will ensure the equipment is neither sold nor damaged. If no payment offer is made, the vehicles will be auctioned to recover the owed amount,” Milazi explained.

nnnn

The CoM is now under pressure to resolve the matter to retain its critical emergency response assets.

nnnn

nnnn

post_title: Judgment Reserved in AKA Murder Bail Case
post_content:
n

The Durban Magistrate’s Court has reserved judgment until Wednesday in the bail hearing of Mziwethemba Harvey Gwabeni (36) and Lindokuhle Ndimande (29), who stand accused in the murders of rapper Kiernan “AKA” Forbes and his friend Tebello “Tibz” Motsoane in February 2023.

nnnn

Magistrate Vincent Hlatshwayo stated that more time was needed to consider the lengthy proceedings and arguments presented on Tuesday. The state, represented by Advocates Elvis Gcweka and Lawrence Gcaba, opposed bail, citing new evidence linking Gwabeni to the crime.

nnnn

“We have video footage of Gwabeni at King Shaka International Airport upon Mr. Forbes’s arrival, evidence of him following the entourage, standing near the deceased at the vehicle hire area, driving the BMW used in the crime, and telephone records placing him near the hotel,” said Gcaba.

nnnn

In their defense, Gwabeni and Ndimande, through Advocate Simphiwe Mlotshwa, argued for bail due to the personal and financial hardships their incarceration has caused. Gwabeni claimed his absence had left his family struggling, with school fees unpaid and therapy required for his wife and child due to the trauma of his arrest.

nnnn

Ndimande, meanwhile, highlighted financial losses from his non-operational minibus taxi and poultry farm, which he said generated R20,000 and R70,000 monthly, respectively. However, the state questioned the validity of these claims, particularly the lack of repairs to the taxi.

nnnn

Hlatshwayo, dissatisfied with the explanations provided, adjourned proceedings, confirming that the decision will be announced on 15 January.

n

post_title: Motsoaledi's Remarks Spark Outrage Among Unemployed Doctors
post_content:
n

Health Minister Dr. Aaron Motsoaledi has faced criticism for his comments addressing the plight of 500 unemployed doctors in South Africa. Amid protests by jobless medical professionals, Motsoaledi reportedly stated that they would not receive special treatment and suggested they either enter private practice or leave the country.

nnnn

This comes against the backdrop of a healthcare system plagued by staff shortages, with patients often waiting hours for attention at state hospitals and clinics.

nnnn

While Motsoaledi cited budget constraints as the reason for the lack of employment opportunities, critics argue that mismanagement and corruption within the ANC have drained resources meant for essential services like healthcare.

nnnn

“The reality is that taxpayers fund medical training in this country, yet the government fails to utilize these trained professionals,” said an unemployed doctors’ spokesperson, Dr. Philisiwe Ngcai.

nnnn

Ngcai criticized Motsoaledi’s remarks, highlighting that leaders with access to private healthcare fail to grasp the severity of the public health crisis. He also noted the irony of such statements as the government pushes for National Health Insurance reforms.

nnnn

Motsoaledi’s comments have been widely perceived as dismissive, with critics accusing the government of failing to prioritize healthcare and the needs of its people.

nnnn

post_title: Residents Warned of Flood Risks Amid Lydenburg Downpours
post_content:
n

Residents of Lydenburg and surrounding areas have been urged to remain vigilant as heavy rainfall continues, raising river levels and increasing the risk of flash floods.

nnnn

The Thaba Chweu DA issued a warning on January 1, noting that the Lydenburg Dam wall is overflowing, and river levels are rising. An orange level 8 warning was issued by the South African Weather Service (SAWS) on January 6, predicting disruptive rainfall for the week, with potential widespread flooding of roads and settlements, danger to life from fast-flowing water, and significant property damage.

nnnn

SAWS forecasts indicate that rainfall could persist until Thursday, January 9, fueled by warm, moist air from the tropics. Areas affected include Mpumalanga, Gauteng, and parts of the North West and Free State.

nnnn

Councillor Spiros Couvaras of the DA advised residents to prepare for potential evacuation orders. “The Dorps River is holding strong for now, but with continued rainfall, we must be ready for any scenario,” he said. Low-lying areas and critical infrastructure, such as the Sekhukhune road bridge, are already experiencing disruptions, with access limited to high-clearance vehicles.

nnnn

Past flooding events in 2008, 2016, and 2021 caused significant damage in Lydenburg, necessitating evacuations. Residents in flood-prone areas have been urged to secure personal belongings and monitor updates as conditions evolve.

nnnn

post_title: Mpumalanga Premier Focuses on Growth Plans
post_content:
n

Mpumalanga Premier Mandla Ndlovu recently convened an executive council (Exco) sitting in Mbombela to implement measures aimed at improving socio-economic conditions. This aligns with the seventh administration’s priorities to promote inclusive growth, create jobs, reduce poverty, and build a capable, ethical, and developmental state.

nnnn

Infrastructure development and service delivery are key focus areas, including completing major projects such as the Mpumalanga International Fresh Produce Market (MIFPM). Officially handed over on August 1, the R1.7 billion MIFPM will boost the province’s economy by facilitating agricultural exports and creating direct and indirect jobs.

nnnn

The market, initially launched in November 2018, faced delays due to community unrest, worker protests, and other interruptions. It is now ready to provide access to local, regional, and international fresh produce markets. It includes agroprocessing facilities, roads, parking, and related infrastructure.

nnnn

During the Exco sitting, MEC Thulasizwe Thomo, the council’s spokesperson, confirmed the MIFPM is complete, with measures underway for operationalisation. “It is Mpumalanga’s first large-scale market infrastructure, poised to create employment opportunities through agricultural exports,” he said.

nnnn

To support this initiative, Premier Ndlovu will lead a mission to China from January 14 to 20, focusing on Tianshui City, Longricunan City, and Xiamen City. The delegation, including senior officials, will sign agreements with major trade institutions to establish co-operation in the food industry and logistics for the MIFPM.

post_title: Eight Killed in Pienaar Tavern Shooting
post_content:
n

The death toll from the January 11 shooting at Dludlu Tavern in Pienaar has risen from six to eight, with two victims succumbing to their injuries in the hospital.

nnnn

Lieutenant Colonel Jabu Ndubane, provincial police spokesperson, confirmed that six individuals were fatally shot at the scene. Two additional victims, a male and a female, later died from their injuries. Three others, two males and a female, are still receiving medical treatment.

nnnn

“Two VW Polos at the scene were riddled with bullet holes. One victim was found dead inside one of the vehicles. The motive for the shooting remains unclear, and a team of investigation experts has been assembled to handle the case. A 72-hour activation plan is in place to expedite the investigation,” said Ndubane.

nnnn

Authorities are urging anyone with information to contact Crime Stop at 08600 10111 or provide tips via the My SAPS app.

nnnn

Jackie Macie, MEC for the Department of Community Safety, Security, and Liaison, condemned the incident. “We strongly condemn this barbaric and senseless loss of lives. We urge the community to allow the police time to investigate thoroughly. The perpetrators must be brought to justice.”

nnnn

Macie also appealed to liquor traders to prioritize patron safety and extended condolences to the victims’ families while wishing the injured a speedy recovery.

nnnn

n

Two suspected armed robbers from Barberton were arrested near Absa Square in Mbombela on January 11.

nnnn

Divergent Ops received a tip-off about a minibus taxi transporting suspected armed robbers and drug dealers from Barberton to Mbombela. “The taxi was stopped at the Puma fuel station, and the suspects were questioned. SAPS Crime Intelligence assisted with searches and interrogation,” said Ghost from Divergent Ops.

nnnn

During questioning, it was revealed that one of the suspects' residences in Barberton was being used to store firearms. Police recovered two firearms and explosives at the location.

nnnn

The suspects then led authorities to two additional houses occupied by alleged zama zamas. At the first hideout, one armed suspect escaped as the team approached. Six zama zamas were arrested at the second house and taken to Barberton Police Station.

nnnn

The operation continued in Mbombela, where police accompanied Divergent Ops to a guest house in Sonheuwel, where the suspects had booked a four-day stay. Eight suspects were arrested in total.

nnnn

post_title: Suspect Arrested in Deadly Pienaar Shooting
post_content:
n

A suspect was arrested on January 12 in connection with the shooting that claimed eight lives in Pienaar during the early hours of January 11.

nnnn

Police detectives apprehended the 39-year-old male suspect at a residence in Pienaar just before midnight. A pistol with 13 live rounds of ammunition was confiscated during the arrest, according to provincial police spokesperson Lieutenant Colonel Jabu Ndubane.

The suspect is expected to appear in court soon. The shooting occurred at about 04:00 near a tavern, leaving six people, including a woman, dead on the scene. Two others, a man and a woman, later succumbed to their injuries in the hospital. Three individuals remain hospitalized, while one has been discharged.

nnnn

The government encourages the matriculants to carry forward their values of resilience, dedication, and excellence as they embark on new chapters in their lives. post_title: Minister Urges Matriculants to Explore Training Options
post_content:

The Minister of Science, Technology, and Innovation (DSTI), Professor Blade Nzimande, has encouraged matriculants who did not achieve their desired results to remain optimistic and explore alternative paths, including post-school training opportunities or improving their grades through a second chance initiative.

nnnn

Addressing the nation as part of the celebrations for the Matric Class of 2024, Nzimande highlighted the need for learners to persist in their educational journey despite setbacks.

nnnn

“As the Minister responsible for science, technology, and innovation, I share the concerns of the Minister of Basic Education about our learners’ underperformance in mathematics and science at the Grades 5 to 9 levels compared to their global peers,” he stated.

nnnn

Nzimande also expressed concern over the declining enrolments in critical subjects such as mathematics, physical sciences, accounting, and economics, which are vital for driving science, innovation, and economic development.

nnnn

The Minister emphasized the need for significant growth in producing STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) graduates to achieve a technology-driven future for South Africa. He affirmed the department’s commitment to placing science, technology, and innovation at the core of government, education, industry, and society.

To address challenges in maths and science education, the DSTI aims to strengthen collaboration with the Department of Basic Education and provincial education departments. “These science engagement initiatives are crucial for improving learner outcomes in maths and science while advancing our strategic goal of embedding science, technology, and innovation across all sectors,” Nzimande said.

The DSTI remains committed to working closely with the Department of Higher Education to address skills development in science and other critical fields, ensuring South Africa’s future progress.

Ward 24 (Legokgwe Cunningmoor) in Bushbuckridge, Ehlanzeni, Mpumalanga, saw the ANC retain its seat in a high-turnout by-election following the passing of the ward councillor. The ANC secured 74% of the vote, an improvement from its 62% performance in the 2021 local elections, while the EFF garnered 26%, a slight dip from 34%.

nnnn

Ward Overview

nnnn

Nestled near the Kruger National Park, northwest of Skukuza and west of Sabi Sands and Mala Mala, Ward 24 lies in the southern part of Bushbuckridge, Mpumalanga’s second-most-populous municipality and a vote-rich region within Ehlanzeni. The ward includes Legokgwe (Oakley) and Cunningmoor (Tiyemeleni), with distinct voting patterns.

nnnn

Local Government and Provincial Election Trends

nnnn

In the 2021 local elections, the ANC underperformed relative to its Bushbuckridge average, obtaining 66%, while the EFF outperformed, achieving 10%. Notably, the EFF captured one voting district, Cunningmoor, with 62%, while the ANC swept the rest, particularly excelling in the Church of the Nazarene district with 81%.

nnnn

By the 2024 provincial elections, the ANC improved to 73% in the ward, though down from 84% in 2019. The EFF grew from 10% to 19%, cementing its presence, while MK secured 4%, trailing the DA at 3%. Across Bushbuckridge, the ANC maintained dominance with 76%, down slightly from 79% in 2019. The EFF's rise to 13% reflected its growing support.

nnnn

By-Election Results

nnnn

The ANC decisively retained Ward 24, outperforming the EFF by 1,799 votes. This stronghold saw notable shifts in voter dynamics:

nnnn
    n
  • Legokgwe (Oakley): The ANC grew significantly, with 96% in the Church of the Nazarene district (up from 81%), 85% at Oakley Primary School (up from 68%), and similar dominance in other districts. The EFF's share fell to single digits in these areas.
    • nnnn
  • Cunningmoor (Tiyemeleni): The EFF maintained its 61% majority, similar to its 2021 showing, while the ANC improved slightly from 36% to 39%.
    • n
nnnn

Voter Turnout and Next Steps

nnnn

Voter turnout in Ward 24 increased to 49% from 40% in 2021, reflecting robust engagement in this by-election.

nnnn

Looking ahead, the ANC will defend two safe seats in the Eastern Cape during the next round of by-elections on 22 January.

post_title: Hawks Nab Trio in Tax Fraud Case
post_content:

Lieutenant Colonel Magonseni Nkosi, spokesperson for the Serious Commercial Crime Investigation unit (Hawks), announced the arrest of a third suspect on 14 January following a four-year investigation into tax fraud.

The suspect joins Daniel Maluleke, 57, and Martha Mphahlele, 43, who were arrested in August and September 2024, respectively. The trio allegedly colluded to defraud the South African Revenue Service (SARS) of R293,958.33, which was deposited into their individual bank accounts in 2015.

The matter was reported to authorities five years later, in 2020, and subsequently handed to the Hawks. “An intense investigation resulted in Maluleke’s arrest in August 2024, followed by Mphahlele in September 2024,” said Nkosi. In a related case, the Polokwane Specialised Commercial Crime Court heard charges in November 2024 against company director Mmaseala Kekana, bookkeeper Richard Sekgantsha Makgasa, and their business, Mmarekhu Retail and Suppliers CC. The group allegedly attempted to defraud SARS of R1.6 million during the 2013/2014 tax period by submitting falsified income tax returns.

Provincial Hawks spokesperson Warrant Officer Lethunya Mmuroa stated that the accused acted with common intent to unlawfully obtain the refund. “They were about to be refunded R1,665,089 when the scheme was uncovered,” said Mmuroa.

post_title: Kipampa Sentenced for Poaching Syndicate Role
post_content:
n

Francis Kipampa was sentenced to 18 years in prison by the Middelburg Regional Court in Mpumalanga on January 15, 2025. Eight years of the sentence are suspended for five years, contingent on Kipampa not committing similar crimes during the suspension period.

nnnn

Syndicate Involvement and Charges

nnnn

Kipampa was arrested in June 2023 alongside 15 other individuals charged with money laundering and poaching. The group is alleged to have been part of a syndicate targeting rhinos in the Kruger National Park. They reportedly paid field rangers and their families for insider information to facilitate their illegal activities.

nnnn

While Kipampa remained in custody awaiting trial since February 2023, his co-accused were released on bail. Kipampa pleaded guilty to all charges, leading to his conviction.

nnnn

post_title: Eskom Targets Year Without Load Shedding
post_content:
n

Eskom is setting its sights on achieving a full year without load shedding, a goal it hopes to reach by midnight on March 26, 2025. The announcement comes as the utility celebrates 300 consecutive days without implementing rolling blackouts—a significant milestone for South Africa’s often-strained power supply system.

nnnn

“Credit goes to all our 40,000 dedicated and skilled Eskom employees, who are committed to serving South Africa,” said Eskom’s Group Executive for Generation, Bheki Nxumalo. “Our sights are now firmly focused on delivering one year without load shedding.”

nnnn

The past 300 days have seen remarkable improvements in Eskom’s operational performance. One of the key achievements has been a 7% increase in the energy availability factor, a reduction in unplanned outages, and a massive saving of R16.42 billion in diesel expenditure.

nnnn

Eskom’s Group Chief Executive, Dan Marokane, noted that these improvements are part of a broader effort to steer the utility toward financial and operational stability. “The savings we are making in diesel spend are being reinvested to drive efficiencies further and place Eskom on a path to profitability. Public sentiment is shifting, and business leaders who once relied on self-generation are reconsidering Eskom for their power needs,” said Marokane.

nnnn

Plans Backed by Strategic Initiatives

nnnn

The turnaround is attributed to the successful implementation of two key strategies: the Energy Action Plan introduced by President Cyril Ramaphosa in July 2022 and Eskom’s own Generation Recovery Plan. Together, these initiatives have helped stabilize the utility’s operations, reduce load shedding, and foster confidence in Eskom’s ability to deliver reliable electricity.

nnnn

Nxumalo emphasized the importance of collaboration in reaching this milestone. “We express our gratitude to all stakeholders, including the Minister of Electricity and Energy, the Eskom Board, government, and the National Energy Crisis Committee. Their collective efforts have been instrumental in addressing South Africa’s electricity challenges,” he said.

nnnn

Focus Areas for the Future

nnnn

As Eskom moves forward, it plans to continue implementing its generation recovery strategy while addressing systemic issues such as governance weaknesses, crime, and corruption. These measures aim to ensure the utility’s long-term sustainability and contribute to South Africa’s economic growth.

nnnn

Eskom is also looking to “future-proof” its operations to support energy security not only for South Africa but also for the broader sub-Saharan region. By reinvesting savings and focusing on operational efficiency, the utility hopes to enhance its reliability as a power supplier and position itself as a cornerstone of regional development.

nnnn

A Milestone for South Africa

nnnn

The achievement of 300 days without load shedding has not only saved billions in diesel costs but has also shifted public perception. Businesses that previously invested in private power generation are now reconsidering Eskom as a dependable source of electricity.

nnnn

“This milestone is proof of what can be achieved with determination, collaboration, and a clear strategy,” said Nxumalo. “Our focus remains on sustaining this momentum and ensuring reliable electricity for all South Africans.”

nnnn

As the utility inches closer to its one-year target, the improvements in Eskom’s performance are a hopeful sign for the country’s energy future. If successful, this would mark a significant turning point for South Africa, signaling the start of a more stable and sustainable electricity supply system.

The Mpumalanga Province marked a historic milestone with the official launch of the Mpumalanga Traditional Council on 22 January 2025. The event, held in the City of Mbombela, began with a prayer and opening remarks delivered by the Executive Mayor, Cllr of Mbombela.

nnnn

Addressing the purpose of the traditional council elections, Mr S. Ngubane, Head of Department (HOD), highlighted the significance of the initiative. The traditional council, originally established in 2021 by President Cyril Ramaphosa, aims to transform and recognise traditional councils under the Traditional and Khoi-San Leadership Act (TKLA) No. 3 of 2019, Section 16(1).

nnnnnnnn

Under this act, traditional communities are empowered to nominate and vote for 40% of the council’s members to serve a five-year term. The remaining 60% is appointed by the senior traditional leader. This process ensures that communities can exercise their democratic right to choose leaders who will represent them in the traditional council.

nnnn

The traditional council is tasked with playing a vital role in community development by collaborating with municipalities and government departments. It will also work alongside community councillors and speakers to enhance governance and service delivery within traditional communities.

nnnn

Key Details of the Elections
The traditional council elections will take place across all 61 communities in Mpumalanga. Registration is scheduled from 20 to 24 January 2025, between 07:00 and 19:00 daily. Voting dates are as follows:

nnnnnnnn

31 January 2025: Gert Sibande District
3 February 2025: Nkangala District
4 February 2025: Ehlanzeni District
Voters must ensure they cast their ballot at the location where they registered.

nnnn

Nomination Requirements
Candidates wishing to be nominated for election must meet the following criteria:

nnnn

Reside within the jurisdiction of the traditional community.
Hold a valid South African identity document.
Be registered on the voters’ roll.
Not be a public servant.
Not have already been selected as part of the 60% appointed by the senior traditional leader.
This launch and the subsequent elections signify a pivotal step in recognising the role of traditional leadership in fostering community development and ensuring that traditional councils work effectively with municipalities to serve their communities

Red Alert: Rabbit Virus Spreads Across South Africa
post_content:
n

South Africa is grappling with the spread of a deadly rabbit virus, rabbit haemorrhagic disease (RHD), which is causing alarm among rabbit owners and conservationists. Originally identified in China, the virus made its way into South Africa through illegal imports.

nnnn

The disease was first detected in the Northern and Western Cape provinces in November 2022. It soon spread to the Eastern Cape, where wild rabbits began dying in significant numbers. By February 2024, the outbreak had worsened, spreading to neighbouring provinces, and has now reached all corners of the country. Rabbit owners and the public have been urged to report any cases of deceased rabbits to help curb the virus’s spread.

nnnn

RHD is particularly dangerous as it can survive in dry conditions and is transmitted between rabbits. Rabbits aged 6-8 weeks can carry the virus asymptomatically, making early detection challenging.

nnnn

Emotional Support Animals at Risk

nnnn

Rabbits have become increasingly popular as emotional support animals for neurodivergent individuals, as they produce less sensory overstimulation. With over 80% of domestic rabbits vaccinated against RHD, this group of pet owners has played a vital role in managing the spread.

nnnn

However, the cost of vaccination—around R600 per dose—has posed a barrier for many. Some rabbit owners, particularly those who view rabbits as disposable pets or ornamental animals, have neglected to vaccinate or report infections, exacerbating the crisis.

nnnn

A Call for Responsible Rabbit Care

nnnn

The Southern Cape Bunny Haven conducted an informal census in 2020, estimating South Africa’s rabbit population to be around 128,000, including feral rabbits. Between May 2023 and May 2024, over 40,000 rabbit deaths were attributed to RHD, though reporting has dwindled due to misinformation, online bullying, and resistance from anti-vaccination groups.

nnnn

Data collected through the website rhd-of-africa.com and WhatsApp channels has revealed inconsistencies, with some false cases being reported. Despite these efforts, nearly half of the rabbit-keeping population did not participate in surveys or report cases, leaving a significant gap in understanding the full extent of the outbreak.

nnnn

The Way Forward

nnnn

To combat RHD, experts stress the importance of vaccination, responsible rabbit care, and adherence to guidelines on reporting and proper disposal of deceased rabbits. Owners are urged to seek accurate information and prioritise the welfare of their pets.

nnnn

The fight against RHD is a collective responsibility. By taking action and fostering cooperation among rabbit owners, South Africa can protect its rabbit population and prevent further devastation caused by this highly contagious disease.

The DPME plans to engage with other departments to leverage this legislative milestone for sustainable transformation and ensure inclusive development that leaves no one behind.

post_title: Patient Information Leaflets: A Barrier to Understanding Medication
post_content:
n

Medication is intended to improve a patient’s health and quality of life. However, when misused or misunderstood, it can have the opposite effect—even worsening health or hastening death. To prevent this, all medications, whether prescribed or bought over the counter, include Patient Information Leaflets (PILs). These leaflets provide essential details about the medication, including dosage, side effects, and instructions for safe use.

nnnn

While the intention behind PILs is commendable—helping patients use medications effectively and safely—the reality often falls short. Many patients are confronted with overly technical language, lengthy paragraphs, tiny font sizes, and confusing statistics. This creates barriers to understanding, leading to poor adherence to prescribed treatments and, consequently, deteriorating health, increased healthcare costs, or worse, fatalities.

nnnn

One key issue is that medical professionals often fail to explain medication instructions in detail. Perhaps doctors assume patients will read the information provided in the PILs, but the truth is that most patients do not. When unwell, few people have the energy or focus to decipher dense medical jargon. Those who do attempt to read the leaflets often skim over the text, focusing only on the potential side effects. Alarmed by the risks, some patients may stop taking their medication altogether, further complicating their health.

nnnn

The issue is compounded by the technical language and acronyms used in PILs. These documents, written by pharmaceutical companies, often feel inaccessible to the average reader. It almost seems as though the intention is to obscure rather than clarify. Take the example of over-the-counter medications like Grand-Pa headache powders. While they work quickly to relieve pain, misuse—such as taking more than the recommended dose—can lead to serious side effects or complications.

nnnn

In hospital settings, healthcare professionals usually explain medications directly to patients, bypassing the need for leaflets. This personalised guidance ensures that patients understand their treatment and make informed decisions. Outside of hospitals, however, patients are left to navigate PILs on their own, with little guidance.

nnnn

So, what can be done? Patients must take a proactive approach. Ask your doctor or pharmacist to explain your medication in plain language, and don’t be afraid to seek clarification. If you choose to rely on the PILs, take the time to read them carefully, even if the text is challenging.

nnnn

Ultimately, the responsibility for ensuring medication safety is shared. Medical professionals must make the effort to explain treatments clearly, while patients must advocate for themselves. As the late Steve Biko once wrote, "Black Man, You Are On Your Own." This sentiment rings true for all patients navigating the complexities of modern healthcare.

nnnn

Bheki Nyathikazi is a communication practitioner. He writes in his personal capacity.

nnnn

n

post_title: Ramaphosa Signs Law to Protect Oceans
post_content:
n

President Cyril Ramaphosa has signed the Marine Pollution (Prevention of Pollution from Ships) Amendment Bill into law, strengthening measures to protect South Africa’s oceans from ship-related pollution.

nnnn

In a statement, The Presidency emphasised the significance of the new legislation, which also contributes to global efforts aimed at safeguarding the marine environment and ensuring the sustainable use of marine resources.

nnnn

“With a coastline stretching over 3,000 kilometres from Namibia on the Atlantic Ocean to Mozambique on the Indian Ocean, the new legislation is seen as vital to protecting the country’s environmental and economic security,” the Presidency stated.

nnnn

South Africa's exclusive economic zone at sea and marine economy support about 400,000 jobs across sectors such as shipping, associated construction, tourism, and fisheries. In 2022, these sectors played a crucial role in the nation's economy.

nnnn

The new law recognises the numerous ways ships can pollute oceans, including oil spills, harmful chemical sewage, and garbage. It amends the Marine Pollution Act to incorporate the provisions of Annex IV and Annex VI of the International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships.

nnnn

Annex IV addresses the treatment and safe disposal of sewage from ships, while Annex VI serves as the global standard for ship energy-efficiency management and the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions.

nnnn

The amendment also expands the powers of the Minister of Transport, enabling the creation of regulations to prevent air pollution and sewage pollution from ships.

nnnn

A key feature of the new law is the significant increase in fines for serious offences under the Marine Pollution Act and the International Convention, from R500,000 to R10 million.

nnnn

“This legislation marks a decisive step in our efforts to preserve the oceans for future generations while fostering sustainable economic growth,” The Presidency concluded.

Police Confirm the Burglary

nnnn

Provincial police spokesperson, Brigadier Donald Mdhluli, confirmed the break-in, stating that cases of housebreaking and theft had been registered at the Nelspruit Police Station for investigation.

nnnn

When questioned about why the burglary had not been immediately disclosed, Mdhluli cited overlapping priorities as the reason for the delay.

nnnn

Senior Officers Were Away at National Police Day

nnnn

Mdhluli explained that senior police officers were attending the National Police Day event in KwaZulu-Natal on January 27. Shortly after their return, more than 50 buses were torched in the Nkangala District, further diverting police resources.

nnnn

“Our hands were full,” said Mdhluli, emphasizing that officers had been dealing with multiple high-priority cases at the time.

nnnn

Burglary Follows Allegations of Police Misconduct

nnnn

The break-in occurred just days after two senior police officers were charged with serious misconduct, reportedly linked to the illegal installation of CCTV cameras in the headquarters. These installations allegedly took place during the tenure of suspended provincial police commissioner, Lieutenant General Semakaleng Manamela.

nnnn

Manamela is facing multiple charges, brought forward by the office of the National Police Commissioner, General Fannie Masemola. However, the SAPS has refused to comment on the status of Manamela’s case, stating that it remains an internal employer-employee matter.

nnnn

Investigations Ongoing

nnnn

Police have not revealed whether the stolen computers contained sensitive information or if the burglary is connected to internal disputes within the police force. Investigations are ongoing, and authorities have assured the public that efforts are underway to recover the stolen equipment and identify the culprits.

nnnn

The incident raises serious concerns about security at the provincial headquarters, with questions being asked about how criminals managed to break into a highly secured police facility without immediate detection.

nnnn

As the investigation unfolds, the public awaits further updates from law enforcement regarding the burglary and any potential links to ongoing misconduct cases within the provincial police leadership.

nnnn

n

Three people were wounded during a business robbery at a tavern in Zwelisha, Pienaar, in the early hours of February 2.

post_title: Bomb Threat Disrupts Nelspruit Police Station
post_content:
n

A bomb threat led to the evacuation of Nelspruit police station on January 31 after a private security company reported that an explosive device had been planted inside the building.

nnnn

According to provincial police spokesperson, Lieutenant Colonel Jabu Ndubane, the bomb threat was received by a member of the explosives unit from a Polsec security officer at 7:00 PM.

nnnn

“All role players, including the K9 unit, were called to the station. Officers were evacuated, and police services were temporarily disrupted while a thorough search was conducted,” said Ndubane.

nnnn

Police explosives experts and K9 units carried out an extensive sweep of the premises, but no explosive device was found. Authorities are now investigating the origin of the threat.

nnnn

Following the search, normal operations resumed at the Nelspruit police station.

nnnn

This incident comes months after a similar bomb threat disrupted the Durban Magistrate’s Court in July last year. At the time, a caller warned that a bomb would detonate at 10:30 AM, prompting evacuations. The Public Servants Association (PSA) later demanded a full safety report from the police.

nnnn

Authorities urge anyone with information regarding the Nelspruit bomb threat to contact Crime Stop at 08600 1011 or report via the My SAPS app.

On January 20, residents from villages under the late Chief Siboshwa Ngomane protested, leading to the closure of the R571 road. They insisted the provincial government rebuild the dilapidated school, originally built in 1956 with poles and mud.

post_title: Government Boosts E-Waste Recycling in Mpumalanga
post_content:
n

The Department of Forestry, Fisheries, and the Environment (DFFE) has launched e-waste recycling initiatives in Bushbuckridge and Nkomazi, aiming to tackle the growing environmental threat posed by electronic waste. Partnering with Producer Responsibility Organisations (PROs), the department seeks to raise awareness and make e-waste disposal more accessible for communities.

nnnn

Deputy Minister Bernice Swarts officially launched the two e-waste recycling projects over the weekend, emphasizing the urgency of managing this rapidly growing waste stream.

nnnn
n

“E-waste is now considered the fastest-growing waste stream worldwide. The proliferation of technology and the consumer-driven nature of our society have led to millions of tons of electronic devices being discarded each year,” Swarts stated during the launch event in Bushbuckridge.

n
nnnn

She highlighted the dangers of e-waste, which often contains hazardous materials such as lead, mercury, and cadmium. Improper disposal can result in these toxins leaching into the soil and groundwater, posing significant risks to both the environment and public health.

nnnn

South Africa’s E-Waste Challenge

nnnn

South Africa generates approximately 360,000 tons of e-waste annually, but only 10% is recycled. Many discarded electronic devices also contain valuable metals that could be reused, reducing the demand for raw materials.

nnnn

To address this issue, the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) Regulations were introduced. Under this framework, PROs for Electrical and Electronic Equipment collect fees from electronics producers to support e-waste management efforts. According to Swarts, these fees amount to R158 million annually, funding waste collection programs, recycling initiatives, and waste picker incentives.

nnnn

Encouraging Community Participation

nnnn

At the launch event, the DFFE partnered with ERA and R2E2 to encourage community engagement by rewarding residents for collecting e-waste. Community members who brought discarded electronics to the event received vouchers ranging from R200 to R500, a move aimed at incentivizing responsible waste disposal.

nnnn

However, Swarts stressed that beyond financial incentives, the initiative seeks to change public attitudes toward waste management.

nnnn
n

“The success of this project relies heavily on community participation. By providing households with easy access to recycling facilities and guidance on proper disposal, we aim to transform the way residents manage their waste,” she explained.

n
nnnn

To ensure the sustainability of the program, PROs will collaborate with local enterprises and municipalities to establish designated collection points equipped with specialized bins for e-waste. Local businesses will be responsible for maintaining these sites, ensuring efficient and ongoing waste collection.

nnnn

Job Creation Through E-Waste Recycling

nnnn

Beyond environmental benefits, tackling e-waste also presents economic opportunities. The initiative will pay waste pickers for the e-waste they collect, offering them an additional income stream alongside regular waste collection.

nnnn
n

“E-waste collection and recycling is a key program overseen by the department and implemented through various PROs, including EWASA, ERA, Circular Energy, and R2E2. These organizations are required to work with municipalities to ensure e-waste collection is effective nationwide,” Swarts stated.

n
nnnn

By addressing the e-waste problem head-on, the government is not only protecting the environment but also creating jobs and fostering a circular economy. With many South Africans relying on the land for livelihoods, food production, and recreation, proper waste management is crucial to preserving these essential resources.

nnnn

The DFFE’s new initiatives mark a significant step toward responsible e-waste disposal, job creation, and environmental protection, reinforcing the importance of collaboration between government, industry, and communities in ensuring a cleaner, safer future.

n

post_title: All Eyes on President Ramaphosa Ahead of SONA 2025
post_content:
n

 South Africans eagerly await President Cyril Ramaphosa’s State of the Nation Address (SONA) tomorrow evening, the first under the seventh administration’s Government of National Unity (GNU). The address will outline the nation’s roadmap amid domestic and global challenges.

nnnn

Economic Outlook & G20 Presidency

nnnn

The President is expected to discuss South Africa’s hosting of the G20 Summit in November, marking the first time the event will be held on African soil. Economic recovery will also be a focal point, with the country achieving its first primary budget surplus in 15 years. The IMF projects GDP growth to rise from 0.8% in 2024 to 1.5% in 2025, aided by improved electricity generation and investor confidence.

nnnn

Key Legislation & Reforms

nnnn

The President will highlight key legislative advancements, including the Expropriation Bill, which modernizes land expropriation laws, and the Employment Equity Amendment Act, reducing compliance burdens for small businesses. The Basic Education Laws Amendment (BELA) Act also aims to transform the education system.

nnnn

Crime & Safety Initiatives

nnnn

SAPS has deployed 20,000 new constables, with operations like Shanela and Vala Umgodi tackling crime and illegal mining. The latest crime statistics show a decline in serious crimes, including murder, robbery, and carjacking.

nnnn

Energy & Load Shedding Progress

nnnn

Despite recent Stage 3 load shedding, Eskom achieved a record 300 consecutive days without power cuts, thanks to the Energy Action Plan and its Generation Recovery Plan.

nnnn

South Africa’s ICJ Case Against Israel

nnnn

The government remains firm in its genocide case against Israel at the International Court of Justice (ICJ), underscoring its commitment to international law.

nnnn

A Call for National Unity

nnnn

In his previous address, President Ramaphosa urged South Africans to work together like "weaver birds," emphasizing cooperation and resilience.

nnnn

As the nation tunes on  6 February 2025, all eyes will be on the President to chart South Africa’s path forward.

post_content:

South Africa’s National Minimum Wage (NMW) Act, implemented in 2019, undergoes annual reviews and increases every March.

post_title: SASSA Warns Public About Grant Scam
post_content:
n

The South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) has warned senior citizens aged 75 and older, as well as people with disabilities, about a social media scam falsely claiming they will receive an additional R500 payment.

nnnn

SASSA Mpumalanga spokesperson Senzeni Ngubeni clarified that the grant-in-aid is not a separate grant but an additional payment for those already receiving older persons, disability, or war veteran grants and needing full-time care.

nnnn

Grant-in-Aid Eligibility Criteria:

nnnn

✔ Must already receive a qualifying grant.
✔ Requires regular care due to physical or mental disabilities.
✔ Cannot be receiving a state subsidy while in an institution.
✔ Must undergo a medical assessment confirming disability.

nnnn

The grant-in-aid is R530 per month and is paid alongside the main social grant. Payments can be collected in cash, through a bank or Postbank account, or via an authorized institution.

nnnn

Ngubeni urged beneficiaries to verify information through official SASSA platforms and avoid sharing personal details. Suspicious activity should be reported to SASSA or the police. Beneficiaries unable to collect their grant can appoint a trusted procurator or use power of attorney.

The match continued with end-to-end action, as Celtics took the lead in the 78th minute through Hlawulekile, only for Cosmos to snatch a late equalizer via Mohlakoane Perfect in the 84th minute.

nnnn

The game was intense, with both sides receiving multiple cautions, but no player was sent off. A fair result in a well-conteste

n

post_title: Farmer Arrested for Rotten Food Storage
post_content:
n

Pieter Johannes Grobler spent a night in custody before being released on R8,000 bail at the Secunda Magistrate's Court on 6 February 2025.

nnnn

Grobler was arrested by the Hawks’ Secunda-based Serious Organised Crime Investigation unit on 5 February 2025, following a tip-off about hazardous food storage on his farm. Law enforcement, along with SAPS and Govan Mbeki Local Municipality Health Inspectors, investigated the premises and discovered two warehouses containing four cold rooms filled with expired and rotten food, including meat, chicken, and dairy products.

nnnnnnnn

Following his court appearance, Grobler’s case was postponed to 27 March 2025 for further investigation. The court ordered him to report to Charl Cillier SAPS every Monday between 08:00 and 18:00 and to surrender his travel documents until further notice.

nnnn

Mpumalanga’s Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation head, Major General Nico Gerber, praised the officers for preventing the sale of unsafe food, saying the investigation aims to uncover other individuals involved in the operation.

nnnn

n

post_title: Mpumalanga Government Offices Left in Darkness
post_content:
n

A dispute over unpaid electricity bills has led to a blackout at the Mpumalanga government complex, including the office of Premier Mandla Ndlovu. The Democratic Alliance (DA) raised concerns on 4 February after power was cut at the provincial headquarters in Mbombela.

nnnn

The 90,000m² complex, managed by the provincial department of public works, is usually exempt from loadshedding. However, unlike tertiary hospitals, Rob Ferreira Hospital, a regional facility, does not share this exemption.

nnnn

The DA claims that the Mbombela local municipality cut the power due to the department of public works owing over R5.5 billion in unpaid rates and taxes. The party likened the amount to the cost of building the R1-billion Mbombela Stadium five times over.

nnnn

Schools May Be Next

nnnn

Teboho Sekaledi, the DA’s spokesperson on public works, called the situation “sad,” warning that schools in Mbombela could face similar power cuts if the department fails to pay. The party alleges that the department has ignored payment demands since June 2024, prompting the municipality to act.

nnnn

However, public works spokesperson Bongani Dlamini refuted the DA’s claim, stating that the actual outstanding debt for the 2024/2025 financial year is R113 million, with R61 million already paid. He confirmed ongoing discussions with the municipality and provincial treasury.

nnnn

Municipalities Enforce Tougher Measures

nnnn

The Mbombela local municipality has yet to disclose the exact amount owed. Meanwhile, the Mpumalanga government complex is not alone in this crisis. Recently, the Mangaung local municipality also cut power to government buildings over unpaid electricity bills, highlighting a growing trend of municipalities cracking down on non-payment.

nnnn

As of publishing, municipal spokesperson Joseph Ngala had not responded to inquiries. Similarly, provincial health department spokesperson Dumisani Malamule acknowledged media questions regarding the power cut’s impact on Rob Ferreira Hospital but had not yet provided a response.

nnnn

n

n

Government ministers have voiced strong support for President Cyril Ramaphosa’s State of the Nation Address (SONA), which emphasized economic growth, job creation, infrastructure development, and reducing household expenses.

nnnn

A Focus on Economic Growth and Jobs

nnnn

The President stressed the urgent need for a robust economy that benefits all South Africans, with a goal of economic growth surpassing 3% to drive investment, job creation, and poverty reduction.

nnnn

Agriculture Minister John Steenhuisen echoed this sentiment, calling for private-sector involvement to boost agricultural exports. He noted that the citrus industry could quadruple production if ports were more reliable.

nnnn

Deputy Minister for Women, Youth, and Persons with Disabilities, Mmapaseka Steve Letsike, welcomed the President’s focus on job creation and economic growth, particularly for marginalized groups. She praised the new R20 billion Transformation Fund to support black-owned businesses and small enterprises.

nnnn

Investments in Infrastructure and Public Services

nnnn

Steenhuisen commended investments in infrastructure, Early Childhood Development (ECD), and social relief grants, which will serve as a foundation for a sustainable income support system for the unemployed.

nnnn

Health Minister Dr. Aaron Motsoaledi highlighted key health-sector announcements, including the National Health Insurance (NHI), improvements to public health infrastructure, and efforts to eliminate HIV/AIDS by 2030. He emphasized that public health infrastructure and NHI can be implemented simultaneously.

nnnn

Minister in the Presidency, Khumbudzo Ntshavheni, stressed the need for better health infrastructure to ensure accessible hospitals and clinics for all.

nnnn

Modernizing Home Affairs and Boosting Tourism

nnnn

Home Affairs Minister Dr. Leon Schreiber welcomed the adoption of digital technology in his department, aligning with plans to create a "digitally first" Home Affairs system. He also emphasized the importance of automated visa processing to boost tourism and attract skilled workers.

nnnn

COSATU Welcomes Social Relief Grant Commitment

nnnn

COSATU President Zingiswa Losi praised the continuation of the Social Relief of Distress (SRD) grant, which will transition into a basic income grant. She also supported the focus on Technical, Vocational, Education, and Training (TVET) colleges, essential for infrastructure projects requiring skilled labor.

nnnn

With R940 billion allocated for infrastructure over the next three years, Losi warned that construction mafias must not hijack these projects.

nnnn

A Call for Urgency

nnnn

Steenhuisen emphasized that the government must act swiftly:

nnnn
n

“We can’t reach the 2029 elections with projects still stuck on the drawing board. Now is the time to move with speed and urgency.”

n
nnnn

As ministers rally behind the President’s vision, South Africa faces a pivotal moment to transform its economy, modernize infrastructure, and improve public services.

n

post_title: South Africa Strengthens Fight Against Corruption
post_content:
n

South Africa is intensifying efforts to combat corruption by equipping law enforcement agencies with better resources, stronger legislation, and advanced digital tools.

nnnn

Permanent Anti-Corruption Directorate

nnnn

In his State of the Nation Address (SONA), President Cyril Ramaphosa reaffirmed the government's commitment to tackling corruption, highlighting the establishment of the Investigating Directorate Against Corruption (IDAC) as a permanent unit within the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA).

nnnn
n

“We will ensure that the directorate is fully resourced and has access to all necessary information to prosecute state capture cases and hold those responsible to account,” said the President.

n
nnnn

Cutting-Edge Forensic Tools

nnnn

To bolster investigations into financial crimes and corruption, South Africa is setting up a world-class digital forensics lab equipped with advanced tools and expertise.

nnnn

Recovering Stolen Funds

nnnn

The government is actively recovering money lost to corruption and state capture. According to the President:

nnnn
n

“The Special Investigating Unit (SIU) and the Asset Forfeiture Unit (AFU) have already recovered over R10 billion linked to state capture cases.”

n
nnnn

He also confirmed that multiple legislative reforms have been signed into law based on the Zondo Commission’s recommendations.

nnnn

Strengthening Anti-Corruption Laws

nnnn

Efforts are underway to streamline anti-corruption legislation and enhance cooperation among law enforcement agencies. Key initiatives include:
✅ A review of anti-corruption laws by the National Anti-Corruption Advisory Council
✅ The Whistleblower Protections Bill, set to be introduced in Parliament this financial year
✅ Measures to prevent duplication of mandates among agencies

nnnn

Fighting Money Laundering and Greylist Removal

nnnn

South Africa was placed on the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) greylist due to concerns about money laundering and terror financing. However, the government has made significant progress in addressing 16 out of 22 action items required for removal.

nnnn
n

“We have strengthened our law enforcement system and will implement further legislative and system improvements this year,” Ramaphosa assured the nation.

n
nnnn

With stronger institutions, better oversight, and global best practices, South Africa is taking decisive steps to eliminate corruption and restore public trust. 🚨💰

nnnn

n
