post_title: Government Struggles to Eradicate Mud Houses
post_content:
n

The Department of Human Settlements continues its mission to eliminate mud houses in eMkhondo, Bushbuckridge, and Chief Albert Luthuli local municipalities.

nnnn

However, complete eradication remains challenging, as many residents resist demolishing their mud homes even after receiving RDP houses from the government.

nnnn

“With this initiative, we aim to provide safer, more dignified housing,” said department spokesperson Freddy Ngobe. “But many mud houses remain in use as extra rooms or kitchens. Additionally, budget constraints limit our efforts.”

nnnn

Amos Mkhwanazi, 82, from Ezinkomeni Village in eMkhondo, received a newly built house in December after his mud dwelling was demolished.

nnnn

Ngobe reported that over 7,000 mud houses exist across the province, concentrated in Nkomazi, Bushbuckridge, eMkhondo, Thembisile Hani, and Chief Albert Luthuli. The department plans to replace 261 of them in the 2024/25 financial year.

nnnn

By the end of the third quarter, 210 mud houses had been replaced—180 in eMkhondo, 17 in Chief Albert Luthuli, and 13 in Bushbuckridge.

nnnn

“The government remains committed to providing decent housing,” Ngobe emphasized. “For 2024/25, the target is 2,342 RDP houses. By December 31, 2024, only 1,104 had been completed—47% of the annual goal. Contractors must accelerate efforts to meet targets by year-end.”

nnnn

Despite challenges, the government continues working toward safer, more habitable communities.

n

post_title: Man Appears in Court for Toddler’s Rape
post_content:
n

A 26-year-old man appeared in the Chief Albert Luthuli Magistrate’s Court on February 7, facing charges of raping a two-year-old girl in Nhlazatshe. The case has been postponed to February 12. Mpumalanga police spokesperson, Lieutenant Colonel Jabu Ndubane, stated that the suspect allegedly lured the child, who was on her way to a tuckshop, into an abandoned house near Elukwatini. “The girl’s grandmother was alerted by a passerby who noticed the child bleeding. Witnesses had reportedly seen the suspect with her earlier, heading toward the area where the attack took place,” said Ndubane. Outraged community members quickly mobilized to track down the suspect. “They found him drinking alcohol and confronted him. A scuffle broke out, during which he sustained injuries before being apprehended. The police were notified, and he was arrested and charged with rape,” Ndubane confirmed. Authorities continue their investigation to ensure justice for the young victim.

n

post_title: Trump’s Refugee Order Sparks SA Debate
post_content:
n

The Trump administration has ignited a heated debate in South Africa, polarizing political discourse overnight, according to political analyst Daniel Silke.

nnnn

“It’s a polarization we certainly needed in SA, but it could also destabilize the country. Those critical of the ANC may now feel emboldened, believing Trump supports them,” Silke said.

nnnn

ANC’s Dilemma: Bow to Trump or Resist?

nnnn

Silke noted that the decision revives historical and current tensions, exposing deep-seated resentments among radical black and conservative white groups.

nnnn

“This is problematic for a country trying to rebuild. It places South Africa and the ANC in a difficult position—either they placate Trump or stand firm on policies like the Bela Act and Expropriation Act,” he added.

nnnn

Trump recently signed an executive order granting Afrikaners refugee status in the U.S. in response to South Africa’s land expropriation policy and its genocide case against Israel at the International Court of Justice.

nnnn

Silke believes the ANC is unlikely to concede, as standing firm could help rally nationalist support ahead of elections.

nnnn

“How the ANC responds is crucial, and it presents challenges for the opposition DA as well,” he said.

nnnn

Afrikaners React to Trump’s Offer

nnnn

Political analyst Piet Croucamp dismissed the notion of Afrikaners being specifically targeted, calling for unity between all South Africans and the government instead.

nnnn

“Afrikaners are not under attack. We need a national accord that is maintained and respected by the government,” he said.

nnnn

Dr. Benjamin Rapanyane, a senior political lecturer at North-West University, echoed this sentiment, stating that Afrikaners were unlikely to leave South Africa.

nnnn

“They are being dramatic for nothing. The consequences of this drama now outweigh any perceived benefits,” Rapanyane said.

nnnn

Thousands Show Interest in Relocation

nnnn

Despite differing opinions, interest in Trump’s order surged. South African Chamber of Commerce in the USA president Neil Diamond revealed that over 10,000 inquiries about relocating were received within 18 hours of the announcement.

nnnn

Meanwhile, Southern African Agriculture Initiative board chair Dr. Theo de Jager wrote an open letter to Trump, thanking him for the special provisions made for Afrikaners while urging him to extend opportunities to black farmers.

nnnn

“We need real opportunities for future generations to study, learn, and compete globally while preserving our diverse cultures and languages,” De Jager wrote.

nnnn

He acknowledged the challenges farmers face, including land expropriation threats, rising rural crime, and limited access to financing.

nnnn

“For some, the opportunity you have extended may be their only viable path forward,” he added.

nnnn

De Jager emphasized that many Afrikaners remain committed to South Africa, striving to build a non-racial society within the framework of the constitution.

n

post_title: Two Men Arrested for Attacking Putco Buses
post_content:
n

Two Mpumalanga men, Isaac Mabena, 36, and Luthando Skosana, 29, were arrested for allegedly torching 51 Putco buses at three depots. The pair appeared in court on 6 February 2025, to face charges related to the crimes.

nnnn

The men were arrested on 28 January, and appeared in the Mdutjane Magistrate's Court in Siyabuswa on 30 January. The case was postponed for a formal bail application.

nnnn

The arrests followed a violent spree by armed suspects in a Toyota Quantum, Mercedes-Benz Vito, and VW Polo, who went on a rampage across the Nkangala District on 27 January.

nnnn

The suspects allegedly set fire to 16 buses in Moloto, within the Kwamhlanga policing precinct, and 35 in the Siyabuswa policing areas of Thabane and Maphotla.

nnnn

Police spokesperson Brigadier Donald Mdhluli said the suspects also assaulted several employees, with a security guard sustaining a gunshot wound.

nnnn

“The men arrested are believed to be involved in these incidents. Investigations are ongoing,” Mdhluli said.

nnnn

The suspects face charges of malicious damage to property and robbery.

nnnn

Transport Minister Barbara Creecy condemned the attack, calling it economic sabotage. She instructed the department to collaborate with the National Joint Operational and Intelligence Structure (NatJoints) for an urgent response.

nnnn

The case was postponed to 13 February for a formal bail application, and the suspects remain in custody.

n

post_title: Minister Ramokgopa Announces Economic Reform Plans
post_content:
n

The Minister in the Presidency for Planning, Monitoring, and Evaluation, Maropene Ramokgopa, has unveiled plans to improve institutional effectiveness and accelerate the delivery of the Medium-Term Development Plan (MTDP) through targeted economic structural reforms.

nnnn

“The MTDP will address critical constraints in energy, transport, and logistics to unlock growth and enable job creation,” Ramokgopa announced on 7 February.

nnnn

Ramokgopa addressed the media during a session focused on the progress of the MTDP 2024-2029, which serves as a five-year strategic framework outlining the government’s priorities.

nnnn

It acts as a roadmap for translating the commitments of the seventh administration into actionable programs and policies, drawing on the Government of National Unity’s (GNU) statement of intent and the manifestos of 10 political parties.

nnnn

The MTDP's main priorities include fostering inclusive economic growth, reducing poverty, and establishing a capable State.

nnnn

Ramokgopa highlighted the alignment of the MTDP with President Cyril Ramaphosa’s State of the Nation Address (SONA) and its role in ensuring the effective implementation of national priorities.

nnnn

In his SONA, President Ramaphosa emphasized the importance of economic growth, job creation, infrastructure development, and reducing household expenses. He called for economic growth to surpass 3% to boost investment and job creation.

nnnn

Ramokgopa acknowledged the limitations in state capacity that have hindered progress in achieving inclusive economic development.

nnnn

“The MTDP, therefore, enhances the President’s capacity to effectively coordinate policy planning and implementation,” she explained.

nnnn

She emphasized that the reforms will improve agenda-setting mechanisms, streamline the intergovernmental cluster system, and ensure cohesive execution of national priorities, particularly regarding institutional organizational structure reforms.

nnnn

“We’ve now developed a method to modernize institutions by streamlining processes and clarifying the roles of different departments,” Ramokgopa said.

nnnn

She believes that by enhancing competitiveness, modernizing infrastructure, and eliminating bottlenecks, sustainable economic development will be achieved, with a stable and functional local government.

nnnn

Ramokgopa mentioned that local government reforms would focus on enhancing service delivery and ensuring development reaches all communities. This will be done by strengthening municipal governance through revised policy frameworks and targeted empowerment initiatives.

nnnn

Furthermore, the department plans to align State-owned entities (SOEs) with a developmental mandate, addressing governance challenges, ensuring accountability, and maintaining commercial viability.

nnnn

“This process involved inputs from a wide range of government stakeholders to ensure alignment with MTDP strategic priorities,” she stated.

nnnn

Cabinet has considered the plan and will make a decision on its approval at the next meeting. Ramokgopa indicated that the resolutions have already been adopted at the local government level.

nnnn

“We will take the plan to Cabinet to adopt it as a policy document for the seventh administration,” she explained, emphasizing that the success of this plan will be demonstrated by achieving its set targets and improving the living conditions of citizens.

nnnn

She believes that effective service delivery will build citizens’ trust and confidence in government institutions.

nnnn

“In his State of the Nation Address yesterday, the President directed all government functionaries to embrace a culture of quality orientation within the public sector. Our department and the Presidency will monitor cluster progress and address underperformance through corrective actions,” she concluded.

nnnn

n

post_title: Two Robbers Shot Dead in Mpumalanga
post_content:
n

Police in Mpumalanga are investigating an incident in which two alleged robbers were fatally shot during an attempted robbery at Tonga View on 09 February.

nnnn

Lieutenant Colonel Jabu Ndubane confirmed the incident, stating it occurred around 2 a.m. “According to reports, police responded to a shooting and, upon arrival, found a man with head injuries. The victim explained that he had been walking alone in Tonga View when two men attacked him,” said Ndubane.

nnnn

One of the assailants reportedly grabbed the victim from behind while the other pointed a firearm at him. The victim fought back and managed to retrieve his licensed firearm.

nnnn

“In the struggle, he shot both alleged robbers. They sustained gunshot wounds and were later declared dead by paramedics,” Ndubane added.

nnnn

Police recovered spent cartridges at the scene for further investigation. The victim’s firearm was seized as part of standard procedure.

nnnn

“A replica firearm loaded with cartridges was found next to the bodies of the deceased,” said Ndubane. “Police have confirmed that the firearm used by the victim is legally registered to him.”

nnnn

Authorities continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident.

n

post_title: NSPCA Offers Reward for Baboon Killers
post_content:
n

The National Council of SPCAs (NSPCA) has issued a R20,000 reward for information leading to the conviction of those responsible for the brutal killing of a male Chacma baboon, affectionately known as “Raygun,” in Mpumalanga.

nnnn

The baboon was reportedly chased at Botleng Secondary School in Delmas, beaten, and set alight. His body was later mutilated, with his hands, feet, head, and heart removed.

nnnn

The attack was allegedly captured on video, and the NSPCA has urged those who filmed the incident to come forward.

nnnn

“Videos circulating online went viral on Friday. Despite this, the school management refuses to identify those responsible. Our discussions with them revealed that the case is deeply linked to superstitions about baboons and witchcraft,” the NSPCA stated.

nnnn

The organisation said its investigation is being obstructed by some community members.

nnnn

“We are horrified by this level of cruelty. Raygun was merely seeking new territory, as all baboons instinctively do,” said Chief Inspector Douglas Wolhuter, Manager of the NSPCA’s Wildlife Protection Unit.

nnnn

To prevent similar acts of animal cruelty, the NSPCA plans to launch an educational campaign for both children and adults about animal sentience, legal protections, and appropriate responses to wildlife in urban areas.

nnnn

“Our goal is to broadcast this information via television and radio, but such efforts come at a significant cost. No animal should ever endure such suffering.”

nnnn

Anyone with information can contact the NSPCA anonymously at wild3@nspca.co.za or call 011 907 3590.

n

post_title: Arson Suspected in School Fire Disaster
post_content:
n

Dlamini visited a local school after a fire broke out in its administration block on February 8, destroying critical resources, including furniture, computers, surveillance cameras, and food supplies for pupils.

nnnn

Speaking to the media, Dlamini assured that the education department would implement interim measures to ensure operations continue.

nnnn

“As an immediate solution, we will secure a mobile office to prevent disruptions to administrative activities,” Dlamini said. “We are also providing mobile offices with toilets for teachers.”

nnnn

Dlamini attributed the fire to arson after assessing the damage.

nnnn

“I initially suspected an electrical fault, but after inspecting the building, I saw clear signs of forced entry. The back glass near the deputy principal’s office was cut, and the fire originated there,” Dlamini explained.

nnnn

“They likely stole items from the admin block before setting the fire. Unfortunately, almost everything was destroyed—food for learners, stationery, printers, and photocopiers that teachers rely on to assist students.”

nnnn

Dlamini expressed frustration over the setback, emphasizing the department’s ongoing struggle with infrastructure shortages.

nnnn

“This incident is a major setback for us as a department and as a province. We already have a backlog of infrastructure projects, and many of our schools are overcrowded due to urban migration,” Dlamini said.

nnnn

He condemned the alleged arson, stressing the impact on the community.

nnnn

“If this was deliberate, it is unacceptable. The perpetrators are not just destroying school property; they are damaging a facility meant to uplift the community and educate our children,” Dlamini stated.

nnnn

Authorities are investigating the incident, and the department is working on long-term solutions to restore the school.

n

post_title: School Abuse Allegations Spark Urgent Investigation
post_content:
n

The provincial Department of Education has issued a stern warning to educators following allegations of corporal punishment at Majika Primary School. This comes after multiple parents reported that their children had been subjected to physical discipline, despite it being outlawed in South African schools.

nnnn

One concerned mother, who wished to remain anonymous, shared that her 12-year-old son came home in tears after a teacher allegedly struck him with a pipe, worsening an existing injury. "My child was already in pain from a burn wound, and now he has suffered even more," she said. Another parent reported similar instances of physical punishment, stating that their daughters, aged 10 and 12, had also been beaten.

nnnn

Despite attempts to address these concerns with the school administration, parents claim that their complaints have been ignored. "Instead of acknowledging the problem, the principal dismissed our concerns and accused the children of lying," one parent lamented.

nnnn

Responding to these reports, the Department of Education’s spokesperson, Gerald Sambo, reaffirmed that corporal punishment remains a criminal offense and warned educators to immediately cease such practices. "If these allegations are confirmed, disciplinary action will be taken against those responsible. We urge any parents aware of similar cases to come forward and report them," he said.

nnnn

This is not the first time Majika Primary has come under scrutiny. Recent reports have surfaced alleging serious incidents of violence within the school, including claims of sexual assault among students. While the full details remain under investigation, community members have expressed deep concern over the safety of children on school premises.

nnnn

"We demand accountability and transparency from the school and the Department of Education. These children deserve a safe learning environment," said one local activist. Parents and advocacy groups are calling for urgent intervention, including better security measures and trauma support services for affected students.

nnnn

Authorities have assured the public that a thorough investigation is underway. The community is encouraged to report any further incidents to law enforcement or child protection agencies to ensure the safety and well-being of all learners.

nnnn

If you or someone you know has been affected by school violence or abuse, please contact the Childline South Africa helpline at 0800 055 555 or the Department of Education’s complaints office for further assistance.

nnnn

n

post_title: South Africa Releases Latest Greenhouse Gas Report
post_content:
n

The Minister of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment, Dr Dion George, has officially published South Africa’s 9th National Greenhouse Gas Inventory Report, providing estimates of the current emissions levels.

nnnn

“An accurate, complete, and updated greenhouse gas emissions inventory is a good foundation for effective mitigation responses,” the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment said on 10 February.

nnnn

The National Greenhouse Gas Inventory Report (NIR) was published in Gazette Number: 52067 on 7 February 2025. It covers the period 2000-2022 and will be part of the First Biennial Transparency Report to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

nnnn

“South Africa is required by the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change to provide in its national inventory, on a gas-by-gas basis and in mass units, estimates of anthropogenic emissions of carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), and nitrous oxide (N2O), by sources and removals by sinks.

nnnn

“The 9th NIR is compiled in accordance with the standard National Inventory Report format in line with the Convention Reporting Guidelines,” the department explained.

nnnn

In 1997, the Republic of South Africa ratified the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, 1992 (Convention).

nnnn

The Republic of South Africa is obliged under Articles 4(1)(a) and 12(1)(a) of the Convention to prepare and report on national Greenhouse Gas emissions and removals to the Conference of the Parties (COP).

nnnn

“The main objective of the Convention is to stabilize Greenhouse Gas (GHG) concentrations in the atmosphere at a level that would prevent dangerous human-induced interference with the climate change system.

nnnn

“The primary use cases of the inventory report are to support informed policy and decision-making on viable climate change mitigation response measures for South Africa, to achieve the envisioned transition to a lower carbon economy and a climate-resilient society, as aspired by the National Development Plan (Vision 2030) and the National Climate Change Response Policy (2011),” the department said.

nnnn

Government’s National Climate Change Response Policy was approved in October 2011 and was formally published as a White Paper in the Government Gazette.

nnnn

The objectives of the policy include effectively managing inevitable climate change impacts through interventions that build and sustain South Africa’s social, economic, and environmental resilience and emergency response capacity.

nnnn

The 9th National GHG Inventory Report can be accessed for more information at this link.

nnnn

n

n

Hlangalezwe Primary School, located in Mkuhlu Ward 24, has more than 200 learners, but its infrastructure is in a state of disrepair. Built in 1999, the school has not undergone any renovations since its inception.

nnnn

The classrooms are in poor condition, creating an unsuitable learning environment for students. The principal, Mr. Ratshwene Kgashane, has declined to comment to the media, citing a contract that prevents him from speaking negatively about the school.

nnnn

Additionally, the principal’s office serves as both a workspace and a storeroom, and there is no proper reception area. We urge the authorities to prioritize Hlangalezwe Primary School for much-needed repairs, so that students can have a more comfortable learning experience, regardless of the season.

n

post_title: Four Arrested for Putco Bus Torchings
post_content:
n

Two additional suspects, aged 31 and 33, have been arrested in connection with the recent torching of 51 Putco buses.

nnnn

It is reported that the provincial police arrested them in Siyabuswa on 11 February.

nnnn

They join Isaac Mabena (29) and Luthando Trevor Skosana (37), who were arrested on January 28, a day after the buses were torched.

nnnn

According to provincial police spokesperson Brigadier Donald Mdhluli, the suspects have been charged with malicious damage to property.

nnnn

“The arrests by the assigned team were made as part of an ongoing investigation into the incident that occurred on January 27. The suspects are believed to have been involved in the co-ordinated attack on the bus fleet, causing significant damage to the vehicles and posing a threat to public safety,” he says.

nnnn

Mdhluli adds that the suspects are scheduled to appear in the Mdutjane Magistrate’s Court on 12 February.

n

post_title: Woman in Court for Farm Murder
post_content:
n

A 45-year-old woman, Sonell Joubert, appeared before the Tonga Magistrate's Court on 10 February after being arrested for murder.

nnnn

Joubert, the owner of Tswale Educational Elephant Interactions, was arrested earlier this month following the discovery of Jurgen Nel’s body at Lowhills Farm.

nnnn

Mpumalanga provincial police spokesperson, Lieutenant Colonel Jabu Ndubane, said the brutal murder took place on 3 February.

nnnn

“According to a report, on that fateful day, the suspect allegedly stabbed and killed Jurgens Nel, 45, at a certain farm in Kamhlushwa near Komatipoort,” she said.

nnnn

Police and paramedics were notified about the incident.

nnnn

“Upon arrival at the farm, the victim had sustained multiple visible wounds and was unfortunately certified dead at the scene,” said Ndubane.

nnnn

A murder case was opened, and an investigation was launched.

nnnn

Preliminary police findings indicate that Nel was allegedly stabbed by Joubert, although the motive is yet to be determined.

nnnn

“Further investigation suggests that there could have been some kind of a scuffle that broke out prior to the fatal stabbing. However, through further investigations, the truth of what transpired will be revealed,” said Ndubane.

nnnn

Joubert was later arrested, and after her court appearance, the case was postponed to February 18.

nnnn

She is expected to seek bail during her next court appearance.

nnnn

Reports indicate that Joubert had recently laid a charge against Nel for violating a protection order she had obtained against him. According to the report, Joubert claimed that Nel had insulted and assaulted her.

post_title: Police Crack Down on Illegal Mining Operations
post_content:
n

In a significant crackdown on illegal mining activities, Mpumalanga police arrested six suspects, aged between 22 and 38, in Barberton after they were allegedly found in possession of prohibited explosives.

nnnn

Arrests in Mpumalanga

nnnn

The arrests occurred during a routine vehicle check along the R38 Road when police stopped a maroon vehicle with three occupants and conducted a thorough search.

nnnn

According to Provincial Police Lieutenant Colonel Jabu Ndubane, officers discovered four superpower 90 blasting cartridges, a capped fuse, and nine meters of detonating cord—materials suspected to be intended for illegal mining operations.

nnnn

Additionally, two of the arrested individuals were found without valid documentation and were charged under the Immigration Act.

nnnn

Three more individuals were later apprehended for failing to provide legal documentation for their presence in the country.

nnnn

All suspects are scheduled to appear before the Barberton Magistrate's Court on Wednesday, February 12, 2025.

nnnn

Meanwhile, Acting Provincial Police Commissioner Major General Zeph Mkhwanazi reiterated law enforcement’s firm stance against illegal mining and emphasized the continuation of Operation Vala Umgodi to combat these activities.

nnnn

Illegal Gold Processing Lab Busted in Limpopo

nnnn

In a separate operation in Limpopo, police arrested four suspects—three Zimbabwean nationals and one Mozambican—after discovering an illegal gold processing laboratory along the R71 near Tarentaalrand in the Letsitele policing area under Mopani District.

Provincial police spokesperson Colonel Malesela Ledwaba identified the suspects as:

According to Ledwaba, two of the suspects are alleged to be key figures in illicit mining operations in the area.

post_title: Fire Destroys Student Residence and Local Shop
post_content:
n

A fire destroyed a student residence at Mapulaneng Technical College in Acornhoek on the morning of February 11, leaving several students and other occupants stranded.

nnnn

According to a source, the blaze broke out around 06:00, consuming multiple rooms occupied mainly by students.

nnnn

“Nobody knows how the fire started, but the residence was completely destroyed this morning. A number of students and other people who lived there have lost all their belongings,” the source said.

nnnn

Fortunately, no injuries were reported, and all residents have been accounted for.

nnnn

Shop Fire in Acornhoek

nnnn

In a separate incident on February 10, a shop previously owned by the late Bishop Benjamin Silinda of the Nazarene Revival Church also caught fire.

nnnn

“We do not know what caused the fire, but some people managed to loot bed mattresses and other goods before the shop was completely destroyed,” said another source.

nnnn

Similar to the student residence fire, no injuries were reported.

nnnn

Police Response

nnnn

Provincial police spokesperson Colonel Jabu Ndubane confirmed awareness of both incidents but stated that no cases had been opened at the Acornhoek Police Station.

nnnn

Attempts to reach the shop’s management, the owner of the student residence, and affected students were unsuccessful.

nnnn

Investigations into the cause of both fires are ongoing.

post_title: Court Remands Two More Suspects in Putco Bus Arson Case
post_content:
n

The Mdutjane Magistrate’s Court has remanded Mduduzi Masango (31) and Steven Mthombeni (27) in custody following their arrest in connection with the torching of 51 Putco buses in KwaNdebele in January.

nnnn

The suspects were arrested in Siyabuswa on February 11 and appeared in court on February 12. They are facing charges of malicious damage to property and are set to return to court on February 13 for a possible bail application.

nnnn

Ongoing Investigation

nnnn

Masango and Mthombeni are the latest suspects linked to the incident. They join Isaac Mabena (29) and Luthando Trevor Skosana (37), who were arrested on January 28, just a day after the buses were set ablaze.

nnnn

Mabena and Skosana appeared in court on February 5, and their case was postponed to February 13, when they are expected to apply for bail.

nnnn

Police Statement

nnnn

Provincial police spokesperson Brigadier Donald Mdhluli confirmed that the arrests are part of an ongoing investigation into the January 27 attack on the bus fleet.

nnnn

“The suspects are believed to have been involved in the co-ordinated attack on the buses, causing significant damage and posing a threat to public safety,” Mdhluli said.

nnnn

The investigation continues, with authorities determined to hold all responsible parties accountable.

post_title: GNU will ensure SONA commitments become a lived reality
post_content:
n

Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs (CoGTA) Minister, Velenkosini Hlabisa, has assured President Cyril Ramaphosa that the Government of National Unity (GNU) will ensure that commitments made to the nation are fulfilled.

nnnn

“Honourable President, the GNU will ensure that the commitments you made to the nation do not become empty promises, but a lived reality,” he said during the State of the Nation Address (SONA) debate in Parliament on Tuesday.

nnnn

Members of Parliament (MPs) discussed President Ramaphosa’s SONA, which was delivered last Thursday, addressing issues such as tensions with the United States and the fallen soldiers in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), among others.

nnnn

The President’s address emphasised economic growth, job creation, infrastructure development, and the reduction of household expenses.

nnnn

“At the heart of this vision is a government that works for its people. The GNU must, therefore, be applauded for its commitment to building a capable, ethical, and developmental state, comprising ethical, skilled, and properly qualified public servants.

nnnn

“This work has already begun under the capable leadership of the Minister of Public Service and Administration, Honourable Inkosi Mzamo Buthelezi,” said Hlabisa.

nnnn

He welcomed the President’s recognition of the role traditional leaders can play in improving service delivery.

nnnn

State of municipalities

nnnn

Hlabisa acknowledged citizens’ concerns regarding failing municipalities and the urgent need for improved local governance.

nnnn

“Basic services must be delivered, and delivered efficiently,” he told MPs.

nnnn

He identified resource constraints as a key challenge affecting many municipalities and argued that the current funding model exacerbates inequality between wealthy and impoverished areas.

nnnn

“A new funding model is essential—one that considers each municipality’s unique needs and challenges and ensures a more equitable distribution of resources.”

nnnn

Infrastructure development

nnnn

Hlabisa supported the President’s focus on new infrastructure projects but emphasised the importance of maintaining and upgrading existing infrastructure.

nnnn

“To rebuild South Africa, we need to rebuild our education system, our healthcare system, and our economy.”

nnnn

Public healthcare

nnnn

He expressed support for the National Health Insurance (NHI) but raised concerns over its feasibility and affordability in its current form.

nnnn

“Government must prioritise strengthening the existing public healthcare system, which is plagued by inefficiencies and shortages of equipment and medical personnel.”

nnnn

Growing the economy

nnnn

Hlabisa welcomed the government’s commitment to job creation and economic growth.

nnnn

“We look forward to the implementation of the Medium-Term Development Plan (MTDP), particularly in relation to the three strategic priorities: driving inclusive growth and job creation, reducing poverty, and tackling the high cost of living.”

nnnn

The MTDP serves as a roadmap for translating the commitments of the seventh administration into actionable programmes and policies.

nnnn

Global developments

nnnn

Turning to international matters, Hlabisa expressed concern over the diplomatic fallout surrounding the Expropriation Act.

nnnn

“We condemn those who spread misinformation and work against our collective national interest to rebuild South Africa. That said, Honourable President, the IFP believes greater clarity and certainty must be provided on key issues of the Act, such as compensation and the definition of public interest.”

nnnn

He also paid tribute to the 14 South African National Defence Force (SANDF) soldiers who lost their lives in the escalating conflict in the DRC’s Goma region. The soldiers were part of the Southern African Development Community Mission in the DRC (SAMIDRC), aimed at restoring peace and stability in Africa’s second-largest country.

nnnn

“Their selfless sacrifice will never be forgotten. We support initiatives to restore peace across the continent, knowing that peace and stability are essential for economic development, social justice, and human dignity. Abrupt withdrawal would not be in the interests of the continent.”

n

post_title: Acornhoek Woman in Hiding After Ex Granted Bail
post_content:
n

An Acornhoek woman has gone into hiding, fearing for her safety after her ex-boyfriend was granted R1 000 bail in the Acornhoek Magistrate’s Court.

nnnn

The man, who cannot be named to protect the victim, was arrested on February 10 and charged with assault with intent to inflict grievous bodily harm (GBH). The case was postponed to March 3 for further investigations.

nnnn

The victim had opened a case against him on January 15, alleging that he slapped her and broke her arm with a spade. After seeking medical attention, she returned to the police station, where officers accompanied her to his residence, but he had already fled.

nnnn

The suspect remained on the run until his father took him to the police station on February 10, leading to his arrest.

nnnn

Fearing retaliation, the woman has since gone into hiding, saying, "I fear he will harm me if he finds me."

nnnn

The police continue to investigate the case.

post_title: Sassa Urges Beneficiaries to Replace Gold Cards
post_content:
n

The South African Social Security Agency (Sassa) and Postbank have urged social grant beneficiaries to replace their gold Sassa cards with the new black Postbank cards by February 28.

nnnn

Sassa spokesperson Paseka Letsatsi warned that gold Sassa cards will stop working after this date, regardless of the expiry date printed on them.

nnnn

“The grant payments in the week of February 4 to 5 were the last to be made with gold cards. Beneficiaries must visit their nearest Postbank site—located at major retailers like Checkers, Shoprite, Pick n Pay, Usave, and Boxer—to collect their black Postbank card,” said Letsatsi.

nnnn

The new Postbank card can be used at ATMs, retailer point-of-sale machines, and anywhere that accepts a bank card. It also offers benefits such as one free card replacement per year, three free in-store withdrawals per month, and one free monthly statement over the counter.

nnnn

To collect the new card, beneficiaries must bring a valid South African ID or temporary ID, as no card will be issued without it.

post_title: Man Dies After Snakebite on His Genitals
post_content:
n

A 45-year-old man, Caiphus Monareng, died after a snake bit him on his genitals while he was relieving himself next to rubble at his home in Casteel on January 6.

nnnn

His wife said the snake vanished into the bushes after the attack. Despite her pleas to go to the hospital, Monareng chose to consult a traditional healer, believing the bite was linked to witchcraft.

nnnn

After realizing his medicine was ineffective, the healer advised hospitalization, but Monareng lost consciousness on the way and died before reaching medical care.

nnnn

Local snake catcher, Cockroach Mdluli, urged immediate hospital visits after a snakebite, warning that traditional remedies cannot replace antivenom treatment.

nnnn

He also advised residents to clear rubble and close windows and doors to prevent snakes from entering homes.

post_title: Hawks Probe Fraud in Agriculture Tenders
post_content:
n

The Hawks’ National Anti-Corruption Unit is investigating fraud and corruption in two provincial Department of Agriculture tenders that were supposed to end in 2024.

nnnn

A police captain has begun interviewing six Bid Evaluation Committee (BEC) members, four women and two men, at the department’s offices in Nelspruit. Officials must provide statements, financial documents, and expenditure breakdowns dating back to 2021.

nnnn

Several companies are under scrutiny, including Izandla Ziyagezana Trading 44, Thulatshepo General Trading, and Nutri SA.

nnnn

Brigadier Thandi Mbambo confirmed the ongoing probe but declined to disclose further details, citing the investigation’s integrity.

nnnn

n

n

President Cyril Ramaphosa has reaffirmed that forced removals will never happen again in South Africa, citing the painful legacy of the 1913 Natives Land Act and apartheid-era land dispossession.

nnnn

Speaking in response to the State of the Nation (SONA) debate, Ramaphosa emphasized that the Expropriation Act 13 of 2024 ensures land can only be expropriated for public interest and with fair compensation.

nnnn

He recalled historical injustices, including the forced removals of 3.5 million people from areas like District Six, Sophiatown, and Cato Manor, calling them “one of the largest mass removals of people in modern history.”

nnnn

Ramaphosa stressed that the Constitution guarantees land access, restitution, and protection against arbitrary dispossession.

nnnn

“We are firmly committed to a non-racial, non-sexist society where South Africa belongs to all who live in it,” he stated.

post_title: ANC Leader Under Investigation for Sjambok Attack
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga SAPS is investigating a common assault case against an ANC branch secretary in Hazyview after he allegedly attacked an ANC Women’s League (ANCWL) leader with a sjambok on February 5.

nnnn

According to the victim, the suspect ordered her not to enter a school premises where she was attending a league meeting. When she questioned his actions, he allegedly retrieved a sjambok from his car and attempted to whip her, striking her vehicle as she fled the scene.

nnnn

The victim reported the incident to Hazyview Police Station. Lieutenant Colonel Jabu Ndubane confirmed that a case was opened and the suspect provided a warning statement. The prosecutor will decide on further action.

nnnn

The Ehlanzeni ANC secretary, Folas Sibuyi, confirmed receiving a formal complaint and stated that the party is committed to fighting gender-based violence and will conduct an internal investigation.

nnnn

post_title: President Ramaphosa Honours 14 Fallen SANDF Soldiers
post_content:
n

President Cyril Ramaphosa has paid tribute to the 14 South African National Defence Force (SANDF) soldiers killed in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), describing them as gallant heroes who made the ultimate sacrifice for peace.

nnnn

Speaking at the transfer ceremony and memorial service at Swartkop Air Force Base, President Ramaphosa expressed the nation’s gratitude for their service.

nnnn
n

"You died on the battlefield, far from all you held dear. But you are home now. You have come to your resting place. We are here to receive you with open arms and to lay you to rest."

n
nnnn

The soldiers were deployed as part of South Africa’s peacekeeping mission under the Southern African Development Community (SADC), protecting civilians and working towards a conflict-free Africa.

nnnn

A Nation in Mourning

nnnn

The sombre ceremony took place amid rainfall, symbolizing the nation’s grief. General Rudzani Maphwanya, Chief of the SANDF, condemned political debates surrounding the mission, urging respect for the fallen troops.

nnnn
n

"A nation in grief should not be throwing accusations about the merits of our deployment. Our people were armed, resourced, and capable of meeting the challenge."

n
nnnn

President Ramaphosa echoed this sentiment, calling for unity and respect instead of politicizing their deaths.

nnnn

Bravery and Sacrifice

nnnn

General Maphwanya praised the soldiers’ courage in the face of M23 rebel threats, saying they fought with unwavering resolve and resilience.

nnnn
n

"They did not back down in the face of adversity; instead, they rose to the occasion."

n
nnnn

To the grieving families, President Ramaphosa assured them that their sons’ sacrifices would never be forgotten.

nnnn

Commitment to Peace

nnnn

Despite the loss of soldiers, President Ramaphosa reaffirmed South Africa’s commitment to peace and stability on the continent.

nnnn
n

"We will not weaken in our resolve to realise an Africa free from war, poverty, and conflict. The greatest honour to their memory is to achieve this vision."

n
nnnn

As South Africa bows its head in collective mourning, the nation stands in remembrance of its fallen heroes who gave their lives in the pursuit of peace.

nnnn

Linda Zwane re-elected Mpumalanga Sport Confederation president
post_content:
n

Experienced sport administrator Linda Zwane has been re-elected as president of the Mpumalanga Sport Confederation (MSC) for another four-year term.

nnnn

Following his re-election this past weekend at Middelburg Regional Library, Zwane aims to use his renewed mandate to elevate sport development and ensure Mpumalanga athletes excel on national and international stages.

nnnn

“I am humbled by the confidence of MSC members. I do not take their support for granted. This is a sign of trust in the work I have been doing,” Zwane said.

nnnn

With several high-profile tournaments on the horizon, including the 2026 FIFA World Cup, the 2027 Rugby World Cup, the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon), and the 2027 Cricket World Cup, MSC wants to ensure the province is well represented in national teams—provided athletes qualify.

nnnn

“For us, the priority is athlete support so that we can make a meaningful contribution to the Los Angeles 2028 Summer Olympics target. We also want to ensure that federations receive the necessary backing for their developmental programmes,” said the MSC president.

nnnn

MSC enjoys strong support from the provincial government. Speaking at the Congress, Culture, Sport and Recreation MEC Leah Mabuza reaffirmed the department’s commitment to working with Zwane and his committee.

nnnn

“The Department is responsible for the development of sport throughout the province, and our work is made much easier by the presence of formidable structures such as the Mpumalanga Sport Confederation. We extend our profound thanks to all affiliates who play a key role in delivering sport programmes in the province,” said Mabuza.

nnnn

Zwane’s involvement in sport dates back to his playing days with Botleng Classic FC. He later ventured into coaching before transitioning into administration in 1996. Over the years, he has held various leadership roles, including vice-president of the South African Football Association (SAFA), president of SAFA Nkangala, president and secretary of the Victor Khanye Local Football Association, and board member of the South African Sports Confederation and Olympic Committee.

post_content:

An alleged thief who had been in hiding for several months has been arrested by police in Mpumalanga.

Provincial police spokesperson, Lieutenant Colonel Jabu Ndubane, confirmed that Innocent John Pretorius (51) was apprehended on the evening of February 12 on theft charges.

Eyewitnesses managed to intervene, but the suspect escaped before he could be apprehended. His current whereabouts remain unknown.

The victim’s condition is unclear, and it is uncertain whether she has reported the incident to the police. However, given the severity of the situation, community members are encouraged to remain alert and take safety precautions while authorities are being informed.

Community Concern and Safety Measures

Residents are urged to report any suspicious individuals or activity immediately to law enforcement. Additionally, security companies such as Taysec, HiTech, and Spesplan should be alerted to increase patrols and monitor the area more closely.

post_title: Matrics' Future Uncertain After Court Delay
post_content:
n

On January 31, the National Department of Basic Education’s high court appeal on the withheld results of some 2022 matrics was postponed to March. This means the plaintiffs will still not be able to apply or register for further studies while waiting on the outcome.

nnnn

The Mpumalanga Division of the High Court’s officials communicated the postponement to Adv DJ Sibuyi of Mthunzi Law Chambers, who represents more than 300 of the plaintiffs, and Ephraim Khambako, who represents another group, after 16:00 on January 30.

nnnn

“It was a day before the scheduled appeal hearing. The court rescheduled the matter to any time between March 26 to 28,” said Khambako.

nnnn

“Under the circumstances, this means our clients will enter a third year without knowing what their future holds. They cannot be admitted into a university or any institution of higher learning until the matter is resolved.”

nnnn

Meanwhile, this publication reached out to the Office of the Chief Justice’s (OCJ) communications department to understand what really led to the postponement of the case.

nnnn

“On Thursday [January 30], the parties in the matter, Rodgers Mkhonto and 62 learners/Minister of Basic Education and four others: Case no. A70/2022, were formally notified that the documents filed were not in accordance with the practice directives as issued by the court. As such, this matter could not be heard and was removed from the roll, and parties were alerted and requested to rectify the documentation,” said a statement from the OCJ.

nnnn

“On Friday [January 31], a response was received affirming a commitment by all parties in the matter to rectify the court bundles. The parties will have to re-enrol the matter once they are able to comply.”

nnnn

Sibuyi said an agreement was reached with all parties that the matter must return to court in March.

nnnn

The high court had ruled in favor of the plaintiffs on August 12 last year and ordered the education department to release their results during a scathing landmark judgment. This ruling was mostly based on the department’s failure at the time to follow its own rules regarding the procedures for withholding results and the subsequent investigations.

nnnn

After some suspicions of cheating arose, the department called the learners to attend disciplinary hearings and found them guilty of irregularities during the exams. Some of the learners were allegedly not even accompanied by their parents during the hearing.

nnnn

Hard Work, Goals, and Smart Effort
post_content:
n

Hard work truly pays off, but it’s not just about putting in the hours. It's about setting clear goals, managing your time, and staying focused on what truly matters. While starting from the bottom may seem challenging, it’s essential to take that first step with confidence and clarity. Once you know what you want, stay persistent, and don’t give up. Success doesn’t come overnight, but with patience, hard work, and the right mindset, it’s achievable.

nnnn

When you set specific goals for yourself, you create a path toward achievement. Working hard is crucial, but so is working smart. The combination of effort and strategy can lead you to new opportunities and personal growth. It's important to understand that hard work can help you develop valuable skills, and it can also open doors to new experiences and possibilities. Although success is never guaranteed, working toward your goals increases the chances of reaching them, even when external factors are at play.

nnnn

One of the main reasons people fail isn’t due to lack of effort—it’s often because their efforts are misdirected or misaligned with their true interests. Sometimes, individuals chase goals because they see others achieving the same things. They may follow trends or pursue something because it's popular, rather than something that excites them. This misalignment can lead to frustration, and without the right passion, it’s easy to give up. Finding what truly motivates you is crucial to sustaining effort and reaching your ultimate goal.

nnnn

Take, for example, those who work multiple jobs to support themselves. It may be exhausting, but the commitment to improving their circumstances is a testament to the power of hard work. In the same way, if you want to be successful or reach a specific goal—whether it's becoming wealthy, famous, or achieving personal milestones—you need to work toward that goal with dedication. The key is consistency and never losing sight of what you want.

nnnn

Success doesn’t only come from working hard. It comes from working smart, being strategic about your efforts, and focusing on the right goals. Working smarter means using your energy efficiently, staying organized, and constantly evaluating your progress. By aligning your work with your desires, you’re setting yourself up for the best chance of success. Believe in yourself, stay positive, and remember that every step forward, no matter how small, brings you closer to where you want to be.

n

post_title: Africa Adopts Convention to End Violence
post_content:
n

The Department of Women, Youth, and Persons with Disabilities has expressed strong support for the African Union’s (AU) adoption of the African Union Convention on Ending Violence Against Women and Girls (AU-CEVAWG). This milestone occurred during the 38th Ordinary Session of the Assembly of Heads of State and Government of the AU in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

nnnn

The AU-CEVAWG is a crucial legal framework aimed at preventing and eliminating violence against women and girls across the continent. This development follows a landmark decision made by the AU Heads of State in February 2023 during the African Union Summit, which reaffirmed Africa’s collective commitment to ending violence that has long silenced and oppressed women and girls.

nnnn

The convention was shaped by extensive consultations with various stakeholders across Africa, including traditional and religious leaders, youth, women leaders, and civil society organizations, among others. These consultations ensured that the voices of African citizens informed the design and objectives of the convention. Some of the key objectives include holding perpetrators accountable, providing justice and remedies for victims, and creating strategies that are rooted in African values and institutions, such as family and community support systems.

nnnn

The Department of Women, Youth, and Persons with Disabilities emphasized that violence against women and girls is not only a violation of human rights but also a fundamental breach of freedom, deeply ingrained in historical and traditional power dynamics between men and women. As the convention is implemented, a human rights-based approach will be taken, ensuring that it aligns with international, continental, and regional human rights standards. A victim-centred approach will be prioritized, providing access to justice, support, and comprehensive services for those affected by violence.

nnnn

This significant step marks a continued effort toward creating a safer, more equal environment for women and girls across Africa.

post_title: Two Suspects Killed in Business Robbery
post_content:
n

Two men were shot dead during a business robbery in Gedlembane, Pienaar, at around 02:30 on February 17.

nnnn

According to police reports, the suspects were part of an armed group that gained entry into a shop by using explosives on the door. Upon hearing about the robbery, the business owner contacted security for assistance.

nnnn

When the security team arrived, they found the robbery still in progress. The suspects opened fire, prompting the security personnel to retaliate. In the shoot-out, two of the suspects were fatally shot—one died at the scene, while the other collapsed and died approximately 500 meters away.

nnnn

A shop employee, a Somali national who resides at the business premises, was also injured in the exchange of gunfire. He sustained a gunshot wound to his left thigh and is currently recovering in hospital.

nnnn

The remaining suspects managed to escape, leaving behind their deceased accomplices. Police are urging anyone with information to come forward by contacting Detective Lieutenant Colonel Nokuthula Nkhoma at 082 469 2338, Crime Stop at 08600 10111, or by submitting details through the My SAPS App.

nnnn

Acting provincial police commissioner, Major General Dr. Zeph Mkhwanazi, condemned the incident and confirmed that a team of investigators has been assembled to track down the remaining suspects. “We are working around the clock to ensure the perpetrators are swiftly brought to justice,” he stated.

post_content:

In a dramatic turn of events at the Ermelo Magistrate's Court in Mpumalanga, four of the five suspects accused in the murder of Lieutenant Colonel Piet Pretorius abandoned their bail application.

nnnn

The suspects, Mthobisi Nkosi (40), Aubrey Xaba (35), Skhumbuzo Skhakhane (40), and Nyiko Mujovo (30), opted to remain in custody during their court appearance on February 18. The only female suspect, Valencia Skhosana (36), proceeded with her bail application.

The suspects were arrested by the Hawks' Secunda-based Serious Organised Crime Investigation unit in the early hours of January 17, 2025, following their alleged involvement in the brutal murder of Pretorius. Investigations revealed that a BMW, identical to one stolen in Witbank in 2018, was found torched in Ermelo. This vehicle was allegedly used as a getaway car in the murder.

The four suspects who abandoned bail will appear in court again on April 10, 2025, while Skhosana’s bail hearing is set for February 27.

Mpumalanga Provincial Head of the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation, Major General Nico Gerber, welcomed the postponement, stating that it would allow investigators to gather further evidence and ensure a strong case for trial. post_title: SAPS to Roll Out Body Cameras in April
post_content:

Police Minister Senzo Mchunu has announced that South African police officers will start using body cameras from April, with an initial rollout of 100 devices.

nnnn

In a written response to Democratic Alliance (DA) MP Billy Mzamo, Mchunu explained that the South African Police Service (SAPS) plans to introduce body-worn cameras during the 2025–2026 financial year. This initiative aims to enhance transparency and accountability in police operations.

nnnn

Following extensive testing to ensure the technology meets SAPS requirements, the police plan to acquire 100 body cameras annually. The exact number needed will be determined based on operational priorities, and the estimated cost per camera is R28,818.

nnnn

Mchunu emphasized that budget constraints and emerging priorities would influence the pace of procurement. A phased approach will be used to integrate the technology across different police units, ensuring a smooth transition.

nnnn

For years, lawmakers have advocated for body cameras to monitor police interactions with the public and curb bribery. Responding to Mchunu’s announcement, Mzamo welcomed the move but urged the minister to accelerate the rollout and ensure officers receive proper training.

nnnn

“The DA believes that body cameras are vital for enhancing transparency, accountability, and public trust in policing. They also protect officers against false accusations and malicious lawsuits,” Mzamo said.

nnnn

The introduction of body-worn cameras marks a significant step towards improving public confidence in law enforcement while supporting officers in their duties.

Private Sector Growth Key to Job Creation
post_content:
n

South Africa must shift its focus from short-term public sector job creation to fostering private sector-driven economic growth, according to the Foundation for Rights of Expression and Equality (Free SA).

nnnn

The latest Quarterly Labour Force Survey (QLFS) for Q4 2024 revealed a slight drop in the official unemployment rate from 32.1% to 31.9%. However, South Africa remains among the top five countries with the highest unemployment rates, far above the global average of 5%.

nnnn

The Need for Private Sector Growth

nnnn

Free SA argues that the government’s reliance on public sector employment and state-led job schemes is costly for taxpayers and fails to drive sustainable economic growth. Currently, 73.3% of South Africa’s workforce is employed by the private sector, yet its potential for job creation is hindered by restrictive regulations, policy uncertainty, and failing infrastructure.

nnnn

Global success stories such as Singapore and South Korea demonstrate that prioritizing private sector job creation leads to long-term economic prosperity. Small and medium enterprises (SMEs), in particular, need fewer barriers to growth and excessive government intervention.

nnnn

A Sustainable Path Forward

nnnn

Reuben Coetzer, spokesperson for Free SA, highlighted the urgency of the crisis:

nnnn

"South Africa leads the world in only two things: the rolling maul and youth unemployment. But unlike the rolling maul, youth unemployment has no try-line, no victory—only an ever-expanding scoreboard of despair with each quarterly report."

nnnn

While any decrease in unemployment is welcome, Free SA stresses that celebrating small gains while ignoring the larger crisis is dangerous. At 31.9%, unemployment remains a national emergency that requires bold reforms, not government dependency.

nnnn

Government Must Enable, Not Hinder, Job Creation

nnnn

Free SA believes the persistent unemployment crisis stems from excessive government control rather than a lack of intervention. Expanding the public sector without addressing inefficiencies, corruption, and unsustainable spending exacerbates the problem.

nnnn

To create a business-friendly environment and drive private sector job creation, Free SA recommends that the government:

nnnn
    n
  • Cut red tape and reduce policy uncertainty to attract investment
    • nnnn
  • Reform restrictive labor laws that discourage hiring
    • nnnn
  • Improve infrastructure to support business growth
    • nnnn
  • Encourage entrepreneurship and innovation
    • nnnn
  • Ensure fair competition by tackling corruption and political interference
    • n
nnnn

Without urgent structural reforms, South Africa risks deepening its economic stagnation. Now is the time for decisive action that empowers businesses and entrepreneurs, paving the way for sustainable job creation and economic growth.

post_title: Tour Bus Crash Near Dullstroom Injures Two American Tourists
post_content:
n

A tour bus carrying 11 passengers veered off the road and crashed into a rock embankment on the Dullstroom/R540 road just before 13:00 on February 19.

nnnn

The bus was transporting 10 American tourists along with a driver and a tour guide. The group was traveling from Johannesburg to the Kruger National Park, intending to take the scenic Panorama Route when the accident occurred.

nnnn

According to reports, two of the tourists sustained serious injuries and were taken to Belfast Hospital for treatment. They were stabilized and are not in critical condition. The remaining eight tourists were also transported to the hospital for observation.

nnnn

The driver and tour guide remained at the scene. One of the tourists, Barry Cuples from California, recounted the terrifying experience. A qualified first responder and firefighter, Cuples assisted emergency personnel in safely evacuating the other passengers.

nnnn

“It’s a miracle that there were no other serious injuries. Most of us were wearing our seat belts, including my wife and me,” he said.

nnnn

Apart from minor scrapes and cuts, Cuples, his wife, and six other tourists were unharmed.

nnnn

The visibly shaken bus driver explained that wet road conditions caused the vehicle to lose traction around a bend, slide into the oncoming lane, and collide with the embankment. No other vehicles were involved in the accident.

nnnn

Emergency personnel, including Netcare 911, the Ehlanzeni Fire and Rescue Department, and police officers from Dullstroom and Lydenburg, arrived within minutes.

nnnn

All passengers will be accommodated in various guest houses in Belfast until alternative transport is arranged. It remains uncertain whether the tour will continue.

Kruger National Park Battles Rhino Poaching
post_content:
n

More than 35 rhinos have already been poached for their horns in Kruger National Park since the start of this year, highlighting the relentless threat posed by poachers.

nnnn

On February 15, a black rhino bull was killed near Paul Kruger Gate, demonstrating the evolving tactics of criminals who continuously find ways to bypass security measures.

nnnn

Growing Demand Fuels Poaching Crisis
According to Bruce Leslie, regional ranger of Special Operations in the Kruger, the recent spike in rhino poaching is driven by persistent international demand for rhino horn.

nnnn

“Transnational syndicates targeting these endangered animals are relentless. We also suspect the ongoing unrest in Mozambique could be contributing to the problem,” he said.

nnnn

Despite proactive measures such as dehorning rhinos, poachers continue to target them, indicating that there is still a thriving market for their horns. Leslie urged local and international communities, as well as conservationists, to step up and assist in protecting the park’s rhino population.

nnnn

“We need actionable information about poachers and syndicates so we can stop them before they strike,” he said.

nnnn

Security Measures and Challenges
Law enforcement agencies are working closely with Kruger Park officials to apprehend poachers, but resource constraints remain a challenge. Covering more than one million hectares, the park requires additional manpower and equipment to strengthen its defenses.

nnnn

Poachers continue to adapt their methods to evade detection. “Despite limited resources, we have implemented various anti-poaching strategies, including installing solar-powered cameras in hotspot areas and deploying hound dogs and aerial support. These measures have proven effective, but criminals are willing to take extreme risks to kill rhinos,” Leslie explained.

nnnn

A Call for Support
Kruger National Park remains committed to combating rhino poaching but needs greater support from the public and private sectors. Leslie called on donors to assist by contributing funds or vehicles to enhance anti-poaching efforts.

nnnn

“Protecting these animals requires a collective effort. We urge anyone with information to come forward and help us save the remaining rhinos,” he said.

nnnn

With rhino numbers dwindling due to relentless poaching, urgent action is needed to prevent further losses and secure the future of these iconic animals.

nnnn

Child Rape Cases Surge, Justice Demanded Nationwide
post_content:
n

The alarming rise in child rape cases, particularly involving toddlers in Mpumalanga and the Free State, has raised serious concerns about the lack of swift action by authorities against perpetrators.

nnnn

Thandi Nontenja, secretary-general of the United Democratic Movement Women’s Organisation (Udemwo), expressed shock at the increasing incidents of sexual violence against children and urged the government to take decisive steps to address the crisis.

nnnn

Disturbing Incidents Across Provinces
Nontenja cited several disturbing incidents that occurred between November last year and early February. These include the alleged rape of a three-year-old and two-year-old in Siyabuswa and Elukwatini, Mpumalanga.

nnnn

In the Free State, a 12-year-old girl and a nine-year-old boy were allegedly raped in Welkom. Additionally, a three-year-old girl was reportedly raped, assaulted, and burned with a cigarette in Virginia.

nnnn

“These horrific cases serve as a stark reminder that child abuse affects both girls and boys. We demand urgent action to ensure justice is swiftly served,” said Nontenja.

nnnn

Call for Immediate Government Action
Udemwo has outlined several measures for the government to implement in addressing child rape and abuse. These include:

nnnn

Increased funding for support services for survivors of child abuse.

nnnn

Improved efficiency of the justice system in handling such cases.

nnnn

A national awareness campaign to prevent child abuse and promote child safety.

nnnn

“Justice delayed is justice denied. We cannot allow these perpetrators to roam free while young victims suffer,” Nontenja emphasized.

nnnn

Justice System Criticized for Delayed Action
One of the cases that sparked outrage is the alleged rape of a three-year-old girl in Siyabuswa. Although the incident occurred in December, it was only reported to the police on February 2. The case was assigned to the KwaMhlanga Family Violence, Child Protection, and Sexual Offences Unit, and the child was taken for medical examination.

nnnn

However, despite the suspect being apprehended by community members and handed over to the police, the case was not enrolled by the senior prosecutor. This led to the suspect’s release, sparking public anger and renewed calls for accountability.

nnnn

Provincial police spokesperson Brigadier Donald Mdhluli reassured the public that law enforcement remains committed to investigating all cases of sexual assault and rape, particularly those involving children.

nnnn

Community Outrage and Arrests
In Elukwatini, a 26-year-old man was arrested for allegedly raping a two-year-old girl. According to police spokesperson Lieutenant-Colonel Jabu Ndubane, the suspect lured the toddler into an abandoned house while she was on her way to a tuck shop. A passerby noticed the child showing signs of distress, prompting the community to take action. The suspect was injured during a confrontation before being arrested and charged with rape.

nnnn

National Call for Justice
Nontenja urged South Africans to stand together in condemning these heinous crimes and pressuring the government to take immediate action.

nnnn

“We cannot remain silent while our children suffer. The government must prioritize justice and protection for the most vulnerable members of our society,” she said.

nnnn

As the cases continue to rise, the demand for stronger law enforcement and faster judicial processes grows louder. Communities, civil society groups, and activists are calling for reforms to ensure that no child suffers in silence and that perpetrators face the full might of the law.

post_title: Ex-Kruger Ranger on Trial for Poaching
post_content:
n

The trial of Rodney Landela, a former Kruger National Park (KNP) regional ranger, and his co-accused, Kenneth Motshotsho, continues in the Skukuza Regional Court. The two appeared in court on February 20, where forensic investigator Cindy Harper testified.

nnnn

Harper revealed that blood found on two pairs of shoes and an axe in Landela’s car matched the DNA of two rhino horns discovered in Motshotsho’s vehicle at the time of their arrest on July 27, 2016. However, she noted that some evidence bags were not properly sealed. “The plastic bag containing the knife and axe was partially unsealed, and the boots, sandals, and jacket were packed in different plastic bags but later placed together in one large, unsealed bag,” she testified.

nnnn

Advocate Mswazi Makhubela, representing Landela and Motshotsho, argued that the mishandling of evidence could have led to contamination, questioning the reliability of the forensic results and demanding their exclusion.

nnnn

The State is expected to call more witnesses as the trial progresses.

nnnn

KNP spokesperson Isaac Phaahla acknowledged the park’s ongoing battle with poaching, revealing that over 40 staff members have been arrested and convicted, while others await trial for their alleged involvement in rhino poaching.

nnnn

Landela, a long-serving KNP employee with 15 years of experience, had received multiple achievement awards and was highly regarded by the Game Rangers Association, where he served as an executive member. He began his career as a general worker before rising through the ranks.

nnnn

His arrest followed an anti-poaching patrol in the Satara area on July 27, 2016, when rangers heard three gunshots near Kingfisherspruit around 13:00. Rushing to investigate, they spotted two men—one in a green ranger uniform and another in khaki clothing—fleeing toward a parked bakkie before speeding off. Moments later, rangers discovered the carcass of a freshly poached white rhino.

nnnn

A pursuit ensued, with SANParks deploying a helicopter and additional rangers to intercept the suspects. The bakkie was eventually stopped at Satara. Landela allegedly instructed Motshotsho to flee while he remained behind. Motshotsho initially drove away, discarding key evidence before returning. A subsequent search of the vehicle uncovered blood-stained shoes, a high-caliber hunting rifle, and two rhino horns allegedly discarded by Motshotsho in the veld.

nnnn

The case highlights the ongoing crisis of internal corruption within the park as authorities work to combat rhino poaching.

KaNyamazane Youth Protest Against Job Nepotism
post_content:
n

Members of the community, mostly the youth, from KaNyamazane Township protested at the City of Mbombela (CoM) premises on February 21, demanding an end to nepotism and corruption.

nnnn

They also called for the replacement of the project liaison committees (PLCs) overseeing the Kiaora/KaNyamazane N4 and KaNyamazane/Matsulu Interchange Projects.

nnnn

The community accused PLC members of political affiliations that grant them exclusive access to job-related information, leading to favoritism. “These projects were meant to be non-political community development initiatives, but the PLCs undermine transparency and fair employment opportunities,” stated the group’s memorandum submitted to CoM.

nnnn

“Many PLC members hold political positions, giving them an unfair advantage in selecting candidates for project jobs. Reports of after-hours hiring further limit community access.”

Public Order Police and CoM security monitored the peaceful protest.

CoM spokesperson Joseph Ngala dismissed the allegations, stating that the N4 highway projects fall under Sanral’s jurisdiction, not the City of Mbombela.

post_title: KaNyamazane Youth Demand Fair Job Opportunities
Load Shedding Crisis to End Soon
post_content:
n

The Minister of Electricity and Energy, Dr. Kgosientsho Ramokgopa, has assured South Africans that the country will overcome the current load shedding crisis by the end of the week.

nnnn

The minister, along with Eskom executives, briefed the media on February 23 to provide an update on South Africa’s electricity generation performance. This follows Eskom’s announcement that it had implemented Stage 6 load shedding as of 1:30 am on February 23.

nnnn

"I'm confident that by the end of the week, we should be out of this difficult situation. We are confident we're going to return to normal conditions. By the end of the week, there will be no load shedding. We would have gone through this wave, and load shedding should be considered extremely abnormal," Ramokgopa said.

nnnn

The minister explained that despite 300 consecutive days of uninterrupted power supply, recent setbacks occurred, including the loss of five generation units at Majuba and four units at Camden power stations.

nnnn

Eskom CEO Dan Marokane reported that out of the 10 lost units, six were back online. “We have five to six units planned to return to operation today, and we will reassess the situation after the evening peak. Our teams are focused on restoring these units,” Marokane said at the briefing in Pretoria.

nnnn

He explained that multiple unit failures at Majuba Power Station were caused by an overload on a transformer. The situation worsened when a unit startup from a long-term outage triggered a domino effect, leading to supply cuts to other units.

nnnn

“At Majuba, five units were lost, but by 6 am on Sunday, two had been brought back online, along with one unit at Camden. The remaining units will be restored soon,” Marokane said.

nnnn

Marokane added that Eskom had identified the root cause of the issue and was working to prevent similar occurrences in the future. “We will be diving deeper into system design to ensure containment of such incidents and assess risks across our fleet,” he explained.

nnnn

Government Apology
Ramokgopa apologized for the recent setback, emphasizing the government's commitment to ending load shedding.

nnnn

“On behalf of the government and Eskom leadership, I want to express our regret and apologize to the country for the load shedding crisis and its severity. The frustration and disappointment are understood, as we are working tirelessly to eradicate load shedding,” he said.

nnnn

He dismissed claims of sabotage, stating that available evidence pointed to technical failures. “The evidence before us indicates this is a technical issue. We must not manufacture explanations or shift blame elsewhere,” he concluded.

post_title: Gunmen Kill Two, Police Seek Suspects
post_content:
n

Mpumalanga police are investigating a murder case where two victims were shot and killed at Sheba Siding in Low’s Creek.

nnnn

Provincial police spokesperson, Lieutenant Colonel Jabu Ndubane, said the victims were killed on February 19 when two gunmen entered one of the victims' homes in the afternoon.

nnnn

"The two gunmen followed a 40-year-old man behind the house. Shortly after, gunshots were heard, and two men were seen holding firearms," said Ndubane.

nnnn

Another man inside the house responded by firing at the suspects before fleeing.

nnnn

"A 47-year-old neighbor, who peered through her shack after hearing gunshots, was also shot and killed," Ndubane added.

nnnn

The gunmen fled the scene, and the man who had escaped later returned, only to find both victims dead.

nnnn

Police recovered empty cartridges, live ammunition, and other evidence at the scene. No arrests have been made, and the motive remains unknown.

nnnn

Authorities urge anyone with information to contact Crime Stop at 08600 10111 or Detective Sergeant George Mazibuko at 082 546 2039. Anonymous tips can also be submitted via MYSAPSAPP.

nnnn

Mpumalanga's acting police commissioner, Major General Zeph Mkhwanazi, condemned the killings and ordered officers to act swiftly in apprehending the suspects.

Pastor, Three Others Arrested for Gold Crimes

A 40-year-old Barberton-based pastor and a 37-year-old man were arrested after police caught them in possession of gold-bearing material (GBM) on the R38 Road in Mpumalanga.

Meanwhile, during routine patrols on the R40 and R38 Roads, law enforcement officials apprehended two Zimbabwean nationals, aged 25 and 27, who were in South Africa without valid documentation. They were arrested for contravening the Immigration Act.

Authorities also conducted disruptive operations in Verulam Village, where they discovered two abandoned gas cylinders, which were confiscated for further investigation.

All four suspects are expected to appear in the Barberton Magistrate’s Court soon on charges of possession of GBM and immigration violations.

NSFAS Non-Payment Pushes Landlords to Crisis
post_content:
n

More than 150 landlords in Mpumalanga face financial ruin as the National Student Financial Aid Scheme (NSFAS) has failed to pay them for 2024 student accommodation.

nnnn

Contracted to provide housing for University of Mpumalanga (UMP) students, the landlords—under the Mpumalanga Accommodation Service Association (Masa)—are struggling with mounting debts, unpaid mortgages, and staff salaries.

nnnn

“We thought we were investing in a stable business,” said Masa chairperson Robert Dlamini. “Instead, we are expected to provide services without compensation while our businesses collapse.”

nnnn

Despite months of pleas, NSFAS only responded after media exposure, making partial payments to just 20 out of 150 landlords. Some have begun eviction processes, warning that students will be forced out if payments aren’t settled by month-end.

nnnn

Student Dineo Nyakane, 22, owes R14,000 from last year and was required to pay R7,000 upfront before registering. “I had to beg relatives for help just to be accepted,” she said.

nnnn

UMP spokesperson Tlangelani Ubisi confirmed that students with outstanding debt from 2023 cannot register, even if they have NSFAS funding for 2024.

nnnn

Parliament’s higher education committee chairperson, Tebogo Letsie, called for urgent action, saying, “Students should not be struggling with accommodation and funding when NSFAS should have resolved these issues.”

nnnn

post_title: Fakude Sentenced for Brutal Murder Case
post_content:
n

The conviction stems from a horrific incident on September 9, 2022, in Mkhondo, where Sipho Fakude and unidentified accomplices broke into a woman's home intending to rob her, said Monica Nyuswa, spokesperson for the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) in Mpumalanga.

nnnn

When the victim, 70-year-old Nomsa Simelane, stated she had no money, Fakude attacked her with a bush knife, severely mutilating her body before dumping her remains in a nearby river.

nnnn

During police investigations, her lifeless body was found in the river, leading to Fakude’s arrest. Despite pleading not guilty, he was convicted based on strong circumstantial evidence, including formal admissions and a police-led pointing-out procedure.

nnnn

Senior advocate Themba Lusenga presented key evidence, including eyewitness testimony confirming Fakude led police to the crime scene and described how he disposed of the body. Forensic analysis confirmed the victim’s blood on the weapon used in the attack.

nnnn

A post-mortem report revealed Simelane died from partial decapitation and severe injuries sustained during the attack.

nnnn

During sentencing, Simelane’s granddaughter gave an emotional victim impact statement, describing the psychological trauma her family endured after burying their brutally murdered grandmother.

nnnn

Lusenga urged the court to impose a harsh sentence, emphasizing the brutality of the crime and the need for deterrence.

nnnn

The NPA in Mpumalanga welcomed the conviction, reaffirming its commitment to ensuring justice for victims of violent crimes.

nnnn

“Every day, the NPA prosecutes cases that impact the safety and well-being of our communities, reinforcing our dedication to upholding the rule of law,” said Nyuswa.
