Africa Takes Centre Stage at G20 Meeting
post_content:
n

African perspectives and priorities are in full focus this week as South Africa hosts the G20 Finance and Central Bank Deputies meeting at the Cape Town International Convention Centre (CTICC).

nnnn

This is according to the Director-General of National Treasury, Dr Duncan Pieterse, who spoke to SAnews on the sidelines of the meeting.

nnnn

The G20 Finance Track is one of the few global platforms where Finance Ministers and central bank governors convene to discuss the global economy and its framework. Leaders also present key issues their respective countries seek to advance.

nnnn

"[It’s] a very unique and important opportunity for key discussions to take place. Of course, for our Presidency, we have placed Africa at the core of our agenda.

nnnn

“There are many different issues we are discussing this week that impact the future of the continent. These include the reform of multilateral development banks and increasing African voices in that space, infrastructure development, and financing options," Pieterse said.

nnnn

He further explained how the technical discussions will now feed into preparations for the Finance Ministers’ deliberations, which begin on Wednesday.

nnnn

“There are many technical details associated with matters such as quotas, replenishment of funds for African countries, and issues around the cost of capital and debt. These impact Africa’s developmental challenges and financing needs.

nnnn

“All these areas are covered by different G20 working groups. Each group focuses on a specific area, and when we meet as Deputies, we consolidate these discussions before presenting them to Ministers and governors. A statement is then released to capture the essence of these deliberations,” he said.

nnnn

One of the pressing issues for developing countries, particularly in Africa, is the growing debt burden. Rising borrowing costs and increasing interest rates contribute to economic instability.

nnnn

“To address this, we have established an Africa Panel, chaired by former Finance Minister Trevor Manuel. One of its key mandates is to examine ways to assist African nations in managing their debt challenges.

nnnn

“This includes governance, fiscal policy, and better financial management, as these factors influence borrowing costs. Additionally, economic growth is crucial to ensuring countries can service their debts. The G20 Africa Panel will play a significant role in integrating these concerns into the broader G20 agenda,” Pieterse stated.

nnnn

The G20 Finance and Central Bank Deputies meeting continues in Cape Town on 25 February 2025.

post_title: Energise Mzansi Campaign Empowers Energy Transition
post_content:
n

The Energy Council of South Africa has launched a nationwide campaign to empower citizens with knowledge and engagement opportunities regarding the energy transition.

nnnn

South Africa has pledged to reduce carbon emissions to net-zero by 2050 and transition towards a green economy. To achieve this, the government has committed to a just and inclusive energy transition that meets the country’s developmental needs, ensuring no one is left behind.

nnnn

“Energy literacy goes beyond understanding the basics—it forms the foundation for informed decision-making, constructive collaboration, and driving investment and economic growth through positive public sentiment.

nnnn

“Through this campaign, we aim to connect South Africans with factual information to help them navigate challenges and seize opportunities presented by the energy transition,” said Energy Council CEO James Mackay.

nnnn

The campaign focuses on six key technical energy topics:

nnnn
    n
  • Energy as an integrated system: Moving beyond a polarised “supply mix” ideology to a practical, integrated approach that balances supply-side actions with demand response, infrastructure, and digital integration.
    • nnnn
  • Vital emissions obligations: Addressing South Africa’s high carbon footprint and its exposure to carbon tax and border adjustments from 2026, particularly with Europe, its largest trade partner.
    • nnnn
  • Ongoing coal dependency: Recognising coal’s continued role in the energy mix beyond 2026 while promoting cleaner, more efficient usage and a balanced transition without compromising energy security.
    • nnnn
  • Bridging the transition with gas: Exploring gas as a stabilising force in the energy system, meeting fluctuating demand and supporting renewable energy growth as coal stations are phased out.
    • nnnn
  • Scaling renewables and storage: Assessing the expansion of solar, wind, and battery storage, overcoming deployment barriers, and integrating technology to make renewables central to South Africa’s energy future.
    • nnnn
  • Reforming the energy market: Highlighting the need for a competitive wholesale electricity market to unlock investment, drive efficiency, lower prices, and secure the country’s future power sector ecosystem.
    • n
nnnn

“The Energy Council estimates that R2 trillion will be required by 2035 for new technology financing and system upgrades. Government policy and commitment are clear. The two key drivers of our energy reform agenda are now anchored in law: The Electricity Regulation Amendment Act of 2004 and the Climate Change Act of 2024.

nnnn

“It is crucial that informed responses lead the transition, ensuring collaboration across all stakeholders to create sustainable, long-term energy solutions for South Africa,” the Energy Council stated. – SAnews.gov.za

post_title: President Ramaphosa to Open G20 Finance Meeting
post_content:
n

President Cyril Ramaphosa will officially open the first meeting of the Group of 20 (G20) Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors under South Africa’s Presidency.

nnnn

“The first G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors Meeting in South Africa will focus on key thematic areas, including the global economy, debt, infrastructure, the joint finance and health task force, international taxation, financial sector issues, and sustainable finance,” the Presidency stated on 25 February.

nnnn

This high-level engagement is set to take place at the Cape Town International Convention Centre on, 26 February 2025.

nnnn

The meeting is hosted by Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana and South African Reserve Bank Governor Lesetja Kganyago, under the G20 Presidency theme of “Solidarity, Equality and Sustainability.” It follows the second meeting of the Finance and Central Bank Deputies, held on 24 and 25 February 2025.

nnnn

“South Africa’s G20 Presidency commenced in December 2024, and the Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors’ meeting is part of a series of 23 ministerial meetings and approximately 130 working group sessions scheduled throughout 2025. The discussions will culminate in the G20 Leaders’ Summit in November 2025,” the Presidency added.

nnnn

The G20 was initially established as a platform for Finance Ministers in response to the Asian financial crisis of 1997-99, with the aim of coordinating policies to promote international financial stability. Following the global financial crisis of 2007, the initiative was elevated to a Heads of State and Government Leaders Meeting in 2008.

nnnn

Collectively, G20 members account for approximately 85% of global Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and 75% of international trade. The group comprises 19 countries—Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Republic of Korea, Mexico, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Türkiye, the United Kingdom, and the United States—alongside two regional bodies, the European Union and the African Union.

nnnn

The G20 continues to play a critical role in shaping global policy and fostering economic stability worldwide. – SAnews.gov.za

post_title: AgriSETA Summit Inspires Youth in Agriculture
post_content:
n

The AgriSETA Summit is a crucial initiative aimed at raising awareness about the agricultural industry and its career opportunities. The National Skills Development Plan (NSDP) 2030 highlights the importance of career development services, particularly for learners in rural areas. This summit serves as a platform to provide comprehensive career guidance, bringing together Sector Education and Training Authorities (SETAs), industry employers, higher education institutions, and agricultural training providers to help students make informed career choices.

nnnn

There are 21 SETAs, each covering different career sectors, including HWSETA, EWSETA, PSETA, and TETA, among others. The 2025 AgriSETA Summit was held at Acornhoek Ehlanzeni TVET College on 25 February, bringing together learners from 16 schools in Bushbuckridge.

nnnn

Opening Ceremony

nnnn

The event commenced with a prayer by Mr. B. Kwayiyo, the Deputy Principal of Ehlanzeni College, who welcomed all the learners. Mr. E. Mbuyane, the College Principal, then addressed the students, encouraging them to focus not only on academics but also on skill development, which could help them start businesses and create job opportunities. He emphasized that skills should not be taken lightly, as they are essential for future success.

nnnn

AgriSETA Leadership Encourages Agricultural Careers

nnnn

Mr. F. Phetla, the Acting CEO of AgriSETA, expressed his gratitude to all attendees. He addressed the high unemployment rate in South Africa, pointing out that Mpumalanga is an agricultural province, yet lacks sufficient agricultural colleges and universities. He urged learners to dream big in agriculture and emphasized the need for basic education to promote agriculture as a subject.

nnnn

"Walk with me to make agriculture fashionable," he said.

nnnn

Ms. S. Makhoba shared a message of support, emphasizing the motto of the day:

nnnn

"You don’t need a CV to work the soil. You don’t need a CV to feed your family. Agriculture is everything."

nnnn

She highlighted the various career opportunities in agriculture, such as becoming a soil scientist or agricultural engineer, and encouraged learners to explore this field.

nnnn

Inspiring Success Story: Mr. Mxolisi Mapalala

nnnn

A standout moment of the event was the inspirational journey of Mr. Mxolisi Mapalala, a self-made agricultural entrepreneur.

nnnn

Originally studying law, he later fell in love with agriculture and returned to high school to study mathematics and sciences, starting again from Grade 10. He excelled in his matric exams, ranking among Mpumalanga’s top 10 learners, and is now pursuing a PhD at Wits University.

nnnn

Today, he owns a chicken farm producing 40,000 eggs per day. He encouraged students to believe in themselves, saying:

nnnn

"Stop thinking that success is impossible. I am proof that it can be done."

nnnn

Education MEC’s Commitment to Agricultural Development

nnnn

The MEC of Education addressed the summit, emphasizing the importance of empowering youth through agricultural education.

nnnn

"If you want to promote anything, you need to be educated about it. Agriculture is part of our daily lives, and we cannot underestimate its significance," he said.

nnnn

The MEC announced that 22 schools in the province will increase their focus on agricultural studies, with plans to expand further. Additionally, 110 schools now require students to take mathematics and sciences, a step toward improving education quality in rural areas.

nnnn

"This summit is about building our youth and providing them with the right education. We must work together to strengthen our local TVET colleges and agricultural businesses."

nnnn

Career Exhibition and Conclusion

nnnn

After the speeches, learners attended an exhibition in a separate hall, where they received pamphlets and career information about different agricultural fields.

nnnnnnnn

The summit successfully inspired young minds, provided valuable career insights, and emphasized the importance of agriculture in economic growth and self-sustainability.

A woman from Alexandria, whose identity remains undisclosed, allegedly attempted to poison her late sister’s child for financial gain but tragically ended up killing her own child instead.

Sources say the woman, who cares for both her children and her late sister’s children, was in severe debt and sought to collect donation money from the community. In an attempt to do so, she reportedly laced a meal with poison, intending for her sister’s child to consume it.

However, on that fateful day, the targeted child returned home later than usual, while the woman’s own child, a Grade R learner with a bright future ahead, arrived early and unknowingly ate the poisoned meal. When the mother returned home, she found her child dead.

post_content:
n

President Cyril Ramaphosa convened a special Cabinet meeting on 24 February to discuss the ongoing Budget uncertainties. Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana presented an alternative proposal after his initial Budget plan faced rejection for the second time in a week.

nnnn

The first Budget, which proposed tax increases, was met with strong opposition from ministers. As a result, the Budget announcement has been postponed to March 12 due to ongoing disagreements.

nnnn

A Cabinet insider revealed that the rejection of Godongwana’s proposal has created significant challenges, damaging the minister’s reputation. In response, a subcommittee chaired by Deputy President Paul Mashatile has been established to address the issue with Cabinet’s assistance.

nnnn

Despite the controversy, another source confirmed that the Budget will still be tabled next month. However, Cabinet spokesperson and Minister in the Presidency, Khumbudzo Ntshavheni, dismissed the reports as "fake news." Her media liaison officer, Sipho Mbele, declined to comment further.

nnnn

During a six-hour discussion, Godongwana explained that avoiding VAT increases meant that proposed budget cuts would be necessary. These cuts included:

nnnn

R29 billion over the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF), affecting the hiring of unemployed doctors and healthcare services.
Funding cuts preventing the hiring of 11,000 teachers, impacting early childhood development initiatives required by the BELA Act.
A R2 billion reduction for prison warders, limiting staffing for correctional facilities.
R23 billion allocated for government employee salary increases, affecting a planned 5.5% pay raise.
R13 billion in Defence budget savings, intended for salaries and recruitment of young soldiers.
R5 billion for military deployment in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with reliance on reserve forces due to unbudgeted deployments.
A Treasury proposal to defer government contributions to the Government Employees Pension Fund for a year was also discussed. While this would free up R53 billion, it is expected to face strong resistance from unions.

nnnn

A source close to the discussions questioned the fairness of the proposed cuts, particularly regarding military funding. "South Africa is regarded as a military powerhouse in Africa, yet its armed forces are in a dire state due to budget reductions," they said.

nnnn

Despite these challenges, efforts continue to reach a consensus and finalize the Budget ahead of the March deadline.

nnnn

nnnnnnnn

Economic Growth and Job Creation

nnnn

The Medium-Term Development Plan (MTDP) 2025-2029 prioritises economic growth, job creation, and reducing poverty. The province aims for a 3% economic growth rate, with efforts to attract R50 billion in domestic and foreign investments. The government is targeting 60,000 job opportunities annually, with a focus on the agriculture, mining, tourism, and renewable energy sectors.

nnnn

To combat youth unemployment, which has risen to 50%, initiatives such as the Premier’s Youth Development Fund have been launched, funding 238 youth-owned enterprises with R257.9 million.

nnnn

Infrastructure Development

nnnn

Mpumalanga is undergoing major infrastructure upgrades, including road expansions, school construction, and healthcare facilities. The province aims to upgrade 75% of roads to 'good' condition by 2031. The Moloto Road upgrade, R40 expansion, and new bridges are among key transport projects.

nnnnnnnn

Safety, Security, and Social Development

nnnn

nnnn

Conclusion

nnnn

Premier Ndlovu reaffirmed his government’s commitment to delivering infrastructure projects, economic growth, and social services. He urged public-private partnerships to accelerate development, ensuring Mpumalanga remains a province of opportunity and progress.

"We make commitments and deliver," he stated. "Failure is not an option. We must build a better life for all."

A 28-year-old man, Batsheleni Dladla, has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for damaging essential infrastructure belonging to the Msukaligwa Local Municipality. The Ermelo Regional Court handed down the sentence after finding him guilty.

nnnn

The incident occurred on May 28, 2023, when members of the Community Policing Forum (CPF) were patrolling Chris de Villiers Street in Sun City, Ermelo. They spotted Dladla at a mini-substation with its door open, cutting cables using a side cutter. He attempted to flee but was caught and handed over to the police.

nnnn

Worker-Owned Arnot Opco Mine Faces Collapse
post_content:
n

A bold worker-ownership experiment in South Africa’s coal mining sector is on the verge of failure as Arnot Opco Coal Mine in Mpumalanga struggles to secure funding and resume full operations.

nnnn

The mine, acquired by retrenched workers after Exxaro ceased operations in 2015, symbolized hope for more than 1,000 former employees. However, financial troubles, legal battles, and the global transition away from coal now threaten its survival.

nnnn

Funding Crisis and Legal Battle

nnnn

During an oversight visit by the Portfolio Committee on Mineral and Petroleum Resources, Arnot Opco’s management revealed that the mine is under business rescue and locked in a court battle with Wescoal, its former shareholder.

nnnn

“Wescoal committed R150 million in funding but failed to provide it,” said Arnot Opco’s management. “Combined with the impact of Covid-19, this has left us unable to fully operate the mine.”

nnnn

The Rise and Fall of Worker Ownership

nnnn

Arnot Opco’s story began in 2015, when Exxaro retrenched 1,500 workers after losing its Eskom coal supply contract. Determined to take control of their futures, eight former employees formed Innovators Resources and took over the mine, establishing a trust benefiting 1,029 retrenched workers.

nnnn

They partnered with Wescoal to secure funding and expertise. However, the failure of Wescoal’s financial commitment, coupled with economic fallout from the pandemic, prevented the mine from operating at full capacity.

nnnn

A Mine Without Mining

nnnn

Today, no mining takes place at Arnot Opco. Instead, the company buys coal from third parties, washes it, and sells it—a stark contrast to the dream of a thriving, worker-run mine.

nnnn

The coal industry’s financial struggles have made securing capital nearly impossible, as lenders shift away from fossil fuel projects.

nnnn

“It is very difficult to raise funding right now,” said the company’s management. “Lenders are hesitant to support distressed businesses, especially in the coal sector, due to the global transition to clean energy.”

nnnn

Government’s Concerns and Community Impact

nnnn

Committee Chairperson Mikateko Mahlaule emphasized the importance of the worker-ownership model but stressed the need for accountability.

nnnn

“We want this mine to succeed. This is a model we have not seen before, and it must work. But companies must also benefit communities, not just extract and leave,” he said.

nnnn

The committee’s visit also exposed broader concerns in Mpumalanga’s coal sector:

nnnn
    n
  • Failure to uphold Social Labour Plans (SLPs): Community leaders accused mining companies of securing licenses with promises of development but failing to deliver once profitable.
    • nnnn
  • Mass retrenchments: Labour unions claimed companies are replacing permanent workers with contract employees, undermining job security and worker rights.
    • n
nnnn

Uncertain Future for Arnot Opco

nnnn

With no active mining and thousands of jobs at stake, Arnot Opco’s future hangs in the balance. Plans to appoint contractors and restart operations are underway, but without urgent funding, the worker-owned experiment may soon collapse.

nnnn

South Africa's B20 and G20 Leadership
post_content:
n

A Pivotal Moment for Business and Global Cooperation
Last week was a significant one for South Africa as we took center stage in global economic discussions through the B20 and G20 launches. While Cape Town’s beautiful weather set the scene, the world’s geopolitical tensions served as a stark reminder of the complex environment in which we operate.

nnnn

South Africa Hosts Historic B20 Launch
The B20, the business engagement arm of the G20, was launched, marking the first time this initiative is being hosted in Africa. Business Unity South Africa (BUSA) and Business Leadership South Africa (BLSA) are co-chairing this critical forum, ensuring that African business leaders contribute meaningfully to global economic policy.

nnnn

At the B20 gala dinner, BLSA Chairman Nonkululeko Nyembezi emphasized the importance of Africa's growing role in global economic affairs. B20 Sherpa Cas Coovadia highlighted the significance of South Africa leading this process, as businesses work together to develop actionable policy recommendations.

nnnn

Recognizing the complex geopolitical landscape, World Economic Forum CEO Børge Brende commended South Africa’s experience in conflict resolution. He acknowledged that this G20 cycle is particularly challenging but expressed confidence in South Africa’s ability to lead effectively.

nnnn

Africa’s Role in the Global Economy
Susan Lund, Vice President of the International Finance Corporation, underscored Africa’s potential as a key driver of future global growth. While many developed economies face population decline, Africa’s workforce is expanding, offering a young, dynamic market with critical minerals, arable land, and growing investment interest.

nnnn

However, Lund also raised concerns about credit rating agencies’ methodologies, which often disadvantage emerging economies like South Africa. This highlights a broader issue of fair financial assessments for developing markets.

nnnn

A crucial takeaway from the discussions was the shift in focus from individual countries to regional blocs. For South Africa, this means positioning ourselves as a leader in driving regional trade through the African Continental Free Trade Agreement (AfCFTA). A robust logistics system will be essential to unlock Africa’s full potential.

nnnn

G20 Finance Summit and Multilateral Challenges
Parallel to the B20 launch, the G20 Finance Summit took place in Cape Town, where finance ministers from member states addressed pressing global issues. President Cyril Ramaphosa warned that “the erosion of multilateralism presents a threat to global growth and stability.”

nnnn

The ministers debated critical topics, including climate financing and debt sustainability for developing nations, but failed to issue a joint communiqué due to geopolitical tensions—a reflection of today’s fragmented global landscape.

nnnn

Opportunities and Responsibilities for South Africa
Despite global uncertainty, South Africa’s role in the B20 and G20 presents both an opportunity and a responsibility. As one of the leading voices from Africa, we have a chance to shape a new global economic framework that prioritizes inclusive growth, sustainable trade, and regional cooperation.

nnnn

At the domestic level, transformation remains a critical agenda. Minister of Trade, Industry and Competition, Parks Tau, addressed the BLSA Council on his proposal for a Transformation Fund. The concept aims to support companies in meeting BEE obligations and assist SMEs that lack the resources to establish their own enterprise development programs.

nnnn

The success of this fund will depend on good governance and effective resource allocation to ensure it truly drives transformation while fostering economic growth.

nnnn

Looking Ahead: A Call for Leadership and Collaboration
While challenges exist both at home and abroad, South Africa is well-positioned to lead in shaping the future of business and global cooperation. Our ability to navigate relationships with key partners, including the United States and China, while strengthening regional trade, will be key to long-term economic stability.

nnnn

With open lines of communication and strategic leadership, South Africa has an opportunity to rise to the challenge and influence global economic policy at a time when the world needs fresh perspectives and bold solutions.

post_title: Overworked and Underpaid A Maid’s Silent Struggle
post_content:
n

Every morning, before the sun rises, she is already awake, preparing herself for another long day of work. From Monday to Saturday, she travels to the Ethiopian household where she works as a domestic worker, cleaning a house that is always a mess.

nnnn

Dirty dishes are piled high in the sink, sticky spills stain the countertops, and the floors are littered with food crumbs and discarded clothes. No matter how much she scrubs and sweeps, by the time she leaves in the evening, the house is just as chaotic as when she arrived.

nnnn

She looks after their three children, chasing after them as they scatter toys across the house, spill drinks, and leave their food half-eaten on the floor. Their parents do not seem to care. They watch as she picks up after the children, expecting her to handle everything without complaint.

nnnn

At the end of the month, she receives only R1,000—far below the legal minimum wage. She knows this is unfair, but speaking up could cost her the job. The last time she mentioned how difficult things were, they dismissed her concerns. “You should be grateful you have work,” they said.

nnnn

But how can she be grateful when most of her money is gone before she even sees it? Some months, she barely has enough for food and transport. There are days when she skips meals just to make sure she can afford to get to work the next day.

nnnn

She is not a live-in maid. Every evening, after hours of exhausting labor, she takes a taxi back to her small rented room, only to return early the next morning.

nnnn

They demand everything from her but give so little in return.

nnnn

She dreams of a better life, of fair wages, of being treated with dignity. But for now, she silently wipes down the kitchen counter, knowing that tomorrow, the mess will be there again, and she will have to start all over.

Global Fund Pledges HIV Jab Rollout Despite Uncertainty Over US Support
post_content:
n

The Global Fund for HIV, TB, and Malaria has committed to funding the rollout of the twice-yearly anti-HIV jab, lenacapavir, in low-income countries, including South Africa, regardless of support from the US government’s AIDS fund, Pepfar.

nnnn

Studies have shown lenacapavir is 100% effective for young women and 96% for gay and bisexual men. In December, Pepfar and the Global Fund announced plans to fund the rollout of the jab once regulatory approval was granted. However, concerns have risen over Pepfar’s continued participation, especially following the Trump administration’s termination of USAID-funded projects.

nnnn

Peter Sands, executive director of the Global Fund, reaffirmed their commitment: “We see lenacapavir as a game-changer in HIV prevention. Even if the rollout is on a smaller scale, we cannot afford to miss this opportunity.”

nnnn

Uncertain Future for US Support

nnnn

Pepfar has historically funded HIV programs in 28 developing countries, while the Global Fund supports over 100 nations, including South Africa. Initially, both entities, along with the Gates Foundation and the Children’s Investment Fund Foundation, pledged to provide two million people with access to lenacapavir over three years.

nnnn

The US government has not clarified whether it will honor its December commitment. Experts fear the Trump administration’s hostility towards HIV prevention projects signals Pepfar’s withdrawal from the deal.

nnnn

The Economic Case for HIV Investment

nnnn

The Global Fund argues that investing in health yields economic benefits. Research from Imperial College London found that every dollar spent on effective health interventions results in a $19 return. The Global Fund has invested $26.6 billion in HIV programs since its inception, with the US contributing $26.31 billion.

nnnn

This year, the Global Fund is seeking $18 billion in donor contributions to prevent 400 million infections and save 23 million lives by 2029. If US funding decreases or disappears, the scale of the lenacapavir rollout could be severely impacted.

nnnn

The Challenge of Affordability

nnnn

Lenacapavir, developed by Gilead Sciences, is still awaiting regulatory approval in various regions, including the US, EU, and South Africa. Gilead has licensed six companies to produce generic versions, but these are not expected to be available before 2027.

nnnn

To ensure widespread availability, cost is a crucial factor. Gilead has promised to sell the branded version at a no-profit rate, but its price remains unknown. A cost model suggests that for the South African government to afford lenacapavir, the price per shot should not exceed R629.40. However, advocacy group Avac estimates the initial price will be about $100 (R1,870), significantly higher than South Africa’s affordability threshold.

nnnn

The Path Forward

nnnn

Health experts stress the need for strategic planning in deploying the limited supply of lenacapavir. Dr. Linda-Gail Bekker, head of the Desmond Tutu Health Foundation, suggests assembling experts to determine the most equitable and cost-effective distribution strategy.

nnnn

Investment in HIV prevention has proven long-term benefits. A 2023 South African HIV investment case found that prevention strategies significantly boost productivity and economic growth. However, failure to sustain investments could lead to a resurgence of diseases, as seen with rising TB and measles cases in the US.

nnnn

Sands emphasized that the Global Fund’s broader mission extends beyond HIV, TB, and malaria, focusing on strengthening global health systems. “Diseases don’t respect borders. While we have made progress, the fight isn’t over. If we let up, these diseases will come back.”

nnnn

With or without US support, the Global Fund remains determined to push forward with lenacapavir, ensuring that HIV prevention remains a global priority.

Government Cracks Down on NPOs Linked to Terrorism and Money Laundering
post_content:
n

About 50 dubious non-profit organisations (NPOs) in South Africa are under government scrutiny for suspected terrorist funding and money laundering.

nnnn

“These organisations are believed to be used by foreign terrorist-supporting groups to recruit individuals, undermining the sovereignty of the country,” said Peter Netshipale, the acting director-general of the Department of Social Development.

nnnn

Government’s Crackdown on NPOs

nnnn

The crackdown aligns with the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendation 8, which focuses on NPO oversight. As the registrar and regulator of the non-profit sector, the Department of Social Development is responsible for ensuring compliance and eliminating high-risk organisations.

nnnn

“Recommendation 8 mandates our department to supervise the NPO sector, using a risk assessment framework. We work alongside law enforcement agencies such as the South African Police Service (SAPS), state intelligence, and the Special Investigating Unit (SIU),” Netshipale explained.

nnnn

Additionally, he emphasized the department’s role in educating NPOs on legal compliance and monitoring financial transactions to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing.

nnnn

NPOs as Vehicles for Money Laundering

nnnn

A major concern is the use of NPOs to launder money.

nnnn

“There have been cases where individuals deposit large sums—sometimes as much as R7 million—into an NPO’s bank account, only to withdraw it later without paying tax,” said Netshipale.

nnnn

The Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorist and Related Activities Act outlines crimes related to acquiring, owning, trading, or utilizing funds intended to support terrorist activities. Terrorist financing involves the movement and storage of both legal and illicit funds to support individuals, organisations, or operations linked to terrorism.

nnnn

South Africa Identified as a Medium-Risk Country

nnnn

According to National Treasury’s deputy director-general, Ismail Momoniat, South Africa’s national risk assessment on terror financing identifies the country as medium-risk.

nnnn

“While the phenomenon is not widespread in South Africa, we are required to implement mechanisms to assess risks across various sectors, including NPOs, and to conduct investigations where necessary. Law enforcement agencies must act on any breaches of the law,” Momoniat said.

nnnn

Progress in Tackling Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing

nnnn

Momoniat expressed optimism that South Africa would exit the FATF greylist by October.

nnnn

“Our biggest issue is money laundering, driven by corruption and organised crime. Addressing serious and complex cases of money laundering remains a key FATF requirement,” he said.

nnnn

The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) and the Hawks (Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation) have been making strides in addressing financial crimes. “I hope outstanding cases will be resolved by June, allowing for an onsite FATF visit,” Momoniat concluded.

nnnn

South Africa’s efforts to combat financial crime and ensure compliance with FATF recommendations remain critical in restoring global confidence and securing the integrity of its financial system.

The event served as a platform for stakeholders to discuss ways to drive inclusivity, expand access to resources, and nurture talent both on and off the field.

nnnn

Mashatile, unable to attend in person due to national duties, expressed regret but emphasized the importance of such platforms in promoting unity and development.

nnnn

The release of the 2024 South African Social Cohesion Index by the Inclusive Society Institute coincided with the event. The report revealed a moderate national cohesion score of 53.3, showing a slight decline from previous years. However, the North West and Eastern Cape were the only provinces to show improvement since 2021.

nnnn

“I encourage the Eastern Cape to continue this positive trajectory. Strong social cohesion enhances community resilience and contributes significantly to economic, social, and political progress,” Mashatile said.

nnnn

Sports as a Catalyst for Change
Mashatile highlighted the historical role of sports in breaking societal barriers. He referenced moments such as President Nelson Mandela’s attendance at Ellis Park Stadium, where South Africa triumphed over Zambia, and his iconic moment wearing a Springbok jersey alongside captain Francois Pienaar in 1995.

nnnn

“These were more than just sporting events; they were acts of reconciliation, showing how sports can heal historical wounds and foster national unity,” he reflected.

nnnn

Beyond bringing communities together, Mashatile stressed that sports, arts, and culture can be used to address critical social issues, including drug and substance abuse, gender-based violence, racial divisions, and economic inequality.

nnnn

“We must use these platforms to stand together against societal challenges and ensure the full inclusion of women, children, people with disabilities, and youth in sports and cultural activities,” he urged.

nnnn

Sports, Human Rights, and Inclusion
As South Africa observes Human Rights Month in March, Mashatile reminded citizens of the deep connection between sports and human rights principles.

nnnn

“Sport embodies fairness, non-discrimination, respect, and equal opportunities for all. It reaches billions, especially young people, making it a powerful instrument for social change, empowerment, and inclusion,” he said.

nnnn

With a renewed call to action, Mashatile encouraged attendees and stakeholders to harness the power of sports to bridge divides and build a more united and inclusive South Africa.

nnnn

Poaching Threatens Wildlife, Jobs, and Communities
post_content:
n

The poaching of wild animals and the destruction of the Kruger National Park’s fence not only harm the park and reduce tourism income but also lead to job losses and the spread of diseases to livestock and even humans.

nnnn

Wildlife reserves like Kruger are meant to conserve habitats and protect endangered species. These sanctuaries are crucial for biodiversity, providing safe havens for animals to live freely without human threats. However, the increasing use of snares and the illegal bush meat trade violate conservation goals.

nnnn

Communities must understand that the number of animals in the park is limited. Once they are all poached, everyone will suffer. According to Kruger spokesperson Isaac Phaahla, local and international tourists visit the park to see Africa’s wildlife. If these animals disappear, tourism will decline, leaving many unemployed and worsening poverty.

nnnn

“The province benefits from visitors who spend money on transport, accommodation, and food. The park employs many people whose jobs depend on tourism. If animals continue to be poached, businesses will shut down, and unemployment will rise,” Phaahla said.

nnnn

Poaching and snares are killing jobs and increasing poverty. Wildlife is protected to maintain nature’s balance and preserve the environment for future generations. Every species plays a role in the ecosystem, and their extinction would harm human habitats.

nnnn

Damaging the park’s safety fence to lure animals into residential areas poses a serious threat. It increases the risk of disease transmission between wild and domestic animals, some of which (zoonotic diseases) can even affect humans.

nnnn

“Our animals have diseases that can harm livestock, and domestic animals have diseases that can spread to wildlife. The fence is there to ensure both are protected. We must all work together to preserve wildlife and boost tourism,” Phaahla explained.

nnnn

He urged communities to safeguard wild animals and avoid tampering with the park’s fence. He also warned Kruger staff assisting poachers that they will face severe legal consequences if caught.

Uncertainty Looms Over April 2025 SASSA Grants
post_content:
n

The fate of more than four million elderly beneficiaries remains uncertain as April 2025 approaches. The South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) has yet to announce official details regarding the Older Person Grant, including payment dates and annual increases. With only three weeks until disbursement, pensioners are left in the dark.

nnnn

Adding to their woes is the ongoing SASSA/Postbank card migration crisis. Of the three million affected beneficiaries, only 1.2 million have successfully transitioned to the new system. A parliamentary committee recently admitted that meeting the March 20 deadline is "impossible." Despite this, SASSA insists that while old cards will soon be invalid, grant payments will proceed. However, many beneficiaries will struggle to access funds as they normally would. Alternative withdrawal methods will be available at SA Post Office branches, though this presents challenges for those in rural areas.

nnnn

To make matters worse, uncertainty surrounds the amount pensioners will receive in April. The last confirmed grant payments on March 4 saw recipients aged 60–74 receive R2 190, while those over 75 received R2 210. With no official communication on increases, pensioners are left to speculate.

nnnn

Much depends on Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana’s upcoming budget speech. However, political discord further complicates the situation. The Cabinet announced approval of the revised budget, yet DA leader John Steenhuisen contradicted this, stating no final agreement had been reached.

nnnn

What We Know About SASSA Grants
Applications can take over three months, but successful applicants will receive backdated payments.
Grants are only available to residents aged 60+ and are means-tested.
All applications must be submitted in person at a SASSA branch.
Due to long queues, booking an appointment online is recommended.
Required Documents for Applications
Applicants must bring:

nnnn

Proof of marital status
Utility bill (not older than three months)
Bar-coded ID (smart card or green booklet)
Proof of income and asset valuation
Declaration of private pension (if applicable)
Three months’ certified bank statements
UIF membership book or discharge certificate
Will, liquidation, and distribution accounts if a spouse passed away in the last five years
A trusted person may assist an applicant with a doctor’s letter and certified documents.

nnnn

Income and Asset Limits for Eligibility
Single: Maximum R8 070/month (R96 840/year), assets below R1 372 800
Married: Maximum R16 140/month (R193 680/year), assets below R2 745 600
Denied applicants have 90 days to appeal with the Department of Social Development. SASSA reserves the right to review grants with three months’ prior notice.

nnnn

Contact SASSA
For inquiries, contact:

nnnn

Toll-free: 0800 601 011
Head Office: 012 400 2322
Postbank USSD: 120218*3#
Email: grantsenquiries@sassa.gov.za
WhatsApp: 082 046 8553

Financial Accountability Protects NPOs from Financial Crimes
post_content:
n

The importance of financial accountability and regulatory compliance in protecting non-profit organisations (NPOs) from being exploited for money laundering and terrorist financing came to the forefront at the Department of Social Development’s (DSD) stakeholder engagement session.

nnnn

One of the stakeholders at the session on the Financial Action Task Force’s (FATF) Recommendation 8 was the Chartered Institute for Business Accountants, who underscored this point.

nnnn

The institute’s Technical Manager, Eszter Rapanos, outlined key interventions and innovations aimed at aligning regulatory frameworks with the FATF’s latest measures.

nnnn

The FATF is the international standard-setting body that oversees global compliance with anti-money laundering rules.

nnnn

Recommendation 8 of the Financial Action Task Force aims to protect NPOs from potential terrorist financing and money laundering abuse through effective implementation of risk-based measures.

nnnn

She highlighted the institute’s role as a professional body in advancing these measures to protect NPOs from financial crime, emphasising its commitment to upholding financial integrity.

nnnn

Rapanos addressed the unique challenges faced by South African NPOs, including limited access to technology, insufficient funding, and a lack of financial management skills, which make them particularly vulnerable to financial crimes.

nnnn

“The risk-based approach must be applied throughout the process, ensuring that high-risk areas are targeted while avoiding unnecessary burdens on compliant NPOs,” she stated.

nnnn

Among the significant regulatory changes, Rapanos pointed to the new requirement for compulsory registration of NPOs that operate across borders.

nnnn

In addition, organisations must now maintain detailed records of their beneficial ownership and enhance governance structures to prevent individuals with a history of financial crimes from assuming leadership roles.

nnnn

“The increased governance and transparency requirements will ensure that NPOs maintain credibility, but it also places additional administrative responsibilities on them,” she noted.

nnnn

Rapanos stressed that the new framework presents opportunities for collaboration.

nnnn

“By working closely with regulatory bodies such as the Department of Social Development, the Financial Intelligence Centre, the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission, and the South African Revenue Service, we can align compliance processes and reduce duplications,” she explained.

nnnn

The Chartered Institute for Business Accountants’ recommendations include implementing a tiered risk-based approach to compliance, where low-risk NPOs face fewer administrative burdens, while higher-risk organisations undergo more stringent oversight.

nnnn

Rapanos also called for increased training and capacity-building efforts to help NPOs navigate the evolving regulatory landscape.

nnnn

“The goal is to strike a balance between preventing illicit financial activities and allowing NPOs to continue their essential work without being overburdened by red tape,” Rapanos concluded.

nnnn

On Monday, the Deputy Minister of Social Development, Ganief Hendricks, called on NPOs and the civil society sector to work with government in seeing South Africa exit the FATF’s grey list by year-end.

nnnn

In his address, Hendricks cautioned government against using legislation to stifle the operations of legitimate NPOs that play a vital role in communities across South Africa.

nnnn

“Our National Development Plan calls for active citizenry, especially from the grassroots level. We must therefore guard against overburdening and frustrating grassroots initiatives through the use of legislation.

nnnn

“The objective of the NPO Act is to create an enabling legislative environment for the NPO sector to thrive and contribute to our national development agenda,” the Deputy Minister said at the time.

nnnn

At Monday’s session in Kempton Park, National Treasury said the FATF was not satisfied with the mere existence of national legislation, but also the enforcement of administrative penalties for high-risk NPOs that fail to comply with the provisions of the law.

nnnn

One of the FATF’s requirements is that Social Development, as the regulator of the NPO sector in terms of the NPO Act (Act No. 71 of 1997, as amended through the General Laws Amendment Act 22 of 2022), has to conduct more outreach and educational programmes with NPOs to promote a better understanding of the global anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing standards.

nnnn

The FATF grey-listed South Africa at its February 2023 plenary meeting held in Paris. It developed an Action Plan with 22 action items linked to the eight strategic deficiencies identified in the country’s anti-money laundering and combating of financial terrorism regime.

n

post_title: Spaza Shop Deadline Leaves Many Struggling
post_content:
n

Friday, 28 February 2025, marked the final spaza shop registration deadline for all informal traders. With the deadline now passed, Gauteng MEC for Finance and Economic Development, Lebogang Maile, confirmed that all non-compliant traders would be shut down without exception. However, immigrant shop owners—who make up the majority of informal traders in South Africa—claim the Department of Home Affairs (DHA) failed to issue necessary asylum-seeker documents, reports GroundUp.

nnnn

The registration requirement was introduced last year following the tragic deaths of 24 children from consuming expired or contaminated food. The crisis was so severe that President Cyril Ramaphosa addressed the nation. Initially, a 21-day deadline was set but later extended. However, Nelson Mandela Bay Mayoral Committee Member for Public Health, Thsonono Buyeye, described the compliance response as "extremely disappointing."

nnnn

In the Eastern Cape, of the 1,637 spaza shops, only 293 (17%) successfully submitted complete applications before the deadline. 843 applications (73%) were incomplete and therefore invalid. Despite being informed of their application deficiencies, many failed to make the necessary corrections. Buyeye stated that the department made extensive efforts to raise awareness and assist traders with compliance, yet 90% of spaza shops in Nelson Mandela Bay are run by immigrants who faced challenges in meeting the requirements.

nnnn

However, Chris Mapingure of the Zimbabwe Migrants Support Network tells a different story. He claims that many immigrant traders missed the deadline due to delays in obtaining documents from Home Affairs, particularly asylum-seeker permits that were not renewed on time.

nnnn

Registration required compliance with legal and health regulations, including immigration verification, food safety checks, pest control measures, fire safety certification, and zoning approvals. Thousands of inspections were conducted to ensure adherence to these standards, alongside training for food handlers. A business license processing fee was also mandatory.

nnnn

Despite these requirements, the South African Spaza-Shops Association argues that limited access to formal financial systems made it difficult for traders to pay fees. Additionally, some landlords refused to provide title deeds because their properties were not zoned for business operations.

nnnn

In response to the missed deadline, the association is urging the government to introduce a phased registration process. They propose an initial focus on health and food safety compliance, followed by later checks on immigration status, land zoning, and business licenses to allow traders more time to meet all the requirements.

DA Demands Full Disclosure on Licence Tender
post_content:
n

The Democratic Alliance (DA) has called on Transport Minister Barbara Creecy to release the full details of irregularities in the controversial R898 million driver’s licence card machine tender awarded to French company Idemia Security in 2024.

nnnn

Following an investigation by the Auditor-General (AG) that uncovered procurement irregularities, Creecy sought a High Court clarity order and confirmed that no funds had yet been spent on the project. She stressed that proceeding with the contract under these circumstances would be classified as irregular expenditure under the Public Finance Management Act.

nnnn

The DA argues that without the AG’s full report being made public, the root causes of procurement failures remain hidden. The party’s transport spokesperson, Chris Hunsinger, insists that beyond legal procedural issues, South Africans need answers on why the tender required external investigation in the first place.

nnnn

“The licence card issue highlights systemic mismanagement and corruption in the Department of Transport. Minister Creecy must disclose who and what caused the serious procurement non-compliance,” said Hunsinger.

nnnn

The tender process was first advertised in November 2022, re-advertised in April 2023, and ultimately awarded to Idemia in August 2024. Shortly after, Creecy instructed the AG to investigate. With the contract now under legal scrutiny, the rollout of new driver’s licence cards is expected to be delayed further.

Young Farmer Thrives Through Vocational Education
post_content:
n

In the heart of Mpumalanga, young entrepreneur Simangele Makutu is transforming the agricultural sector and proving that vocational education is a powerful tool for success. A former student of Ehlanzeni TVET College’s Mthimba Campus, Simangele has built a thriving agribusiness, supplying spinach and cabbage to major retailers such as Spar and Boxer.

nnnn

From Student to Business Owner
Simangele’s journey began with the National Certificate (Vocational) (NCV) in Primary Agriculture, which equipped her with practical skills essential for farming and agribusiness. Her breakthrough came during Work Integrated Learning (WIL) at BB Feeds, where she gained invaluable experience in supply chain management, financial literacy, and farm operations.

nnnn

Today, she employs four people on her farm, contributing to food security and economic growth. However, her ambition extends beyond personal success—she is passionate about youth empowerment and encourages young people to explore agriculture as a viable career path.

nnnn

Investing in Future Farmers
To support skills development, Simangele has partnered with Sifuyosethu, an AgriSETA-accredited organization, to mentor five students from the University of Mpumalanga (UMP). These students receive stipends while gaining practical farming experience, ensuring they are well-prepared for careers in agriculture.

nnnn

Overcoming Agricultural Challenges
Despite her success, Simangele faces significant challenges, particularly in accessing land—a common barrier for young black farmers in South Africa. Currently, she leases farmland for 15 years from her former high school, Bushbuckridge Secondary School, but she hopes to secure her own land in the future.

nnnn

Financial constraints also limit expansion. To improve productivity, she needs a proper irrigation system to ensure year-round crop growth. Without adequate water infrastructure, scaling up production remains difficult.

nnnn

A Call for Greater Support
Simangele’s story highlights the need for stronger support for young farmers, particularly in land ownership and funding for agricultural infrastructure. Her journey proves that agriculture is not just about food production—it is a driver of economic growth, job creation, and community development.

nnnn

As she continues to grow her business, one thing is certain: Simangele Makutu exemplifies the success of vocational education in agriculture. With the right opportunities and support, young South Africans can transform their futures through farming.

n

post_title: Street Sellers Struggle After Forced Relocation
post_content:
n

For us as street sellers and mothers, making a living is incredibly tough. There’s never a guarantee that we’ll go home with money or even enough to support our families.

nnnn

Our struggles worsened when we were removed from our market at Junction Mall in Hazyview by Mbombela Municipality and Twin City. That location was ideal, as it attracted overseas tourists who supported our businesses. The market itself was built for us by tourists, yet we were forced out.

nnnn

Twin City tried to assist by giving each of us R5,000 and providing containers for our businesses. They also promised that we would be given a new space back at Junction Mall, near the car wash, but to this day, no one has followed up on that promise.

nnnnnnnn

A Difficult New Location
We were relocated to 4 Ways in Hazyview, but this area is far from where we used to operate. Most tourists don’t use this road or stop here, as it’s on the main road with little foot traffic.

nnnn

Authorities also promised to put up a signboard to direct people to our new location with our business name, Phumulane Art and Crafts. They even assured us that they would officially register us, but that too never happened.

nnnn

A Declining Community of Sellers
When we were removed, there were 16 of us. Now, only three sellers remain, as many have given up and stopped coming. The lack of customers and broken promises have made it impossible for them to continue.

nnnn

A Shelter Built Through Kindness
The current shelter we use was built for us by the late Mr. Shengu Mabuza. He generously donated the money for building materials so we could have a space to work. Even today, we still operate from this market, holding onto hope that Mbombela Municipality will finally return to fulfill their promises.

nnnn

A Plea for Action
We are calling on the municipality and those in power to honor their commitments. We need:
✅ A proper market space with good customer access.
✅ Recognition and official registration of our business.
✅ Signage to help direct customers to our location.

nnnn

We do not want handouts—we just want the opportunity to earn an honest living and support our families, just as we did before we were forced out.

post_content:
n

The Skukuza Regional Court has sentenced Silas Mathebula (38), a Mozambican national, to 30 years in prison for poaching-related crimes committed in 2019.

nnnn

According to Monica Nyuswa, spokesperson for the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) in Mpumalanga, Mathebula was convicted on multiple charges, including trespassing, conspiracy to commit a crime, killing three rhinos, possession of illegal firearms, and possession of hunting weapons and ammunition.

nnnn

Arrest and Trial
On November 23, 2019, a section ranger patrolling the Malelane area stopped a suspicious vehicle carrying five men. Inside, authorities found a rifle, ammunition, and six fresh rhino horns. The suspects—Zwelithini Mathebula, Lucky Mhlongo, Teddy Dlamini, Silas Mathebula, and Forster Lubisi—were arrested. Lubisi later died after being attacked by crocodiles while trying to escape.

nnnn

Mathebula and another suspect, Lucky Hlungwane, fled after being granted bail. However, Mathebula was rearrested while attempting another poaching crime in Hluhluwe Game Reserve, KwaZulu-Natal, leading to his transfer back to Skukuza for trial.

nnnn

Conviction and Sentencing
During the trial, State prosecutor Lot Mgiba presented strong evidence, including DNA analysis that matched the rhino horns found in the suspects’ vehicle to three poached rhino carcasses. Ballistic tests also confirmed that bullets recovered from the carcasses came from the firearm found in the suspects' possession.

nnnn

The court sentenced Mathebula to 30 years in prison and declared him unfit to own a firearm under the Firearms Control Act 60 of 2000.

nnnn

A Win Against Poaching
Nyuswa emphasized that poaching continues to threaten biodiversity and endangered species, causing long-term environmental damage. She added that the NPA welcomes the sentence as a step towards protecting South Africa’s wildlife for future generations.

nnnn

South Africa Plans Public Sector Overhaul
post_content:
n

The South African government is set to implement a voluntary early retirement program for 30,000 civil servants to reduce the public sector wage bill. This initiative aligns with recommendations from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which has emphasized the urgent need for structural reforms to stabilize the country’s struggling economy.

nnnn

With national debt nearing R6 trillion and economic growth projected at under 1%, Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana is expected to introduce strict fiscal measures in the 2025 Budget Review. The government has allocated R11 billion for the 2025/26 fiscal year to incentivize early retirements, aiming to ease financial pressure on state resources.

nnnn

IMF senior resident representative Tidiane Kinda stressed that South Africa must adopt a more aggressive fiscal consolidation plan to reduce its debt trajectory. He also pointed to the high operating costs of State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs), which have drained approximately 5% of GDP since 2008. He recommended rationalizing wages, divesting non-core assets, and enforcing tighter financial controls.

nnnn

Kinda further noted that the public sector wage bill has grown by 2.2 percentage points of GDP since 2007 due to above-inflation salary hikes and an expanding workforce. To address this, the IMF proposes limiting wage increases below inflation, reducing allowances, and controlling workforce growth through measures like early retirement.

nnnn

The IMF’s latest assessment also underscores the need for broader economic reforms, including cutting bureaucratic red tape, improving public sector governance, and implementing labor market adjustments to support job creation. If South Africa implements these structural reforms, IMF projections suggest the country’s economic output could increase by 9% in the medium term while also reducing income inequality.

nnnn

With growing public debt and economic stagnation, South Africa faces a critical juncture. The IMF argues that swift and decisive action could set the country on a path to long-term stability and inclusive growth.

In February 2024, a group of armed men attacked Lawrence Mashego, 44, at his home in Boikutsong Trust. He was with one of his mistresses when the assailants forced him to reveal where he kept his money. Mashego allegedly directed them to another woman in Zoeknog A, who had his bank cards.

post_content:

The State Security Agency (SSA) has strongly denied claims linking it to a covert operation allegedly orchestrated by Minister in the Presidency, Khumbudzo Ntshavheni.

nnnn

Which claimed to have seen a classified intelligence document implicating Ntshavheni in an operation referred to as “Sibonkolo”. According to the publication, the operation aimed to elevate Ntshavheni’s standing within the ANC's top six leadership.

nnnn

In a statement issued yesterday by the Ministry in the Presidency, the SSA dismissed the report as entirely false. The agency said it usually refrains from commenting on media articles but was compelled to do so due to the gravity and implications of the accusations.

nnnn

"The allegations regarding the so-called Operation Sibonkolo seek to undermine the important progress we have made to reform and transform the SSA in line with the recommendations of the High-Level Review Panel," the statement read.

nnnn

It added that reports of such operations misrepresent the agency as one still engaged in rogue activities and political interference—an image the SSA insists it has worked hard to shed.

nnnn

“The SSA does not have an operation named Sibonkolo, nor any operation aimed at manipulating state machinery to benefit or harm the political ambitions of any individual,” the agency clarified.

nnnn

The SSA further emphasised that all its operations are conducted under strict procedural frameworks. It stated that the agency operates within established operational directives and is in the process of developing the necessary regulatory mechanisms.

nnnn

“In addition, oversight mechanisms as outlined by legislation are fully operational and functional. These are in place to ensure accountability and transparency in all aspects of the SSA’s work,” the statement concluded.

nnnn

The SSA reaffirmed its commitment to national security, free from political interference, and called on the media to report responsibly, particularly on sensitive matters that affect state institutions and public trust.

Naomi Engelbrecht, the Regional Court President (RCP) of Mpumalanga, is under fire following her controversial decision to transfer criminal cases—primarily involving rhino poaching—from the Skukuza Regional Court to Hazyview.

nnnn

A letter dated 6 March, authored by Judge Segopotje Sheila Mphahlele, the Judge President of Mpumalanga, unequivocally stated that no cases were to be moved from Skukuza to Hazyview. This directive followed an emergency meeting on 5 March between Engelbrecht, Mphahlele, and representatives from the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA).

nnnn

Despite this instruction, Engelbrecht had, two weeks earlier, ordered regional magistrate Mbongeni Ngobeni to prepare for court proceedings in Hazyview. This sparked confusion and operational chaos. On the scheduled court day, prosecutor Abednigo Mgiba, along with suspects, witnesses, and legal representatives, gathered at the Skukuza Court. Meanwhile, Ngobeni awaited them in Hazyview, under Engelbrecht’s directive.

nnnn

When Ngobeni attempted to relocate the entire proceeding to Hazyview, it was met with resistance. Legal teams, suspects out on bail, and even the police refused to comply with the abrupt instruction. Ultimately, it was agreed that all the cases would be postponed in absentia until 13 March.

nnnn

Judge President Mphahlele has since instructed Engelbrecht to draft a revised court sitting schedule. However, as of publication, no updated programme had been received by regional court magistrates or prosecutors.

nnnn

This is not the first time Engelbrecht’s decisions have come under scrutiny. In 2019/20, she clashed with then-Judge President Francis Legodi after attempting to relocate the Skukuza Regional Court to Mhala. Legodi challenged the legality of the move, leading to a full bench of High Court judges ruling Engelbrecht’s action unlawful and beyond her mandate.

nnnn

Her subsequent appeal efforts were dismissed by both the Supreme Court of Appeal and the Constitutional Court, with both institutions finding the appeal lacking in merit.

nnnn

The latest controversy once again places Engelbrecht’s leadership and judgement under the spotlight. For now, all affected criminal cases—particularly those related to rhino poaching—have been officially reinstated to Skukuza Regional Court, pending further clarity from the judiciary.

The Department of Health has urged former mine workers and their families to register for social security benefits related to occupational diseases, as part of a nationwide effort to address historic injustices in the mining sector.

The initiative, launched in collaboration with the Medical Bureau for Occupational Diseases (MBOD), aims to help eligible individuals access unclaimed compensation for work-related illnesses. It also ensures that the families of deceased miners can claim outstanding funds owed to them.

nnnn

Registration will include free medical screening to assess any occupational diseases such as silicosis, tuberculosis (TB), and hearing loss—common among mine workers due to prolonged exposure to hazardous environments.

nnnn

Eligible ex-mine workers are advised to bring relevant documents when registering. These include a national identity document, any paperwork received from previous mining employers, and the traditional “Makhulu-skop” or mineworker’s identity card, which was historically used in the mining industry.

nnnn

Data from the MBOD shows that more than 2,000 ex-mine workers in the West Rand alone have yet to claim their benefits. Across Gauteng, an additional 7,500 individuals are believed to be unregistered, with many unaware of their entitlements or how to claim them.

nnnn

The Department of Health believes this programme is a critical step in righting past wrongs, particularly for workers who left the mining sector without fair compensation or access to appropriate healthcare.

nnnn

Gauteng MEC for Health and Wellness, Nomantu Nkomo-Ralehoko, emphasised the importance of the initiative:
“Mining built this country’s economy, yet thousands of ex-mine workers were left without proper health care or financial support. This programme seeks to change that by ensuring they receive the assistance they rightfully deserve.”

nnnn

She added that the department is working closely with community leaders and local organisations to ensure that information about the programme reaches as many affected individuals as possible.

nnnn

The campaign will expand to other provinces in the coming months, targeting former miners and their families who may still be unaware of their right to claim.

April Fuel Price Cut Brings Relief
post_content:
n

Motorists are set to benefit from a notable drop in petrol prices next month, as economists predict a substantial reduction driven by a stronger rand and easing international oil prices.

nnnn

On 24 March, several economists forecast a petrol price cut ranging between 85 cents and R1 per litre in April, offering some reprieve for financially constrained South African consumers. This follows the Reserve Bank's recent decision to keep interest rates unchanged at 7.5% amid gradually rising inflation.

nnnn

Old Mutual Group’s Chief Economist, Johann Els, expects a petrol price cut of around 85 cents per litre. “Currently, the daily recovery is 58 cents per litre, with the monthly average at 87 cents. I anticipate the final figure to settle around 85 cents,” he said. “This remains a significant reduction, and if oil prices continue easing and the rand strengthens, we could see further cuts in the coming months.”

nnnn

Els added that Brent crude oil is likely to settle around $70 per barrel, contributing to the positive fuel price outlook.

nnnn

Efficient Group’s Chief Economist, Dawie Roodt, echoed the optimism, estimating a reduction of between 90 cents and R1 per litre. “Both the declining international oil price and the improving rand have contributed to this anticipated decrease. It’s excellent news for inflation and for motorists.”

nnnn

Waldo Krugell, an economics professor at North-West University, said the Central Energy Fund’s data showed an over-recovery of 87 cents for 95-octane petrol and 96 cents for diesel. “If the trend holds, we’ll see a sizeable cut next month, which bodes well for inflation expectations.”

nnnn

Independent economist Prof Bonke Dumisa agreed, stating that March’s lower oil price and stronger rand compared to February support the case for price cuts in both petrol and diesel.

nnnn

Tracey-Lee Solomon from the Bureau for Economic Research noted that global oil prices had eased due to increased production and hopes for a Russia-Ukraine resolution. “The rand’s relative strength, coupled with declining product prices, means consumers can expect a welcome break.”

nnnn

Annabel Bishop, Investec’s Chief Economist, said the fuel price drop in April follows previous changes: “January and February saw increases of 12c and 82c respectively, while March delivered a minor cut of 7c. With petroleum product prices now falling, April brings long-awaited relief.”

nnnn

“This marks a crucial step towards completing one of South Africa’s largest infrastructure projects,” Eskom noted.

nnnn

Once fully operational, Kusile Power Station is expected to contribute 4,800MW to the national grid, reinforcing its status as the country’s largest infrastructure investment.

nnnn

Meanwhile, Medupi Power Station—Kusile’s sister facility—is set to return Unit 4 to service by the end of April 2025, following repairs to a generator stator fault. The unit is expected to provide an additional 800MW.

nnnn

nnnn

n

nnnn

post_content:
n

As part of World Tuberculosis (TB) Month commemorations in March, community members from Pienaar and surrounding areas took part in a TB Awareness Walk on March 28. The walk aimed to educate residents about the dangers of TB and the importance of early testing and consistent treatment.

nnnn

The event was spearheaded by Lifa Lesive Community Development (LLCD), in collaboration with the Mpumalanga Department of Health and the Traditional Healers Organisation (THO).

nnnn

According to LLCD founder Lucky Nkosi, the initiative was born out of the community’s struggles with limited access to healthcare.

nnnn

“TB is a highly infectious disease that requires urgent attention. The walk was a success, and the support from residents was encouraging. We started this initiative because many local clinics lack the resources to adequately support TB patients,” he said.

nnnn

Recent statistics from the National Department of Health revealed that over 50,000 people died from TB in 2022, making it one of the deadliest diseases in the country.

nnnn

Sizwe Nkosi, a TB coordinator for the Department of Health in Mpumalanga, emphasized the need for community-level awareness.

nnnn

“We have clinics in Pienaar, Daantjie, and Msogwaba assisting TB patients. However, many people diagnosed with TB stop taking their medication, which worsens their condition. Education is key in fighting this disease,” he explained.

nnnn

The event also underscored the critical role that traditional healers play in addressing public health challenges. Levy Nkosi, a representative from the THO, noted that many people still seek traditional remedies for serious illnesses like TB.

nnnn

“TB is the second most dangerous disease in South Africa after HIV. While traditional healing is important in our culture, TB needs medical attention. We’re here to encourage people to combine our support with clinical treatment, proper medication, and nutrition,” he said.

nnnn

The awareness walk not only brought the community together but also served as a call to action — urging residents to get tested, seek treatment early, and help reduce TB infections in the region.

nnnn

nnnn

The visit also provided a platform to address pressing concerns faced by the college. The College Principal highlighted issues such as ageing infrastructure and the limited resources available for upgrades and expansions. He also stressed the need for increased collaboration between TVET institutions and industry partners to enhance work-integrated learning opportunities.

nnnn

One of the key challenges TVET students face is the lack of access to workplace experience, which is crucial for their professional development. The Deputy Minister acknowledged this concern and reaffirmed the government’s commitment to working closely with the private sector to create more opportunities for students.

nnnn

The Department of Higher Education, Science and Innovation has prioritised improving the TVET sector by enhancing infrastructure, increasing funding, and fostering partnerships with businesses to ensure that graduates are work-ready. post_title: Body of Missing Traditional Healer Recovered from Crocodile River in Mpumalanga
post_content:
n

Police divers have recovered the body of a missing traditional healer who disappeared in the Crocodile River, near Kanyamazane in Mpumalanga. The tragic discovery was made on the afternoon of 13 April, three days after the man was reported missing.

nnnn

According to provincial police spokesperson Lieutenant Colonel Jabu Ndubane, the incident occurred on 10 April, when the traditional healer and a prophet went to the river to conduct prayers and perform spiritual rituals.

nnnn

"While they were performing the rituals, the prophet noticed that his companion had suddenly vanished," said Ndubane. "He called out his name and searched the surrounding area but could not find him."

nnnn

The prophet later gathered their belongings and went to inform the traditional healer's family about the incident. He then accompanied the man's wife to the local police station to formally report the disappearance.

nnnn

A search operation was immediately launched, involving members of the SAPS Diving Unit and other emergency services. After an extensive three-day search, the body of the traditional healer was finally retrieved from the river. Emergency medical services pronounced him dead at the scene.

nnnn

In response to the incident, Acting Provincial Police Commissioner of Mpumalanga, Major General Zeph Mkhwanazi, expressed his condolences and urged community members to exercise caution when conducting spiritual or religious activities near bodies of water.

nnnn

“As we approach the Easter weekend, we appeal to the public to be extremely cautious when holding baptism ceremonies or rituals at rivers and dams. These areas are dangerous, and we often see a rise in drowning incidents during this time,” Mkhwanazi said.

High Court Rescues R500 Million University of Mpumalanga Project After Site Chaos and Legal Missteps
R500 Million Legal Battle Erupts Over University of Mpumalanga Construction Site
post_content:
n

The University of Mpumalanga has found itself at the centre of a high-stakes legal dispute involving two construction giants, local community leaders, and senior police officials. The matter stems from a R500 million development project currently underway at the university’s Mbombela campus.

nnnn

NPE Construction (Pty) Ltd and Trencon Construction (Pty) Ltd, the companies managing the massive construction project, approached the courts in 2023 seeking protection from individuals who allegedly stormed the site, issued threats, and caused damage. According to court papers, the situation escalated to the point where an attorney was reportedly attacked, and a vehicle vandalised, leaving workers fearing for their safety.

nnnn

Initially, the two firms turned to the Mbombela Magistrate’s Court, requesting an urgent interdict to bar the group from accessing the site. However, the court dismissed their application, claiming it lacked jurisdiction due to the project's R500 million value—far exceeding the court's R400,000 threshold.

nnnn

This week, Acting Judge Kgama Shai and Mpumalanga Deputy Judge President Takalani Ratshibvumo of the Mpumalanga High Court overturned that ruling. They slammed the magistrate’s court for misinterpreting the issue of jurisdiction.

nnnn

“The lower court wrongly assumed that jurisdiction was determined by the value of the project,” said Judge Shai. “In fact, jurisdiction in interdicts should be based on the cost to stop unlawful conduct, not the overall value of a business or project.”

nnnn

The judges further criticised the magistrate for raising the jurisdiction issue mero motu (of their own accord), noting that while courts are permitted to do so, the facts of this case did not justify such action. “This was a misdirection,” they ruled.

nnnn

The University of Mpumalanga, as the site owner, was named as the fourteenth respondent in the matter. Also cited were the Nelspruit police station commander and the Mpumalanga police commissioner, accused of failing to intervene during the tense 2023 standoff.

nnnn

Importantly, the High Court found that the omission of the project’s R500 million value in the founding affidavit was not sufficient grounds to dismiss the case.

nnnn

The ruling is expected to pave the way for further legal proceedings and may reignite tensions between the construction firms, local stakeholders, and law enforcement.

post_title: Man rides a bicycle in the city on a bicycle path

post_content:
n

The Department of Transport has announced a new initiative aimed at enhancing road safety and promoting uniform traffic regulation across all modes of transport. Beginning 1 July 2025, all bicycles used on public roads, cycle lanes, and shared pathways will be required to be licensed.

nnnn

This policy aligns with the national road traffic management strategy and is designed to:

nnnn

Improve safety for both cyclists and motorists,

nnnn

Standardise regulation of all vehicles on public roads,

nnnn

Support the development of dedicated cycling infrastructure across the country.

nnnn

Key Details of the Bicycle Licensing System:

nnnn

License Requirement: All bicycles operated in public spaces must be licensed.

nnnn

License Fee: R1,214 for a five-year cycle.

nnnn

Registration: Each licensed bicycle will receive a unique registration number and a mandatory reflective license disc, which must be clearly affixed to the bicycle frame.

nnnn

Application Process: Licensing applications open on 1 May 2025 and can be submitted via the eNTIS online portal or at the nearest licensing department.

nnnn

Competency Test: Cyclists will need to complete a basic road safety competency test to ensure awareness of traffic regulations.

nnnn

Failure to comply with the licensing requirements may result in fines or the impoundment of unlicensed bicycles.

nnnn

The department urges all cyclists to prepare ahead of time to avoid disruptions and to contribute to safer, more organised road usage.

nnnn
