post_title: Hijacking, Kidnapping Suspects Caught Near Balfour
post_content:
n

Two suspects, aged 23 and 37, were arrested in Balfour on the evening of 9 April 2025 around 22:30, for their alleged involvement in a hijacking, kidnapping, and possession of an unlicensed firearm with ammunition.

nnnn

According to information received, police in Balfour were alerted about a hijacked white Ford single cab bakkie, which had reportedly been taken at gunpoint in Morgenzon. It was further reported that the driver of the vehicle had also been kidnapped during the incident by the armed suspects.

nnnnnnnn

The South African Police Service (SAPS) in Balfour responded swiftly and immediately set up a roadblock, closing off all exit points. The operation was supported by private security company POLSEC (Aubrey Securities).

nnnn

Officers spotted the hijacked vehicle, matching the description provided, travelling on the R23 Road. The suspects attempted to evade capture by veering off towards the old Greylingstad Road in the direction of Balfour.

nnnn

Attempts to stop the vehicle failed, leading to a high-speed chase. Realising they were being cornered, the suspects abandoned the bakkie and fled on foot into nearby maize fields under the cover of darkness.

nnnn

Transnet’s drone technology was deployed to aid the search. A detailed sweep of the surrounding area was conducted, leading to the suspects being spotted later walking along a road near the field.

nnnn

The suspects were searched, and a firearm with ammunition was discovered in their possession. They were subsequently arrested and taken into custody.

nnnn

Police later found the victim tied up with rope along the roadside. Fortunately, the victim was unharmed and safely reunited with their family.

nnnn

The two suspects, identified as Baveli Robert Maseko (37) and Orbin Mith Mohammed (23), appeared in the Balfour Magistrate’s Court on 14 April 2025. They were formally charged with possession of an unlicensed firearm with ammunition, hijacking, and kidnapping.

nnnnnnnn

The court remanded them in custody until their next appearance, scheduled for 17 April 2025.

nnnn

Police have praised the teamwork between SAPS Balfour, POLSEC, and Transnet, which led to the successful apprehension of the suspects and the safe recovery of the victim.

nnnn

Investigations are ongoing, and more arrests have not been ruled out as police follow further leads

post_title: Fifteen suspects arrested during Operation Vala Umgodi in Pilgrim’s Rest for contravening the Immigration Act and possession of gold-bearing material.

post_title: NSFAS payment blunder leaves TVET students facing eviction, as unverified accommodation allowances cause confusion and unpaid rent
NSFAS Allowance Missteps Cause Student Evictions
post_content:
n

The failure by the National Student Financial Aid Scheme (NSFAS) to pay TVET college landlords directly has resulted in confusion, evictions, and frustration after some students received R13,800 in allowances — including for accommodation — despite not being eligible, while others failed to pay their landlords.

nnnn

On 4 April 2025, NSFAS disbursed the amount to students, of which R10,800 was specifically intended for accommodation. According to NSFAS spokesperson Ishmael Mnisi, this led to a “misunderstanding” between NSFAS, institutions, and students, resulting in the payment of funds to individuals who had not been verified as eligible for accommodation support.

nnnn

NSFAS had requested updated lists of students applying for NSFAS-accredited housing from its “solution partners” — intermediaries responsible for coordinating with institutions. These lists were supposed to verify students’ eligibility for accommodation and transport assistance.

nnnn

However, Mnisi said confusion arose when NSFAS paid allowances to students who were not on the verified lists, or whose eligibility was not confirmed in time by institutions. This led to the disbursement of funds to students who may not have qualified for accommodation support.

nnnn

When asked why NSFAS does not pay landlords directly, Mnisi explained that many TVET colleges lack the infrastructure and systems required to manage payments effectively. He added that paying students directly ensures timely delivery of funds and reduces administrative burdens on colleges while they work to improve their internal processes.

nnnn

Despite this, the consequences have been severe. Students at Waterberg TVET College in Lebowakgomo were evicted after failing to pay landlords. College spokesperson Mahlako Phasha confirmed that while some students submitted proof of payment, others refused to pay, leading to their eviction.

nnnn

Accommodation allowances for TVET students are capped at R33,000 annually for approved residences. For private accommodation, the cap is R52,000 per year in metro areas and R42,640 in non-metro areas.

nnnn

NSFAS is now urging students who received the R10,800 meant for accommodation to urgently pay their landlords and avoid further evictions. Mnisi stated that students had been made aware of their monthly allowance structures and were expected to use the funds accordingly.

post_title: An Apple a Day A Sweet Way to Stay Healthy

nnnn

nnnn

Apples have a type of fiber called soluble fiber. This fiber can help lower bad cholesterol levels and keep your heart healthy. Apples also contain antioxidants, which protect your heart from damage.

nnnn

nnnn

The fiber in apples also helps with digestion. It keeps your stomach and intestines working well and can prevent constipation. Eating apples regularly can help keep your tummy happy.

nnnn

3. Boost Your Immune System

nnnn

Apples have vitamin C, which helps your body fight off colds and infections. If you want to stay healthy, eating apples can be a great help.

nnnn

4. Give You Energy

nnnn

Apples have natural sugar that gives your body energy. They are a great snack during the day, especially if you need a little boost without drinking energy drinks or soda.

nnnn

5. Good for Your Brain

nnnn

Some studies say that apples can help improve memory and protect your brain as you get older. The antioxidants in apples help reduce stress in your body and brain.

nnnn

6. May Help You Lose Weight

nnnn

Because apples are full of fiber and water, they make you feel full longer. This means you might eat less and still feel satisfied, which can help you lose weight.

post_title: Why Watermelon Is a Summer Superfruit

Watermelon also contains citrulline, an amino acid that may help improve blood flow and reduce muscle soreness. This makes it a great post-workout snack for athletes or anyone trying to stay active.

nnnn

For pregnant women, watermelon can help ease heartburn and reduce swelling due to its water content and natural nutrients. Its fiber also supports digestion and helps keep your system regular.

nnnn

From hydration to heart health, watermelon offers a range of benefits in every juicy bite. So the next time you’re at the fruit stand or planning a picnic, make sure to add watermelon to your basket — your body will thank you.

post_title: Mourners gather in solemn reflection during a traditional South African funeral, honouring the departed with dignity, unity, and cultural respect
Funerals No Longer Reflect Our Values
post_content:
n

A funeral service is meant to be an emotionally intimate occasion—our final farewell to someone we loved and still hold dear. Traditionally, it was about honour, remembrance, and community support. Today, however, funerals have taken a turn that raises serious questions about how we grieve and honour our loved ones.

nnnn

There’s growing pressure on bereaved families to organise the “perfect” funeral, often driven by societal expectations and not necessarily the family’s wishes. One wonders—who set these new “norms”? What do traditional and tribal authorities say about modern additions such as After Tears parties, often framed as celebrations of the deceased’s life?

nnnn

In South African culture, funerals were deeply rooted in heritage, offering time to honour both the departed and their ancestors. Now, they're often marked by conflict—disputes over burial versus cremation, lavish versus modest services, and who said what the deceased supposedly wanted. Ironically, those who stir up the most trouble during planning often contribute the least.

nnnn

While it's natural for traditions to evolve, some developments are troubling. Many funerals today are noisy and chaotic affairs. Some attendees arrive drunk, cause disruptions, ignore proceedings, and rush through the service just to resume partying. Loud music, dancing, and alcohol have taken centre stage—often at funerals for elders who never embraced such lifestyles. If there’s no After Tears, the funeral is deemed dull.

nnnn

Even food becomes a subject of judgement. People complain about what's served—the meat, the veg, the salad. The mourning family, already carrying a heavy emotional burden, is unfairly scrutinised.

nnnn

This shift distracts from what funerals should be about: unity, compassion, and respect. Community members and neighbours once rallied to provide emotional and practical support. Today, that tradition is fading.

nnnn

Yes, the Fourth and Fifth Industrial Revolutions are reshaping our lives. But should they erode our cultural identity? Should they dilute the respect and dignity we once upheld in saying goodbye?

nnnn

It’s not too late to go back to basics. We must re-centre funerals as sacred moments of remembrance, not just events for spectacle.

nnnn

Bheki Nyathikazi is a Communication Practitioner. He writes in his personal capacity.

post_title: SACP Electoral Move Threatens ANC Stability
post_content:
n

By Thulani Castro Waka Mhlanga

nnnn

The South African Communist Party’s (SACP) decision to contest the 2026 local government elections marks a significant political development and a potential threat to the dominance of the African National Congress (ANC). Historically, the SACP and ANC, alongside the Congress of South African Trade Unions (COSATU), have operated as a united front through the Tripartite Alliance, rooted in their collective fight against apartheid and formally established in 1990 after the unbanning of the ANC.
Traditionally, the SACP and COSATU have not contested elections but have played influential roles in shaping ANC policy and mobilising voter support. However, the SACP’s registration with the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) to contest independently in November 2026 signals a break from tradition and poses serious political ramifications.
This move is not unprecedented. In 2017, the SACP fielded its own candidate in the Metsimaholo local municipality by-elections in the Free State, challenging the ANC directly. Now, the decision to contest again reflects growing dissatisfaction within the alliance and could lead to deep divisions, particularly at local government level, where many members of the SACP and COSATU are also ANC members.
SACP General Secretary Solly Mapaila has publicly criticised aspects of the Government of National Unity (GNU), further highlighting tensions. As local elections are largely issue-based, the fragmentation of alliance support may open opportunities for other organisations, including civil society groups such as SANCO, to win proportional representation seats or wards.
The ANC faces a dilemma. Without urgent dialogue, the alliance risks collapse at grassroots level, potentially handing power to smaller parties through coalition governments. Previous experience with coalition-led municipalities has often resulted in governance instability and poor service delivery.
Local dynamics differ significantly across municipalities. For example, residents in Mbombela’s Ward One may not face the same service issues as those in Bushbuckridge. This makes the local elections a more volatile battleground.
To avoid a splintered vote and weakened governance, the ANC and SACP must consider holding a national consultative conference. Without it, the 2026 local government elections may usher in a new era of fragmentation and further decline in service delivery across South Africa.

post_title: Public Protector Exposes Rigged Hiring Bushbuckridge Officials Face Disciplinary Action Over Unqualified Appointments
Six Officials Face Action for Unfair Hiring
post_content:
n

Six senior officials at the Bushbuckridge Municipality in Mpumalanga are facing disciplinary action after a report by Public Protector Kholeka Gcaleka revealed a corrupt hiring process.
According to the report, two people — Pawngeorge Zwane and Tshwarelo Kgwedi — were given administrative clerk jobs even though they didn’t meet the minimum requirements.
Zwane was hired as an Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) administration clerk, but he had no experience or qualification in that field. Kgwedi was hired as a Human Resources (HR) administration clerk even though she didn’t have a matric certificate, which was a required qualification.
The Democratic Municipal and Allied Workers Union of South Africa (Demawusa) had warned the former municipal manager, Cynthia Nkuna, about rumours that the hiring process had been rigged. They even gave her a note on the day of the interviews, but the appointments went ahead anyway.
Zwane later admitted that he didn’t have experience in OHS. Kgwedi submitted an N3 certificate, but the Public Protector found that it was not the same as a matric, as required by the job post.
The Public Protector said that the interview scoring patterns suggested the panel may have worked together to favour certain candidates. She concluded that the panel’s actions showed unfairness, poor ethics, and a lack of transparency.
Nkuna said she received the warning note but claimed she didn’t look at it. However, she also did nothing to stop the process.
The Public Protector ordered Executive Mayor Lydia Moroane to present the report to the council and take legal steps to undo the unfair appointments.
Municipal Manager Jasper Ngobeni was told to discipline the six officials and ensure HR staff receive proper training on ethical hiring.
Municipal spokesperson Fhumulani Thovakale confirmed the matter is being taken seriously. She said the disciplinary board would review the report and advise on next steps, including whether to go to court or follow all of the Public Protector’s recommendations.

post_title: Mpumalanga man arrested for sleeping with exhumed bones, while search ends in tragedy as three missing police officers found dead in Hennops River.
Man With Bones, Officers Found Dead

A 29-year-old man from Masoyi, Mpumalanga, was arrested after police found him asleep next to human bones that he had allegedly dug up from two graves.
According to police spokesperson Brigadier Donald Mdhluli, the graves were located in the Swalala cemetery, and the bones are believed to belong to the suspect’s father and grandfather, who died and were buried in 2010.
Police were alerted on April 28, 2025, after someone reported that graves had been disturbed in the area. Officers responded quickly and confirmed that the graves had indeed been tampered with.
The suspect was tracked down to his home in the RDP section of Swalala. When police entered, they found him sleeping with the exhumed bones lying beside him on the bed.
He was immediately arrested and charged with violating graves. The bones have since been taken by police as part of a larger investigation. Authorities are working to understand the motive behind this disturbing incident.
The man is scheduled to appear in the Masoyi Magistrate’s Court on April 30, 2025.
Separate Tragedy: Police Officers Found Dead In a separate incident, three police officers who had been missing since April 24 were among five bodies discovered in the Hennops River.
National Police Commissioner General Fannie Masemola confirmed the news during a media briefing near the river. The deceased officers — Constable Keamogetswe Buys, Constable Boipelo Senoge, and Constable Cebekhulu Linda — were identified by their families at the Tshwane mortuary.
“It has been a painful six days for the SAPS and the families as we searched for our missing officers,” Masemola said.
The trio was last seen at a petrol station near the Grasmere Toll Plaza in the early hours of April 24. After that, their cellphones, car tracking system, and vehicle — a Volkswagen Polo — went offline.
A high-level investigation team searched throughout Gauteng, the Free State, and Limpopo. Their work led them to the Hennops River area, where the bodies were recovered near John Vorster Drive in Centurion.
The investigation into both incidents continues.

They are a smart carbohydrate choice for people with diabetes or those looking to maintain steady energy levels throughout the day.

Misrepresentation of procurement processes and outcomes to the Premier and MEC.

A service provider who falsely claimed full contract compliance.

Disciplinary action against all implicated officials.

Blacklisting of the supplier.

Recovery of financial losses through legal means.

Lifestyle audits for involved individuals.

A broader governance review of the education department.

post_title: Two police officers face multiple charges for extortion and corruption after allegedly targeting a truck driver with a fake dagga bust.
Two police officers face multiple charges for extortion and corruption after allegedly targeting a truck driver with a fake dagga bust.2
Cops Arrested for Dagga Extortion Scheme
post_content:
n

The Hawks’ Secunda-based Serious Corruption Investigation unit has successfully secured the court appearance of two police officers implicated in a string of serious crimes committed within a span of two days.
Sergeant Ntsizwa Mthimunye (47) and Constable Malefane Mofokeng (38) allegedly abused their authority while on duty. On 9 October 2023, at approximately 04:20, the officers stopped and searched a truck on the N17 road near Leslie (Leandra), where they reportedly discovered four bags of dagga.
Investigations reveal that the officers assaulted the truck driver and demanded a R5,000 bribe for his release. When the driver's banking app delayed opening, they instructed him to contact his employer to obtain the funds. The employer deposited the money, and the driver managed to withdraw R4,050, which was handed over to the officers. The dagga was seized but not booked officially.
The following day, 10 October, the driver returned to the police station hoping to retrieve R1,000 to cover his personal expenses. Upon arrival, he encountered the same officers, who allegedly assaulted, handcuffed, and abducted him. He was taken to a secluded area along the N17, guarded by one officer while the other drove off in a police vehicle. When the vehicle returned, it contained two of the four previously seized dagga bags.
The officers then arrested the driver for possession of dagga.
Following this, the Leslie police were alerted to the incident, and the Hawks were brought in. A formal case was opened, and an intensive investigation followed. A warrant was served on both officers on 16 April 2025, and they made their first court appearance on 12 May 2025 before the Evander Magistrate’s Court.
The duo face multiple charges, including corruption, assault, theft, kidnapping, extortion, and defeating the ends of justice. The case has been postponed to 27 July 2025. The accused were warned to appear in person at their next hearing.
Major General Nico Gerber, the Provincial Head of the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation in Mpumalanga, reaffirmed the unit's commitment:
“We will continue to root out corruption both inside and outside our ranks.”

nnnn

The charges stem from a brutal attack on February 5, 2024, when a group of armed men stormed the home of her estranged husband, Mashego, in Boikhotso near Bushbuckridge. nnnn

The attackers then looted the home, stealing R4,000 in cash and Mashego’s bank card.

nnnn

Four suspects were later arrested. One of them, Witness Monareng (28), pleaded guilty after his fingerprints were found at the scene. He received a 77-year prison sentence for premeditated murder, armed robbery, theft, and kidnapping. The trial against the remaining accused—Themba Mokoena, Thabang Malumane, and Thabiso Malope—is still ongoing.

nnnn

Nyathi turned herself in on March 10 after evading arrest. Police officers had tried to apprehend her on March 7, but a premature broadcast on the SABC’s Morning Live show reportedly alerted her, prompting her to go into hiding.

nnnn

She has remained in custody since her surrender. During the bail proceedings, Nyathi’s lawyer, Advocate Vusi Segodi, filed an application for Magistrate Tanya du Preez to recuse herself, citing a potential conflict of interest. Du Preez is married to Nyathi’s former commander, and Segodi argued this relationship could affect the fairness of the trial.

post_content:
n

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of the South African Police Service in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, has welcomed the 14-year prison sentence handed down to Philip Mfana Masuku (62) for rhino poaching in the Kruger National Park.

nnnn

Masuku was sentenced by the Skukuza Regional Court on 05 June 2025 after being convicted on multiple charges, including trespassing in a national park, illegal hunting of two white rhinos, conspiracy to commit a crime, and possession of dangerous weapons. He was also declared unfit to possess a firearm.

nnnn

The court heard that on 17 February 2019, at approximately the Kruger National Park's Technical Manager detected movement in the Pretoriuskop section, suspected to be poachers. Field Rangers were immediately dispatched after being notified by the Section Ranger.

nnnn

During the operation, Rangers picked up three fresh sets of footprints and began tracking the suspects. Hours later, three men were spotted sitting along Voortrekker Road. As Rangers approached, two suspects escaped, while the third later identified as Masuku was apprehended.

nnnn

Masuku was found in possession of four rhino horns, two knives, and other suspicious items. The incident was reported to the Skukuza Police Station, and Masuku was formally charged.

nnnn

Masuku initially appeared at the Bushbuckridge District Court, where he was granted bail. However, after his case was transferred to Skukuza Regional Court, he absconded from attending proceedings, resulting in a warrant of arrest.

nnnn

A trace operation led to his rearrest. During this time, he attempted to secure bail again, but his application was denied after it was discovered that he submitted a fraudulent medical certificate, confirmed through police investigation.

nnnn

Commissioner Applauds Justice System

nnnn

Major General Mkhwanazi praised the Field Rangers, investigating officers, prosecutors, and the judiciary for their coordinated effort in ensuring justice.

nnnn

“This sentence sends a strong message that poaching will not be tolerated. We remain committed to protecting our wildlife heritage,” he said.

However, he was struck by gunfire, causing his vehicle to veer out of control, collide with a tree and wall, and come to a stop.

nnnn

The assailants fled the scene without taking anything. The vehicle was later found with bullet holes on the rear and right side.

nnnn

Constable Mathebula was a member of the Pienaar SAPS Visible Policing Unit and had served the South African Police Service for ten years. The motive behind the killing remains unclear, and investigations are ongoing.

nnnn

In response, the Acting Provincial Commissioner of the SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, has mobilised the 72-hour Activation Plan, ensuring that all critical resources are directed toward tracking and arresting the suspects.

nnnn

“Anyone who attacks a police officer is directly attacking the state and will face the full might of the law,” said Major General Mkhwanazi. “This brutal murder comes just a week after another officer was killed. This violence against law enforcement cannot continue unchecked.”

nnnn

Police are urging members of the public who may have any information to come forward. Tip-offs can be made anonymously via the Crime Stop number 08600 10111 or through the MySAPS App. All information will be treated with the strictest confidentiality.

post_title: Strawberry Moon to Dazzle South Africa
post_content:
n

South Africa – June 10, 2025 – Stargazers are in for a once-in-a-generation celestial treat this week as the full Strawberry Moon will appear at its lowest point in the sky in 19 years.

nnnn

While the official full moon occurs at 09:43 on June 11, South Africans are advised to look up shortly after sunset on June 10 for the best view of this rare lunar spectacle. According to Project Nightfall, this remarkable alignment won’t happen again until 2043.

nnnn

Why It's Special

nnnn

Known as the Strawberry Moon, June’s full moon gets its name from the Algonquian tribes of North America, who marked this time of year with the short strawberry harvest season. Despite the fruity name, the moon won’t turn red—but due to its low position in the sky, it may take on a golden or orange hue, thanks to atmospheric light scattering.

nnnn

The moon’s unusually low arc across the sky means it will appear larger and more dramatic near the south-eastern horizon, creating a visual spectacle not to be missed.

nnnn

When and Where to Look

nnnn

Date: Evening of June 10, 2025

nnnn

Time: Shortly after sunset, as the moon rises

nnnn

Peak Full Moon: 09:43 on June 11 (not visible, as it’s during daylight)

nnnn

Make sure to check your local moonrise time, grab a comfortable viewing spot, and enjoy this rare astronomical event.

nnnn

nnnn

Source: Mpumalanga News

post_title: Strong Winds Damage Homes, Schools in Casteel

Casteel Residents of the Maboke/Casteel circuit, located outside Acornhoek under the Bohlabela District, are reeling from the devastating effects of a powerful windstorm that tore through the area on the night of 09 June 2025.

The storm left a trail of destruction in its wake, damaging several houses and schools under the Bushbuckridge Local Municipality.

nnnnnnnn

According to affected residents, the storm was one of the worst weather events they have experienced. "It was terrifying. The wind sounded like a train rushing past. Roofs were flying, and we didn’t know if we would make it through the night," said one community member.

nnnn

Ben W Mashego Secondary School

nnnn

Ben Matlushe High School

nnnn

Lekanang Primary School

nnnn

M.O. Mashego Primary School

nnnn

In addition to structural damage to both homes and educational facilities, some areas also experienced electricity outages, adding to the residents’ challenges.

nnnn

Authorities have yet to confirm the full extent of the damage or whether any injuries were reported. However, school administrations and local government officials are expected to assess the situation and coordinate responses for immediate repairs and support to displaced families.

nnnnnnnn

Community leaders have called on the Mpumalanga Department of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs (COGTA) and Department of Education to intervene and provide relief, particularly to affected learners who may now face interruptions in their schooling.

post_title: Woman Due in Court for Murder
post_content:
n

A 54-year-old female suspect is set to appear before the Acornhoek Magistrate’s Court on 17 June 2025, following her arrest in connection with the murder of her 63-year-old male partner at Boelang Trust, Acornhoek.

nnnn

According to reports, police were alerted to the discovery of a deceased male in a room at the specified location on 13 June 2025. Upon arrival at the scene, officers found the lifeless body of the man lying on the ground, with visible bruises on his neck, indicating signs of strangulation.

nnnn

Preliminary investigations suggest that the deceased and the suspect, who had been in a long-term relationship, had a heated argument on the night of 12 June 2025. The altercation allegedly escalated to the point where the suspect is believed to have strangled the victim.

nnnn

Detectives working on the case managed to trace the suspect to Makhushane Village in the Phalaborwa area of Limpopo Province, where she was arrested on 14 June 2025. The arrest was carried out by detectives who were on standby and responded swiftly once credible information on the suspect’s whereabouts was received.

nnnn

The woman is facing charges of murder and has been remanded in custody pending her court appearance. Police investigations are ongoing to gather further evidence and establish the full circumstances surrounding the incident. Authorities are also working to determine whether there was a history of domestic violence between the couple.

nnnn

Court Update:
The suspect, Nicholas Thwala (35), was granted R2,000 bail during her court appearance. The matter has been postponed to 17 July 2025 for further proceedings.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of the SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, has expressed his concern over the incident and extended his condolences to the victim’s family. He also called on communities to pursue peaceful and lawful means to resolve domestic and relationship-related conflicts.

nnnn

“As a nation, we look up to our elders for guidance and wisdom. It is deeply disheartening when disputes between individuals result in the loss of life,” said Major General Mkhwanazi. “We urge all citizens to seek help from appropriate channels—such as social workers, family support centres, and community forums—before resorting to violence.”

nnnn

Anyone with further information that could assist the ongoing investigation is encouraged to contact the SAPS Crime Stop number on 08600 10111, or provide anonymous tips through the MYSAPS App.

post_title: Suspect Jonathan Ilungwa Kulimba arrested during a compliance inspection at a local surgery in Embalenhle.
Bogus Doctor Arrested in Embalenhle Surgery
post_content:
n

A 38-year-old male suspect from the Democratic Republic of Congo has been arrested in Embalenhle for impersonating a medical doctor, in contravention of the Health Professions Act, 56 of 1974. The arrest took place on 12 June 2025 during a compliance inspection at a local medical practice.

nnnn

At approximately 14:00, a Health Inspector conducted an unannounced visit to a surgery operating under the name of a registered medical practitioner at Extension 07 in Embalenhle. Upon arrival, the inspector observed a patient exiting the consultation room. On entering the room, the inspector found an adult male, later identified as Jonathan Ilungwa Kulimba, attending to patients.

nnnn

When questioned, the man presented five patient files, one of which belonged to the patient who had just been seen. During the engagement, the suspect admitted to working under the supervision of the registered practice owner but also confessed that he is not registered with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA).

nnnn

He was immediately arrested and detained at Embalenhle SAPS for practising as a healthcare professional without the necessary qualifications or registration. One of the patient files was seized as evidence to support the ongoing investigation.

nnnn

Further enquiries are being conducted to determine the extent and duration of the illegal medical practice. Authorities are also probing the nature of the relationship between the suspect and the registered doctor, who allegedly allowed him to operate at the facility. Additionally, officials are verifying the authenticity of the suspect’s asylum documentation, which is currently under scrutiny.

nnnn

The suspect appeared before the Evander Magistrate’s Court on 17 June 2025 and was released on free bail. He is scheduled to reappear on 17 July 2025, where additional charges may be brought against him depending on the outcome of the investigation.

nnnn

The Provincial Commissioner of SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, has commended the swift action of the Health Inspector and law enforcement officers.

nnnn

“We urge members of the public to always verify the credentials of medical professionals before seeking consultation. Unqualified individuals operating illegally place lives at risk. SAPS remains committed to protecting communities from such unlawful and dangerous practices,” said Major General Mkhwanazi.

nnnn

The case remains under investigation as police work to determine whether further regulations have been violated and if other individuals were complicit in enabling the suspect’s activities.

post_title: South Africa Seeks Partnership with G7
post_content:
n

South Africa regards the Group of Seven (G7) as a strategic partner in its pursuit of climate resilience, a just energy transition, and value-added investment in its abundant mineral resources.

nnnn

This was stated by President Cyril Ramaphosa following his working visit to Canada, where he participated in the G7 Summit Outreach Session. The session took place on the sidelines of the G7 Leaders’ Summit, held in Kananaskis, Alberta.

nnnn

“South Africa views the G7 as a strategic partner. We seek greater cooperation in areas such as investment, financing for development, international crime, climate change and just transitions, as well as inclusive global growth and development,” the President said on 17 June.

nnnn

The G7 comprises the world’s largest advanced economies: Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States. The European Union also participates in G7 Summits, although it is not a member.

nnnn

The Outreach Session aimed “to explore leadership and collaboration in driving a comprehensive approach to energy security with a focus on technology and innovation; diversification and strengthening critical mineral supply chains; and infrastructure and investment.”

nnnn

This theme aligned closely with South Africa’s national priorities as the current Chair of the G20.

nnnn

Outreach Sessions have long been a feature of the G7, aiming to strengthen unity among member states and like-minded countries in addressing some of the world’s most urgent challenges.

nnnn

President Ramaphosa described the summit as “most meaningful,” particularly given South Africa’s role as G20 Chair.

nnnn

“We’ve just concluded our visit to Canada to attend the G7 Summit. It has been most meaningful for us, particularly as we are the President of the G20. We’ve had the opportunity to engage with a number of heads of state and government,” he said.

nnnn

Climate Change

nnnn

The President placed climate change and its devastating impacts at the heart of South Africa’s message to G7 leaders. He highlighted the destruction caused by floods in KwaZulu-Natal and the Eastern Cape, as well as ongoing droughts in parts of the Western Cape.

nnnn

“We put that firmly on the global agenda — that there should be sufficient funding for incidents such as these, which recur frequently, especially in our sub-region, the Southern African Development Community (SADC), and more specifically in KwaZulu-Natal and the Eastern Cape, which have suffered repeated flood damage, along with drought in the Western Cape,” he explained.

nnnn

Beneficiation

nnnn

On the economic front, President Ramaphosa advocated for a global shift in how Africa’s critical minerals are managed, emphasising beneficiation and inclusive value chains.

nnnn

“We discussed the importance of treating our critical minerals not merely as extractive commodities but ensuring value addition through beneficiation. Minerals play a vital role in energy security, and South Africa aims to move beyond exporting raw materials towards producing finished goods,” he said.

nnnn

Investors are being advised upfront that South Africa expects value chain development alongside extraction.

nnnn

“Those who invest in our minerals should know that we seek not only extraction but also beneficiation, so that ultimately we sell value-added products to the world,” the President stressed.

nnnn

Bilateral Engagements

nnnn

President Ramaphosa held bilateral meetings with leaders from Canada, France, Germany and the Republic of Korea during the summit, which he described as “most beneficial” for advancing South Africa’s diplomatic and economic interests.

nnnn

He welcomed the strengthening cooperation with Canada, particularly in relation to the G20 and G7.

nnnn

“Canada’s Africa strategy is comprehensive, and there is strong potential for cooperation aligned with the African Agenda.”

nnnn

Several engagements have taken place between South Africa and Canada at Sherpa and Ministerial levels. – SAnews.gov.za

post_title: South Africa Strengthens Marine Pollution Legislation
post_content:
n

South Africa is ramping up efforts to combat climate change and ocean pollution with the recent signing of the Marine Pollution (Prevention of Pollution from Ships) Amendment Bill into law by President Cyril Ramaphosa.

nnnn

The bill aligns the country’s laws with the International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships (MARPOL), addressing both sewage and air pollution from ships. It incorporates Annex IV, which governs sewage management, and Annex VI, which targets greenhouse gas emissions and energy efficiency.

nnnn

Janine Osborne, Chief Executive Officer of the Sustainable Seas Trust (SST), welcomed the development: “The amendment strengthens South Africa’s marine environmental protection and aligns it with international standards. It’s a timely response to growing marine pollution challenges.”

nnnn

South Africa boasts a coastline of over 3,000 kilometres and a large Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ). Marine-based industries, including shipping, fisheries and tourism, contribute significantly to the economy and supported approximately 400,000 jobs in 2022.

nnnn

The new legislation increases penalties for environmental offences — raising fines from R500,000 to R10 million and prison sentences from five to ten years. Osborne believes these penalties will act as strong deterrents, but stressed that their success depends on effective enforcement and monitoring.

nnnn

“The government’s commitment is evident, but implementation will be the true test,” she said. “Robust oversight, consistent enforcement, and transparency are essential to ensuring that this legislation produces meaningful change.”

nnnn

Marine pollution remains a serious concern in South Africa, particularly from plastic waste. Osborne noted that recent estimates suggest between 15,000 and 40,000 tonnes of plastic waste enter the country’s oceans annually, a marked reduction from earlier figures but still significant.

nnnn

In response, SST continues to promote public education through programmes like Munch and the African Waste Academy, which support environmental education in schools and provide free training on waste management.

nnnn

Environment Month, commemorated every June, highlights these issues. This year’s theme was echoed in the launch of the National Clean Cities and Towns Campaign in Kliptown by Deputy President Paul Mashatile. The initiative promotes citizen-driven clean-ups and long-term sustainability.

nnnn

Osborne also acknowledged the broader efforts being made by the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment, particularly through Operation Phakisa and the Climate Change Coastal Adaptation Response Plan. These initiatives aim to unlock R177 billion in GDP and create up to one million jobs by 2033.

nnnn

While legislation like the Marine Pollution Amendment Act marks a major stride, Osborne cautions that success will require broad collaboration: “Laws alone won’t solve our problems — we need public participation, responsible behaviour, and cross-sector partnerships to protect our oceans for generations to come.”

post_title: The Minister of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs (CoGTA), Velenkosini Hlabisa

post_content:
n

 The government has reaffirmed its commitment to assisting families affected by storms and strong winds, accelerating recovery efforts and investing in long-term climate adaptation measures.

nnnn

Citizens are urged to remain vigilant, heed official alerts, and promptly report any hazards to local authorities during adverse weather conditions.

nnnn

The Minister of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs (CoGTA), Velenkosini Hlabisa, alongside KwaZulu-Natal Premier Thami Ntuli, conducted an oversight visit to the Impendle Local Municipality on 17 June.

nnnn

They assessed the damage caused by recent extreme weather events, which displaced hundreds of residents.

nnnn

The visit followed a Level 5 weather warning issued by the South African Weather Service (SAWS) last week.

nnnn

Impendle was among the most severely impacted areas in the province, following violent windstorms that damaged homes and community infrastructure.

nnnn

According to the department, a total of 140 households were affected—58 homes were destroyed and 137 others sustained partial damage.

nnnn

Approximately 962 people were directly impacted, with 31 families currently displaced and depending on the support of relatives and neighbours for shelter.

nnnn

The worst-affected communities are spread across five wards. Disaster management teams from local, district, and provincial structures have been deployed to assist.

nnnn

Relief efforts are currently underway, including the provision of temporary shelter—some of which is being provided by community members—along with food parcels and monetary vouchers for affected families.

nnnn

Minister Hlabisa commended the swift coordination between different spheres of government and called for the implementation of long-term resilience measures.

nnnn

“What we are seeing here must push us to improve our response systems and build safer communities. We must not only rebuild but rebuild better,” he said.

nnnn

Premier Ntuli echoed the importance of proactive planning, calling the disaster a “wake-up call”.

nnnn

“Our systems must be more resilient to protect lives and livelihoods,” he added.

nnnn

The department confirmed that leaders engaged directly with community members and disaster response teams on the ground to ensure that immediate needs were addressed and that medium- to long-term recovery plans are well-informed.

nnnn

In addition to addressing the situation in Impendle, government leaders extended condolences to the families of two people who lost their lives in eThekwini due to storm-related incidents.

nnnn

Sympathies were also extended to the families of 12 people who tragically died in a road accident involving a bus and a truck in KwaZulu-Natal during the same period.

nnnn

The department noted that KwaZulu-Natal continues to face increasingly frequent and severe weather patterns, which are attributed to the growing effects of climate change.

nnnn

As part of the response, the National Disaster Management Centre has been tasked with conducting comprehensive vulnerability assessments across the country. These are aimed at informing improved early warning systems, infrastructure resilience planning, and proactive community risk management.

nnnn

On 13 June, President Cyril Ramaphosa visited Mthatha in the Eastern Cape to offer support and assess damage following recent floods that claimed approximately 90 lives.

nnnn

The floods caused widespread destruction to homes, government buildings, roads, hospitals, and schools—highlighting the urgent need to confront climate change.

nnnn

President Ramaphosa remarked that such extreme weather events are becoming a new reality for South Africa, with both the Eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal experiencing recurrent annual disasters.

post_title: Five Suspects Arrested At Middleburg Plaza
post_content:

Five foreign nationals, aged between 19 and 25, were arrested on 06 July 2025 during a multidisciplinary law enforcement operation known as Operation Vala Umgodi, in the Mpumalanga Province.

The suspects were apprehended at the Middleburg Toll Plaza during routine stop-and-searches conducted by the Combat and Proactive team. They were found to be in contravention of the Immigration Act of South Africa after failing to produce valid documentation permitting their stay in the country.

nnnn

The team intercepted a grey Toyota Quantum minibus with Mozambican registration plates, which was transporting a number of passengers. Upon inspection, five individuals were identified as being in the country unlawfully.

nnnnnnnn

The suspects were immediately arrested and charged, and are expected to appear before the Emalahleni Magistrate’s Court in due course.

nnnn

The arrests form part of ongoing efforts by law enforcement authorities to tackle illegal mining, undocumented migration, and associated criminal activities, particularly in hotspot areas like Middleburg and surrounding mining regions.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner of the SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, commended the officers involved in the operation for their vigilance and dedication to maintaining the rule of law.

nnnnnnnn

“We remain committed to protecting the integrity of our borders and ensuring that all persons residing within South Africa do so lawfully. Operations such as Vala Umgodi continue to yield significant results,” said Major General Mkhwanazi.

The SAPS has reiterated its appeal to the public to report any suspicious activity related to undocumented individuals, illegal mining, or organised crime to Crime Stop on 08600 10111 or via the MySAPS App.

post_title: Ramaphosa Calls For BRICS, G20 Synergy
post_content:
n

Rio de Janeiro, Brazil – President Cyril Ramaphosa has emphasised the importance of unified leadership among developing nations, citing the concurrent presidencies of Brazil in BRICS and COP30, and South Africa in the G20, as a unique opportunity to strengthen multilateral cooperation.

nnnn

Delivering his keynote address on 6 July 2025 during the “Environment, COP30 and Global Health” session at the 17th BRICS Summit in Rio de Janeiro, Ramaphosa called for urgent global efforts to address development and climate challenges.

nnnnnnnn

“Our shared leadership of these bodies must highlight the need to close the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) implementation gap, bridge the climate ambition gap, and ensure that no one is left behind in just transition pathways,” he said.

nnnn

He stated that BRICS – Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa – remains key to shaping a fairer model of international cooperation, grounded in equity, sustainability, and inclusive development. He urged that the bloc be leveraged to support climate-resilient growth throughout Africa and the broader Global South.

nnnn

President Ramaphosa called for the reform of multilateral development banks to ensure they better reflect the priorities of developing countries and promote access to concessional finance. This, he said, would catalyse investments in early warning systems, resilient infrastructure, and community-led climate adaptation.

nnnn

The President also addressed the impact of declining global health funding, particularly the withdrawal of official development assistance, which threatens critical programmes for disease elimination and support for vulnerable groups.

nnnn

Acknowledging the role of the Global Fund in combating Tuberculosis, HIV and Malaria, Ramaphosa warned that political neglect and funding cuts jeopardise hard-won progress.

nnnn

As co-host of the Global Fund’s 8th replenishment campaign alongside UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer, he urged countries, businesses, and donors to help raise US$18 billion for the 2027–2029 cycle.

nnnn

“If successful, this will save 23 million lives, reduce the combined mortality rate by 64% compared to 2023, and prevent roughly 400 million infections,” he said.

nnnn

Ramaphosa also highlighted the importance of investing in health systems and universal healthcare access for vulnerable nations in the Global South.

nnnn

“BRICS must champion a new inclusive multilateralism. Let us use our collective voice to shape a just global order that uplifts all people and safeguards our planet,” he concluded.

nnnn

The BRICS Summit, held from 6 to 7 July 2025, also focused on humanitarian crises in Gaza, Sudan, Ukraine, and Iran, while exploring stronger trade, tourism, and investment ties among BRICS members and their partners.

nnnn

– SAnews.gov.za

post_title: Ramaphosa Responds To US Tariff Decision
post_content:
n

Tuesday, 8 July 2025 – President Cyril Ramaphosa has acknowledged receipt of a formal communication from United States President Donald Trump, notifying South Africa of a new unilateral 30% trade tariff to be imposed on goods imported from South Africa.

nnnn

In a letter dated 7 July 2025, President Trump stated that the tariffs would come into effect from 1 August 2025, citing a disputed interpretation of the balance of trade between the two nations.

nnnn

“This 30% tariff is based on a particular interpretation of the balance of trade between South Africa and the United States. This contested interpretation forms part of the issues currently under discussion between the two countries' negotiating teams,” the Presidency said in an official statement.

nnnn

South Africa has rejected the interpretation that underpins the new tariff, asserting that it does not reflect accurate trade data. According to the Presidency, South Africa’s analysis shows that the average tariff on imported goods stands at 7.6%, while 56% of all goods enter South Africa at a 0% most favoured nation (MFN) tariff. Furthermore, 77% of goods imported from the United States are currently subject to 0% duty.

nnnn

“South Africa will continue its diplomatic engagements aimed at achieving a more balanced and mutually beneficial trade relationship with the United States,” the Presidency stated.

nnnn

The statement also welcomed the US government's willingness to revise the 30% tariff, subject to the outcome of ongoing negotiations. Discussions have been underway, with a key meeting held on the side-lines of the US-Africa Summit in Luanda on 23 June 2025.

nnnn

“It was during this meeting that South Africa became aware of a template the US intends to use in its trade engagements with sub-Saharan Africa. Although South Africa has yet to receive this template, President Ramaphosa has instructed the negotiating team to engage urgently, based on the Framework Deal submitted by South Africa on 20 May 2025,” the statement read.

nnnn

The framework addresses US concerns around trade surplus, perceived unfair trade practices, and issues of reciprocity.

nnnn

President Ramaphosa has also encouraged government trade negotiators and South African businesses to fast-track efforts towards market diversification, aimed at strengthening the country's economic resilience and global supply chain integration.

nnnn

He further noted that South Africa is not alone in receiving this tariff notice, which was also sent to several other countries on 7 July 2025.

Why Eating Carrots Is Good For You
post_content:
n

Carrots are more than just a crunchy, colorful addition to your plate—they are a powerhouse of nutrients with a wide range of health benefits. Whether eaten raw, cooked, or juiced, carrots offer numerous reasons to make them a regular part of your diet.

nnnn
    n
  1. Rich in Vitamins and Antioxidants Carrots are an excellent source of vitamin A, primarily in the form of beta-carotene, which is essential for maintaining good vision, especially in low light. Beta-carotene also acts as a powerful antioxidant, helping the body fight off free radicals that can damage cells and contribute to chronic diseases.
    2. nnnn
  2. Supports Eye Health The high levels of vitamin A in carrots play a key role in protecting your eyesight and preventing conditions like night blindness and age-related macular degeneration. This is one of the most well-known benefits of carrots.

post_title: President declares State Funeral for David Mabuza with national mourning observed until July 12.
State Funeral For Former Deputy Mabuza
post_content:
n

President Cyril Ramaphosa has announced that the late former Deputy President David Dabede Mabuza will be honoured with a State Funeral Category 2 on 12 July 2025.

nnnn

Mabuza, who served as South Africa’s Deputy President from 2018 to 2023, passed away on 03 July at the age of 64 following a short illness.

nnnn

In a statement released on 06 July, the Presidency confirmed that the State Funeral Category 2 is in accordance with the State, Official and Provincial Official Funeral Policy Manual, which grants this level of honour to serving or former Deputy Presidents, Acting Presidents, and select high-ranking officials. The funeral will be conducted with military ceremonial honours and will take place in Mpumalanga, with full details to be announced in the coming days.

nnnn

President Ramaphosa has also declared a period of national mourning, to be observed from 07 July until the evening of 12 July 2025. During this time, all national flags will be flown at half-mast at government buildings and official sites across the country.

nnnn

“The President wishes the family strength as they and the nation reflect on the life of a family member, activist, educator, intellectual and leader in government who contributed greatly to the attainment of freedom and development in our society,” the statement read.

nnnn

President Ramaphosa extended his deep condolences to the Mabuza family and urged the nation to remember the legacy of a man who served both his province and his country during a critical time in South Africa’s democracy.

post_title: Eswatini national arrested for child murder and attempted femicide in ongoing GBVF crackdown.
Police Arrest Man For Child’s Murder
post_content:
n

Police detectives have made a significant breakthrough in a Gender-Based Violence and Femicide (GBVF) case involving child murder, attempted murder, and perjury. The suspect, Sanele Fakudze (37), a national from the Kingdom of Eswatini, was arrested in connection with the violent crimes that occurred on 27 June 2025.

nnnn

The victims, a 28-year-old woman and her 4-year-old daughter, were reported missing at the Kanyamazane Police Station after they were last seen entering the suspect’s vehicle. Fakudze is believed to have been the woman’s male friend.

nnnn

On 28 June, the woman was found unconscious next to a road in Kaapmuiden by community members who immediately called for help. She was rushed to hospital for treatment, and police confirmed her identity as the missing woman.

nnnn

Tragically, on 03 July, a partially burned body of the young girl was discovered by a farmer in the same area. Authorities confirmed the girl had been abandoned and murdered, leading to an official charge of murder being added to the case.

nnnn

Following intensive investigation, police located and arrested the suspect on 04 July 2025. He appeared before the Kanyamazane Periodical Court on 07 July, and the case has been postponed to 14 July 2025 for further investigation. Fakudze remains in police custody.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General Dr Zeph Mkhwanazi, commended the investigating officers for their swift action and reaffirmed the SAPS’s firm stance on GBVF.

nnnn

post_title: Ramaphosa Launches Inquiry Into Crime Infiltration
post_content:
n

President Cyril Ramaphosa has announced the formation of a judicial commission of inquiry to investigate allegations that criminal syndicates have infiltrated South Africa's law enforcement, intelligence, and justice institutions.

nnnn

The commission, unveiled during a national address on 13 July, will be chaired by Acting Deputy Chief Justice Mbuyiseli Madlanga. It follows alarming allegations made by KwaZulu-Natal police commissioner, Lieutenant General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi, pointing to deep-rooted corruption within the country’s criminal justice system.

nnnn

Ramaphosa outlined that the commission’s mandate includes probing claims of:

nnnn

Organised crime facilitation,

nnnn

Manipulation or suppression of investigations,

nnnn

Coercion by law enforcement leadership into criminal acts,

nnnn

Intimidation or removal of whistleblowers,

nnnn

And other criminal offenses linked to officials within key justice institutions.

nnnn

The commission will scrutinise current and former senior officials who may have enabled or ignored criminal operations. These include members of the SAPS, National Prosecuting Authority, State Security Agency, judiciary and magistracy, and metro police departments in Johannesburg, Ekurhuleni, and Tshwane.

nnnn

National executive members overseeing the criminal justice system will also fall under the commission’s scope if they are suspected of complicity or negligence.

nnnn

In addition to investigating wrongdoing, the commission will assess the adequacy of current legislation and oversight mechanisms, and will recommend criminal prosecutions, disciplinary action, or structural reform.

nnnn

It will deliver interim reports at three and six months, with a final report to be submitted to the president, the National Assembly speaker, and the chief justice. The commission will also have powers to refer matters for urgent investigation or prosecution.

nnnn

Ramaphosa stressed that this initiative reflects a national commitment to restoring trust, enforcing accountability, and protecting the integrity of South Africa’s justice system.

post_title: Fake Cash Bandit Cons Cops With Comic Sans
post_content:
n

South African police have launched a manhunt for a bold and unusually persuasive suspect who has allegedly bribed at least seven traffic officers using some of the worst counterfeit money ever seen described as so fake, it makes Monopoly money look legit.

nnnn

According to authorities, the suspect described as "charismatic with dangerous levels of confidence" managed to slip the dodgy notes to officers at traffic stops and walk away without raising immediate suspicion.

nnnn

What makes this case even more bizarre is the quality of the fake notes. Experts say the counterfeits appear to be printed on recycled Shoprite flyers, featuring a crudely drawn Nelson Mandela, a watermarked boerewors sausage, and the words “Legal Tenderish” boldly written in Comic Sans.

nnnn

One officer, speaking anonymously, recalled the moment he realised something was off:

nnnn

“He gave me a R200 note. It felt a bit light, but I thought maybe it was the new eco-friendly edition from the Reserve Bank.”

nnnn

Despite the absurdity, police are taking the case seriously. They warn the public not to approach the man, as he may be capable of convincing you that biltong-wrapped tin foil is legal tender.

nnnn

Traffic officers have now been advised to double-check all bribes a policy that raises eyebrows, considering accepting bribes is illegal in the first place. But in the words of one bystander.

post_title: Busisiwe Mkhwebane warns SAPS inquiry could drain resources and undermine accountability.2
Mkhwebane Slams Ramaphosa Over SAPS Inquiry
post_content:
n

Former Public Protector and Umkhonto weSizwe (MK Party) Mpumalanga convenor, Busisiwe Mkhwebane, has strongly criticised President Cyril Ramaphosa’s recent decision to place Police Minister Senzo Mchunu on special leave and establish a commission of inquiry into law enforcement agencies.

nnnn

Speaking to Newzroom Afrika, Mkhwebane accused Ramaphosa of misusing state resources, saying that the funds spent on the commission could be better allocated toward improving the South African Police Service (SAPS), especially in under-resourced provinces like Mpumalanga.

nnnnnnnn

“You put a minister on special leave why not remove the minister, because the president has the powers to do that immediately. Why waste resources?” she said. Mkhwebane also raised concerns about the appointment of Professor Firoz Cachalia, a legal academic and chairperson of the National Anti-Corruption Advisory Council, as acting minister of police.

nnnn

“He’s a director of Corruption Watch, funded by foreign backers like George Soros. I think he is putting the country deep, deep into trouble,” she added.

nnnn

While some welcomed Mchunu’s special leave, the commission itself has drawn sharp criticism. Analysts told IOL that the commission could end up being another costly and inconclusive process, similar to the Zondo Commission on State Capture.

nnnn

Ramaphosa appointed Professor Cachalia as acting police minister until the commission concludes its work. A seasoned legal expert and former anti-apartheid activist, Cachalia is expected to take up the role in August.

nnnn

Mkhwebane warned that the move undermines Chapter 9 institutions and accused the president of holding the country in “suspense” with inquiries that offer recommendations but lack enforcement.

n

Mpumalanga Premier Mandla Ndlovu has officially dismissed Godfrey Ntombela, the Head of Department for Sports, Arts and Culture, following a dispute over a questionable contract extension and allegations of fraud.

Ntombela's employment contract expired in February 2025. According to Premier Ndlovu, the previous administration extended the contract from March to September 2024. post_title: Packed with vitamin C and antioxidants, oranges are a delicious way to support your immune system and overall health.
Why an Orange a Day Is a Smart Choice
post_content:
n

Oranges are one of the world’s most popular fruits and for good reason. Not only are they juicy, refreshing, and naturally sweet, but they also pack a powerful nutritional punch that benefits your body in numerous ways.

nnnn

This vibrant citrus fruit, known for its bright orange skin and tangy flavor, is an excellent source of vitamin C, a key nutrient that supports immune health, skin repair, and collagen production. Just one medium orange can provide more than 100% of your daily vitamin C needs.

nnnnnnnn

Top Health Benefits of Eating Oranges:

nnnn

Thanks to its high vitamin C content, eating oranges helps strengthen the immune system, protecting the body against infections like colds and flu.

nnnn

Oranges are loaded with antioxidants, including flavonoids and carotenoids, which help fight free radicals and reduce inflammation. This may lower your risk of chronic diseases such as heart disease and cancer.

nnnn

Vitamin C also plays a vital role in skin health. It supports the production of collagen, which keeps your skin firm, youthful, and less prone to wrinkles.

nnnn

Oranges contain potassium, a mineral that helps regulate blood pressure, and fiber, which lowers cholesterol levels both crucial for maintaining a healthy heart.

nnnn

The fiber in oranges promotes regular bowel movements and supports a healthy digestive system. One orange contains about 3 grams of dietary fiber.

nnnn

With a high water content and only about 60 calories per fruit, oranges are a satisfying, low-calorie snack that helps keep you hydrated throughout the day.

nnnn

Oranges are incredibly versatile. You can enjoy them fresh, juiced, in smoothies, fruit salads, or even added to savory dishes for a citrusy twist. For a quick energy boost, keep a peeled orange on hand as a natural, nutritious snack.

n

post_title: Cathy Dlamini Bids Farewell After Cabinet Exit
post_content:
n

Mpumalanga’s former Education MEC Cathy Dlamini has spoken publicly for the first time since her removal from Premier Mandla Ndlovu’s cabinet, calling her time in office “a privilege, not a right,” and thanking the people she served.

nnnn

Dlamini’s dismissal was part of a broader cabinet reshuffle announced on 15 July 2025, in which Premier Ndlovu restructured four departments to, in his words, “strengthen governance and improve service delivery.” Among the most notable changes was the removal of Dlamini and Economic Development MEC Makhosazana Masilela.

nnnn

In a heartfelt statement released shortly after the announcement, Dlamini defended her record and expressed pride in her achievements.
“Supported by incredible and dedicated staff, we delivered the province’s record-breaking matric pass rate and improvement across the board,” she said.
“We fought corruption and capture at every corner. We saved the department millions. And we sought innovative solutions to deliver quality education in both rural and urban areas.”

nnnn

She emphasized that her short tenure had laid critical foundations for long-term transformation in the education sector:
“During this short stint, we embarked on a task to transform the biggest department in the province. And I’m happy the building blocks were put in place.”

nnnn

While Ndlovu reiterated that the reshuffle was in the interest of better governance and public trust, Dlamini used her farewell to extend gratitude to a wide range of education stakeholders, including teachers, principals, school governing bodies, unions, parents, and even school security staff, cooks, and cleaners.

nnnn

“To the students of Mpumalanga — I love every single one of you. And I have nothing but faith that you will continue to shine bright and make us proud,” she added warmly.

nnnn

Dlamini also welcomed her successor, Lindi Masina, offering words of encouragement and unity:
“As the ANC, we have many capable members. And I believe the incoming MEC of education will keep the fire burning and take this province to the next level. Welcome her and support her work. Congratulations, sesi.”

nnnn

She concluded by thanking God and all those who supported her through prayer during her time in office:

post_title: Police Honour Mandela Day Through Outreach
post_content:

Members deployed under Operation Vala Umgodi in Mpumalanga marked Mandela Day, observed annually on 18 July, by hosting an awareness campaign dedicated to the well-being of children with disabilities. The event took place on 17 July 2025 at Mystical Mansion Guest House in the Witbank area.

nnnn

As part of the initiative, police members prepared and served food for the children and staff from surrounding disability centres. The gesture was a tribute to the spirit of service embodied by the late former President Nelson Mandela, who championed human dignity and social justice.

The South African Police Service (SAPS) in Masoyi is urgently appealing to members of the public to assist in locating a missing three-year-old boy, Nkosingiphile Ndwane Ntiwane, who disappeared from his home in Mshadza Trust, Masoyi, on Saturday, 20 July 2025 at approximately 13:00.

nnnn

According to the information received, Nkosingiphile was playing in the yard at his residence when his father noticed that he was no longer visible. After a brief search of the immediate area, the father called on neighbours and members of the community for assistance. Despite a coordinated search, the child could not be located.

nnnn

Other emergency response stakeholders were summoned to the scene, and a search operation was initiated. However, at the time of reporting, the child remains missing.

nnnn

At the time of his disappearance, Nkosingiphile was wearing a military-coloured jumpsuit and a peach-coloured jersey. He is deaf and mute, which has intensified concerns for his safety and well-being. His condition may limit his ability to respond to calls or navigate his surroundings, making the need to locate him both urgent and critical.

nnnn

The police are appealing to anyone who may have seen Nkosingiphile or has information that could assist in reuniting him with his family to come forward. Every detail, no matter how small, could make a difference in locating the child and ensuring his safe return.

nnnn

Members of the public with information are urged to contact Captain David Hlatshwayo on 076 451 5495. Alternatively, tip-offs can be shared anonymously via the SAPS Crime Stop line on 08600 10111 or through the MYSAPS mobile application.

nnnn

“All information will be treated with the utmost confidentiality. Callers may remain anonymous,” said police spokesperson Brigadier Selvy Mohlala, appealing to communities around Masoyi and neighbouring areas to assist.

nnnn

The police are urging residents to stay alert, check their premises thoroughly—especially unused buildings, storerooms, and outdoor spaces—and report anything suspicious.

nnnn

As the search continues, the SAPS remains hopeful that with the help of the public, Nkosingiphile will be found and safely reunited with his family.

The South African Police Service (SAPS) in Chrissiesmeer has successfully recovered 14 sheep that were reportedly stolen from a local farm. Police are currently searching for the suspects believed to be behind the theft.

nnnn

According to the farmer who reported the incident, he regularly visits the grazing camp each morning to count his livestock. On the day in question, while conducting his usual headcount, he discovered that 14 sheep were missing. He promptly contacted the police for assistance.

nnnn

Upon arriving at the scene, SAPS officers noticed that the fence had been cut – a likely entry point used by the thieves. A thorough investigation was immediately launched, which led the officers to a location near Warburton, approximately 25 kilometres from the farm.

nnnn

At the site, the police found all 14 sheep tied up. The estimated value of the livestock is R35,000. The animals have since been returned to the rightful owner. However, the suspects are still at large.

nnnn

Police are actively pursuing the perpetrators and have called on members of the public to assist. Anyone with relevant information is urged to contact Detective Captain Aziz Phiri on 082 556 5861. Alternatively, tips may be submitted via the SAPS Crime Stop number at 08600 10111 or through the MYSAPS mobile app. All shared information will be treated with the utmost confidentiality, and callers may remain anonymous.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, commended the swift and coordinated action by the Visible Policing (Vispol) members in Chrissiesmeer. He also praised the collaboration with the local wardens and the Stock Theft and Endangered Species (STES) unit, which led to the successful recovery.

nnnn

“Stock theft continues to be a significant challenge, particularly in rural areas. However, with collaborative efforts and heightened awareness, we can win this battle. We urge our communities not to purchase stolen goods, especially livestock, as doing so fuels the illegal trade,” said Major General Mkhwanazi.

nnnn

The SAPS remains committed to protecting the agricultural sector and ensuring that justice is served. Investigations continue.

post_title: Four Men Arrested in DJ Sumbody Murder
post_content:
n

A major breakthrough has been made in the murder investigation of popular musician Oupa John Sefoka, widely known as DJ Sumbody, who was tragically gunned down in November 2022. The South African Police Service (SAPS) has confirmed the arrest of four men in connection with the crime.

nnnn

The arrests were carried out in Gauteng on, 21 July 2025, and include three alleged hitmen and one individual suspected of orchestrating the murder. The men, aged between 45 and 60, are currently in police custody and are expected to appear in court soon. They are facing multiple charges, including murder and conspiracy to commit murder.

nnnn

The National Commissioner of the SAPS, General Fannie Masemola, praised the investigative teams for their commitment and coordination. The investigation was led by the Gauteng Organised Crime Unit, working closely with the SAPS Political Killings Task Team.

nnnn

“This is a significant breakthrough in a case that shocked the nation,” said General Masemola. “The teams involved have demonstrated exceptional commitment by tirelessly piecing together evidence for more than two years. Their hard work has resulted in these critical arrests and brings us a step closer to justice.”

nnnn

According to a police statement, the firearm allegedly used in the fatal shooting of DJ Sumbody has been recovered and has been positively linked to other murder cases currently under investigation. This discovery has opened further avenues of inquiry into related organised crime activities in the province.

nnnn

The late DJ Sumbody, known for hit songs such as "Monate Mpolaye," was a beloved figure in South Africa's music industry. His untimely death at the age of 38 sent shockwaves through the entertainment community and prompted nationwide calls for accountability and justice.

nnnn

General Masemola expressed hope that this development will offer some closure to Sefoka’s family, fans, and fellow artists. “Our thoughts remain with the family during this difficult time. We will continue to pursue justice relentlessly,” he added.

nnnn

The SAPS also reiterated its commitment to dismantling criminal syndicates involved in targeted killings, particularly those affecting public figures, political leaders, and prominent community members.

nnnn

Members of the public with further information that could assist with the ongoing investigation are encouraged to come forward. Tips can be submitted anonymously through the SAPS Crime Stop number 08600 10111 or via the MYSAPS mobile app.

nnnn

As the suspects prepare to face court, South Africans watch with interest, hopeful that justice will be served for DJ Sumbody and others affected by violent crime.

post_title: Banyana Banyana Praised Despite Semi Loss
post_content:
n

The Department of Sport, Arts and Culture has praised Banyana Banyana for their strong showing at the 2025 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) in Morocco.

nnnn

“Well done Banyana Banyana! Mzansi is very proud of how far you’ve come,” read a post shared by the department on X, following the team’s semi-final clash with Nigeria on 22 July.

nnnn

Despite a spirited performance, South Africa’s senior women’s team was edged out 2–1 by Nigeria in a tightly contested match at the Larbi Zaouli Stadium in Casablanca.

nnnn

According to the South African Football Association (SAFA), the match took a distressing turn in the 83rd minute when midfielder Gabriela Salgado suffered a serious injury. The incident visibly shook the Banyana Banyana squad and coaching staff, disrupting the team’s momentum in the final stages of the game.

nnnn

SAFA President, Dr Danny Jordaan, extended his well wishes to the injured player, while commending the team for their fighting spirit.

nnnn

“First of all, we would like to wish a speedy recovery to Gabriela Salgado,” Jordaan said. “Banyana Banyana fought very well, and it was a brave performance from the WAFCON defending champions. You have established yourselves as one of the best teams on the continent.

nnnn

“We fought bravely, and we are proud of your performance. Well done to the whole team, the team’s Head of Delegation Thabile Msomi, the coach Dr Desiree Ellis, the captain Refiloe Jane and all players. We are proud of your efforts.”

nnnn

Banyana Banyana entered the 2025 tournament as defending champions, having won the previous WAFCON title in 2022. Their journey in this year’s competition has been marked by determination and teamwork, earning them admiration both at home and across the continent.

nnnn

With the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations set to conclude on 26 July 2025, South Africa’s focus now shifts to the third-place play-off, where the team will seek to finish the tournament on a high note.

nnnn

The Department of Sport, Arts and Culture also encouraged the nation to continue supporting the team, saying their performance was an inspiration to young girls and future sports stars in South Africa.

nnnn

As the tournament nears its end, Banyana Banyana’s resilience remains a beacon of hope and pride for the country’s sporting fraternity.
