post_title: Operation Shanela Arrests Suspects With Drugs
post_content:
n

Operation Shanela continues to bear fruit, with several suspects arrested for drug-related offences in Amersfoort and Vosman on 25 July 2025.

nnnn

In Amersfoort, a 37-year-old man was arrested at around 15h30 after intelligence-led coordination between police officers and the Standerton K9 Unit. The suspect, believed to be dealing in drugs, was found in possession of 34 sachets of suspected nyaope, 13 tablets of suspected mandrax, and 16 packets of suspected crystal meth. The estimated street value of the drugs is approximately R4,600.

nnnn

The suspect is set to appear before the Standerton Magistrate’s Court on 28 July 2025, facing charges of possession of drugs.

nnnn

Meanwhile, in Vosman, police operations involving the Middelburg K9 Unit, Anti-Hijacking and Tracking Team, and Middelburg Highway Patrol led to the arrest of two more suspects on the same day. A 33-year-old was caught with two sachets of suspected crystal meth and five tablets of suspected mandrax worth an estimated R2,000. A 45-year-old suspect was found with 96 units of suspected drugs concealed in a green plastic bag, with a street value estimated at R4,800.

nnnn

Both suspects are due to appear at the Emalahleni Magistrate’s Court on 28 July 2025.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of the SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, commended the teams involved. “These results demonstrate our commitment to combat drug trafficking and safeguard communities,” said the General.

nnnnn

post_title: Seven Illegal Immigrants Nabbed During Operation
post_content:
n

Seven undocumented foreign nationals, aged between 20 and 28, were arrested during Operation Vala Umgodi in Karino, Nelspruit, on 25 July 2025. The operation was spearheaded by members of the South African Police Service's (SAPS) Proactive and Combat Teams as part of an ongoing effort to curb illegal mining and related criminal activities in the province.

nnnn

During a stop-and-search operation, the suspects failed to produce valid identification or permits that would authorise them to be in the Republic of South Africa. The officers arrested them on the spot for contravening the Immigration Act of South Africa.

nnnn

The suspects were charged accordingly and remain in custody as officials from the Department of Home Affairs conduct further investigations to verify their nationalities and immigration statuses. The process will also determine whether the suspects have any pending cases or prior deportation orders against them.

nnnn

The arrested individuals are scheduled to appear in the Nelspruit Magistrate’s Court on 28 July 2025, where they will face charges related to their unlawful presence in the country.

nnnn

This arrest comes as part of intensified efforts by law enforcement to clamp down on illegal mining, unauthorised border crossings, and other forms of criminality often associated with unregulated migration. Operation Vala Umgodi has yielded numerous successes in recent months, with similar operations conducted across various parts of Mpumalanga.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of the SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, praised the team for their diligence and ongoing commitment to safeguarding the country’s sovereignty and upholding the rule of law.

nnnn

"I commend the members involved for their relentless efforts in maintaining law and order. These operations send a strong message that illegal activities, including unauthorised entry into the country, will not be tolerated. We will continue working with all relevant departments to ensure that our communities are safe and secure," said Major General Mkhwanazi.

post_title: Mbombela Business woman Jailed For Sars Fraud
post_content:
n

A 38-year-old businesswoman from Mbombela has been sentenced to 36 months’ direct imprisonment for fraud by the Mpumalanga Specialised Commercial Crimes Court.

nnnn

Philisiwe Miriam Pretty Lephoko, the sole director of Premax Trading 43 CC, was convicted on 15 July under Section 276(1)(i) of the Criminal Procedure Act. Her company was also fined R100 000, though the fine was wholly suspended for five years, on the condition that no further fraud or theft is committed during that period.

nnnn

According to Monica Nyuswa, spokesperson for the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) in Mpumalanga, Lephoko fraudulently submitted Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) returns to the South African Revenue Service (Sars) in February 2019, which resulted in an undue payment of R464 550.28 into her company’s bank account.

nnnn

The fraudulent activity was uncovered during a routine Sars audit, which led to Lephoko’s arrest in 2023. During the trial, she pleaded not guilty and claimed to be a victim of cybercrime, but this version of events was dismissed by the court due to the overwhelming evidence presented.

nnnn

Advocates Ntwanano Singwane and Kutullo Nyakane led the prosecution, submitting both oral and documentary evidence from Sars and the bank, demonstrating how Lephoko transferred R200 000 from the Premax Trading account into her personal bank account after the false refund was paid.

nnnn

In handing down the sentence, the court found that Lephoko showed no remorse for her actions and instead continued to shift the blame, despite the evidence stacked against her. The magistrate remarked that tax-related fraud is increasingly prevalent in the province and that the sentence should serve as a strong deterrent to would-be offenders.

nnnn

Nyuswa welcomed the sentence, stating that the NPA remains committed to prosecuting those who defraud state institutions. “This case sends a clear message that fraudulent activities, particularly against tax authorities, will not go unpunished,” she said.

nnnn

The public is urged to report suspicious tax activities to Sars or the relevant law enforcement authorities.

post_title: Commission Probing Mkhwanazi Allegations Moves Forward
post_content:
n

The work of the Commission of Inquiry into Criminality, Political Interference and Corruption in the Criminal Justice System—known as the Madlanga Commission—has officially begun.

nnnn

Acting Deputy Chief Justice Mbuyiseli Madlanga, who chairs the commission, confirmed this during a media briefing on 28 July 2025. The commission was established by President Cyril Ramaphosa in response to serious allegations made by KwaZulu-Natal Police Commissioner, Lieutenant General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi.

nnnn

Mkhwanazi’s claims point to a criminal syndicate allegedly operating within South Africa’s law enforcement, intelligence services, the judiciary, and the National Prosecuting Authority. He also implicated politicians and the now suspended Police Minister Senzo Mchunu.

nnnn

“We can assure South Africans that the work of the commission has commenced in earnest. Our first consultation with a witness is imminent, and it will inform the direction of further inquiries,” said Justice Madlanga.

nnnn

He acknowledged public interest in the commission's proceedings and stressed the need to follow correct procedures before public hearings begin. “Just because Lieutenant General Mkhwanazi made the allegations does not mean we can immediately proceed to hear evidence. Information must be assessed, verified and, if necessary, further supported,” he added.

nnnn

Justice Madlanga indicated that public hearings are expected to begin during August 2025. “We are treating the matter with urgency. The commission hearings will commence as soon as the necessary preparatory steps have been finalised,” he said.

nnnn

The commission will investigate the South African Police Service, Gauteng metro police, National Prosecuting Authority, State Security Agency, Correctional Services, the judiciary, and any members of the executive responsible for criminal justice.

nnnn

The primary objective is to investigate whether criminal syndicates have infiltrated these institutions. Madlanga stated that the commission aims to deliver an interim report by the end of its first three-month phase, potentially recommending immediate actions based on the evidence received.

nnnn

Meanwhile, the commission is finalising the procurement of office space and infrastructure in Gauteng, where hearings will take place. “The lack of physical premises does not impact our preparatory work. We are moving full steam ahead,” Madlanga assured.

nnnn

The commission’s core team has been appointed and includes:

nnnn

· Advocate Sesi Baloyi SC and Advocate Sandile Khumalo SC – assisting Madlanga.

nnnn

· Dr Nolitha Vukuza – Commission Secretary.

nnnn

· Advocate Terry Motau SC – Chief Evidence Leader.

nnnn

· Dr Peter Goss – Chief Investigator.

nnnn

· Jeremy Michaels – Spokesperson.

nnnn

Evidence leaders include Advocates Matthew Chaskalson SC, Mahlape Sello SC, Adila Hassim SC, Lee Segeels-Ncube, Ofentse Motlhasedi, and Thabang Pooe.

nnnn

Justice Madlanga concluded that public hearings would be streamed live and open to in-person attendance.

n

post_title: Mpumalanga Fresh Produce Market Faces Uncertainty
post_content:
n

Earlier this month, Mpumalanga Premier Mandla Ndlovu gave Khethiwe Moeketsi, the current MEC for Agriculture, Rural Development, Land and Environmental Affairs (DARDLEA), a two-week deadline to open the province’s long-delayed fresh produce market.

nnnn

This placed the expected launch on Friday, 1 August. However, an insider at DARDLEA has since confirmed that the market will not open on that date, and a new official opening date remains unconfirmed.

nnnn

The Mpumalanga government maintains that the market will boost the local economy, attract regional and international investment, create jobs, and empower women and communities.

nnnn

However, agricultural sector leaders remain critical. They question the necessity, scale, and cost of the project, especially given the low volume of vegetables produced in the surrounding area.

nnnn

“Most of Mpumalanga’s fruit is exported and does not require a local fresh produce market,” said a source close to the project.

nnnn

The government has claimed the market will serve as a sales point for macadamia nuts, since Mpumalanga is South Africa’s largest producer. However, over 95% of the nuts are exported, often processed within the province and not traded locally.

nnnn

Tersia Marshall, the DA’s spokesperson for DARDLEA, was sharply critical, calling the project a "multibillion-rand piece of nothing" that is “not going to help Mpumalanga” and risks becoming another white elephant.

nnnn

She said the Mpumalanga International Fresh Produce Market (MIFPM) was supposed to support produce from government-backed agrihubs, but these hubs never became operational.

nnnn

“Farmers haven’t received the skills or tools to farm. Some have even bought produce from Makro to resell at the market,” she added.

nnnn

Marshall also warned that a market of this magnitude needs consistent, high-volume supply to survive.

nnnn

“You can’t run a massive facility on a few bunches of spinach from emerging farmers every other week,” she said.

nnnn

The MIFPM has faced numerous operational and administrative issues since its development began.

nnnn

The DARDLEA allegedly failed to pay municipal utility bills, resulting in the City of Mbombela cutting off electricity to the facility. A temporary solution was arranged with adjacent landowners to supply power.

nnnn

In addition, when the property was purchased, the necessary water rights were not transferred, a legal oversight that has further delayed progress.

nnnn

“This should have been addressed from the beginning,” said Marshall, “but it was only picked up at the start of the year.”

nnnn

As pressure mounts and costs continue to rise, many are questioning whether the MIFPM will ever function as intended or if it will become yet another costly failure in the province’s agricultural sector.

n

post_title: Shabalala Secondary School hosted a high-profile briefing
Shabalala Secondary School hosted a high-profile briefing
MEC Praises Rural School's Academic Excellence
post_content:
n

Shabalala Secondary School hosted a high-profile briefing on 07 August that opened with a prayer and warm welcome from Chairperson of the SGB Mr. Kgwedi, a dedicated parent who expressed his deep love for the school, community, and education.

nnnn

“I love society, and I love education. I want to contribute to ensure our children do well,” Mr. Kgwedi said as he welcomed guests, including the MEC and 2 other visiting schools. He emphasized the significance of recognising schools in rural areas and expressed gratitude for the privilege of hosting the MEC at Shabalala Secondary School.

nnnn

The school, which enrolled 217 Grade 12 learners in 2025, aims to maintain a 100% matric pass rate. So far, it has achieved 96% in Term 1 and 98% in Term 2. “Our target remains 100%,” said the school’s leadership.

nnnn

The MEC Ms. Lindi Masina thanked everyone in attendance and offered special praise to the teachers for their dedication, hard work, and commitment. “To our learners, we are here today because of you,” the MEC added, also acknowledging two partnering primary schools Mhwayi Primary school and Sifunfekhaya Primary School

nnnn

The visit was part of the department’s Rhandza Xikolo Xa Wena campaign, which supports and appreciates schools in need. The MEC applauded Shabalala Secondary School’s consistent high performance over the past three years and encouraged the principal to share the school’s success strategies with neighbouring institutions.

nnnn

In celebration of Women’s Month, the department announced a generous donation of full school uniforms to 104 learners across three schools: 40 sets to Shabalala Secondary, 44 to Mhwayi Primary, and 50 to Sifunfekhaya Primary.

nnnn

The MEC reaffirmed the department’s confidence that Shabalala will once again achieve a 100% pass rate. “Keep pushing, never give up. It doesn’t matter how slow you go, as long as you don’t stop,” the MEC encouraged learners. The visit concluded with a renewed call for cooperation among parents, teachers, and school leaders to ensure that education in rural communities continues to thrive.

post_title: Government Vows to Keep US Markets Open
post_content:
n

Trade, Industry and Competition Minister Parks Tau has reaffirmed government’s commitment to keeping American markets open for South African goods, despite the recent imposition of a 30% unilateral tariff by the United States (US) on local exports.

nnnn

Speaking in Pretoria alongside Agriculture Minister John Steenhuisen, Tau said South Africa was “pulling out all the stops” to secure continued access while also accelerating efforts to diversify export markets.

nnnn

“We will leverage all our existing partnerships to secure markets for our products, ensure trade predictability, and expand into new territories,” he said.

nnnn

Government’s response is anchored on five key elements: continued engagement with the US to reduce tariffs; diversifying exports to alternative markets; implementing an economic response package for vulnerable companies and workers; introducing trade defence measures against import surges and dumping; and demand-side interventions.

nnnn

Cabinet has approved a revised offer to the US, building on the proposal submitted in May 2025, addressing concerns raised in the US 2025 National Trade Estimates Report. The USA-Africa Trade Desk has confirmed that shipments of poultry and pork from US states will resume within two weeks, signalling progress on some disputes.

nnnn

The US has also requested that South Africa consider lowering certain tariffs to align more closely with the SADC-EU Economic Partnership Agreement. Consultations with industry and other Southern African Customs Union members are underway to identify product lines for adjustment.

nnnn

Tau stressed that the US tariff decision necessitates a “clear and decisive response”, adding that South Africa is strengthening trade ties under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) and deepening relations with European partners. Expansion into Asia, the Middle East and India is also being prioritised, with Japan, Vietnam and Thailand identified as high-potential markets.

nnnn

“This is not just about trade figures; it is about job protection, rural livelihoods, and sustainable agricultural growth,” Tau said. Efforts include deploying trade and agricultural attachés, enhancing export certification capacity, and aligning biosecurity standards with new market requirements.

nnnn

Earlier this month, government announced an economic response package, including an export support desk and a localisation fund, to cushion the impact of the US tariffs, which took effect on 8 August 2025.

nnnn

Tau emphasised that the US tariffs are not unique to South Africa, affecting over 130 of America’s trading partners. “Our aim is to demonstrate that South African exports do not threaten US industries and that our trade relationship is complementary,” he said.

n

post_title: Eskom Urges Reporting of Electrical Safety Hazards
post_content:
n

Eskom has called on South Africans to report illegal electricity connections and exposed wires as part of its Electricity Safety Month campaign, warning that unsafe electrical practices are endangering lives.

nnnn

Eskom’s Senior Manager for Health and Safety, Miranda Moahlodi, revealed that the power utility has recorded around 200 public injuries and fatalities related to electricity. She said many more incidents go unreported because communities often feel compelled to protect illegal connections.

nnnn

“It is genuinely distressing to think that many electricity-related injuries and deaths go unreported to Eskom. Furthermore, criminal activities are on the rise, with increasing cases of infrastructure vandalism, cable theft, and attacks on Eskom staff,” Moahlodi said.

nnnn

She appealed to communities to help curb the aggression faced by Eskom employees. “Like everyone else, we have families waiting for us at home after work,” she noted.

nnnn

The utility emphasised that exposed wires and illegal connections pose a serious threat to community safety, infrastructure, and lives. Poorly installed or tampered-with lines are among the leading causes of fires in informal settlements and residential areas.

nnnn

“By reporting hazards early, we can prevent fires that destroy homes and disrupt lives,” Eskom stated. The utility urged residents to be vigilant and act when they see a dangling or low-hanging wire, an open electrical box, or unsafe connections running through trees, along streets, or across rooftops.

nnnn

Eskom encouraged regular checks of electrical systems, adherence to safety guidelines, and swift action when risks are identified.

nnnn

Illegal activities affecting Eskom’s infrastructure can be reported via the Eskom Crime Line on 0800 11 27 22, by email at eskom@whistleblowing.co.za, or via SMS to 31090.

nnnn

“Together, we can create safer homes, safer workplaces, and ultimately a safer South Africa. By reporting dangerous wiring, illegal connections, or exposed wires to Eskom or your local municipality, you could save a life — perhaps that of a child or someone unaware of the danger,” Eskom said.

nnnn

The call forms part of Eskom’s broader campaign to promote responsible electricity use and protect both the public and the utility’s infrastructure.

n

post_title: Capitec, FNB Join Drive for Digital IDs
post_content:
n

Capitec Bank and First National Bank (FNB) have joined the Department of Home Affairs’ new digital partnership model to expand access to Smart ID and passport services across South Africa.

nnnn

Home Affairs Minister Dr Leon Schreiber announced that the partnership will increase service points from the current 30 bank branches to hundreds more in both urban and rural areas. The initiative will also extend these services to secure digital banking applications.

nnnn

“In line with the Medium-Term Development Plan target for Home Affairs to expand services to 1 000 bank branches by 2029, the Director-General, Mr Tommy Makhode, wrote on 30 April 2025 to the Chief Executive Officers of nine major banks, inviting them to participate in this transformative, digital-first phase of our collaboration with the banking sector,” the department said.

nnnn

The existing partnership, which began over a decade ago, has so far delivered Smart ID and passport services at 30 branches across five banks. However, the original model relied on duplicating Home Affairs staff and hardware in bank branches, limiting its reach and failing to fully utilise technology to expand services nationwide.

nnnn

The new approach will leverage banks’ existing branch networks and widely used digital banking platforms to make services more accessible, particularly for rural communities.

nnnn

According to the department, the move signals “the beginning of the end” for long travel distances, lengthy queues, and the outdated Green ID book, which is vulnerable to fraud and identity theft. It also marks another step in the Government of National Unity’s push for a “digital-first era” of public service delivery.

nnnn

Minister Schreiber will this week visit Capitec and FNB to provide further details on the reform. On 12 August, he will be at Capitec’s head office in Stellenbosch, followed by a visit to FNB’s Portside Tower in Cape Town on Wednesday.

nnnn

The department reiterated its call for other banks, including ABSA, African Bank, TymeBank, Discovery Bank, Investec, Nedbank, and Standard Bank, to join the initiative to ensure all South Africans can access Smart ID and passport services within their communities.

nnnn

“This reform marks a critical milestone in unlocking the power of digital transformation to deliver Home Affairs @ home,” the department said.

n

post_title: Hawks Probe Standerton Drug Lab Connection
post_content:
n

Three suspects — two men aged 26 and 44, and a 23-year-old woman — have been arrested after drugs with an estimated street value of R2 million, along with R7 000 in cash, were recovered in Sakhile, Standerton, on 8 August 2025.

nnnn

The Hawks’ Secunda-based Serious Organised Crime Investigation Unit, working with the Standerton K9 Unit, acted on intelligence about suspects allegedly dealing in drugs at a specific premises in Sakhile township.

nnnn

When officers executed the operation, they discovered drugs concealed in two vehicles — a KwaZulu-Natal registered BMW and a Gauteng registered VW Polo. Two safes were also seized from the property. Upon opening them, large quantities of drugs were found, including Kat, Mandrax, and crystal meth.

nnnn

The Hawks in Mpumalanga are investigating potential links between the recovered drugs and the clandestine laboratory and warehouse uncovered earlier this year.

nnnn

The combined value of the recovered drugs, vehicles, and equipment is estimated at R2.5 million.

nnnn

The suspects are scheduled to appear before the Standerton Magistrate’s Court on 11 August 2025.

nnnn

Provincial Head of the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation, Major General Nico Gerber, praised the team’s continued success in dismantling drug operations.

nnnn

“The Hawks have intensified efforts to target the manufacturing and distribution of drugs in the area. These recent successes are a testament to our commitment. We will never relent in our fight to curb this scourge,” Gerber said.

nnnn

Enquiries: Lieutenant Colonel Magonseni Nkosi – 071 481 3437

post_title: Violence and Disputes Stall Mapulaneng Hospital Project
post_content:
n

 Contractors working on the New Mapulaneng Hospital project in Bushbuckridge are raising alarm over escalating intimidation, theft, and site hijackings that have disrupted progress and compromised the quality of work.

nnnn

Subcontractors claim a notorious local subcontractor and his associates are using threats and violence to seize control of the site, forcing others to surrender work or abandon projects. “They take plants and machines and demand payment to return them. This is like site hijack,” an anonymous whistleblower wrote.

nnnn

Despite several police cases being opened, contractors say little action has been taken. They warn that the project, currently in phase three, is now in the hands of “mafia and criminals,” endangering its completion and purpose of serving the community.

nnnn

Disputes between local community zones have added fuel to the fire. The Midlands Zone claims it has received fewer benefits compared to other zones and has demanded the exclusion of the North and South Zones from the project. Tensions have resulted in multiple work stoppages, hijacked equipment, and threats to staff.

nnnn

Efforts at mediation have yielded only temporary relief, with repeated disruptions halting construction. “If this continues, the entire project could collapse,” said Papi Wessie, director of Nala Consulting. Contractors are now pleading for urgent intervention from the provincial government, SAPS, and even President Cyril Ramaphosa to restore order and ensure the hospital’s completion.

post_title: SASSA CEO Concludes National Media Engagements
post_content:
n

The South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) has concluded its nationwide media engagement sessions, with the final event held in Mbombela, Mpumalanga, on 12 August 2025.

nnnn

Speaking at the session, SASSA Chief Executive Officer, Mr Themba Matlou, expressed his delight at ending the campaign in a province close to his heart. “Mpumalanga is my second home. The people here have so much love for everyone,” he said, noting that the engagements began in March in KwaZulu-Natal when he was still Acting CEO.

nnnn

The initiative aimed to strengthen communication with the media, recognising their vital role in providing accurate information on social grants to the public. Matlou emphasised that these engagements were part of SASSA’s commitment to the Batho Pele principles of openness, transparency, and accessibility.

nnnn

He also addressed misinformation surrounding the agency, stating: “Almost daily, we wake up to fresh disinformation. We acknowledge the crucial role the media plays in correcting this and providing accurate facts to our citizens.”

nnnn

In Mpumalanga, SASSA pays approximately 1.5 million grants monthly, including COVID-19 Social Relief of Distress benefits. Of the 19 million regular social grants distributed nationally, women receive 54%, and 51% of the COVID-19 SRD R370 grants. Over 13 million Child Support Grants are also provided, the majority to women.

nnnn

Matlou stressed SASSA’s commitment to improving service delivery through:

nnnn
    n
  • Faster processing of grant applications.
    • nnnn
  • Alternative service delivery models for better accessibility.
    • nnnn
  • Measures to reduce queues at local offices.
    • nnnn
  • Expanded community outreach and beneficiary education.
    • n
nnnn

He confirmed that the current review of grants targets beneficiaries suspected of having undeclared income. “No social grant payments have been suspended or halted because of this review process. All approved grants remain valid,” he clarified.

nnnn

The review process, required under the Social Assistance Act, helps ensure grants reach eligible recipients and prevents fraud. Data checks have flagged 210 000 cases nationally, with 13 000 in Mpumalanga. Fraud prevention measures include biometric beneficiary verification, increased risk and compliance capacity, and collaboration with law enforcement agencies.

nnnn

Matlou concluded by thanking the media for their support, stating, “Please continue to engage with us. We also have positive stories to share, and we are making tremendous progress.”

nnnn

SASSA remains committed to transparent communication, operational efficiency, and restoring trust in the social grant system.

nnnnn

Mpumalanga police are investigating a stabbing incident that claimed the life of a Grade 8 pupil from Senzangakhona Secondary School.

nnnn

According to the provincial Department of Education, the learner was attacked by another Grade 8 pupil on 14 August after school. Emergency services, called to the scene by a teacher, declared the victim dead.

nnnn

Department spokesperson Gerald Sambo confirmed that the suspect was arrested shortly after the incident.

nnnn

“The circumstances leading to this tragic event remain unclear and are under investigation by law enforcement authorities. The department extends its deepest condolences to the bereaved family, friends, classmates, and the entire school community during this time of immense grief,” said Sambo.

nnnn

Mpumalanga police are investigating a stabbing incident that claimed the life of a Grade 8 pupil from Senzangakhona Secondary School.

post_title: Minister Gwarube Calls for Stronger Education Partnerships
post_content:
n

Basic Education Minister Siviwe Gwarube has emphasised the urgent need for collective leadership and robust partnerships between government, universities, and communities to strengthen South Africa’s education system.

nnnn

Speaking at the Western Cape G20 Provincial Education Indaba, held at the Century City Conference Centre, Gwarube said collaboration was central to transforming education outcomes.

nnnn

“Our challenge and our opportunity lie in partnerships. For too long, government, universities, and communities have worked alongside each other but not always in full alignment. That must change. We need shared stewardship of the education system, one where accountability is reciprocal and leadership is collective,” she said.

nnnn

The Indaba, themed “Quality Foundational Learning with emphasis on Early Childhood Development” and “Educational Professional Development for a Changing World”, forms part of South Africa’s G20 Presidency programme. It follows President Cyril Ramaphosa’s call to ensure public participation in shaping the global agenda.

nnnn

“As G20 President for 2025, South Africa has pledged to ‘take the G20 to the people’. This commitment means aligning global priorities with our people’s lived realities. Today, that journey brings us here, to the Western Cape,” Gwarube added.

nnnn

She praised the province’s contribution to the national economy and education sector, highlighting its ability to create 69 000 jobs and maintain the lowest unemployment rate in the country.

nnnn

The Minister stressed that the Indaba’s purpose was not abstract discussion, but tangible connection between global debates and local classrooms — from early childhood centres in George, to rural schools in the Karoo, and high schools in Cape Town.

nnnn

Gwarube outlined six focus areas for collaboration:

nnnn

Policy Alignment and Responsiveness: ensuring teacher training matches evolving priorities like literacy, numeracy, and bilingual education.

nnnn

Professional Learning Communities: fostering dialogue between subject advisers and academics.

nnnn

Teacher Supply and Demand Planning: addressing shortages in key subjects and rural schools.

nnnn

Work-Integrated Learning: placing student teachers in schools with proper mentorship.

nnnn

Induction and Continuous Development: strengthening teacher preparation and lifelong learning.

nnnn

Monitoring, Evaluation and Research: combining government data with academic expertise for reforms.

nnnn

She noted that global best practices, such as Finland’s high-level teacher qualifications and Singapore’s government-university collaboration, offered valuable lessons. However, she emphasised that South Africa must design its own model, rooted in local realities.

nnnn

“This Indaba must not be remembered for speeches alone, but for the partnerships it builds and the commitments it inspires,” Gwarube said.

nnnn

Baka Ngwane is a historical biopic that tells the story of the Swati people as they face displacement and war. I’m proud to share my accomplishments with the people of Mpumalanga, and I hope this serves as a yardstick for aspiring filmmakers to aim high, produce exceptional work, and create films with commercial potential that can reach global audiences while showcasing the culture and pride of our province,” said King Shaft, adding that Baka Ngwane will resonate with fans of historical epics such as Shaka Zulu, Vikings, The Woman King and Barbarians.

nnnn

He has also committed to supporting MIFF in the future as part of his mission to grow the film industry in Mpumalanga. “I will make myself available for film training, workshops, panel discussions, or premiering new films shot in the province.”

post_title: Three Zimbabwean bodies retrieved from Nkomazi River
post_content:
n

Elukwatini, 24 August 2025 – Police in Elukwatini are investigating an inquest after the bodies of three men were recovered from the Nkomazi River at a game reserve on Friday, 22 August. The discovery was made by SAPS divers, who confirmed that the bodies bore no visible injuries.

nnnn

According to police reports, the three men had been reported missing earlier the same day at Elukwatini SAPS. Concerned housemates told officers that the men had left for the game reserve but failed to return.

nnnn

Police accompanied the complainants to the reserve, where officials revealed that unauthorised entry by individuals had been observed in recent weeks. About a week ago, some people were reportedly spotted on the premises but fled when approached by authorities and were not seen again.

nnnn

When SAPS members checked the area where the men were last sighted, they discovered three bodies floating in the river. The Search and Rescue Unit, together with divers, was called in to retrieve the remains.

nnnn

An inquest docket has been opened, and a post-mortem will be conducted to determine the exact cause of death. Police have confirmed that the men were originally from Zimbabwe, though their identities will only be released once their next of kin have been notified.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner of SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, has ordered a thorough investigation into the matter. “We must uncover the truth of what transpired and led to the deaths of these three individuals,” he said.

post_title: Madlanga Commission Hearings Face Start Delay
post_content:
n

The Delay

nnnn
nnnn

The long-awaited hearings of the Judicial Commission of Inquiry into Criminality, Political Interference and Corruption in the Criminal Justice System, widely known as the Madlanga Commission, have been delayed.

nnnnnnnn

The Commission, chaired by former Constitutional Court Justice Mbuyiseli Madlanga, was scheduled to begin on 1 September 2025. However, the Department of Justice and Constitutional Development failed to procure the necessary infrastructure in time, forcing the postponement.

nnnn

In a statement, the Commission expressed regret that valuable time had already been lost: “A substantial portion of the three-month period, at the end of which an interim report is due, has gone by without a single witness being heard. This is not of the Commission’s making.”

nnnn

The Commission said it would only announce a new start date once all requirements were in place, assuring South Africans that it was ready to proceed as soon as logistical obstacles were resolved.

nnnn
nnnn

Why the Commission Matters

nnnn

The Madlanga Commission is more than just another inquiry. It is central to South Africa’s struggle to restore accountability and credibility within the justice system.

nnnn

Why it matters for ordinary South Africans:

nnnn
    n
  • Exposing criminal networks
    Allegations suggest organised crime has infiltrated institutions such as the SAPS, NPA, metro police and Correctional Services. This undermines community safety and weakens law enforcement.
    • nnnn
  • Uncovering political interference
    Claims of political meddling in prosecutions allow influential figures to escape justice, fuelling public mistrust in the system.
    • nnnn
  • Delivering justice for victims
    Communities often see cases of corruption, violent crime and gender-based violence collapse because of interference or flawed investigations. The Commission could highlight reforms to prevent this.
    • nnnn
  • Strengthening accountability
    While its findings are not legally binding, the Commission can shape future prosecutions, influence policy reform and expose wrongdoing in the justice system.
    • nnnn
  • Restoring trust in institutions
    Years of corruption scandals have eroded confidence in government institutions. A credible and transparent inquiry can rebuild public trust.
    • n
nnnn

The stakes are high. If the Commission succeeds, it could lead to safer communities, stronger prosecutions and renewed accountability. If it fails, perceptions of impunity will deepen, leaving ordinary citizens more vulnerable and more sceptical of the justice system.

nnnn

For many South Africans, the Commission is not about politics alone, but about whether the justice system can protect rights and deliver fairness for all.

nnnn

nappy yin’wana na yin’wana yi rhwala mahungu lamatsongo malunghana ni rihanyo ra n’wana wa wena.

nnnn

Leswi "wee" swi nga ku byela swona

    n
  • Ya xitshopana (Yellow): N’wana u na mati lawa ma ringaneke – a hanye kahle.
    • nnnn

    • nnnn
  • Ya tshwuka (Red): Kungava ku ri ngati – vona dokodela hi xihatla.
    • nnnn
  • Ya rihlaza (Green): Swi nga kombisa vuvabyi bya urinary – kambela n’wana emavokweni ya dokodela.
    • n

Leswi "poo" yi nga ku byelaku swona

nnnn
    n
  • Ntima na ku namarhela (meconium): Swi tolovelekile hi masiku yo sungula. Loko swi ya emahlweni endzhaku ka vhiki, kambela eka dokodela wa vana.

  • Ya xitshopana, yi olovile: Yi kombisa rihanyo lerinene eka vana lava mamisaka. Loko ku ri tan kumbe brown naswona yi tiya ngopfu eka lava dyaka formula – na swona swi tolovelekile.
    • nnnn

    • n

Ku hlayisa n’wana loko a khomiwile hi ku pfumala mati

Loko n’wana a va ni ti-poo ta mati to tala, a nga ha tshama a pfumala mati emirini. Muongori na mu-beburi Lynn Bluff u endla xileriso xo tirhisa murhi wa le kaya: hlanganisa mati lama virisiweke, chukele na munyu ku endla Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS). Loko n’wana a hlanta, nyikela swikandza swintsongo nkarhi na nkarhi – hambiloko a hlanta, a nge hlanti hinkwaswo. Nomu wun’wana na wun’wana lowu a tekaka wu endla ku hambana kukulu.

post_title: Ramaphosa Attends Zimbabwe Agricultural Show Opening
post_content:
n

President Cyril Ramaphosa has arrived in Harare, Zimbabwe, for a working visit at the invitation of President Emmerson Mnangagwa. The South African leader will attend the official opening of the Zimbabwe Agricultural Show as Guest of Honour.

nnnn

The show, organised annually by the Zimbabwe Agricultural Society, is the country’s largest exhibition aimed at promoting agricultural development and fostering links with industry and commerce. This year’s edition is particularly historic as it marks the 130th anniversary of the event since its establishment in 1895. Running under the theme “Building Bridges: Connecting Agriculture, Industry and Commerce”, the show is expected to attract thousands of visitors and exhibitors.

nnnn

In 2024, the event hosted 570 exhibitors, including 13 international participants, and drew more than 230,000 visitors. This year, organisers are expecting even greater participation as the show continues to expand its regional and international footprint.

nnnn

The Presidency emphasised that Ramaphosa’s participation will not only celebrate agricultural progress but also strengthen bilateral and regional ties. “The Zimbabwe Agricultural Show will help promote intra-regional trade and economic integration within the Southern African Development Community (SADC) region,” a statement said.

nnnn

Zimbabwe remains one of South Africa’s key trading partners in the region. In 2024, South Africa exported goods worth R69.21 billion to Zimbabwe, compared with R57.5 billion in 2023. Vegetables topped the list of exports, contributing R11.9 billion to the total. Imports from Zimbabwe also rose to R5.4 billion in 2024, up from R4.4 billion the previous year.

nnnn

More than 120 South African companies currently operate in Zimbabwe across sectors such as mining, aviation, banking, tourism, retail, construction and fast food, reflecting the depth of economic ties between the two nations.

nnnn

The event carries historic significance for South Africa as well. Former President Nelson Mandela attended the show as Guest of Honour on 26 August 1994, underscoring its symbolic importance in regional cooperation.

nnnn

President Ramaphosa is accompanied by Deputy Minister of International Relations and Cooperation Alvin Botes, along with senior government officials, during his working visit.

n

post_title: Hawks Arrest Mkhondo Senior Manager Over Fraud
post_content:
n

A senior official at Mkhondo Local Municipality has been arrested in connection with an alleged price-fixing scandal dating back to 2019.

nnnn

Sydney Masango (46), Senior Manager for Public Safety, was taken into custody by the Hawks’ Middelburg-based Serious Organised Crime Investigation Unit on 28 August 2025. His alleged accomplice, company director Gugulethu Zulu (48), was arrested on the same day at a filling station in Piet Retief.

nnnn

The arrests relate to the repair of a municipal road-marking machine that was damaged in 2019. Investigations revealed that while the actual service provider charged only R718.20 for the repair, an inflated invoice of R85 875.00 was submitted to the municipality.

nnnn

According to the Hawks, Masango was responsible for arranging the repairs and authorised the payment. Zulu, through his company Legent 12, allegedly received the inflated funds into his business account after colluding in the scheme.

nnnn

Following a lengthy probe, investigators uncovered evidence linking both men to the fraudulent transaction, which resulted in the alleged theft of municipal funds.

nnnn

Masango was arrested at his municipal offices, while Zulu was apprehended in Piet Retief. The duo appeared in the Mkhondo District Court shortly after their arrests, where they were each released on R4 000 bail. The case was postponed to 6 October 2025 for the setting of a regional court trial date.

nnnn

Brigadier Bruce Davenport, Acting Provincial Head of the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation in Mpumalanga, praised the team’s work.

nnnn
n

“We once again warn the public that the Hawks will always seek, find, and strike at the right time,” Brigadier Davenport said.

n
nnnn

The arrests underscore ongoing efforts by law enforcement to root out corruption and financial misconduct within municipalities across Mpumalanga.

post_title: Stillbirths We Can Prevent — Accountability Mpumalanga Owes Families
post_content:
n

Stillbirth is one of the most painful losses a family can face, and it is a loss that, far too often, could have been prevented. Globally, nearly two million babies were stillborn last year. Shockingly, almost half of these deaths happened during labour — the very moment when skilled staff, proper monitoring, and swift medical response could make the difference between life and death. This is not simply bad luck; it is a reflection of how reliable, or unreliable, our health systems truly are.

nnnn

Here in Mpumalanga, answers remain hard to find. The provincial Department of Health has not released its stillbirth statistics for August 2025. Yet courtrooms continue to reveal the truth families face. In June 2025, the Mpumalanga High Court awarded damages in the case of Z.N. obo N. v MEC for Health, Mpumalanga Province. The court found that negligent care during labour caused severe brain injury to a newborn child, leading to cerebral palsy and, later, his death. The mother, who initially claimed R4 million, was awarded R540,000 in damages. The judge acknowledged that no amount of money could truly compensate for the child’s suffering — but the judgment made clear that systemic negligence in maternity care has devastating consequences.

nnnn

The World Health Organisation points to well-known causes: complications during labour, untreated infections, unmanaged high blood pressure or diabetes, and growth problems that go unnoticed. These are not rare medical puzzles; they are everyday matters in maternity care. With consistent monitoring, proper screening, timely treatment, and quick access to emergency caesarean sections when needed, many lives can be saved.

nnnn

So, what needs to change? First, transparency. The Department should publish monthly data on stillbirths at each hospital, alongside clear explanations of causes and lessons learnt. Second, basics must be guaranteed in every labour ward: enough staff on duty day and night, working monitoring equipment, and clear procedures for emergencies. Third, women must be treated with respect. No one should be turned away in labour. A simple hotline for patients, visible progress dashboards in wards, and firm accountability would help rebuild trust. When negligence is proven in court, the response should not end with a payout — it must lead to audits, retraining, and stronger systems.

nnnn

Communities in Mpumalanga carry the sorrow of these avoidable losses. It is time for the health system to carry its share of the responsibility. Stillbirths should not be dismissed as inevitable statistics. They are a measure of the quality of our healthcare — and we cannot afford to look away while the numbers stay the same.

post_title: Silent Killer: Raising Awareness on Kidney Disease
post_content:
n

The first week of September marks National Kidney Awareness Week, a campaign highlighting the vital role kidneys play in keeping us alive and healthy. Kidneys help maintain fluid balance, regulate blood pressure and filter waste products from the blood. Yet, despite their importance, many people underestimate the risks of kidney disease until it is too late.

nnnn

Often referred to as a “silent killer,” kidney disease develops gradually, showing no clear symptoms until it reaches advanced stages. In South Africa, it is estimated that between 6 and 10 per cent of the population live with some form of kidney disease, many without knowing it.

nnnn

Experts warn that unhealthy lifestyle choices are fuelling this hidden crisis. Smoking, excessive alcohol use, lack of exercise and poor diets all contribute to kidney damage. The rising prevalence of uncontrolled diabetes, hypertension and obesity in urban areas is of particular concern, as these conditions are leading causes of kidney failure.

nnnn

The good news is that kidney disease is often preventable. Doctors recommend regular health screenings, especially for people with diabetes or high blood pressure. The World Health Organisation advises adults to engage in at least 150 minutes of moderate physical activity or 75 minutes of vigorous exercise weekly. Activities such as brisk walking, cycling, or aerobics not only boost heart health but also protect kidney function.

nnnn

A balanced diet low in salt and processed foods, maintaining a healthy weight, and staying hydrated are further steps individuals can take. Avoiding unnecessary use of painkillers and consulting a doctor before using herbal remedies or supplements can also protect kidney health.

nnnn

Beyond prevention, awareness of organ and tissue donation remains crucial. Over 6,500 people in South Africa are waiting for organ transplants, with 1,100 in Gauteng alone needing new kidneys. Becoming an organ donor is a life-saving act of compassion that could transform the futures of many families.

nnnn

National Kidney Awareness Week is therefore more than a health campaign. It is a call to communities to live healthier lives, look out for one another, and consider the gift of organ donation.

n

post_title: A Gentle Guide to Ending Breastfeeding
post_content:
n

For many mothers, the decision to stop breastfeeding is both emotional and practical. Whether returning to work, introducing solid foods, or simply feeling the time is right, weaning can be a gentle transition rather than a stressful battle. The key lies in patience, planning, and compassion – for both baby and mother.

nnnn

Take It Slowly

nnnn

Gradual weaning is often the least distressing approach. Begin by dropping one feeding session at a time, ideally starting with the one your baby is least attached to. Replace it with a bottle of expressed milk, formula, or a small healthy snack if your child is older. This step-by-step method allows your body to adjust its milk supply naturally and avoids discomfort such as engorgement.

nnnn

Create New Comfort Routines

nnnn

For babies, breastfeeding is about closeness as much as nutrition. Offer extra cuddles, bedtime stories, or soothing songs to fill the gap. This reassures your little one that comfort and security remain, even without the breast.

nnnn

Distraction and Substitution

nnnn

As your baby becomes curious about the world, introduce playtime, walks, or new activities at moments when they might normally feed. For toddlers, a special cup or a favourite snack can serve as a helpful substitute.

nnnn

Night-time Weaning

nnnn

Night feeds are often the hardest to stop. Ask a partner or family member to take over bedtime or night-time soothing, helping to break the association between breastfeeding and sleep. Keeping a consistent bedtime routine will also make the adjustment smoother.

nnnn

Caring for Yourself

nnnn

Weaning can be as emotional for mothers as it is for babies. Hormonal changes may leave you feeling sensitive, so allow yourself space for rest and reflection. If your breasts feel uncomfortable, hand-expressing a little milk or applying warm compresses can ease the pressure.

nnnn

Seek Support

nnnn

Every baby is different, and some will take longer than others. Health visitors, GPs, or local parenting groups can offer guidance tailored to your circumstances. Remember: there is no “perfect” timeline – the best pace is the one that works for you and your child.

nnnn

By approaching weaning with kindness and patience, families can move into this new stage of growth without unnecessary tears.

n

post_title: Energy Drinks: A Short Buzz, But at What Cost?
post_content:
n

A Growing Trend Among Young People

nnnn

Energy drinks have become a common sight in spaza shops, supermarkets, and even school bags. Marketed as a quick fix for energy or concentration, they have surged in popularity among young people in South Africa. Yet, health experts warn that the short-lived buzz may come with long-term consequences.

nnnn

The Immediate Effects

nnnn

“Many of these drinks are packed with sugar and caffeine. They might keep you awake for a few hours, but they can also raise your heart rate, disturb your sleep, and leave you more exhausted afterwards,” explained a local nutritionist.

nnnn

Risky Habits in Schools

nnnn

A survey of learners in the North West province revealed that pupils often reach for brands such as Dragon, Switch, and Red Bull to stay awake and focus on their studies. However, doctors caution that this coping mechanism is risky. “Children and teenagers are especially vulnerable to caffeine. Excessive intake can cause headaches, mood swings, anxiety, and in serious cases, heart problems,” said a Johannesburg GP.

nnnn

South Africa’s Expanding Market

nnnn

South Africa is one of the largest energy drink markets on the continent, with consumption continuing to rise. But with this boom comes growing health concerns. “We are seeing more young patients presenting with sleep disorders, dental issues, and even signs of dependency linked to energy drinks,” warned a Mediclinic health practitioner.

nnnn

Choosing Healthier Alternatives

nnnn

Community members are urged to think carefully before consuming these beverages. “Ask yourself: do I really need this, or could I opt for something healthier such as water, tea, or fresh juice? Energy drinks may provide a quick lift, but they will not address long-term tiredness,” advised a public health expert.

post_title: South Africans Join Global Flotilla to Gaza
post_content:

A group of nine South Africans, including Mandla Mandela—the grandson of former President Nelson Mandela—are among hundreds of international activists taking part in the Global Sumud Flotilla, the largest civilian maritime mission yet attempting to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza.

nnnn

The African National Congress (ANC) has praised the courage of the South African participants. In a statement issued on 3 September, the ANC described their voyage as a powerful symbol of international solidarity with the Palestinian people, one that strongly echoes South Africa’s own liberation struggle. The party stressed that this peaceful mission reflects its long-standing support for the Palestinian cause and complements the government’s legal action at the International Court of Justice.

nnnn

The flotilla consists of more than 50 vessels from at least 44 countries, carrying supplies such as baby formula, antibiotics, medical kits, staple foods, clothing and essential medicines. Those on board include activists, doctors, lawyers, journalists, human rights defenders and public figures such as Swedish climate campaigner Greta Thunberg, former Barcelona Mayor Ada Colau, and American actress Susan Sarandon.

nnnn

The mission began from ports including Barcelona on 31 August, with vessels set to rendezvous in Tunisia before sailing towards Gaza.

nnnn

The name “Sumud”, meaning steadfastness in Arabic, reflects the determination of participants to challenge Israel’s long-standing naval blockade of Gaza and open a humanitarian corridor. Organisers argue that international governments have failed to exert adequate pressure, leaving civil society to act.

nnnn

Greta Thunberg, participating for a second time after being deported during an earlier attempt in June, criticised global inaction and underlined the mission’s importance in defending human rights.

nnnn

In its statement, the ANC reaffirmed its solidarity with those who believe humanity must triumph over oppression. It also called on the South African government to extend full consular assistance to the participants.

The event, hosted at Oakley in the Bushbuckridge Local Municipality, brought together community members, traditional leaders, and government departments to plant trees, vegetables, and restore the local environment.

nnnn

As part of the Legacy Programme, 275 spekboom trees were planted on the day. Widely recognised for its ability to absorb carbon dioxide, spekboom is being promoted as a natural solution to climate change. The programme has set a wider target of planting 1,500 trees and plants before it concludes.

nnnn

In addition to trees, vegetables such as spinach and beetroot were planted, supporting food security initiatives in the community. The Department of Forestry donated mango and marula trees, which will provide shade and fruit for future generations.

nnnn

The day also included a clean-up campaign, symbolising a renewed commitment to keeping the environment clean and green.

nnnn

The Department of Agriculture reminded residents that these efforts form part of the national response to climate change. At the same time, President Cyril Ramaphosa has urged South Africans to plant one million trees across the country on Heritage Day, 24 September 2025.

nnnn

Traditional councils pledged their full support, stating: “We are standing firmly behind this programme and will continue to protect the crops and trees planted for the benefit of our people.”

nnnn

Arbor Day is not only about planting trees but also about building a sustainable future. With each tree and crop planted in Bushbuckridge, the community is making strides towards food security, biodiversity, and climate resilience.

nnnnn

post_title: Informal Settlements Highlight Housing and Jobs Crisis
post_content:
n

The Socio-Economic Rights Institute (SERI) has cautioned that the growing number of informal settlements in Gauteng reflects widespread unemployment and the lack of affordable housing.

nnnn

This follows Premier Panyaza Lesufi’s announcement that the province will demolish informal settlements regarded as illegal. He indicated that the evictions would take place at night while residents are asleep.

nnnn

Provincial data suggests that more than 400 informal settlements have been established in Gauteng over the past year.

nnnn

SERI has argued that government is using the criminalisation of poor communities to justify unlawful raids. The organisation maintains that informal settlements arise from historical landlessness and the shortage of affordable, well-located housing.

nnnn

Instead of demolitions, SERI has called on government to make use of its Upgrading of Informal Settlements Programme (UISP). The programme, already in existence, is designed to improve living conditions in informal communities. SERI pointed out that the state has acknowledged the significant backlog in the delivery of RDP homes, which has left many settlements without basic services such as water, electricity and sanitation for decades.

nnnn

The organisation believes that upgrading informal settlements through existing policy is a more constructive approach than criminalisation. It argues that evictions and raids displace residents without addressing the underlying housing crisis, whereas upgrading would offer a more humane and long-term solution.

n

Arbor Day: A Celebration of Trees

nnnn

Why Arbor Day Matters

nnnn

Arbor Day is more than just a date on the calendar; it is a reminder of the vital role trees play in sustaining life and building healthy communities.

Water Conservation

Temperature Regulation

post_title: New Ebola Outbreak Declared in DRC
post_content:
n

Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have confirmed a new outbreak of the Ebola virus, which has claimed 15 lives since late August. The country’s health minister announced that the outbreak is centred in Kasai province.

nnnn

This marks the 16th recorded outbreak of Ebola in the DRC. The most recent outbreak occurred three years ago and resulted in six deaths. Provisional figures from the current situation show 28 suspected cases, with the first identified on 20 August in a 34-year-old pregnant woman who had been admitted to hospital.

nnnn

Ebola, first detected in 1976, is a severe viral illness believed to originate in bats. It spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids and can cause internal bleeding, organ failure and, in many cases, death. Between 2018 and 2020, the DRC experienced its deadliest outbreak, which killed nearly 2,300 people.

nnnn

Health officials have confirmed that the Zaire strain is responsible for the current cases. A vaccine does exist for this strain, but logistical challenges remain in deploying it effectively across the vast nation. The DRC, which has a population of more than 100 million and is four times the size of France, continues to face difficulties with infrastructure and communication, making rapid responses to health crises more complex.

n

post_title: New Prison Wardens Urged to Shun Contraband
post_content:
n

The National Commissioner of Correctional Services, Makgothi Thobakgale, has cautioned newly qualified prison wardens against involvement in smuggling contraband into correctional facilities.

nnnn

He addressed the message during the passing-out parade of 491 trainees at the Zonderwater Training College in Cullinan, Pretoria, on Thursday. The group will be deployed to correctional centres across the country from next week.

nnnn

The cohort includes trainees from Limpopo, Mpumalanga, the North West, Free State and Northern Cape. Of the 491, there are 345 men, 146 women, and five trainees with disabilities.

nnnn

Thobakgale stressed the importance of professionalism, discipline and integrity, warning that any involvement in smuggling would endanger both officials and inmates while undermining the department’s mandate of rehabilitation.

nnnn

The Correctional Services Warden programme involves a combination of academic study and practical workplace training, with external verification conducted by the Safety and Security Sector Education and Training Authority (SASSETA).

nnnn

The commissioner also confirmed that the training programme was not without tragedy. Two trainees lost their lives – one in a car accident while travelling home for the weekend, and another who took his own life at the college. A third trainee withdrew from the programme.

nnnn

Despite the challenges, the majority successfully completed their training and are now set to begin their duties in correctional centres nationwide.

n

n

Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping were caught on a hot microphone speculating about whether medical advances such as organ transplants could extend human life well beyond 150 years – or even make immortality possible. Their conversation, recorded during a summit in Beijing, has sparked questions about how close science is to defeating ageing.

nnnn

While the idea of humans living forever remains firmly in the realm of speculation, researchers are making significant progress in understanding why we age and how the process might be slowed. Experts point out that there is currently no evidence that immortality is achievable, nor agreement on whether there is a fixed biological limit to human lifespan.

nnnn

Despite major advances in medicine, no one has surpassed the longevity record set by Jeanne Calment of France, who died in 1997 at the age of 122. Some studies suggest that mortality rates level off at extreme ages, but others caution that records of such longevity can be unreliable.

nnnn

The notion of replacing organs to extend life is seen as highly unrealistic. Scientists warn that repeatedly transplanting organs would be physically traumatic and that ageing affects far more than just organs, involving bones, tissue and other complex systems of the body.

nnnn

Nevertheless, the field of longevity research is attracting vast investment. Russia has launched a multi-billion-ruble programme in regenerative medicine, while Silicon Valley entrepreneurs continue to fund experimental anti-ageing projects. Some wealthy individuals have even turned themselves into test subjects for new treatments. Mainstream researchers, however, stress that many of these attempts lack scientific rigour and could be unsafe.

nnnn

One area of serious interest is epigenetics, which looks at how genes switch on and off without changing DNA itself. This process appears to break down over time and may be central to ageing. Laboratory work with the drug rapamycin has extended the lives of animals, though there is no evidence it would have the same effect on humans.

nnnn

For now, scientists argue that efforts should focus less on fantasies of immortality and more on improving the number of years people spend in good health.

n

post_title: Chief Justice Warns of Justice System Threats
post_content:
n

Chief Justice Mandisa Maya has cautioned that court delays, underfunded infrastructure, and weak security are placing South Africa’s justice system under severe strain.

nnnn

Speaking at the J20 Summit in Sandton on Wednesday, where judicial leaders from across the globe gathered, she highlighted the urgent need for reforms to safeguard both communities and the courts.

nnnn

Maya stressed that heavy case backlogs leave individuals and communities vulnerable, turning court delays into more than just administrative frustrations. For people challenging unfair dismissals or communities defending land rights, these delays amount to a denial of basic human rights.

nnnn

She also drew attention to security failures that have placed lives at risk. One of the most shocking examples, she said, was the killing of Dingalo Moya Kinzo, a witness in a murder trial, who was shot dead inside Wynberg Magistrate’s Court in Cape Town earlier this year.

nnnn

Calling for stronger oversight of court resources and infrastructure, Maya said greater administrative autonomy is essential for the judiciary to establish tailored safety protocols and ensure courts operate efficiently.

nnnn

While some reforms are already in progress, she stressed that without adequate support and resources, the system cannot protect the public or judicial officers, nor can it deliver justice in a timely and effective manner.

n

post_title: Limpopo Boosts Road Safety Ahead of Religious Gatherings
post_content:
n

The Limpopo Department of Transport and Community Safety has announced heightened traffic measures as thousands of visitors are expected to travel to the province for religious gatherings taking place from today until Sunday, 7 September 2025.

nnnn

Traffic law enforcement officers have been deployed along major routes and critical intersections, including the N1, N11, R101, R81, R71, R579, R37, R36, R40, R528, R574, R516, R521, D4040, D19, R524, and R523, to ensure traffic flows smoothly and that motorists remain safe.

nnnn

The department has adopted a zero-tolerance stance towards reckless behaviour on the roads, including speeding, drunk driving, overloading, and the use of unroadworthy vehicles. Motorists are urged to check that their vehicles are roadworthy, ensure all passengers wear seatbelts, and avoid fatigue or distractions such as mobile phone use while driving.

nnnn

MEC for Transport and Community Safety, Violet Mathye, appealed to all road users to make safety their top priority. She stressed that drivers should exercise patience and care, and avoid speeding, fatigue, and overloading, which remain some of the leading causes of crashes.

post_title: SARS Seizes R56 Million Cocaine Haul in Durban
post_content:
n

The South African Revenue Service (SARS) has intercepted a vessel off the east coast of Durban, uncovering a cocaine shipment with an estimated street value of R56 million.

nnnn

The operation was part of a collaborative, intelligence-driven effort. A Customs Marine Patrol vessel intercepted a cargo ship near the Fairway Buoy, about four nautical miles from Durban, and escorted it to harbour. Customs enforcement officers boarded the vessel, inspecting containers that had been flagged as high risk for smuggling.

nnnn

Their search revealed 25 large bricks of cocaine concealed within the refrigeration units of several containers. Field tests confirmed the substance as cocaine of exceptionally high quality, suitable for further dilution and illicit distribution.

nnnn

The seized drugs have been handed over to the South African Police Service (SAPS) for safekeeping, investigation, and prosecution.

nnnn

SARS Commissioner Edward Kieswetter credited the success to cooperation with Brazilian authorities. He said this joint effort demonstrated strong collaboration among BRICS nations in the fight against organised crime, while also highlighting the commitment of South African law enforcement agencies to protect the country’s borders.

n

post_title: Breetzke Stars as Proteas Clinch Series at Lord’s
post_content:
n

South Africa sealed a thrilling five-run win over England at Lord’s on Thursday, claiming the one-day international series 2-0.

nnnn

The Proteas posted 330-8, with Matthew Breetzke once again the standout. The 26-year-old made 85, becoming the first batsman in ODI history to begin his career with five consecutive scores of fifty or more. He and Tristan Stubbs (58) shared a vital 147-run stand after South Africa had slipped to 93-3.

nnnn

England, needing 331 for victory, fought back through Joe Root and Jos Buttler (both 61) and Jacob Bethell (58). Jofra Archer’s late hitting gave them hope, but they fell just short at 325-9.

nnnn

Nandre Burger led the South African attack with 3-63, while Archer took 4-62 for England. The combined 655 runs set a new ODI record at Lord’s, adding drama to a contest that went down to the final over.

nnnn

Breetzke, playing only due to Tony de Zorzi’s injury, has now scored 463 runs in five ODIs at an astonishing average of 92.6. The teams meet again in Southampton on Sunday, though South Africa already hold an unassailable lead.

n

post_title: Prisoner and Accomplice Nabbed for Bogus Hawks Scam
post_content:
n

A prisoner serving a lengthy sentence and his cousin have been linked to a scam that cost a woman R41 760 after she was duped into believing she faced arrest.

nnnn

The Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation (Hawks) in Mpumalanga revealed that the scam originated from a prison cell. The victim, who cannot be named for safety reasons, was targeted in September 2022 when she received a call from a man posing as a Hawks captain.

nnnn

The bogus officer, introducing himself as “Captain Monama”, claimed her 2006 murder case had been reopened and that a warrant of arrest had been issued. He demanded R25 000 to prevent her arrest and promised to destroy evidence against her. The woman paid the amount in two instalments.

nnnn

Two months later, the scammer contacted her again, saying that a “Detective Wessels” had discovered the supposed arrangement and demanded more money to suppress the matter.

nnnn

The conman was later identified as Bonginkosi Masango (29), who is currently serving a 16-year prison sentence for a 2015 rape conviction. Investigations linked him after the arrest of his cousin, Koosnight Mahlangu (28), on Wednesday, 3 September 2025.

nnnn

Both men appeared in the Mdutjane Magistrate’s Court on Thursday. Mahlangu was released on R1 000 bail, while Masango remains behind bars. The court has ordered the pair to reappear in the Mdutjana Regional Court on 6 October 2025.

nnnn

Brigadier Bruce Davenport, Acting Provincial Head of the Hawks in Mpumalanga, commended the investigation team.

nnnn

“A number of people have fallen victim to police impersonators, denting the image of the police. This arrest might be a breakthrough to some of the unsolved cases,” he said.

nnnn

The case was initially registered at Siyabuswa SAPS in 2024 and referred to the Hawks’ Middelburg-based Serious Corruption Investigation unit.

post_title: Why Mosquitoes Bite Some People More
post_content:
n

Debunking the sweet blood myth

nnnn

Many believe mosquitoes prefer people with “sweet blood,” but science shows otherwise. Their biting habits are driven by biology and environment, not sweetness.

nnnn

Mosquitoes are strongly attracted to carbon dioxide, which humans exhale with every breath. People who breathe out more—such as adults or those who have been exercising—are often bitten more frequently. Body odour also plays a role. Natural skin chemicals, influenced by genetics and bacteria, can act as signals, while sweat after physical activity heightens the risk.

nnnn

Blood type adds another factor: research suggests people with Type O blood are more prone to bites than those with Type A or B. Clothing choices matter too, as dark colours like black or navy make individuals stand out more to mosquitoes.

nnnn

So, the next time you find yourself bitten more than others, remember it is not about “sweet blood” but science, environment, and chance.

n

post_title: Police Probe Murder of Delmas Campus Manager
post_content:
n

Police in Delmas are investigating the murder of a campus manager who was gunned down on Wednesday afternoon.

nnnn

The incident happened at around 4pm on 3 September 2025, near a learning institution in Delmas. According to police, officers responded to a shooting report on a gravel road next to the campus.

nnnn

On arrival, they found a white Kia sedan with Gauteng registration plates. Inside the vehicle was the driver, confirmed to be the campus manager, who had sustained gunshot wounds.

nnnn

Preliminary investigations suggest the victim had been on a routine inspection of the premises when a black VW Polo approached. An armed suspect is believed to have emerged from the vehicle and fired shots at close range before fleeing the scene in the same Polo.

nnnn

The motive for the killing is not yet known. Police have appealed to the public for assistance in tracing the suspect or suspects.

post_title: SADAG Appeals for Urgent Funding to Save Crisis Helpline
post_content:
n

The South African Depression and Anxiety Group (SADAG) has made an urgent appeal for funding to keep its national crisis helpline in operation.

nnnn

The toll-free service, which answers up to 2,500 calls daily, is facing closure due to rising costs. Alarming figures show that one in three of these calls is related to suicide.

nnnn

To address the shortfall, SADAG has launched an online fundraising campaign on Back-a-Buddy, aiming to raise R180,000 to cover expenses for September. The appeal coincides with World Suicide Prevention Month.

nnnn

Development Manager Fatima Seedat warned that if the helpline is forced to scale back, many people in crisis will be left without critical intervention. South Africa continues to see a rise in mental health conditions, with almost 16% of the population affected by depression, anxiety, and mood disorders.

nnnn

Seedat explained that SADAG runs the country’s only suicide crisis helpline, which is not backed by corporate sponsorships and relies entirely on donations. Operating costs amount to about R180,000 per month.

nnnn

She added that the helpline is often the last source of hope for people in distress, urging individuals, businesses, and even mobile network providers to step in and help sustain the service. “Even R50 can make a difference,” she stressed, calling on network providers to consider making crisis calls zero-rated to ease the burden.

n

The African National Congress (ANC) has rejected Limpopo provincial chairperson Stanley Mathabatha’s request to step aside from his position.

nnnn

This follows a high-level meeting on Thursday between ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula, members of the party’s National Executive Committee (NEC), and the Limpopo Provincial Executive Committee (PEC).

nnnn

ANC national spokesperson Mahlengi Bhengu confirmed that the meeting considered Mathabatha’s letter of intention but resolved that the matter should first be dealt with at provincial level. She said the meeting agreed to refer the issue back to the province to allow space for the concerns raised by Mathabatha to be addressed internally. Once provincial deliberations are concluded, the outcome will be formally communicated to national officials.

nnnn

Mathabatha, who has served as Limpopo chairperson since 2014, wrote to Mbalula earlier this week, citing allegations of misconduct and what he described as “un-ANC conduct” during the Vhembe and Waterberg regional conferences.

nnnn

The ANC has, however, dismissed these claims, insisting that all regional conferences in Limpopo were “concluded successfully.”

nnnn

The decision effectively places responsibility back on the provincial structures to resolve the tensions, while Mathabatha remains in his position for the time being.

post_title: Two Illegal Immigrants Arrested During Operation Vala Umgodi
post_content:
n

Police officers deployed under Operation Vala Umgodi have arrested two illegal immigrants during a stop-and-search operation in Emalahleni.

nnnn

The arrests took place on Saturday, 6 September 2025, along the N4 road near a local shopping mall. The suspects, aged 19 and 20, were found without valid documentation permitting them to be in South Africa.

Both have been charged under the Immigration Act and are expected to appear before the Emalahleni Magistrates’ Court on Monday, 8 September 2025. Police detectives are working with officials from the Department of Home Affairs to verify the immigration status of the suspects

Three killed in N4 Toll Road Crash Near Mbombela

Three people lost their lives on Saturday night, 6 September 2025, following a car crash on the N4 toll road between Karino and Valencia interchange.

nnnn

The accident occurred when a Volkswagen Polo collided with the rear of a light delivery vehicle (LDV). The sedan overturned after the impact, flinging three occupants - two men and a woman from the car. All three were declared dead at the scene.

Two other passengers in the Polo sustained serious injuries and were stabilised by paramedics before being taken to medical facilities in Mbombela. No injuries were reported in the LDV.

The cause of the crash is not yet known. Police have opened three cases of culpable homicide as investigations continue.

post_title: Ford Ranger Crashes into Pool in Mbombela
post_content:
n

A white Ford Ranger crashed through a wall and landed in a resident’s swimming pool in Mbombela, leaving the occupants of the home in shock.

nnnn

The incident occurred on the evening of 4 September in the West End. Local security companies were alerted to reports of reckless driving shortly before 8:00 pm, when the bakkie smashed into the rented residence of Kyle Scott in Aurora Street, Enterprise, Steiltes.

nnnn

Scott and his wife were in their backyard at the time. Speaking to Lowvelder, he said: “We were sitting in our backyard when a vehicle crashed through the wall into our pool.” Despite their shock, the couple quickly alerted emergency services.

nnnn

When responders arrived, it was confirmed that the driver had sustained only minor injuries. It is alleged that he was under the influence of alcohol at the time of the crash.

nnnn

Lowvelder also reported that a second vehicle was involved. Witnesses claim the Ford Ranger collided with a Mercedes-Benz before the driver lost control and ended up in the pool.

nnnn

Further details about the driver have not yet been released.

post_title: Transnet Terminals Show Strong Performance Gains
post_content:
n

The Department of Transport has reported a marked improvement in the performance of Transnet’s Port Terminals between June and August this year.

nnnn

Transnet Port Terminals (TPT), which oversees cargo handling operations across the country’s commercial ports, is responsible for loading and offloading containers, vehicles, breakbulk, and bulk cargo.

nnnn

According to the department, weekly performance averaged more than 90,000 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) during the period, compared with 65,000 units over the same months last year. This reflects a year-on-year increase of 7.2% in container volumes by the end of August.

nnnn

Transport spokesperson Collen Msibi attributed the improvement to targeted maintenance that reduced equipment breakdowns, the introduction of a fourth shift to safeguard employee well-being, and substantial investment in new machinery.

nnnn

Among the equipment introduced were nine rubber-tyred gantry cranes for Durban Container Terminal Pier 1, 20 straddle carriers for Pier 2, a ship-to-shore crane at Port Elizabeth, and more than 200 hauliers and trailers distributed across all container terminals.

nnnn

Msibi highlighted that in the week ending 20 July 2025, a record 101,295 TEUs were processed across TPT container facilities. The all-time peak of 105,650 TEUs in a single week was last achieved in the 2014/2015 financial year.

nnnn

He added that the improved performance gives the department confidence that cargo volumes lost in the 2023/2024 financial year will return, strengthening the ports’ role in job retention and creating opportunities for future employment.
