post_title: Higher Education Minister Buti Manamela Picture HigherEduGovZA
NSFAS Reprioritises Funds to Support Students
post_content:
n

The National Student Financial Aid Scheme (NSFAS) has announced that it will redirect R13 billion currently available in its coffers to assist students facing blocked registrations.

nnnn

The update was delivered in Pretoria on Monday as part of a briefing on the readiness of the 2026 academic year and the status of NSFAS applications.

nnnn

According to the Department of Higher Education, 34,000 students with blocked registrations and a further 15,000 second-semester students will now be prioritised for funding. The scheme faced challenges earlier this year after miscalculating its available funds by R10 billion, leaving many qualifying students unable to register.

nnnn

The issue has since been addressed through a reallocation of funds, with the aim of ensuring smooth registration processes ahead of the new academic year. Student accommodation providers who had been impacted by delayed payments are also expected to receive relief following this adjustment.

n

post_title: Trade, Industry and Competition, Parks Tau
Minister Withdraws Controversial Credit Act Amendments
post_content:
n

Trade and Industry Minister Parks Tau has withdrawn draft regulations that could have led to the blacklisting of people with student debt.

nnnn

The department had recently gazetted draft amendments to the National Credit Act of 2005 for public comment. These changes were presented as a way to strengthen consumer protections, regulate how credit bureaus manage customer information, and improve affordability assessments.

nnnn

However, the proposals sparked widespread public outcry. The amendments would have given credit bureaus access to information from state organs involved in fraud investigations, as well as consumers’ criminal records.

nnnn

The department received more than 20,000 submissions before the closing date, with the majority opposing the draft regulations.

nnnn

Tau explained that the withdrawal was informed by the overwhelming public response. He added that while efforts will continue to improve access to finance for Small, Medium, and Micro Enterprises (SMMEs), a new process will be considered to better protect students from financial exclusion.

n

post_title: Matriculants urged to explore multiple career pathways
Manamela Urges Matriculants to Explore Alternatives
post_content:
n

Higher Education and Training Minister Buti Manamela has encouraged matriculants to consider a variety of post-school opportunities, as universities cannot accommodate all qualifying learners.

nnnn

The department has projected about 235,000 first-year university spaces for the 2026 academic year. While this is a substantial intake, it falls short of the total number of eligible applicants. Learners are therefore being urged to apply on time and to explore alternative routes such as Sector Education and Training Authorities (SETAs), Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) colleges, and Community Education and Training (CET) colleges. These are recognised as important pathways into further study, skills development, and employment.

nnnn

Although access to higher education has improved over time, dropout rates, especially among first-year students, remain a concern. Discussions are underway with institutions to make student success rates more transparent.

nnnn

At present, South Africa’s universities enrol around 1.1 million students, TVET colleges about 527,000, and CET colleges approximately 130,000 learners. Through NSFAS, around 900,000 students receive bursaries and loans each year, while SETAs continue to provide thousands of learnerships, apprenticeships, and skills programmes.

nnnn

On student funding, the department has developed a mechanism to address the shortfall experienced in 2025. By reprioritising R13.3 billion, support will be extended to 34,000 students with blocked registrations and 15,000 with second-semester registrations. NSFAS will also reopen its registration portal and release outstanding payments to accommodation providers.

nnnn

Despite these measures, the scheme remains under pressure due to rising demand, increasing living costs, and reduced state resources. The department is expected to announce further steps towards sustainable funding later this year.

post_title: Chairperson of the ANC’s Integrity Committee, Comrade Frank Chikane, delivered the presentation
ANC Admits Failings, Promises Service Delivery Fixes

The African National Congress (ANC) has admitted it has fallen short in delivering quality services through its municipalities and pledged urgent action.

More than 4,000 ANC councillors gathered at the FNB Stadium in Soweto on Monday to receive an action plan aimed at improving governance and restoring public trust. With 4,929 ward and PR councillors across the country, the party remains the largest in local government but faces criticism over poor performance in areas such as the Free State and North West.

Dickson Masemola, deputy chair of the ANC’s Local Government Intervention Committee, said: “We cannot continue to subject our people to inconsistent performances which does not resonate with the support and love the people have for the ANC.”

Measures include stricter oversight, financial penalties for failing municipalities, and capacity‐building programmes. The ANC stressed that citizens will judge them on delivery, promising that visible improvements will come before the 2026 local elections.

Multiple Injuries Reported After R40 Crash

The crash involved a Buscor bus, a minibus taxi and a VW Polo hatchback. The cause of the accident has not yet been confirmed. Emergency workers used the Jaws of Life to free the Polo driver and the front passenger of the taxi.

Several passengers from the bus and taxi sustained injuries ranging from minor to serious and were transported to nearby hospitals. The Buscor driver was not harmed.

According to a video circulating on social media, the taxi, travelling towards Mbombela, allegedly turned right at a red traffic light without stopping, colliding with the sedan before hitting the bus. Both the sedan and the bus were travelling towards White River.

Moeti Mmusi, spokesperson for the Department of Community Safety and Security Liaison, confirmed that an investigation is underway to determine the cause of the accident. He urged motorists to exercise caution to prevent road crashes.

post_title: Operation Shanela Nets 785 Suspects in Mpumalanga
post_content:
n

Mpumalanga police have reported a successful week of law enforcement, with 785 suspects arrested across the province between 8 and 14 September 2025. The arrests were made during Operation Shanela II, which ran alongside major events hosted in the province.

nnnn

The high-profile gatherings included the G20 Framework Working Group and Ministerial meeting held at Skukuza in the Kruger National Park, as well as the MTN8 Final Soccer Match in Mbombela. Despite the scale of these events, police ensured that routine operations continued across all three districts: Ehlanzeni, Gert Sibande and Nkangala.

The arrests were linked to a wide range of offences, including drug possession and dealing, murder, attempted murder, rape, robbery with aggravating circumstances, and driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Others were apprehended for possession of unlicensed firearms and ammunition, contraventions of the Immigration Act, and violations of the Liquor Act.

nnnn

Confiscated items during the operation included 10 firearms, 24 vehicles, a variety of drugs such as crystal meth, nyaope, cocaine and heroin, as well as 987 litres of liquor and 275 litres of suspected stolen fuel.

nnnn

The suspects are expected to appear in various courts across the province. Police confirmed that Operation Shanela II will continue this week, with activities including stop-and-searches, vehicle checkpoints, compliance inspections, liquor outlet visits, and patrols in public areas.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner of SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, praised the efforts of law enforcement officers and thanked law-abiding citizens for their cooperation.

“We remain committed to ensuring that communities are and feel safe. We also appreciate the support from our National Head Office and other law enforcement partners, especially during the G20 event,” he said.

post_title: Inflation Slows in August as Costs Ease
post_content:
n

Annual consumer price inflation slowed to 3.3 per cent in August, down from 3.5 per cent in July, Statistics South Africa reported on Wednesday.

nnnn

Patrick Kelly, Chief Director of Price Statistics, said softer food and fuel costs helped ease the overall inflation rate. “Annual inflation for food and non-alcoholic beverages slowed to 5.2 per cent, down from 5.7 per cent the previous month. Within this, several categories eased, including cereals, seafood, dairy products, fruit, nuts and vegetables,” he explained.

nnnn

Cereal products showed the biggest improvement, dropping from 2.1 per cent in July to 1.5 per cent in August. Kelly noted that some staples, such as hot cereals, white rice, bread and pasta, are cheaper now than a year ago. However, maize meal and samp remain expensive, while beef products continue to register high annual increases, although at their slowest pace since April.

nnnn

Fuel prices also dropped by 5.7 per cent year-on-year, further supporting the slowdown. Inflation remains within the Reserve Bank’s target range of 3 to 6 per cent.

nnnn

Dr Elna Moolman, Head of South Africa Macroeconomic Research at Standard Bank Group, said the outcome was slightly better than expected. She noted that the current benign inflation environment could, at some point, create room for the Reserve Bank to ease interest rates. However, she cautioned that the timing of such relief was uncertain, particularly as the Bank is now focused on anchoring inflation closer to the lower end rather than the midpoint of its 3 to 6 per cent target range.

nnnn

The Reserve Bank’s Monetary Policy Committee is expected to announce the repo rate on Thursday.

post_title: The people’s movement, the largest liberation movement in Africa is gathered at the #ANCCouncill
Ramaphosa Tells ANC to Learn from DA
post_content:
n

President Cyril Ramaphosa has sparked debate after urging ANC councillors to learn from the Democratic Alliance (DA) on improving local governance.

nnnn

Speaking to more than 4,000 ANC councillors in Johannesburg, Ramaphosa admitted that some municipalities were “going backwards instead of forwards” and encouraged leaders to study best practices from DA-run councils. “We must not be afraid to learn from them,” he said.

nnnn

Critics argue the remarks handed the DA a political advantage by openly praising its performance. Some ANC members fear his words could demoralise councillors and voters in poorly performing municipalities.

nnnn

Supporters, however, see the move as bold leadership. Analysts say Ramaphosa should be commended for frankness and accountability. “We cannot continue doing things the same way and expect different results,” he told councillors, calling for urgent reforms to improve service delivery.

nnnn

While the remarks have drawn mixed reactions, they could mark a turning point. If the ANC uses this moment to reform and rebuild trust, it may strengthen its position. If not, critics warn, the DA could benefit from what some have called a “silver platter” opportunity.

post_title: Limpopo Teacher Sentenced for Triple Murder
post_content:
n

A Limpopo teacher has been sentenced to 25 years in prison for the brutal 2022 murders of his estranged wife, her boyfriend, and her daughter.

nnnn

The High Court in Polokwane found 61-year-old Wilfred Moruthanyane Nkadimeng guilty on three counts of murder and one of attempted murder. Although he was handed a total of 83 years for his crimes, the sentences will run concurrently, meaning he will serve 25 years. The court also declared him unfit to possess a firearm.

nnnn

Nkadimeng pleaded not guilty, but the state proved its case. Evidence showed that on 26 September 2022, in Bothashoek, Nkadimeng fatally shot his estranged wife, Themia Clara Morema, following an argument. He then shot and killed her boyfriend, Tlou Solomon, who had arrived at the scene, before turning the gun on his stepdaughter, Nomasonto Morema. He also fired at a tenant but missed.

nnnn

Community members called the police, who arrived at around 11 pm to find three lifeless bodies. Nkadimeng had fled but was later traced and arrested.

n

n

After more than 40 years of waiting, Alexandra residents finally witnessed history being made today, 18 September 2025, when the Mpumalanga MEC for Health and the Bushbuckridge Local Municipality held the sod-turning ceremony for the long-promised Alexandra Clinic. The event drew loud cheers, tears of joy and sighs of relief from a community that has fought for this moment for decades.

nnnn

The MEC reminded residents that the project was pledged earlier this year during the State of the Province Address. “By next April, the building process will be done. We encourage community members to visit the clinic regularly,” she said, promising that this time the government would deliver.

nnnn

For many, the news was overwhelming. “I feel happy that what they are doing here, they are doing it for us as the Ward 5 community,” said local resident Mxolisi Khumalo. “Now we can finally walk to the clinic. We used to catch taxis to Oakley or Marite, which are both far from us.”

nnnn

Traditional leader Kgoshi LM Mokoena described the clinic as a dream finally becoming reality: “This community has been asking for a clinic for over 40 years. We will monitor the project to make sure nothing disturbs it.”

nnnn

Ward Councillor Sabelo Mkhabela confirmed that 16 local workers have already been employed on site. “Since the dawn of democracy, we have been longing for this clinic. We are happy that it is finally happening,” he said.

nnnn

Today’s sod-turning ceremony is more than a promise kept — it is a powerful symbol of resilience. For Alexandra, the clinic is not just a building; it is dignity restored, healthcare within reach, and hope brought home at last.

nnnn

post_title: Water Supply Interrupted After Infrastructure Vandalism
post_content:
n

The Bushbuckridge Local Municipality has announced a water supply interruption affecting communities serviced by the Hoxane Water Treatment Plant.

nnnn

The Hoxane plant relies on electricity for the production and purification of water. Due to the damage, water supply to several areas has been interrupted. Communities affected include Mkhuhlu township, Calcutta, Trust, Cork Thulani, Ronaldsey, Mkhuhlu F, Malubane, Goromane, Madras, Kildare and surrounding areas.

nnnnnnnn

Executive Mayor Cllr Lydia Moroane Zitha strongly condemned the act, describing it as “cowardly behaviour” that deprives residents of their constitutional right to clean drinking water. She called on law enforcement to ensure those responsible are held accountable, while urging communities to be vigilant and report any illegal activity in their neighbourhoods.

nnnn

“We appeal to community structures, especially in the affected areas, to assist in safeguarding water infrastructure,” said Cllr Zitha. “The municipality spends a significant amount to ensure residents have clean water. Vandalism not only costs money but also delays other essential projects.”

nnnn

The mayor urged residents to remain calm while Eskom works on repairs, assuring them that the water supply will be restored as soon as the infrastructure is fixed. She further appealed to the police to intensify their efforts in apprehending the perpetrators.

nnnn

The municipality reiterated its commitment to providing quality services and protecting state-of-the-art infrastructure from criminal damage.

post_title: Woman Arrested in Lydenburg with Human Tissues
post_content:
n

Residents of Mashishing, Lydenburg, have been left shocked after a local hospital worker was arrested for being in possession of human tissues.

nnnn

The 39-year-old suspect, identified as Rose Mnisi, was apprehended by the Lydenburg K9 Unit on Wednesday, 17 September, after police received a tip-off that she was allegedly looking for potential buyers for the tissues.

nnnn

According to police reports, Mnisi was stopped along Voortrekker Street while carrying a plastic bag. On inspection, officers discovered human placentas inside. She later confirmed that she works as a cleaner in the maternity ward of a local hospital.

nnnn

The suspect was arrested on the spot, and the contents of the bag were seized for forensic analysis. She has been charged with illegal possession of human tissues, and police say further charges may follow as the investigation continues.

nnnn

Mnisi appeared before the Mashishing District Court on Thursday, 18 September, where her case was postponed to 25 September for further investigation and her bail application. She remains in custody.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner of SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, welcomed the arrest.

nnnn

“This incident once again reflects deep moral decay in society. The Police will continue to work with communities in addressing crime,” he said.

nnnn

Police have commended community members for coming forward with information, stressing that cooperation between residents and law enforcement remains vital in tackling crime in the province.

nnnn

post_title: Police Nab Coal Theft Suspect in Witbank
post_content:
n

Members of the South African Police Service (SAPS) have arrested a 33-year-old man during Operation Vala Umgodi in Witbank, following a successful stop-and-search near a mine on Wednesday, 18 September 2025.

nnnn

The suspect was driving a Ford Ranger with Limpopo registration plates when officers stopped the vehicle. Upon inspection, police discovered 10 bags of coal. The man was unable to produce proof of ownership or explain how he had obtained the coal.

nnnn

The suspect was immediately arrested, and both the vehicle and the coal were confiscated. He is expected to appear before the Emalahleni Magistrate’s Court today, Friday, 19 September 2025.

nnnnnnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr.) Zeph Mkhwanazi, commended the officers involved. “We welcome the exceptional work done by our dedicated members under Operation Vala Umgodi,” he said.

nnnn

Operation Vala Umgodi is an ongoing initiative targeting illegal mining and related criminal activities in the province. Police have urged the public to continue providing tip-offs, assuring communities that such information helps in curbing crime and protecting natural resources.

post_title: Twelve Suspects Caught in Acornhoek Raid
post_content:
n

Police in Mpumalanga have arrested twelve suspects during Operation Shanela in Acornhoek on Thursday, 18 September 2025. The suspects, aged between 17 and 33, were found without valid documentation to be in South Africa.

According to the South African Police Service (SAPS), the suspects were taken into custody and are expected to appear before the Acornhoek Magistrate’s Court today, Friday, 19 September 2025. They face charges under the Immigration Act.

In addition to the arrests, six other individuals were issued fines for various offences. These included failure to display a licence disc, driving without a valid driver’s licence, contravening the Road Traffic Act, and public drinking.

Police detectives are working closely with the Department of Home Affairs to verify the legal status of the arrested suspects.

post_title: Bushbuckridge Voices Boil Over at TLP
post_content:
n

Premier fires back at R10bn demand as residents demand urgent action

nnnn

The final day of the Taking Legislature to the People (TLP) programme at Ximungwe Sports Ground in Bushbuckridge ended in fiery exchanges, bold promises, and raw community frustrations. For a week, residents poured out their anger over collapsing roads, dry taps, housing backlogs, and villages left in the dark — and politicians were forced to face the heat.

nnnn

Members of the Mpumalanga Legislature used the platform to highlight what they view as critical shortcomings in Bushbuckridge. The MK party accused the ANC-led government of “playing with people’s lives” and demanded urgent steps to improve service delivery. “The people of Hluvukani and Manyeleti have waited too long. Their lives must change now,” the party stressed.

nnnn

The EFF called for a staggering R10 billion to be set aside exclusively for Bushbuckridge to address unemployment and service delivery failures. The DA, on the other hand, demanded an urgent investigation into why many communities remain excluded from electrification projects. The party proposed a 21-day deadline for a preliminary report with practical recommendations to ensure schools, clinics and households receive access to electricity without further delays.

nnnnnnnn

In his closing address, Mpumalanga Premier Mandla Ndlovu acknowledged residents’ frustrations but dismissed the EFF’s proposal as unrealistic. He said:

nnnn

“The budget of the province is 67, a billion. So we don’t have, for infrastructure, in the program, the budget is not even 10 billion. So they know that it is not possible. I wish I can be like them. If you are not in government, you can even promise people to build one million houses in the 1st 5 years. That’s what we did. I don’t understand why they decided to lie, knowing that they are lying, but they continue to lie. So it is not right. Ourselves, we should not be ambitious. We must tell people what we can be able to meet. So don’t come with ambitious program that we will not be able to make.”

nnnn

Premier Ndlovu reassured communities that access to water, roads, and electricity remains a government priority. He confirmed that household connections are underway, with newly established stands also scheduled to be connected. On unemployment, he pointed to local manufacturing projects such as GNG Welding, which has already created 14 jobs, as a model for sustainable growth.

nnnn

Bushbuckridge by Numbers

nnnn

· 11.2% of households lack running water

nnnn

· 28,000 houses are urgently needed

nnnn

· 1,500 toilets budgeted for Bushbuckridge South

nnnn

· 97 graveyards without fencing

nnnn

· 1.9% of residents live in informal settlements

nnnn

As the dust settled at Ximungwe, one reality remained: Bushbuckridge’s 38 wards demand more than political theatre. The TLP has ended, but for residents, the real struggle for services, jobs, and dignity continues.

Five suspects, aged between 29 and 43, are set to appear before the Balfour Magistrate’s Court today, Friday, 19 September 2025, following their arrest in Greylingstad earlier this week.

According to police reports, officers were conducting patrols along the R23 Road in the early hours of Wednesday, 17 September 2025, when they spotted a suspicious vehicle carrying a heavy load. post_title: Poacher Shot During Kruger Rangers’ Bold Pursuit
post_content:
n

A dramatic confrontation in the Crocodile Bridge section of Kruger National Park has left a suspected poacher injured and in custody, while his accomplice remains at large. The incident, which took place on Thursday evening, 18 September 2025, highlights ongoing tensions between wildlife protection efforts and illegal hunting activity. 

nnnn

According to Mpumalanga police, field rangers first discovered human footprints during a routine patrol around 07:30 that morning. They followed the tracks toward the park’s southern boundary as part of a follow-up operation. 

nnnn

At approximately 20:00, two armed suspects were spotted moving toward the rangers. When ordered to stop, they attempted to flee and scaled a nearby fence. During the pursuit, one suspect allegedly raised a rifle at the rangers, prompting them to open fire in self-defence. Both made it over the fence. One dropped his weapon and collapsed near a sugarcane field; the other fled into the fields and has not yet been found. 

nnnn

The detained 32-year-old suspect was found with a backpack containing two rhino horns and a knife. He failed to produce any permits for his presence in the park or for the firearm. He is facing charges including trespassing, illegal hunting, possession of an unlicensed firearm, and possession of a dangerous weapon. After receiving medical treatment, he will appear in the Masoyi Periodical Court once fit. 

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi warned that anyone threatening field rangers or endangered wildlife will face legal consequences. 

nnnn

Police are appealing for the public’s assistance in locating the fugitive suspect. Anyone with information is urged to contact Detective Constable Shegofatso Moreku on 082 077 5826, or to use Crime Stop (08600 10111) or the MySAPS App.

post_title: Crystal Meth Lab Busted, Five Foreigners Arrested
post_content:
n

Police in Mpumalanga have scored a major victory in the fight against drug trafficking after dismantling a crystal methamphetamine laboratory worth an estimated R350 million in Volksrust. The bust occurred on Friday, 19 September 2025, under Operation Shanela 2, officials confirmed. 

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi praised the team for their rapid response following a tip-off about suspicious activity at a farm in Oudehoutkloof, Volksrust, notably a strange chemical smell. 

nnnn

When officers arrived, the gates were locked, and several suspects attempted to flee on foot. However, five foreign nationals—reportedly from a North American country—were caught immediately. Two others, believed to be from West African nations, managed to escape into nearby bushes. 

nnnn

A search of the premises uncovered large quantities of precursor chemicals for drug manufacturing, specialised equipment, and crystal meth hidden in lunch boxes and buckets stored in freezers. Officials also found a pellet gun loaded with blanks, and three live 9mm rounds were recovered from the South African farm caretaker. 

nnnnnnnn

The arrested suspects are expected to face charges under the Drugs and Drug Trafficking Act, the Immigration Act, and, in the caretaker’s case, for ammunition possession. The scene has been handed over to the Hawks after forensic teams processed the evidence. 

nnnn

Major General Mkhwanazi described the operation as proof of the power of intelligence-driven policing and community cooperation. He urged residents to continue reporting suspicious activity, saying the police will “stop at nothing in our quest to collapse the illicit drug trade.”

post_title: A Leopard Emerging from a grassy hideout.
ActionSA Raises Alarm Over Road Project Delays
post_content:
n

ActionSA has warned that the R114 million upgrade of the D4382 road between Belfast and Justicia is unlikely to meet its extended January 2026 deadline.

nnnn

The warning follows findings made during an oversight visit by the Portfolio Committee on Public Works, joined by the Department of Public Works and other stakeholders, as part of the Taking the Legislature to the People programme.

nnnn

The visit revealed that work on the 13.6km project has been repeatedly halted due to the non-payment of contractors. Shockingly, no activity was taking place even during the oversight inspection. The project, originally scheduled for completion in November 2025, has already been pushed back to 23 January 2026.

nnnn

Despite the initial budget of R114 million, costs have now risen to R128 million. ActionSA expressed concern that variation orders already account for 14% of the total. Treasury regulations require a re-tender if this figure reaches 20%, which could further delay completion and increase costs.

nnnn

With the rainy season approaching, the partially dug road risks turning into a “mud pool,” leaving local households in danger as deep trenches line their gates. Residents say the poor progress has left them living with daily hazards and restricted mobility.

nnnn

ActionSA also questioned reports of disputes between labourers and the Department over pay rates, noting that such issues should have been settled once the tender was awarded. The party has called for stronger communication between the Department, contractors, and communities to prevent further disruptions.

nnnn

“The non-payment of contractors is indefensible. A project of this magnitude cannot be abandoned mid-way,” said ActionSA MPL Thoko Mashiane. “The community deserves better than half-dug roads, empty promises, and wasted millions.”

nnnn

ActionSA added that failure to complete the road project will worsen the suffering of residents and stand as further proof of weak project management and poor accountability within the Department of Public Works.

nnnn

post_title: Court Grants Parents Go-Ahead in SANParks Case
post_content:
n

South African National Parks (SANParks) has confirmed that it is studying the Mpumalanga High Court’s recent ruling concerning a 2019 tragedy in which a 30-month-old toddler was killed by a leopard at the Malelane Technical Services Living Quarters in the Kruger National Park.

nnnn

In its media statement issued on Friday, 19 September 2025, SANParks said:

nnnn

“As a state entity, we are committed to comply with findings of our courts. In addition, we are also studying the court’s judgment for a more in-depth understanding of the findings as set out by Acting Judge Zodwa Gumede.”

nnnn

The court dismissed SANParks’ special plea that the incident should be treated under the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act (COIDA). The organisation had argued that the death constituted an occupational injury since the child’s father, an employee, was required to reside in the Park and was aware of the risks posed by wild animals.

nnnn

Acting Judge Gumede disagreed, ruling that COIDA was not applicable. She emphasised that the death of a child in such circumstances could not reasonably have been foreseen, and the family therefore has the right to pursue a damages claim against SANParks.

nnnn

The parents are seeking compensation for funeral expenses, pain and suffering, and emotional trauma.

nnnn

According to the father, the toddler was playing with his mother’s phone when he wandered behind him one evening. A leopard reportedly climbed a tree near the fence, leapt into the yard, and seized the child. Despite the father’s attempts to intervene, the leopard tried to drag the child over the fence before dropping him and fleeing into the bush.

nnnn

The child was rushed to Shongwe Hospital but was declared dead on arrival.

nnnn

At the time, SANParks rangers conducted a search for the animal, resulting in two leopards being destroyed in the immediate vicinity of the quarters.

nnnn

SANParks has acknowledged the sensitivity of the case. In its official statement, it said:

nnnn

“Considering the sensitivity of the issue as well as out of respect for the family, SANParks will not be providing further commentary on the matter.”

Selela confirmed that the cause of the fire is still under investigation.

post_title: You deserve the truth, not AI’s interpretation of it
post_content:
n

We all want to understand the world around us. Whether it’s the war in Gaza, government policy on healthcare, or something as ordinary as changes to a bus route, people deserve accurate information they can trust.

nnnn

Yet, in today’s digital environment, we are forced to question what is real and what is generated by artificial intelligence. AI-produced content is so convincing that it risks eroding the very notion of truth. This mistrust fuels conspiracy theories, division, and disengagement from democracy.

nnnn

On this World News Day, we want to emphasise that the public is entitled to facts gathered, checked, and shared by professional journalists. But the technology companies creating AI systems are failing to meet their responsibility to the truth.

nnnn

Research by the BBC this year found that half of AI-generated responses to news-related questions contained significant errors or omissions. These tools produced distorted facts, fabricated quotes, and decontextualised reporting without crediting the original source.

nnnn

This is not harmless. It goes far beyond minor mistakes in recipes or holiday tips. A society without a common understanding of truth cannot make informed decisions, while individuals relying on distorted journalism risk being misled. The internet is already crowded with fake content designed to deceive, attract clicks, and serve vested interests. AI-generated material is often recycled from journalists’ work, stripped of context, and redistributed without permission or payment.

nnnn

This subtle manipulation is more dangerous than obvious deepfakes because it appears plausible. It undermines trust in journalism at a time when local, regional, and independent media are already facing significant challenges.

n

n

Whether you are ready or not, the Rapture is near, according to South African preacher Joshua Mhlakela.

nnnn

Mhlakela’s claims about the return of Jesus Christ have made headlines worldwide, attracting both scepticism and belief.

nnnn

In a video shared on the Cettwinz TV YouTube channel, Mhlakela declared that Jesus will return to Earth on 23 and 24 September 2025. Citing the Book of Revelation, he said this would mark Judgement Day.

nnnn

“The Rapture is upon us. Whether you are ready or not,” Mhlakela proclaimed. “I saw Jesus sitting on His throne, and I could hear Him very loud and clear saying, ‘I am coming soon’.”

nnnn

He added that Jesus told him: “On the 23rd and 24th of September 2025, I will come back to the Earth.” According to Mhlakela, the event will be announced by the Feast of Trumpets, signalling both the Rapture and Judgement Day.

nnnn

The preacher is not alone in his predictions. Danie Botha, a South African singer-turned-preacher, has echoed similar claims, saying the Holy Spirit revealed the message to him.

nnnn

In one of his YouTube sermons, Botha told followers: “Our departure point to the next destination is here. We are in the last days. After a service that morning, I walked into my house and switched on the TV. Before me appeared in big golden letters: Flight 923… You must be ready to depart.”

nnnn

Both Mhlakela and Botha continue to use online platforms to share their message, insisting that believers should prepare for what they describe as the final days.

post_title: School roof blew out by storm Photo Pieenar News.
Storm-Stricken Lowveld Communities Receive Urgent Relief

Communities across the Lowveld are still reeling from the severe storm that struck on Sunday, 14 September, leaving widespread damage in Nkomazi, Mbombela and Bushbuckridge. The Mpumalanga Provincial Government has prioritised relief efforts to support those affected.

nnnn

Officials reported that more than 30 homes, schools, community halls and health facilities in Sikhwahlane, Mangweni, Madadeni and Buffelsspruit were damaged when roofs were blown off during the storm. While no fatalities occurred, several residents sustained minor injuries.

nnnn

The Department of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs (CoGTA) is leading Joint Operations Committees in the affected municipalities to coordinate relief. Efforts include restoring essential services and providing urgent community support.

nnnn

Special focus has been placed on ensuring schools resume normal operations. The Provincial Government confirmed that steps are being taken to ensure learners can sit for their year-end examinations without disruption.

nnnn

In a call for unity, the government urged residents to cooperate with relief teams and stakeholders working on the ground. “Our goal is to restore normalcy as quickly as possible,” officials said.

For urgent assistance or to report needs, residents may contact Mr Freddy Ngobe of CoGTA at 082 859 4630 or Mr Gerald Sambo of the Department of Education at 081 526 7802.

post_title: Saps fake documents. Picture Supplied Sapps
SAPS Issues Warning Over Vishing Scam
post_content:
n

The South African Police Service (SAPS) has warned the public about a growing vishing scam in which criminals hijack the police name, insignia, and the identities of senior officers to defraud unsuspecting citizens.

nnnn

According to the police, fraudsters distribute fake letters, often circulated through WhatsApp, bearing the SAPS logo and the names of real officers or stations to appear authentic. “In some cases, the perpetrators even invent non-existent police stations in their letters. The SAPS can confirm that no police station exists in Green Point, Cape Town,” a statement noted.

nnnn

The scam also involves threatening phone calls from impostors pretending to be police officials. Victims are falsely told that a criminal case has been opened against them, followed by demands for money to make it “disappear.”

nnnn

SAPS has distanced itself from these practices, stressing that it will never demand payment to cancel a case, nor will it communicate with the public via WhatsApp or video calls.

nnnn

Authorities urged the public to remain vigilant and follow safety measures:

nnnn
    n
  • Do not respond to suspicious calls, letters or messages.
    • nnnn
  • Never share personal or banking details.
    • nnnn
  • Do not pay money to anyone claiming to be a police officer.
    • n
nnnn

The police appealed to communities to assist in tracing those behind the scam. Anyone with information is encouraged to contact their nearest police station, call Crime Stop on 08600 10111, or submit an anonymous tip-off via the MySAPS App.

n

post_title: Operation Shanela Nets 253 Suspects in Mpumalanga
post_content:
n

Mpumalanga police have arrested 253 suspects during a province-wide high-density operation aimed at clamping down on crime. Operation Shanela II, which ran from 17 to 21 September, focused on hotspots and high-risk areas across the province.

nnnn

The arrests were made for a range of offences, including assault, drug-related crimes and driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

nnnn

During the five-day campaign, police conducted 93 separate operations, which included 16 roadblocks, 2 823 vehicle searches, 6 756 person searches, 3 835 patrols, and 1 188 stop-and-searches.

nnnn

The breakdown of arrests showed 105 assault cases, 38 drug-related cases, and 25 drivers caught under the influence. A total of 217 J534 notices were issued, and seven traffic fines were recorded.

nnnn

Police also confiscated 74,27 kg of drugs, uncovered a drug laboratory worth an estimated R350 million, seized 12 illegal firearms, and removed more than 1 200 litres of liquor.

nnnn

A total of 776 compliance inspections were carried out at liquor outlets, firearm dealers and second-hand goods stores.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, praised the coordinated effort:
“These operations are part of our sustained effort to root out criminal activities. The public must be aware that SAPS members are deployed across the province — criminals will have nowhere to hide.”

nnnn

He further commended the cooperation of private security, community members and other stakeholders, saying their tip-offs remain vital in the fight against crime.

post_title: Police launch manhunt after caretaker murder
post_content:
n

Police in Limpopo have launched a manhunt for suspects following a violent house robbery and the brutal murder of a 56-year-old caretaker in a Polokwane residential area.

nnnn

According to authorities, the caretaker was last seen alive on Friday by a co-worker. His body was discovered by the landlord yesterday morning.

nnnn

Upon arrival, the landlord noticed the gate slightly open and the front door ajar. Inside, he found the house ransacked and the caretaker lying in a pool of blood.

nnnn

“Paramedics confirmed him dead at the scene. The victim had been tied up and stabbed multiple times,” said Limpopo police spokesperson, Hlulani Mashaba.

nnnn

He described the killing as deeply unsettling for the community, stressing that it was not only a robbery but also a cruel act of violence.

nnnn

Police believe the motive was house robbery, but the suspects remain unknown. Investigations are under way, and community members are urged to assist with any information that could help track down the perpetrators.

post_title: NUMSA Slams Delays in Electricity Tariff Crisis
post_content:
n

The National Union of Metalworkers of South Africa (NUMSA) has accused the government of moving too slowly in resolving the electricity tariff crisis that is crippling the ferrochrome industry, warning of possible mass action if urgent steps are not taken.

nnnn

The criticism comes after a meeting between Electricity Minister Kgosientso Ramokgopa, senior Eskom executives, and CEOs from Glencore, Samancor, and Almar Investment, where proposals for a special electricity tariff to reopen mothballed smelters were discussed.

nnnn

NUMSA expressed concern that, despite the discussions being described as promising, companies have not withdrawn retrenchment notices issued under Section 189A. Job losses are continuing, with more than 2,000 workers already retrenched in the first wave.

nnnn

The union blames government delays, pointing out that Cabinet had approved interventions months ago. NUMSA believes that Eskom and the Minister’s inaction have intensified the jobs crisis, creating a “bloodbath” in the sector.

nnnn

It further highlighted that South African ferrochrome producers pay about 12 US cents per kilowatt hour, while producers in China pay less than 6 cents. This price gap is seen as a major factor driving smelting operations offshore and threatening local jobs.

nnnn

The union has called for bold measures, including a moratorium on retrenchments, import restrictions on products undermining local producers, and a ban on chrome ore and manganese exports. It argues that such a ban would force international markets to invest in local smelting facilities, thereby creating employment.

nnnn

NUMSA also restated its long-standing position that Eskom must remain a strategic state-owned entity to provide affordable electricity for both industry and communities. Unless the government acts swiftly, the union has warned that rolling mass action by its members will be unavoidable.

n

The Kruger National Park (KNP) experienced record-breaking attendance on National Heritage Day, which coincided with the week-long South African National Parks (SANParks) Week. Thousands of visitors flocked to the park to enjoy its world-renowned wildlife and landscapes.

nnnn

post_title: Ramaphosa Urges Renewal of AGOA Trade Deal
post_content:
n

President Cyril Ramaphosa has called on the United States to renew the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), warning that its expiry later this month could severely damage South Africa’s economy and undo decades of progress in US–Africa trade.

nnnn

Speaking at the South Africa–US Trade and Investment Dialogue in New York, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, Ramaphosa described AGOA as the cornerstone of trade relations for nearly 25 years.

nnnn

“In South Africa, it has supported jobs from auto assembly plants to farms to high-tech manufacturing hubs. Its expiry would not only undermine those gains but also weaken links to the Generalised System of Preferences, which have been critical to many of our exporters,” he said.

nnnn

Ramaphosa appealed for support in advocating renewal, stressing that predictable, preferential access to the US market benefits both countries. He acknowledged recent trade tensions, but emphasised the need for resolution, noting that tariffs impact industries and communities on both sides.

nnnn

Highlighting the scale of American investment, Ramaphosa said the US is a top source of foreign direct investment in South Africa, supporting hundreds of thousands of jobs. More than 600 American companies operate locally across various industries, including aerospace, mining, energy, consumer goods, and finance.

nnnn

He also noted that South African firms have established a strong presence in the US across various sectors, including chemicals, financial services, mining, hospitality, and food products, serving as ambassadors of the country’s entrepreneurial spirit.

nnnn

Looking ahead, Ramaphosa positioned South Africa as a strategic entry point into Africa’s 1.4-billion-strong market. “Our goal is simple: to sustain and expand trade flows, keep our companies competitive, and ensure that consumers and workers in both countries benefit from our partnership,” he said.

nnnnnnnn

The theme of the conference is Driving Investment for a Sustainable and Inclusive Economy. The MEC confirmed that government would showcase an “investment book” of key projects covering mining, renewable energy, tourism, and agro-processing.

The MEC also revealed that the province aims to secure at least R50 billion in investment pledges, with international partners and ambassadors invited. “Together with the private sector, we will cultivate foresight to anticipate challenges and unlock opportunities,” she said.

post_title: Anthrax Cases Reported in Kruger Park
post_content:
n

South African National Parks (SANParks) has confirmed localised anthrax cases in the Kruger National Park (KNP), assuring visitors there is no cause for alarm.

nnnn

According to SANParks, anthrax is endemic to the region and sporadic cases are recorded annually, especially in the northern areas. This year, kudu and buffalo have been most affected, which officials describe as typical and not a threat to biodiversity or species survival.

nnnn

Visitors remain safe as anthrax requires direct contact to spread. SANParks reminded the public that tourists are not permitted to leave vehicles outside designated areas and that guided activities are conducted by trained professionals. Tourists are also urged not to approach or touch dead animals, a rule already in place.

nnnn

Veterinary teams are monitoring the situation closely and will remove or treat carcasses if they pose a risk. SANParks has also notified the Department of Agriculture, Land Reform and Rural Development, alongside State Veterinary authorities.

nnnn

Officials expect the outbreak to subside with the first rains, following the disease’s natural cycle. SANParks emphasised that tourism activities continue as normal and the park remains safe for all visitors.

post_title: Twelve Dead in Limpopo Road Collision
post_content:

Limpopo Premier Dr Phophi Ramathuba has expressed deep sorrow following a tragic accident involving two trucks and a minibus taxi, which claimed the lives of 12 people, including a young girl.

nnnn

Initial reports suggested that 13 people had died in the crash. The horrific collision occurred on the R81 in Ga-Sekgopo, Capricorn District, on Sunday afternoon.

Authorities confirmed that all those who perished were passengers and the driver of the taxi, which had been transporting congregants from a church service in Solomondale back to their homes in Giyani.

While reports suggest that the taxi was crushed between the two trucks, officials are still investigating the exact cause of the accident.

Ramathuba will be joined by the MEC for Transport and Community Safety, Violet Mathye, and the MEC for Health, Dieketseng Mashego.

The Department of Transport and Community Safety will provide regular updates. The R81 was reopened in the early hours of Monday morning.

nnnn

“The provincial government stands in solidarity with the families during this difficult time and is committed to providing them with the necessary support. We urge all road users to exercise caution and adhere to safety regulations,” Muavha added.

post_title: Child Marriages Still Haunt Our Communities
post_content:
n

Child marriages, often hidden behind the traditional practice of ukuthwala, continue to haunt certain communities in the Eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal. While defenders sometimes argue that it is part of cultural heritage, the reality is that today it frequently results in the forced union of young girls under the age of 18 — a practice that is both unlawful and devastating to those affected.

nnnn

The impact reaches far beyond the individual child. Girls are pulled out of school, stripping them of the opportunity to learn, grow and achieve independence. Once married off, many are burdened with early pregnancies, exposing them to serious health complications and increasing the likelihood of maternal and infant mortality. Emotionally, these girls often live with fear, trauma and feelings of powerlessness, leaving invisible wounds that linger well into adulthood.

nnnn

Communities, too, carry the weight of these practices. When children are denied education and autonomy, cycles of poverty and inequality are reinforced. Families lose daughters who could have become doctors, teachers, entrepreneurs or leaders, instead seeing them trapped in circumstances that rob them of their potential. This undermines development and weakens the social fabric that should hold communities together.

nnnn

Ending child marriage is not only a legal necessity but also a moral responsibility. Protecting children starts at home, within families, and extends to neighbours, schools, faith groups and traditional leaders. Speaking out, raising awareness, and challenging harmful traditions can create safer environments where every child has the freedom to dream and to pursue a better future.

nnnn

A strong and united stance against child marriage ensures healthier, more resilient communities — and a brighter tomorrow for South Africa’s children.

n

post_title: Sars Urges Taxpayers to Pay Early
post_content:
n

The South African Revenue Service (SARS) has called on taxpayers to settle outstanding amounts promptly to avoid penalties, interest and delays.

nnnn

In a statement, Sars said it “encourages all taxpayers who are due to make payments to do so by the earliest available date to avoid unnecessary delays, penalties and interests for late payment.”

nnnn

The agency noted that early compliance helps reduce the risk of enforcement action and supports the smooth running of the tax system. With September marking the halfway point of the financial year, SARS thanked those who have already met their obligations.

Payments can be made via eFiling, electronic funds transfer (EFT) or at a bank. Sars assured the public these platforms are “robust, secure and user-friendly,” in line with international standards.

Meanwhile, Sars and the Office of the Tax Ombud (OTO) raised concerns over cybercriminals hijacking eFiling profiles, though they stressed a draft OTO report will only be released on 1 October 2025.

post_title: Three Illegal Immigrants Arrested In Pilgrim’s Rest
post_content:
n

Three illegal immigrants appeared in the Graskop Magistrate’s Court on Monday, 29 September, after being arrested during an Operation Vala Umgodi clampdown in the Pilgrim’s Rest area the previous day.

nnnn

The suspects, identified as Carlos Masinga (51), Machikiyana Gauteng (21) and Kabelo Tau (36), were detained by the Combat and Proactive team while police conducted disruptive operations at Majaks. They were found without valid documentation to be in South Africa.

Illicit mining equipment, including phendukas, steel balls, generators, industrial motors and gas cylinders, was also seized during the operation.

nnnn

Spokesperson Daphne Mokoena confirmed on Monday that the milestone forms part of Eskom’s generation recovery plan and also marks the end of construction at South Africa’s two supercritical coal-fired stations, Medupi and Kusile.

nnnn

“Commercial operation indicates that the unit has passed all testing and optimisation phases and is now fully integrated into Eskom’s fleet. nnnn

She added that Unit 6’s output will now be included in Eskom’s Energy Availability Factor, boosting overall performance metrics. The unit contributes 800MW to the grid, completing Eskom’s twelve-unit mega-project.

nnnn

“This achievement is a significant step towards our strategic goal of adding 2 500MW of new capacity by March. We extend our gratitude to employees and contractors whose perseverance made this possible,” said Eskom Group Executive for Generation, Bheki Nxumalo.

Eskom Chief Executive Dan Marokane added that both Medupi and Kusile will remain central to the country’s power supply for decades. “These stations are designed to operate for around 50 years. post_title: Four Suspects Remain in Custody After Arrest in Elukwatini
post_content:
n

Four men appeared at the Albert Luthuli Magistrate’s Court on Monday, 29 September, following their arrest during a police operation in Elukwatini.

nnnn

The suspects, aged between 23 and 30, were apprehended on Saturday, 27 September, during Operation Vala Umgodi. Police said the men were found without valid documentation and have been charged under the Immigration Act of South Africa. Illicit mining equipment was also confiscated at the scene.

post_title: Court Halts Payout of Mabuza's R44m Pension
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga High Court in has barred Alexander Forbes from releasing the late former Deputy President David Mabuza’s R44-million pension to his widow, Patience Mnisi, until the full dispute over his estate is resolved.

nnnn

Judge Johannes Roelofse granted interim relief to Mabuza’s daughter, Tamara Silinda, on Tuesday, ordering that the funds be preserved until all dependents are identified and considered. At issue is whether Mnisi, nominated as the sole beneficiary on a living annuity form, is entitled to the entire sum, or whether the money should be distributed among Mabuza’s children and dependents under the Pension Funds Act.

nnnn

Roelofse emphasised that the order was necessary to prevent irreparable harm. “If the money leaves the court today, it will immediately be transferred to the first respondent. Then the money is gone,” he said, directing Alexander Forbes to keep the funds in an interest-bearing account.

nnnn

The court also approved interim maintenance, including R127,990 per year in tuition and R40,000 per month in living expenses for Silinda, a University of Cape Town student.

nnnn

Roelofse questioned Alexander Forbes’ role in handling the pension, noting gaps in its affidavit, and ordered the company to cover legal costs. He urged the Mabuza family to reconcile, warning that legal disputes often leave “scars between family members that never heal.”

nnnn

Mabuza, a former deputy president and Mpumalanga premier, died in July at 63 after a short illness. The matter, referred to as Part B, will return to court after 15 October 2025, when a decision on the pension’s final distribution will be made.

post_title: Auditor General Flags Serious Flaws at Higher Education Department
Audit Flags Serious Higher Education Flaws
post_content:
n

Auditor-General (A-G) Tsakani Maluleke has raised serious concerns about the accuracy of performance reporting at the Department of Higher Education and Training in its 2024/25 annual report.

nnnn

Maluleke’s audit uncovered material misstatements in several areas, including planning, policy and strategy, Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), skills development, and Community Education and Training. She reported that not all misstatements were corrected, despite assurances from management.

nnnn

This stands in contrast to the department’s head, Nkosinathi Sishi, who confirmed in the annual report that the information disclosed was consistent, complete, and accurate. “In my opinion, the annual report fairly reflects the operations, performance, human resources information, and financial affairs of the department for the financial year ended 31 March 2025,” Sishi stated.

nnnn

However, Maluleke’s audit found otherwise. For example, the department claimed to have completed three TVET campuses, meeting its annual target, but the audit evidence did not support this. The A-G estimated the achievement to be materially less than reported. Similarly, the department reported delivering 2,471 student beds against a target of 5,000, yet adequate evidence to verify this was missing.

nnnn

The report also questioned figures on apprenticeships, internships, and work-integrated learning, as well as the number of learners enrolled in engineering and trade-related courses at TVET colleges. A total of 34,324 students were reported against a target of 33,000, but audit evidence suggested the figure was higher than stated.

nnnn

On skills development, Maluleke said the reported achievements did not match actual results and were likely far less than presented. She attributed the shortcomings to a lack of adequate controls in performance reporting and monitoring.

nnnn

“The processes in place for the collection and review of performance information and underlying data were ineffective. The department did not have a proper records management system to maintain evidence supporting reported achievements,” Maluleke said.

nnnn

The Auditor-General further noted that the department’s action plan failed to address deficiencies, resulting in repeat findings.

nnnn

Audit committee chairperson Trevor Boltman acknowledged the shortcomings, saying that while steps had been taken to respond to previous issues, they were ineffective. He confirmed that the committee had advised management to develop a stronger plan to address the root causes highlighted in Maluleke’s findings.

n

n

Eskom has announced a profit before tax of R23.9 billion for the 2025 financial year, marking its first return to profitability in eight years.

nnnn

The achievement signals a dramatic turnaround for the state-owned power utility, which only a few years ago was at the centre of a load shedding crisis that severely disrupted South Africa’s economy.

nnnn

Eskom Group Chief Executive, Dan Marokane, said the profit will be reinvested into the organisation.

nnnn

“The focused and ongoing efforts of Eskom’s 42 000 employees in delivering the turnaround strategy have produced tangible results. We are reinvesting profits back into national assets. Over the next five years, we will invest more than R320 billion in sustaining and expanding infrastructure for the long-term benefit of the nation,” Marokane said.

nnnn

He added that the utility is accelerating cost reviews and restructuring in line with tariff frameworks set by the National Energy Regulator of South Africa (NERSA), while driving efficiencies to make electricity more affordable.

nnnn

According to Marokane, the country’s economy lost R2.8 trillion to load shedding in 2023, but this dropped by 83% to R481 billion in 2024.

nnnn

Key performance highlights

nnnn
    n
  • Profit before tax of R23.9 billion, supported by a stronger margin and lower fuel costs.
    • nnnn
  • Diesel savings of R16.3 billion due to improved coal plant reliability and reduced reliance on Open-Cycle Gas Turbines.
    • nnnn
  • Load shedding fell sharply to just 175 hours in 2025, compared to 6 367 hours in 2024.
    • nnnn
  • Electricity was supplied on 96% of days in the reporting year.
    • nnnn
  • A normalised profit of R11.9 billion after adjusting for a once-off fuel levy rebate.
    • n
nnnn

Eskom board chairperson, Mteto Nyati, said the company has stabilised significantly.

nnnn

“Eskom is increasingly a sustainable, investable company ready to compete in a liberalised market, very different from the crisis we inherited in 2022. Stronger systems and smarter technology are protecting revenue and ensuring reliable electricity for all South Africans,” Nyati said.

nnnn

The power utility presented its annual results at Megawatt Park on Tuesday, affirming that the lights are staying on for longer — and with profits finally back on the balance sheet.

post_title: Alexforbes Responds to Mabuza Pension Ruling
post_content:
n

Alexforbes has issued a statement following the interim order delivered by the Mpumalanga High Court on Tuesday in the ongoing dispute over the late former deputy president David Mabuza’s R44-million living annuity.

nnnn

The case, brought by Emunah Silinda and Tamara Silinda, contests how the pension benefits should be distributed. The High Court issued an interim order preventing Alexforbes from paying any funds to Mabuza’s widow, Patience Mnisi, pending finalisation of Part B of the application, which will determine the allocation of the pension among all dependents.

nnnn

In its response, Alexforbes said it respected the ruling but would review its legal options, particularly the cost order imposed against it, which the company described as “unjustified.” The firm stressed that it had complied fully with the court’s directions.

nnnn

Alexforbes also clarified the distinction between pension funds and living annuities. It explained that Mabuza had transferred his pension from the Political Office-Bearers Pension Fund to a living annuity in early 2023. Unlike pension funds, which are regulated under Section 37C of the Pension Funds Act, living annuities fall under the Long-Term Insurance Act and the Income Tax Act.

nnnn

According to Alexforbes, death benefits in a retirement fund require trustees to distribute them fairly among dependents and nominees, whereas living annuities are paid strictly according to the policyholder’s beneficiary nomination form and do not form part of the deceased’s estate.

nnnn

The company emphasised that “the difference is critical,” as trustees’ discretion under Section 37C can delay payments and may not align with a member’s stated wishes.

nnnn

Judge Johannes Roelofse instructed that the parties return to the registrar by 15 October to manage the next stage of proceedings.

post_title: Limpopo Legislature Faces R1.8m Travel Scandal
post_content:
n

The Secretary of the Limpopo Legislature, Timothy Maake, is under fire after taxpayers were billed R1.8 million for cancelled travel bookings linked to his insistence on being addressed as “Dr” on airline tickets.

nnnn

The costs reportedly stemmed from multiple flight cancellations, re-bookings, and unused accommodation for a delegation travelling to a Commonwealth Parliamentary Association event in Gambia. Delays stretched the journey to almost 39 hours, creating major logistical challenges for delegates.

nnnn

According to reports, three bookings for flights and accommodation were cancelled after Qatar Airways refused to include the “Dr” title on tickets. The repeated cancellations and re-issues drove costs up to R1.8 million.

nnnn

nnnn

nnnn

The Limpopo Legislature, however, defended its secretary, saying he had the right to attend the event and to use his academic title.

nnnn

Opposition parties have demanded a full breakdown of the costs, questioning who authorised the bookings and why cancellation fees were so high. They have also urged the Auditor-General or the Public Protector to investigate the matter.

nnnn

Past audits have already flagged Limpopo departments for irregular travel and catering expenses, fuelling concerns about weak controls on public spending.

n

Am I the only one who thought of anti-apartheid activist Dulcie September when news broke that Ambassador Nathi Mthethwa had died in Paris? South Africans have long known that public figures do not simply fall to their deaths from the 22nd floor of a hotel without deeper truths lurking beneath official explanations.

nnnn

The circumstances surrounding Mthethwa’s death are troubling. The Hyatt Regency Paris Étoile, where he allegedly fell, is only 3.5 kilometres from the South African Embassy, where he had an official residence. Why was the Ambassador at the hotel at all? Who was he meeting that he could not meet at the embassy or his residence? These are questions his diary, his personal assistant, and his secretary should be able to answer.

nnnn

International law places responsibility on France to ensure the safety of ambassadors on its soil. The French authorities must therefore account for what measures were in place and how such a tragedy could occur under their watch.

nnnn

There are further pressing concerns. Ambassadors do not drive themselves; if Mthethwa left the embassy, he would have had an official driver. That individual should provide a full account of the journey, while vehicle tracking records — standard for diplomatic cars — must be released.

nnnn

Reports also claim that Mthethwa’s last phone activity was near Bois de Boulogne, a park not far from the embassy or hotel. If true, this suggests he stopped there before his death. Why was he there, and who was he with?

nnnn

His final text message, reportedly sent to his wife, must also be verified. Linguistic patterns, spelling, and even emoji use could reveal whether the message was genuinely authored by him. Equally, hotel records and surveillance footage could shed light on whether someone else booked or accessed his room.

nnnn

Attention should also fall on the embassy itself. Brigadier-General M. Lepheane, the Defence Attaché stationed in Paris since 2021, may hold crucial information about the Ambassador’s final movements.

nnnn

These are not conspiracies. They are legitimate, uncomfortable truths that must be pursued. Too often in our history, official accounts have smothered the facts. For the sake of transparency, justice, and the dignity of Ambassador Mthethwa’s memory, South Africans must demand a full and independent investigation

post_title: ConCourt Grants Fathers Equal Parental Leave
post_content:
n

The Constitutional Court has ruled that fathers are now entitled to the same parental leave as mothers, marking a historic step towards gender equality in South Africa’s workplace policies.

nnnn

The court found that the current law was discriminatory and unconstitutional, as it unfairly limited fathers’ role in childcare. Until now, the Basic Conditions of Employment Act granted mothers four months of maternity leave, while fathers were restricted to just ten days.

nnnn

In its judgment, the court emphasised that the law perpetuated the outdated view that women should be the primary caregivers. Justice Zukiswa Tshiqi, delivering the ruling, said that fathers had been marginalised by the legislation, depriving them of the choice to share childcare responsibilities more equally.

nnnn

While the total leave allocation remains four months and ten days, parents will now have the right to divide this time between them. This means that mothers and fathers can choose to split the leave in a way that best suits their family, including dividing it equally.

nnnn

The ruling is expected to ease the burden on mothers and create greater flexibility for families, while also challenging traditional gender roles. It is being hailed as a victory for both gender equality and children’s right to nurturing care from both parents.

post_title: Eskom Reports Stable Grid, No Loadshedding
post_content:
n

Eskom has confirmed that the national power system remains stable, supported by steady improvements in generation performance through its ongoing Generation Recovery Plan.

nnnn

In a statement on 3 October, the utility reported that the month-to-date Energy Availability Factor (EAF) stood at 70.45%, reflecting improved plant reliability and fewer unplanned outages. This, Eskom said, is key to stabilising the grid and supporting economic growth.

nnnn

Technical improvements under the plan have enabled electricity demand to be met for over 97.8% of the time in the current financial year. Diesel expenditure also remains below budget, with reduced reliance on the costly Open Cycle Gas Turbine fleet.

nnnn

A major milestone was reached on 29 September when Unit 6 at Kusile Power Station entered commercial operation, concluding Eskom’s New-Build Programme and adding to the country’s 9 600MW baseload capacity.

nnnn

Between 26 September and 2 October, unplanned outages averaged 9 534MW, down from 11 505MW in the same period last year—an improvement nearly equal to the full capacity of Koeberg Power Station.

nnnn

The country has now gone 140 consecutive days without loadshedding, with only 26 hours recorded since April. Eskom’s Summer Outlook, covering September 2025 to March 2026, forecasts no loadshedding as a result of structural improvements in plant performance.

nnnn

However, the utility urged customers to avoid illegal connections, purchase electricity only from accredited vendors, and regularise accounts. Load reduction, it warned, may still be implemented in high-risk areas to protect infrastructure and ensure public safety.

nnnn

Eskom aims to eliminate load reduction within the next 12 to 18 months by addressing 640,000 illegal connections, upgrading infrastructure with smart meters, curbing illegal vending, and expanding access to free basic electricity.

post_title: ActionSA Slams Mismanagement in Culture Department

ActionSA has raised alarm over severe governance failures and financial mismanagement in the Mpumalanga Department of Culture, Sport and Recreation (DCSR), following the release of the Auditor-General’s 2024/25 audit findings.

nnnn

The report shows that the department has regressed to a qualified audit opinion, signalling a decline in financial accountability. According to ActionSA, this situation is worsened by long-standing vacancies in critical financial positions, including the Chief Financial Officer post, which has remained vacant for more than six years. Other key posts, such as the management accountant and deputy director of finance, have been left unfilled for over three years.

nnnn

“These leadership gaps have left the department unable to implement basic financial controls,” said ActionSA Member of the Mpumalanga Legislature, Thoko Mashiane MPL.

nnnn

The party stressed that such failures are particularly damaging in a department responsible for promoting culture, sport, and heritage — sectors that play an important role in building community identity, strengthening social cohesion, and boosting the local economy. Mismanagement, they argue, deprives artists, sports bodies, and heritage initiatives of the resources they need to flourish.

nnnn

ActionSA has called on the MEC for Culture, Sport and Recreation to urgently fill the vacant posts, take disciplinary action against negligent officials, and present a clear turnaround plan with timelines and measurable outcomes.

nnnn

“It is unacceptable that year after year, the Auditor-General repeats the same findings while the department relies on the audit process to expose failures instead of fixing them,” Mashiane added.

nnnn

The pledges, made by companies in the mining, forestry and fuel sectors, mark one of the largest investment commitments ever made to the province. Premier Ndlovu described the development as a “game-changer” that will advance the 7th Administration’s key priorities of inclusive growth, job creation, poverty reduction, and building a capable and ethical state.

nnnn

“This investment will help us reduce the unemployment rate, currently at 34 percent, and tackle poverty levels that sit at around 50 percent,” said Ndlovu. He expressed gratitude to business leaders and investors for showing confidence in Mpumalanga’s economy, adding that government would closely monitor the implementation of service-level agreements and corporate social investment commitments.

nnnn

During his closing remarks, Premier Ndlovu also expressed disappointment over the absence of representatives from Eskom and the Department of Minerals and Energy, emphasising the need for collaboration across all sectors to drive economic growth.

nnnn

He praised the province’s achievements in infrastructure delivery, agriculture, and human settlements, noting that Mpumalanga is currently ranked the best-performing province in the country for infrastructure projects.

nnnn

Ndlovu assured investors that the provincial government would work to remove bureaucratic barriers and create a more conducive environment for business. “We know where we are, and we know where we are going. With your support, we dare not fail the people of Mpumalanga,” he said.

post_title: Police Launch Manhunt After Burgersfort Murder
post_content:
n

The South African Police Service in Limpopo has launched a manhunt following the tragic murder of an 18-year-old in Ga-Phasha Molawetse Village, near Burgersfort.

nnnn

The incident occurred on Sunday, 5 October 2025, at around 05:30, when the victim, accompanied by a friend, was confronted by two men. According to reports, the confrontation stemmed from allegations that the teenager had shown disrespect to others in the community.

nnnn

During the altercation, one of the suspects, who was reportedly visiting the village, allegedly drew a knife and stabbed the teenager in the upper body. The young man was rushed to a local clinic before being transferred to Mankweng Hospital. Despite medical intervention, he succumbed to his injuries on Tuesday, 7 October 2025.

nnnn

Provincial police spokesperson, Colonel Malesela Ledwaba, confirmed that a case of murder has been opened. The suspect has already been identified, but remains at large. Police have urged members of the public to come forward with any information that could assist in the arrest.

nnnn

Investigating Officer Constable Duncan Aphane can be contacted directly on 072 767 3286. Alternatively, information can be shared through the Crime Stop number 08600 10111, the nearest police station, or via the MySAPS App.

nnnn

The police have assured the community that investigations are ongoing and appealed for calm as efforts to track down the suspect continue.

n

n

Swift action from the Provincial Anti-Hijacking Task Team stopped a business robbery in Kanyamazane on Tuesday, 7 October 2025, bringing relief to residents and business owners in the area.

nnnn

Police were patrolling when they received information about a white Kia without registration plates circling shops suspiciously. Soon after, officers were alerted to an armed robbery in progress at T & Sons Supermarket.

nnnn

The team rushed to the scene and confronted the suspects. According to police, the suspects allegedly opened fire, leading to a shootout. One suspect was fatally wounded, another was injured, while three others escaped in the getaway vehicle.

nnnn

A firearm was recovered, and cases of business robbery and possession of unlicensed firearms and ammunition have been opened. Emergency Services, Forensics and the Independent Police Investigative Directorate attended the scene.

nnnn

Police have launched a manhunt for the remaining suspects. Community members are urged to report any information that may help in their arrest.

n

n

The Bushbuckridge creative community is mourning the passing of Ronald “Kapture Beats” Malele, a respected hip-hop producer whose quiet influence helped shape the careers of several emerging artists from the region.

nnnn

Born and raised in Ga Relane, Bushbuckridge, Kapture later moved to Johannesburg for tertiary studies and went on to work at an IT company. Despite building a life in the city, he always returned home during holidays and remained closely connected to his community. According to his longtime friend and collaborator, Macdonald Hlompho Lekhuleni, known as Masta H, Kapture was “a very humble person, always smiling and grounded, no matter how far his talents took him.”

nnnn

Friends and colleagues described him as a man with a great personality who treated everyone with respect, regardless of their background. Though blessed with talent, he remained humble and avoided the spotlight, preferring to work quietly behind the scenes while uplifting others.

nnnn

Among his most meaningful achievements was his work on the Mapulaneng Vol. 2 Mixtape by Masta H, which he considered a turning point in his career. “He said that after producing that project, it elevated him. That’s when people started recognising him. It introduced him to a broader audience, especially since he was considered an underground producer,” recalls Masta H. Another significant project was his musical poetry collaboration with Gakwi Mashego, which showcased his ability to merge spoken word with music.

nnnn

Kapture also served as a mentor to many aspiring artists. “Even myself, I was an upcoming artist when I met him,” says Masta H. He guided artists such as KAYCEEZO, now known as KAMO, and Refrieca, who has since risen to prominence as a South African DJ and dancer. One of his proudest moments, according to his friend, was seeing artists he worked with appear on television and acknowledge him publicly while he was still alive.

nnnn

Plans are under way to honour his life and legacy, including a community show with Shogun C Well and the release of unreleased songs he produced.

nnnn

Reflecting on his legacy, Masta H said: “I hope the community of Ga Relane and Bushbuckridge as a whole will remember him as a producer who contributed enormously to Bushbuckridge music. Sometimes producers are the unsung heroes. We artists grab all the attention and forget how hard our producers work behind the scenes to make us shine. He will forever be remembered. He played a huge role — may his soul rest in peace.”

nnnn

Bushbuckridge News extends its heartfelt condolences to the Malele family, friends, and all artists who walked this journey with him.
