post_title: From Decks to Design: Meet Mkhuhlu’s Own DJ Guski
post_content:
n

Born on 3 March 1994 in Malelane and raised in Mkhuhlu, Nyiko “DJ Guski” Nkuna is a name steadily rising in both the entertainment and creative industries. Affectionately nicknamed “Master KG” by locals due to his striking resemblance to the famous music producer, Guski has crafted a journey fuelled by passion, resilience and community spirit.

nnnn

He began his schooling at Bhejani Primary School in 2000 before moving on to Chayaza Secondary School, where he matriculated in 2011. Although he was initially unable to secure space at the University of Limpopo, he refused to let that setback dim his ambitions. Instead, he turned to what he loved most — music and creativity.

nnnn

In 2012, after receiving his first computer, he began producing DJ mixes and soon discovered Adobe Photoshop. This opened the door to graphic design, and he quickly made a name for himself by designing flyers for local events. This marked his official entrance into the entertainment and creative sector.

nnnn

Determined to further his education, Guski enrolled at UNISA to study Safety Management before transferring to the Vaal University of Technology, where he graduated in 2018. While at VUT, he joined the DJ Society and worked as both a DJ and a graphic designer for campus events — an experience he says boosted his confidence and helped him build valuable industry connections.

nnnn

By 2014, he was performing full-time as a DJ around Mkhuhlu while also designing branding material for small businesses. His entrepreneurial journey continued in 2015 with the launch of his own clothing brand, Guski, which started with caps and later expanded to include T-shirts and jerseys. After completing his studies, he returned home and founded MK Printing, investing in his own printing equipment to produce posters, branded clothing and promotional material. The business remains active and continues to support local brands and events.

nnnn

Drawing from his experience in planning and supporting events, he eventually established GM Entertainment, under which he launched Mkhuhlu Comes Alive – Daytime Vibe. The first event took place on 31 December 2024. The latest edition, held on 4 October 2025, was a major success, drawing over 1,000 attendees, showcasing more than 30 local acts and hosting over 10 vendors, giving young talents and entrepreneurs a platform to shine.

nnnn

Alongside his creative ventures, Guski has also built a professional career. He has worked as a Construction Health and Safety Officer for the past five years, applying his Safety Management training to create safer workplaces.

nnnn

Passionate about music, design, safety and community development, DJ Guski continues to balance his career with his mission to uplift others.

nnnn

With his growing influence and unwavering commitment to community empowerment, Nyiko “DJ Guski” Nkuna is proving that talent paired with determination can turn a dream into a movement.

n

post_title: Government Acts to Resolve BEEI Stipend Delays
post_content:
n

Government has moved swiftly to address delays in stipend payments for Education Assistants and General School Assistants employed under the Basic Education Employment Initiative (BEEI).

nnnn

Employment and Labour Deputy Minister Jomo Sibiya assured the public at a media briefing in Pretoria on Wednesday that funds had now been released, following urgent talks between the Department of Basic Education (DBE), the Department of Employment and Labour (DEL), the Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF), and the Industrial Development Corporation (IDC).

nnnn

“Government has resolved the payment impasse. As of this morning, the UIF has released funds, and Education Assistants and General School Assistants began receiving their payments from 10am,” Sibiya said. Beneficiaries banking with Capitec and FNB received their stipends first, while those using other banks will be paid once inter-bank processes are complete.

nnnn

The Deputy Minister explained that the delays under Phase V of the programme were linked to compliance requirements under the Public Finance Management Act (PFMA), and not negligence. He also offered an apology to thousands of young South Africans affected by the late payments.

nnnn

“We must always uphold integrity when managing public funds, but we acknowledge that verification delays caused hardship. For that, government unreservedly apologises,” he said.

nnnn

To prevent future disruptions, Sibiya outlined measures including the faster submission of compliance documents, strengthened monitoring of the Kwantu Payment System, and the creation of a joint technical team to speed up verification. He stressed that consequence management would be enforced in cases of negligence.

nnnn

The BEEI has created 158,000 employment opportunities for young people, offering valuable work experience, training, and skills development. Sibiya emphasised that these youth are not just beneficiaries but active contributors to social progress.

nnnn

“Interdepartmental unity is a model we want to replicate across other youth employment programmes. Our people do not want excuses; they want delivery. And that is exactly what we are doing today,” he concluded.

n

post_title: Ntsako Masilela Face of Acornhoek Mall

post_content:
n

At just 22 years old, Ntsako Malesa from Greenvalley, Acornhoek, is already making her mark as a student, entrepreneur, and now the newly crowned Face of Acornhoek Mall 2025–2027. Currently studying through UNISA and running her own hair care brand, Sparks Moves, Ntsako represents a new wave of young women who are reshaping the narrative of rural youth through ambition and community-driven leadership.

nnnn

Ntsako says her passion for community development is what pushed her to enter the competition. “I’ve always had a drive for helping in my community and creating change. Over the years, I’ve witnessed Acornhoek Mall as a company that has a huge interest in community development. I auditioned because I felt that my love for community engagement aligns with Acornhoek Mall’s core values,” she explains.

nnnn

Unlike many contestants who enter pageants solely for the crown, Ntsako had a different mission. She wanted to enjoy the journey and build friendships. But when she made it into the Top 5, reality sank in. “I started being nervous from there as I didn’t know what to hope for, but I kept my hopes alive. Being announced as the winner brought a roller coaster of emotions. I was happy but in disbelief at the same time because the competition was very tight.”

nnnn

Balancing her studies, business commitments and the demands of the competition was not easy. The pressure intensified when she fell ill during one of the busiest weeks. “I had to give my final push and make sure I completed everything in time. I learnt how to work under pressure, prioritise important tasks, communicate effectively, multitask and manage my time well,” she reflects.

nnnn

For Ntsako, holding this title is more than just a personal achievement. “Being the Face of Acornhoek Mall is an incredible honour and a platform to inspire youth. It signifies the opportunity to be a role model, particularly for young women, showcasing confidence, resilience and determination.” She hopes to use her role to drive conversations around entrepreneurship, leadership and youth empowerment.

nnnn

Her vision for the next two years is clear and purposeful. “I will be engaging with the community, supporting local businesses with networking and contributing to the mall’s vibrant atmosphere. This role will also allow me to network with stakeholders including tenants, customers and ambassadors to foster collaborations and opportunities,” she says.

nnnn

Ntsako is passionate about women inclusion, youth empowerment and community development, and plans to anchor her initiatives around these causes. She firmly believes that platforms like Face of Acornhoek Mall play a vital role in shaping young leaders. “They teach youth about leadership and responsibility at a tender age and boost self-esteem. They also promote entrepreneurship by providing a platform for local businesses to showcase their products, contributing to local economic growth,” she adds.

nnnn

As she steps into her new role, Ntsako carries with her the hopes of many young people in Acornhoek who see themselves in her story — a story of determination, service, and the belief that greatness can be achieved right here at home.

nnnn

post_title: Police Hunt Armed Suspects After Bus Attack
post_content:
n

The South African Police Service in Limpopo has launched a manhunt after a violent bus attack left two passengers dead and others traumatised along the N1 near Mokopane.

nnnn

According to police, the incident occurred on Wednesday night, 8 October 2025, at around 21:40, approximately eight kilometres before the Nylplaza Tollgate. A 42-year-old bus driver from Zimbabwe was transporting 54 passengers from Randfontein to Zimbabwe when the attack unfolded.

nnnn

Reports indicate that two male passengers seated at the back of the Volvo 60-seater bus drew firearms and threatened those on board. A 30-year-old male passenger attempted to disarm one of the suspects while others tried to intervene. Shots were fired during the struggle, fatally wounding the male passenger and a woman believed to be around 25 years old.

nnnn

The armed men then robbed passengers of cash and mobile phones before fleeing the scene. They were picked up by an unidentified vehicle that had been following the bus. The make, model, and registration number of the vehicle remain unknown.

nnnn

Police have opened cases of murder and armed robbery.

nnnn

Anyone with information is urged to contact Sergeant Matsipi Makwela on 076 786 1447, call Crime Stop on 08600 10111, report to the nearest police station, or use the MySAPS App.

nnnn

Police investigations are ongoing.

n

n

A joint operation led by the Hawks’ Serious Organised Crime Investigation Unit in Nelspruit, together with the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA), White River Flying Squad and Acornhoek Local Criminal Record Centre, resulted in the arrest of a 50-year-old pharmacy owner and four employees in Acornhoek on Thursday, 9 October 2025.

nnnn

The arrests follow information received by SAHPRA regarding unlawful activities at the pharmacy. Officers executed a search warrant at the premises, where four employees — two women aged 35 and 44, and two men aged 35 and 48 — were found dispensing medication without being able to provide proof of the required qualifications.

nnnn

The owner was not present at the time but was called to the scene. Upon arrival, he also failed to produce a valid operating licence or any qualifications. Authorities further discovered that the business was not registered with the South African Pharmacy Council.

nnnn

Scheduled medicines, from Schedule 1 to Schedule 6, were confiscated. The value of the seized medication is yet to be confirmed pending expert assessment and further investigation.

nnnnnnnn

Major General Nico Gerber, Provincial Head of the Hawks in Mpumalanga, welcomed the successful operation and partnership between the agencies involved.

nnnn

“It has been six years, since 2019, that this establishment has been operating. One cannot imagine how many people may have been affected. We are relieved that it has now been shut down and further harm to the community will be prevented,” he said.

post_title: Toyota Quantum seized by the Hawks
Hawks Seize Assets Linked to R5 Million PPE Fraud
post_content:
n

A High Court order has resulted in the forfeiture of a property and vehicles worth a combined R2.5 million, linked to an alleged Covid-19 PPE corruption scandal involving a former secretary of the Mpumalanga Department of Health.

nnnn

The Division of the High Court in Mbombela granted the forfeiture order on 1 October 2025 for a house valued at R1.5 million in Sunninghill, Johannesburg, and three vehicles worth R1 million. The order was formally received by the Hawks’ Asset Investigation Unit in Mpumalanga on Thursday, 9 October 2025.

nnnn

Investigations revealed that during the height of the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020, former departmental secretary Sanele Sanderson allegedly siphoned R5 million intended for community services. She reportedly channelled the money through two fraudulent service providers, who were paid for services never rendered. Fake delivery notes were issued to facilitate the payments.

nnnn

Part of the proceeds was allegedly used to buy a house worth R1.5 million in Barberton, which was later sold to purchase the Sunninghill property registered under her daughter’s name. She also acquired three vehicles — a Toyota Quantum, Hyundai LDV and VW Golf — worth R1 million.

nnnn

The Hawks successfully located and seized the Johannesburg property and the Toyota Quantum. The two remaining vehicles have not yet been recovered, but all necessary paperwork to enforce the order has been completed

nnnn

.

nnnnnnnn

The criminal investigation is ongoing, and arrests are expected once the process is finalised.

post_title: Police officers arrested in Lydenburg robbery
post_content:
n

The South African Police Service (SAPS) in Mpumalanga has arrested four police officers from Limpopo and one civilian in connection with a house robbery in Lydenburg (Mashishing).

nnnn

The suspects, aged between 29 and 41, were apprehended in the early hours of Friday, 10 October 2025, after police responded swiftly to a robbery in progress. The victims, believed to be Ethiopian nationals, were asleep when armed suspects stormed their home around 23h50 on Thursday evening.

nnnn

Three vehicles were allegedly used during the robbery: a grey Toyota double-cab bakkie, a private vehicle, and a marked SAPS VW Golf GTI belonging to the Polokwane Flying Squad. The private vehicle fled the scene with boxes of suspected illicit cigarettes and cash.

nnnnnnnn

At the scene, police seized the Toyota bakkie and the marked VW Golf. Officers also recovered illicit cigarettes valued at approximately R1.5 million and R950,000 in cash. Investigators found that the registration plates had been tampered with using black sellotape, and ammunition was also confiscated.

nnnn

Two of the arrested officers were in possession of their official service firearms, which have been seized. All five suspects remain in custody and are expected to appear in the Mashishing Magistrate’s Court on Monday, 13 October 2025, facing charges of house robbery. Additional charges may follow.

nnnn

The Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation (DPCI), also known as the Hawks, has taken over the case. Acting Provincial Commissioner, Major General Dr Zeph Mkhwanazi, has stated that “No one is above the law. We will not tolerate any form of criminality within our ranks. The swift arrest of these individuals demonstrates our zero-tolerance approach to corruption and criminal behaviour.”

n

post_title: Mpumalanga Triumphs in Road Safety Competitions
post_content:
n

Mpumalanga Province has emerged victorious at the 2025 National Road Safety Debates and Participatory Educational Techniques (PET) competitions, with the announcement made during a prize-giving ceremony held at Time Square in Pretoria on Friday, 10 October 2025.

nnnn

The province claimed the top spot in the rural category of the Road Safety Debates and tied with Limpopo in the urban category. Mpumalanga further dominated the PET competitions, winning both the rural and urban categories.

nnnn

Learners who excelled in each category received medals, trophies and a cheque worth R6 600. Among the top achievers was Sasha Nkabinde, a Grade 11 learner from Jerusalem Secondary School in Hazyview, who won Best Speaker in the Urban Debate category.

nnnn

All four trainers from the winning categories also walked away with Best Trainer awards, receiving medals and trophies in recognition of their efforts.

nnnn

The PET competitions awarded R100 000 each to Sikhwahlane Secondary School (urban category) and Skhila Secondary School (rural category) to implement road safety initiatives in their communities.

nnnn

The national competitions, which target Grade 10 and 11 learners, encourage young people to research road safety challenges and propose solutions while developing public speaking and research skills.

nnnn

Road Traffic Management Corporation (RTMC) Interim CEO, Ms Refilwe Mongale, said the programme impacts over 1 000 learners nationwide. “Learners not only gain knowledge on road safety but also acquire valuable skills such as research and public speaking,” she explained.

nnnn

Mpumalanga MEC for Community Safety, Security and Liaison, Mr Jackie Macie, praised the learners, trainers, and officials for their outstanding performance. “These competitions are not just about winning. They are about creating a culture of road safety and preventing unnecessary loss of life,” he said.

nnnn

Macie called on all participants to serve as road safety ambassadors in their communities.

post_title: More Than 40 Killed in Limpopo Crash
post_content:
n

FORTY-TWO people have died and dozens more were injured after a bus transporting passengers from the Eastern Cape to Harare plunged off a steep section of the N1 highway in Limpopo on Sunday evening.

nnnn

The Road Traffic Management Corporation confirmed that emergency crews recovered 42 bodies from the wreckage. Meanwhile, 49 survivors were rushed to hospitals in Louis Trichardt and Siloam for treatment.

nnnn

According to spokesperson Simon Zwane, the bus overturned on a steep section of road. The exact cause remains under investigation.

nnnn

The deceased are reported to include Zimbabwean and Malawian nationals, many of whom were returning home. Among the victims was a ten-month-old infant.

nnnn

Limpopo Premier Dr Phophi Ramathuba is due to visit the crash site and meet emergency services teams responding to the tragedy. She has expressed her condolences to the families affected and said the provincial government will assist wherever possible.

nnnn

The scale of the disaster has shocked not only local communities but also neighbouring countries. Zimbabwean and Malawian consular services are coordinating with South African authorities to identify victims and assist next of kin. Psychosocial support is being provided to survivors.

nnnn

This tragedy comes during South Africa’s annual Transport Month, which focuses on road safety nationwide. As investigations unfold, questions remain about whether vehicle maintenance, speed, road conditions or driver fatigue played a role in this devastating crash.

post_title: St Marks Crowned Kay Motsepe Champions
post_content:
n

The Department of Education has congratulated St. Marks Academy from the Mbombela Circuit in Ehlanzeni District for their remarkable triumph at the 2025 Kay Motsepe Schools’ Soccer Tournament.

nnnn

The school’s Under-19 boys’ team were crowned national champions after defeating Fumani Secondary School from Katlehong, Gauteng, in a hard-fought final. The deciding goal secured a 1–0 victory and a prestigious R3 million prize. Their journey to glory included overcoming the formidable Clapham High School, a side with a strong reputation in school football, proving that determination and teamwork can conquer all odds.

nnnn

Adding to the celebrations, the St. Marks Under-19 girls’ team impressed with their spirited display, earning second place after a dramatic 5–4 penalty shootout against St. Anne’s of the Free State. Their runners-up finish secured an additional R400,000 in prize money.

The Department commended all schools for their remarkable performances and extended heartfelt congratulations to learners, coaches, and educators for flying the Mpumalanga flag with pride.

post_title: Bushbuckridge Derby Launches ABC Motsepe League
post_content:
n

The ABC Motsepe League kicked off in electrifying fashion as Acornhoek United and Liver Brothers delivered a high-intensity Bushbuckridge derby at a fully packed Acorn to Oaks Stadium. With both sides being the only representatives from Bushbuckridge at this level of competition, pride and bragging rights were at stake as much as the three points.

nnnn

From the first whistle, the atmosphere was electric, with supporters from both camps turning the stadium into a sea of colour, song and anticipation. The match lived up to expectations, offering end-to-end action, passionate challenges and moments of brilliance.

nnnn

The deadlock was finally broken in the 85th minute when Acornhoek United were awarded a penalty. Harry Ndlovu stepped up with confidence and slotted the ball past the goalkeeper, sending United fans into a wild celebration.

However, the joy was short-lived. Just two minutes later, Liver Brothers were handed a lifeline after a foul in the box resulted in a penalty of their own. They made no mistake, levelling matters in the 87th minute and shifting the game's momentum.

Despite the loss, Acornhoek United showed determination and flair, with Harry Ndlovu standing out as a key performer. Liver Brothers, on the other hand, showcased resilience and a fighting spirit that earned them a memorable comeback win.

post_title: Two Men Arrested For Illegal Mining
post_content:
n

Two men suspected of involvement in illegal mining activities were arrested at Slaaihoek near Machadodorp during a police operation conducted under Operation Vala Umgodi on Sunday, 12 October 2025.

nnnn

The suspects, aged between 20 and 28, were found to be in South Africa without valid documentation and were immediately charged under the Immigration Act. Their arrest comes as part of broader efforts by law enforcement to tackle illegal mining and associated crimes in Mpumalanga.

nnnn

During the operation, police seized a generator, shovels and a variety of beverages believed to have been used at the illegal mining site. The confiscations form part of the SAPS’s continued drive to disrupt illegal mining networks in the province.

nnnn

The suspects are expected to appear before the Belfast Magistrate’s Court soon. Police detectives are working alongside officials from the Department of Home Affairs to confirm the immigration status of the individuals involved.

post_title: Lightning Strikes Tourists at God’s Window
post_content:
n

On 10 October 2025, a brief but intense thunderstorm struck the popular tourist destination of God’s Window, leaving around 25 vehicles affected by lightning. The Mpumalanga Tourism and Parks Agency (MTPA) swiftly stepped in to assist those impacted.

nnnn

Only two people were reported to have sustained injuries: a curio seller and her daughter. Both were taken to Sabi Hospital, where the mother was treated and released the same day, while her daughter remained under observation over the weekend. At the time of this statement, she was awaiting a doctor’s release.

nnnn

Acting Chief Executive Officer of MTPA, Mr Lemmy Mdluli, expressed his sympathy to all victims, saying, “I am seriously touched by the lightning incident at God’s Window and sympathise with the victims. This is a very rare occurrence at this popular tourist spot. I also want to appreciate the Blyde Hospitality Service team for helping the victims.”

nnnn

Among the vehicles struck, only one suffered serious burns on the dashboard, while others experienced electrical faults or tyre punctures. The Blyde Hospitality Service team provided support by offering phones to contact insurance companies and towing vehicles to destinations specified by insurers.

nnnn

Tourists were assisted with accommodation or transportation to pre-booked hotels and lodges. Among those affected were two international visitors from Greece and Belgium. A Gauteng-based family of four, whose car was uninsured, received transport and temporary lodging at the Grasskop Hotel while their vehicle and trailer were safely stored.

nnnn

The MTPA team also ensured that many tourists safely reached their homes or booked destinations following the incident.

post_title: MEC Thulasizwe Thomo at the launch of the Transport Month

post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga Provincial Government has reaffirmed its commitment to safe and reliable transport as Transport Month officially kicked off in Grootvlei, Dipaleseng Local Municipality.

nnnn

MEC Thulasizwe Thomo of Public Works, Roads and Transport led the launch of the 2025 Transport Month, which was conducted through an Inter-Provincial Law Enforcement Operation along the N3 Corridor. The impactful operation, held in collaboration with the N3 Forum, involved law enforcement stakeholders from Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal and the Free State. This joint effort highlighted a shared commitment to strengthening road safety, ensuring compliance, and enhancing cross-border law enforcement on one of South Africa’s busiest national routes.

nnnn

In his address during the parade, MEC Thomo emphasised the importance of public transport in the daily lives of thousands of commuters, as well as its role in economic growth and social development. “The launch is part of the broader Transport Month Programme, which aims to raise awareness about road safety, promote responsible driving behaviour, and highlight the Department’s ongoing efforts to maintain and improve transport infrastructure across the province,” he said.

nnnn

The Provincial Government further noted that around 70,000 learners in the province depend on public transport to get to school and back as part of a social intervention programme aimed at improving access to education.

nnnn

Throughout October, the Departments of Public Works, Roads and Transport, together with Community Safety, Security and Liaison, will intensify law enforcement operations to ensure compliance with road safety regulations. Awareness campaigns will also be conducted to encourage responsible driving and reduce accidents on the province’s roads.

nnnn

Additionally, the Provincial Government has committed to strengthening transport infrastructure through ongoing maintenance of bridges, culverts and road networks, intending to create a safer, more reliable, and efficient transport system for all.

n

n

A group of police officials and civilians accused of involvement in a house robbery in Lydenburg will remain behind bars after their urgent bail application was halted, thanks to coordinated efforts by the Hawks and the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA).

nnnn

The case, which has sparked strong public interest, involves four Limpopo-based police officers who were allegedly caught at the scene of a house robbery in a police-branded vehicle belonging to the Limpopo Flying Squad. Local SAPS members responded swiftly to the robbery call, only to find their counterparts allegedly implicated in the crime.

nnnn

The accused officers were identified as Sergeant Lucky Shogolo (40), Constable Thapelo Ledwaba (34), Constable Malesela Huma (34), and Constable Saraphina Senama (34). They were reportedly identified by the victims as the robbers.

nnnn

A further twist unfolded when two vehicles loaded with illicit cigarettes fled the scene. One of the vehicles, fitted with tampered number plates, was intercepted. The driver, 29-year-old Sello Komane, was also identified as one of the suspects. Inside a bulletproof vest found in the police vehicle, officers recovered a stash of cash.

nnnn

A search of the targeted flat uncovered illicit cigarettes valued at approximately R1.5 million, along with R950,000 in cash hidden in plastic bags around the house.

nnnn

In addition to the five South African suspects, two Ethiopian nationals — Daniel Wikino (38) and Aleyo Shgutey (28) — were charged with possession and dealing in illicit cigarettes. Their matter was postponed to 20 October 2025 to secure an interpreter.

nnnn

The NPA and Hawks successfully opposed immediate bail, arguing that the investigation must be completed before formal proceedings can continue. The five accused will remain in custody, with a formal bail hearing set for Friday, 17 October 2025.

nnnn

Authorities say investigations are ongoing to trace the source of the illicit cigarettes and the large sum of cash recovered.

post_title: Traffic Officer Dies in N4 Hit-and-Run
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga Department of Community Safety, Security and Liaison has expressed shock following the tragic death of a traffic law enforcement officer on the N4 toll road near Middelburg.

nnnn

Joseph Mtselu, 49, a Principal Provincial Inspector attached to Overload Control in Middelburg, was directing an LDV pulling a trailer to the Middelburg Weighbridge in the early hours of 14 October 2025 when he was struck by the vehicle. The driver reportedly failed to stop and allegedly fled the scene on foot.

nnnn

Mr Mtselu tragically died at the scene. Police have opened a case of culpable homicide and are actively searching for the suspect. An investigation is ongoing.

nnnn

Mpumalanga MEC for Community Safety, Security and Liaison, Mr Jackie Macie, extended his heartfelt condolences to Mr Mtselu’s family, friends and colleagues. “It is devastating for the Department to lose traffic officers while they are working tirelessly to save lives on our roads,” he said.

nnnnnnnn

MEC Macie urged police to pursue the driver with urgency and called on traffic law enforcement officers to remain vigilant, noting that some motorists continue to disregard road rules.

nnnn

The Department and community mourn the loss of a dedicated officer whose life was taken in the line of duty  

n

post_title: Sala Fruit Inspires Local Fragrance Brand
post_content:
n

Local Entrepreneurs Turn Bushbuckridge’s Beloved Sala Fruit into Thriving Fragrance Brand

nnnn

What began as a simple appreciation for the scent of a local fruit has grown into a proudly Bushbuckridge-owned manufacturing business, supplying well-known retailers and empowering community members through entrepreneurship.

nnnn

Conference Khoza, together with his sister Antoinnet Khoza, co-founded Sala in 2017. The brand takes its name and inspiration from the sala fruit—a fragrant fruit that many local motorists traditionally place in their cars as a natural air freshener. Their father, upon holding the fruit and admiring its fresh scent, suggested turning that beloved fragrance into something more lasting. That moment sparked what is now a growing local brand.

nnnn

Today, Sala manufactures a wide range of scented household and personal care products, including perfumes, colognes, body and hand lotions, roll-ons, shampoos, dishwashing liquids, pine gel, and more. The very first product ever developed was a perfume, created to capture the distinct scent of the sala that many in the community love.

nnnn

The business operates from a manufacturing space in Rolle, with an administrative office also based in the area. Despite starting small, Sala Fragrance now supplies established outlets including Spar, Makhoma butchery and Roots. They also offer delivery through PAXI, making it easier for customers and resellers across the country to access their products.

nnnn

What sets their model apart is their community-based approach to employment. Instead of traditional full-time hiring, the Khoza siblings offer commission-based opportunities, allowing individuals to buy stock and resell for profit — creating a platform for many to start small businesses of their own.

nnnn

Their online presence continues to grow, with the Sala brand active on Facebook, where customers can follow product updates, promotions and success stories.

n

post_title: Godide School’s New Buildings Inspire Hope
post_content:
n

The community of Rolle celebrated a historic milestone on Wednesday, 15 October 2025, as Premier Mandla Ndlovu officially handed over the new state-of-the-art buildings at Godide Secondary School. The event marked a major infrastructure achievement by the Mpumalanga Provincial Government, aimed at improving education and providing learners with modern resources.

nnnn

The upgraded school now boasts new classrooms, a modern science laboratory, computer centre, library, kitchen, administration block, Grade R centre, hall, guard house, and reliable water and electrical infrastructure.

nnnn

Premier Ndlovu praised the development, saying, “The Provincial Government is delivering infrastructure that matches the potential of our children, even in rural areas. Similar schools like this are found in Model C areas. We are happy that our children, in their own school, can now do proper experiments. We have asked them to take care of these buildings so that these buildings can take care of them.”

nnnn

Godide Secondary School, established years ago, has a strong academic record: 90% pass rate in 2021, 88% in 2022, 63% in 2023, and 80.4% in 2024. With 598 learners enrolled this year, it remains one of Bushbuckridge’s largest schools.

nnnn

Kgoshi Lameck Mokoena, Chairperson of the Mpumalanga House of Traditional and Khoisan Leaders, welcomed the new facilities: “Other provinces may prioritise other things, but here in Mpumalanga we prioritise education. As traditional leaders, we support projects like this and will always honour such invitations.”

nnnn

MEC for Public Works, Roads and Transport, Thulasizwe Thomo, commended the community for fighting for meaningful development. “You have fought for this because you want to secure the future of your children. Today we celebrate victory. But if there is ever discontent, do not destroy this school. It is worth R55 million — destroying it would destroy your children’s future.”

nnnn

Learners expressed their pride in the upgraded school. The SRC President said, “We thank our parents and the community for not giving up. Because they fought, today we walk into new buildings that look like those we see in cities.”

nnnn

A Grade 11 learner added, “I cannot wait to use the new computer lab. It makes me feel like my dreams are valid.”

nnnn

With its new infrastructure, Godide Secondary School is poised to offer learners modern facilities, better learning opportunities, and hope for a brighter future.

n

n

A Mozambican woman, Clara Masinga (37), has been sentenced to 23 years’ direct imprisonment by the High Court sitting in Mbombela for the premeditated murder of her 11-year-old stepdaughter, Jennifer Gumbi.

nnnn

Masinga, who lived with Jennifer’s father, Rodgers Gumbi, in KwaMhlushwa, Phosaville Section near Malelane, pleaded guilty and entered into a Section 105A plea and sentence agreement with the State.

nnnn

The tragic incident took place on 21 March 2015. Masinga sent a friend of the child to fetch her, then lured Jennifer to her house under the false pretence that someone wanted to buy her clothes. She then bought ice cream and rat poison (Rattex) from a nearby tuck shop. Together with an accomplice, she crushed the poison into the ice cream and gave it to the child.

nnnn

Jennifer later died from the poisoning, and her body was found dumped in a shallow ditch near the Mlumati River. During court proceedings, Masinga admitted she killed the child to spite Jennifer’s biological mother.

nnnn

State Advocate Senzo Zindela argued for a harsh sentence, highlighting the cruel manner in which the child was killed and the further desecration of the body with boiled water to ensure the murder succeeded.

nnnn

Judge Vukeya strongly condemned the rise in domestic violence and the killing of children in South Africa, stating that while no sentence could ever bring Jennifer back, justice had to be served. The court found compelling reasons to deviate from the minimum sentence and handed down 23 years’ imprisonment. Masinga has also been declared unfit to own a firearm.

nnnn

The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) welcomed the sentence and praised the law enforcement teams involved. The NPA reaffirmed its commitment to fighting domestic and gender-based violence, stating that “the value of human life is immeasurable.”

n

post_title: Bushbuckridge Families Walk Kilometres for Water
post_content:
n

Residents of New Forest in Bushbuckridge say they are forced to walk more than three kilometres every Wednesday just to access water at the main road. The community, which has been relying on this weekly supply for months, describes the situation as exhausting and undignified.

nnnn

Water is released once a week, with households from the highway section receiving it at around 6 am. Those in the lower section only get their turn at about 11 am. Community members must ensure they are present on the day, as missing the Wednesday supply means waiting another full week.

nnnn

Some arrive pushing wheelbarrows, carrying between 20 and 40 containers depending on the size of the household. “If you are not here on time, you don’t get water. There are no second chances,” said one resident.

nnnn

In June, residents were promised water taps closer to their homes, but there has been no communication or visible progress since then. The community is now demanding answers, saying walking long distances in the heat, especially for the elderly and children, is becoming unbearable.

nnnn

Locals say all they want is access to water with dignity, something they believe should not require a weekly struggle.

n

n

Four foreign nationals and a South African man, aged between 18 and 30, have been arrested in Leslie for their alleged involvement in a large stock theft case.

nnnn

According to reports, a total of 12 cows were stolen and then slaughtered at two separate locations in the area. Police responded swiftly after receiving a tip-off and launched an operation.

nnnn

At one of the scenes, officers discovered seven carcasses of slaughtered cattle, estimated to be worth around R250,000. Acting on further intelligence, police intercepted a brown VW Amarok with Gauteng registration plates during stop-and-search operations. Meat was found inside the vehicle, leading to the arrest of the driver.

nnnn

Officers proceeded to a second location, where they found another five carcasses, valued at approximately R175,000, inside a kraal. Four suspects were detained on the scene, while two others managed to flee, abandoning the vehicle they were using.

nnnn

The five suspects are expected to appear before the Leslie Magistrate’s Court on Friday, 17 October 2025.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner of the SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, urged livestock owners to ensure their animals are properly brand marked, as it greatly assists in recovery and investigations.

n

n

Mathibela High School in Alexandria, Bushbuckridge, hosted a motivational ceremony on Wednesday to encourage Grade 12 learners as they prepare for their final examinations starting on 21 October 2025.

nnnn

The highlight of the event was the launch of the Lazarus Phiri Top Achiever Award, created in memory of the late Lazarus Phiri, a long-serving member of the School Governing Body. The award comes with a voucher worth R2 500, which will be presented annually to the school’s top-performing matric learner. The school confirmed that the value of the voucher will increase in the coming years, with a target of R5 000, ensuring the award grows as a lasting investment in academic excellence.

nnnn

Opening with a prayer led by Pastor Mabuza, the programme was filled with words of encouragement from a range of dignitaries. These included representatives from SADTU, feeder schools, and the local ward councillor, Honourable Mkhabela S., all of whom urged learners to embrace education as a life-changing opportunity.

nnnn

Honourable Khumalo R., Speaker of the Ehlanzeni District, encouraged learners to draw strength from Phiri’s legacy and to focus on producing excellent results. Guest speaker Mrs Masuku reminded learners that discipline, determination, and self-belief are key to success, particularly in the final stretch before exams.

nnnn

Parents and learners also pledged their commitment to supporting one another, with student representative Fortunate Makhubela speaking on behalf of the Class of 2025. The event concluded with a vote of thanks from SGB Chairperson Mr Khumalo L.S., who commended the community for its united support of the learners.

nnnn

The Lazarus Phiri Award is expected to boost morale and inspire learners to give their very best during exams and beyond. As the Class of 2025 prepares to write, the message was clear: your community believes in you, your hard work will be rewarded, and your future is worth striving for.

nnnn

To the Matric Class of 2025: stay strong, stay focused, and write your story of success with courage and determination. The finish line is near, and the future is waiting for you.

n

post_title: Police Hunt Suspect After Bushbuckridge Shooting
post_content:
n

The South African Police Service (SAPS) in Bushbuckridge has launched a manhunt after an attempted murder incident at a tavern in Mandela Village on Tuesday evening, 14 October 2025.

nnnn

According to police, a 39-year-old man was seated with a friend, watching television, when the suspect, known to him, approached and asked for a beer. The victim reportedly told the man that he had no money to buy him a drink. The suspect then became aggressive, insulted the victim, and allegedly produced a firearm before shooting him in the left leg.

nnnn

Shockingly, after the shooting, the suspect is said to have apologised, claiming it was a mistake, before fleeing the scene. Although his identity is known to the authorities, efforts to arrest him have so far been unsuccessful.

nnnn

The case is being investigated by Warrant Officer Busisiwe Dlamini, who appealed to anyone with information to contact her on 082 056 9507.

n

post_title: Pastor Accused of Child Rape Denied Bail
post_content:
n

A 66-year-old pastor from Botlokwa in Limpopo has been denied bail after appearing in the Morebeng Magistrate’s Court on allegations of raping a three-year-old girl.

nnnn

The accused, identified as Justice Mongalo, also works as a driver at a crèche owned by his wife. It is alleged that on the day of the incident, he dropped the child off at her home later than usual. Shortly afterwards, the girl reportedly complained of pain in her private parts.

nnnn

Her family took her to hospital, where medical examinations confirmed that she had been raped. Mongalo has pleaded not guilty to the charge.

nnnn

The court ruled that he remain in custody until his next appearance, scheduled for 3 December.

nnnn

The case has drawn strong emotions within the community. Members of Mongalo’s church and his relatives attended the court proceedings to show their support, while other residents gathered outside to oppose bail.

nnnn

Police and social workers continue to investigate the matter, and the case has sparked renewed calls for the protection of children against abuse.

n

post_title: Provincial prayer for the class of 2025
Province Holds Prayer Session for Class of 2025
post_content:
n

The Department of Education, in partnership with the Moral Regeneration Movement, held a Provincial Prayer Session on Thursday, 16 October 2025, at Graceland Hotel in Secunda, within the Govan Mbeki Local Municipality.

nnnn

The event was dedicated to the Class of 2025 as learners prepare to sit for their final examinations. The prayer gathering sought to instil hope, strengthen faith, and unite communities in support of learners during this critical stage of their academic journey.

nnnn

MEC for Education, Ms Lindi Masina, urged faith-based communities across Mpumalanga to keep learners in their prayers. “Today, we gather in prayer, not in fear, but in faith. We stand united in spirit to seek divine favour and protection for the Class of 2025 as they prepare to begin their National Senior Certificate examinations in just five days,” she said.

nnnn

Quoting scripture, MEC Masina encouraged learners to remain strong and courageous: “Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged, for the Lord your God will be with you wherever you go.”

nnnn

Honouring Teachers

nnnn

The session also coincided with Teachers’ Month, providing an opportunity to recognise the dedication of educators. Four teachers from Mpumalanga were honoured at the National Teaching Awards, with Mr Thulani Sibiya from the Ehlanzeni District receiving the title of Best Teacher in South Africa.

nnnnnnnn

“Teachers are the true custodians of hope, the architects of knowledge, the reservoirs of dreams, and the builders of our nation’s future,” said MEC Masina. She praised Mr Sibiya’s achievement as a testament to dedication and humility, describing him as a source of pride for the province.

nnnn

Learners Encouraged to Stay Focused

nnnn

With 69,980 candidates registered to write this year’s examinations, the MEC assured parents and communities that all systems are in place to ensure a credible and secure exam process. Invigilators have been trained, centres audited, and security reinforced to maintain Mpumalanga’s record of integrity over the past 14 years.

nnnn

To learners, MEC Masina offered words of encouragement: “You are ready. You are capable. You are destined for greatness. Stay focused. Believe in yourself. Honour your teachers and your parents by giving your very best.”

nnnn

The session ended with a collective prayer, uniting communities, teachers, parents, and faith leaders in support of the province’s learners.

post_title: Probe Finds Overloading and Faulty Brakes in Limpopo Bus Crash
post_content:
n

The Ministry of Transport has released preliminary findings into the deadly bus crash on the N1 north that killed 43 people on Sunday.

nnnn

According to the Road Traffic Management Corporation (RTMC), the bus, which was travelling to Zimbabwe, was severely overloaded, carrying 91 passengers in a vehicle designed to seat only 62. Investigators found that only five of the bus’ ten brakes were functional, while the trailer’s braking system was not working at all.

nnnn

The investigation further revealed that the driver was speeding down a mountain pass, worsening the risks posed by the overloaded and unroadworthy vehicle.

nnnn

The RTMC has been instructed to inspect the bus company’s entire fleet to determine roadworthiness and to assess the company’s accountability for the condition of its vehicles. Maintenance records, service history, and the roadworthy certificate of the bus will be scrutinised. The Anti-Corruption Unit will also examine which testing centre issued the roadworthy certificate.

nnnn

Authorities will look into whether DNC coach depots operating in South Africa comply with safety standards, with compulsory inspections ordered at border posts for their fleet.

nnnn

The final report on the crash is expected within 21 weeks.

nnnn

n

post_title: Social Development DG Suspended Amid Appointment Scandal
post_content:
n

The Department of Social Development is facing renewed controversy following the suspension of its Director-General, Peter Netshipale. He is accused of gross dishonesty and bringing the department into disrepute.

nnnn

Netshipale’s suspension relates to the signing of a five-year employment contract, despite the Cabinet having only approved a one-year tenure. His contract was later amended after Minister Sisisi Tolashe initially described the matter as a clerical error when addressing Parliament last week.

nnnn

The situation has since escalated, with Tolashe charging Netshipale not only for the contract discrepancy but also for failing to properly oversee appointments in her office. These appointments have attracted negative publicity, including the case of a 22-year-old chief of staff accused of falsifying her CV. Allegations have also surfaced around a special advisor allegedly receiving a second salary from another government department.

nnnn

Netshipale, who is due to reach retirement age next year, has been given until Monday to respond to the charges.

nnnn

The chairperson of Parliament’s Portfolio Committee on Social Development, Bridget Masango, has indicated that Minister Tolashe may be called back to explain the sudden shift in her position and the mounting allegations.

n

post_title: From Church Choir to Award-Winning Music Star
post_content:
n

Dennis Makhubela, popularly known as King Xikaveni, has emerged as a standout talent in South Africa’s music scene. An award-winning R&B and disco singer, he recently released a groundbreaking EP titled Kuwa Rale Thyakeni, which is already making waves across the industry.

nnnn

King Xikaveni’s journey began in the humble setting of his church choir, where he first discovered his vocal gift. ‘I started singing from church at an early age, even during Sunday school,’ he recalls. ‘I was born with this gift.’

nnnn

His soulful voice and captivating melodies quickly gained recognition, setting him on a path that would lead beyond his hometown of Mpumalanga.

nnnn

Over the years, his musical style evolved significantly. Inspired by local Xitsonga artist Thomas Chauke, King Xikaveni initially considered pursuing traditional Xigaza music. ‘At first, I didn’t want to sing or do disco. I wanted to do Xigaza,’ he explains. ‘But I realised my community was used to disco music. To connect with them, I had to stick to what they loved.’

nnnn

Despite his preference for other genres, adapting to disco helped him win the support of his community and build his initial fan base.

nnnn

Before fully pursuing music, King Xikaveni studied Electrical Engineering at Mopani TVET College, a path that reflected his determination to succeed despite challenges. ‘I was not known, so it was very difficult at first when I released my first album with Junior Mkhari,’ he admits. Yet his perseverance paid off. His breakthrough came in 2021 with the release of his debut album, Volume ya Rirhandzu, which received positive attention and laid the foundation for his rise.

nnnn

In 2019, he began releasing disco tracks that resonated strongly with his audience. ‘I kept pushing, and eventually, my music started to reach more people,’ he says. His hard work culminated in winning the Best R&B Singer award at the 2024 Radio Bushbuckridge Music Awards, cementing his reputation as a formidable artist.

nnnn

Collaborations with seasoned musicians further boosted his profile. He is proud to be the first artist from Bushbuckridge to work with legends such as Sunglen Chabalala, Cool B and Mozambique’s Makhwirhi Baloyi. ‘It’s a great honour to work with these legends,’ he reflects. ‘It shows that my hard work is paying off and that I’m making my community proud.’

nnnn

King Xikaveni is also a businessman. He owns King Xikaveni Construction, an electrical company that reflects his entrepreneurial spirit.

nnnn

His versatility shines through in his many collaborations, including the hit track Ava Hlahluveli with Mozambican artists, which expanded his reach beyond South Africa’s borders. Singles such as Phosta Nkatanga and Wrong Number also strengthened his growing reputation.

nnnn

A major challenge came in early 2025, when he was forced to change his producer. Instead of slowing him down, the setback gave him renewed determination. The result was his latest EP, Kuwa Rale Thyakeni, featuring collaborations with Stanley Chiloane, Kenny Khosa and Cool B.

nnnn

Reflecting on his journey, King Xikaveni emphasises the importance of resilience. ‘Music is my life. No matter the hurdles, I keep pushing. I want to inspire young artists from my community to chase their dreams,’ he affirms.

nnnn

n

post_title: Man Killed and Woman Injured in Calcutta Tavern Shooting
post_content:
n

Police in Calcutta have launched an investigation following a fatal shooting at a local tavern on Friday night, 17 October 2025.

nnnn

According to police, officers responded to a report at around 22:00 and arrived to find a man and a woman lying in a pool of blood with gunshot wounds. Sadly, the 46-year-old man was declared dead at the scene by medical personnel. The woman was rushed to a nearby hospital for urgent medical treatment.

nnnn

It is believed that the victims, who were reportedly in a relationship, were together at the tavern when unknown armed suspects allegedly opened fire and fled immediately after the shooting.

nnnn

Police recovered a 9mm pistol with a visible serial number at the scene. The firearm has since been seized for further investigation.

nnnn

The motive behind the shooting is not yet known. Police are appealing to anyone with information that could assist in identifying or tracing the suspects to contact Lieutenant Colonel Sikhumbuzo Ceko on 082 922 9902, or to call the Crime Stop number on 08600 10111. Community members may also submit anonymous tips via the MYSAPSAPP. All information will be treated with strict confidentiality.

n

post_title: Young Entrepreneur Blooms With Ribbon Bouquets
post_content:
n

In the heart of Mkhuhlu, a determined young woman has turned adversity into opportunity, launching a business that is winning hearts and inspiring hope. Pacience Lwazi Mokoena, the founder of Lwaa’s Bouquet, officially opened her handmade bouquet brand on 20 September 2025 after months of struggling to secure employment or a learnership.

nnnn

Instead of surrendering to disappointment, Mokoena chose to carve her own path. Her business specialises in hand-crafted floral arrangements made entirely from ribbon, with every rose and bouquet designed from scratch. What began as an idea to keep her creativity alive has blossomed into a service cherished by her community.

nnnnnnnn

“Starting this business has allowed me to be my own boss, be creative with floral arrangements and contribute to my community by providing a personalised service,” Mokoena said.

nnnn

The response from Mkhuhlu residents has been overwhelmingly supportive. Locals praise not only the unique artistry of her ribbon roses but also the personal touch she brings to each creation. From birthdays to weddings, her bouquets are becoming a signature choice for special occasions.

nnnn

Mokoena explained that her secret lies in the detail and care she puts into every piece. “We hand craft roses from scratch using ribbons, and every piece is made with love,” she said.

nnnn

Though still in its early stages, Lwaa’s Bouquet is already planting seeds of bigger dreams. Mokoena envisions opening multiple branches in the future, creating opportunities for herself and others, while inspiring young people facing similar challenges to embrace entrepreneurship.

nnnn

Her journey is a powerful reminder that resilience, creativity and community support can turn struggle into success. With each ribbon rose, she is not only building a business but also weaving hope for the next generation of entrepreneurs in Bushbuckridge.

n

post_title: Community Urged to Help Find Missing Violetbank Nurse
post_content:
n

Police in Bushbuckridge are appealing to the public for assistance in locating 35-year-old Armstrong Monareng from Violetbank. Monareng, who works as a male nurse at Dwarsloop Clinic, has been missing since Wednesday, 15 October 2025.

nnnn

According to the police, he left home that morning to report for duty but never returned. His family and colleagues have not heard from him since, and efforts to trace his whereabouts have so far been unsuccessful. At the time of his disappearance, Monareng was dressed in his work uniform.

nnnn

Police are urging anyone who may have seen him or has information that could help trace him to come forward. Community members can contact Warrant Officer Busisiwe Dlamini on 082 056 9507 or call the Crime Stop line on 08600 10111. Tip-offs can also be submitted anonymously via the MySAPS App.

nnnn

Authorities have assured the public that all information will be treated with strict confidentiality, and callers may remain anonymous.

nnnn

The search continues as concern grows among family, friends and the community.

post_title: Mpumalanga’s GBV Crisis Demands Urgent Action
post_content:
n

On 18 October 2025, community leaders, activists and survivors gathered online for a gender-based violence (GBV) symposium focusing on Mbombela. The event exposed how GBV continues to devastate families, children and even healthcare workers. At the same time, local courts are hearing two of the province’s most harrowing cases: the murders of Hillary Gardee and Dr Nondumiso Nkosi.

nnnn

The symposium highlighted the dangers of “sugar daddy culture”, which fuels teenage pregnancies and exploitation of young girls. Speakers warned that older men who prey on vulnerable children trap them in cycles of poverty and abuse. Another key theme was financial abuse, a silent but destructive form of GBV that keeps victims powerless.

nnnn

This issue resonates strongly with the Nkosi case. Dr Nkosi, a respected medical practitioner, was shot dead in November 2024 in the Riverside Virgin Active parking lot. Her estranged husband, Sifiso Sibanyoni, has been charged with premeditated murder and denied bail. The State revealed he allegedly benefited from more than R1.5 million in life insurance payouts after her death. The case has sparked community protests and raised concerns about the lethal role of financial control in abusive relationships.

nnnn

The Gardee trial has also drawn national attention. Hillary Gardee, daughter of EFF deputy president Godrich Gardee, was murdered in 2022. The case stalled in 2023 when they key witness disappeared, but it has now resumed at the Mpumalanga High Court. The family has urged prosecutors not to “fumble” again. This trial underscores how delays and weak witness protection repeatedly undermine justice in GBV cases.

nnnn

The symposium also addressed the emotional toll of GBV on healthcare workers, who face burnout from constant exposure to violence. Presentations called for survivor-centred support, consent education in schools, and rewriting masculinity narratives to shift responsibility onto men rather than victims.

nnnn

If Mpumalanga is to turn the tide, awareness must lead to action. This means stronger witness protection, time-bound prosecution standards, survivor support services, and school-based prevention. Hospitals also need GBV desks to help both patients and staff.

nnnn

The symposium offered solutions, and the courts remind us of the stakes. Unless urgent steps are taken, Mbombela risks being remembered for GBV headlines rather than for the safety and dignity of its people.

post_title: IFP president Velenkosini Hlabisa at the party 50th anniversary celebration Picture The Citizen
Hlabisa Warns of Illegal Migration Crisis
post_content:
n

Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) president Velenkosini Hlabisa has described illegal migration as a national crisis and called for stricter employment priorities for South Africans.

nnnn

He was speaking in Soweto at the weekend where the party marked its 50th anniversary. Hlabisa said companies should adopt an 80–20 employment ratio, reserving at least 80% of jobs for South Africans. He linked this to the need to create opportunities for young people, women and small business owners, warning that without this, the country’s prosperity would remain out of reach.

nnnn

The IFP leader argued that illegal migration places a heavy strain on the fiscus, compromises national security and undermines job creation. Estimates suggest that up to 15% of South Africa’s population may be undocumented, adding further pressure on already fragile resources.

nnnn

While firm on the need to secure borders and defend local jobs, Hlabisa acknowledged the importance of foreign nationals with scarce skills, saying that legal migration remains vital for economic growth.

post_title: President Cyril Ramaphosa is set to deliver the keynote address
Ramaphosa Pledges Action on Rising Hunger
post_content:
n

President Cyril Ramaphosa says overcoming poverty and tackling the cost of living remain top priorities for the Government of National Unity (GNU).

nnnn

In his weekly newsletter on Monday, the President revealed that 15 to 16 million South Africans still face inadequate or severely inadequate access to food.

nnnn

“Access to nutritious food directly affects the physical health and development of individuals and societies,” he wrote.

nnnn

Ramaphosa stressed that South Africa is one of only 29 countries where the right to food and water is written into the Constitution.

nnnn

“The Constitution imposes a duty on the state to take reasonable legislative and other measures, within its available resources, to progressively realise this right,” he said.

nnnn

Since 1994, government has implemented a range of initiatives — from legislative reform and nutrition programmes in clinics to the National School Nutrition Programme, which feeds more than nine million learners every day.

nnnn

The President highlighted that social grants and free services have played a vital role in easing pressure on households.

nnnn

“In South Africa, the social wage accounts for approximately 60% of spending by Government before interest payments. This is amongst the highest of upper-middle income countries,” he noted.

nnnn

A 2021 World Bank report praised the country’s social assistance system, saying it “effectively reduces poverty and inequality rates.”

nnnn

Despite these interventions, millions remain food insecure. “In a context of high unemployment and poverty and limited economic growth, many households across the country are finding it difficult to afford nutritious food,” Ramaphosa said.

nnnn

Statistics South Africa reports that food inflation continues to climb, with meat and vegetable prices putting household budgets under strain.

nnnn

The President acknowledged that external factors — such as transport costs, drought and global supply chain disruptions — affect prices, but he also criticised unfair practices in the sector.

nnnn

“Practices like price-fixing that inflate food prices are directly contributing to food insecurity for households,” he warned.

nnnn

Ramaphosa urged retailers to do their part.

nnnn

“As retailers work to grow their market share among low-income households, they have a responsibility to ensure this includes affordable healthy food choices such as plant and animal proteins, fruits and vegetables,” he said.

nnnn

He added that food security remains a “society-wide effort” and called on communities, businesses and government to strengthen initiatives that ensure no South African goes hungry.

post_title: Fake Labour Department Worker Arrested After Years
post_content:
n

A 42-year-old man who posed as an employee of the Department of Employment and Labour has been arrested after evading justice for more than two years.

nnnn

According to the Hawks in Mpumalanga, the suspect, identified as Kwena Mohlala, was rearrested in the early hours of Saturday, 18 October 2025, at Ivory Park in Gauteng. His arrest followed an intensive operation by the Secunda-based Serious Corruption Investigation team, which executed a warrant that had been outstanding since his disappearance.

nnnn

Mohlala was initially arrested in February 2022 in Piet Retief after attempting to convince a legitimate Department of Labour employee to fraudulently process fake Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) claims. He allegedly promised to share the proceeds with the employee, who instead reported the matter to the Hawks.

nnnn

When Mohlala met with the employee on 22 February 2022, the Hawks monitored the meeting closely and arrested him after he handed over five fraudulent claim forms containing details of applicants from Mpumalanga, KwaZulu-Natal, and Gauteng.

nnnn

After being granted bail, Mohlala appeared in court three times before absconding. A warrant for his arrest was then issued.

nnnn

During his latest arrest, investigators found a notebook in his possession containing numerous identity numbers, bank account details, and uncompleted UIF claim forms, suggesting he may have continued his fraudulent activities.

nnnn

Provincial Head of the Hawks in Mpumalanga, Major General Nico Gerber, commended the investigation team for their dedication.

nnnn

“The suspect’s actions indicate that he has not ceased his criminal activities. He must explain how he obtained personal details of people who have never met him before. I really appreciate the commitment from our team, and I believe more information will be exposed soon,” said Major General Gerber.

nnnn

Mohlala appeared before the Piet Retief Magistrate’s Court on Monday, 20 October 2025, and has been remanded in custody until 28 October 2025 for a formal bail application.

post_title: Cllr Fane Donates Food to Support Matrics
Cllr Fane Donates Food to Support Matrics
post_content:
n

Ward Councillor Mafia Fane has extended a helping hand to matric learners in Ward 11, Nkomazi, as they prepare for their final examinations. On Monday, 20 October 2025, the councillor donated three cows and 15 bags of maize meal to three secondary schools in KaHoyi Village – Sophungane, Ntiyi, and Zenzele.

nnnn

The donation is meant to supplement meals during the matric school camps, which commenced on Monday and will run until 20 November, when the last paper is written. These camps are designed to provide learners with a focused environment to study and revise ahead of the crucial examinations.

nnnn

During the handover, Cllr Fane urged school principals not to exclude learners whose parents cannot afford to pay camp fees. He emphasised that education should be accessible to all, regardless of family financial challenges.

nnnn

“I have been reliably informed that a number of learners were excluded from attending the camps because their parents could not contribute financially. I humbly and respectfully request principals to bring all excluded learners back so that no child is left behind,” said Cllr Fane.

nnnn

He noted that many families in Ward 11 are economically disadvantaged, and denying learners the opportunity to attend these camps would only deepen existing inequalities. “This small donation is meant to supplement the feeding plan so that it accommodates even those who come from indigent and destitute backgrounds,” he added.

nnnn

Cllr Fane, who adopted the three schools after taking office in October 2022, reaffirmed his commitment to supporting education in the ward. He concluded by wishing all matric learners in Nkomazi well as they begin their final examinations.

nnnn

“The future of this municipality depends on you. We believe in your potential and are standing by you during this important journey,” he said.

post_title: Mkhuhlu Teachers Protest Over Unfair Principal Appointment
post_content:
n

Teachers from the Mkhuhlu Circuit took to the streets on Tuesday, 21 October 2025, to protest against what they call an unfair and irregular appointment of the new principal at Mapaleni Primary School.

nnnn

Led by the South African Democratic Teachers’ Union (SADTU), the educators marched to the Mkhuhlu Circuit offices demanding accountability from Circuit Manager Mthethwa, whom they accuse of hiring the new principal without following proper procedures or consulting the union.

nnnn

According to SADTU, Mthethwa appointed a principal from the Ehlanzeni Circuit after the resignation of former principal, Silaule. The union alleges that information about Silaule’s resignation was deliberately withheld until January 2025, when the newly appointed principal suddenly assumed duty.

nnnnnnnn

Union representatives say this is not the first time Mthethwa has been accused of favouritism, claiming she has been placing her relatives in senior positions within major schools across the circuit. “We are tired of this kind of corruption. The department is not helping at all. How can they investigate the principal and the circuit manager without suspending them?” said one SADTU representative.

nnnn

Teachers and union members have been protesting since February, accusing the Department of Education of turning a blind eye to the situation. The group has vowed to continue marching to the Mkhuhlu Circuit offices every Tuesday and Wednesday until their concerns are addressed.

nnnn

They warned that if the matter is not resolved by January 2026, when schools reopen, they will embark on a full-scale strike that could disrupt the start of the academic year.

nnnn

For now, tensions remain high as teachers call for transparency, fairness, and urgent intervention from the provincial education department.

post_title: MEC Masina Applauds Makhosana High’s Ongoing Excellence
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga MEC for Education, Lindi Lettie Masina, paid a special visit to Makhosana Manzini High School on Tuesday, 21 October 2025, to congratulate the school on its 30 years of excellence and to motivate the matric class of 2025 as they began their final examinations.

nnnn

The school, officially opened in 1995 and named after the late Alfred Makhosana Manzini, celebrated its 30th anniversary on Saturday, 18 October 2025. Over the years, it has built a solid reputation for outstanding academic performance and community impact.

nnnn

This year, the school achieved an impressive 84% pass rate in the trial exams, an improvement from last year. Out of 250 matric learners sitting for the final examinations, 43 learners who are struggling have been placed in special programmes to ensure they perform well in the finals.

nnnn

Makhosana Manzini High currently accommodates 1,973 learners with 59 teachers, resulting in overcrowded classrooms — the smallest holding 55 learners and the largest 112. Despite these challenges, the school continues to top the district’s performance charts, attracting partnerships and sponsorships that support its mission of excellence.

nnnnnnnn

The MEC’s visit had originally been planned to coincide with that of G20 officials, but their trip was cancelled after a storm on Sunday disrupted landings at Kruger Mpumalanga International Airport, forcing flights to be rerouted to Johannesburg.

nnnn

During her visit, MEC Masina commended the school’s resilience and commitment to education, calling it “a model of determination and success.”

nnnn

The principal expressed pride in the school’s achievements and revealed plans to introduce a transformative learning model offering two pathways — academic and vocational — to cater to learners’ diverse strengths and career ambitions.

nnnn

“Makhosana Manzini High is a school of excellence,” he said. “We aim to continue shaping learners who are ready for the future — whether in universities, workplaces, or their communities.”

post_title: Severe Flight Disruptions Hit Kruger Airport
post_content:
n

Kruger Mpumalanga International Airport (KMIA) has confirmed severe disruptions to scheduled flights due to the suspension of instrument flight procedures (IFPs) by the South African Civil Aviation Authority (SACAA). The suspension follows Air Traffic and Navigation Services' (ATNS) failure to meet critical deadlines to maintain the validity of these procedures.

nnnn

The airport assured travellers that its runways, lighting, and instrument landing systems (ILS) are fully functional and regularly audited. "The suspension of instrument flight procedures is not due to any non-compliance by KMIA," the airport said in a statement.

nnnn

Without approved IFPs, aircraft can only land or take off under clear weather conditions, leading to delays, cancellations and diversions. The disruptions have affected hundreds of passengers travelling between Johannesburg, Cape Town and Kruger Mpumalanga International Airport since last week.

nnnnnnnn

According to reports, ATNS has suspended more than 200 IFPs nationwide since July, including those at regional airports in Polokwane, Richards Bay and Mthatha. The delays are linked to a backlog in renewing procedures that require SACAA approval.

nnnn

The Mpumalanga Tourism and Parks Agency (MTPA), which oversees KMIA, said it is working closely with airlines to minimise inconvenience. "We will continue to keep the public informed as ATNS works to resolve the issue," said the MTPA.

nnnn

Tourism businesses in the province fear that the disruptions could impact visitor numbers to the Kruger Lowveld region, especially as the festive season approaches.

nnnn

KMIA and its airline partners await ATNS to complete the required submissions so SACAA can reinstate the flight procedures. Passengers are advised to check with airlines before travelling and to monitor updates from the airport.

post_title: Executive Mayor Hosts Wellness and Leadership Empowerment Seminar
post_content:
n

The Bushbuckridge Local Municipality hosted a Wellness and Leadership Empowerment Seminar on Wednesday, 22 October 2025, led by the renowned motivational speaker, educator, and leadership coach, Dr David Molapo.

nnnn

The seminar, initiated by Executive Mayor Lydia Moroane, aimed to inspire municipal employees, community leaders, and young professionals to prioritise personal wellness while strengthening their leadership abilities.

nnnn

Mayor Moroane emphasised the importance of wellness in leadership. "As leaders, we carry the responsibility of serving our people with both strength and humility. Wellness is the foundation that allows us to lead with clarity and integrity," she said.

nnnn

Dr Molapo captivated the audience with his trademark energy and practical wisdom. He encouraged attendees to embrace self-awareness, discipline, and emotional wellness as key ingredients of impactful leadership. "You cannot lead others if you have not first learned to lead yourself. Leadership begins within — through purpose, character, and consistency," he said.

nnnnnnnn

An iconic yet sometimes polarising figure in Africa, Dr Molapo is the founder of the I Can Leadership Institute Africa and CEO of I CAN 4IR. He also serves as the Dean of Logos University USA's Southern African Campus but describes himself, above all, as an educator.

nnnn

Attendees left the seminar inspired and motivated to serve their communities with renewed purpose.

post_title: Over 1,300 Suspects Nabbed in Operation Shanela
post_content:
n

 A total of 1 327 suspects were arrested during a high-impact, multi-departmental crime-fighting blitz held across the province between 16 and 19 October. The latest phase of Operation Shanela II saw police intensify efforts to curb criminal activity in Mpumalanga, working alongside various law enforcement agencies and government departments.

nnnn

During the four-day operation, authorities conducted 12 475 actions, which included searches, roadblocks, tracing of wanted suspects, and compliance inspections at businesses, farms and mines. Police searched more than 7 600 people, 362 premises, 1 679 vehicles, and held 214 vehicle checkpoints as well as 14 roadblocks.

nnnn

The crackdown also led to 31 successful arrest raids targeting wanted suspects, including four linked to rape and nine facing charges of assault with intent to cause grievous bodily harm.

nnnn

Offences for which arrests were made include murder, attempted murder, rape, robbery, assault, burglary, illicit mining, illegal immigration, human trafficking and driving under the influence. A significant number of arrests – 198 – were related to drunk driving, while 103 people were arrested for immigration-related offences.

nnnn

Police also confiscated large quantities of illegal items, including 501 litres of alcohol, 140 rounds of ammunition, 15 handguns, 4 rifles, 55 Mandrax tablets, dagga, crystal meth and nyaope. Counterfeit goods, contraband, copper cables, precious metals and 17 vehicles were also recovered.

post_title: MEC Takes Test Ride on New Electric Bus
post_content:
n

Mpumalanga MEC for Public Works, Roads and Transport, Thulasizwe Thomo, kicked off an early morning with a symbolic yet practical bus ride aboard Buscor’s new electric bus as part of the ongoing October Transport Month activities.

The test ride, joined by MEC for Community Safety, Security and Liaison, Jackie Macie, and senior officials from both departments, was aimed at experiencing first-hand the benefits of the electric bus currently on pilot by Buscor. The initiative marks a major step towards greener, safer, and more sustainable public transport in the province.

nnnnnnnn

MEC Thomo applauded Buscor for leading innovation in the transportation sector and championing clean energy solutions. “Public transport plays a vital role in driving inclusive growth and reducing carbon emissions. We commend Buscor for leading by example in embracing green technology and ensuring that our people have access to modern, efficient, and environmentally friendly transport,” he said.

nnnn

He further emphasised that strong collaboration between government and the private sector remains essential in improving the efficiency, safety, and reliability of public transport services.

nnnn

The Transport Month campaign continues to promote the importance of safe, accessible, and sustainable transport systems that contribute to Mpumalanga’s economic and social development.

post_title: Bushbuckridge Outraged After Child-Rape Accused Granted Bail
post_content:
n

The Bushbuckridge community has been left shocked, angered and deeply disappointed after a man accused of raping a 14-year-old girl was granted bail. Residents who had previously marched and appealed for him to remain behind bars now feel their voices were ignored, reigniting community outrage and calls for justice.

nnnn

The case, which first drew public attention in September, involves a Grade 7 learner from the Alexandria area of Bushbuckridge who reportedly displayed severe emotional distress at school following the alleged rape by her stepfather in August. Community members, supported by the Kaizer Mgiba Branch, gathered outside the Mkhuhlu Magistrate’s Court in September, demanding that the accused not be released on bail for the safety of the victim and other children. Councillor Sabelo Mkhabela stated firmly: “We do not want Norman to get bail. The children in our neighbourhood are not safe with him at large.”

nnnn

Despite these concerns, the accused’s lawyer submitted bail applications on 10 and 14 October. On 21 October 2025, the court granted bail of R5,000, allowing the accused to return to Bushbuckridge while awaiting trial. His next court appearance is scheduled for 21 November 2025. The decision has sparked fear among residents who believe the safety of children has been compromised and that the justice system has failed to prioritise the vulnerability of the victim.

nnnn

Parents have expressed their dismay, questioning how a person facing such a grave charge can be permitted to return to the same community where children continue to live, learn and play. “If he’s out on bail, what about our children? We demanded no bail — but we got it anyway,” said one resident. Families are calling for stricter monitoring of bail conditions to ensure the accused does not intimidate the victim or interfere with the case.

nnnn

As the matter continues, schools and community organisations have been urged to remain vigilant regarding children’s wellbeing. Parents are encouraged to report any signs of trauma or distress and to seek immediate help if necessary. Community leaders are also planning further engagements to keep residents updated. Many have pledged to attend the 21 November hearing to show solidarity with the victim and to ensure justice is not delayed.

nnnn
