post_title: Father Shoots Teenage Son in Levubu
post_content:
n

The Limpopo police are investigating a harrowing domestic violence case in Ha-Mutsha Tshitandani village, Levubu, after a father allegedly shot and killed his teenage son before attempting to end his own life.

nnnn

The incident occurred early on Sunday morning at around 06:17. Police spokesperson Colonel Malesela Ledwaba confirmed that officers rushed to the scene after receiving reports of a shooting. Upon arrival, they found the 53-year-old father lying in a pool of blood outside the house, still alive but injured, with a 9mm pistol and spent cartridges nearby.

nnnn

Inside the house, police discovered the lifeless body of the 17-year-old victim, identified as Ranwedzi Mulaudzi. He had sustained fatal gunshot wounds to the head and was declared dead at the scene.

nnnn

Preliminary reports suggest the father, a member of the South African National Defence Force stationed outside Mookgophong, turned the firearm on himself after fatally wounding his son. He was rushed to hospital under police guard and has since been placed under arrest.

nnnn

Provincial police commissioner Lieutenant General Thembi Hadebe condemned the incident and expressed concern over the rise of domestic violence across Limpopo. “These tragic acts tear families and communities apart. We urge anyone facing conflict or abuse at home to seek help before resorting to violence,” she said.

nnnn

Investigations continue into the motive. Police sources indicated that domestic tensions may have played a role, and it has been alleged that the teenager recently returned from the Moloto Discipline Centre, where he was undergoing rehabilitation for substance abuse.

nnnn

Authorities have urged the community to remain calm and allow the police to complete their investigation.

n

post_title: Six Armed Suspects Bomb ATM in Mkhuhlu Plaza
post_content:
n

A security guard on night duty narrowly escaped harm when six armed suspects stormed Mkhuhlu Plaza in the early hours of Thursday, 23 October. The guard reported that, at around 2 am, while patrolling the shopping centre, he noticed movement near the small gate beside the A1 Food Store.

nnnn

As he approached, gunshots were fired in his direction, forcing him to run for cover. Moments later, a loud explosion was heard from the A1 Food Store. When the scene was safe enough to inspect, the guard found the shop’s front glass door shattered. The EasyPay ATM and the store safe had been blown open, with an undisclosed amount of cash stolen. Specialised units, including a Bomb Expert and the Local Criminal Record Centre (LCRC), attended the scene.

nnnn

They collected several exhibits including 15 rifle cartridge cases, two live rifle rounds, 25 nine-millimetre pistol cartridge cases, and one live nine-millimetre round. CCTV footage later confirmed that six suspects entered the plaza through the small gate, though their identities remain unknown.

nnnn

Police have launched an investigation and urge anyone with information to come forward.

post_title: Residents Voice Concerns at Bushbuckridge Mayoral Imbizo
post_content:
n

Bushbuckridge community members used the recent Mayoral Imbizo to raise their concerns directly with the Executive Mayor of Bushbuckridge, Cllr ML Moroane, and the District Mayor of Ehlanzeni, Cllr E.I.T. Shabangu, during a joint engagement held in Ward 9.

nnnn

The Imbizo created a platform for residents to speak openly about issues affecting their daily lives. Several government departments were present, including Home Affairs, which assisted residents with essential services.

nnnn

One of the key updates shared was that Bushbuckridge Local Municipality is making progress in developing the Acorn Smart City at Arconhoek, a project aimed at modernising the area and boosting local development. The municipality also confirmed that every area in Bushbuckridge will have two street lights installed to help improve safety at night.

nnnnnnnn

Housing development remains a priority, with two houses already completed in Shatale and two more currently under construction in Boikhutso.

nnnn

However, crime has emerged as a major concern raised by residents, who say it continues to affect their peace of mind and livelihood. “We are tired of living in fear. Crime is getting worse and we don’t see enough action. Our children are not safe,” said a frustrated community member.

nnnn

The mayors are committed to addressing the concerns raised and encourage the community to continue participating in such platforms to ensure accountability and progress.

nnnn

The Imbizo forms part of ongoing efforts to strengthen communication between the municipality and its residents, ensuring that service delivery challenges are acknowledged and addressed.

post_title: Six Killed in Dullstroom Road Crash
post_content:
n

A tragic collision on the R540 near Dullstroom on Sunday afternoon has claimed the lives of six people. The crash, which occurred at around 14:00, involved a GWM sport utility vehicle (SUV) and a minibus taxi in what authorities have described as a T-bone collision.

nnnn

All six victims, who died at the scene, were passengers in the taxi. A further eight people sustained serious injuries, including seven passengers and the SUV driver. The taxi driver suffered minor injuries. Those injured were rushed to a hospital in Belfast for medical treatment.

nnnn

The cause of the crash has not yet been determined, and an investigation is currently underway.

nnnn

Mpumalanga MEC for Community Safety, Security and Liaison, Jackie Macie, urged motorists to exercise greater vigilance to prevent further loss of life on the province's roads.

nnnnnnnn

"We remain deeply concerned by the number of fatalities caused by road crashes that could be avoided with more responsible driving. Motorists should always be mindful that their mistakes while driving could be devastating not only for them but for other road users," said Macie.

nnnn

He expressed disappointment that such a tragedy occurred during October Transport Month – a period dedicated to promoting road safety and responsible transport.

nnnn

"This needs to change and motorists are an integral part of making the road safer," he added.

nnnn

Macie conveyed his heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and wished the injured a speedy recovery.

nnnn

The Mpumalanga Department of Community Safety, Security and Liaison is urging witnesses or anyone with information to assist authorities as investigations continue.

nnnn

Issued by the Mpumalanga Department of Community Safety, Security and Liaison

post_title: Man Arrested for Unlicensed Firearm in Bushbuckridge

A 40-year-old man has been arrested after he was allegedly found in possession of an unlicensed firearm and ammunition at a tavern in Mandela Village, Bushbuckridge.

nnnn

The arrest was carried out by members of the Enhlazeni District crime prevention team on Friday, 24 October 2025, at around 22:00. Police acted on a tip-off regarding a man believed to be carrying a firearm and reportedly wanted in connection with other cases under investigation by the Bushbuckridge SAPS.

nnnn

Upon arrival at the tavern, officers identified a suspect matching the description provided. A search was conducted, leading to the discovery of an unlicensed firearm and eight live rounds of ammunition.

nnnn

The suspect was taken into custody and charged with possession of an unlicensed firearm and ammunition. Police are continuing with investigations to determine whether he may be linked to other criminal activities in the area.

nnnn

He is expected to appear at the Bushbuckridge Magistrates' Court on Monday, 27 October 2025.

post_title: Acornhoek United Claim First League Victory
post_content:
n

Acornhoek United secured their first win of the ABC Motsepe League campaign with a thrilling 2–1 comeback against Sibange Young Bucks at Orks Sporting Field on Saturday, 25 October.

nnnn

The visitors, Sibange Young Bucks, broke the deadlock in the 65th minute. However, Acornhoek United captain Shaka Manzini rose to the occasion, equalising with a powerful header in the 83rd minute before sealing the victory with a stunning free kick just three minutes later. His brace ensured the home side collected their first three points of the season.

nnnn

Meanwhile, Bushbuckridge favourites Liver Brothers FC suffered their first defeat of the league, losing 2–0 away to Fannie Battalions.

nnnn

In other fixtures, Nkomazi-based side The Bees fell 2–1 to Cape Town City in the Motsepe Foundation Championship, while Kruger United were held to a goalless draw by Gauteng's Gomora United.

n

n

The much-anticipated Water Lekgotla was successfully held on Monday, 27 October 2025, at Thulamahashe Community Hall, where government, community leaders and residents gathered to confront the urgent and worsening water crisis in Bushbuckridge.

nnnn

More than 40% of water produced for residents is lost before reaching households, schools and businesses. While infrastructure breakdown, burst pipes and ageing systems remain major contributors, community-related issues such as illegal connections, unreported leaks and the careless use of water continue to deepen the crisis.

nnnn

Residents from various areas attended, including those from Thulamahashe and New Forest, who shared the harsh reality of daily water struggles. Many New Forest households receive water only once a week, on Wednesdays, and residents queue along the main road to fill containers. Some walk more than 5km to access water, often pushing wheelbarrows or carrying heavy buckets in the scorching sun.

nnnnnnnn

Thulamahashe resident Nomsa Magagula expressed frustration, saying, "We report leaks and burst pipes, but nothing gets fixed for weeks. We are losing water every day while families are without a drop to drink."

nnnn

A New Forest community member, Sibusiso Nkuna, added, "We can't survive on water once a week. Some of us walk long distances just to fill a bucket. It feels like we are forgotten."

nnnn

Speaking at the event, the Executive Mayor of Ehlanzeni District said the government must urgently rethink reliance on water tanks. "Government must stop water tanks. The problem we are faced with today is the issue of water tanks — people go around selling water. Some of the same people selling water are the ones who destroy water infrastructure so that they get business with their water tanks. The Constitution says water is life; every citizen must have clean water, and that does not mean we should sell water to people. The Constitution says we must give people clean water. Water problems started with the water tanks."

post_title: South Africa leads Africa with approval of new anti-HIV injection
post_content:
n

South Africa has made history as the first African country to approve a long-acting injection to prevent HIV. The South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA) announced on 27 October that it had registered lenacapavir, developed by global pharmaceutical company Gilead Sciences.

nnnn

Unlike daily tablets, the injection is given only twice a year. It begins with an initial jab and two tablets, followed by six-monthly injections. It is intended for HIV-negative adults and adolescents weighing at least 35 kg who are considered at high risk. Authorities emphasise that it should still be used alongside safe sex practices, as it does not guard against other sexually transmitted infections.

nnnn

Health Minister Dr Aaron Motsoaledi said government plans to roll out the injection in March 2026. With one of the world’s highest HIV rates, South Africa hopes the new option will fill critical gaps in prevention for people who struggle with daily medication.

nnnn

SAHPRA chief executive Boitumelo Semete Makokotlela described the development as a “game-changer.”

nnnn

A key breakthrough is cost. Originally priced at $28 000, the treatment will now be made available for about $40 (roughly R730) per person per year through partnerships with local and international manufacturers. Government also plans to integrate it into national health funding.

nnnn

Preparations are underway to train health workers, secure supply chains and run awareness campaigns. For communities, especially those facing stigma or barriers to consistent pill use, a discreet six-monthly injection offers new hope in the fight against HIV.

nnnn

high-priority medicines. 

nnnn

Crucially, costs have been drastically reduced. Gilead and six partnering pharmaceutical companies, including one in Egypt, aim to produce the injection at a cost of around US $40 per person per year — a steep drop from the original US $28 000. 

nnnn

Furthermore, the government plans to integrate lenacapavir into its domestic financing mechanisms and move towards routine funding within two years. Local manufacturing capacity is also being pursued. 

nnnn

What this means for local communities

nnnn

For communities across South Africa — urban, rural and peri-urban — this development offers hope. A six-monthly injection could provide a more manageable and discreet prevention option for individuals who struggle with daily medication, or who face social or structural barriers to consistent adherence.

post_title: Sisonke Gender Justice Strengthens Community Against GBV
post_content:
n

Sisonke Gender Justice is making a powerful impact across the Bushbuckridge Municipality by empowering women and the wider community to take a stand against gender-based violence (GBV) and to promote gender equality.

nnnn

The organisation hosts regular community dialogues that provide safe spaces for residents to share their experiences, concerns and ideas on how to address GBV. These gatherings encourage open discussions, strengthen unity and help communities to create practical solutions to the challenges they face.

nnnn

After the dialogues, Sisonke compiles the information and presents it to the municipality. This process highlights the existing gaps in service delivery and policy implementation, ensuring that GBV issues are not only heard but also acted upon at the local government level.

nnnn

Beyond raising awareness, Sisonke also supports survivors of GBV by offering case monitoring. The team works closely with the National Prosecuting Authority, tracks case progress, and accompanies victims to court. This commitment ensures that survivors are not left to navigate the justice system alone, while also holding institutions accountable for proper handling of cases.

nnnn

Through its dedicated efforts, Sisonke Gender Justice continues to bring the Bushbuckridge community together in the fight against GBV, fostering resilience, support and hope for a safer society.

post_title: Rapist Receives Seven Life Sentences In Limpopo
post_content:
n

The South African Police Service (SAPS) in Limpopo has welcomed the heavy sentence imposed on a 27-year-old man, Vongani Sobala Shikwambana, who was convicted of multiple counts of rape and robbery. The Nkowankowa Regional Court handed down the sentence on Monday, 27 October 2025.

nnnn

Shikwambana received seven life imprisonment terms for seven counts of rape and an additional 15 years for robbery with aggravating circumstances. The crimes date back to 26 February 2017, when the accused attacked three young girls, aged 9, 11, and 13, at Bonn Village under the Letsitele policing area.

nnnn

Armed with a panga and accompanied by a dog, he forced the children into nearby bushes where he raped them. Two of the victims managed to escape, but the youngest was subjected to further assault before the attacker robbed her of two cellphones.

nnnn

A joint effort by community members and police led to his swift arrest. The case was thoroughly investigated by Detective Sergeant Phumudzo Mabongo of the Tzaneen Family Violence, Child Protection and Sexual Offences (FCS) Unit. His meticulous work ensured that the evidence presented in court was strong and comprehensive, resulting in a conviction on all charges.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of Police in Limpopo, Major General Jan Scheepers, praised the investigating officer and the prosecution team for their dedication in securing justice for the young victims.

nnnn

“This sentence sends a strong message that crimes against women and children will never be tolerated. We applaud the outstanding work by the investigating officer and the criminal justice system for ensuring that such a heartless perpetrator is permanently removed from society,” said Major General Scheepers.

nnnn

The outcome has been welcomed as a significant victory in the fight against gender-based violence, reinforcing the commitment of the police and justice system to protect the most vulnerable members of the community.

post_title: Two Women Killed in Separate GBV Incidents
post_content:
n

Police in Mpumalanga are investigating two separate incidents of gender-based violence (GBV) that claimed the lives of two women in Masoyi and Vosman over the weekend.

nnnn

The first incident occurred on Monday morning, 27 October 2025, at Jerusalem Trust in Masoyi, near a tavern. Police were alerted after a 22-year-old woman was stabbed to death by her 26-year-old male partner. Officers found the victim lying on the front lawn of the suspect’s home with multiple stab wounds to her neck. Emergency Medical Services (EMS) declared her dead at the scene.

nnnn

According to police, the suspect’s father reported that his son had stabbed his girlfriend during a domestic dispute and was hiding in a locked room. Officers forced entry, apprehended the injured suspect, and took him to hospital under police guard. He is expected to appear in court soon on a charge of murder.

nnnn

In a separate case on Sunday evening, 26 October 2025, police were called to a domestic violence complaint in Vosman. Upon arrival, they found the body of a woman with a gunshot wound to the chest in a back room occupied by a tenant. A man, believed to be her partner, was discovered on the floor with a gunshot wound to the head. A firearm was found beside him. Paramedics confirmed both were deceased at the scene. Preliminary investigations suggest the man shot the woman before turning the gun on himself.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General Dr Zeph Mkhwanazi, condemned the murders, urging community members to seek professional or community support when facing domestic difficulties rather than resorting to violence.

nnnn

“These tragedies are a reminder that violence is never a solution. We appeal to communities to speak out and seek help before situations escalate,” he said.

nnnn

Police have opened cases of murder in both matters, with an additional inquest docket in the Vosman case.

post_title: Motsoaledi Relaunches TB Caucus with Renewed Commitment
post_content:
n

Health Minister Aaron Motsoaledi has declared that South Africa is entering a new era of accountability, innovation, and political will in the fight against tuberculosis (TB).

nnnn

Speaking at the relaunch of Parliament’s TB Caucus in Cape Town, Motsoaledi said the platform would unite MPs, government departments, and civil society to address the country’s leading infectious killer. He emphasised that TB must be given the same urgency as pandemics such as HIV and COVID-19.

nnnn

“We cannot continue treating TB as a background disease. It is curable, yet it still kills more people than any other infectious illness. That shows the fight has not been loud enough, coordinated enough, or politically driven enough,” he said.

nnnn

The minister reminded lawmakers that TB has claimed more lives globally than HIV, cholera, malaria, and even COVID-19 combined. “It kills silently, and that is why we must speak louder,” he added.

nnnn

The reactivation of the TB Caucus, he explained, would give Parliament a stronger role in ensuring accountability, funding, and policies that match the scale of the crisis. He called on MPs to make TB their personal fight on behalf of the communities they represent.

nnnn

As part of new measures, the Department of Health has launched a public-facing TB dashboard. This digital tool allows real-time monitoring of TB testing and treatment across the country and forms part of the End TB Campaign, which aims to test five million people annually.

nnnn

Motsoaledi also called for broader involvement, stressing that TB is not only a health issue but a societal one. “We need the voices of communities, the strength of civil society, and the leadership of Parliament. Ending TB is not a dream; it is our shared responsibility,” he concluded.

post_title: Bushbuckridge Entrepreneur Builds Beauty Brand from Scratch
post_content:
n

From humble beginnings in Alexandria (Marite), Bushbuckridge, Goodness Mokoena Mlimi is building more than just a beauty brand — she is creating hope, confidence, and opportunity for her community.

nnnn

Born and raised in Mpumalanga, Goodness discovered her passion for beauty at the age of 21. Her skills in hairstyling, haircutting, nail care, and make-up quickly became more than just a hobby. "I realised my talent could open doors for me and for others," she recalls.

nnnn

In 2022, she officially registered her company, GM Beauty Care (Pty) Ltd, determined to turn her passion into a sustainable business. Like many entrepreneurs, her journey was far from easy.

nnnn

"When I started, I didn't have enough customers, so I began selling cosmetics and cleaning products from other companies," she explains. "That kept me going until I found the opportunity to start manufacturing my own products in 2023."

nnnn

Operating from her home, Goodness began experimenting with her own range of perfumes, foam baths, dishwashing liquids, and fabric softeners. The process came with challenges. "My first products didn't come out right. I lost money trying again and again. It was only on the third attempt that everything came out perfectly," she says proudly.

nnnn

What kept her going was a greater vision — to create jobs and empower others in Bushbuckridge. "I didn't give up because I want to see people, especially women, earning their own income. It hurts me to see others suffering while there are opportunities we can create for ourselves," she says.

nnnn

Goodness believes that empowerment can change lives and reduce social issues such as gender-based violence and crime. "When people have something to do and earn their own money, they live with dignity. It's painful, especially for women, to depend on others for basic needs. That's why I encourage everyone to start small and grow from there."

nnnn

Her business model reflects that belief. She sells her products to others at a wholesale price so that they can resell them and make a profit. "I don't make much from it, but I know I'm saving lives and giving hope. We are proud of what we're doing because we hurt no one — we are building together."

nnnn

Despite her determination, Goodness continues to face major challenges. "At the moment, I don't have the proper machinery or a delivery vehicle, and my products still need to go through professional testing," she explains. "But I'm not discouraged. Every day I learn something new, and I keep moving forward."

nnnn

Her message to others is simple but powerful: "While you're waiting for a job, start selling something. Don't wait for a big opportunity to begin — the little you have can take you far. Stop doubting yourself and use what you've got."

nnnn

Goodness's business, trading as GM Health and Beauty Care (Pty) Ltd, carries a name full of meaning — GM stands for Great Moments. For her, every step forward is indeed a great moment worth celebrating.

nnnn

"I dream of making GM Beauty Care a big brand that creates jobs for others," she says. "I'm still struggling, but I'll never lose hope. With the right support and sponsorship, I know this dream will come true."

nnnn

Through her resilience and vision, Goodness Mokoena Mlimi is proving that real beauty lies not only in appearance, but in courage, perseverance, and the will to uplift others.

n

post_title: Toddler Dies After Being Left Inside Car
post_content:
n

A tragic incident in Seshego has left the community in shock after a three-year-old girl was found dead inside a locked vehicle on Monday, 27 October 2025.

nnnn

Police confirmed that a culpable homicide case has been opened at Seshego Police Station following the child’s untimely death.

nnnn

According to reports, police were alerted at around 15:10 to Seshego Hospital, where they discovered a blue Toyota Corolla Cross parked in the hospital yard. A medical practitioner informed officers that the child had been found locked inside the car with the windows closed. Despite efforts, she was pronounced dead at the scene, having succumbed to extreme heat and lack of oxygen.

Preliminary investigations suggest that the mother had left her daughter in the vehicle earlier that morning, at approximately 07:00, while attending a handover session at the medical facility. It appears she forgot about the child until the devastating discovery later that afternoon.

Police have confirmed that a post-mortem will be conducted to establish the exact cause of death. Investigations into the matter are ongoing.

Authorities have reminded the public of the severe dangers of leaving children unattended in vehicles, even for a short period.

post_title: Two Sentenced for Dagga Dealing Offence
post_content:
n

Two people — a South African man and a woman from Eswatini — have been sentenced for dealing in dagga following their arrest near the Waverley/Dumberton borderline in Mpumalanga.

nnnn

According to the South African Police Service (SAPS), Mahlubi Dlamini (26) and Nelisiwe Nokwazi Lukhele (31) were each sentenced by the Mayflower Periodical Court to six months’ imprisonment, wholly suspended for five years, on condition that they are not convicted of a similar offence during that time.

nnnn

They were also fined R15 000 or face an additional six months in prison. Both have been declared unfit to possess firearms.

nnnn

The pair were arrested on 21 October 2025 after police officers on patrol stopped and searched a Ford Ranger with Gauteng registration plates, discovering 12 dagga rolls and three sacks wrapped in black plastic bags. The confiscated dagga weighed 50.28 kilograms, with an estimated street value of R211 176.

nnnn

Police confirmed that the vehicle belongs to a person from Eswatini, and investigations are continuing to determine whether it was used in other crimes.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General Dr Zeph Mkhwanazi, welcomed the outcome, saying the police remain committed to stopping drug trafficking in the province.

nnnn

“Our roads cannot be used to traffic dagga. Those who continue to do so will find themselves behind bars,” said Major General Mkhwanazi.

nnnn

The swift action by police and the court’s firm sentence were praised as an example of ongoing efforts to curb drug-related crimes in border areas of Mpumalanga.

post_title: MEC Masina Calls on Public to Read
post_content:
n

The MEC for Education in Mpumalanga, Ms Lindi Masina, has called on the provincial community to embrace reading as a daily practice that strengthens both the individual and society.

nnnn

Speaking at the relaunch of the MEC Book Club in Umjindi, Mbombela, on Tuesday afternoon, Masina stressed that reading must become a social norm. The event was held in collaboration with the National Education Collaboration Trust (NECT) and Room to Read.

nnnn

“We are making a commitment to lead from the front, to read, discuss, and promote books that inspire thought and community dialogue,” she said. “When the MEC reads, teachers read. When teachers read, learners read. And when learners read, communities thrive.”

nnnn

The MEC highlighted statistics showing that 41% of learners in the province are at emerging reading levels, 45% are evolving, and only 13% are enhancing their skills. She urged parents to play their part by reading at home during family gatherings, at bedtime, or around the dinner table.

nnnn

Masina further encouraged the use of digital platforms, e-books, and literacy apps to complement traditional reading. “Technology must not replace reading, it must enhance it,” she noted.

nnnn

She expressed gratitude to NECT, its leadership, and author Mr MVG Lephoko for their role in making the relaunch a success. She also thanked the media for amplifying literacy campaigns across the province.

nnnn

Looking ahead, the MEC outlined a vision for every district to host reading forums, every school to form Parent Reading Committees, and every community to establish book circles.

nnnn

“By this time next year, we want every child to hold a book not because it is prescribed, but because they love it,” Masina concluded.

post_title: Court Rules Against Bookmakers Offering Casino Games
post_content:
n

The National Gambling Board (NGB) has welcomed a ruling by the Supreme Court of Appeal (SCA) which confirms that bookmakers are not permitted to offer roulette and other casino-style games under the guise of fixed-odds betting.

nnnn

The case, Portapa (Pty) Limited t/a Supabets and Others v Casino Association of South Africa and Another, centred on whether bookmakers could legally provide online bets linked to outcomes of casino games. The SCA ruled that such practices contravene the Gauteng Gambling Act of 1995 and reaffirmed the principle that each mode of gambling—casinos, betting, limited payout machines, and bingo—must be licensed and regulated separately.

nnnn

According to the judgment, casino games cannot be classified as “events or occurrences” for betting purposes under the National Gambling Act of 2004. This means that bookmakers who offer such games are effectively operating casinos illegally.

nnnn

The NGB described this as an “unfair practice”, highlighting that licensed casinos face stricter tax obligations and regulatory controls compared to bookmakers. “The ruling affirms that interactive gambling remains unlawful in South Africa,” said Acting Chief Executive Officer, Mr Dukwana.

nnnn

The Board warned that any bookmaker found offering unlawful casino-style betting could face serious consequences. Under the National Gambling Act, the NGB has the power to confiscate winnings from illegal gambling activities. Offenders also face criminal sanctions, including fines of up to R10 million or imprisonment of up to ten years.

nnnn

Mr Dukwana called on all Provincial Licensing Authorities to tighten oversight of their licensees and act swiftly in cases of non-compliance. “We urge bookmakers to comply fully with the law and refrain from practices that undermine the integrity of the gambling industry,” he said.

nnnn

The ruling has implications beyond Gauteng, extending to all bookmakers nationwide. The NGB stressed its commitment to working with stakeholders to ensure consistent enforcement, protect consumers, and safeguard the country’s gambling policy framework.

n

The Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation (Hawks) has confirmed that the decommissioning and cleaning of a multi-million-rand clandestine drug laboratory in Volksrust, Mpumalanga, is set to be completed by Friday, 31 October 2025.

nnnn

The case was referred to the Hawks’ Secunda-based Serious Organised Crime Investigation team for further handling. Authorities successfully opposed bail for the foreign suspects, leading to them abandoning their applications. The South African, believed to be the caretaker of the farm where the laboratory was located, was granted bail of R50,000.

In addition to arrests, the Hawks commenced decommissioning of the property, which had been declared a public health and environmental hazard. Officials warned that the presence of chemicals carried a significant risk of fire and other dangers to the community. The premises have remained under police guard since the initial raid.

nnnn

All chemicals and equipment used in the illegal drug manufacturing process are to be destroyed, marking a complete shutdown of the operation.

nnnnnnnn

Provincial Head of the Hawks in Mpumalanga, Major General Nico Gerber, said the investigation remains ongoing.

n

Authorities emphasised that the clean-up is vital to safeguard the health and safety of residents while ensuring accountability for those responsible.

post_title: Skukuza Safari Lodge Open Despite Fire Incident
post_content:
n

The Skukuza Safari Lodge in the Kruger National Park remains fully operational after a fire damaged part of its restaurant dining hall on Wednesday, 29 October 2025.

nnnn

According to SANParks, all diners were safely evacuated during the incident, and no injuries were reported. Investigations are currently under way to determine the cause of the fire.

nnnn

The blaze, along with the water used to extinguish it, destroyed a section of the restaurant roof. However, to minimise disruptions, a temporary dining facility has been set up using back-up systems, ensuring that guests continue to enjoy their stay without major inconvenience.

nnnn

Clean-up and repair operations are already in progress, with further updates expected once assessments are completed.

SANParks and AHA extended their gratitude to the Skukuza Airport and SANParks emergency response teams, as well as the Bushbuckridge Fire Brigade, for their swift action in containing the fire and protecting guests and staff.

Despite the damage, management has assured visitors that the lodge remains open and safe.

post_title: South Africa Reaffirms Stance Against Ivory Trade
post_content:
n

The government has strongly dismissed reports claiming that South Africa plans to support lifting the international ban on the commercial trade of ivory and rhino horn.

nnnn

According to the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), such claims are without basis and do not reflect the country’s longstanding commitment to responsible wildlife management under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES).

nnnn

The department reaffirmed that South Africa remains committed to global cooperation and biodiversity protection ahead of the upcoming CITES COP20 meeting later this year, where international discussions on wildlife trade and conservation are expected to take centre stage.

nnnn

South Africa’s stance is rooted in conservation rather than commerce, with policies guided by science, ethics, and sustainability. The country’s approach focuses on safeguarding biodiversity while also supporting the livelihoods of communities living alongside wildlife.

nnnn

The DFFE emphasised that its participation in CITES processes seeks to protect endangered species, maintain ecological balance, and ensure that conservation efforts bring long-term social and economic benefits.

nnnn

In addition, the department outlined ongoing work with regional and international partners to curb poaching, dismantle trafficking networks, and reinforce wildlife law enforcement. Its stated priority remains securing a future in which elephants, rhinos, and people can coexist sustainably.

post_title: Government Moves to Tighten University Oversight
post_content:
n

Higher Education and Training Minister Buti Manamela has introduced draft reforms aimed at tightening oversight of South Africa’s public universities. The proposed reporting regulations are intended to detect governance and financial problems before they escalate into full crises.

nnnn

The reforms follow recent unrest at the University of Fort Hare, where protests escalated into violent clashes with police and security personnel, resulting in the torching of university buildings and the suspension of academic activities. The University of the Free State also suspended its academic programme earlier this month due to widespread protest action across its three campuses.

nnnn

The draft amended Regulations for Reporting by Public Higher Education Institutions, published this week, will be open for public comment for 30 days. The new rules propose stricter and more frequent reporting by university councils, vice-chancellors, and management structures. They are designed to encourage early detection of governance failures and prevent financial mismanagement or leadership paralysis from causing long-term damage.

nnnn

Under the proposed regulations, universities will be required to submit mandatory mid-year and annual reports. These will include detailed disclosures on infrastructure backlogs, employment equity, student debt exclusions, consultant spending, legal costs, and activities of commercial subsidiaries. The framework will also formalise the role of Ethics Officers and require council members to declare potential conflicts of interest, undergo performance assessments, and report on executive remuneration.

nnnn

The Department of Higher Education and Training emphasised that the reforms are not intended to limit institutional autonomy but rather to strengthen accountability and restore public confidence in the sector. The new reporting rules form part of a broader shift towards proactive governance across the Post-School Education and Training System.

post_title: MER CEO Secures Key Global Regulatory Roles
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga Economic Regulator (MER) has announced a major milestone for its Chief Executive Officer, Vusi Mtsweni, who has been appointed to two influential roles within the continental and international gambling regulatory landscape.

nnnn

At a continental level, Mtsweni has been confirmed as a member of the African Lotteries & Gaming Association (ALGA) CEO’s Forum Steering Committee. nnnn

On the international stage, Mtsweni has also been appointed to the Board of Trustees of the International Association of Gaming Regulators (IAGR), representing the African Region. IAGR is a global network that fosters collaboration among regulators, promotes knowledge exchange, and strengthens best practices in gambling governance.

nnnn

“These appointments are not only a recognition of Mtsweni’s personal leadership but also a proud moment for the Mpumalanga Economic Regulator and the Province of Mpumalanga,” said Ms Thando Lamula-Shirinda, Chairperson of the MER Board. “They position our province and our country at the forefront of global discussions on responsible gambling and sustainable regulation.”

nnnn

Under Mtsweni’s guidance, MER has prioritised governance reform, modernised regulatory systems, and championed responsible gambling initiatives in line with international standards. His involvement in these continental and global forums is expected to boost cross-border cooperation, enhance regulatory capacity, and strengthen knowledge-sharing across Africa.

nnnn

The Mpumalanga Economic Regulator congratulated Mr Mtsweni on the achievement, noting that his appointments bring honour not only to MER but also to South Africa’s broader regulatory fraternity.

Rural Learners Excel Despite National School Readiness Decline
post_content:
n

With school readiness levels across South Africa continuing to decline, a rural nonprofit in KwaZulu-Natal is offering a beacon of hope for the sector.

nnnn

As Term 4 assessments take place in Early Childhood Development (ECD) centres nationwide, concerns are mounting about how well children are prepared to enter Grade R or Grade 1. National figures paint a bleak picture: only 42% of children are meeting age-appropriate developmental milestones, according to the latest Thrive by Five Index. This decline follows an earlier 2021 study showing that just 46% of children nationally were ‘on track’, with only 31% reaching expected levels in KwaZulu-Natal.

nnnn

However, Thanda, a nonprofit organisation based in Mtwalume, is proving that quality early learning is possible even in low-resource settings. Despite families in the area surviving on an average of R1,225 a month, Thanda’s ECD programme has achieved remarkable results. Its most recent assessments show that 95% of Grade 00 learners are developmentally on track, compared to just 30% nationally.

nnnnnnnn

Thanda’s success lies in its evidence-based curriculum, which uses storybooks and provides teachers with step-by-step guidance for every activity. “Our results show that a structured curriculum can transform classroom practice down to the minute,” said Angela Larkan, Thanda’s Co-Founder and Executive Director. “Even in the most remote classrooms, consistent mentorship and a clear teaching framework make all the difference.”

nnnn

Experts emphasise that readiness is about more than literacy and numeracy. It includes well-being, social confidence, emotional regulation, and the ability to adapt to structured environments. By addressing these areas, Thanda demonstrates how targeted investments in early education can strengthen South Africa’s wider school system.

nnnn

As the country prepares for 2026, Thanda’s model offers valuable lessons for policymakers and practitioners alike: quality early learning is not only possible, it is essential for building a stronger foundation for future success.

post_title: Partnerships Bring Vital Family Healthcare Closer Home
post_content:
n

Access to healthcare remains one of South Africa’s most pressing public health challenges, particularly for families in rural and low-income communities. Long travel distances, overburdened clinics, and limited screening opportunities often mean that preventable or manageable conditions go undetected until they become severe.

nnnn

To address these gaps, Bonitas Medical Fund recently joined forces with key partners to host a Family Health Day at Elukwatini Stadium in Mpumalanga on 30 October 2025. The initiative, supported by the Gift of the Givers Foundation, the Rotary Action Group for Family Health & AIDS Prevention (RFHA) and the Department of Health, formed part of the national Close the Gap campaign, which seeks to place one million additional people on antiretroviral therapy by December 2025.

nnnn
n

“Our goal is to take healthcare to where people are,” said Dr Themba Hadebe, Clinical Executive at Bonitas Medical Fund. “When families have easy access to screening and counselling, they’re more likely to seek help early and prevent health issues from becoming life-threatening.”

n
nnnn

The Family Health Day offered an integrated package of free services, including HIV testing and counselling, TB screening, diabetes and vital-signs checks, STI testing, and immunisations. Additional services such as optometry and audiology screening, dental care, mental health support, and menstrual health education were provided through Gift of the Givers.

nnnnnnnn

Dr Hadebe emphasised that clustering multiple services in one place helps reduce three major barriers to healthcare — cost, travel distance, and fragmented service delivery. “Families were able to have several checks done in a single visit, making it easier to access comprehensive care,” he added.

nnnn

Studies have shown that access to healthcare among low-income households is often determined by proximity, affordability, and quality of facilities. Vision, hearing, and dental issues are frequently left untreated as people prioritise survival needs. By offering these services directly to communities, initiatives like this help restore dignity and promote early intervention.

nnnn

The Mpumalanga Family Health Day also contributed to national health priorities by expanding testing, treatment referrals, and education, while addressing the broader determinants of family well-being — including mental and oral health.

nnnn
n

“Good health begins with access,” Hadebe concluded. “When the public and private sectors work together, we can close the gap and give families the care they need to live healthier, more productive lives.”

post_title: Banks Dismiss Rumours of November Withdrawal Limits
post_content:
n

South African banks and the Reserve Bank have moved to reassure the public following widespread rumours that new restrictions on cash withdrawals would take effect from 1 November 2025.

nnnn

Messages circulating on social media and unverified websites claimed that banks would impose nationwide limits on how much cash customers could withdraw daily or weekly, sparking concern among account holders.

nnnn

However, checks by this publication have found no official confirmation of such measures from the South African Reserve Bank (SARB) or any of the country’s major commercial banks, including Standard Bank, Absa, FNB, Nedbank and Capitec.

nnnn

According to the SARB, no directive has been issued requiring banks to restrict withdrawals. Banks themselves have also not released any statements introducing new withdrawal caps.

nnnn

While some account types already include daily or monthly limits that can be adjusted by customers for security purposes, these have long been standard features of online and mobile banking – not new regulations.

nnnn

Financial experts warn that rumours like these often resurface online and can cause unnecessary panic. They advise consumers to always verify financial claims through official channels such as bank websites, customer care lines or the Reserve Bank’s notices.

nnnn

In a statement earlier this year, the SARB cautioned South Africans to be wary of misinformation spread through unofficial platforms: “All policy or regulatory changes are communicated directly to the public through credible channels. Any claim of sudden or secret implementation is likely to be false.”

nnnn

Customers are encouraged to continue using their normal banking services without fear of sudden changes. Any updates affecting fees, transaction limits or account conditions will be formally communicated by each financial institution.

nnnn

post_title: The SACP’s Local Election Move Could Divide South Africa’s Democratic Movement
post_content:
n

South Africa is gearing up for local government elections expected between November 2026 and January 2027. As the country prepares for this crucial poll, debates around political participation are intensifying — particularly following the South African Communist Party’s (SACP) announcement that it will contest the elections independently.

nnnn

This decision has sparked strong reactions within the Mass Democratic Movement, raising concerns that the SACP’s move could weaken long-standing alliances and divide the working-class movement that has shaped South Africa’s political landscape since the struggle years.

nnnn

The Historic Alliance Between the SACP and ANC

nnnn

The SACP has historically positioned itself as the political vanguard of South Africa’s working class — championing the interests of the oppressed and exploited masses. For decades, it has been an integral partner in the Tripartite Alliance, working alongside the African National Congress (ANC) and the Congress of South African Trade Unions (COSATU).

nnnn

The alliance, forged in the struggle against apartheid, was described by former ANC President Oliver Reginald Tambo as “a living organism that has grown out of the struggle… reinforced by a common determination to destroy the enemy and by our shared belief in the certainty of victory.”

nnnn

Historically, both organisations maintained ideological independence while sharing a unified vision for a non-racial, democratic South Africa rooted in the principles of the Freedom Charter.

nnnn

Challenges in the Post-2024 Political Landscape

nnnn

Following the 2024 general elections, the ANC lost its outright majority in Parliament for the first time since 1994, securing just over 40% of the vote. The party also lost control in key provinces, including KwaZulu-Natal, Gauteng, and the Northern Cape.

nnnn

Although the ANC remained the largest party, it retained national power through a Government of National Unity (GNU). However, the SACP — part of this coalition — has expressed dissatisfaction with aspects of the arrangement, arguing that it compromises the progressive agenda that once united the alliance.

nnnn

The Risk of Division Ahead of the 2026 Local Elections

nnnn

The SACP’s decision to register with the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) to contest the 2026/27 local elections is likely to have significant political implications. Many members of the SACP and COSATU also belong to the ANC, which could lead to voter confusion and internal division at the local government level.

nnnn

Critics argue that this move could fracture the unity of the Mass Democratic Movement, historically rooted in cooperation between labour, the working class, and liberation structures. It may also open opportunities for civil society organisations such as SANCO and independent candidates to gain ground in municipalities across the country.

nnnn

Guarding the Gains of the Liberation Movement

nnnn

The alliance between the ANC and SACP has been central to South Africa’s political transformation. It has guided the country from apartheid to democracy and has been instrumental in advancing the rights of workers and the poor.

nnnn

As the 2026/27 local elections approach, it remains to be seen whether this alliance can withstand new political pressures or whether the SACP’s independent contestation will reshape the dynamics of progressive politics in South Africa.

n

It is further alleged that one of the suspects was a former friend of the victim. One of the accused is also a Grade 12 learner, who is expected to write his final examination while in custody.

nnnn

In a deeply emotional message, her father described Lusanda as:

nnnn

“A light in my life — my joy, my laughter, my reason to keep going.”

nnnn

He spoke of his sorrow, regret, and enduring love for his daughter, vowing never to let her memory fade or her death be in vain.

nnnn

The Mathabela family expressed heartfelt gratitude to all who have reached out with messages of love, support, and prayers during this devastating time.

nnnn

“Lusanda Mathabela will not be reduced to a statistic. Her life mattered, and there will be justice for her. We stand firmly against all forms of Gender-Based Violence,” the family stated.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of Mpumalanga, Major General Dr Zeph Mkhwanazi, has strongly condemned the senseless killing and praised the quick response of law enforcement.

nnnn

“It is shocking that such a young girl, with a bright future ahead, was killed in such a brutal manner. We thank the construction workers for alerting the family. The suspects will face the full might of the law,” said Major General Mkhwanazi.

nnnn

Lusanda’s death has sparked widespread grief across the province, with residents calling for justice and greater protection for young women. Community members gathered outside the court during the suspects’ first appearance, holding placards that read “Justice for Lusanda” and “Enough is enough.”

nnnn

nnnn

For many, Lusanda was more than a statistic—she was a daughter, a friend, and a young woman who had her whole life ahead of her. Her story has become a painful reminder of the continued violence faced by women and girls across South Africa.

post_title: Premier Ndlovu Leads United Front Against Gender-Based Violence
post_content:
n

Mpumalanga Premier Mandla Ndlovu has officially opened the first sitting of the Provincial Council on Gender-Based Violence and Femicide (GBVF), describing it as a defining step in the province's commitment to end violence against women and children.

nnnn

The inaugural session, held at the Emnotweni Arena in Mbombela on Thursday, brought together members of the Executive Council, mayors, traditional leaders, law enforcement officials, and representatives from civil society.

nnnn

Premier Ndlovu said the establishment of the Council marked a moment of "deep purpose and responsibility," aimed at strengthening coordination and accountability in addressing GBVF across all sectors of society.

nnnn

"We pledged to account, coordinate and provide leadership in fighting GBVF; to ensure effective implementation of the Provincial Strategic Plan; and to restore dignity to the citizens of Mpumalanga," he said.

nnnn

The Premier reminded attendees that President Cyril Ramaphosa had declared gender-based violence and femicide as South Africa's "second pandemic", highlighting its devastating impact on communities. He added that the issue continues to draw global attention, featuring prominently on the agenda of the upcoming G20 Summit, where world leaders are expected to endorse a Ministerial Declaration on Women's Empowerment.

nnnn

Premier Ndlovu further called for stronger community structures, including Rapid Response Teams, to ensure survivors receive immediate assistance and justice.

nnnn

Council Urges Action on Budgets, DNA Delays and Survivor Support

nnnn

Members of the GBVF Council used the occasion to spotlight the urgent challenges that continue to hinder justice and recovery for survivors.

nnnn

They stressed that the fight against GBVF requires more than awareness — it demands a full understanding of the "pathways" survivors navigate, from seeking shelter and counselling to standing in court and testifying.

nnnn

"When we talk about pathways, we're referring to the social support that strengthens a person to stand in court, the legal advice they receive before getting there, and the shelters that accommodate them as they try to rebuild their lives," the Council said.

nnnn

Civil society organisations within the Council have been working to integrate these services through Pathways to Justice meetings and stakeholder engagements. However, they warned that major gaps remain due to funding shortages, limited human resources, and weak coordination.

nnnn

"One of the strongest messages from our engagements is the urgent need for gender-responsive budgeting at municipal and provincial levels," they said.

nnnn

"While Integrated Development Plans acknowledge gender-based violence, their priorities are not supported by clear and funded commitments. Too often we are told there is no money — this must change."

nnnnnnnn

The Council also raised concern over the shortage of forensic nurses and social workers, noting that trauma-trained professionals are essential for supporting survivors of sexual violence. Delays in DNA results were identified as another significant obstacle to justice.

nnnn

"When DNA results take months, cases are struck off the roll and survivors lose faith in the system. We urgently need a dedicated DNA laboratory to ensure timely results," they added.

nnnn

Communities such as Bushbuckridge were highlighted as areas in need of fully functional one-stop centres, where survivors can access medical care, counselling, and legal support under one roof.

nnnn

"As the Council, we are not here merely to coordinate — we are here to take accountability and to hold one another accountable," the Council concluded.

nnnn

Closing the session, Premier Ndlovu called on all sectors to act with unity, compassion, and urgency.

nnnn

"Let us not fail the people we serve. Together, we can build a Mpumalanga where every person lives in safety, dignity, and respect," he said.

post_title: Four Security Guards Arrested for Attempted Murder
post_content:
n

Four private security officers have been arrested for attempted murder, malicious damage to property, and intimidation following a violent altercation at Nhlazatshe Crossing in Elukwatini earlier this week.

nnnn

According to a police statement issued by the Office of the Provincial Commissioner in Mpumalanga, the incident occurred on 4 November 2025, when the guards allegedly stopped a vehicle driven by a man and demanded to search it. The driver reportedly refused, leading to a heated argument.

nnnn

It is alleged that the security officers then began pelting the vehicle with stones and fired several gunshots at the driver, who managed to escape unharmed and reported the matter to the police.

nnnn

The suspects — Phumlani Muzi Nene (31), Mongameli Xaba (29), Mhlengu Shange (32) and Siyabonga Zondo (29) — were arrested later the same day. During the arrest, police confiscated four firearms, including two semi-automatic rifles, a shotgun, a pistol, and 104 live rounds of ammunition.

nnnnnnnn

The men appeared briefly before the Chief Albert Luthuli Magistrate's Court on 5 November 2025, where they were remanded in custody. They are expected to return to court on 12 November 2025 for a formal bail application.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of the South African Police Service in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, welcomed the arrests and praised officers for their swift response.

nnnn

"We commend our members for their unwavering dedication and commitment in ensuring that the law is upheld, regardless of who is involved," said Mkhwanazi.

nnnn

Police investigations into the matter are continuing.

post_title: Solar-Powered Boreholes Bring Hope to Cork Community
post_content:
n

Residents of Cork and Saringwa in Ward 23, Bushbuckridge, are celebrating a new era of clean water access following the official handover of solar-powered boreholes that promise to change daily life for hundreds of families.

nnnn

The project was delivered through a partnership between Innovation: Africa, Kruger Gate Hotel, and the Bushbuckridge Local Municipality (BLM), with Mbileni Engineers as the implementing contractor. It forms part of a broader initiative to bring sustainable water solutions to rural areas that have long struggled with unreliable supply and failing infrastructure.

nnnn

For years, villagers in Saringwa and surrounding sections have faced persistent water shortages, relying on streams or purchasing water from vendors at high cost. Now, with the installation of solar-powered pumps, storage tanks, and communal taps, many residents say they finally have access to safe and consistent water.

nnnn

“This project has brought relief to us,” said community member Maria Mhlongo, who lives near one of the newly installed taps. “Before, we used to wake up at dawn to fetch water far from home, but now our children can go to school clean and on time.”

nnnn

Closing the gap in access to clean water

nnnn

The initiative highlights the critical role that partnerships can play in bridging the service-delivery gap in rural municipalities like Bushbuckridge. By using solar energy, the boreholes eliminate the need for costly electricity connections and ensure round-the-clock operation even in off-grid areas.

nnnn

Beyond improving water access, the project has created local jobs and offered training opportunities to young people. Several residents were employed during the construction phase and received hands-on training in borehole drilling, plumbing, and solar maintenance — skills that can help them start small businesses or secure future employment.

nnnn

For communities where job opportunities are scarce, this approach not only addresses immediate needs but also contributes to long-term empowerment.

nnnn

Partnership for sustainable change

nnnn

The involvement of the private sector, particularly Kruger Gate Hotel, reflects a growing awareness among local businesses of the importance of investing in surrounding communities. Through collaboration with Innovation: Africa and the municipality, the hotel has helped ensure that development extends beyond its tourism footprint to directly benefit nearby villages.

nnnn

Local residents say they hope similar projects will reach other wards that still face chronic water shortages.

nnnn

“We are grateful, but we also hope more villages can get the same help,” added Mhlongo. “Water should not be a luxury — it’s something every family deserves.”

nnnn

Looking ahead

nnnn

As Bushbuckridge continues to face challenges in service delivery, such public-private partnerships are offering practical solutions that align with community needs. The solar-powered boreholes represent more than just infrastructure — they symbolise dignity, sustainability, and progress for the people who have waited far too long for reliable access to one of life’s most basic necessities.

n

Kruger National Park Staff Honoured for Excellence
post_content:

nnnn

post_title: Matikwana Hospital Strengthens Community Ties Through Open Day
post_content:
n

Matikwana Hospital opened its doors to the public on Friday, 7 November 2025, for its annual Open Day — a day dedicated to strengthening the bond between the hospital and the community it serves.

nnnn

The event aimed to educate residents about the hospital’s services, achievements, and innovations while encouraging health awareness and community involvement.

nnnn

Matikwana Hospital CEO, Matilda Makukule, said the initiative was meant to bridge the gap between the hospital and the people it serves.

nnnn

“We want the public to learn about the hospital and its services,” she explained. “We don’t want the hospital to be operating alone and the community operating alone. This day is about showcasing our work, engaging with the community, and promoting health awareness.”

nnnn

Various health stations were set up on the hospital premises, where visitors could undergo basic health screenings, receive health information, and ask questions about their wellbeing. Among the key focuses of the day was the Sazise campaign, which encourages patients to bring their identity documents when visiting the hospital to ensure proper record-keeping and service categorisation.

nnnn

Chairperson of the Matikwana Hospital Board, Given Nikiwe Ngobeni, highlighted the governance aspect of the event, stating that it forms part of the hospital’s accountability to the community.

nnnn

“As the board, we act as the mouth and ears of the public and liaise directly with the MEC. This open day reflects good governance and transparency, which is why it is held annually,” said Ngobeni.

nnnn

Local leaders also commended the hospital’s progress. Ward Councillor Bio Mpangana said the Open Day provided an opportunity for residents to see the hospital’s positive developments and take an active role in monitoring their own health.

nnnn

“The hospital is doing very well. This day allows the public to appreciate that progress and check the status of their health,” he said.

Adding to the celebrations, Bushbuckridge Executive Mayor, Cllr Lydia Moroane, visited the maternity ward, where she presented care packages to new mothers in honour of their newborns.

nnnn

In support of the hospital’s efforts, Old Mutual donated whiteboards and additional care packages for children admitted to the hospital, further demonstrating community partnership and corporate involvement in healthcare development.

nnnn

The day concluded with an atmosphere of unity and shared responsibility, reminding all that quality healthcare thrives when communities and institutions work hand in hand.

post_title: Is the Mushrooming of Political Organisations Strengthening or Weakening Our Democracy?
post_content:
n

Chapter Two, Section 19 of the South African Constitution, guarantees every citizen the right to make political choices. This includes forming or joining a political party, participating in its activities, campaigning for it, and standing for public office. It also affirms the right to free, fair and regular elections.

nnnn

In principle, this freedom strengthens democracy — but in practice, the explosion of political parties raises questions about effectiveness, accountability and stability.

nnnn

The Growing Political Landscape

nnnn

Currently, South Africa has 609 registered political parties, with 383 registered nationally and 226 registered provincially or municipally. The Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) regularly updates this list as parties become active or inactive.

nnnn

In Mpumalanga, six political parties are represented in the Provincial Legislature:

nnnn
    n
  • African National Congress (ANC) – 27
    • nnnn
  • Umkhonto Wesizwe (MK) Party – 9
    • nnnn
  • Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) – 7
    • nnnn
  • Democratic Alliance (DA) – 6
    • nnnn
  • Freedom Front Plus (FF Plus) – 1
    • nnnn
  • ActionSA – 1
    • n
nnnn

At the Bushbuckridge Local Municipality, the council has 11 parties represented following the November 2021 local government elections, distributed as follows:

nnnn

ANC – 53 | EFF – 8 | ISANCO – 5 | APC – 2 | DA – 2 | BRA – 2 | SAMHRA – 1 | DCM – 1 | BLM – 1 | ATM – 1

nnnn

The following table shows the composition of the council after past elections.

nnnnnnnn

While new parties continue to emerge, many fade away by the next election cycle. The ACDP, BRA, and PAC are examples of organisations that have declined significantly in representation over time.

nnnn

Purpose Versus Survival

nnnn

Historically, political parties were formed to address specific social or economic issues. For instance, the Pan Africanist Congress of Azania (PAC) was founded to champion land restitution, while the Bushbuckridge Residents Association (BRA) emerged to combat crime in the greater Acornhoek area.

nnnn

However, today, many parties seem more focused on survival and securing seats rather than driving genuine service delivery. Instead of uniting behind shared goals, political competition often fragments representation, dilutes accountability, and confuses voters.

nnnn

Electoral Systems and Accountability

nnnn

South Africa’s electoral system also plays a key role in this debate. At the local government level, ward councillors are elected directly by voters. However, at provincial and national levels, a proportional representation (PR) system is used — meaning voters cast ballots for parties, not individuals.

nnnn

Under this system, parties allocate seats based on the percentage of votes received, making it easy for party leadership to remove or replace representatives, as seen recently with the MK Party.

nnnn

If South Africa were to adopt a constituency-based system, citizens would vote directly for individual candidates to represent their areas, potentially improving accountability.

nnnn

Too Much of a Good Thing?

nnnn

While a multi-party system is a cornerstone of democracy, the sheer number of political parties — many of which lack clear policies or long-term sustainability — may weaken rather than strengthen governance. In several countries, only two dominant parties exist, ensuring clearer choices and greater stability.

nnnn

South Africa’s growing list of parties, many formed out of political disputes or short-term ambitions, risks fragmenting the electorate and complicating service delivery.

nnnn

Conclusion

nnnn

The formation of political parties is a constitutional right and a sign of a vibrant democracy. However, when political organisations multiply without a clear purpose, unity or accountability, they risk weakening rather than deepening our democratic values.

nnnn

As we move towards the 2026/7 local government elections, citizens must reflect carefully before voting — prioritising leadership that delivers tangible service and stability over endless political fragmentation.

n

post_title: Unusual but Wise? When a Man Waits Until 50 to Become a Father
post_content:
n

It is not often that a man openly declares his decision to postpone fatherhood until he is completely ready for the responsibility. Yet this is precisely what veteran broadcaster David Mashabela, known as King David, revealed in a recent interview with Mbuyiseni Ndlozi on POWER FM. He spoke candidly about having his first child at the age of fifty, explaining that his choice was deliberate and deeply personal rather than dictated by circumstance.

nnnn

Mashabela said he waited because he wanted to be financially stable, emotionally mature and mentally prepared before bringing a child into the world. His decision challenges the long-held belief in many South African communities that a man’s adulthood or masculinity is confirmed through early fatherhood. Instead, his story offers a refreshing perspective on responsibility and self-awareness.

nnnn

In South Africa, as in many parts of the world, men are often expected to marry and have children early in adulthood. The notion of a man deliberately delaying fatherhood is therefore unusual and even frowned upon in some circles. Yet Mashabela’s choice compels society to rethink what responsible parenthood really means. Waiting until one is ready may appear unconventional, but it can also reflect maturity, foresight and self-discipline.

nnnn

Many men feel enormous pressure to conform to social expectations. In cultures where fatherhood is viewed as a rite of passage, those who delay it are sometimes seen as avoiding responsibility. However, the modern economic and emotional realities of life paint a different picture. The cost of living is high, job security is uncertain, and raising children requires not only love but also consistent financial support and presence. For some, it makes far more sense to wait until one can provide stability and quality of life.

nnnn

Mashabela’s approach demonstrates that fatherhood is not a race to be first, but a journey to be walked with purpose. His decision to wait challenges the stereotype that a man’s value lies in how early he can start a family. Instead, it suggests that a man’s true strength lies in his ability to plan wisely, act responsibly, and prioritise the wellbeing of his future children over social approval.

nnnn

Becoming a father at fifty also redefines generational roles. It raises interesting questions about the meaning of age in parenting. While some may see it as late, others might argue that maturity brings patience, wisdom and emotional balance—qualities every child deserves in a parent.

nnnn

Mashabela’s story resonates with a broader social shift where both men and women are re-evaluating life choices once considered fixed. His openness helps to destigmatise men who choose to delay parenthood for practical and personal reasons. It encourages communities to view fatherhood not merely as an expected milestone but as a sacred responsibility that requires readiness in every sense.

nnnn

Ultimately, the timing of fatherhood should be a personal decision, not one determined by cultural pressure. Mashabela’s experience reminds us that being a parent is not about how soon one starts, but about how well one fulfils the role. His decision may seem unusual, but it also reflects a profound understanding of what it means to nurture, provide and love consciously.

n
nn

post_title: Brothers Extradited Over AKA and Tibz Murder Case
post_content:

Two brothers accused of involvement in the murders of rapper Kiernan “AKA” Forbes and celebrity chef Tebello “Tibz” Motsoane are expected to be extradited from Eswatini to South Africa today. Siyabonga Gezani Ndimande and Malusi Dave Ndimande were arrested in Mbabane earlier in Mbabane Eswatini, following a joint operation between South African and Eswatini police.

nnnnnnnn

Their return follows the withdrawal of their appeal against an extradition order granted by Eswatini authorities. The suspects face charges including murder, conspiracy to commit murder, and unlawful possession of firearms and ammunition.

The high-profile killings took place in February 2023 outside a Durban restaurant, shocking the nation and sparking widespread calls for justice.
