post_title: Tonga Roadshow Mobilises Community to Defeat Malaria
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga Department of Health marked SADC Malaria Day with an awareness roadshow in Tonga, Nkomazi Sub-District, on 7 November 2025. The initiative aimed to educate residents about malaria prevention and control, particularly in high-risk border areas.

nnnn

The event brought together malaria control staff, environmental health practitioners, surveillance and vector-control teams, spray operators, and partners from the Lubombo Spatial Development Initiative 2 (LSDI2). The march began at Tonga Hospital and proceeded to Tonga Mall, where participants carried placards with malaria awareness messages and handed out educational pamphlets to members of the public.

nnnn

Health officials continue to stress the importance of early testing, prompt treatment, and cooperation with indoor residual spraying campaigns to reduce malaria transmission. With summer approaching, communities are urged to remain vigilant and take precautions against mosquito bites.

nnnn

Malaria remains prevalent in the Lowveld, particularly in Ehlanzeni District, including municipalities such as Nkomazi and Bushbuckridge, where transmission is most intense. Uncommon symptoms can include dark or bloody urine, jaundice, abnormal bleeding, impaired consciousness, or difficulty breathing—all signs of severe malaria requiring urgent medical attention.

nnnn

Residents are advised to prevent malaria by using insect repellent, sleeping under treated nets, wearing long sleeves and trousers at dusk, closing windows at night, and supporting spraying campaigns. Early diagnosis and treatment save lives, and vigilance remains essential, especially in border and low-lying areas.

n

post_title: Women Living in Fear Amid Femicide Crisis
post_content:
n

In South Africa, I am weakened, afraid, vulnerable — and mostly afraid. We live in a country where femicide has thrived as a “just punishment” for women simply existing. From a young age, we have been taught to shrink ourselves, while our male counterparts have been groomed to see themselves as superior. What this has created is a world where women are unsafe, often from those closest to them.

nnnn

This violence is not new. It is a deep wound that has festered for centuries. Yet the blatant, vile attitude of “she must die” has become louder, more visible, and more frightening. It is destroying womanhood.

nnnn

Physical harm, humiliation, and death have become disturbingly normalised. Conversations about killing women for perceived betrayal are spoken of casually. I once overheard three young men say they would kill their girlfriends if they cheated — their tone was light, as if discussing football, not murder.

nnnn

Women in South Africa have been killed for “crimes” such as ending a relationship, refusing advances, or simply choosing themselves. How dare you walk away? How dare you say no? You must die.

nnnn

These deaths are rooted in a terrifying belief that women are not human — that we are possessions, pets, or slaves. Our children, too, are sometimes seen as tools or extensions of control. Even in public, a woman’s right to exist is questioned. For daring to walk tall, speak loudly, or reject unwanted attention, she can be slapped, insulted, or worse — branded with names like sifebe or jezebel for the “crime” of existing freely.

nnnn

To stand your ground in this country is an act of courage. But to remain silent is worse than death — because silence feeds the monster.

nnnn

The statistics lay bare the truth. South Africa’s femicide rate is five times the global average, according to the UN Office on Drugs and Crime. Police data shows that 1,101 women were murdered between July and September 2024 alone, meaning roughly 12 women are killed every day. In the same period, 15,000 sexual offences were reported — many against children. Most of these crimes were committed by men known to their victims.

nnnn

We are dying not at the hands of strangers, but at the hands of those who claim to love us.

nnnn

Unless we, as a society, decide that women’s lives matter, our collective humanity will continue to die with them.

n

post_title: SA Launches First Locally Made Oral Cholera Vaccine Trials
post_content:
n

South Africa has reached a historic milestone in public health, with Biovac receiving approval from the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA) to begin clinical trials for the country’s first locally manufactured oral cholera vaccine.

nnnn

This breakthrough positions South Africa as the only country in Africa capable of producing this life-saving vaccine entirely in-house — a significant step towards the continent’s goal of vaccine self-reliance.

nnnn

Minister of Health Dr Aaron Motsoaledi hailed the development as a moment of national pride.

nnnn
n

“The ability to manufacture a life-saving vaccine from start to finish right here at home strengthens our capacity to respond swiftly to potential outbreaks and enhances Africa’s self-reliance in vaccine production. This milestone aligns with the government’s vision of ensuring health security and universal access to essential medicines,” he said.

n
nnnn

Deputy Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation Dr Nomalungelo Gina echoed these sentiments, reaffirming government’s commitment to local manufacturing, technology transfer, and commercialisation of scientific innovation.

nnnn
n

“These efforts are vital not only for public health but also for job creation, skills development, and industrial growth — not just for South Africa, but for Africa,” she said.

n
nnnn

The launch event, held at Chris Hani Baragwanath Academic Hospital in Soweto, marked the first locally manufactured vaccine in over 50 years. Both ministers highlighted the urgency of the project, noting the increasing frequency of cholera outbreaks across Africa and the shortage of vaccines that has left many communities vulnerable.

nnnn

Cholera is a preventable disease that can be fatal during outbreaks if treatments such as oral rehydration therapy, antibiotics, and vaccines are unavailable.

nnnn

The Biovac vaccine development project is supported by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Open Philanthropy, the Wellcome Trust (UK), and the ELMA Vaccines and Immunisation Foundation.

nnnn

The African Union (AU) aims for 60% of routine vaccines used in Africa to be manufactured on the continent by 2030, a massive leap from the current figure of less than 1%.

nnnn

Phase 1 of the Biovac trial began in October 2025 at the University of the Witwatersrand’s Perinatal HIV Research Unit (Wits PHRU). This stage focuses on testing the vaccine’s safety in adults, followed by Phase 3, which will assess its ability to generate immunity against cholera. Trials will take place at five sites — two in Johannesburg, two in Durban, and one in East London — coordinated by the South African Medical Research Council (SAMRC).

nnnn

If successful, the vaccine will be compared with Euvichol-Plus, a WHO-approved cholera vaccine produced by EuBiologics. Pending positive outcomes, approval for use in Africa could come by 2028, with global availability expected in 2028/29.

nnnn

Biovac CEO Dr Morena Makhoana expressed pride in the achievement.

nnnn
n

“If the trials succeed, South Africa will become the first country on the continent to produce a cholera vaccine. This development addresses a critical, life-saving need, given the global vaccine shortages and recurring outbreaks,” he said.

n
nnnn

Founded in 2003 through a public-private partnership, Biovac has been at the forefront of rebuilding South Africa’s vaccine manufacturing capacity.

nnnn

Professor Glenda Gray, Chief Scientific Officer at SAMRC and a Distinguished Professor at Wits University, described the trial as a landmark moment.

nnnn
n

“We are honoured to lead the clinical trials for this vaccine. It represents a vital step in strengthening our national response to infectious diseases, conducted with the highest ethical and safety standards,” she said.

n
n

post_title: Border Officials Warned Against Corruption Acts
post_content:
n

The Border Management and Immigration Anti-Corruption Forum (BMIACF) delivered a stern warning against corruption during its awareness campaign held at the Beitbridge Port of Entry on Tuesday, 11 November 2025. The campaign sent a powerful message to border officials that those involved in corrupt activities will face severe consequences.

nnnn

During the event, offenders convicted of corruption shared emotional testimonies about their experiences behind bars, urging public servants to uphold integrity and avoid the mistakes that led to their imprisonment. One offender described prison as “very painful,” warning officials to stop engaging in corruption for their own sake and that of their families. Another offender, once a law enforcement officer, spoke about the shame of explaining her absence to her grandchildren and the heavy toll of losing both her job and freedom.

nnnn

BMA Commissioner and CEO, Dr Michael Masiapato, said the campaign was aimed at encouraging honest service among border officials. “Beitbridge is one of our busiest ports and a gateway to the rest of the continent. It is vital that officials understand the consequences of corruption,” he said.

nnnn

The BMIACF, chaired by Special Investigations Unit (SIU) Head Adv Andy Mothibi, was established in March 2025 to coordinate efforts against corruption in the border management and immigration sector. Adv Mothibi emphasised that corruption undermines public trust and that the Forum would act decisively against offenders.

nnnn

The BMIACF includes the SIU, BMA, Home Affairs, the National Prosecuting Authority, the Hawks, and civil society organisations. It forms part of the government’s “all-of-government” strategy to combat corruption through collaboration and data sharing among key agencies.

nnnn

The Beitbridge campaign reinforced the BMIACF’s commitment to promoting ethical conduct and accountability among officials. Members of the public are encouraged to report suspicious activities through Operation Hi-TIVISE by calling 0801 229 019 or visiting www.bma.gov.za.

post_title: Operation Shanela II Continues Showing Results
post_content:
n

Operation Shanela II has once again demonstrated its effectiveness in combating crime and promoting safety across Mpumalanga. Conducted between 6 and 9 November 2025, the operation brought together several law enforcement and government departments working collaboratively to maintain law and order.

nnnn

According to the Office of the Provincial Commissioner, the multi-agency initiative included members from the South African Police Service (SAPS), South African National Defence Force (SANDF), Traffic, Home Affairs, Health, Emergency Medical Services, and various community safety structures.

nnnn

A total of 142 SAPS officers were deployed, supported by 59 Home Affairs officials, 17 Department of Health workers, and 110 private security personnel, among others. Their combined efforts led to hundreds of searches, arrests, and the recovery of illegal goods.

nnnn

During the operation, 4 419 people and 1 443 vehicles were searched, while 168 stop-and-search operations and 10 roadblocks were conducted. Police also inspected 40 liquor outlets, 11 second-hand dealers, and several scrapyards and farms to ensure legal compliance.

nnnn

Officers arrested suspects for a range of offences, including five for murder, one for attempted murder, one for rape, 15 for assault with intent to cause grievous bodily harm, and 10 for driving under the influence. In addition, 67 people were arrested for possession of counterfeit goods and 26 for contravening the Second-Hand Goods Act. Police also confiscated firearms, ammunition, counterfeit products, and over 6 900 grams of precious metals

post_title: De Jager Banned After Dangerous Tackle
post_content:
n

South African lock Lood de Jager has been handed a four-match suspension following a no-arms tackle during the Springboks’ 32–17 win over France in Paris at the weekend.

De Jager received a red card in the first half after a shoulder charge on French full-back Thomas Ramos during Saturday’s Autumn Series Test. Despite being reduced to 14 men for the entire second half, the Springboks underlined their world-champion credentials with a commanding performance. The match was particularly memorable as it marked captain Siya Kolisi’s 100th appearance for South Africa. The two-time World Cup-winning skipper celebrated the milestone in style, leading his team to another impressive win on foreign soil.

post_title: Minister of Finance Medium Term Budget
Finance Minister Lowers Inflation Target to Three Percent
post_content:
n

Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana has announced a significant policy shift by reducing South Africa’s inflation target to 3%, with a one percentage point tolerance band. The announcement was made during his presentation of the Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement in Parliament on Wednesday afternoon.

nnnn

The decision marks a historic change in the country’s monetary policy framework and aims to bring South Africa in line with international best practice. For years, the inflation target range of between 3% and 6% has been a point of debate between the National Treasury and the South African Reserve Bank.

nnnn

Godongwana said the move would ultimately benefit ordinary South Africans, particularly cash-strapped households battling rising costs. “Over time, the lower target will decrease inflation expectations and inflation, creating room for lower interest rates. This supports household spending and business investment, boosting economic growth and job creation,” he explained.

nnnn

He acknowledged that adopting a 3% inflation target may temporarily slow gross domestic product and revenue growth but emphasised that the long-term benefits would outweigh the short-term costs. “The short-term fiscal costs of a lower target, which include lower nominal GDP and revenue growth, will make achieving fiscal targets more challenging,” he added.

nnnn

Economists have for years urged government to revise its inflation target, noting that South Africa’s average inflation rate has remained higher than that of its major trading partners and emerging market peers.

nnnn

The Reserve Bank is now expected to gradually steer inflation towards the new 3% target over the next two years, signalling a tighter monetary stance in the short term but improved economic stability in the future.

n

post_title: Police Hunt Killers of Seven-Year-Old Girl
post_content:
n

Police in Delmas have launched a manhunt following the brutal murder of seven-year-old Thandolwethu Mahlangu, whose body was discovered this morning in Delpark Extension 2.

nnnn

According to police reports, Thandolwethu’s mother, Ms Ayanda Ngwenyama, reported her daughter missing on 11 November 2025, after the child failed to return home the previous evening. It is alleged that Thandolwethu had gone to her father’s house on 10 November around 18:00 and never came back.

nnnn

A frantic search by community members throughout the night yielded no results. The following morning, Ms Ngwenyama reportedly received a disturbing text message from an unknown number demanding R30 000, allegedly owed by the child’s father, in exchange for the child’s safety.

nnnn

Police immediately opened a missing person inquiry and began tracing the number, which was linked to the Botleng area. Several loan sharks were questioned, and multiple addresses were visited, but no arrests were made.

nnnn

Tragically, at about 07:30 on 12 November, a neighbour discovered the young girl’s body under a pile of rubble behind a shack in Delpark Extension 2. Authorities were called to the scene, and a murder case has since been opened.

nnnnnnnn

The suspects remain at large, and police are appealing to the public for any information that could assist in the investigation. Members of the public can contact Lieutenant Colonel Victor Dibakoane on 079 268 0040, or call Crime Stop on 08600 10111. Information can also be submitted via the MySAPS App, and all reports will be treated confidentially.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner of the SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General Dr Zeph Mkhwanazi, condemned the killing, describing it as “a senseless act of cruelty.”

nnnn
n

“People have lost their sense of humanity. How can anyone kill an innocent young girl who had her whole future ahead of her? We will not rest until the suspect or suspects are behind bars,” he said.

n
nnnn

Police have activated a 72-hour plan to track down those responsible for the horrific crime.

n

post_title: Thirteen Suspects Face Court for Murder
post_content:
n

Nelspruit, 12 November 2025 — Thirteen suspects have appeared before the Mbibane Magistrate’s Court in connection with a brutal mob justice incident that claimed three lives in Vaalbank in 2023.

nnnn

The initial eight suspects — three men and five women — were arrested by the Provincial Murder and Robbery Unit on 7 November 2025 around the Bloedfontein area. They were identified as Gilbert Tlaka (58), Alidah Ramatsetse (56), Grace Mashiane (55), Fridah Komape (53), Mamsi Sambo (56), Simon Kotlolo (51), Giveness Maja (51), and George Modiba (55).

nnnn

Their arrests follow a 2023 investigation into the death of an eight-year-old girl who went missing on 12 February 2023 in Bloedfontein. Her body was later discovered inside a pit toilet at the residence of three victims — Zele Machika (53), Thabo Maubane (22), and Paulinah Maubane (51) — who were later accused by community members of involvement in the child’s death.

nnnn

In the early hours of 18 February 2023, at around 02:00, police responded to a distress call and found the three victims lying dead on the street with severe injuries. Both a Ford Bantam and a VW Jetta 4, later identified as belonging to Maubane, were found burnt to ashes at the scene.

nnnn

In a recent development, the Provincial Murder and Robbery Unit arrested five additional suspects on 11 November 2025, bringing the total number of accused to thirteen. The new suspects have been identified as Given Sambo (36), Thabiso Lekgoathi (42), Julia Boshielo (43), Dineo Sambo (33), and Mmapule Sambo (36).

nnnn

All thirteen suspects have been remanded in custody and are expected to return to court on Thursday, 13 November 2025, for a formal bail application.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of the SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General Dr Zeph Mkhwanazi, commended the investigating team for their relentless pursuit of justice.

nnnn
n

“It is unfortunate that a family lost their lives in such a barbaric act. We cannot bring them back, but we hope the community will learn that taking the law into their own hands is never the solution. Justice always prevails, and the truth eventually comes out,” said Major General Mkhwanazi.

n
nnnn

Police have urged residents to refrain from mob justice and to allow law enforcement authorities to handle criminal investigations.

n

post_title: MEC Macie Urges Communities to Protect Women and Girls
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga MEC for Community Safety, Security and Liaison, Mr Jackie Macie, has called on communities across the province to take an active role in protecting women and girls, following the recent killing of a seven-year-old girl in Delpark near Delmas.

nnnn

Macie expressed deep concern over the rising levels of brutality directed at women and children, describing the situation as “disturbing and unacceptable in any self-loving society.”

nnnn
n

“We must not only condemn these incidents, but work closely together to better protect women and children,” he said.

n
nnnn

According to police reports, the lifeless body of the seven-year-old was discovered a few days after she was reported missing on 10 November 2025. The child’s death has sparked widespread outrage, coming just days after another horrific incident in which a 19-year-old woman from Mbombela was stabbed to death at her home in Mattafin on 3 November 2025.

nnnn

Macie said that despite government efforts — including new and revised legislation aimed at protecting vulnerable groups — cases of Gender-Based Violence and Femicide (GBVF) continue to rise.

nnnn
n

“We must work harder to turn the tide against GBVF. These acts of callousness have no place in our society,” he said.

n
nnnn

He urged communities to remain calm while law enforcement agencies work tirelessly to bring the perpetrators to justice, noting that several offenders have been successfully convicted and are serving lengthy prison sentences.

nnnn

The MEC also called on police officers to handle abuse and murder cases with greater urgency and precision, commending the provincial SAPS for swiftly activating a 72-hour plan to track down suspects in the Delmas case.

nnnn

In his closing remarks, Macie appealed to parents and guardians to be more vigilant about the whereabouts and safety of their children.

nnnn
n

“Protecting our women and children is a shared responsibility. We must all play our part in ensuring that no child or woman suffers at the hands of violence again,” he said.

post_title: Hawks Seize Mandrax and Dagga Worth R900 000 at Oshoek Border
post_content:

Members of the Hawks in Mpumalanga have intercepted a major drug consignment worth an estimated R900 000 at the Oshoek Port of Entry.

The two occupants of the truck — a 33-year-old driver and his 40-year-old crew member, both South African citizens originally from Lesotho — were immediately arrested. In addition to the drugs, police also seized R3 200 in cash and 4 600 Eswatini Emalangeni found in their possession.

Provincial Head of the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation in Mpumalanga, Major General Nico Gerber, commended the joint effort between law enforcement units, saying the operation reflects the province’s readiness for intensified Festive Season operations.

n

“We are already processing the exhibits for forensic investigation. The Hawks in Mpumalanga will continue to work closely with other units to ensure the speedy processing of priority crime dockets,” said Major General Gerber.

n

The Hawks have reaffirmed their commitment to curbing the trafficking of drugs and other serious organised crimes in the province.

post_title: Historic Leopard Sighting Marks Conservation Triumph
post_content:
n

In a remarkable ecological milestone, a leopard has been photographed in the West Coast National Park for the first time in 170 years. The sighting — confirmed through a remote camera trap — marks the natural return of the species to this coastal region after it was wiped out in the mid-1800s.

nnnn

The discovery is the result of a collaborative effort led by the Landmark Leopard and Predator Project, working alongside South African National Parks (SANParks), the University of the Western Cape, Saldanha Bay Municipality and several private landowners. For years, the partnership has been monitoring leopard movement along the West Coast, stretching between Cape Town and the Berg River.

nnnn

According to conservationists, this significant return can be attributed to a combination of long-term efforts. These include improved land-use practices, growing conservation areas such as the West Coast National Park, stronger environmental legislation and increasing tolerance from local communities towards predators.

nnnn

Over the last two decades, the Landmark Leopard and Predator Project and SANParks have focused on restoring ecological corridors and reconnecting fragmented habitats across the Western, Eastern and Northern Cape. These interventions have enabled wildlife, including leopards, to move more freely and safely through the landscape. A key part of this progress has been the willingness of landowners to coexist with predators and to support wildlife protection laws.

nnnn

SANParks has described the leopard’s return as a conservation victory deserving of celebration, emphasising the importance of continued collaboration to ensure the species’ long-term survival in the region.

n

n

The Border Management Authority (BMA) has confirmed that 153 Palestinian travellers arrived at OR Tambo International Airport at around 08:15 on Thursday, 13 November 2025. The group landed via a chartered Lift Global Airways flight from Kenya.

nnnnnnnn

During routine processing, BMA immigration officers noted several inconsistencies. The travellers did not provide details of their intended duration of stay or accommodation in South Africa, and their passports lacked the usual departure stamps. As none of the individuals indicated an intention to apply for asylum, the group initially failed the immigration requirements and was denied entry.

nnnn

Later in the day, the Ministry of Home Affairs received correspondence from the humanitarian organisation Gift of the Givers, confirming that they would take responsibility for hosting the group during their stay. Following verification of this commitment, the BMA authorised the travellers’ entry on Thursday evening.

nnnn

By the time the decision was made, 23 of the original 153 travellers had already proceeded through South Africa to their final destinations. The remaining 130 were formally admitted under the care of Gift of the Givers.

nnnn

As Palestinian nationals qualify for visa-exempt entry into South Africa for stays of up to 90 days, the travellers were processed in line with standard immigration procedures and are required to comply with all conditions of entry.

nnnn

The BMA reaffirmed its commitment to upholding South Africa’s immigration laws and regulatory frameworks.

post_content:
n

Two shop employees in White River have been arrested for allegedly dealing in drugs after a tip-off from a local school led police to uncover a large-scale drug operation.

nnnn

The arrests on Wednesday, 12 November 2025, followed reports that learners at a nearby school were caught smoking vape pipes laced with cannabis, leading to unusual behaviour and poor concentration during exams.

nnnn

According to the police, the school reported the matter, prompting an urgent investigation by the White River K9 Unit. Undercover officers conducted a test purchase of cannabis products from the shop located at 21 William Street, which had only been open since 1 November 2025.

A subsequent raid uncovered cannabis-infused products including vape juice, sweets, chocolates, lollipops, dagga, pot plants, and even cannabis-flavoured cola. The total estimated value of the seized items is R2.3 million.

Two suspects, Estelle de Beer (43) and Zinhle Mabuza (23), appeared in the White River Magistrate’s Court on Thursday, 13 November 2025. De Beer was granted R1,000 bail, while Mabuza remains in custody pending address verification. Both will appear in court again on 17 November 2025.

Acting Provincial Commissioner of SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, praised the school for its vigilance and urged the public to continue collaborating with law enforcement to protect children from drug exposure.

Independent Publishers Celebrate Two Decades Milestone

n

The Association of Independent Publishers (AIP) marked its 20th anniversary in style with a gala dinner held on 13 November 2025 at the Holiday Inn Sunnyside Park in Johannesburg.

nnnn

Founded in 2005 through the merger of the Community Press Association (CPA) and the Independent Media Alliance (IMA), the AIP has grown to represent more than 150 member organisations and nearly 200 publications across South Africa’s print and digital independent media sector.

nnnn

The evening brought together publishers, media stakeholders, and sponsors, offering reflection, recognition and commitment. The AIP highlighted its long-standing role in promoting media diversity, empowering community publishers, and amplifying marginalised voices across the country’s 11 official languages. Guests were treated to dignitary addresses, recognition of veteran publishers, and networking opportunities aimed at strengthening the sector’s future.

nnnnnnnn

In a keynote address, the AIP noted the significant challenges facing independent media — from digital disruption to funding pressures — and reaffirmed its mission to provide capacity-building, advocacy and peer support to small and community-based media outlets. The association also encouraged attendees to invest in advertising messages and sponsorships to help sustain independent media’s vital role in local democracy.

nnnn

For community publishers such as your newspaper, this milestone offers both inspiration and opportunity. The AIP’s anniversary underlines the value of locally rooted journalism — publications that understand community context, reflect local voices and hold power to account. The celebration also presents a chance to connect with the broader independent media network, seek collaborative partnerships, and leverage AIP’s resources for training and growth.

nnnn

As the independent sector enters its next decade, the AIP dinner in November serves as both a milestone of achievement and a rallying moment. For readers, advertisers, and community leaders alike, the message is clear: independent media remains central to vibrant local civic life and sustainable community development.

post_title: Roadside Search Leads To Drug Arrest
post_content:
n

A 41-year-old man has been arrested in Kaapmuiden after police allegedly found crystal meth worth an estimated R350 000 hidden inside two books wrapped in decorative paper.

nnnn

The arrest took place on 15 November at around 07:00 along the N4 near Kaapmuiden, after a police officer received a tip-off about a suspicious man standing beside the road. When the officer approached and requested to search the man’s bag, he uncovered the concealed packages.

nnnn

Inside the books, officers discovered white compressed substances which were later confirmed to be crystal meth weighing 1.455 kilograms.

nnnn

According to police, the suspect claimed he did not know what he was carrying. He allegedly told officers that he is homeless, originally from Springs, and had been picked up from the street, given the parcel, and instructed to deliver it to Mozambique. From there, he was allegedly expected to travel on to Brazil.

The man was arrested on the spot and is set to appear before the Barberton Magistrate’s Court on 17 November 2025 on charges of drug possession.

The man was arrested at the scene and will soon appear before the Jane Furse Magistrate’s Court on charges of possession of suspected stolen property (stock theft). The recovered vehicle has been seized as part of the ongoing investigation.

The Mpumalanga Department of Community Safety, Security and Liaison has issued an urgent appeal to motorists to exercise extreme caution on the province’s roads following persistent rainy weather and a fatal crash that claimed four lives on Sunday.

The tragedy comes as the province continues to experience widespread rainfall, prompting renewed warnings about road safety. Mpumalanga MEC for Community Safety, Security and Liaison, Mr Jackie Macie, has appealed for heightened vigilance, emphasising that wet weather conditions severely affect visibility and vehicle control.

“We are therefore calling for stricter adherence to the rules of the road to prevent devastating crashes. Motorists must adjust their speed and increase following distances in line with the prevailing conditions,” said MEC Macie.

The Department has also cautioned motorists to be particularly alert around roadworks on the N4, N11, N2 and R40, where rain can worsen

post_title: DSD Urges Vigilance Against Underage Drinking
post_content:
n

As communities across South Africa prepare for the festive season, the Department of Social Development (DSD) has issued a firm warning about the heightened risks of underage drinking and substance abuse. With schools closing, families gathering, and thousands of matriculants celebrating the end of their examinations, the department is urging parents and caregivers to strengthen supervision and ensure young people remain safe.

nnnn

This time of year is known for increased social activities, including pens-down parties, music festivals, beach outings, and late-night celebrations. While these events often symbolise freedom and accomplishment for young people, particularly matriculants, they also carry significant dangers when alcohol and drugs are involved.

nnnn

The warning comes as the country continues to grapple with the painful memory of the Enyobeni Tavern tragedy in East London, where 21 young people — most of them minors, the youngest just 13 — lost their lives during a night out in June 2022. Three years later, affected families are still seeking closure, and key questions about the circumstances of the incident remain unanswered.

nnnn

Against this backdrop, Minister Nokuzola Sisisi Tolashe and the DSD are appealing to young people to avoid alcohol and drugs during festive gatherings. The department further urges parents and communities not to normalise the consumption of alcohol “in the name of celebration”.

nnnn

Mr Mogotsi Kalaeamodimo, Director for Social Crime Prevention and Anti-Substance Abuse, stressed that the department is working tirelessly to prevent similar tragedies. “At this time of the year, we often notice that school-going children, after completing their examinations, start engaging in alcohol consumption and experimenting with drugs,” he said. “Parents should always know where their children are and who they are spending time with. Without proper supervision, things can easily get out of control.”

nnnn

Mr Kalaeamodimo highlighted key DSD programmes aimed at prevention and early intervention. These include the Ke Moja initiative, which educates learners across the country about the dangers of substance abuse, and the Festive Season Awareness Campaign, which equips parents and communities with information on recognising early signs of alcohol and drug use.

nnnn

The department is also engaging liquor outlet owners, including tavern operators, to enforce regulations and prevent the sale of alcohol to minors. In addition, specialised programmes targeting first-year university students aim to help them cope with academic and social pressures without turning to substances.

nnnn

The DSD emphasised the need for stronger cooperation between government, families, and communities to safeguard young people. Preventing another tragedy like Enyobeni, the department noted, requires collective vigilance, education, and timely intervention.

nnnn

Anyone needing assistance with substance abuse or wishing to report underage drinking can contact the DSD Substance Abuse Helpline on 0800 12 13 14 or WhatsApp 087 163 2025. The helpline operates 24 hours a day and provides free, confidential support and counselling.

n

post_title: MEC Manzini Unveils Upgraded Dental Unit

post_title: Man Sentenced to Life for Killing Mother
post_content:
n

A 43-year-old Mpumalanga man has been sentenced to life imprisonment for the brutal murder of his elderly mother in Sinqobile, near Daggakraal.

nnnn

The Regional Court in Amersfoort handed down the sentence to Thami Sydney Mnyandu following a detailed police investigation into the death of his 75-year-old mother, Ntobizodwa Masina.

nnnn

According to police reports, the incident occurred on 25 July 2024 at around 10:35am. Officers responded to a call and found an elderly woman lying unconscious in her yard with severe facial injuries.

nnnn

Provincial police spokesperson, Captain Mpho Nonyane-Mpe, said: “Upon arrival, officers found the victim with serious facial wounds. Inside the house, police located Mnyandu, who confirmed that the woman was his mother. He told police that they had argued and that he lost his temper and assaulted her.”

nnnn

Masina was rushed to hospital, where medical staff identified further injuries, including a wound beneath her left breast and a cut to her forehead. Mnyandu was initially charged with assault with intent to cause grievous bodily harm.

nnnn

However, investigators later uncovered that a protection order had previously been issued against him, prohibiting him from assaulting, threatening, or verbally abusing his mother.

nnnn

Masina died a few days after being discharged from hospital due to complications arising from the assault, and the charge was upgraded to murder.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner of Police in Mpumalanga, Major General Zeph Mkhwanazi, commended the investigating officer, Detective Sergeant Mahlaba, for his dedication and thorough work which secured the conviction.

nnnn

He added that he hoped the life sentence would bring some measure of comfort to the victim’s family. “The SAPS reiterates its zero tolerance for gender-based violence and crimes against vulnerable members of society,” Mkhwanazi said.

post_title: Netball Tournament Unites Community For Empowerment
post_content:
n

The spirit of youth empowerment shone brightly on 15 November 2025 when young girls from across Bushbuckridge gathered at Oakley Primary School for the Mathibela Foundation Netball Tournament. The event was hosted by the Mathibela Foundation, with The Lucia O Foundation participating as a partner by donating essential support items to help uplift and empower learners.

nnnn

Fourteen schools took part in the tournament, which celebrated not only sporting talent but also the importance of education, confidence, dignity and community development. Each school received support materials to help keep learners in school and thriving academically and socially.

nnnn

The Lucia O Foundation, which partnered with the tournament, reaffirmed its mission to champion sustainable development and advance the wellbeing of young people in Mpumalanga. The organisation focuses on entrepreneurship development, menstrual health management, access to Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR), bodily autonomy, anti-bullying efforts, GBVF prevention, and gender equality.

nnnn

As part of its ongoing programmes in schools, the foundation leads awareness campaigns, provides health and rights education, distributes sanitary packs, and promotes menstrual hygiene and WASH initiatives. Through its participation and donations at the netball event, the foundation emphasised its commitment to ensuring that every learner—girl and boy—remains dignified, informed and empowered.

nnnn

In the same spirit, the foundation also expressed its support for LoveLife Mpumalanga’s Sports4Change Netball Tournament, held under the theme “Teenage Pregnancy & Adolescent Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights Awareness.” The theme highlights the pressing need to educate and equip young people with the knowledge and confidence to make informed decisions about their futures.

nnnn

Both the Mathibela Foundation—through the successful hosting of the event—and the Lucia O Foundation, supported by the Glow Up Make a Difference Initiative, reaffirmed their dedication to strengthening community engagement and driving meaningful, transformative change. Through sport, education and advocacy, these organisations continue to uplift young people across Mpumalanga and beyond.

post_title: Miss Bushbuckridge Inspires Young Learners at Ezrom Primary
post_content:
n

The reigning Miss Bushbuckridge, Mkhenso Lubisi, spent her morning uplifting the future leaders of Ezrom Primary School in Thulamahashe, where she donated 50 sanitary towels to girls and roll-ons to boys. The generous gesture was made possible through the sponsorship of Sunbake Bushbuckridge.

nnnn

The visit formed part of her ongoing give-back drive, aimed at motivating Grade 7 learners as they prepare for their final primary school examinations. With the transition to high school fast approaching, Mkhenso reminded the learners of the importance of self-belief, discipline, and education.

nnnn

She described her presence at the school as an opportunity to act as a “big sister”, encouraging the pupils to stay focused and to recognise their own potential. “Education is vital, and you must always remember who you are,” she told the learners.

nnnn

During the engagement, both boys and girls were taught about the importance of personal hygiene and how to carry themselves with confidence and responsibility. The donated items, she said, were meant not only as gifts but as tools of dignity — something essential for all young people, especially those who may be underprivileged.

nnnn

Mkhenso emphasised that her reign is dedicated to community upliftment, development, and academic empowerment. Her focus continues to be on learners, students, and individuals facing difficult circumstances. “My goal is to give back, to serve where there is need, and to support initiatives that uplift and empower our communities,” she added.

nnnn

As she continues her journey as Miss Bushbuckridge, Mkhenso hopes to attend more events centred on development and empowerment, ensuring that her influence leaves a lasting, positive impact on the youth of Bushbuckridge.

post_title: Truck Drivers Targeted in Acornhoek Extortion Plot
post_content:
n

Police in Acornhoek are investigating a case of extortion and the possession of an unlicensed firearm and ammunition after a truck driver was allegedly threatened on the R40 near a local mall on Friday, 14 November 2025.

nnnn

According to police reports, the truck driver, travelling from Phalaborwa to Nelspruit, was stopped by a group of individuals who allegedly instructed him not to use the road again. It is believed this was the second time the driver had received such a warning on the same day.

nnnn

When representatives of the trucking company arrived at the scene, they were reportedly confronted by approximately twelve members of the Acornhoek Forum. The group is said to have demanded that the company employ three truck drivers from the area. They allegedly ordered company officials to bring senior management back the following week to finalise an agreement involving the hiring of local drivers and the payment of a monthly “protection fee”. The group further threatened that failure to comply would result in the company’s trucks being barred from using the R40.

nnnn

Police later received information about one of the suspects. Officers proceeded to his business premises, where the suspect was searched. A firearm and ammunition were allegedly found in his possession, leading to his arrest on charges of extortion and possession of an unlicensed firearm and ammunition.

nnnn

The suspect is expected to appear in the Acornhoek Magistrate’s Court on Tuesday, 18 November 2025.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner of the SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, strongly condemned the incident and warned that acts of intimidation and extortion would not be tolerated. He commended the swift police response and reaffirmed the SAPS’s commitment to ensuring the safety of all road users and businesses across the province.

n

post_title: Purple Movement Shines Light on GBVF Crisis
post_content:
n

South Africa is facing a relentless crisis of gender-based violence and femicide. Every day, women are harmed, silenced, and, too often, killed. It is a national emergency that continues to test the moral fibre of the country. The growing purple movement has emerged as a powerful response — a collective call for society to confront the scale of this violence and to demand meaningful change.

nnnn

The purple movement is more than symbolic. Citizens across the country are wearing purple, filling timelines on social media, and taking part in acts of stillness and protest to draw attention to the thousands of women who die each year. Activists are calling for gender-based violence to be treated as a national disaster, demanding coordinated interventions, increased resources, and accountability at all levels of society.

nnnn

What people need to know about the purple movement: it is a national campaign led primarily by women and supported by organisations like Women For Change. Its aim is to make the country pause and reflect on the scale of GBVF. On designated days, participants are encouraged to wear purple, refrain from paid and unpaid work, and take symbolic acts of protest such as lying down in public spaces for a few minutes. The movement seeks to create visibility for the crisis, challenge societal indifference, and push for concrete governmental action, including stronger laws, better enforcement, and support services for survivors.

nnnn

The tragic killing of Dr Nondumiso Sibanyoni last year is one example of the urgent problem the purple movement highlights. Her death shocked the nation and exposed the reality that even educated and independent women can be left vulnerable in a system that too often fails to protect its citizens. Her case has become a symbol of the human cost of GBVF, galvanising activism and reminding the public of the scale and severity of the crisis.

nnnn

What makes the purple movement particularly striking is its refusal to settle for performative gestures or empty promises. Women across the country are calling for structural change: better policing, stronger legal protection, justice reforms, and community accountability. They demand a society where women can live safely, free from fear, and where the response to violence is timely, serious, and effective.

nnnn

The movement has sparked national conversations about safety, accountability, and government responsibility. It forces the country to confront uncomfortable truths about misogyny, systemic failures, and the human toll of continued inaction. The purple movement is not just a protest; it is a demand that South Africa take responsibility for the lives of its women and girls, and act to prevent further tragedies.

nnnn

As the purple wave gains momentum, it challenges the nation to move beyond awareness and toward action. It is a powerful reminder that GBVF is not only a series of individual tragedies, but a societal crisis that demands urgent and sustained intervention. South Africa’s future will be judged not by the headlines of today, but by the safety and dignity it ensures for women tomorrow.

n

post_title: South Africa’s Top Spellers Head to Sun City for National Finals
post_content:
n

South Africa’s brightest young linguistic talents are preparing for the prestigious 2025 National Spelling Bee Finals, set to take place on 11 December 2025 at the iconic Sun City Resort in the North West. The annual competition, now firmly established as one of the country’s flagship literacy events, continues to play a crucial role in nurturing a strong reading culture, enhancing academic excellence, and building multilingual confidence among learners.

nnnn

According to an official media release from the South African Spelling Bee, this year’s finalists have advanced through local contests, district eliminations, and provincial championships to secure their place on the national stage. For many, the journey to Sun City represents not only months of preparation but years of dedication supported by teachers, families, and schools committed to literacy development.

nnnn

A Competition Built on Literacy Excellence

nnnn

For more than 15 years, the South African National Spelling Bee has stood as a cornerstone of youth literacy advancement. The programme is jointly run by A Better Africa Foundation and the Department of Basic Education (DBE), in partnership with the National Education Collaboration Trust (NECT) and literacy organisations such as Nal’ibali. This collaboration places the spelling bee at the heart of national efforts to strengthen literacy across communities.

nnnn

The DBE confirms that spelling bees form part of its broader reading strategy aimed at improving vocabulary, comprehension, and learner confidence throughout the schooling system. Education platforms and independent reports have consistently highlighted the positive impact of spelling competitions on language development and academic performance across the provinces.

nnnn

As Roger Dickinson, CEO of the South African Spelling Bee, explains:
“Every word a child learns strengthens the standing of the nation. Confident readers uplift families, schools, and communities.”
His message captures the growing recognition that literacy is not merely an educational requirement, but a national tool for empowerment.

nnnn

A Truly South African Celebration of Language

nnnn

The South African Spelling Bee is renowned for its commitment to multilingualism and inclusivity. The competition assesses spelling ability across all 11 official languages as well as South African Sign Language (SASL), reflecting the country’s rich linguistic diversity.

nnnn

This year’s programme also features a written component with words drawn from Italian and Shona, expanding linguistic awareness and encouraging learners to appreciate global language connections. For many participants, this exposure deepens their understanding of language origins and patterns.

nnnn

Beyond the competition rounds, finalists will enjoy cultural and recreational activities at Sun City — including the famed Valley of Waves — underscoring the organisers’ goal of balancing academic challenge with memorable childhood experiences.

nnnn

The Road to the Continental Stage

nnnn

Once the top three spellers in each category are selected, they will go on to represent South Africa at the African Spelling Bee Finals, scheduled for March 2026 in Zimbabwe. South Africa has historically performed strongly at continental level, with previous participants recognised for their discipline, articulation, and extensive linguistic knowledge.

nnnn

This progression highlights the importance of the national finals, which serve both as a celebration of achievement and as a gateway to international opportunities for young wordsmiths.

nnnn

Community Impact and Education Legacy

nnnn

The competition’s true impact lies not merely in trophies, but in the personal transformation experienced by the learners. Participants develop resilience, confidence, public-speaking skills, and a lifelong appreciation for learning — qualities that enrich families, schools, and communities.

nnnn

A Better Africa Foundation, which has run literacy programmes since 2010, continues to reinforce the message that literacy is a shared societal responsibility. As part of the DBE’s Reading Collective and National Reading Coalition, the organisation remains committed to long-term youth development and national literacy improvement.

nnnn

A Moment of Pride for All Provinces

nnnn

This year’s finalists represent every province — from rural villages to small towns and major urban centres — demonstrating that excellence in literacy knows no geographical or economic boundaries. Their participation showcases what determined learners, committed educators, and supportive communities can achieve together.

nnnn

As the countdown to the finals begins, the nation watches with pride as these young linguistic champions prepare to step onto the Sun City stage. Regardless of the final results, every participant has already earned a place in a growing national movement dedicated to strengthening literacy and celebrating the transformative power of words.

n

post_title: Acornhoek Musician Breaks into Global Scene
post_content:
n

Hailing from the dusty streets of Acornhoek in Bushbuckridge, Gift Russell Selomi, better known as Gift of Africa, has carved an extraordinary path in the world of music.

nnnn

Gift of Africa began his musical journey in 2012, diving into the digital realm with FL Studio, formerly known as Fruity Loops. “It took me a while to master the software as I am a self-taught musician,” he recalls.

nnnn

His dedication paid off, and over the years, he developed a distinctive style rooted in deep house music.

nnnn

Before venturing into music, Gift of Africa led an ordinary life, but his lifelong ambition to become a musician kept him pushing forward. “Before music, I lived an ordinary life, but because I always wanted to be a musician,” he explains.

nnnn

Family played a crucial role in shaping his musical journey. Growing up, he was surrounded by music enthusiasts—his older brother Majola, who played keyboards, and another half-brother, Selomi, both influenced his passion.

nnnn

“Music runs in the family. Watching my brother Majola playing a keyboard really inspired me,” he shares.

nnnn

However, the road to success was not without obstacles. It took over seven years of relentless practice and self-education before he released his first official song. “It took me over seven years to master FL Studio while consulting my brothers on music advice,” he admits.

nnnn

His breakthrough came in 2019 with a deep house track featured by his brother Majola. “That project marked a turning point. I gained confidence and never looked back,” he says. His distinctive style, heavily influenced by DJ Fresh, emerged from his deep obsession with deep house music.

nnnn

Gift of Africa’s rise to prominence was further cemented with his brother’s debut EP, Mwariwangu, released in June 2021, which introduced him to the broader music industry.

nnnn

International recognition followed in 2023 when he collaborated with UK artist Darles Flow on the song Memories of You. “Setting targets is what really led to my international breakthrough. I don’t just make music for myself; I make music that resonates with many,” he states. His discography includes several impactful projects. His first EP, Spiritual Calling, was followed by the 10-track album Teknology in 2022, which also featured his Inaugural album.

nnnn

His biggest hit to date remains the track House Music from the Teknology album. His latest work, a five-track EP titled Tales from the Jungle, continues to showcase his evolving artistry.

nnnnnnnn

Gift of Africa’s story is one of perseverance, family influence, and unwavering dedication. As he puts it, “I make music to connect with people, and my goal is to keep inspiring others from my community and beyond.”

n

n

History was made in Mpumalanga over the weekend as the African National Congress Women’s League (ANCWL) finally elected a constitutionally mandated provincial executive committee (PEC) after a decade without a formal structure. The previous PEC was disbanded ten years ago, leaving the league without leadership until this landmark gathering. In another unprecedented moment, all officials were elected unopposed — a rare sign of unity in today’s competitive political landscape.

nnnn

The newly elected PEC deserves warm congratulations, but their rise also invites a deeper question: are the ANC’s leagues still relevant in the current political environment?

nnnn

To answer this, one must revisit the reasons the Women’s League was formed. Its aims and objectives include:

nnnn
    n
  • Mobilising and uniting South African women in the struggle for liberation.
    • nnnn
  • Advancing the objectives of the ANCWL and the ANC across society.
    • nnnn
  • Driving the emancipation of women in the ANC, government, and society at large.
    • nnnn
  • Promoting women’s development and confidence.
    • nnnn
  • Fostering national consciousness, unity, and accountability among women.
    • nnnn
  • Ensuring women’s participation in all sectors of public life.
    • nnnn
  • Combating discrimination and dismantling patriarchal systems.
    • nnnn
  • Campaigning for affirmative action to overcome gender and racial inequality.
    • nnnn
  • Fighting violence against women, children, and vulnerable groups.
    • nnnn
  • Promoting peace, development, and recognition of women’s rights as human rights.
    • n
nnnn

These objectives remain profoundly relevant in South Africa today. Yet, elective conferences — not only within the ANC but across most political parties — have shifted their focus from policy discussions to leadership contests. Political organisations, including the ANC Youth and Women’s Leagues, are no longer significantly influencing policy direction or contributing research on issues affecting communities.

nnnn

With the establishment of the Ministry for Women, Children and Persons with Disabilities, there is an urgent need to clarify the national gender machinery and revise outdated policy frameworks. Equally concerning is the inadequate response to LGBTQ+ rights. Stigma remains widespread, often fuelled by conservative religious and traditional views. Many communities mistakenly believe that promoting LGBTQ+ rights equates to promoting LGBTQ+ identity. Proper education and awareness programmes are needed, especially in schools, to foster understanding and respect.

nnnn

A 2010 UNDP report highlighted progress in education, noting that more women graduate than men. However, female participation in Science, Engineering, and Technology (SET) fields remains alarmingly low. Government must intervene to close this gap and address ongoing shortages in technical and scientific skills.

nnnn

Women and girls continue to face challenges such as high dropout rates due to early pregnancy, high levels of illiteracy, and limited access to meaningful skills development. Existing programmes, including ABET and Kharikhude, have not sufficiently transformed the skills landscape. SETAs and development agencies must adopt stronger, more targeted strategies, especially for women living in rural areas and informal settlements.

nnnn

As the province heads into local government elections within the next 12 months, the newly elected PEC faces a significant task. It must provide strong leadership, ensuring that young and older women alike are supported to occupy senior positions in government and across all sectors of society.

nnnn

We wish the new PEC well as it steps into this pivotal role.

n

n

The Mpumalanga Department of Education has commenced a physical verification exercise for all its employees, as part of a national initiative led by the Department of Basic Education (DBE) in partnership with the Education Labour Relations Council (ELRC). The process, conducted on Tuesday, 18 November, aims to strengthen accountability and ensure that every public servant in the education sector is properly recorded.

nnnn

Employees from the Head Office reported for verification with their original Identity Documents, fulfilling the requirement to confirm their physical presence and employment status. The strong turnout reflected professionalism and a shared commitment to transparent governance.

nnnn

According to the Department, the exercise is a vital step in maintaining a clean and accurate employee database. By confirming each official’s identity and employment details, the initiative helps improve payroll management and reduces the risk of salaries being paid to ghost employees.

nnnn

The verification process also serves to curb potential fraud arising from outdated or incorrect personnel information, thereby safeguarding public funds and reinforcing confidence in the public service.

nnnn

The Mpumalanga Department of Education expressed appreciation for the cooperation shown by its employees and reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening human resource management, enhancing service delivery, and ensuring full accountability across the workforce.

post_title: Education Department Denies Claims Over Russia Programme
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga Department of Education has firmly dismissed allegations that local students sent to study in Russia were left destitute and hungry, following an article published by Sunday World on 17 November 2025. The online report accused the Department of sending learners abroad and abandoning them without adequate support.

nnnn

In a detailed statement released on Wednesday, 19 November, the Department refuted the claims as misleading and lacking factual basis. It emphasised that since the inception of the Russia study programme, it has consistently processed tuition fees, accommodation, and stipend payments for participating students.

nnnn

The Department acknowledged that an unexpected delay in stipend payments occurred due to the expiration of the facilitator’s contract. When the tender for a new facilitator was advertised, only one bid was received, rendering the process unresponsive. However, the Department said it worked closely with the Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) to ensure that students continued receiving their stipends while supply chain processes were being addressed.

nnnn

According to the statement, any suggestion that learners were knowingly abandoned abroad is both inaccurate and disingenuous. The Department insisted that urgent measures were implemented at every stage to prevent students from being left without financial support.

nnnn

The statement further clarified that the two deceased students mentioned in the Sunday World article did not pass away in Russia, as claimed. Both were in South Africa at the time and died of natural causes. The Department added that it has no record of ever initiating a repatriation process for any student in the programme.

nnnn

The Department also rejected suggestions that the Russia study programme amounted to wasted expenditure. Out of the 368 Mpumalanga students who enrolled, 296 successfully graduated in fields such as General Medicine, Civil Engineering, Mathematics and Science Education, Aeromedical Engineering, Veterinary Science and Information Technology.

nnnn

Some of these graduates have already entered internships through provincial departments:

nnnn

• Thirty-nine veterinary graduates are placed under the Department of Agriculture, Rural Development, Land and Environmental Affairs (DARDLEA).

nnnn

• Seventeen civil engineering graduates have joined internship programmes under the Department of Public Works, Roads and Transport.

nnnn

• Ninety medical graduates have written board exams funded by the Department, with fifty already placed in internships by the National Department of Health.

nnnn

An additional seventy-four medical graduates are awaiting invitations to write their board exams with the Health Professions Council of South Africa. Upon completing their internships and community service, the medical graduates will qualify as medical officers.

nnnn

Throughout the programme, the Department says it has consistently funded living expenses, accommodation, medical insurance and visa costs for all students abroad.

nnnn

“No amount of fabricated information can undermine the Department’s efforts to empower young people and prepare them to contribute meaningfully to Mpumalanga’s socio-economic development,” the statement concluded.

n

n

A 30-year-old man has been arrested following a daring hijacking and robbery of a cigarette delivery van on the Sabie–White River road on Tuesday morning, 18 November 2025.

nnnn

According to police, the incident occurred at around 08:30 when the victims were travelling in a white Haval delivery van. A white Kia allegedly overtook them before abruptly stopping in front of their vehicle. Two armed men – one carrying a pistol and the other a rifle – stepped out and threatened the victims at gunpoint.

nnnn

The victims were forced out of their vehicle and into the Kia, after which they were driven deep into a nearby plantation. Once inside the plantation, the suspects ordered them to run and not look back. The shaken victims later found workers in the area and borrowed a phone to call for assistance.

nnnnnnnn

Car-tracking services and the Flying Squad were activated immediately. The stolen Haval was later recovered along the Sabie–White River road. Officers followed fresh tyre tracks leading into the plantation where they discovered a Toyota Quantum loaded with stolen cigarette stock — 28 boxes valued at approximately R500 000.

nnnn

Police arrested one suspect at the scene, while the remaining individuals fled and are still being sought.

nnnn

The arrested suspect is expected to appear before the Sabie Magistrate’s Court on Thursday, 20 November 2025, facing charges of hijacking and robbery.

nnnn

Police urge anyone with information on the outstanding suspects to contact Crime Stop on 08600 10111 or make use of the MySAPS App. Callers may remain anonymous, and all information will be handled confidentially.

n

n

The community of Ngodwana has been shaken by a horrific incident in which a 42-year-old man was arrested for kidnapping, rape and house robbery at Bhamjee Squatter Camp. The attack occurred in the early hours of Monday, 17 November 2025.

nnnn

According to police, the 30-year-old victim was sleeping alone in her rented room when she heard a noise at around 01:00. Upon waking, she found a man known to her already inside the room. Despite her cries for help, no one heard her. The intruder allegedly ordered her to keep quiet and began strangling her. Though she tried to fight back, she was overpowered and lost consciousness.

nnnn

When she later regained consciousness, the suspect was still inside the room. After another attempt to scream, he reportedly strangled her again. In desperation, the victim grabbed a knife from the stove and stabbed him in the shoulder. However, he overpowered her once more, assaulted her, and she fell to the floor.

nnnn

Police say the assailant then demanded money, took her bank card and mobile phone, and covered her face with a cloth before raping her. He allegedly forced her to his residence afterwards, locked her inside, and denied her food.

nnnn

The following day, 18 November, a community meeting was held after the victim’s family raised concerns about her disappearance. Shockingly, the suspect also attended this meeting.

nnnn

The victim later managed to escape through a window. She was spotted by her sister, who had been searching for her. The suspect was immediately identified, and the police were called to the scene. He was arrested and taken into custody at Ngodwana SAPS.

nnnn

The suspect is expected to appear in the Nelspruit Magistrate’s Court on Thursday, 20 November 2025, on charges of kidnapping, rape and house robbery.

n

post_title: Additional Accused Appears in Fraud Case
post_content:
n

A 36-year-old man, Sibusiso Jeffrey Ngwenyama, has appeared before the Ermelo Magistrate’s Court on charges of fraud, money laundering, and contravention of the Tax Administration Act. He was arrested on Wednesday, 17 November 2025, by the Hawks’ Nelspruit-based Serious Commercial Crime Investigation Unit following the issuing of a warrant of arrest.

nnnn

According to the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation, the charges stem from fraudulent tax submissions made during the 2015/2016 tax period. The company Wezzamarie CC, under the directorship of Weza Wayne Mondlane, allegedly submitted false tax returns for tax periods 2013, 2014, 2015 and 2016 in order to unlawfully claim foreign tax credits from the South African Revenue Service (SARS).

nnnn

Mondlane is accused of intentionally misrepresenting information, which resulted in a financial loss of R640 664.64 to SARS. The illegally obtained funds were reportedly distributed to several beneficiaries, including Ngwenyama, who is said to have received R11 000. The money was transferred into the business account of Teamslavit (Pty) Ltd, a company for which Ngwenyama is the sole director and signatory.

nnnn

The matter was referred to the Hawks for further investigation, which led to the arrest of five accused in August, including two corporate entities.

nnnn

All accused were granted bail of R3 000 each. The case has been postponed to 18 February 2026 and transferred to the Middelburg Specialised Commercial Crimes Court, where all accused will appear together.

n

post_title: Drug Transport Vehicle Forfeited to State
post_content:
n

A Volkswagen Jetta valued at R280 000 has officially been forfeited to the State after it was found to have been used in the commission of a serious drug-related crime.

nnnn

The vehicle was seized in January 2023 after members of the Hectorspruit K9 Unit discovered 58 packets of a substance suspected to be crystal meth, with an estimated street value of R8.7 million. The drugs were hidden in a concealed compartment beneath the vehicle’s base shortly after it passed through the Nkomazi Toll Plaza in Kaapmuiden on its way to Nelspruit.

nnnn

Two suspects, both Mozambican nationals, were arrested at the scene following the discovery. The suspected drugs and the vehicle were confiscated pending further investigation.

nnnn

The matter was subsequently handed over to the Hawks’ Priority Crime Specialised Investigation Asset Forfeiture team. Working in collaboration with the Asset Forfeiture Unit, investigators pursued an asset-forfeiture process which culminated in a court ruling.

nnnn

On Monday, 3 November 2025, the Mpumalanga Division of the High Court in Mbombela granted a forfeiture order, formally transferring ownership of the vehicle to the State.

n

n

A hijacked vehicle has been successfully recovered by members of the Kwamhlanga Crime Intelligence Unit following swift action and coordinated police work on Monday, 17 November.

nnnn

According to the police, a white Polo Classic with Mpumalanga registration was hijacked in the Suncity Albert Luthuli Section. The owner, an Ethiopian national, was reportedly held hostage by three armed suspects during the ordeal.

nnnn

The suspects, who were travelling in an old Toyota Corolla 16-valve, fled with the stolen Polo and several components, including the engine, two front tyres, gearbox, licence disc and starter.

nnnn

Police have confirmed that a case of carjacking is under investigation. Efforts to trace and arrest the suspects are ongoing.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of the SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, praised the Kwamhlanga Crime Intelligence Support Unit for their commendable work in recovering the vehicle.

nnnn

Residents with information that may assist the investigation are encouraged to contact the SAPS on 08600 10111 or submit anonymous tip-offs via the MySAPS App.

n

n

Police in Pienaar have launched an investigation after a number of abandoned firearms were recovered on Wednesday, 19 November, as part of the ongoing Operation Safer Festive Season.

nnnn

According to authorities, officers received information about a group allegedly transporting firearms from Mataffin near Nelspruit to Pienaar in a white Nissan NP300 bakkie. A police member later spotted the vehicle in the Mkhatsini (Karino) area and followed it while alerting colleagues at Pienaar SAPS.

nnnn

As the vehicle approached Moyeni Mall, two men seated at the back reportedly jumped off with a white bag and fled into nearby bushes. The bakkie then sped away.

nnnn

During the chase, police found two bags of maize meal abandoned by the suspects. On closer inspection, the bags were found to contain three rifles and 25 rounds of ammunition.

nnnn

The items recovered included:

nnnn
    n
  • A brown rifle
    • nnnn
  • A black Gladiator shotgun with a shoulder belt
    • nnnn
  • A brown rifle fitted with a zoomed scope and shoulder belt
    • nnnn
  • A black waist ammunition belt
    • nnnn
  • Various shotgun rounds
    • n
nnnnnnnn

Police have confirmed that the firearms were stolen during a residential burglary in White River. All items have been confiscated and will undergo forensic ballistic testing to determine whether they were used in any other criminal activities. The police are appealing to the public for assistance in tracing the suspects. Anyone with information is urged to contact Crime Stop on 08600 10111 or to submit a tip-off anonymously via the MySAPS App.

post_title: GRIP Head Office Targeted in Overnight Break-In
post_content:
n

The GRIP (Gender-Based Violence Response) Head Office in Mbombela was broken into during the night of 19 November 2025, with the full extent of the theft and damage still being assessed.

nnnn

According to GRIP Chief Executive Officer, Tarryn Leigh Lokotsch, the incident left the premises in disarray.

nnnn

“We had a break-in during the night at our Head Office. The front door was smashed, and they managed to fiddle and get our security gate open. They went through all of our drawers and made a real mess,” she said.

nnnnnnnn

Several items were stolen, including dignity care pack supplies, office consumables, laptop chargers and the organisation’s Wi-Fi router — all heartfelt donations used to support survivors of gender-based violence. Lokotsch expressed deep concern over the loss, noting that these resources are vital to GRIP’s work and community outreach.

nnnn

Police confirmed that one suspect was arrested in the early hours of the morning, while two others remain at large.

nnnn

GRIP has urged residents to remain vigilant and to report any information that may assist in locating the outstanding suspects. Despite the setback, the organisation continues its efforts to provide essential services to vulnerable community members.

n

post_title: Mpumalanga Launches United Festive Safety Drive
post_content:
n

Mbombela – Mpumalanga has officially launched its first-ever provincial Roll Call, bringing together all traffic law enforcement officers ahead of what is expected to be one of the busiest and most demanding festive seasons. The historic gathering, held at Mbombela Stadium on Thursday, 20 November 2025, featured a powerful address by MEC for Community Safety, Security and Liaison, Mr Jackie Macie, and a keynote speech by Deputy Minister of Transport, Mr Mkhuleko Hlengwa.

nnnn

The event drew Executive Mayors from across all districts, senior SAPS officials, municipal MMCs, transport stakeholders including BUSCOR and the Border Management Authority, as well as hundreds of provincial and municipal traffic officers.

nnnn

MEC Macie: ‘Visibility Is Non-Negotiable’

nnnn

MEC Macie said the Roll Call marks the beginning of an annual tradition that will precede each festive season. He thanked officers for their dedication and reminded them of their immense responsibility.

nnnn

“You are the face of safety on our roads,” Macie said. “Your presence, discipline, courage and sacrifices save lives in our province.”

nnnn

He revealed that Mpumalanga recorded 742 crashes and 143 fatalities during the previous festive season—slightly lower than the previous year—and stressed that the province is committed to halving road deaths by 2030, in line with the United Nations’ targets.

nnnn

To achieve this, Macie announced intensified operations from Thursdays through Mondays, with additional corridor operations during peak travel periods. Twelve major high-risk routes—including the N4, R40, R573, R38 and N11—will be closely monitored.

nnnn

He issued firm warnings to motorists driving without number plates and to speedsters attempting to dodge law enforcement.

nnnn

“Vehicles without number plates will be impounded. Anyone caught speeding will be traced and arrested—even in their deep sleep. Asidlali siyasebenze lana,” he said.

nnnn

Ports of entry such as Lebombo, Matsamo, Oshoek and Mahamba will also see heightened monitoring.

nnnn

Macie further directed the Provincial Commissioner to deploy anti-corruption agents during the festive season.

nnnn

“They must show no mercy—both the corruptor and the corruptee will be arrested,” he warned.

nnnn

He concluded by announcing the revival of excellence awards for traffic officers, with the top performer set to win a brand-new vehicle.

nnnnnnnn

Deputy Minister Hlengwa: Road Deaths a National Crisis

nnnn

In his keynote address, Deputy Minister Hlengwa said the Roll Call was taking place at a painful time for the nation, with many families still grieving recent road tragedies.

nnnn

“This Roll Call happens while we are mourning many lives lost on our roads. We extend our deepest condolences,” he said.

nnnn

Hlengwa emphasised that road safety is a shared national priority that requires strong partnerships across all three spheres of government. He warned that road crashes continue to drain the economy and devastate families.

nnnn

Citing the National Road Safety Strategy, he said road crashes cost South Africa R143 billion in 2015, rising to over R164 billion in the subsequent years—highlighting “a stubbornly sticky crisis”.

nnnn

He said the solution lies in three pillars:

nnnn

professional traffic enforcement, safe road infrastructure, and behavioural change among road users.

nnnn

“The safety of people and cargo rests on the shoulders of the men and women in this force,” he told officers, stressing the need for integrity, ethical conduct, modern tools, safe working conditions and continuous training.

nnnn

Infrastructure, AARTO and Intergovernmental Cooperation

nnnn

Hlengwa noted that major national road upgrades are underway in Mpumalanga and the rest of the country. He welcomed the recent transfer of certain provincial roads to SANRAL for improved management but emphasised that provinces must eventually be able to sustain their own road infrastructure through the equitable share.

nnnn

He reaffirmed that the long-delayed AARTO demerit system is scheduled for launch in July 2026, calling it a critical step in reducing reckless driving.

nnnn

“A sustainable solution to road fatalities depends on better behaviour by road users and safer road infrastructure,” he said.

nnnn

The Deputy Minister pledged national support to Mpumalanga and other provinces to resolve challenges affecting road safety: “These challenges must be collectively resolved by all of us. We are committed to supporting every province.”

nnnn

United Front for a Safer Festive Season

nnnn

Both leaders praised the collaborative spirit displayed at the Roll Call and urged officers to approach the festive season with discipline, professionalism and renewed commitment.

nnnn

“Every family that arrives home safely is a victory,” said MEC Macie. “Let us protect lives with pride, honour and dedication.”

nnnn

The combined message from provincial and national leadership was clear: Road safety is everyone’s responsibility, and this festive season Mpumalanga will leave nothing to chance.
