The Border Management Authority (BMA) has made another significant breakthrough in its ongoing efforts to curb illicit trade, following the seizure of illicit tobacco at the Beitbridge commercial port of entry in the early hours of 19 November 2025.

nnnn

According to BMA Commissioner Dr Michael Masiapato, the operation unfolded at around 01:00, when Junior Border Guards conducted a detailed inspection of a commercial truck entering South Africa from Zimbabwe. Using the BMA’s newly acquired Video Scope inspection toolkit, officers detected suspicious concealed cargo.

nnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnn

A subsequent physical inspection revealed 14 master boxes of Remington Gold cigarettes hidden inside the truck. One Zimbabwean national was arrested at the scene, and a docket has been opened for further investigation.

nnnn

Dr Masiapato said the successful detection highlighted the importance of investing in modern border-control technologies. “Illicit tobacco deprives the South African Revenue Service (SARS) of critical revenue. By intercepting such consignments, the BMA helps to safeguard tax integrity and public finances. Beyond the immediate financial loss, illicit cigarettes pose health risks and fuel organised crime,” he said.

nnnn

He added that the coordinated efforts of Junior Border Guards, supported by advanced scanning tools, remain central to disrupting sophisticated smuggling networks operating in vulnerable border areas.

nnnn

Members of the public are encouraged to report suspicious border-related activities through Operation HI-TIVISE on 0801 229 019 or via the BMA online platform.

post_title: Attorney Sentenced to Ten Years for Theft of RAF Money
post_content:
n

An attorney from Mpumalanga has been sentenced to ten years of direct imprisonment after being found guilty on four counts of theft involving Road Accident Fund (RAF) payments. Jo-Anne Mantladi Mmela (44) was sentenced on Thursday, 20 November 2025, by the Middelburg Serious Commercial Crimes Court.

nnnn

Mmela, who operated under her law firm, Mmela and Associates, had been appointed to manage an RAF claim on behalf of a child. After the RAF processed the claim and transferred the payout into her trust account, she diverted the funds into another person’s account. She later claimed that she had paid the money to the child’s guardian, which was found to be untrue.

nnnn

A complaint was lodged, prompting an investigation by the Middelburg-based Serious Commercial Investigation team. Mmela was arrested on 20 September 2022 and appeared in the Middelburg Magistrates’ Court the next day, where she was granted bail of R25 000. The matter was postponed to 5 December 2022 for further investigation, but the attorney absconded and failed to appear.

nnnn

A media statement issued on 21 February 2024 appealed to the public for assistance in locating her. Thanks to information received, investigators traced and arrested Mmela in Pretoria. She was denied bail and remained in custody. During this period, additional victims came forward, leading to three more counts of RAF-related theft being added to her charges.

nnnn

On 20 November 2025, the Middelburg Commercial Crimes Court handed down a sentence of ten years’ direct imprisonment. The Provincial Head of the Hawks in Mpumalanga welcomed the ruling, praising both the investigative team and the National Prosecuting Authority for securing a firm and appropriate sentence.

post_title: GBV Declared National Disaster at G20
post_content:
n

South Africa has taken a historic step in the fight against Gender-Based Violence and Femicide (GBVF), following President Cyril Ramaphosa’s announcement at the G20 Social Summit that the crisis will be formally classified as a National Disaster.

nnnn

The announcement comes after an international petition started by Women For Change, led by founder Sabrina Walter, drew support from more than 1.1 million people worldwide. For nearly a decade, Walter and her organisation have been at the forefront of advocating for survivors, supporting grieving families, and demanding urgent government action.

nnnn

In her official statement, Walter described the moment as the culmination of years of painful stories, tireless campaigning, and unwavering public support. “We have witnessed the unbearable grief of families who had to identify the bodies of the women they loved. Today, that persistence has been recognised. We have won,” she said.

nnnn

Following the President’s announcement, an internal meeting was held with the Minister of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs, Velenkosini Hlabisa, the authority responsible for declaring national disasters. According to Walter, ministers from multiple key departments have reached an agreement, and the formal declaration is expected to be signed on Friday. A follow-up meeting next week will outline the implementation plan and timelines for action.

nnnn

Walter paid tribute to her team, describing them as the “heartbeat of Women For Change” and credited every individual who signed the petition, shared the message, or supported the movement. “We have written history together. We forced the country to finally confront the truth,” she said.

nnnn

In a powerful act of national solidarity, South African women, children, and members of the LGBTQI+ community are expected to participate in a nationwide shutdown on Friday, 21 November. Participants will withdraw their labour and lie down for 15 minutes at 12:00 PM in silence to honour victims and survivors of GBVF.

nnnn

“We will do this for the women who died begging to be believed… for every survivor who still suffers in silence… for the next generation,” Walter said.

nnnn

She emphasised that the declaration is only the beginning of a long fight for safety and justice. “Tomorrow, we lie down — not in defeat, but in power. Tomorrow, we rise — for every woman, every child,” she concluded.

nnnn

The world will be watching as South Africa stands still to confront one of its most urgent national crises.

post_title: BMA Ensures Smooth G20 Delegation Arrivals
post_content:
n

With the G20 Leaders’ Summit just a day away, the Border Management Authority (BMA) has confirmed that all designated Ports of Entry across South Africa have remained stable, fully operational, and incident-free as high-level delegations continue to arrive.

nnnn

BMA Commissioner Dr Michael Masiapato said the authority has successfully facilitated arrivals of several world leaders, including European Union President Ursula von der Leyen, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Malaysian President Dato’ Seri Anwar Ibrahim, European Council President António Costa, Vietnamese Prime Minister Pham Minh Chinh, China’s Premier Li Qiang and United Kingdom Prime Minister Keir Starmer, among others. More arrivals are expected as summit activities intensify.

nnnn

Over the past week, BMA teams have managed the arrivals of delegates attending the G20 Sherpa Meeting, the G20 Social Summit, and the B20 Summit. Despite increased traveller volumes and heightened security demands, all processing has remained efficient and uninterrupted.

nnnn

Key airports, including OR Tambo International, Lanseria International and Waterkloof Air Force Base, are receiving dedicated ICT support to maintain seamless systems operation. Special G20 processing counters are fully staffed to handle the high volumes associated with the summit.

nnnn

Enhanced security measures are in place across all operational zones, supported by routine SAPS security sweeps and strict access-control protocols. Unattended luggage continues to be attended to in line with international security standards.

nnnn

To strengthen operational readiness, additional BMA personnel have been deployed, and senior officials remain on-site to oversee operations. High-visibility patrols, crime-prevention efforts and screening-point searches form part of a layered security approach to ensure compliance and safety.

nnnn

Land Ports of Entry serving as contingency support points for ground transport remain in close coordination with regional and international partners. Patrols along port corridors have also been intensified to prevent traffic bottlenecks and ensure a smooth flow of movement.

nnnn

The BMA says it remains committed to delivering world-class border operations throughout the G20 Summit.

nnnn

The public is encouraged to report suspicious activity through Operation HI-TIVISE on 0801 229 019 or via the BMA website.

Bushbuckridge SAPS have launched an urgent investigation following the disappearance of 52-year-old Mmika Johnson Mogakane. According to information released by the police, Mr Mogakane was last seen at Dwarsloop Mall on Thursday at approximately 15:00.

Green Scorpions Honoured in Landmark Celebration
post_content:
n

South African National Parks (SANParks) has joined the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) in marking the inaugural Environmental Management Inspectorate (EMI) Day, celebrated nationwide on 20 November 2025. The day forms part of the DFFE’s EMI Brand Promotion Strategy, aimed at raising awareness about the vital role played by Environmental Management Inspectors—widely known as the Green Scorpions—in protecting the country’s natural and cultural heritage.

nnnn

SANParks, as an accredited EMI institution, employs a significant number of these inspectors across its national parks. Their responsibilities include enforcing environmental legislation, combating ecological crimes, and ensuring the preservation of South Africa’s rich biodiversity. EMI Day provides an opportunity to recognise their commitment, highlight their work, and engage the public in understanding the importance of environmental law enforcement.

nnnn

Several national parks participated in the celebrations, including Kgalagadi Transfrontier Park, Camdeboo National Park, Kruger National Park, and Table Mountain National Park. Activities were hosted in collaboration with various stakeholders, focusing on visible law enforcement aligned with this year’s theme: “Green Scorpions: The Protectors of the Environment for Future Generations.”

nnnnnnnn

These initiatives aim to improve public visibility of the Green Scorpions and promote a deeper appreciation of their daily efforts. From tackling wildlife crime to maintaining the integrity of protected areas, EMIs continue to play a fundamental role in safeguarding South Africa’s environmental future.

SALGA Mpumalanga Strengthens Governance and Service Delivery
post_content:
n

The South African Local Government Association (SALGA) Mpumalanga Provincial Executive Committee (PEC) held its 88th sitting on Wednesday, 19 November 2025, at the Steve Tshwete Local Municipality Council Chamber. The meeting reaffirmed its commitment to ethical leadership, improved service delivery, and sustainable development across the province.

nnnn

Chairperson Councillor Walter Mngomezulu emphasised the importance of capable and people-centred municipalities. He stressed that the District Development Model must align with the Constitution and the Municipal Systems Act to prevent parallel planning processes. He also noted the need for a dedicated funding model to support the model’s implementation.

nnnn

Key Outcomes and Highlights

nnnn

Governance and Accountability:
Workshops held in Lekwa, Victor Khanye and Mkhondo municipalities focused on reducing Unauthorised, Irregular, Fruitless and Wasteful (UIFW) expenditure, strengthening Municipal Public Accounts Committees (MPACs), and enhancing consequence management.

nnnn

Community Safety and By-law Enforcement:
Municipalities received support to revive Community Safety Forums and boost by-law enforcement. Engagements with the Private Security Industry Regulatory Authority (PSiRA) addressed compliance and standard operating procedures.

nnnn

Social Cohesion and Vulnerable Groups:
Programmes were implemented in Thaba Chweu, Steve Tshwete and Nkomazi to advance sport, arts, culture and heritage. Plans to better support vulnerable groups were also discussed.

nnnn

Migration and Health Integration:
Capacity-building with the International Organization for Migration (IOM) highlighted the need to integrate migration into Integrated Development Plans (IDPs). Nkangala District achieved an 80% score for Municipal Health Services integration, with recommendations for improved disease surveillance.

nnnn

Infrastructure and Service Delivery:
Progress was noted in water and sanitation through Green Drop audits and the Blue Deal Crocodile River project. Emakhazeni Local Municipality is adopting a Waste Management App, while Nkomazi is rolling out a tariff-setting model to improve cost recovery.

nnnn

Energy Transition and Compliance:
In partnership with GIZ, UK PACT and SANEDI, municipalities received training on embedded generation tariffs, bi-directional metering and Energy Performance Certificates (EPCs). Municipalities were urged to finalise EPC registrations before the December 2025 deadline.

nnnn

Economic Development and Township Economy:
A Provincial Local Economic Development Forum was launched to align recovery plans with provincial priorities. Nineteen municipalities have adopted the Standard Draft By-law for Township, Village and Rural Economies, with gazetting support currently underway. SALGA further facilitated SMME training in Dr JS Moroka Local Municipality.

nnnn

The PEC resolved to fast-track township economy by-law gazetting, strengthen planning and enforcement capacity, expand technical support for water and energy programmes, and reinforce oversight across municipalities.

post_title: Court Protest Erupts Over Murder Accused
post_content:
n

The Saselani community and residents from nearby villages gathered outside the Mhlala Magistrate Court in Thulamahashe earlier today(Monday 24 November), demanding that bail be denied for murder-accused businessman Sidwell Khoza, popularly known as Tshep Tshep.

nnnnnnnn

Khoza, a well-known figure in Buyisonto with businesses including a tavern, bottle store, mortuary and taxi operations, stands accused of the brutal murders of Hlamariso Sambo (35) and Kenneth Nkuna (34).

nnnn

nnnn

Tensions were high as community members voiced their frustrations, calling for justice and expressing fear over safety should Khoza be released. Placards, chants and a strong turnout highlighted the community’s demand for accountability.

nnnn

During today’s proceedings, the Magistrate presiding over the case made a formal request to recuse himself, citing reasons not disclosed publicly. The matter has now been postponed to 27 November, when further clarity on the recusal and bail application is expected.

nnnn

According to information presented in court, the alleged motive behind the killings is linked to a dispute over the victims’ Road Accident Fund (RAF)payout — a development that has shocked and angered the community even further.

post_title: IFP Warns Against Risky Matric Celebrations
post_content:
n

The Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) has urged parents and guardians to ensure that matric learners avoid attending the increasingly popular “Pens Down” celebrations, warning that these events often expose young people to significant danger.

nnnn

The party emphasised that while completing matric is a major milestone, celebrations must be handled responsibly. Concerns include public drinking, drug use, and unsafe environments that place learners at risk. The IFP referenced the tragic loss of 21 young people at the Enyobeni Tavern in June 2022, calling it a sobering reminder of the devastation caused by unsafe festivities.

nnnn

The party has also noted a growing trend of learners tearing or writing messages on their school uniforms. While it recognises the excitement and symbolic significance behind the practice, the IFP appeals to learners to reserve such activities for old or unusable uniforms. Wearable items should instead be donated to pupils returning to school in 2026.

nnnn

Parents and families are further encouraged to provide emotional support to matriculants as they wait for their final results. The IFP warns that excessive pressure can lead to heightened stress, anxiety or depression. Observing behavioural changes during this period is vital.

nnnn

Addressing the Matric Class of 2025, the IFP acknowledged their resilience and commitment throughout a demanding school year. The party encouraged them to celebrate safely, enjoy the festive season responsibly, and seize new opportunities in the coming year — whether through learnerships, volunteering, part-time jobs or work experience.

nnnn

“Education remains one of the most powerful tools at your disposal. Continue to dream boldly, strive for excellence and walk with purpose,” the statement concluded.

post_title: ANC Questions SACP's Independent Election Move
post_content:
n

The African National Congress (ANC) has reiterated its concern over the South African Communist Party’s (SACP) decision to contest the 2026 local government elections independently. The issue was a key focus during a meeting of alliance partners held at Luthuli House in Johannesburg on Monday.

nnnn

The SACP recently resolved to participate in the elections outside of its long-standing alliance with the ANC. This decision followed the party’s dissatisfaction with the ANC’s cooperation with the Democratic Alliance (DA) in the government of national unity, rather than engaging what it views as progressive political partners such as the EFF and MK Party.

nnnn

According to the ANC, the SACP’s decision is believed to undermine the broader coordinated efforts aimed at advancing a national democratic society and continuing the historical mission of the national democratic revolution. The governing party maintains that the move may present practical challenges and weaken collective influence within the political landscape.

nnnn

Despite its decision, the SACP has emphasised its commitment to maintaining strong relations within the tripartite alliance, which includes the ANC and trade union federation Cosatu. The party considers its resolution to contest independently as a product of thorough internal analysis, while still valuing the long-standing political cooperation that underpins the alliance.

nnnn

As discussions continue, both parties have expressed interest in preserving unity, even as they navigate differing views on electoral strategy.

post_title: Research Key to Safeguarding Food Future
post_content:
n

Many of us can recall the familiar childhood warning to finish our vegetables or risk never growing up strong like our favourite superheroes. As children, we imagined caped crusaders swooping in to rescue us from the dreaded broccoli on our plates. Yet today, researchers are focused on a different kind of rescue — protecting the very food that sustains us.

nnnn

As adults, we now know that real-life heroes do not wear capes. One such hero is the National Planning Commission (NPC), a body undertaking critical research in agriculture at a time when climate change is reshaping landscapes across the world.

nnnn

NPC Commissioner Dr Lebogang Pheko recently shared her concerns about a future where essential foods may become scarce or expensive.

nnnn

“What would it look like if certain crops are no longer available? What does it mean for the cost of staples such as pap? And what does that mean for our cultural legacy and the way food shapes our celebrations, traditions, and daily life?” she asked.

nnnn

Her questions highlight the crucial role that long-term research plays in preparing society for uncertainties.

nnnn

Appointed by the President, the NPC serves as an independent advisory body and custodian of the National Development Plan (NDP), which aims to eliminate poverty and reduce inequality by 2030. Economic growth, exports, and a more labour-absorbing economy form part of its central goals.

nnnn

Dr Pheko, one of 26 Commissioners, has been deeply involved in commissioning research on agricultural methods, small business development, irrigation systems, and reducing regulatory barriers. Chapter 6 of the NDP emphasises agriculture as a key driver of job creation, particularly in rural areas, with the vegetable industry identified as a major potential contributor.

nnnn

A significant portion of the Commission’s work focuses on the impact of climate change on water availability, irrigation, and food production. “Water scarcity is expected to worsen unless we act now,” she warned. This will affect planting seasons, food availability, and the cost of many staple foods.

nnnn

Beyond economics, the research also explores the legacy of food — the meals woven into our cultural identity — and how these might be affected by shifting climate patterns. It further examines ways to reframe South Africa’s agricultural footprint, especially as fewer young people pursue careers in farming. Pheko believes the country must rethink the appeal of agricultural studies and encourage young people to see farming as part of nation-building.

nnnn

President Cyril Ramaphosa has echoed the importance of this sector. In a recent national newsletter, he described agriculture as central to the economy, noting that the value and volume of the sector has more than doubled since 1994. By the end of 2024, over 924,000 people were directly employed in agriculture, with a further 200,000 working across the value chain. South Africa also exported a record $13.7 billion in agricultural products in 2024, with nearly half going to other African countries.

nnnn

To reach the NDP’s target of creating one million new jobs in agriculture, the NPC recommends increased investment in irrigation infrastructure and greater support for agricultural research and development. Climate change remains a central concern, with repeated floods in KwaZulu-Natal demonstrating the urgent need for improved planning.

nnnn

Dr Pheko argues that rural and urban planning must be aligned to create sustainable, self-sufficient communities. “People move to cities because they do not see opportunities in rural areas. We must rethink development so every generation can imagine a future where they live,” she said.

nnnn

Looking beyond 2030, the Commission is examining future scenarios to ensure South Africa is not caught unprepared. Socio-spatial arrangements, agricultural systems, and water and energy planning all form part of this forward-looking research.

nnnn

Reflecting on South Africa’s current economic landscape, Pheko describes it as historically complex and overly reliant on labour-intensive models. She expressed concern about poor literacy and numeracy levels among young learners, which limits progress in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics — areas crucial for future development. Skills in agriculture are also being overtaken by mechanisation, requiring renewed focus on training and diversification.

nnnn

With her term ending in 2026, Pheko hopes her legacy will be one of foresight, collaboration, and the creation of a strong foundation for future policy. “I hope people see that we tried to chart a long-term course for the country,” she said.

nnnn

Just as superheroes protect their communities, the NPC’s work is quietly shaping a safer future for the next generation — ensuring that, despite the challenges ahead, South Africa’s food security and agricultural legacy remain intact.

n

Hazyview residents will come together this Saturday for a heartfelt cause as Hazyview Primary, Panda Preschool and Hazy Runners host a Fun Run/Walk for Bongeka at the Hazyview Primary School grounds. The event, taking place on 29 November 2025 from 08:00 to 13:00, aims to raise funds and awareness for nine-year-old Bongeka, a courageous young girl battling a life-threatening congenital condition.

nnnn

Bongeka has lived with liver cirrhosis since birth, enduring numerous surgeries and hospital stays. In 2021, specialists at Wits Donald Gordon Hospital assessed her for a liver transplant, but severe lung complications made the procedure too dangerous. Despite receiving a terminal prognosis, she continues to defy expectations with extraordinary resilience and the unwavering support of her family and community.

nnnnnnnn

In recent months, her condition has worsened. She suffered severe internal bleeding and now requires frequent surgical interventions to repair her veins. Bongeka also depends on a daily oxygen concentrator, as her oxygen levels often fall below 60%, making continuous oxygen therapy essential for her survival.

nnnn

Saturday's event is designed not only to bring the community together but also to provide much-needed financial support for her ongoing medical care, surgical procedures and home-based oxygen therapy. Organisers have encouraged participants, well-wishers and potential sponsors to attend and contribute towards easing the family's growing medical expenses.

nnnn

The organisers say the Fun Run/Walk represents more than just a fitness activity—it symbolises hope in every step taken for Bongeka's future.

nnnn

Willing sponsors and supporters are welcome to join on the day.

post_title: Calcutta Suspect Arrested After Deadly Attack
post_content:
n

A 45-year-old man has been arrested in connection with a brutal murder and attempted murder that took place in Oakley Trust, Calcutta, in the early hours of 22 November 2025.

nnnn

Police were called to an RDP house just after 04:30, where they discovered the body of a man lying in a pool of blood with severe upper-body injuries. He was declared dead at the scene. A second victim, a woman believed to be the suspect’s friend, was found in the same house with serious injuries. Although unable to speak, she was still alive and was rushed to a nearby hospital for urgent medical care.

nnnn

A crowbar, believed to have been used during the attack, was recovered by investigators.

nnnn

Following swift investigative work, police arrested the suspect, identified as Alfred Dumisani Shabalala. He appeared before the Mkhuhlu Magistrate’s Court on 25 November on charges of murder and attempted murder. His case was postponed to 27 November, and he will remain in custody.

post_title: Paediatric Echo Workshop Strengthens Child Healthcare
post_content:
n

The first-ever Paediatric Echocardiography Workshop was held on 23 November 2025 at Rob Ferreira Hospital in the City of Mbombela, marking an important step forward for child healthcare in Mpumalanga. The event was led by the Paediatric Cardiology team under the guidance of Dr Zinzile Ngwenyama and formed part of the nationwide South African Paediatric Association (SAPA) and Paediatric Cardiac Society of South Africa (PCCSA) echocardiography training initiative.

nnnnnnnn

The programme was conducted simultaneously at several major centres across the country, including the University of Cape Town, Steve Biko Academic Hospital, Inkosi Albert Luthuli Central Hospital, and Polokwane.

nnnn

The workshop aimed to equip doctors from referral hospitals with the skills needed to perform basic screening echocardiograms. By improving doctors’ ability to detect cardiac abnormalities early, the training seeks to reduce delays in diagnosis and prevent avoidable deaths linked to heart disease at district and base-hospital level.

nnnn

Doctors from across the province attended in notable numbers, representing Themba, Tintswalo, Mapulaneng, Barberton, Ermelo, Matikwana, Lydenburg, Shongwe and Rob Ferreira hospitals.

nnnn

Participants were especially privileged to learn under the mentorship of Professor John Lawrenson, the retired Head of Paediatric Cardiology at the University of Cape Town. He facilitated the training alongside Dr Ngwenyama, offering invaluable knowledge and experience to the attending clinicians.

nnnn

“We are confident that this training will positively impact the clinical care of paediatric patients across the province. We extend our sincere appreciation to everyone who provided support in various forms,” said Dr Ngwenyama.

nnnn

The initiative reflects a growing provincial commitment to strengthening healthcare systems and improving outcomes for children living with heart conditions.

n

post_title: Group Stages Ignite Youth Sports Spirit
post_content:
n

The 2025 GKEPF–JMF U19 Cup officially kicked off on 25 November, with excitement rising as teams received their kits ahead of the men’s Group Stages, which began on 26 November. For young athletes across the Greater Kruger landscape, the journey to this prestigious youth tournament is now well underway.

nnnn

The men’s football Group Stages run from 26 November to 6 December, hosted across four Bushbuckridge stadiums: Thulamahashe Old Stadium, Cunningmore Stadium, HUBS Sports Field, and Acorn–Oaks Stadium. Women’s football, featuring eight teams, and netball, with sixteen teams, will follow from 8–13 December at Thulamahashe New Stadium.

nnnn

Sixteen men’s teams from communities throughout the Greater Kruger region are competing for a place in the Knock Out Stages. Fixtures will be played every second day at the four stadiums, with the full match schedule confirmed during the official launch event. Only the top eight teams will progress to the Knock Outs, scheduled for 8–13 December at Thulamahashe New Stadium.

nnnn

This year introduces a significant shift, with Group Stage matches being hosted within the participating communities themselves. This community-centred approach strengthens local ownership, leadership, and the connection between youth, sport, and conservation efforts in the Greater Kruger landscape.

nnnn

The kit handover ceremony once again proved to be a highlight of the tournament. More than just uniforms, the kits symbolise unity, identity, and pride. Players step onto the pitch representing not only their teams, but a shared vision to uplift local youth, strengthen community ties, and create meaningful opportunities through sport.

nnnnnnnn

Organisers expressed gratitude to partner reserves, the Oak Foundation, donors, supporters, and community leaders whose dedication continues to make the tournament possible.

nnnn

nnnn

The case dates back to 2009 when the pair, along with a third accused, the late Solly Zitha, assaulted a woman who had confronted them for allegedly stealing her cattle. An argument broke out during the confrontation, leading to a violent attack in which the victim was severely beaten. She later died from her injuries.

nnnn

The trio were arrested the following day and subsequently released on bail. Dissatisfied with the progress of the initial investigation, the victim’s family pushed for further action, resulting in the case being transferred to the Hawks’ Nelspruit-based Serious Organised Crime Investigation unit.

post_title: Public Protector Probes President’s Conduct Allegations

The confirmation was issued on Monday after the office assessed the complaint and found sufficient grounds to proceed with an inquiry into possible violations of clauses relating to abuse of power, improper conduct, acting inconsistently with constitutional responsibilities, and failing to act in the best interests of the Republic.

In a statement released on Wednesday, the MK Party welcomed the development, describing it as an important step towards accountability for what it views as ongoing ethical concerns during President Cyril Ramaphosa’s administration. The party stated that it regards the investigation as vital for restoring public confidence in the Presidency and ensuring that all elected leaders are subject to the same standards of accountability.

The party also raised broader concerns about what it considers the weakening of oversight institutions and the alleged misuse of state resources to shield the President and those close to him. It referenced longstanding issues, including the Phala Phala matter and other governance challenges, arguing that South Africans are entitled to transparent and ethical leadership.

nnnn

According to the Public Protector’s office, the decision to investigate follows a thorough assessment of the MK Party’s submission, which was deemed to provide adequate grounds for inquiry. post_title: South Africa Renews Fight Against HIV
post_content:
n

South Africa joined the global community on Monday to mark World Aids Day, with national leaders calling for renewed momentum to close the remaining gaps in HIV prevention and treatment. The official commemoration took place at the Ga-Masemola Stadium in Limpopo, led by Deputy President Paul Mashatile in his capacity as Chairperson of the South African National Aids Council (SANAC). He was accompanied by Health Minister Dr Aaron Motsoaledi, along with provincial and community representatives.

nnnn

The day served as a reminder that, despite major achievements, HIV remains one of the biggest public health challenges facing the country. South Africa continues to record the world’s highest number of people living with HIV, estimated at around eight million. Of these, roughly six million are currently receiving life-saving antiretroviral therapy, while more than 3.5 million have reached viral suppression — significantly reducing their risk of transmitting the virus.

nnnn

According to National Department of Health spokesperson Foster Mohale, this year’s event underscores the importance of staying focused on the fight against HIV. He noted that millions still require support to start treatment, remain in care, and protect themselves from new infections. Mohale said South Africans must continue to test regularly, initiate treatment early, and stay on their medication.

nnnn

Government interventions are being intensified through the 1.1 Million – Close the Gap HIV Treatment Campaign. This drive aims to reach more than one million people who have already been diagnosed but are not yet on treatment. The national rollout of Six Multi-Month Dispensing (6MMD) is another key measure, enabling stable patients to collect a six-month supply of medication and reducing the need for frequent clinic visits. Authorities say this approach eases congestion at facilities and improves adherence.

nnnn

The Department of Health emphasises that prevention services, testing, and treatment remain available at all public clinics. Communities are encouraged to take responsibility for their health by knowing their status and seeking help early.

nnnn

As the country reflects on its progress, government leaders say World Aids Day is both a celebration of resilience and a renewed call to action. South Africa continues to work towards achieving the global 95-95-95 targets and ending Aids as a public health threat.

post_title: Six-Month HIV Prevention Injection Rolled Out
post_content:
n

A groundbreaking HIV-prevention injection is being introduced in South Africa, Eswatini and Zambia, marking the first public rollout of the treatment in Africa — the region with the highest HIV burden in the world.

nnnn

The injectable drug, lenacapavir, is administered twice a year and has shown remarkable results, reducing the risk of HIV transmission by more than 99.9%. Experts have described it as functioning almost like a powerful vaccine due to its long-lasting protection.

nnnn

In South Africa — where an estimated one in five adults lives with HIV — the rollout is being overseen by a Wits University research unit as part of a Unitaid-funded initiative. Unitaid confirmed that the first individuals have now begun receiving the 6-monthly injection, placing the country among the first low- and middle-income nations to access the treatment outside clinical trials.

nnnn

While Unitaid did not disclose how many people received the initial doses, the drug’s cost in the United States — around $28,000 (over R500,000) per person annually — has raised concerns about global accessibility. A wider national rollout in South Africa is expected next year.

nnnn

Neighbouring Zambia and Eswatini, which each received 1,000 doses last month through a United States-backed programme, were expected to launch their public rollouts during World AIDS Day commemorations.

nnnn

As part of the programme, Gilead Sciences, the drug’s manufacturer, has committed to supplying lenacapavir at no profit to two million people across high-burden countries over the next three years. However, health activists argue that this supply falls far short of the actual need.

nnnn

According to UNAIDS 2024 data, eastern and southern Africa account for 52% of the 40.8 million people living with HIV globally.

nnnn

More affordable generic versions of lenacapavir are expected from 2027, through agreements facilitated by Unitaid and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation with manufacturers in India. These generics are expected to cost about $40 per year, improving access across more than 100 countries.

nnnn

Although pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) has been available for over a decade, the requirement of a daily pill has limited its uptake. Health experts believe the new twice-yearly injection could be a game-changer in preventing new infections across the continent.

post_title: Five Killed In Horrific R33 Crash
post_content:
n

Five people were tragically killed on Monday afternoon when a bus overturned on the R33 Road between eMkhondo and Amsterdam. The accident happened on 1 December 2025 after the driver reportedly lost control of the vehicle, causing it to overturn.

nnnn

According to authorities, six passengers sustained serious injuries, while 20 others suffered minor injuries. The driver is among those injured. Emergency services transported all injured passengers to a nearby hospital in Mkhondo.

nnnn

Initial reports suggested that the bus was carrying more than 80 passengers; however, officials have clarified that the passenger list recorded 65 people when it departed Johannesburg. Some travellers disembarked along the route, and only 31 passengers, including the driver, were on board at the time of the crash.

nnnn

Although the cause of the crash is still under investigation, wet weather conditions are suspected to have contributed to the tragic incident.

nnnn

Mpumalanga MEC for Community Safety, Security and Liaison, Mr Jackie Macie, has urged motorists to adjust their driving according to prevailing road conditions, especially during wet weather.

nnnn

“Every driver must prioritise their own safety and that of other road users. Let us save lives by being highly alert and obeying the rules. Long-distance drivers must rest sufficiently along the way,” said Macie.

nnnn

He extended his heartfelt condolences to the families of the deceased and wished a speedy recovery to the injured.

post_title: Civil Society Demands Urgent Action for LGBTQIA+ Safety
post_content:
n

Civil society organisations working within the LGBTQIA+ sector are calling for urgent reforms in the policing and justice system to address the growing crisis of secondary victimisation experienced by LGBTQIA+ survivors of hate crimes, discrimination and abuse.

nnnn

On Saturday, representatives from Bushbuckridge Local Municipality, the Civil Society Forum (LGBTQIA+ Sector), Sonke Gender Justice, Colour Splash, Conservation South Africa and the Forum for the Empowerment of Women handed over a memorandum to the Officer in Charge at Mhala Police Station.

nnnnnnnn

The memorandum highlights the widespread withdrawal of cases by LGBTQIA+ survivors, which organisations say is caused by insensitive treatment, lack of support and discriminatory conduct from some police officers.

nnnn

“We cannot ignore the reality that a system meant to protect people is instead re-traumatising them. Survivors are withdrawing cases because they fear secondary victimisation more than the perpetrators themselves,” said Nomalanga Ngwenya, Project Manager for Gender Justice in Mpumalanga.

nnnn

According to the memorandum, LGBTQIA+ people — particularly women, trans and gender-diverse individuals — face heightened risks of violence, which are worsened when survivors encounter biased questioning, a lack of empathy or inadequate protection from the police.

nnnn

Caroline Sibuyi, organiser of the LGBTQIA+ Bushbuckridge sector, said the march was not only about visibility but also about demanding dignity.

nnnn

“I feel happy and very positive about the march because we wanted Bushbuckridge residents and police officers to see that we exist and can stand together as the LGBTIQ+ community. All we need is acceptance and safety in our community. I am glad it was a peaceful march,” she said.

nnnn

Sibuyi also voiced fears shared by many queer individuals in the area. “The hatred that comes from society… I live in fear that any day it could be me who is raped or murdered. I live my life without harming anyone, yet I fear for my own,” she added.

nnnn

Organisations warn that many case withdrawals are not voluntary. Survivors often feel coerced or pressured after encountering unsupportive treatment from officers or fearing further victimisation.

nnnn

“When a survivor walks into a police station and is met with judgement or ridicule, that case is already lost. Trust collapses instantly,” one advocacy representative said during the handover.

nnnn

Key Issues Raised

nnnn

The memorandum outlines three pressing concerns:

nnnn
    n
  • Secondary Victimisation: LGBTQIA+ survivors face repeated trauma through insensitive or discriminatory police behaviour.
    • nnnn
  • Withdrawal of Cases: Fear, intimidation and lack of trust continue to drive high case-withdrawal rates.
    • nnnn
  • Protection of Survivors: There is an urgent need for stronger, survivor-centred reporting and investigation protocols.
    • n
nnnn

Proposed Actions for Police

nnnn

To address the crisis, organisations submitted several recommendations:

nnnn
    n
  1. Sensitivity Training for Law Enforcement: To improve understanding of LGBTQIA+ issues and reduce discriminatory behaviour.
    2. nnnn
  2. Creation of Safe Spaces: LGBTQIA+-friendly reporting areas within police stations where survivors can seek help without judgement.
    3. nnnn
  3. Increased Awareness and Outreach: Encouraging survivors to report cases by educating them on their rights and available support.
    4. nnnn
  4. Support Throughout the Legal Process: Ensuring survivors have access to mental-health support, legal assistance and physical protection.
    5. nnnn
  5. Stronger Collaboration With Advocacy Groups: Working with LGBTQIA+ organisations to monitor cases and uphold survivors’ rights.
    6. n
nnnn

In the conclusion of the memorandum, Ngwenya emphasised the moral responsibility of law enforcement agencies. “This is not only a legal responsibility — it is a moral imperative. We are talking about protecting some of the most vulnerable members of our society,” she said.

nnnn

“We look forward to working together for a more inclusive and equitable future where justice is accessible to all, regardless of gender or sexual identity.”

nnnn

Receiving the memorandum, Lieutenant-Colonel Brian Mnisi, Station Commander at Mhala SAPS, assured marchers that their concerns would be taken seriously.

nnnn

“We understand your frustrations and challenges as highlighted in this memorandum, and we will forward it to the district so that it reaches the provincial office. The SAPS must take immediate action to create a safer environment for all and ensure your voices are heard,” Mnisi said.

nnnn

“As police, we work collectively to address every challenge faced by our communities.”

nnnn

The organisations urged the police to act swiftly and committed to ongoing engagement to ensure meaningful change for LGBTQIA+ individuals in Mpumalanga and beyond.

post_title: Health Workers Celebrate Long-Awaited Permanent Posts
post_content:
n

Community Health Workers (CHWs) across Mpumalanga erupted in joy on Monday as the MEC for Health, Sasekani Manzini, officially confirmed their permanent employment with the provincial Department of Health. The announcement was made on 1 December 2025 during a ceremony at the Rob Ferreira Tertiary Hospital Auditorium, held under the theme “Enhancing Community Health Services – The Resolution for Community Health Workers.” The theme reflects government’s commitment to recognising, professionalising and strengthening the vital work done by CHWs at community level.

nnnn

This milestone follows an implementation agreement signed on 25 November 2025 between the National Department of Health and NEHAWU. The agreement confirms that eligible CHWs will be appointed at salary level 2, effective from 1 September 2025. Importantly, the appointments will not require adherence to Regulation 65(1) of the Public Service Regulations, which usually obliges the advertising of vacant posts. This allows for a smooth and direct transition for qualifying workers.

nnnn

CHWs without Grade 12 will remain on contract but will receive a R1 000 increase to their monthly stipend, ensuring that they benefit from the reforms. By 31 January 2026, a “Token of Appreciation” will also be introduced for CHWs older than 65, acknowledging their years of service. Of the 5 224 CHWs in Mpumalanga, 1 624 have matric while 3 600 do not.

nnnn

Addressing the crowd, MEC Manzini praised the workers’ dedication. “We are here to confirm our commitment. You are now permanent employees of the department, with all the benefits of public servants. You deserve it. You were at the forefront in the fight against Covid-19, you brought health services to the doorsteps of our communities, and you continue to serve through campaigns such as Close the Gap and the immunisation catch-up programme.”

nnnn

Following the ceremony, the MEC led a World AIDS Day build-up activity, conducting HIV/AIDS awareness in the Outpatient Department and the Dental Unit. She was joined by Ehlanzeni District Municipality Speaker, Councillor Renias Khumalo, along with organised labour.

nnnnn

post_title: Illegal Veterinary Medicines Seized at Polokwane Airport
post_content:
n

The Border Management Authority (BMA) has confirmed the interception of a large consignment of illegally imported veterinary medicines at Polokwane International Airport on 26 November 2025. The seizure forms part of intensified efforts to protect South Africa’s livestock industry amid ongoing Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) outbreaks.

nnnn

According to BMA Commissioner Dr Michael Masiapato, Port Agriculture officials intercepted an aircraft arriving from Kenya and Tanzania carrying veterinary medicines known as Berenil. The products were found packed in two polystyrene boxes with a combined weight of approximately 84 kilograms. The shipment was reportedly in transit to Pietermaritzburg Airport.

nnnn

The consignment was denied entry after officials established that it lacked the legally required import permits under Section 6 of the Animal Diseases Act 35 of 1984. Following consultations with the Department of Agriculture, the medicines were confiscated and sent to the Onderstepoort Veterinary Institute – Transboundary Animal Diseases Laboratory (OVI-TAD) for further analysis.

nnnn

Commissioner Masiapato emphasised the BMA’s vigilance, noting the serious biosecurity threat posed by the illegal importation of veterinary products, particularly during the ongoing FMD outbreak. He said strengthened inspections at ports of entry are essential to safeguarding the health of the national herd and protecting the economic stability of local farmers.

nnnn

The attempt to smuggle untested animal medicines is considered a serious violation of South Africa’s veterinary and biosecurity laws. Foot and Mouth Disease is a highly contagious viral illness affecting cattle, sheep, goats and pigs, with severe consequences for livestock production and international trade.

nnnn

There are seven serotypes of the FMD virus, each requiring a specific vaccine. The introduction of foreign serotypes could compromise the Department of Agriculture’s ongoing control measures. Only legally procured FMD vaccines, sourced from the Botswana Vaccine Institute, are permitted for use in South Africa.

nnnn

Farmers have been urged to contact their local State Veterinarian if they suspect any signs of FMD in their livestock. Authorities have reiterated that unauthorised use of vaccines remains strictly prohibited.

nnnn

The BMA’s Port Agriculture unit remains committed to supporting national disease control programmes and strengthening South Africa’s biosecurity.

nnnn

Members of the public are encouraged to report corruption, suspicious activity or smuggling attempts through Operation HI-TIVISE on 0801 229 019, or via the BMA website at www.bma.gov.za

Throughout the day, patients received not only routine healthcare services but also essential health education focused on prevention, treatment adherence and overall well-being. Ambassadors living with HIV shared personal experiences and words of encouragement, urging community members to prioritise their health by going for regular check-ups at their nearest clinics and hospitals.

Healthcare workers emphasised that early testing, consistent treatment and community support remain key to reducing new infections and improving the quality of life for those living with HIV.

Rob Ferreira Hospital in Mbombela has achieved a groundbreaking medical milestone after successfully removing a complex Wilms tumour from a young child, marking the first operation of its kind in a public hospital in Mpumalanga.

nnnn

The surgical team removed the kidney tumour, which had caused a dangerous obstruction in the veins draining the kidney. The condition was further complicated by a blood clot that had travelled from the renal vein into the inferior vena cava (IVC)—the large vein responsible for returning blood from the lower body to the heart.

nnnn

The procedure required extraordinary precision, including the removal and reconstruction of parts of the affected veins to restore normal blood flow from the kidneys to the rest of the body.

nnnn

The surgical team included Dr Dave Tasker, head of the clinical unit at Rob Ferreira Hospital; a paediatric surgeon from Red Cross Children’s Hospital in Cape Town; Dr Omar Khamag; and consultant anaesthetist Dr Paul Nepgen.

nnnn

Mpumalanga’s MEC for Health, Ms Sasekani Manzini, praised the hospital for this historic achievement.

nnnn

“We are delighted and proud of our doctors for doing such a massive job,” she said. “The fact that this operation is the first of its kind to be performed in our public hospital means a lot for us and, more importantly, for the people of the province. This achievement demonstrates our commitment to bringing better health services to our communities.”

nnnn

Manzini added that the department aims to expand specialist services within Mpumalanga to ensure complicated cases can be treated at home rather than relying on Steve Biko Academic Hospital in Gauteng.

nnnn

“To us, this is what we call ‘Umehluko wezempilo ebantwini’—a true difference in the health of our people,” she said.

post_title: Minister Seeks Answers on Degree Scandal
post_content:
n

Minister of Higher Education and Training, Buti Manamela, has ordered a preliminary report from the Vaal University of Technology (VUT) following allegations of a degree-selling syndicate operating within the institution. The minister has given the university until 5 December to submit the report.

nnnn

According to ministerial spokesperson Matshepo Seedat, Manamela is “deeply concerned” by claims that the syndicate allegedly involves foreign nationals and that senior VUT management may have failed to act on credible whistleblower information for more than a year.

nnnn

Manamela criticised the reported inaction, stating that delays of this nature are unacceptable, especially when they threaten the integrity of the National Qualifications Framework.

nnnn

South African universities have faced similar controversies before. In 2016, a Sunday Times investigation revealed that approximately 4,000 fake degrees may have been issued over two decades at the University of Zululand in Empangeni.

nnnn

Seedat confirmed that the minister has requested a detailed explanation for the alleged 12-month delay in responding to the whistleblower’s report, as well as proof that consequence management processes have begun. Manamela has also instructed the university to take immediate steps to safeguard the 2026 registration cycle.

nnnn

Should VUT’s internal measures prove inadequate, the matter may be escalated to the Hawks for further investigation.

post_title: Tsonga Musician Turns Talent Into Brand
post_content:
n

 The rhythmic pulse of Tsonga music is finding a fresh outlet in the work of Pholoso Quietness Mhlongo, widely known as Pholoso Musician.

nnnn

Hailing from the rural town of Bushbuckridge, the young artist has progressed beyond local performances to build a brand that blends traditional sounds with modern production.

nnnn

Pholoso’s recent single, Munhu wa mina – the latest track within his self-styled Xigaza xa ma2K genre – showcases his talent for uniting heritage melodies with contemporary beats.

nnnnnnnn

The song has resonated across age groups, cementing his reputation as a trailblazer in South Africa’s diverse music landscape.

nnnn

His musical journey began in the late 2000s, singing in his church choir. “I gained recognition for being one of the best vocalists in church,” he told Timeless News.

nnnn

“When I moved to high school, I became popular among my peers for my singing.” He also learnt to play the guitar during services and later introduced beat-boxing – locally called “based box” – which helped him stand out.

nnnn

His first major release, the love-song NgaPhandle Kwakho, arrived in 2022 under the production of Candisonic, followed by Hita Humelela in 2023.

nnnn

In 2024, a collaboration with Phalaborwa star Mthimbani on Mhani wa mina earned critical praise and a nomination for Best Emerging Artist at the Munghana Lonene Music Awards, a regional honour recognising Limpopo talent.

nnnn

Beyond the studio, Pholoso has ventured into literature and entrepreneurship. In 2023 he co-authored the Tsonga book Gingirikani with Precious Mhlava and later published Words Can Change Your Life, a motivational work aimed at inspiring young readers.

nnnn

That same year he launched the clothing label “Make Everything Possible” (MEP), a brand created to embody resilience and ambition. “I started with nothing but had a dream. It’s now a source of inspiration for many young people, especially in my village of Saselani,” he said.

nnnn

When asked about his drive, Pholoso summed it up simply: “I believe in the power of working hard and chasing dreams in the music industry. If you’re willing to put in the hours, the doors start opening.”

nnnn

Balancing music, writing and his fashion line, he lives by a mantra of hard work, humility and perseverance. His story is already serving as a blueprint for aspiring artists and entrepreneurs in rural South Africa, proving that cultural roots can translate into national influence.

nnnn

As he continues to produce, publish and promote, Pholoso Musician remains committed to uplifting Tsonga culture – one beat at a time.

According to authorities, officers were called to the scene at around 20:55, where they found a 19-year-old woman suffering from a gunshot wound. She was still alive when police arrived and was rushed to a nearby hospital for urgent medical care.

post_title: Mpumalanga Battles Rising HIV and Malaria Cases
post_content:
n

Mpumalanga continues to rank among the provinces with high HIV and AIDS infections, despite ongoing efforts to curb the epidemic. Government health facilities offer a range of free integrated services, including on-site HIV testing, TB and STI screening, cervical cancer screening, and assessments for non-communicable diseases.

nnnn

Globally, an estimated 31.6 million people are currently receiving treatment, with 1.3 million new infections reported — a sign of steady progress. However, South Africa recorded approximately 8.1 million new HIV infections in 2024, highlighting the urgent need for stronger prevention initiatives and sustained community education.

nnnn

Meanwhile, four Mpumalanga municipalities — the City of Mbombela, Nkomazi, Bushbuckridge and Thaba Chweu — have reported a surge in malaria cases. More than 619 infections and at least five deaths were recorded between April and November this year.

nnnn

As part of SADC Malaria Day activities, the Department of Health visited Matsulu to raise awareness, particularly ahead of the festive season when travel to high-risk areas increases. Officials urged travellers to obtain prophylaxis treatment before visiting malaria-endemic regions and to complete the full course as prescribed.

nnnn

Health experts further stressed the importance of recognising malaria symptoms early. These include fever, headaches, muscle pain, extreme tiredness, nausea and diarrhoea. If untreated, malaria can quickly progress to severe illness, leading to loss of consciousness and organ failure, requiring urgent hospital care.

nnnn

Authorities continue to call for vigilance, early testing and consistent treatment to reduce infections and protect communities across the province.

Hazyview Primary School, together with Panda Pre-School and Hazy Runners, has extended heartfelt gratitude to all sponsors, stakeholders and supporters who contributed to the recent Fun Run/Walk for Bongeka, held on 29 November 2025 at the Hazyview Primary School grounds.

nnnn

The event was organised to assist nine-year-old Bongeka Mavimbela, a brave Grade 3 learner living with liver cirrhosis, a congenital condition that has required numerous surgeries and continuous medical care. Despite the challenges, Bongeka remains a symbol of courage and resilience.

nnnn

According to a letter issued on 03 December 2025, the organisers thanked the community for the financial support, in-kind donations and voluntary help that made the fundraiser a success. They expressed that the contributions provided essential relief for Bongeka’s ongoing treatment, oxygen therapy and home-care needs.

nnnn

The school highlighted how the event brought families, learners and residents together in the true spirit of Ubuntu, offering hope and unity during a very challenging time for the Mavimbela family.

nnnn

Organisers further noted that they will share the final financial outcome of the fundraiser once all accounts have been consolidated.

nnnn

The community’s collective kindness continues to offer comfort to Bongeka’s family and stands as a reminder of the impact of working together for a meaningful cause.

The Mpumalanga Department of Agriculture, Rural Development, Land and Environmental Affairs has issued a warning to service providers about a scammer posing as an official to solicit bribes.

nnnn

According to the Department, several businesses have reported receiving phone calls or SMSes from an unidentified individual claiming to represent the Department and promising guaranteed tenders in exchange for upfront payments. Officials emphasise that this is fraudulent behaviour and must be reported immediately.

nnnn

The Department stated that its employees are not permitted to request money from bidders at any stage of the procurement process. Service providers are urged to remain vigilant and to report any suspicious communication to their nearest police station.

nnnn

The Department also encouraged the public to use official channels for any enquiries to avoid falling victim to fraudulent schemes.

The Mpumalanga Department of Community Safety, Security and Liaison has intensified law-enforcement operations as festive-season traffic increases across the province. On Thursday, 4 December, MEC Thulasizwe Thomo joined the Department’s Transport Inspectorate Unit during a high-visibility operation along the N4 in Mbombela.

nnnnnnnn

The campaign aims to ensure that all motorists, holidaymakers and public-transport passengers travel in roadworthy and safe vehicles during one of the busiest periods of the year. Officers inspected vehicles, monitored traffic flow and engaged with drivers on compliance and safer-driving practices.

nnnn

MEC Thomo emphasised that the province will maintain strong visibility on major routes throughout December. He noted that the safety of road users remains the Department’s priority, particularly as traffic volumes rise and long-distance travel becomes more frequent.

nnnn

These operations form part of a broader festive-season safety strategy focusing on reducing crashes, enforcing compliance and promoting responsible behaviour on the roads. Community members are encouraged to cooperate with officers and to report unsafe or unroadworthy vehicles.

post_title: Mpumalanga Marks World AIDS Day in Nkomazi
post_content:
n

Mpumalanga has commemorated World AIDS Day with a provincial gathering held at Kamhlushwa Stadium in the Nkomazi Local Municipality. The event brought together government leaders, traditional authorities and civil-society representatives to reaffirm the province’s commitment to fighting HIV, stigma and gender-based violence.

nnnn

The day opened with a symbolic gesture as Inkosi Shongwe was presented with two cattle during a gifting ceremony. This act, organisers said, reflected appreciation for traditional leadership in strengthening community health initiatives.

nnnn

Premier Mandla Ndlovu led the proceedings, accompanied by Health MEC Sasekani Manzini, Members of the Executive Council, Deputy Director-General Peter Nyoni from the Office of the Premier, Executive Mayors, Councillors, Traditional Leaders and members of the Mpumalanga Provincial AIDS Council (MPAC).

nnnnnnnn

A representative of people living with HIV delivered a strong message condemning ongoing Gender-Based Violence and Femicide (GBVF), urging men to stop harming young women and girls by infecting them with HIV. The speaker called for accountability, compassion and safer behaviour within communities.

nnnn

Premier Ndlovu appealed for unity and understanding, emphasising that people living with HIV should never face discrimination. He encouraged communities to foster acceptance, support and mutual respect.

nnnn

The commemoration reinforced the province’s commitment to reducing new infections, strengthening prevention programmes and ensuring dignity for all affected individuals.

n

post_title: ROAD CRASH ON N12 CLAIMS SEVEN LIVES
post_content:
n

A tragic road crash on the N12 between Ogies and Emalahleni claimed seven lives on Monday morning, 8 December 2025.

nnnn

The collision occurred when one of the vehicles — a sedan — is believed to have lost control, veering off its roadway and crossing into the opposite direction before crashing into an oncoming light delivery vehicle (LDV). The road layout includes a wide separation between the two opposing carriageways, suggesting that excessive speed may have contributed to the incident.

nnnn

All five occupants of the sedan, comprising two women and three men, died on the scene. The two occupants of the LDV, both men, also died instantly. There were no survivors.

nnnn

An investigation involving the South African Police Service, the Road Traffic Management Corporation, and the Department of Community Safety, Security and Liaison is underway. Authorities have indicated that reckless or negligent driving cannot be ruled out at this stage.

nnnn

Mpumalanga MEC for Community Safety, Security and Liaison, Mr Jackie Macie, called on all motorists to exercise extreme caution on the province’s roads.

nnnn

“Let us all be cautious on the road to curb needless loss of life and injury,” said Macie. “We must all endeavour to abide by the rules of the road at all times.”

n

post_title: Kruger National Park Confirms Festive Season Readiness
post_content:
n

The Kruger National Park (KNP) has declared itself fully prepared to welcome both day visitors and overnight guests for the upcoming festive season. General Manager Reynold Thakhuli said the park is entering the holiday period with strengthened resources, improved visitor services and enhanced safety measures.

nnnn

Thakhuli revealed that the park recently received a new fleet of vehicles, including specialised trails vehicles designed for extended guided experiences. “This is the first time that we have vehicles like this, especially trails that run over a week,” he said, noting that the additions will significantly improve the tourist experience.

nnnn

Visitor safety remains a central focus of the park’s festive readiness plan. Thakhuli confirmed that advanced technology will be deployed inside the park to ensure that all guests are protected during their stay. Alongside the technological upgrades, law enforcement teams will be operating around the clock.

nnnn

“We have got technology that we are going to be utilising within the park to ensure that our visitors’ safety is secured. We will be working 24/7 in terms of our law enforcement,” he explained.

nnnnnnnn

He also issued a firm warning to anyone considering entering the park with malicious intent. “We are sending a caution to those who will be coming to the park with malicious intent that we will be ready for them,” he said.

nnnn

However, his message to tourists was warm and encouraging. Thakhuli urged families, holidaymakers and nature lovers to visit the world-renowned park in large numbers. “Please come in numbers, come and enjoy the facilities that we have to offer,” he said. He reminded day visitors to book in advance and to enjoy the park responsibly.

nnnn

Last year, KNP recorded just under 28,000 visitors during the festive period. With upgraded vehicles, reinforced safety systems and the park’s long-standing commitment to conservation, management is confident that this year’s holiday season will be even better for guests and the park alike.

post_title: Foreign National Arrested with Dagga Haul
post_content:
n

The South African Police Service in Mpumalanga has arrested a 36-year-old man from the Kingdom of Eswatini after 30 kilograms of dagga, valued at around R90 000, were discovered in his vehicle during a festive-season safety operation.

nnnn

The arrest took place on Sunday, 7 December, along the N17 Oshoek road between Ermelo and Chrissiesmeer. Officers stopped and searched a vehicle during an Operation Safer Festive Season patrol, uncovering multiple packages of dagga concealed inside.

nnnnnnnn

The suspect, identified as Sabelo Terrence Ndzabukelwako, was taken into custody and charged with possession of dagga. He appeared in the Ermelo Magistrate’s Court on Monday, 8 December, where he was granted bail of R2 000. His next court appearance is scheduled for 25 February 2026.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, said 

nnnn

“We are pleased with the success of this operation and the efforts of our members in preventing and combating crime. We urge communities to report information on drug dealing or any criminal activities so that together we can build a safer environment, especially during the festive season,” he said.

n

post_title: Granny Among Five Arrested for Selling Rotten Food
post_content:
n

A 75-year-old woman has become the latest family member to be implicated in an alleged scheme involving the repackaging and sale of expired and rotten food to unsuspecting consumers in the Secunda area.

nnnn

Wilhemina Jacoba (75) and Phakamani Hlongwane (36) handed themselves over to the Hawks’ Serious Organised Crime Investigation team in Secunda after being linked to the already-arrested trio – Pieter Grobler (31), Mark Lombard (29) and Sonnet Lombard (46).

nnnn

Jacoba and Hlongwane briefly appeared before the Secunda Magistrate’s Court on Monday, 8 December 2025. Both were released on R2 500 bail and are expected to return to court on 6 February 2026.

nnnn

The arrests stem from a tip-off received by the Hawks regarding illicit activities taking place on a farm in Charl Cilliers, just outside Secunda. During Grobler’s arrest, investigators seized several items, including vehicles and cool rooms allegedly used in the illegal operation.

nnnn

Authorities confirmed that a large quantity of expired and rotten food, deemed unfit for human consumption, was disposed of during the operation.

nnnn

All five accused face charges relating to the contravention of the Foodstuffs, Cosmetics and Disinfectants Act, as well as corruption, fraud and money laundering.

nnnn

Mpumalanga’s Provincial Head of the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation, Major General Nico Gerber, condemned the acts as “inhumane” and vowed that the investigation would continue until every person linked to the scheme is held accountable.

n

post_title: New Kruger Upgrades Ready For Festive Tourism Rush
post_content:
n

Kruger National Park is gearing up for one of its busiest festive seasons yet, with sweeping upgrades to its accommodation, a stronger tourism offering, and a renewed drive to enforce visitor safety. Speaking during a media engagement at Skukuza on Monday, Commercial Manager Thabo Tlalanyane detailed how these improvements are positioning the park for continued post-COVID recovery.

nnnn

Tlalanyane confirmed that SANParks is currently rolling out 86 newly designed bungalows as part of phase four of its large-scale redevelopment plan. Many older units, he explained, had deteriorated over time, prompting management to prioritise a refreshed, modern guest experience.

nnnn

“We used to have challenges of old bungalows being dilapidated… and management saw it fit that we actually get to introduce the new designs. We’re currently rolling out phase four, where we are working on 86 new developments,” he said.

nnnn

Festive rush expected

nnnn

Kruger anticipates a sharp increase in visitors from mid-December, with accommodation capacity expected to reach up to 8,400 guests per day. Average stays range from three to ten nights, with some holidaymakers spending as long as a month in the park.

nnnn

Local tourists remain the backbone of Kruger’s business. In 2024, 71.4% of visitors were South Africans, with more than 1.3 million domestic entries recorded. Tlalanyane noted that this surge in local travel has played a crucial role in stabilising the park’s finances after the pandemic and lockdown disruptions.

nnnn

Safety and rule enforcement under scrutiny

nnnn

With the festive influx approaching, SANParks is increasing enforcement of key park rules, particularly around speeding, drone usage and unsafe behaviour at wildlife sightings.

nnnn

Speeding remains one of the most common violations — often by drivers rushing to sightings — resulting in road kills and significant safety hazards.

nnnn

“We have issues of people speeding when they come into the park… you get road kills. Sometimes they knock off our animals,” Tlalanyane said.

nnnn

He also warned that drones are strictly prohibited, noting that several recent incidents have been escalated to management. While SANParks awaits air-rights approval for ranger-led drone patrols, visitors remain banned from flying drones in or over the park.

nnnn

Management is further clamping down on overcrowding at sightings, children leaning out of windows, and blocking view sites — behaviour that compromises both visitor experience and safety.

nnnnnnnn

Economic benefits through events and partnerships

nnnn

Tlalanyane commended government support in upgrading infrastructure and encouraged both public and private organisations to host more conferences inside the park. Kruger’s conference centre can host up to 500 delegates and includes four breakaway rooms.

nnnn

“This is a product for all South Africans and all Africans as a whole,” he said, urging broader use of the park’s facilities.

nnnn

Recent high-profile events — including hosting key G20 meetings — have significantly boosted occupancy and revenue, contributing to what SANParks describes as one of its strongest financial years in recent times.

nnnn

Kruger National Park enters the festive season with renewed confidence, improved facilities, and a firm focus on safety — ready to welcome thousands of visitors to one of Africa’s most cherished destinations.

n

n

The Kruger National Park has launched a new three-bin waste system as thousands of holidaymakers prepare to stream into the park this festive season. The initiative, unveiled on Tuesday 9 December 2025, is a collaboration between Petco, the Kruger National Park Honorary Rangers amongst others and aims to boost recycling efforts while protecting the park’s fragile environment.

nnnn

With more than 270,000 visitors expected, waste generation is a major concern. The new system—also known as the Green Crew—separates recyclables from food and organic waste, as well as general non-recyclable rubbish. According to the partners, simple changes like effective waste separation can dramatically improve recycling outcomes and keep valuable materials circulating in the economy.

nnnn

“Our mission has always been to keep valuable resources in the economy at their highest value for as long as possible, and to build a strong collection and recycling system in South Africa,” the partners explained. “Recyclables that remain clean can go straight back into the circular economy rather than ending up in landfills or being dumped into this beautiful environment.”

nnnnnnnn

Dr Danny Govender, General Manager for Sustainable Development and Management at KNP, said clean, uncontaminated recyclables hold far greater value. “We want to prevent them from being soiled with food waste and hygiene products,” she said. Dr Govender added that the park hopes the system will inspire visitors to adopt better waste practices at home.

nnnn

“Waste management is not just a protected area issue,” she emphasised. “It affects our communities and the places we live. Waste left behind impacts us all.”

nnnn

The Kruger National Park urges visitors to use the new bins correctly and play their part in keeping South Africa’s most iconic wilderness clean for generations to come.

post_title: Elderly Man Found Alive in Bushes
post_content:
n

A 92-year-old man from Masibekela, Mbuzini, has been found alive after spending two days missing in the dense bushes. Solomon Majomeya Sithole was discovered on Tuesday afternoon following an intensive joint search by police, family members and the local community.

nnnn

According to police, Sithole was reported missing on Monday morning, prompting an immediate search that continued until nightfall. The operation resumed the next day with the support of the Mpumalanga Police Search and Rescue Team, Crime Intelligence, and a drone operated by a Tonga SAPS member.

nnnn

Despite hours of searching on Tuesday, there was still no sign of the elderly man until a police helicopter was deployed around 14:20. The Air Wing team eventually spotted him lying under a tree deep in the bush. He was airlifted to the nearest hospital for medical care.

nnnn
