post_title: Schools Told Not to Withhold Report Cards
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga Department of Education has issued a firm reminder to all schools that learner report cards may not be withheld under any circumstances. This directive applies to both public and independent schools, in line with Section 29(12) of the National Protocol on Assessment (Grades R–12).

nnnn

According to the Department, a report card is an essential document that provides parents and guardians with a full picture of a learner’s academic performance. It offers detailed feedback across subjects, highlighting achievements as well as areas that require improvement. Schools are therefore urged to ensure that parents receive these documents promptly at the end of each term.

nnnn

Parents have been encouraged to report any school that refuses to release a report card to the nearest circuit office. The Department also reminded schools to use proper administrative processes when dealing with parental obligations, without disadvantaging learners or restricting their access to academic records.

nnnn

MEC for Education, Ms Lindi Masina, emphasised the importance of accuracy and transparency in the issuing of report cards. “Parents have the right to receive a full and accurate account of their children’s performance throughout the year. We therefore urge all schools to refrain from withholding learner report cards for any reason,” she said.

nnnn

The Department also congratulated learners for reaching the end of the academic year. Those who did not pass are encouraged to remain positive, with the reminder that support is available and that setbacks can lead to new opportunities.

nnnn

Parents were urged to foster a calm and supportive home environment as learners receive their results. Schools across the province will reopen on Wednesday, 14 January 2026.

nnnn

The Department wished all learners, parents, and teachers a safe and restful holiday.

n

n

South African author and literary advocate Nomawele Njongo never imagined that writing her deeply personal book, Abortion by the Womb of Democracy, would ignite a movement stretching across more than 30 African countries. But that is exactly what happened. When her sons, Kwazi and Thina, began writing their own books in 2020, she realised something powerful: teenagers are more than enthusiastic readers — they are gifted storytellers with voices that deserve to be heard.

nnnn

This awakening led to the birth of KwaziThina Publishers, named after her sons, followed by the Africa Teen Authors Book Initiative (ATABI). Today, ATABI is a thriving pan-African platform nurturing young writers across the continent and the diaspora. “From my sons’ notebooks, we built a literary movement,” says Njongo. “Teenagers carry stories the world needs to hear.”

nnnn

Njongo’s impact has earned her significant national recognition. She is a Voice of Heritage Award winner from the National Heritage Council of South Africa and a Brand South Africa Play Your Part Ambassador, celebrated for flying the national flag and championing active citizenship. She was also a finalist in the 40 Under 40 South Africa Awards in the Community Development category — a clear acknowledgment that empowering young storytellers is nation-building work.

nnnn

Representing South Africa in Moscow

nnnn

Njongo is currently in Moscow, Russia, where she is proudly representing South Africa as one of only 13 authors chosen by the Department of Sport, Arts and Culture to participate in the Moscow International Book Fair. “This endorsement is a tremendous honour,” she says. “It affirmed that stories written by and for young adults belong on the global stage.”

nnnn

At the Fair, Njongo served as a panelist alongside fellow South African writer Anzil Kulsen in a discussion facilitated by Khathu Maestro Ndou. Their conversation explored what defines South African young adult literature, how to inspire new teenage writers, and the importance of African storytelling. At the heart of her message was her defining slogan — “Let Africa Tell Her Stories.” Authenticity, she stressed, is essential in shaping the continent’s narrative.

nnnn

Global Connections and New Inspiration

nnnn

Njongo says the reception from Russian readers and publishers was overwhelmingly encouraging. South African books drew strong interest, and many titles from the national delegation were purchased. She was also impressed by the high standard of Russian book production. “The quality of writing and illustration stood tall among the international offerings,” she notes. Her visit to the Russian State Library was another highlight — an experience she describes as unforgettable and rich with lessons for the South African publishing space.

nnnn

Although there are no formal expansion plans into Eastern Europe yet, Njongo believes the seeds of collaboration are already planted. ATABI previously had a participant living in Moscow, a connection that made this year’s visit feel perfectly aligned. “Sharing our publishing model here has opened doors for future opportunities,” she says.

nnnn

Njongo’s international momentum continues back home. On 13 December, she will serve as the main speaker at the Africa Rising Youth International Summit at Wits University, presenting on Creative Capital: Unlocking the Economic Power of Africa’s Storytellers and Artists. Sharing a platform with leaders such as Dr. Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma marks an important step in positioning storytelling as a key economic driver.

nnnn

From a single book written in her home to a movement empowering young writers across the continent, Nomawele Njongo’s journey is a testament to the transformative power of stories — and the African youth who are rising to tell them.

nnnn

post_title: Farmers Market Ignites Local Agriculture Growth
post_content:
n

Bushbuckridge made a bold statement for local agriculture this past Saturday, 6 December, when the Bushbuckridge Farmers Association hosted a vibrant farmers market that drew growers and agri-entrepreneurs from across the region and beyond. What was intended as a simple platform for farmers to showcase their products quickly became a powerful symbol of unity, innovation and economic revival.

nnnn

Pollen Mokgope, communication officer of Bushbuckridge Farmers Association said the market was created to give farmers—both emerging and experienced—a space to exhibit fresh produce, livestock, handmade goods and value-added products that demonstrate the true potential of local agribusiness. Farmers travelled from as far as Lydenburg, Ga-Phahla and Venda to participate, many choosing to officially join the Association after witnessing the energy and opportunity the market created.

nnnn

“This event has expanded our farmer network in a remarkable way,” Pollen said. “It will inspire more farmers to value-add, package better and think bigger about their products.”

nnnn

But the celebration also highlighted the serious challenges faced by local farmers daily. Among the most pressing issues are limited expertise, lack of funding, inadequate access to markets and heavy losses caused by poor storage or handling. The Association is actively responding to these gaps by hosting monthly training sessions on critical topics such as irrigation, animal health, plant diseases, water management, tax compliance and fire management. They also provide access to expert farmers, promote farmer-to-farmer trading and regularly circulate funding opportunities.

nnnnnnnn

In a community where agriculture is a pathway to economic stability, the Association is proud that women and youth make up the majority of its membership. The market brought additional economic activity to Bushbuckridge, with local service providers—such as photographers and vendors—gaining business and exposure. Some food-sector businesses who attended the event have already committed to sourcing their produce from local farmers they met on the day, signalling long-term opportunities.

nnnn

Pollen urged the Bushbuckridge community to continue supporting farmers directly:

nnnn

“Buying at the farm gate is cheaper than supermarkets and keeps money circulating locally. It improves livelihoods and strengthens our economy.”

nnnn

With the Association registered as a legal NPO, Pollen called on stakeholders, funders and local businesses to partner with them professionally. The organisation is actively seeking sponsorships to scale its impact and improve farming operations for its members.

nnnn

Saturday’s farmers market was more than an event—it was a bold showcase of what Bushbuckridge farmers can achieve when given the platform, support and recognition they deserve.

n

post_title: Vikings Crowned Champions at Mandela Cup Challenge
post_content:
n

The Nelson Mandela Cup Challenge kicked off in style at Mariti Shatleng Sports Ground from 6–7 December, hosted by the Bushbuckridge Local Municipality Chief Whip, Bhunu Malandula.

nnnn

The tournament saw some thrilling encounters, including a much-anticipated clash between Mkhuhlu Masters and Hoxani Masters. Fans were treated to an entertaining display of skill, with halftime featuring lively music and dancing that kept the crowd buzzing.

nnnn

In another closely contested match, Rangers went down 1–0 to Vikings. Despite the narrow defeat, Rangers’ defensive prowess was on full display, impressing spectators with their organisation and resilience.

nnnnnnnn

Ultimately, it was Vikings F.C. who lifted the Mandela Cup Challenge trophy, showcasing consistent performance and determination throughout the tournament. Their victory marks them as the champions of this year’s exciting local football showdown.

nnnn

The Mandela Cup Challenge not only celebrated football talent in the region but also brought the community together through sport, music, and entertainment.

A 43-year-old Zimbabwean national has been arrested after police discovered hundreds of passports and a large amount of cash hidden inside his vehicle. The multidisciplinary team — consisting of the Middelburg Flying Squad, Nkangala District Anti-Hijacking Team and Waterval Boven SAPS — intercepted a white Chevrolet Utility bakkie with Gauteng registration plates on 8 December 2025 at around 1pm.

nnnn

A search of the vehicle uncovered 582 passports, some containing cash hidden between the pages, and an additional R20 000 wrapped in a plastic bag. In total, officers recovered R147 300. The passports were concealed in an under-compartment of the bakkie.

nnnnnnnn

Early investigations suggest the driver may have been on his way to meet someone to have the passports fraudulently stamped, with the cash believed to be intended as payment.

nnnn

The suspect, identified as Mr Edward Chitaizvi, has been charged with contravening the Immigration Act, fraud, and money laundering. The bakkie has also been seized for further investigation.

nnnn

Chitaizvi remains in custody while authorities verify his residential address. He is expected to appear in the Belfast Magistrate’s Court on Monday, 15 December 2025.

post_title: KNP Beef Up Security for Festive Rush
post_content:
n

The Kruger National Park (KNP) is tightening its grip on both wildlife crime and festive-season lawlessness through an expanded anti-poaching dog unit and intensified security operations at key access points.

nnnn

In a significant milestone for conservation, the park has increased its K9 Counter-Poaching Unit to 53 highly trained dogs. According to KNP GM Rey Thakuli, the expansion follows the dogs’ remarkable track record in helping rangers track, corner, and apprehend poachers inside the park. “We have had a lot of success, and these dogs have caught several poachers in action. Their presence is a substantial return on our investment and plays a huge role in conservation,” he said.

nnnn

The specialised unit operates on a two-tiered system. Hound dogs, working in packs, track scent trails over long distances without engaging suspects. Attack and biting dogs are deployed when dealing with armed or aggressive poachers, trained to detect firearms, rhino horns, bushmeat, and other illegal items. With each dog costing a minimum of R100 000 to train, SANParks says the investment reflects its long-term commitment to protecting endangered wildlife. Handlers, who are equally well trained, play a crucial role in ensuring the animals’ performance and safety in challenging environments.

nnnn

At the same time, KNP is preparing for an influx of more than 270 000 visitors over the festive season. On Tuesday, the park conducted a wide-scale stop-and-search operation at major entry points, led by SANParks Protection Services in partnership with SAPS, SANDF, the Border Management Authority, and other agencies. Detector dogs searched vehicles for weapons, contraband, and wildlife products.

nnnn

Protection Services Manager Phindile Makhubela said well-coordinated daily operations are central to keeping visitors safe. “People take chances — from smuggling alcohol and game meat to stolen vehicles. This season alone, we have recovered two stolen vehicles trying to cross into Mozambique through the park,” she said.

nnnn

Thakuli issued a stern warning to criminals: “If anyone wants to take chances, they may spend Christmas in jail.”

nnnn

Authorities say similar operations will continue throughout December to safeguard both visitors and wildlife.

n

post_title: NGB Warns Against Illegal Online Gambling
post_content:
n

As South Africans gear up for the festive season, the National Gambling Board (NGB) has issued a strong warning about the rise in illegal online gambling platforms. The board urges consumers to gamble responsibly and seek help early if they notice signs of problem gambling.

nnnn

Illegal online gambling, including offshore websites and unlicensed betting apps, remains a serious risk. Such platforms often target players via social media, WhatsApp, SMS, or influencer marketing, appearing legitimate while offering no legal protection. Participating can result in criminal charges, fines, or forfeited winnings. Only operators displaying a valid provincial licence are authorised to provide gambling services in South Africa.

nnnn

Acting NGB CEO Lungile Dukwana stressed that the festive season can increase financial and emotional pressures, potentially driving risky gambling behaviour. “Problem gambling can affect anyone, regardless of age or income. Early intervention is crucial to prevent financial loss, broken relationships, or mental-health issues,” he said.

nnnn

Warning signs of gambling problems include spending more time and money than intended, chasing losses, borrowing money, neglecting responsibilities, or using gambling as an escape from stress. The NGB advises families and communities to remain vigilant.

nnnn

For those who choose to gamble, the NGB recommends treating it as entertainment, setting strict budgets, avoiding gambling under stress or influence, and sticking to licensed operators. The South Africa Responsible Gambling Foundation (SARGF) provides free confidential support at 0800 006 008 or via WhatsApp/SMS at 076 675 0710.

nnnn

Consumers are also encouraged to report illegal gambling websites by contacting the NGB at 010 003 3475 or info@ngb.org.za. With public awareness and regulatory oversight, South Africans can enjoy a safer festive season.

n

n

Quality assurance body Umalusi has confirmed that it is closely monitoring the reported irregularities involving the National Senior Certificate (NSC) Mathematics, Physical Sciences and English Home Language examinations. The matter was first raised publicly during a media briefing by the Minister of Basic Education, Ms Siviwe Gwarube, on Thursday.

nnnn

According to Umalusi, the Department of Basic Education (DBE) submitted a preliminary report on Wednesday, 10 December. After reviewing the document, the council said it is satisfied with the actions taken so far, including the DBE’s decision to report the matter to the South African Police Service (SAPS). Umalusi also welcomed the ongoing investigations aimed at determining the scale of the irregularities.

nnnn

The DBE will present the full findings to Umalusi’s Executive Committee during its results-approval meetings scheduled for 6–8 January 2026.

nnnn

To safeguard the integrity and independence of the investigation processes, Umalusi announced it will not engage further with the media on this matter until 9 January 2026. On that date, the council will issue a formal statement on the conduct and management of the 2025 end-of-year examinations.

nnnn

Umalusi assured the Class of 2025, their families, and higher-education institutions that the investigation will not delay the release of results for learners who are not implicated in the irregularities.

n

n

Tensions within the tripartite alliance have sharpened after ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula delivered a firm warning about the implications of the South African Communist Party’s (SACP) decision to contest next year’s municipal elections independently.

nnnn

Speaking during the ANC’s National General Council (NGC) in Boksburg, Mbalula described the SACP’s move as “erratic and dangerous”, arguing that it threatens the very foundations of the National Democratic Revolution (NDR), which he insists is led by the ANC. He stressed that an independent electoral path for the SACP could undermine the ideological unity that has traditionally held the alliance together.

nnnn

Mbalula revealed that the ANC had attempted to persuade the SACP to reconsider its stance but admitted the efforts were unsuccessful. “We have failed to persuade them otherwise. They are steadfast in that decision,” he said. He added that the ANC’s National Executive Committee would now have to examine the practical consequences, particularly the issue of dual membership, which may require Communist Party members to choose between the two organisations.

nnnn

He further emphasised the need for an urgent alliance summit to address the growing rift, noting that the SACP’s leadership struggled to explain the rationale behind standing alone when delivering their message of support at the NGC plenary.

nnnn

While Mbalula underscored the ANC’s leadership of the NDR, political analysts say the tensions signal deeper ideological disputes that have resurfaced within the alliance. The renewed debate has placed additional focus on the historical roots and ownership of the NDR, which has guided alliance policy for decades.

nnnn

post_title: Knock-Out Stage Set for U19 Cup
post_content:

Organisers have encouraged the public to come out in full support, adding that the energy from local fans continues to uplift and motivate the young players. Special thanks have been extended to partners, donors, coaches and volunteers for their commitment to the tournament’s success.

Happy Boys to Semi-Finals

nnnn

Mpumalanga ABC Motsepe League defender Harry Ndlovu was the hero of the day on 9 December, sending Tlhavekisa Happy Boys FC into the semi-finals after saving two penalties in a thrilling James Mayinga U19 Tournament fixture.

nnnn

nnnn

Happy Boys, the defending champions, overcame Welverdiend’s Wonderous FC in dramatic fashion. post_title: Road Users Urged to Drive Safely
post_content:
n

As the school year ends and thousands prepare to travel for holidays, weddings and family events, motorists are being urged to adjust their driving to the prevailing weather and increased traffic volumes. Heavy movement between provinces and neighbouring SADC countries is expected from Friday, 12 December, with peak periods predicted for 19 December and 26 December as Christmas and New-Year travel intensifies.

nnnn

Mpumalanga MEC for Community Safety, Security and Liaison, Jackie Macie, has appealed to all motorists to help prevent further loss of life on the province’s roads. He reminded communities that too many families have suffered heartbreak due to festive-season crashes.

nnnn

Macie stressed the importance of ensuring vehicles are roadworthy before embarking on long trips. “Vehicle owners must ensure their vehicles are roadworthy and all defects are corrected before travelling,” he said. He further called on drivers to obey road rules, avoid alcohol, and adjust to wet and unpredictable weather conditions.

nnnn

This weekend will see intensified traffic-law enforcement across Mpumalanga, with joint operations by the provincial government, municipalities and the police. Road Safety Education teams will be out conducting awareness sessions for drivers, passengers and pedestrians. Law enforcers will take a zero-tolerance stance on drunk driving, speeding, overloading and unroadworthy vehicles. Vehicles found without number plates will be impounded on the spot.

nnnn

Macie said he is confident that the measures in place will contribute to safer roads. “With increased cooperation and compliance by all road users, many lives can be saved,” he emphasised.

post_title: Repeat Poacher Jailed for Ten Years
post_content:
n

A Mozambican repeat offender has been sentenced to 10 years in prison after pleading guilty to several rhino poaching-related offences in the Kruger National Park.

nnnn

A 31-year-old man, Faro Zitha, was handed the sentence by the Skukuza Regional Court following his arrest in June this year. Field rangers patrolling the Houtboschrand section of the park encountered Zitha and a group of accomplices carrying a hunting rifle and an axe. While the others escaped, Zitha was apprehended and later denied bail.

nnnn

He faced seven charges, including trespassing, immigration violations, possession of a firearm with an obliterated serial number, possession of ammunition, possession of a dangerous weapon, and conspiracy to commit an offence. He pleaded guilty to all counts and was convicted accordingly.

nnnn

Zitha faced the following sentences for each of the seven charges:

nnnn
    n
  • Trespassing: 2 years’ imprisonment
    • nnnn
  • Contravention of the Immigration Act: 1 year
    • nnnn
  • Possession of a firearm to commit an offence: 4 years
    • nnnn
  • Possession of a firearm with an obliterated serial number: 8 years
    • nnnn
  • Possession of ammunition: 2 years
    • nnnn
  • Conspiracy to commit an offence: 4 years
    • nnnn
  • Possession of a dangerous weapon: 1 year
    • n
nnnn

Although these sentences amount to a combined total of 22 years, the court ordered some of them to run concurrently, leaving Zitha with an effective 10-year direct imprisonment sentence.

nnnn

During sentencing, the State highlighted that Zitha is a repeat offender with a previous conviction for trespassing in the Kruger National Park, for which he served three years. The court imposed several sentences ranging from one to eight years, some of which will run concurrently, resulting in an effective 10-year term. He was also declared unfit to possess a firearm.

nnnn

The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) welcomed the outcome, saying the conviction demonstrates its continued commitment to holding poachers accountable and protecting South Africa’s wildlife heritage.

nnnn

post_title: Skukuza Poacher Jailed for Sixteen Years
post_content:
n

A 28-year-old man involved in the killing of two rhinos in the Kruger National Park has been sentenced to 16 years’ direct imprisonment after being found guilty on numerous poaching-related charges.

nnnn

The Skukuza Regional Court on 11 December 2025 handed down the sentence to Bethuel Baloyi, who committed the offences in 2020. Baloyi was convicted on multiple counts, including trespassing, killing two rhinos, possession of a firearm, possession of a firearm with an obliterated serial number, possession of a firearm to commit an offence, possession of live ammunition, conspiracy to commit an offence, and possession of a dangerous weapon.

nnnn

The case stems from an incident on 28 March 2020, when rangers patrolling the Pretoriuskop Section encountered three armed suspects: Million Masilane, Bethuel Baloyi and Mozambican national Andries Baloyi. During an attempted arrest, Andries allegedly pointed a firearm at the rangers, who returned fire, resulting in his death.

nnnn

The remaining suspects were arrested and found with a firearm bearing an obliterated serial number and live ammunition. A further search led to the discovery of two rhino carcasses. Although Baloyi and Masilane pleaded not guilty and were initially granted bail, the State presented compelling evidence, including ranger testimony and expert reports confirming that bloodstains on Baloyi’s clothing matched rhino blood.

nnnn

In 2023, co-accused Masilane was convicted and sentenced to 16 years. Baloyi absconded after the matter was postponed for judgment, prompting a separation of trials. He was later re-arrested in the Hluhluwe Game Reserve in KwaZulu-Natal for a similar offence, which remains pending.

nnnn

The court imposed the following sentences:

nnnn

• 2 years – Trespassing

nnnn

• 10 years – Killing two rhinos

nnnn

• 5 years – Possession of a firearm

nnnn

• 6 years – Possession of a firearm with an obliterated serial number

nnnn

• 5 years – Possession of a firearm to commit a crime

nnnn

• 2 years – Possession of live ammunition

nnnn

• 4 years – Conspiracy to commit an offence

nnnn

• 1 year – Possession of a dangerous weapon

nnnn

Some sentences will run concurrently, resulting in an effective 16-year term. Baloyi was also declared unfit to possess a firearm.

nnnn

The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) welcomed the outcome, reaffirming its commitment to accountability and the protection of South Africa’s endangered wildlife.

nnnn

post_title: Four Arrested Over Gold, Bribery Bid
post_content:
n

A routine patrol by a multidisciplinary law enforcement team has led to the arrest of four foreign nationals in Delmas after unwrought gold worth an estimated R800 000 was discovered during a stop-and-search operation.

nnnn

According to a media statement issued by the Office of the Provincial Commissioner in Mpumalanga, the incident occurred in the early hours of Saturday, 13 December 2025, along the N12 route near the Delmas off-ramp. Police officers on patrol noticed a white Toyota Fortuner travelling without registration plates on both sides and proceeded to stop the vehicle.

nnnn

Upon searching the vehicle, officers found unwrought gold, classified as a precious metal, hidden inside a white plastic bag. Three Mozambican nationals, aged between 24 and 34, were immediately arrested for possession of unwrought gold and for failing to produce valid documentation permitting them to be in the country.

nnnn

While police were processing the suspects at Delmas police station at around 02h00, a fourth suspect, a 27-year-old Zimbabwean national, allegedly attempted to bribe a police officer with R5 000 in exchange for the release of the three suspects, whom he identified as his brothers. He was arrested on the spot and charged with bribery.

nnnn

All four suspects are expected to appear before the Delmas Magistrate’s Court on 15 December 2025, where they will face charges related to possession of unwrought gold, contravention of immigration laws, and bribery.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner of the SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General Dr Zeph Mkhwanazi, reaffirmed that criminal activities would not be tolerated in the province and urged communities to work closely with police, especially during the festive season, to help create a safer environment for all.

post_title: He was found at the crime scene

post_content:
n

Police in Acornhoek have arrested a 26-year-old man in connection with a murder that took place at a tavern in Ka Zitha Trust over the weekend.

nnnn

The incident occurred in the early hours of Saturday, 13 December 2025, at around 06h00, within the Acornhoek policing precinct. Officers were alerted to a male victim who had been taken to hospital after sustaining a stab wound.

nnnn

Upon arrival at the hospital, police discovered that the victim had succumbed to his injuries. A case of murder was immediately opened, and investigations commenced without delay.

nnnn

While police were still gathering information and following up leads, a family member brought a suspect to the local police station. The suspect was subsequently arrested and formally charged with murder.

nnnn

At this stage, the motive for the killing remains unclear and will form part of the ongoing investigation. Police have indicated that further details may emerge as inquiries continue.

nnnn

The suspect is expected to appear before the Acornhoek Magistrate’s Court soon to face the charge.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of the South African Police Service in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, has praised the family members for their responsible action in bringing the suspect to the police. He reiterated the SAPS’s commitment to conducting a thorough investigation to uncover the full circumstances surrounding the incident and to ensure justice is served.

nnnn

Police have urged community members to continue working with law enforcement by reporting crime and providing information that may assist investigations.

post_title: Two Minors Arrested for Armed Robbery
post_content:
n

Police in Acornhoek have arrested two 16-year-old boys in connection with an armed robbery that took place in the Happy Dam area on 12 December 2025.

nnnn

 The incident involved a 43-year-old man who was driving a taxi to his home. Upon arriving and parking outside his yard, he was allegedly confronted by four armed males as he exited the vehicle. The suspects are said to have held him at gunpoint before robbing him of cash and disarming him of his licensed pistol.

nnnn

Following the incident, a case of armed robbery was opened and investigations were immediately launched. This led to the arrest of two suspects, both minors aged 16. Police confirmed that the suspects were also found in possession of a firearm.

nnnn

Given the age of the suspects, the South African Police Service is working closely with probation officers to ensure that all legal processes are handled in line with legislation governing children in conflict with the law.

nnnn

The two minors face serious charges, including armed robbery and possession of an unlicensed firearm. Their court appearance at the Acornhoek Magistrate’s Court will be facilitated in collaboration with probation officers.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of the SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, has assured the community that police are working tirelessly to apprehend the remaining two suspects linked to the crime.

nnnn

He further appealed to members of the public to assist law enforcement by reporting any information that could help bring those responsible to justice, stressing that community cooperation remains vital in the fight against crime.

Visitors and staff at the Kruger National Park’s (KNP) Phalaborwa Gate were not affected after a brief water disruption earlier this month, South African National Parks (SANParks) has confirmed.

nnnn

The interruption occurred on 10 December following a misunderstanding between SANParks and the Ba-Phalaborwa Municipality regarding an alleged R44 million in outstanding property rates. SANParks said it became aware of the claim after a debt collector, acting on behalf of the municipality, facilitated the temporary closure of the water supply to the Phalaborwa Gate.

nnnn

SANParks immediately engaged the Municipal Manager on the same day, resulting in an agreement to restore the water supply without delay. The supply was subsequently reinstated.

nnnn

Importantly, SANParks confirmed that throughout the period of the water closure, the park continued to supply water from its own reservoirs. As a result, no visitors or staff experienced any disruption to services.

nnnn

“A temporary water closure did not negatively affect operations, as the park had sufficient reserves in place,” SANParks said in a statement.

nnnn

To prevent similar incidents in the future, SANParks and the Ba-Phalaborwa Municipality are in the process of arranging a formal meeting to address the matter comprehensively. These discussions form part of broader engagements already planned with municipalities bordering the Limpopo section of the Kruger National Park in January 2026.

nnnn

The Kruger National Park spans approximately two million hectares and is bordered by seven municipalities — four in Limpopo and three in Mpumalanga. SANParks noted that it has already reached legally sound and cooperative agreements on the application of property rates with municipalities in Mpumalanga and is working towards achieving similar arrangements in Limpopo.

nnnn

Central to the discussions with Ba-Phalaborwa will be the methodology used to calculate the alleged R44 million debt. SANParks stated that it currently has no records confirming that this amount is legitimately owed and will seek full clarity on how the figure was determined, particularly within the context of legislation governing national parks.

nnnn

SANParks reiterated its commitment to cooperative governance, transparency, and maintaining uninterrupted service delivery to visitors, staff, and surrounding communities. While municipalities do provide certain essential services, the organisation emphasised that the Kruger National Park remains largely self-sufficient.

nnnn

The matter, SANParks said, will be addressed through constructive engagement to ensure long-term sustainability and collaboration.

post_title: Man Jailed For Life Over Girlfriend’s Murder
post_content:
n

A 38-year-old man has been sentenced to life imprisonment for the brutal murder of his girlfriend in Bushbuckridge.

nnnn

Mikah Shalamuka Willy Sithole, who was in a domestic relationship with Nicolene Morgan, was found guilty by the High Court of South Africa, Mpumalanga Division, following a harrowing sequence of events in December 2024.

nnnn

On 21 December 2024, Morgan and her sister attended a party at Cork Trust. Sithole, discovering they had been drinking, demanded Morgan accompany him home. When she refused, an altercation erupted, and he forcibly dragged her away, assaulting her along the way before heading to his own residence.

nnnn

Tragically, the following day Sithole drowned Morgan in a nearby dam. After realising she was still alive, he asked his brother-in-law to fetch help—but while he was away, Sithole strangled her to death and fled the scene. Police investigations led to his arrest days later.

nnnn

Despite pleading not guilty, Sithole was convicted on strong circumstantial evidence, including testimony from witnesses and a postmortem confirming asphyxia caused by external pressure to the neck. The court heard victim impact statements detailing the ongoing trauma endured by Morgan’s family.

nnnn

In handing down the sentence, the court cited the prevalence of domestic violence and femicide in South Africa, noting Sithole showed no remorse. The sentence of life imprisonment reflects the court’s stance that there were no compelling circumstances to mitigate the punishment.

nnnn

Morgan’s family has described the sentencing as a small measure of justice for the devastating loss they have suffered.

n

post_title: Police Hunt Suspects After Double Murder
post_content:
n

Police in Nelspruit have launched a manhunt following the discovery of two women’s bodies at a house in Kamagugu on Tuesday, 16 December.

nnnn

According to a police report, officers were alerted at about 16:30 after neighbours became concerned about a foul smell and an unusual number of flies around a locked house. Attempts to contact the occupants by phone were unsuccessful, prompting residents to call the police.

nnnn

On arrival, police found no visible signs of forced entry. Mbombela Disaster Management was called in to assist with unlocking the house. Once inside, officers discovered that the house appeared to have been ransacked.

nnnn

Two lifeless bodies were found inside the house. The first victim was identified by her family as Ms Eunice Mahlodi (64), whose body was found half naked. The second victim was identified as Ms Eugenia Dineo Masuku (20). Masuku’s body was discovered half naked in her bedroom, with both hands tied with cables. A cable was also found around her neck, leading police to suspect that she may have been strangled. Blood stains were observed in the bedroom.

nnnn

Emergency Services personnel who attended the scene certified both women dead. Police said the bodies were found in the early stages of decomposition. It is further suspected that items, including cellphones, may have been stolen from the house.

nnnn

A case of double murder has been opened, and a specialised investigation team has been established under the leadership of the Acting Provincial Commissioner of the SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi. A 72-hour plan involving all relevant role players has been activated to investigate the incident.

nnnn

Police are appealing to members of the public who may have information that could assist in the arrest of the suspect or suspects to contact Detective Sergeant Debra Matukane on 076 354 9612 or Crime Stop on 08600 10111. Information can also be shared via the MySAPS App. All information will be treated as confidential, and callers may remain anonymous.

nnnn

Major General Mkhwanazi said the assembled team is working around the clock to ensure that those responsible are brought to justice.

nnnn

The operation formed part of ongoing efforts by the South African Police Service, working with other law enforcement agencies, to combat crime during the festive season. During the operation, officers seized various items, including alcoholic beverages, cigarettes and dagga.

post_title: Ten Buscor Buses Destroyed in Fire
post_content:

Ten Buscor buses were destroyed in a fire that broke out at an overnight storage area in Barberton, next to the Provincial Hospital, during the early hours of Wednesday.

nnnn

According to information received, the buses were parked at the Buscor depot when the fire occurred. Buscor has since confirmed that replacement buses have already been arranged and despatched to Barberton to ensure that commuter services continue with minimal disruption.

nnnnnnnn

The MEC for Public Works, Roads and Transport in Mpumalanga, Mr Thulasizwe Thomo, said he noted the incident with concern but was relieved that no injuries or loss of life were reported.

nnnn

“The safety of workers, commuters and surrounding communities in Barberton and neighbouring areas remains our foremost priority,” said MEC Thomo.

nnnn

He has engaged Buscor management to establish the full extent of the damage and to receive assurances on contingency measures put in place, particularly as many commuters rely on Buscor services during the festive season.

The Department is awaiting a full report from Buscor, including preliminary findings into the cause of the fire, while relevant authorities continue with their investigations. Kruger National Park (KNP) has announced that pre-booked day visitors will be prioritised during the busy festive season, as gate quotas are implemented to manage congestion and ensure a safe and enjoyable experience for all visitors.

nnnn

Day visitors are strongly advised to book online in advance via the SANParks website to secure access to the park. An online booking requires a non-refundable administration fee of R59 for adults and R29 for children, which is separate from the conservation fee payable at the gate unless visitors present a valid Wild Card.

nnnn

Conservation fees remain unchanged. South African citizens, as well as nationals of Zimbabwe and Mozambique, will pay R134 per adult and R67 per child aged between two and 11 years. Visitors from SADC countries will pay R275 per adult and R137 per child, while the standard international conservation fee of R602 for adults and R300 for children applies to all other guests. South Africans are required to present a valid identity document or driver’s licence, while international visitors must produce a passport. Failure to provide valid identification will result in the standard international fee being charged.

nnnn

The quota system applies only to day visitors and not to overnight guests. Pre-booked visitors will receive priority access but must arrive within their allocated time slots. These are from 05:30 to 08:00, 08:00 to 10:00, and from 10:00 onwards. Late arrivals will be treated as non-booked visitors and may lose priority access.

nnnn

Once daily visitor limits are reached, only pre-booked visitors will be allowed entry, with access thereafter dependent on vehicles exiting the park. Wild Card holders are reminded that they are not exempt from the pre-booking administration fee.

nnnn

Strict vehicle compliance will be enforced, with vehicles without licence plates or valid temporary numbers denied entry or exit. Security will be heightened during the festive period, with Ranger Services, SAPS and SANDF deployed to support law enforcement and anti-poaching efforts.

nnnn

post_title: Thank you for your support. Wishing our community a joyful Christmas.
Patron shoots DJ, then himself in Masoyi tavern
post_content:
n

A Christmas Eve celebration ended in tragedy after a patron allegedly shot a DJ before turning the firearm on himself at a tavern in Masoyi, near White River.

nnnn

The incident occurred at around 11.30pm on Wednesday, 24 December 2025, at a tavern in Mganduzweni Trust. Police in Masoyi were conducting routine patrols along the R538 road as part of the 2025/2026 Operation Festive Season when they noticed a group of people leaving the establishment.

nnnn

Upon stopping to investigate, officers discovered that a shooting had taken place inside the tavern. Two adult males were found with gunshot injuries. Emergency medical personnel were called to the scene and both men were certified dead.

nnnn

According to preliminary information, the DJ had been playing music for patrons when he stopped and began packing his equipment, indicating that it was time for the tavern to close. Some patrons allegedly insisted that he continue playing because it was Christmas. An argument reportedly followed, during which a 28-year-old patron allegedly produced a firearm and shot the DJ before turning the gun on himself.

nnnn

Police have opened a case of murder as well as an inquest. The firearm used in the incident has not yet been recovered. Early reports indicate that the tavern is a licensed establishment.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of the SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, has strongly condemned the incident, describing it as a senseless act of violence. He has called for a thorough investigation into how a firearm was allowed into the liquor premises, noting that dangerous weapons are strictly prohibited in such establishments.

nnnn

“The increase in shooting incidents within liquor premises is alarming and detrimental to our society,” said Mkhwanazi. “Tavern owners must take responsibility for the safety of their patrons and employees. Failure to comply with safety regulations carries legal consequences. A life has been lost here, and such a tragic incident cannot be allowed to pass without consequences.”

nnnn

Police investigations are continuing.

post_title: Lebombo border returns to normal after festive rush
post_content:
n

The Lebombo Port of Entry has returned to normal operations following a surge in traveller and cargo movements during the Christmas period, the Border Management Authority (BMA) has confirmed.

nnnn

BMA Commissioner Dr Michael Masiapato said more than 18 450 travellers were successfully processed exiting South Africa through the Lebombo border post on Christmas Day, 25 December 2025. Most travellers were cleared through automated systems, while about 450 people, mainly women and children, were processed manually and are still being fully captured and reconciled on the Enhanced Movement Control System.

nnnn

Dr Masiapato reported that no major interceptions were recorded in vulnerable border areas on Christmas Day, attributing this to heightened patrols and law enforcement visibility. However, 88 individuals were declared undesirable after being found to have overstayed the legally permitted 90 days in the country.

nnnn

In the early hours of 26 December, BMA officials intercepted more than 80 pairs of Nike sneakers being smuggled into South Africa. One individual suspected of facilitating illegal migration was also arrested and charged with aiding and abetting under the Immigration Act. All those involved are being processed in line with immigration and law enforcement regulations.

nnnn

On the movement of goods, the Commissioner said approximately 805 trucks were cleared at KM7, travelling from South Africa into Mozambique and onwards to the Port of Maputo. As a result, the N4 corridor leading to the Lebombo Port of Entry is currently free of congestion.

nnnn

“The Border Management Authority remains fully deployed and vigilant, ensuring the smooth movement of legitimate travellers and cargo, while preventing illegal activities, especially during this peak festive period,” Dr Masiapato said.

nnnn

While operations at the Lebombo border post have stabilised, the BMA said it will continue to closely monitor the situation and provide updates where necessary. Members of the public are encouraged to report suspicious activities through Operation HI-TIVISE on 0801 229 019 or via the BMA website.

nnnn

post_title: Remains Found in Komati River Search
post_content:
n

The search for a missing member of the South African National Defence Force (SANDF) has entered a critical phase after human remains were discovered in the Komati River near the South Africa–Mozambique border.

nnnn

According to an official update issued by Brigadier Donald Mdhluli, search and rescue operations have been under way since the SANDF member was reported missing. The multi-agency effort has involved the SANDF, South African Police Service (SAPS), SANParks, Emergency Medical Services (EMS) and local Search and Rescue teams.

nnnn

On 26 December 2025, SAPS divers recovered the lifeless body of one SANDF member from the Komati River in Komatipoort. On the same day, aerial search operations were intensified with helicopters deployed by SANParks and the SANDF. This was followed by a SAPS helicopter on 27 December, while an EMS helicopter continued aerial operations on Sunday, 28 December. Drones and other technological equipment were also used to support the search.

nnnn

During operations on Saturday, 27 December, a SANDF bakkie was retrieved from the river. Two rifles, a mobile phone and other personal items were found inside the vehicle, but the missing SANDF member was not located at that stage. The search was temporarily suspended on Saturday evening and resumed on Sunday morning.

nnnn

The local community has played a vital role in the operation. Notably, a community member assisted authorities by using a crane to help remove the SANDF vehicle from the river.

nnnn

On Monday, 29 December 2025, as the search continued, a local fisherman alerted authorities to remains seen floating in the river. The remains were later confirmed to be those of a male person and were found near the borderline between Mozambique and South Africa.

nnnn

Police have opened an inquest, and DNA tests will be conducted to confirm whether the remains are those of the missing SANDF member. The search has since been temporarily suspended and is expected to resume on Tuesday, 30 December 2025, pending further investigations.

nnnn

Authorities have expressed appreciation for the continued cooperation between all role players and the support shown by the Komatipoort community during the operation.

nnnn

post_title: Police Intensify Investigation Following Fatal Taxi Shootings
post_content:
n

Police in Calcutta have launched a full investigation into a triple murder involving taxi drivers after two separate shooting incidents were reported on Wednesday, 31 December 2025.

nnnn

The first incident was reported at about 10:00 along the Oakley Trust main road. On arrival, officers found two adult men lying on their backs with no signs of life. Both victims had sustained multiple gunshot wounds and were certified dead at the scene by emergency medical personnel. Nine empty rifle cartridges were recovered.

nnnn

Two Quantum taxis, believed to belong to the Mariti Taxi Association, were found at the scene. Preliminary information suggests that the victims were shot outside their vehicles. The motive for the attack remains unknown at this stage. The bodies were transported to a government mortuary for post-mortem examinations.

nnnn

Approximately an hour later, at about 11:00, police attended to a second shooting incident at Alexandria Trust. Officers found the body of an adult male lying face down in a pool of blood with multiple gunshot wounds to the upper body. A total of 26 empty rifle cartridges and 11 pistol cartridges were recovered at the scene.

nnnn

No witnesses came forward to provide information regarding the circumstances surrounding the incident. The deceased is believed to be a taxi driver affiliated with the Mathibela Taxi Association.

nnnn

Police are appealing to members of the public to assist with information that may lead to the arrest of those responsible. Anyone with information is urged to contact Captain Alfred Monareng on 072 699 8769, the Crime Stop number 08600 10111, or submit tips via the MySAPS App. All information will be treated with strict confidentiality, and anonymity is guaranteed.

nnnn

Police investigations into both incidents are continuing.

ARIES (21 March – 19 April)

Gogo Nonyane ya Metsi sees strong movement in the water, but movement without direction. In 2026, rushing clouds your reflection. Strength must be guided, not forced. Career progress comes through patience, planning and measured leadership. Financial stability improves when impulse is restrained. Relationships test your temper, asking for emotional maturity. This is a year to act less and observe more. When action is guided by clarity, your power becomes lasting rather than exhausting.

The South African Police Service (SAPS) in Mpumalanga has arrested twelve suspects during a crime prevention operation conducted in the Bushbuckridge policing area over the weekend.

nnnn

The operation, carried out under Operation Safer Festive Season by the former Acornhoek Cluster Crime Prevention Team, took place from 4pm on Friday, 10 January, until 4am on Saturday, 11 January 2026. It focused on preventing crime and disrupting serious and organised criminal activities.

nnnn

The arrests were made during stop-and-search operations along the R40 road in the Dwarsloop area. Police stopped and searched a taxi with Mozambican registration, leading to the apprehension of the suspects.

nnnn

Ten of the suspects were arrested for contravening South Africa’s Immigration Act and are believed to be undocumented foreign nationals from Mozambique. The remaining two suspects were arrested on charges related to human trafficking.

nnnn

Police also carried out extensive crime prevention activities across the wider Bushbuckridge area as part of the operation.

nnnn

Detectives are working closely with the Department of Home Affairs to verify the legal status of the arrested individuals. All twelve suspects are expected to appear before the Bushbuckridge Magistrate’s Court soon.

post_title: Pafuri, Giriyondo Posts Closed by Floods
post_content:
n

Two international border posts within the Kruger National Park have been temporarily closed following severe weather conditions affecting parts of Limpopo and Mpumalanga.

nnnn

The Border Management Authority has confirmed the closure of the Pafuri and Giriyondo border posts after continuous heavy rainfall across the park, which follows a Level 6 severe weather warning issued for the region. Visitors have been urged to revise their travel plans and comply with guidance from park officials.

nnnn

Several rivers within the park are currently flowing at high speed, with water levels expected to rise further. These include the De Laporte, N’watshitsaka and Crocodile rivers. The Sabie River is also rising and is expected to impact the Sand River, which may disrupt travel routes between Satara Rest Camp, Tshokwane Picnic Site, Lower Sabie Rest Camp and Skukuza Rest Camp.

nnnnnnnn

Park management has cautioned that road closures may occur at short notice for safety reasons. Campers in affected areas will be relocated within camps, with those in caravans and motorhomes being moved closer to chalet zones. Visitors have also been advised not to remain in low-lying camping areas vulnerable to flooding.

nnnn

Guests travelling to Skukuza Airport from north of Tshokwane have been advised to use Kruger Gate via Satara or Orpen Gate, or alternatively access the airport from outside the park via the R40. Travellers are urged to allow extra time to avoid missing flights.

nnnn

Rainfall recorded overnight ranged from 25 mm in Phalaborwa to as high as 90 mm in Pafuri, with Tshokwane, Shingwedzi, Mooiplaas and Houtboschrand also recording significant rainfall.

nnnn

SANParks has strongly urged all visitors and staff to obey no-entry and road-closure signage, avoid flooded roads and low-lying bridges, and not to remove debris or barriers placed on roads.

nnnn

The South African Weather Service continues to monitor conditions and will issue updates as the situation evolves. The safety of visitors, staff and surrounding communities remains the park’s highest priority.

post_title: Recalled Infant Formula Raises Safety Concerns
post_content:
n

Parents and caregivers have been urged to stop using a specific infant formula following a national product recall linked to potential contamination that may pose a health risk to babies.

nnnn

The affected product is Nestlé NAN Special Pro HA Infant Formula (0–12 months), sold in an 800g can, with batch number 51660742F3 and a best-before date of 15 December 2026. The formula, which has been available on the South African market since September 2025, is intended for the dietary management of infants with allergies to cow’s milk.

nnnn

The recall follows the identification of a possible presence of cereulide, a toxin produced by the bacterium Bacillus cereus. Cereulide is considered a food safety concern and, if consumed, may cause symptoms such as severe or persistent vomiting, diarrhoea, or unusual lethargy, particularly in young infants.

nnnn

Health authorities have confirmed that the contamination has been traced back to a manufacturing facility in Germany that supplies several countries, including South Africa. Importantly, South Africa is reported to have received only this specific batch, and no other Nestlé products or batch numbers are affected by the recall.

nnnn

While no illnesses linked to the affected product have been confirmed locally, parents and caregivers are urged to remain vigilant. They are advised to monitor infants for any concerning symptoms and to consult a healthcare provider immediately if there are worries about a child’s health, even if symptoms are mild or absent.

nnnn

Consumers are encouraged to carefully check the batch number and best-before date on the product packaging. Anyone who has the recalled formula in their possession should return it to the place of purchase for a full refund.

nnnn

Authorities have emphasised that there is no need for panic, noting that precautionary measures are being taken in line with strict food safety and quality protocols. Ongoing engagement with relevant stakeholders is underway to ensure the protection of infant health.

nnnn

The recall has also renewed calls to support and promote breastfeeding as the optimal method of infant feeding. Exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for the first six months of life, with continued breastfeeding up to two years or beyond alongside the gradual introduction of solid foods.

nnnn

Parents, caregivers and the public will continue to be informed of any developments related to the recall as more information becomes available.

n

ActionSA has raised serious concerns about South Africa’s matric results, arguing that the widely celebrated 88% pass rate masks deep and ongoing failures within the basic education system.

nnnn

In a statement issued on 12 January 2026, ActionSA Parliamentary Chief Whip Lerato Ngobeni MP congratulated the Class of 2025 for completing their National Senior Certificate under challenging conditions, and acknowledged the role played by teachers and families. She said every learner who perseveres to the end of matric deserves recognition.

nnnn

However, ActionSA cautioned that headline pass rates do not present a full or honest picture of the system’s performance. Using a cohort-based analysis, which tracks how many learners who entered Grade 10 in 2023 eventually passed matric, the party calculates the effective pass rate at just 57.7%. This figure is based on the 1.14 million learners who began Grade 10, nearly half of whom did not successfully complete matric.

nnnn

According to ActionSA, this gap reflects a schooling system that continues to lose learners through dropout, repetition and disengagement long before they reach their final examinations. The party argues that success is being defined by reducing the number of learners who write matric, rather than by improving learning outcomes across the board.

nnnn

The party also highlighted ongoing safety and infrastructure challenges in schools. Ngobeni pointed to the recent death of a six-year-old girl in Nkuzana village, Limpopo, who fell into a pit toilet, despite such facilities being banned since 2013. A parliamentary reply last year revealed that about 590 schools across the country still rely on pit toilets, more than a decade after government committed to eradicating them.

nnnn

“A system that cannot guarantee basic safety and dignity for learners cannot credibly claim success based on pass percentages alone,” Ngobeni said.

nnnn

ActionSA reiterated its call for comprehensive education reform, including honest reporting of matric outcomes against full learner cohorts, the abolition of the 30% pass mark in favour of meaningful minimum standards, and structured academic support for learners who fall behind. The party also supports the reintroduction of Annual National Assessments and transparent school-level performance data to rebuild accountability.

nnnn

Looking ahead, ActionSA argues that South Africa needs an education system aligned with the realities of a modern economy. It has proposed a dual-stream education model from Grade 10, allowing learners to choose between academic and vocational pathways that respond to the country’s skills needs.

nnnn

“Our education system is not failing by accident,” Ngobeni said. “It is failing because leaders repeatedly choose political comfort over honest reform.” ActionSA says it will continue to push for higher standards, safer schools and an education system that prepares young South Africans not only to pass, but to thrive.

n

post_title: Flooded Access Route Cuts Off Wales Village
post_content:
n

Residents of Wales Village in Ward 32 have been left completely cut off from essential services after heavy rains caused the area’s only access route to flood, raising serious safety and humanitarian concerns.

nnnn

According to community members, the flooding has submerged a low-lying bridge that serves as the sole entry and exit point to the village. Residents say the situation is unprecedented, with water levels higher than those experienced during the severe floods of 2000.

nnnn

Although an assessment was previously conducted for the construction of a proper bridge, the process never progressed beyond that stage. In addition, residents were promised a tarred ring road during the 2019 election period, but no development has since taken place.

nnnn

As a result, the community is now isolated. In the event of a medical emergency, residents are unable to reach a clinic, hospital or mortuary. Community leaders warn that this lack of access places lives at immediate risk, as even minor illnesses or accidents could turn fatal due to delays in receiving help.

nnnn

The flooding also poses a serious danger to learners who must cross the affected route to attend school. With persistent rainfall, many children may be unable to travel safely, potentially disrupting their education and exposing them to further risk.

nnnn

Calls have been made for urgent intervention by the Department of Public Works, Roads and Transport to implement immediate temporary measures to restore safe access. Residents are also demanding that long-term solutions, including the construction of a proper bridge and the promised tarred road, be prioritised without further delay.

nnnn

Community members say reliable infrastructure is essential, not optional, and that no village should be left stranded whenever it rains. They are urging authorities to act swiftly to ensure safety, dignity and uninterrupted access to vital services for the people of Wales Village.

n

post_title: Residents Warned As Heavy Rains Persist
post_content:
n

The Bushbuckridge Local Municipality has urged residents to remain highly vigilant following a level 9 weather warning issued due to persistent heavy rainfall in the area.

nnnn

According to the municipality’s Disaster, Fire and Rescue Unit, the warning was issued by the South African Weather Service and signals potentially dangerous conditions that may pose risks to lives, infrastructure and mobility.

nnnn

Parents and guardians have been reminded to closely monitor children and ensure they do not play unsupervised or travel alone during this period. With schools reopening, and some already operational, special caution has been advised for learners who walk to school. Parents are encouraged to accompany children, particularly those who must cross footbridges or low-lying bridges, and to only cross when conditions are safe.

nnnn

Motorists have also been urged to exercise extreme caution on the roads. The municipality has warned drivers never to attempt crossing flooded bridges, regardless of how shallow the water may appear. Road users are advised to switch on fog and rain lights, reduce speed and remain alert due to wet, slippery surfaces and the deteriorating condition of some roads.

nnnn

Residents living near riverbanks and in low-lying areas have been advised to remain on high alert as rainfall continues. Should rivers burst their banks, community members are urged to move immediately to higher ground to avoid potential flooding.

nnnn

The municipality has appealed for cooperation and responsible behaviour from the public to minimise the risk of injury, loss of life and damage to property during this period of severe weather.

nnnn

In the event of an emergency, residents are urged to contact the Municipal Call Centre on 0800 014 751 or 013 065 0827. Alternatively, the Disaster Management, Fire and Rescue Manager, Mr R Silinda, can be reached on 060 506 4020 or 079 887 9814.

Mpumalanga has once again demonstrated its commitment to education after achieving an impressive 86.55% pass rate in the 2025 National Senior Certificate (NSC) examinations.

nnnn

Premier Mandla Ndlovu announced the results with pride, noting that the province improved on its 84.9% pass rate recorded in 2024. Mpumalanga’s performance also contributed to South Africa’s historic national matric pass rate of 88%.

nnnn

A standout success story from the province is Luyanda Ndlozi from Elangwana Secondary School, who emerged as Mpumalanga’s top achiever and ranked among the top 40 learners nationally. His achievement highlights the potential of learners in the province when given the necessary support and opportunities.

nnnn

Reflecting on the journey of the Class of 2025, Premier Ndlovu acknowledged the unique challenges they faced. “The Class of 2025 started high school during the COVID-19 pandemic, yet their commitment prevailed. Behind every success story stands a dedicated teacher, a parent who sacrificed, and a community that believed,” he said.

nnnn

In recognition of excellence and to further support education, the Mandla Ndlovu Foundation, in partnership with the Department of Education, donated full school uniforms to 1,000 learners across 10 top-performing schools that achieved a 100% pass rate.

nnnn

Premier Ndlovu emphasised that education remains central to the province’s development. “We see each successful matriculation as a step towards building a prosperous future—an era where education becomes the foundation for economic empowerment and social progress,” he said.

nnnn

The province extended its congratulations to the Class of 2025, encouraging learners to carry their success forward and continue making Mpumalanga proud.

post_title: Mass Arrests and Seizures in Mpumalanga
post_content:
n

A major law enforcement initiative, Operation Shanela II, has led to numerous arrests, seizures, and inspections across Mpumalanga. The operation, which ran from 8 to 11 January, involved the South African Police Service (SAPS), Traffic Police, law enforcement agencies, and several government departments, including Home Affairs, Health, and Correctional Services, alongside private security and community policing forums.

nnnn

During the operation, authorities conducted:

nnnn

• 72 premises searches and visits

nnnn

• 5 623 people and 1 789 vehicles screened

nnnn

• 1 258 patrols and 546 stop-and-searches

nnnn

• 101 vehicle checkpoints and 28 roadblocks

nnnn

• 3 240 patrols across the province

nnnn

• Tracing of 111 wanted suspects

nnnn

• Searches of 17 hostels

nnnn

Businesses and commercial operations were also inspected, with nine unlicensed liquor outlets closed, 240 licensed liquor outlets checked, 45 second-hand dealers inspected, and 578 informal businesses, including spaza shops, scrutinised for labour-law compliance. Additionally, 160 farms and 23 mines were visited.

nnnn

The operation resulted in arrests for a wide range of crimes, including:

nnnn

• 224 for assault with grievous bodily harm

nnnn

• 256 for driving under the influence

nnnn

• 186 for illegal liquor dealing

nnnn

• 51 for drug possession and 17 for drug dealing

nnnn

• 12 for murder and 28 for rape

nnnn

• 108 illegal immigrants detained

nnnn

Significant items were confiscated during the operation, including 55 kg of dagga, cocaine, heroin, crystal meth, 166.7 litres of alcohol, 65.7 kg of precious metals, 3 028 counterfeit items, cash amounting to R45 400, and several vehicles and firearms.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi praised officers and stakeholders for their “dedication and professionalism,” while also thanking law-abiding community members for their support.

nnnn

“Together, we will continue to intensify our efforts to create a safer and more secure Mpumalanga for all,” he said

nnnn

The Border Management Authority (BMA) has intercepted another group of undocumented minor children at the Beitbridge Port of Entry on Tuesday, 13 January 2026.

nnnn

According to the BMA, the interception took place at around 12:30 when a junior border guard, deployed during the relief shift, stopped and searched a Zimbabwe-registered minibus taxi at the port of entry. The vehicle was found to be transporting 33 undocumented children, aged between four and 15, who were travelling from South Africa to Zimbabwe.

nnnn

Two Zimbabwean men, aged 32 and 23, were arrested on suspicion of facilitating the illegal cross-border movement of the children. Criminal cases have been opened against the suspects under the Immigration Act for the facilitation of the illegal entry and movement of undocumented persons. They are expected to appear in court later this week.

nnnn

All 33 children were immediately handed over to the Department of Social Development for further processing, in accordance with child protection protocols and South Africa’s domestic and international obligations to safeguard vulnerable persons.

nnnn

The Commissioner of the Border Management Authority, Dr Michael Masiapato, praised the junior border guard for his vigilance and professionalism, saying the interception demonstrated the effectiveness of strengthened border controls. He also urged parents and guardians to refrain from sending undocumented children through ports of entry.

nnnn

“The Border Management Authority will not tolerate the exploitation of children or the facilitation of illegal cross-border movement. We remain committed to protecting the integrity of our borders while upholding human rights and child protection principles,” said Dr Masiapato.

nnnn

Investigations into the matter are continuing.

nnnn

post_title: ANCYL Calls for Class Suspension Amid Floods
post_content:
n

The African National Congress Youth League (ANCYL) Ward 3 has issued an urgent call for the immediate suspension of classes at all schools in the Mkhuhlu Circuit following severe rainfall and flooding in the area.

nnnn

nnnn

nnnn

The ANCYL urged relevant authorities to act swiftly to assess the damage, repair affected infrastructure and implement proper safety measures before schools resume. It also called on parents, school management teams and government departments to work together to ensure learners are protected during the ongoing adverse weather conditions.

nnnn

nnnn

The call comes as several communities in the region continue to experience disruptions caused by flooding, with residents reporting difficulties in travelling and accessing essential services.

ActionSA has congratulated the Mpumalanga Matric Class of 2025 for completing one of the most demanding milestones of their academic journey, describing their achievement as a testament to resilience, discipline and determination.

nnnn

In a statement released on Tuesday, ActionSA Member of the Mpumalanga Legislature Thoko Mashiane said the Class of 2025 had persevered under difficult circumstances, often in under-resourced schools, and deserved recognition for their efforts.

nnnn

Mpumalanga recorded an impressive provincial pass rate of 86.55%, contributing to South Africa’s historic national pass rate of 88% in 2025 – the highest ever recorded. Mashiane said the figures reflected not only academic performance but also the courage and commitment of learners who refused to be defined by their challenges.

nnnn

Siyanda Nkuna from Inkomazi High School was recognised as a national top achiever and an exceptional performer in mathematics. Angie Ntuli of Phumzile Secondary School was honoured among the top 40 learners nationally, while Luyanda Ndhlozi from Elangwane Secondary School in Volksrust emerged as Mpumalanga’s top learner, also ranking among the country’s top 40 performers.

nnnn

nnnn

However, she cautioned that pass rate statistics should not mask the deep inequalities that continue to shape the education system. Persistent challenges such as inadequate infrastructure, uneven teaching support and overcrowded classrooms continue to limit many learners’ full potential.

nnnn

“A pass rate alone cannot capture the personal triumphs, resilience and effort behind these results,” she said.

nnnn

ActionSA called on government to move beyond announcements and implement targeted interventions in underperforming schools, invest meaningfully in teacher development and ensure equitable access to learning resources.

nnnn

Addressing the Class of 2025 directly, Mashiane said the journey did not end with matric results. “Whether you passed with distinction, achieved a solid pass or fell short of your goals, your effort matters. You have shown courage in the face of adversity, and South Africa needs that spirit as you take the next step in your lives.”

post_title: Mpumalanga Set for Mass FMD Vaccination Drive
post_content:
n

Parts of Mpumalanga will be prioritised in a nationwide mass vaccination programme aimed at containing the outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease (FMD), Agriculture Minister John Steenhuisen has announced.

nnnn

Addressing the media at the GCIS Imbizo Centre in Cape Town, Steenhuisen said the Department of Agriculture would roll out an intensified vaccination campaign across all nine provinces to curb the spread of the highly contagious viral disease, which affects cloven-hoofed animals.

nnnn

FMD has now been confirmed in eight provinces, with the Northern Cape the only province yet to record any cases. Mpumalanga and Limpopo have been identified as high-risk areas due to recurring infections, particularly in regions where buffalo farming has expanded.

nnnn

According to Steenhuisen, the department has already vaccinated close to two million animals since the disease re-emerged in April last year. He said the new phase of interventions would focus on immediate mass vaccination in affected areas, followed by repeat vaccinations within three months.

nnnn

“In those provinces, we will see 100% vaccination of feedlots and dairy cows, 90% of commercial animals and 80% of communal livestock,” Steenhuisen said.

nnnn

He added that in hotspot areas such as parts of Mpumalanga, bi-annual vaccination campaigns would be introduced, especially along border zones where the risk of transmission remains high. Ongoing vaccination will also continue within designated protection zones.

nnnn

The minister emphasised that the programme is critical to protecting livestock, safeguarding livelihoods and stabilising the agricultural sector, particularly for small-scale and communal farmers who are most vulnerable to the economic impact of outbreaks.

nnnn

Local farmers in Mpumalanga are urged to cooperate with veterinary services and ensure their animals are presented for vaccination as the campaign is rolled out in the coming weeks.

post_title: Classes Suspended in Bushbuckridge Due to Heavy Rains
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga Department of Education has announced the temporary suspension of classes in the Bushbuckridge Local Municipality following persistent heavy rainfall that has disrupted schooling in the area.

nnnn

In a statement issued on Wednesday, 14 January 2026, the department said it held an urgent meeting with District Directors and affected Circuit Managers to assess the impact of the ongoing weather conditions on teaching and learning across the province.

nnnn

The department noted that schools in the Nkangala and Gert Sibande districts have reopened smoothly, with teaching and learning commencing without major challenges. This, it said, has created a positive and focused environment for learners and educators in those areas.

nnnn

However, conditions in the Bohlabela District, particularly in Bushbuckridge, remain a cause for concern. Continuous rainfall has resulted in waterlogged and inaccessible roads, making it difficult for some learners and teachers to reach their schools safely.

nnnn

As a result, the department has decided to temporarily suspend classes in the Bushbuckridge Local Municipality for two days, from Thursday, 15 January to Friday, 16 January 2026.

nnnn

In the broader Ehlanzeni District, school principals have been granted the authority to use their discretion, based on on-the-ground assessments, to determine whether it is safe for schools to operate. This measure is aimed at ensuring the safety of both learners and staff.

nnnn

The department emphasised that the advisory allowing schools to exercise discretion remains in place for all areas currently affected by rainfall. However, due to the severity of conditions reported in Bushbuckridge, a full temporary suspension was deemed necessary.

nnnn

Community members have been urged to remain vigilant and to prioritise safety at all times. The department strongly appealed to residents not to attempt crossing flooded rivers, submerged bridges or unsafe roads under any circumstances.

nnnn

“The safety of our children is a shared responsibility,” the department said, adding that it will continue to closely monitor developments and provide updates as the situation evolves.

post_title: Bushbuckridge Music Community Mourns Sandile Mukasi
post_content:
n

nnnn

She was widely regarded as a unifying force, always willing to lend a helping hand and advocate for the growth of the creative sector.

nnnn

In honour of her life and in solidarity with her family, BUMA has called on its members, as well as other music organisations in Bushbuckridge, to contribute R100 per member towards funeral and related financial arrangements. The association has further noted that any additional contribution, regardless of the amount, will be deeply appreciated and will assist the family during this difficult time.

nnnn

The funeral service will take place on 18 January 2026, with the time to be announced.

nnnn

As the community prepares to lay Sandile Mukasi to rest, musicians and cultural practitioners stand together in remembrance of a woman whose dedication and kindness left a lasting imprint on Bushbuckridge’s music landscape. Her spirit and contribution will continue to resonate through the work of the artists she supported.
