post_title: Prospective Students Urged to Use Central Application Service
post_content:
n

Higher Education and Training Minister Buti Manamela has encouraged prospective students who need guidance in accessing the Post-School Education and Training (PSET) system to make use of the Central Application Service (CAS), as government rolls out reforms aimed at improving access and protecting learners.

nnnn

The Minister said the Department of Higher Education and Training had previously introduced the Central Applications Clearing House (CACH) as a short-term measure to match unplaced applicants with available study spaces. However, from the 2026 academic year, CACH will be discontinued as part of broader changes to the application process.

nnnn

According to Manamela, CAS has been developed as a comprehensive, long-term solution that integrates information across the entire PSET system. He said the service will progressively make visible a wider range of learning pathways beyond traditional universities and colleges, while also helping to eliminate bogus institutions and protect students from exploitation. Learners seeking information and guidance can WhatsApp the CAS Chat number on 081 308 4196.

nnnn

The department has also warned students and parents to be vigilant against illegal colleges that operate outside the law and offer unrecognised qualifications. Manamela stressed that qualifications offered by private skills development providers must be quality assured by recognised bodies, including the Quality Council for Trades and Occupations, relevant Sector Education and Training Authorities and the South African Qualifications Authority. He cautioned that bogus colleges often exploit periods of transition by charging fees without delivering credible outcomes, urging families to verify institutions on the department’s official platforms before making payments.

nnnn

Acknowledging that the move from school to further study can be emotionally demanding, the Minister said the department, through Higher Health, provides free and confidential psychosocial and mental health support. Students requiring assistance with stress, anxiety or crisis-related concerns can contact the 24-hour Higher Health Helpline on 0800 36 36 36.

nnnn

Manamela also announced expanded funding opportunities, noting that more than 15 000 SETA bursaries have been made available for students who do not qualify for National Student Financial Aid Scheme funding, particularly those in the “missing middle” and in scarce skills areas. The bursaries support studies at universities and TVET colleges and cover tuition, learning materials and other study-related costs.

nnnn

The department has advised students and parents to rely only on official communication channels, keep application records, and remain cautious of anyone claiming to guarantee placement or accommodation for a fee. Manamela encouraged learners who do not immediately receive offers to explore alternative pathways, emphasising that South Africa’s PSET system offers multiple entry points and second-chance opportunities for those willing to persist.

n

post_title: Disaster Looms as Level 10 Rainfall Warning Issued
post_content:
n

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has issued a Red Level 10 Warning for Disruptive Rainfall for parts of Limpopo and Mpumalanga, warning that the risk of severe flooding remains critically high over the next 48 hours.

nnnn

According to SAWS, the warning follows several days of intense rainfall that has already saturated catchment areas, rivers and dams. With further heavy rain expected, authorities say the likelihood of widespread flooding has increased significantly, posing a serious threat to lives, livelihoods and infrastructure.

nnnn

SAWS cautions that potential impacts may include fast-flowing rivers and streams that could endanger lives, flooding of roads, bridges and low-lying crossings, and extensive damage to settlements, property and critical infrastructure. Communities may also face displacement, while essential services such as electricity, water supply and transport could be severely disrupted.

nnnn

Forecast guidance indicates that an additional 100 to 200 millimetres of rainfall may fall over parts of Limpopo and Mpumalanga within the next 24 to 48 hours. Areas expected to be most affected include Maruleng and Ba-Phalaborwa Local Municipalities, Nkomazi Local Municipality, the City of Mbombela, Bushbuckridge Local Municipality, Greater Giyani, Greater Tzaneen, Greater Letaba and Collins Chabane.

nnnn

The Red Level 10 Warning will remain in effect for as long as conditions continue to pose a severe risk. Residents in affected areas are urged to remain vigilant, avoid travelling through flooded roads or bridges, and follow guidance from local authorities and disaster management teams.

nnnn

SAWS has advised communities to stay informed through official weather updates and emergency alerts as the situation continues to develop.

n

post_title: Severe Weather Forces Temporary Closure to Kruger Day Visitors
post_content:
n

Day visits to the Kruger National Park have been temporarily suspended as persistent heavy rainfall continues to affect parts of Limpopo and Mpumalanga, raising safety concerns across the region.

nnnn

South African National Parks (SANParks) confirmed that the decision was taken as a precautionary measure in response to deteriorating weather and road conditions. The suspension will remain in place until conditions improve and is being reviewed on an ongoing basis.

nnnn

According to SANParks, the prolonged rainfall has placed considerable strain on operational and emergency response resources. The organisation said it is prioritising real emergencies and the safety of guests, staff and neighbouring communities, rather than risking avoidable incidents linked to non-essential travel within the park.

nnnn

“The safety of all visitors and staff remains our highest priority,” SANParks said, adding that the suspension of day visitors is intended to reduce risk during this period of severe weather.

nnnn

The impact of the heavy rains has already been felt within the park. Letaba Rest Camp is currently evacuating both staff and guests after floodwaters from the Letaba River entered the camp. In addition, Phalaborwa Gate has been closed for at least 24 hours while conditions are closely monitored. As a result, there is presently no access to the northern sections of the park.

nnnn

SANParks has apologised for the inconvenience caused by the ongoing rainfall and thanked the public for their understanding and cooperation. Further updates will be issued as the situation develops and as assessments of weather and road conditions continue.

nnnn

Visitors and community members are encouraged to stay informed through official SANParks communication channels while the severe weather persists.

nnnnnnnnn

post_title: Minster moves to scrap drinking and driving policy
post_content:
n

The Minister of Transport has announced plans to amend South Africa’s drinking and driving laws, declaring that any policy which allows motorists to consume alcohol before getting behind the wheel is no longer acceptable. The announcement was made during the release of the 2025/26 Festive Season Road Safety Campaign report.

nnnn

Presenting the report, the Minister revealed the scale of enforcement conducted over the festive season. A total of 1 632 roadblocks were carried out nationwide, with approximately 1.8 million vehicles stopped and checked. During this period, more than 450 000 traffic fines were issued, while 525 motorists were arrested for excessive speeding.

nnnn

Law-enforcement operations focused on roadworthiness, driver fitness and licensing. In addition, 173 695 drivers were tested for driving under the influence of alcohol. Of these, 8 561 tested positive — representing a 144 percent increase compared to the same period last year.

nnnn

The highest alcohol reading was recorded in KwaZulu-Natal, where one motorist tested at fourteen times above the legal alcohol limit. Meanwhile, the most extreme speeding incident occurred in the Northern Cape, where a driver was arrested after being clocked at 222 km/h in a 120 km/h zone. Officers also arrested 89 motorists for attempting to bribe traffic officials to avoid arrest.

nnnn

Beyond enforcement, the campaign placed strong emphasis on education and awareness. A total of 2 547 physical education and awareness programmes were conducted across the country, including outreach at mass transit departure points, shopping centres and other areas of high public activity. These efforts were supported by extensive awareness campaigns on radio, television and social media platforms.

nnnn

Encouragingly, preliminary annual statistics indicate a downward trend in road crashes and fatalities. In 2025, a total of 9 674 crashes resulted in 11 418 fatalities, compared to 10 633 crashes and 12 581 fatalities in 2021. Compared to 2024, crashes decreased by 6.4 percent, while fatalities declined by 6.2 percent — the lowest figures recorded in the past five years.

nnnn

The Minister thanked traffic officers at national, provincial and local government levels, as well as SAPS and emergency services, for their dedication throughout the year. Appreciation was also extended to provincial MECs, municipal MMCs for Transport, traditional authorities, and the organised bus, taxi and trucking sectors, alongside civil society organisations, for their role in reducing road accidents.

nnnn

Looking ahead, the Department will intensify consistent traffic law enforcement, particularly over weekends and public holidays, and will strengthen education and enforcement initiatives targeting pedestrians. The Minister noted that in towns, cities and rural areas, pedestrians account for roughly half of all road deaths.

nnnn

Describing road fatalities as “a reason for national shame”, the Minister stressed that deaths on the roads are neither inevitable nor unavoidable. Analysis shows that human behaviour — especially reckless driving — remains the leading cause of road trauma, with speeding and drunk driving the primary contributors.

nnnn

It was against this backdrop that the Minister confirmed plans to amend Section 65 of the National Road Traffic Act. The current drinking and driving policy, formulated nearly 30 years ago, allows drivers to consume limited amounts of alcohol before driving. The Minister stated that this law must be scrapped in favour of a clear and unambiguous rule: drinking and driving is not allowed.

nnnn

“If nothing else, we owe this to the memory of the many South Africans who have lost their lives on our roads,” the Minister said.

nnnn

nnnn

n

post_title: Kruger Park Closed Amid Heavy Rains
post_content:
n

Persistent rainfall continues to affect large parts of Limpopo and Mpumalanga, forcing the temporary suspension of day visitation to the Kruger National Park (KNP) until further notice.

nnnn

Access to the park is now strictly limited to essential delivery vehicles, airport transfers with confirmed bookings, guests with existing overnight reservations at Berg en Dal, Pretoriuskop and Skukuza rest camps, and essential staff.

nnnn

The northern regions of the park remain inaccessible due to flooding and damaged roads. Satara Rest Camp has also been affected, with staff quarters submerged; affected staff were safely evacuated and no injuries have been reported. Water and electricity disruptions have led to the temporary closure of the camp.

nnnn

All tourism activities, including guided game drives and bush walks, are suspended as many internal roads remain unsafe. Visitors leaving the park are advised to monitor local road conditions, as flooding has impacted surrounding provincial and regional routes.

nnnn

SANParks continues to work with disaster management authorities and urges the public to follow official channels for updates. Guest and staff safety remains the highest priority.

nnnnnnnn

n

post_title: DBE Urges Matric Second Chance Use
post_content:
n

The Department of Basic Education (DBE) has encouraged National Senior Certificate (NSC) candidates who were unsuccessful in their initial examination attempts to take advantage of the official Second Chance Matric Programme.

nnnn

The programme, which is provided free of charge, allows eligible candidates to rewrite or add subjects during the May/June examination cycle, in line with departmental policies. The DBE has emphasised that no payment is required to participate and has cautioned learners and parents against private or commercial services claiming to offer access to the programme for a fee.

nnnn

“The Department does not endorse any private or commercial services that require payment for participation in the Second Chance Programme,” the DBE said. “For authentic information, candidates are advised to contact the Department of Basic Education directly or visit the official website.”

nnnn

The Second Chance Matric Programme is designed to support learners who have not met the requirements of the NSC or the Extended Senior Certificate. It forms part of government’s broader efforts to improve access to education and increase learner retention, in line with the goals of the National Development Plan and the priorities of the basic education sector.

nnnn

Beyond providing a second opportunity to complete school qualifications, the programme also exposes learners to bursary opportunities for further studies, helping them to pursue post-school education and training pathways.

nnnn

The DBE outlined the categories of candidates who qualify for support under the programme. These include Senior Certificate Examination candidates who are registered to write the June examinations, as well as part-time NSC candidates who first attempted the NSC examinations after 2008 and will be writing in the May/June or November examination sessions.

nnnn

A range of key subjects is covered through the Second Chance Programme. These include Accounting, Agricultural Sciences, Business Studies, Economics, English First Additional Language, Geography, History, Mathematics, Mathematical Literacy, Physical Sciences and Life Sciences.

nnnn

Meanwhile, the DBE confirmed that the 2025 Matric Results will be released on 12 January 2026. More than 900 000 candidates sat for the 2025 examinations across approximately 7 000 examination centres nationwide. The process was supported by thousands of invigilators, as well as more than 51 000 markers and moderators, underscoring the scale of the national assessment effort.

nnnn

The department has reiterated its commitment to supporting learners to complete their schooling and has urged all eligible candidates to make use of the Second Chance Matric Programme to improve their results and future prospects.

n

post_title: Red Alert Issued As Flood Risk Persists
post_content:
n

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has confirmed that the Red Level 10 warning for disruptive rainfall remains in place for Friday across the Lowveld region of Mpumalanga, with communities in Nkomazi, Bushbuckridge and the City of Mbombela identified as the most affected areas.

nnnn

According to SAWS, residents should expect on-and-off showers and periods of persistent rain throughout the day. The ongoing rainfall is attributed to tropical moisture affecting the Lowveld and the escarpment areas of Mpumalanga, creating conditions that significantly increase the risk of flooding.

nnnn

SAWS has warned that the soil across much of the region is already saturated, heightening the likelihood of severe impacts. These include widespread flooding, fast-flowing streams and rivers, and potential danger to life. In some areas, flooding could lead to the displacement of communities and extensive damage to homes and other structures.

nnnn

The weather service further cautioned that there is a strong possibility of damage to property, buildings and essential infrastructure, with many residents facing the risk of losing livelihoods. Road infrastructure is also vulnerable, raising concerns that some communities may become inaccessible or cut off for prolonged periods as a result of damaged bridges and washed-away roads.

nnnn

Emergency services and local authorities are on high alert, and residents living in flood-prone areas have been urged to take extra precautions. SAWS has advised people to avoid crossing flooded roads and streams, to secure valuable belongings, and to relocate to safer areas if instructed to do so by authorities.

nnnn

Members of the public are strongly encouraged to remain vigilant and to stay informed by regularly monitoring official SAWS weather updates and warnings through trusted platforms, including radio, television and verified social media channels. Misinformation during severe weather events can place lives at risk, and residents are advised to rely only on official sources.

nnnn

SAWS has reiterated that it will continue to closely monitor the evolving weather system and will issue further updates as conditions change. Communities in the affected areas are urged to take the warnings seriously and to prioritise safety as heavy rainfall continues across the Lowveld.

n

post_title: Mpumalanga Needs R2.1 Billion For Flood Repairs Infrastructure
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga provincial government says it will require an estimated R2.1 billion to repair infrastructure damaged by recent heavy rains and flooding, with bridges and roads among the most severely affected.

nnnn

Persistent rainfall since late last year has caused widespread flooding across the province, washing away roads, damaging bridges and leaving some communities temporarily cut off from essential services. Provincial authorities say preliminary assessments indicate that the cost of repairing the damage is substantial and could increase as further evaluations are conducted.

nnnn

According to the provincial government, several bridges have been badly damaged or rendered unsafe, making them a top priority for repair. Bridges play a crucial role in connecting rural communities to schools, clinics, hospitals and markets, and their closure has disrupted daily life, emergency services and local economic activity.

nnnn

In addition to bridge damage, numerous roads have been affected by erosion, potholes and collapsing surfaces, while incidents such as rockfalls on key routes, including parts of the R38, have raised safety concerns for motorists.

nnnn

More than 1 200 households across Mpumalanga are reported to have been affected by the flooding, with some families displaced and others struggling with limited access to transport and basic services. Authorities have warned that rivers and dams remain under pressure, increasing the risk of further flooding should heavy rains continue.

nnnn

The scale of the damage has contributed to the national declaration of a disaster, allowing government to coordinate relief efforts and mobilise resources across affected provinces, including Mpumalanga and Limpopo.

nnnn

Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs Minister Velenkosini Hlabisa has assured the public that disaster relief funding will be closely monitored to ensure it reaches the communities most in need. The Mpumalanga government is expected to submit detailed damage reports to the National Disaster Management Centre as part of the process to access national funding.

nnnn

Provincial officials have emphasised that the R2.1 billion figure is a preliminary estimate, and that final costs will depend on further technical assessments and the extent of repairs required.

nnnn

Meanwhile, residents are urged to remain cautious, avoid damaged roads and bridges, and follow safety warnings issued by authorities as recovery and repair efforts continue.

n

post_title: Floods Test Kruger, SANParks Earns Minister’s Praise
post_content:
n

The Minister of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment, Mr Willie Aucamp, has commended South African National Parks (SANParks) for its “safety-first” approach following his visit to the flood-affected Kruger National Park.

nnnn

Minister Aucamp visited the park to assess damage caused by heavy rainfall and to engage with SANParks management and other stakeholders. Large parts of Mpumalanga and Limpopo have experienced severe weather over recent days, resulting in flooding and disruptions to infrastructure and park operations.

nnnn

“While there have been major disruptions and damage due to the heavy rains, it has been encouraging to witness the well-planned and coordinated response by Kruger National Park,” said Aucamp. “Early warning systems allowed emergency teams to act timeously and evacuate staff and guests safely.”

nnnn

The Minister praised SANParks for prioritising human safety despite significant operational challenges, including road and gate closures, power outages and interruptions to basic services.

nnnn

He also announced that SANParks has committed to establishing a Kruger Relief Fund to support rebuilding efforts, emergency supplies and other urgent needs. The fund will be managed and audited by two independent auditing firms to ensure transparency.

nnnn

Although disruptive rainfall may continue in the coming days, the Minister said SANParks and emergency services remain well equipped to manage the situation. Day visits to the Kruger National Park remain prohibited until further notice, while access at several gates is restricted.

nnnn

Entry into the park is currently limited to essential delivery vehicles, airport transfers with valid flight tickets, officials, and guests with confirmed accommodation bookings at Berg-en-Dal, Skukuza and Pretoriuskop camps.

nnnn

Minister Aucamp confirmed that the situation is being closely monitored and that updates will be shared as conditions change. “The safety of guests, staff and infrastructure remains the highest priority,” he said, urging the public to rely on SANParks’ official communication platforms for verified information.

nnnn

“We are grateful that no loss of life has been recorded and that evacuations have been conducted smoothly,” the Minister added, thanking park management and emergency services for their swift response.

nnnn

SANParks is expected to release further details on the Kruger Relief Fund in due course.

nnnnnnn

post_title: Gogo Nonyane ya Metsi – Weekly Message (19–26 January)
post_content:
n

Before the stars speak, Gogo first greets the water.

nnnn

This week, the water is quiet but alert. It does not rush, yet it remembers everything. When Gogo Nonyane ya Metsi looks into it, she sees constellations leaning closer to the earth, their light stretching across the surface like threads connecting the heavens to human lives. These are not loud signs. They are whispers from the ancestors, carried by reflection and shadow.

nnnn

The sky during this week shows movement between endings and beginnings. Some constellations stand firm, others slowly shift their position, reminding us that time does not break suddenly — it turns. The water reveals that many are standing at a crossing: between holding on and letting go, between speaking and remaining silent, between action and patience.

nnnn

Gogo says: “When the stars bend toward the water, they ask us to look inward. What you disturb now will ripple far. What you heal now will settle many seasons.”

nnnn

This is a week for measured steps, honest reflection, and listening more than speaking. The constellations do not demand speed — they ask for awareness. Watch the signs that repeat themselves. Pay attention to dreams, to sudden memories, to words that arrive more than once. These are messages surfacing.

nnnn

Below, each sign receives its message as seen in the water and guided by its constellation for the week of 19–26 January.

nnnn

nnnn

Aries (21 March – 19 April)

nnnnnnnn

Gogo looks into the water and sees Aries burning bright beneath the stars, yet its reflection trembles. The Ram stands high in the sky, urging movement, but the waters warn against force. This week, your fire must learn patience. A matter at work or within the family may test your temper. The constellation shows that strength now lies in waiting. By mid-week, the waters clear and reveal the right moment to act. Move then — not before.

nnnn

Taurus (20 April – 20 May)

nnnnnnnn

The constellation of Taurus appears heavy and grounded, mirrored in deep, unmoving water. Gogo sees burdens you have carried silently — responsibilities others may not notice. This week asks you to release what no longer feeds your spirit. Financial or home matters come into focus. When Taurus loosens its grip, abundance flows again. Rest near the end of the week restores your strength.

nnnn

Gemini (21 May – 20 June)

nnnnnnnn

In the water, Gogo sees Gemini’s twin stars crossing paths, sending ripples in many directions. Words surround you — messages, calls, decisions. Be careful which voice you follow. Not all information is meant for action. One truth, revealed quietly around Wednesday, brings clarity. Let the twins unite rather than compete within you.

nnnn

Cancer (21 June – 22 July)

nnnnnnnn

The Moon walks with Cancer’s constellation, and the water reflects deep emotional tides. Gogo sees old feelings returning, asking to be acknowledged. Do not fear them. Home, ancestors, and family carry healing this week. By the weekend, the waters settle, and your heart feels lighter. What was hidden is now understood.

nnnn

Leo (23 July – 22 August)

nnnnnnnn

Gogo sees Leo shining proudly among the stars, yet its reflection bends in the water. This is a lesson in humility. Recognition comes, but only if shared. Partnerships require listening, not commanding. The Sun blesses you toward the end of the week, restoring confidence — softer, wiser, and more respected.

nnnn

Virgo (23 August – 22 September)

nnnnnnnn

The waters show Virgo’s careful constellation, each star in its place. This is a week of correction and healing. Gogo sees you restoring order — in health, work, or daily routine. Be careful not to fix what does not ask for fixing, especially in relationships. Simplicity brings peace.

nnnn

Libra (23 September – 22 October)

nnnnnnnn

Libra’s scales appear reflected on the water’s surface, gently tipping. Gogo says balance must begin within. Emotional honesty is required — especially in love and creative matters. Speak gently but firmly. By the weekend, harmony returns, guided by truth rather than silence.

nnnn

Scorpio (23 October – 21 November)

nnnnnnnn

The waters are still, and Scorpio’s constellation glows beneath, powerful and unseen. Gogo senses secrets and unspoken intentions around you. This week favours observation. Do not reveal all you know. A hidden truth surfaces — handle it with wisdom. Transformation moves quietly but deeply.

nnnn

Sagittarius (22 November – 21 December)

nnnnnnnn

Gogo sees Sagittarius stretching across the sky, arrow pointed forward. The water ripples with movement — travel, study, or new plans call you. But the ancestors caution against abandoning what is unfinished. A conversation or short journey opens a new path. Choose with care.

nnnn

Capricorn (22 December – 19 January)

nnnnnnnn

The mountain goat of Capricorn reflects firmly in the water, showing progress earned through endurance. This is a powerful week for structure, finances, and long-term goals. Gogo sees doors opening — but only where discipline has been honoured. Do not neglect rest; even the strongest must pause.

nnnn

Aquarius (20 January – 18 February)

nnnnnnnn

Fresh currents swirl as Aquarius rises in the sky, pouring wisdom into the water. New ideas, friendships, and visions emerge. Gogo says your voice carries medicine this week — speak truth, but ground it in reality. Innovation flourishes when guided by responsibility.

nnnn

Pisces (19 February – 20 March)

nnnnnnnn

The waters deepen as Pisces swims between worlds, its constellation shimmering softly. Intuition is strong, but boundaries are thin. Gogo warns against carrying pain that is not yours. Creativity, prayer, and dreams are heightened. By the weekend, clarity returns like dawn over calm water.

n

post_title: KNP Introduces Gate Quotas Due to Flood Damage
post_content:
n

The Kruger National Park (KNP) has implemented a gate quota system with immediate effect following increased overnight rainfall that caused further damage to park roads and infrastructure.

nnnn

According to park management, the decision was taken in the interest of visitor safety and effective traffic control, as persistent rain continues to affect large parts of the park. The quota system will apply at Malelane Gate, Numbi Gate and Paul Kruger Gate, and includes all Open Safari Vehicles (OSVs) entering the park.

nnnn

Visitors have been urged to ensure that their vehicles have sufficient fuel, as filling stations at camps may be affected by the ongoing adverse weather conditions.

nnnn

Park authorities confirmed that essential delivery vehicles, airport transfers—provided proof of a valid flight ticket is presented—and official vehicles will be permitted entry only through Paul Kruger Gate.

nnnn

Several routes and gates remain closed due to flooding and safety concerns. The Skukuza to Phabeni Gate route is currently closed after a stream cut off access along the S1 road, rendering Phabeni Gate inaccessible via Skukuza at this stage.

nnnn

In addition, Orpen Gate will remain closed until further notice due to safety risks. The northern section of the park is also inaccessible, resulting in the closure of all northern gates.

nnnn

The park’s managing authority, SANParks, said it continues to closely monitor weather conditions, road safety and infrastructure damage. Further updates will be communicated as the situation develops.

nnnn

Visitors planning trips to the park are advised to monitor official SANParks communication channels for the latest information and to comply with all safety instructions while the severe weather persists.

nnnn

nnnnnnnn

n

post_title: National Disaster Declared After Severe Floods
post_content:
n

The government has officially declared a national disaster in response to catastrophic severe weather and flooding that have affected several provinces since late December 2025.

nnnn

The classification was confirmed in a statement issued by National Disaster Management Centre, with its head, Elias Sithole, citing the scale and severity of the destruction as the basis for the decision.

nnnn

The declaration follows weeks of torrential rain, lightning and damaging winds that have ravaged Limpopo, Mpumalanga, KwaZulu-Natal, Eastern Cape and the North West.

nnnn

In the official directive, Sithole said the widespread impact of the severe weather left the authorities with no option but to escalate the response.

nnnn

“I regard this occurrence as a disaster and, in terms of Section 23(1)(b) of the Disaster Management Act, 2002, I classify the disaster as a national disaster,” he stated.

nnnn

He noted that the prolonged severe weather has resulted in the loss of life, extensive damage to homes, public infrastructure and the environment, as well as major disruptions to basic services such as electricity, water supply and access to healthcare and education.

nnnn

With the declaration now in place, the primary responsibility for coordinating and managing the disaster response shifts to the National Executive. This enables the mobilisation of additional resources and allows for a more coordinated response across national, provincial and local spheres of government.

nnnn

Sithole has called on all organs of state to strengthen their support to disaster management structures and to ensure that contingency and emergency plans are fully activated to address the ongoing effects of flooding.

nnnn

The National Disaster Management Centre will oversee a multi-sectoral relief and rehabilitation programme aimed at supporting affected communities, restoring essential services and beginning the long process of rebuilding damaged infrastructure across the impacted provinces.

n

post_title: ActionSA Warns Floods Endanger Mpumalanga Learners
post_content:
n

ActionSA has raised serious concerns over the impact of recent heavy rains and flooding across Mpumalanga, warning that failing infrastructure is placing lives at risk, particularly those of school learners.

nnnn

In a statement issued on Sunday, ActionSA said the provincial government has confirmed that an estimated R2.1 billion is needed to repair flood-damaged infrastructure, including roads and crossings that are critical for mobility, safety and economic activity.

nnnn

The party said the human cost of the floods is even more alarming. The death toll linked to the heavy rains in Mpumalanga has risen sharply, with dozens of lives lost across the province and neighbouring areas.

nnnn

“These are not merely statistics. They are families torn apart and communities traumatised by a tragedy that demands urgent and decisive leadership,” said Thoko Mashiane, an ActionSA Member of the Mpumalanga Legislature.

nnnn

Mashiane highlighted conditions in Matsulu, where learners are reportedly being forced to cross roads that have turned into flowing streams just to get to and from school.

nnnn

“This is extremely dangerous and entirely unacceptable. No child should have to risk their life in order to access an education,” she said.

nnnn

According to ActionSA, the crisis exposes a deeper structural problem in the province, with infrastructure that is not designed to withstand extreme weather events. In many rural areas, communities rely on low-lying crossings that were never properly engineered to endure heavy rainfall.

nnnn

“These structures did not fail by chance. They were inadequate by design,” Mashiane said, adding that the predictable result is flooded roads, isolated communities and lives placed in danger.

nnnn

The party said the R2.1 billion repair bill is evidence of a reactive approach by government, arguing that proper planning, engineering and maintenance could have significantly reduced both the financial burden and the loss of life.

nnnn

ActionSA has called on provincial and national authorities to urgently mobilise additional aid for affected communities, prioritise the restoration of safe access routes—especially those used by learners—and commit to a long-term infrastructure strategy that accounts for climate change and extreme weather.

nnnn

“The people of Mpumalanga deserve infrastructure that protects them, not systems that fail them when they are most vulnerable,” Mashiane said.

n

post_title: Floods Leave Death, Destruction Across Province
post_content:
n

kAt least 20 people have lost their lives following severe flooding that has devastated large parts of Mpumalanga, leaving thousands of residents displaced and without basic necessities.

nnnn

Provincial authorities estimate that more than 1,500 homes have been damaged or destroyed, forcing families into temporary shelters or leaving them destitute. Critical infrastructure has also taken a heavy knock, with several roads and bridges washed away or rendered unsafe. Preliminary assessments place the cost of the damage at approximately R2 billion.

nnnn

Mpumalanga Premier Mandla Ndlovu has urged residents to remain vigilant and to avoid affected areas, particularly rivers and low-lying zones where water levels remain dangerously high.

nnnn

“One is one too many, so that is why we are making this call to the people of the province to avoid finding themselves in dangerous places, especially our rivers, which are flowing fast,” Ndlovu said.

nnnn

The floods follow days of relentless rainfall linked to severe weather systems affecting several parts of the country. Emergency services, disaster management teams and volunteers have been deployed to assist affected communities, conduct search-and-rescue operations and provide humanitarian relief.

nnnn

President Cyril Ramaphosa has pledged national government support to assist Mpumalanga as it recovers from the disaster. On Monday, Ramaphosa visited the province to conduct oversight inspections in some of the worst-hit areas.

nnnnnnnn

The President confirmed that government would adopt an “all-hands-on-deck” approach in response to weather-related disasters impacting Mpumalanga, as well as Limpopo and KwaZulu-Natal.

nnnn

Engagements are already under way with the National Treasury following the official disaster classification of the affected regions. Ramaphosa said the scale of the damage requires urgent and coordinated intervention from all spheres of government.

nnnn

“Our Minister of Finance is in Davos, but we are briefing him, and we’re going to see what intervention the government is able to make,” the President said.

nnnn

While acknowledging the swift response by emergency and disaster management teams, Ramaphosa stressed that more resources and long-term solutions are needed.

nnnn

“As government response has been effective, obviously, we need to do more to deal with disasters that continue to befall us,” he said.

nnnn

Authorities have warned that further rainfall could worsen conditions, and residents are encouraged to heed official alerts, cooperate with emergency services and prioritise safety as recovery efforts continue

n

post_title: SACC urges united faith response to devastating floods
post_content:
n

The South African Council of Churches (SACC) has called for a united response from faith communities following severe flooding that has affected large parts of Limpopo and Mpumalanga.

nnnn

In a media statement issued on Tuesday, SACC General Secretary Rev Mzwandile Molo expressed solidarity with communities impacted by persistent heavy rainfall over recent days. The flooding has caused widespread damage to homes, roads and bridges, disrupted essential services and claimed lives. Government has since classified the situation as a National Disaster to strengthen coordination and accelerate relief efforts.

nnnn

The SACC said it was deeply moved by reports of up to 30 people having lost their lives, with others still missing. Rev Molo conveyed heartfelt condolences to bereaved families and assured prayers for those whose loved ones remain unaccounted for.

nnnn

Quoting Galatians 6:2, “Carry each other’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfil the law of Christ,” the council emphasised the importance of compassion and shared responsibility during the crisis. Prayers were also extended to families who have been displaced or traumatised by the floods.

nnnn

The statement raised serious concern about the risks posed by damaged infrastructure, including washed-away bridges, submerged roads and overflowing rivers. These conditions have left some communities isolated from clinics, schools, food supply routes and emergency services. Residents were urged to prioritise safety and strictly heed official warnings, particularly by avoiding flooded roads and fast-moving streams.

nnnn

While welcoming the declaration of a National Disaster, the SACC stressed that disaster funding and procurement processes must be handled honestly and transparently. Rev Molo warned that such emergencies should never be exploited for corruption or the abuse of public resources.

nnnn

The council also acknowledged and gave thanks for the relief efforts already underway, particularly those led by faith-based institutions, including SACC member churches, which have been providing support to affected families and vulnerable groups.

nnnn

In addition, the SACC affirmed its support for a coordinated response involving the South African Women in Dialogue (SAWID), partnering non-governmental organisations, independent human rights defenders and private sector collaborators. Churches and faith groups were encouraged to continue supporting these initiatives.

nnnn

Clergy and people of faith were further urged to offer pastoral care rooted in compassion, especially to families facing loss, displacement and fear.

nnnn

The SACC concluded by praying that God’s mercy and grace would continue to sustain the people of Limpopo and Mpumalanga during this difficult period.

nnnnnnnn

n

post_title: Police probe discovery of two bodies near Lily Mine
post_content:
n

Police  have launched an investigation following the discovery of two deceased men near Lily Mine in Low’s Creek on Tuesday morning.

nnnn

According to a media statement issued by the Office of the Provincial Commissioner, police received information at about 7am regarding two men who were suspected to be dead in the area. Officers responded to the scene together with Emergency Medical Services.

nnnn

On arrival, the men were found covered with blankets and were both certified dead at the scene.

nnnn

One of the deceased has since been positively identified by a relative, who confirmed that the man was his brother and that they originate from the Kingdom of Eswatini. Police are still working to establish the identity of the second deceased male and to locate his family.

nnnn

The circumstances surrounding the deaths are currently under investigation, and police have not yet released further details.

nnnn

Members of the public who may have information that could assist the investigation, or who know the relatives of the unidentified deceased, are urged to contact Crime Stop on 08600 10111. Information can also be submitted via the MySAPS App. Police have assured the public that all information will be treated with the strictest confidentiality, and callers may remain anonymous.

nnnnn

n

The Mpumalanga Department of Education has expressed shock and deep sadness following the tragic death of a 19-year-old Grade 11 learner at LD Moetanalo Secondary School in the Steve Tshwete Circuit 1, within the Steve Tshwete Local Municipality.

nnnn

The incident occurred on Tuesday, 20 January 2026, while learners were changing classes on the school premises. It is alleged that an altercation broke out between two learners, during which the victim was stabbed. Emergency medical personnel were called to the scene and later certified the learner deceased.

nnnn

School management acted promptly by informing the learner’s parents and reporting the matter to the South African Police Service. Police investigations are currently under way, and a fellow learner is alleged to be involved in the incident. The suspect reportedly fled the scene and is being sought by authorities.

nnnn

The Department of Education has strongly condemned the incident, emphasising that violence in schools poses a serious threat to the safety and wellbeing of learners, educators and support staff. Such acts also undermine the constitutional right to education and the creation of safe learning environments.

nnnn

In response to the tragedy, the MEC for Education in Mpumalanga, Ms Lindi Masina, is expected to visit the school and the bereaved family on Wednesday, 21 January 2026. The visit aims to convey condolences, assess the situation on the ground and receive a detailed report on the incident.

nnnn

Officials from the Department’s Inclusive Education and Wellness Unit have also been deployed to provide psychosocial support to learners, educators and staff affected by the incident.

nnnn

The Department has extended its heartfelt condolences to the family, friends and the entire LD Moetanalo Secondary School community during this painful time.

nnnn

May the learner’s soul rest in peace.

n

post_title: MEGA Responds to Floods Affecting Mpumalanga Economy
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga Economic Growth Agency (MEGA) has expressed deep concern for residents, families, and businesses affected by the recent severe floods across the province.

nnnn

The extreme weather has damaged key infrastructure, including roads, bridges, and transport routes, disrupting trade and supply chains for agriculture, retail, and industry. Hundreds of kilometres of road networks are affected, temporarily blocking access to important markets and slowing economic activity. Homes, businesses, and public facilities have also suffered significant damage.

nnnn

MEGA CEO Isaac Mahlangu said the agency is committed to supporting recovery efforts, including restoring infrastructure, market access, and affected enterprises. He emphasised collaboration with government, private sector partners, and communities to minimise long-term economic impacts.

nnnn

MEGA acknowledged President Cyril Ramaphosa’s visit to Nkomazi, highlighting national support for recovery, and praised disaster management teams and volunteers for their tireless efforts. Mahlangu urged stakeholders to focus on safety, resilience, and rebuilding, noting that together the province’s economy can be restored in a sustainable and inclusive manner.

nnnnnnn

post_title: Crocodile Bridge Gate to Reopen After Floods
post_content:
n

Following recent severe weather in parts of Limpopo and Mpumalanga, including areas within Kruger National Park (KNP), Crocodile Bridge Gate will reopen for day visitors from Thursday, 22 January 2026.

nnnn

Visitors are warned that conditions remain unpredictable. A dam wall outside the park has been reported as compromised, which could lead to sudden changes in access at Crocodile Bridge Gate. All gravel roads remain closed, and guests are strongly advised not to remove barricades, which are in place to protect public safety and park infrastructure.

nnnn

Malelane, Numbi, and Paul Kruger Gates remain open under an entry quota system, while Phabeni Gate stays closed. However, the southern and northern sections of the park are still cut off, making Tshokwane Picnic Site, Satara Rest Camp, and northern areas inaccessible.

nnnn

SANParks continues to monitor the situation and urges visitors to follow all instructions and signage for their safety. Guests are also encouraged to take their waste with them as operations remain under pressure following the flooding.

n

n

Heavy rains have left a trail of grief and destruction across Mpumalanga and Limpopo, turning once-familiar villages into scenes of loss, uncertainty and resilience. In Bushbuckridge and neighbouring areas, families are still counting the cost as floodwaters recede, revealing damaged homes, shattered belongings and lives forever changed.

nnnn

According to an update delivered this week by Minister of Human Settlements, Thembi Simelane, the human toll continues to rise. Limpopo has now recorded 18 fatalities, with six people still missing across Limpopo and Mpumalanga. In Mpumalanga alone, 20 lives have been lost. Behind each number is a story of a family waiting for answers, a community mourning one of its own.

nnnn

The physical damage is just as stark. In Limpopo, 1 942 houses have been damaged, while Mpumalanga has recorded 1 808 affected homes. Many of these are mud structures in rural villages, which stood little chance against relentless rains. For families who had already been living on the margins, the floods have deepened hardship and exposed long-standing vulnerabilities.

nnnn

Government teams are now racing against time and weather conditions to bring relief. Verification processes are under way to assess the extent of damage and determine appropriate assistance. Despite difficult conditions, the Department of Human Settlements has begun moving ahead with support for households already verified.

nnnn

Temporary Emergency Accommodation is being procured for families currently housed in evacuation and mass care centres. In a move that brings some relief closer to home, 73 Temporary Residential Units have been earmarked for Bushbuckridge, with additional units planned for Mbaula, Blouberg and Makhado. These structures are expected to offer affected families a measure of safety and dignity while longer-term solutions are developed.

nnnn

Over the coming days, national and provincial leaders will be on the ground in both provinces, working alongside local authorities to ensure aid reaches those who need it most. Yet, amid the devastation, there have been powerful moments of solidarity. Churches, community groups and NGOs have opened their doors, shared food, offered shelter and reminded many that they are not alone.

nnnn

As floodwaters fade from the roads and fields, the real work begins: rebuilding homes, restoring hope and ensuring communities are better protected against future disasters. For Bushbuckridge and many other towns, recovery will take time, but resilience, compassion and collective effort are already lighting the way forward.

n

n

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of the South African Police Service (SAPS) in Mpumalanga has welcomed the sentencing of a 57-year-old man convicted on four counts of murder.

nnnn

Africa Thembinkosi Shongwe was sentenced by the Breyten High Court sitting in Mbombela on Thursday, 22 January 2026, following a thorough investigation into the deaths of an adult woman and her three minor children.

nnnn

The court heard that on 25 February 2023, neighbours at Phola Park became concerned when a woman, known for escorting her children to and from school daily, was not seen that morning. After checking on her home, neighbours noticed worrying signs and immediately alerted the police.

nnnn

Upon entering the house, SAPS members discovered four deceased persons in two rooms. The victims were identified as the woman and her three children, including twin boys and a girl.

nnnn

A comprehensive investigation led to the arrest of Shongwe, a citizen of the Kingdom of Eswatini and the biological father of one of the children. He was charged with four counts of murder, as well as contravening South Africa’s Immigration Act for being in the country without valid documentation.

nnnn

Shongwe pleaded guilty to all charges on 19 January 2026. On sentencing, the court imposed life imprisonment on each of the four murder counts and declared him unfit to possess a firearm.

nnnn

Welcoming the outcome, Acting Provincial Commissioner Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi praised the cooperation between investigators, prosecutors and the judiciary. He also commended community members for their vigilance and swift action in reporting the matter to authorities.

nnnn

SAPS reiterated its commitment to protecting communities and ensuring that serious crimes are thoroughly investigated and successfully prosecuted.

nnnnnnnn

n

n

The Minister of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment, Willie Aucamp, has provided a comprehensive update on the impact of recent floods on the Kruger National Park and surrounding provinces, while announcing the establishment of the SANParks Kruger Recovery Fund to support long-term restoration efforts.

nnnn

Speaking on Thursday, 22 January 2026, the Minister said his recent visit to the flood-stricken park left a lasting impression on him, describing the scale of destruction as devastating. The severe weather has affected not only the Kruger National Park but large parts of Mpumalanga and Limpopo, where lives have been lost and homes and critical infrastructure damaged. He reaffirmed that the declaration of a National Disaster in terms of the Disaster Management Act of 2002 was both necessary and appropriate.

nnnn

In the Kruger National Park alone, damage to infrastructure is estimated to run into hundreds of millions of rand. Roads, bridges, water systems and electricity services have been severely affected, while staff villages and tourist accommodation have also suffered extensive damage. Despite the scale of destruction, the Minister highlighted that no lives were lost inside the park, crediting SANParks’ early warning systems and the swift response of park management and emergency services for the safe evacuation of all staff and visitors.

nnnnnnnn

The floods have had a significant impact on tourism operations. Fifteen camps remain closed, some of them completely inaccessible due to washed-away roads and bridges. Temporary gate closures are still in place in certain areas, limiting both day and overnight visits. Between 9 and 19 January 2026, the park recorded 24,073 guest entries, a decline of 41 per cent compared to the same period last year. The Minister warned that this will result in immediate to medium-term revenue losses, placing pressure on SANParks, which generates nearly 80 per cent of its operating budget through tourism.

nnnn

The latest floods have compounded challenges from previous flooding in 2023, from which the park was still recovering. According to the Minister, the combined impact has exceeded existing contingency and maintenance budgets, increasing the risk of prolonged recovery delays, environmental degradation and socio-economic consequences for surrounding communities.

nnnn

To address these challenges, the Minister confirmed the establishment of the SANParks Kruger Recovery Fund, which he said is essential to ensuring the long-term sustainability of the park as a national heritage asset and economic driver. The fund will be administered with strict fiduciary oversight through three independent audit firms on SANParks’ panel, providing transparency and accountability to donors.

nnnn

Support for the fund has already been received from across society, including pensioners, young people, and both local and international organisations. The SANParks Honorary Rangers will play a key role through their “Kruger Flood 2026 Fund” fundraising campaign, while internationally acclaimed author Tony Park has also committed to supporting the recovery efforts.

nnnn

The Minister cautioned the public that the SANParks Kruger Recovery Fund and the Honorary Rangers’ Kruger Flood 2026 Fund are the only legitimate channels authorised to receive donations, warning against the risk of fraudulent fundraising during times of crisis.

nnnn

Providing an update on conditions in the park, the Minister said several roads in both the northern and southern regions remain inaccessible, with multiple rest camps closed due to flood damage. While Malelane, Numbi and Paul Kruger gates remain open, access is controlled through an entry quota system, and the northern and southern regions of the park are still cut off from each other.

nnnn

Concluding his address, the Minister called on South Africans and the international community to support the recovery of the Kruger National Park. He emphasised that the park is not only a conservation area but an economic lifeline for the region and a symbol of South Africa’s natural heritage. As the park marks its centenary this year, he said collective action is vital to ensure it remains protected for future generations.

n

n

Police in Calcutta have launched a manhunt for suspects following a fatal shooting incident in the Tsemamarhumbu area on Wednesday evening, 22 January 2026.

nnnn

According to the South African Police Service (SAPS), officers were conducting routine patrols in the Mkhuhlu area at about 7.30pm when they received information about a shooting. Police immediately proceeded to the scene, where they discovered a white Isuzu bakkie with Mpumalanga registration plates riddled with bullet holes. The rear window of the vehicle had also been damaged.

nnnn

Inside the bakkie, police found the lifeless body of a 56-year-old man. Preliminary investigations revealed that the victim had just left his home and was attacked a few metres from his residence. Spent cartridges from a high-calibre firearm were also recovered at the scene.

nnnn

The motive for the killing is still unknown and forms part of the ongoing investigation. No arrests have been made at this stage.

nnnn

Police are appealing to members of the public who may have information that could assist the investigation to come forward. Anyone with information is urged to contact Detective Lieutenant Colonel Sikhumbuzo Ceko on 082 922 9902, call Crime Stop on 08600 10111, or submit tips via the MySAPS App. All information will be treated as confidential, and anonymity is guaranteed.

nnnn

Condemning the attack, Acting Provincial Commissioner of the SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, said police would work tirelessly to bring the perpetrators to justice. He described the incident as a senseless and violent act that has no place in communities.

nnnn

Investigations are continuing.

n

post_title: Photo 2 - Dr Bader Kazi of the Gift of the Givers Foundation offically hand over the food and personal hygiene parcels as well as blankets to Mr Oscar Mthimkhulu the KNP Managing Executive
Photo 1.1 - Mr Frank Weitsz explaining to Mr Oscar Mthimkhulu how to prepare the dehydrated soup, soya and carrots packs
Photo 2 - Dr Bader Kazi of the Gift of the Givers Foundation offically hand over the food and personal hygiene parcels as well as blankets to Mr Oscar Mthimkhulu the KNP Managing Executive

post_content:
n

Humanitarian aid has been received to support communities, staff and guests affected by recent flooding in and around the Kruger National Park (KNP).

nnnn

SANParks said the assistance includes food and personal hygiene parcels, water, blankets, cleaning materials, dehydrated soup hampers and financial support — all aimed at strengthening ongoing relief and recovery efforts in flood-hit areas.

nnnn

Support has so far been received from the SANParks Honorary Rangers, assisted by donations of funds and goods from local businesses including Checkers Nelspruit, Pick n Pay Nelspruit and Malelane, and Spar Nelspruit. Additional contributions have been made by Christian Aid Relief (CARE), the Gift of the Givers Foundation, DLS Safari, MUBZ Relief, Ford Nelspruit, and various private entities.

nnnn

Since 19 January 2026, approximately 1,500 hampers have been distributed to those most in need within the KNP, SANParks confirmed. The aid is intended to address immediate and urgent needs of vulnerable households, while also helping affected families regain stability in the weeks ahead.

nnnnnnnn

SANParks said the humanitarian support forms part of broader efforts to alleviate hardship, restore dignity and promote resilience within impacted communities inside the park and along the Kruger’s borders. The organisation reiterated its commitment to working with partners to ensure transparent, fair and efficient distribution of all donated resources.

nnnn

The relief drive comes as SANParks intensifies longer-term plans to rebuild damaged infrastructure and restore operations in areas affected by extreme weather. The park is also positioning these recovery measures within a wider conservation and climate-risk response, recognising that severe weather events are increasingly placing pressure on protected areas and the communities that depend on them.

nnnn

SANParks recently launched the Kruger Recovery Fund through the Minister of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment. The fund is intended to receive donations to support recovery and rebuilding projects within the park, with the aim of protecting KNP’s long-term sustainability as a national heritage asset, a major economic driver, and a symbol of South Africa’s commitment to conservation.

nnnn

SANParks thanked donors, partners and volunteers for their solidarity and continued support during what it described as a challenging period for the park and surrounding communities.

n

n

In Bushbuckridge, where ancestral knowledge remains a trusted source of care alongside clinics and hospitals, Lesaka La Dingaka is helping to bring two worlds of healing closer together.

nnnn

Founded in 2007 as a non-profit organisation, Lesaka La Dingaka promotes cooperation between Traditional Health Practitioners (THPs), faith-based healers and Western medical practitioners, working to ensure rural communities are not excluded from safe, coordinated healthcare.

nnnn

For many families in villages across Bushbuckridge, traditional healers are still the first point of contact during illness, distress or uncertainty. Lesaka La Dingaka was established to organise, educate and help regulate THPs, while building stronger working relationships with clinics, hospitals and key government partners, particularly the Department of Health.

nnnn

Leadership rooted in calling and community

nnnn

At local level, the organisation is coordinated by Dr MN Mnisi, the Mpumalanga Coordinator of Lesaka La Dingaka and a respected traditional health practitioner from Xanthia Village. He was initiated in 2010 at Cork Trust under Gobela Mpandezithi Mavis Mhangane, and is known for his commitment to both cultural responsibility and public health realities.

nnnn

At national level, Lesaka La Dingaka is led by Director Elizabeth Baas, initiated in 1989 by veteran traditional healer Nyoniyezwe Mkhabela. Mkhabela, born 16 April 1918, was initiated in 1974 and is still actively practising and training amathwasa, continuing to shape the generations that carry traditional healing forward.

nnnn

Building safe referral pathways

nnnn

A key focus of the organisation is education and patient safety. Lesaka La Dingaka trains THPs to recognise conditions that require urgent medical attention, and to confidently refer patients to clinics and hospitals when needed. This helps reduce delays in treatment and builds trust between communities and formal healthcare services.

nnnn

The organisation also raises awareness about the dangers of toxic and unregulated medicines, promoting responsible practices that protect lives.

nnnn

Care that goes beyond medicine

nnnn

Lesaka La Dingaka’s work extends into psycho-social support, connecting individuals and families to professional services when dealing with trauma, mental health concerns or social distress.

nnnn

It also supports vulnerable households through practical interventions, including meals for orphaned and vulnerable children and assistance to destitute community members. Through home visits, the organisation reaches the elderly, the ill and those who struggle to access formal services — offering dignity, guidance and human connection.

nnnn

Prevention, awareness and community education

nnnn

Lesaka La Dingaka promotes a drug-free environment and speaks out against substance abuse through community dialogues and education. It also addresses HIV and AIDS, TB, STIs, cancer and mental health in culturally sensitive ways that encourage early intervention and reduce stigma.

nnnn

Strengthening unity among healers

nnnn

To improve coordination and accountability, the organisation is developing a database of Traditional Health Practitioners and hosting regular engagements where healers can share knowledge, align practices and strengthen cooperation with clinics and hospitals.

nnnn

A local symbol of unity

nnnn

In Bushbuckridge and across Mpumalanga, Lesaka La Dingaka continues to show that true wellness is strongest when tradition and modern medicine work side by side — placing the wellbeing of communities at the centre of every decision.

n

post_title: Gogo Nonyane’s message for the week 26 – 01 February
post_content:
n

Eish, my child, the sky is busy-busy. The constellations are moving like people at a taxi rank — everyone trying to arrive at their destination. This week asks for clear words, clean intentions, and steady feet. If you rush, you will spill your own tea. If you listen, the stars will whisper the right direction.

nnnn

♈ Aries

nnnnnnnn

Aries, you are burning like a small fire that wants to become a big one. But remember: even fire needs a proper hearth. This week, choose one goal and give it your full spirit. In love and family matters, speak softly — your tone can cut like a knife without you noticing. Work matters favour courage, but not stubbornness. When the Ram constellation stands tall, it reminds you: lead, but don’t push people off the mountain.

nnnn

♉ Taurus

nnnnnnnn

Taurus, the Bull does not run for every sound. This week you must protect your energy from noise and gossip. Money matters improve when you stop “helping” with your pocket where your heart is not respected. You may be asked to fix someone’s mess — decide if it is your responsibility or your habit. In relationships, consistency will win more than sweet words. The stars say: build slowly, but build properly.

nnnn

♊ Gemini

nnnnnnnn

Gemini, your mind is quick like birds in the morning — but too many birds make too much sound. This week, focus on one conversation at a time. There is good news around work, studies, or a message you have been waiting for. Do not over-explain yourself; the right people will understand. Love improves when you stop testing others and start trusting your own intuition. The Twins constellation says: balance your two sides, not fight them.

nnnn

♋ Cancer

nnnnnnnn

Cancer, your heart is deep like the river after rain. This week you may feel emotional, but it is not weakness — it is information. Something at home or in family life needs attention: a boundary, a repair, or a truth. Work moves slowly, but steadily, like a tortoise that still reaches the gate. If you are single, someone notices your kindness — but don’t mother people who must grow themselves. The Crab constellation says: protect your softness, but don’t hide forever.

nnnn

♌ Leo

nnnnnnnn

Leo, your spirit wants to shine, kodwa people must not be blinded by your light. This week brings recognition if you stop waiting for permission. A leadership moment comes — take it, but share credit. In love, someone needs reassurance, not performance. Money matters: avoid impulse spending that is really you trying to “feel better”. The Lion constellation reminds you: true royalty is calm.

nnnn

♍ Virgo

nnnnnnnn

Virgo, you are seeing details others are missing — and yes, you are right, kodwa being right must still be useful. This week is good for planning, cleaning up paperwork, finishing what has been hanging. Your body also speaks: rest, water, and routine will help your mind. In relationships, don’t correct people when what they need is comfort. The Maiden constellation says: make order, not pressure.

nnnn

♎ Libra

nnnnnnnn

Libra, balance is your gift, but this week you must stop balancing people who are leaning too hard on you. Choose fairness, yes — but also choose yourself. A partnership decision comes: business or love. The stars favour agreements made clearly, in writing, with expectations set. Romance improves when you speak directly instead of hinting. The Scales constellation says: peace is not silence; peace is truth handled gently.

nnnn

♏ Scorpio

nnnnnnnn

Scorpio, your intuition is strong this week — like you can smell lies before they arrive. Use that power for protection, not revenge. Something hidden becomes clear: a motive, a feeling, a plan. At work, you are respected more than you think, but don’t fight every battle. In love, intimacy grows when you stop testing loyalty and start communicating fear. The Scorpion constellation says: transform, don’t destroy.

nnnn

♐ Sagittarius

nnnnnnnn

Sagittarius, your feet want to travel — even if it’s just your mind travelling ahead of your body. This week brings opportunities through learning, networking, and new ideas. Say yes to the invitation that grows you. But be careful: over-promising will embarrass you later. In relationships, you need freedom, but don’t use freedom as an excuse to be inconsistent. The Archer constellation says: aim carefully before you release the arrow.

nnnn

♑ Capricorn

nnnnnnnn

Capricorn, you are climbing, and people can see it. This week favours career moves, structure, and long-term planning. Someone may come to you for guidance — give wisdom, but don’t carry their load. Finances improve when you cut one unnecessary expense. In love, soften your face, my child — not everyone is your competitor. The Goat constellation says: discipline is your magic, but tenderness is your medicine.

nnnn

♒ Aquarius

nnnnnnnn

Aquarius, the sky is stirring your rebellious spirit. This week you may feel “tired of the same old story” — good. It is time for a different chapter. New friends, new collaborations, or a new approach to your work can unlock momentum. Be mindful of emotional distance in relationships; people want to feel you, not just understand you. The Water-Bearer constellation says: your ideas are a blessing when they are shared with heart.

nnnn

♓ Pisces

nnnnnnnn

Pisces, your dreams are talking loudly. This week favours creativity, healing, prayer, and quiet reflection. But don’t escape reality — shape it gently, like clay. If you’ve been feeling drained, check your boundaries: you may be giving too much to people who only take. In love, romance blooms when you stop idealising and start seeing. The Fish constellation says: flow, but don’t drown.

n

n

ANC President Cyril Ramaphosa has told the party’s top leadership that the organisation must shift “decisively from talk to implementation”, warning that South Africans want visible change, not speeches and slogans.

nnnn

Ramaphosa delivered the closing remarks at the ANC’s National Executive Committee (NEC) Lekgotla in Boksburg, held at the Birchwood Hotel and OR Tambo Conference Centre between 24 and 26 January 2026. The gathering brought together senior leaders to receive reports from commissions and map out priorities and work plans for the year ahead.

nnnn

According to the ANC leader, the reports presented at the lekgotla set out what must be done, and include timelines for delivery. He said the party must focus on practical changes that improve people’s lives — from how government programmes are implemented to how officials are held accountable for results.

nnnn

In a strong message on internal governance, Ramaphosa emphasised the need to deploy capable people into positions of responsibility, saying those appointed must be able to fulfil the duties of their offices. He also said monitoring mechanisms would be strengthened so that decisions are based on evidence rather than factional or personal interests.

nnnn

The remarks come amid mounting public frustration over slow service delivery, as communities across the country continue to face challenges such as water interruptions, failing infrastructure, crime and unemployment. Ramaphosa’s message to the party was that credibility will be rebuilt through measurable performance, not promises.

nnnn

The ANC’s public communications around the lekgotla stressed execution and accountability, with commission work intended to consolidate policy direction and implementation plans.

nnnn

For communities, including those in Mpumalanga, the real test will be whether the commitments discussed in Boksburg translate into improved services on the ground — and whether underperforming officials face consequences when targets are missed

n

n

The Mpumalanga Department of Education has strongly refuted allegations of wastage and irregular procurement relating to its e-learning devices programme, following reports published by City Press and News24.

nnnn

In a statement issued on 26 January 2026, the Department said the claims misrepresent the facts surrounding the Ubuhlebuzile E-Learning Programme, which was introduced in 2022 as a phased and strategic intervention to improve teaching and learning across the province.

nnnn

According to the Department, 64 000 tablets were procured in 2022 for Grade 12 learners under a three-year SITA-facilitated contract valued at R224 million, which included a three-year warranty. Bongani Rainmaker Limited (BRL) was appointed as the supplier in full compliance with government procurement regulations.

nnnn

In 2025, these devices were replaced with 60 000 Packard Bell tablets at a cost of R232 million, also inclusive of a three-year warranty. The Department confirmed that the tablets were successfully distributed to Grade 12 learners in quintile 1 to 3 schools and stated that it has received no verified reports of widespread device failure.

nnnn

The Department further attributed the improvement in Grade 12 results — from 79% in 2023 to 86.55% in 2025 — partly to the effective use of e-learning tools introduced through the programme.

nnnn

It rejected claims that the Packard Bell tablets constituted wastage, explaining that the devices issued to the 2025 Grade 12 cohort have been retrieved, reformatted and reloaded with updated content. They will be re-issued to the 2026 Grade 12 learners as part of a cost-efficient and sustainable approach.

nnnn

Looking ahead, the Department confirmed that it has placed an order for 70 000 Windows-based tablet notebooks for Grade 10 learners in 2026, at a cost of R330 million — not R600 million as alleged. These devices will be retained by learners from Grade 10 through to Grade 12, with content updated remotely to reduce future logistics and redistribution costs.

nnnn

The procurement process, facilitated through BRL, allows the service provider to source Department-approved devices, load educational content and manage distribution. Funding is drawn from a dedicated e-learning budget, supplemented by the Learning and Teaching Support Material (LTSM) allocation.

nnnn

For the 2025/26 financial year, the Department allocated R717 million to the e-learning programme, covering both Grade 10 and Grade 12 learners.

nnnn

The Department reiterated that all procurement processes were lawful, strategic and focused on improving learner outcomes, adding that allegations of inflated costs, wastage or non-functional devices are misleading and incorrect.

nnnn

It reaffirmed its commitment to transparency, accountability and the effective use of technology to advance quality education throughout Mpumalanga.

nnnn

n
nn

n

Police in Bushbuckridge have arrested a 43-year-old man for possession of an unlicensed firearm and ammunition following a public disturbance along the R40 road in Dwarsloop.

nnnn

The incident occurred on Monday, 26 January 2026, when groups of community members blocked sections of the R40 at Dwarsloop, GA Beretta and GA Relane. According to police, truck drivers were allegedly forced to park across the road, blocking traffic, while their vehicle keys were confiscated.

nnnn

Police were dispatched to the scene, where they engaged with the group and monitored the situation. While on duty, officers received further information about another group disrupting traffic at a stop-and-go section on an uphill stretch of the road. Police responded promptly and dispersed the group from the roadway.

nnnn

During the operation, officers observed one individual carrying a firearm. The suspect was arrested after failing to produce a valid firearm licence. A firearm with its serial number filed off, as well as 12 live rounds of ammunition, were confiscated.

nnnn

The suspect has been charged with possession of an unlicensed firearm and ammunition and was expected to appear before the Bushbuckridge Magistrate’s Court on Tuesday, 27 January 2026.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of the SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, commended the officers for their swift and professional response. He said the arrest sends a strong message that lawlessness and illegal possession of firearms will not be tolerated, urging communities to raise concerns through lawful channels and work with police to ensure peace and stability.

nnnn

n

n

Police in Mpumalanga have arrested two suspects following the recovery of an unlicensed firearm in the Timbavati Trust area of Acornhoek.

nnnn

The arrests were made on Monday, 26 January 2026, after police received a tip-off about a suspect allegedly in possession of an illegal firearm. While conducting patrols, officers identified a suspect matching the description provided by the informant.

nnnn

Further investigation led police to a parked taxi, where a search was carried out. During the search, a firearm was discovered inside the vehicle and confiscated. The taxi driver was also arrested in connection with the incident.

nnnn

Both suspects have been charged with possession of an unlicensed firearm and were expected to appear before the Acornhoek Magistrate’s Court on Tuesday, 27 January 2026.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of the SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, reiterated that the recovery of illegal firearms remains a priority, as such weapons are often used in serious and violent crimes. He also urged community members to continue working with police by reporting criminal activities.

nnnn

n

n

The Mpumalanga Department of Health has introduced three full-time medical doctors at community health centres in Bushbuckridge as part of efforts to strengthen primary healthcare services.

nnnn

On 26 January 2026, the MEC for Health, Ms Sasekani Manzini, visited Hluvukani, Dwarsloop and Oakley Community Health Centres where the newly appointed doctors were officially introduced to staff and community members. Dr G Moripa has been stationed at Hluvukani CHC, Dr E Ngomana at Dwarsloop CHC and Dr NP Nyambi at Oakley CHC.

nnnn

The strategic placement of doctors at primary healthcare facilities aims to support the implementation of the National Health Insurance (NHI) and advance universal health coverage. This initiative seeks to ensure that communities have improved and consistent access to quality primary healthcare services close to where they live.

nnnn

The department highlighted that strengthening primary healthcare is key to improving life expectancy, enhancing clinical governance and raising the quality of care at the first point of contact. The presence of doctors at clinics is also expected to reduce unnecessary referrals and self-referrals to hospitals, while improving early diagnosis, timely treatment and continuity of care.

nnnnnnnn

During her engagement, the MEC urged community members to support and respect the doctors, emphasising the importance of building strong, trust-based relationships between patients and healthcare professionals. Such relationships, she noted, are vital for better health outcomes, increased patient satisfaction and improved adherence to treatment.

nnnn

The MEC also encouraged residents who have tested HIV-negative to access lenacapavir, which will be rolled out as part of HIV prevention efforts. Community members were further urged to regularly check their health status for early diagnosis and treatment, and those who have tested positive for TB or HIV were encouraged to return to health facilities to collect their treatment.

nnnn

Community members who attended the events welcomed the initiative, expressing appreciation for the deployment of full-time doctors at local clinics. They noted that the move will reduce the need for long and costly trips to hospitals, allowing residents to receive timely medical care within their own communities.
