post_title: Bheki Nyathikazi: Voice for public service
post_content:
n

In Mpumalanga’s noisy information space, where rumours travel faster than facts and headlines often outrun context, Bheki Nyathikazi represents a quieter but essential craft: the discipline of communication as public service.

nnnn

Nyathikazi serves as Media Liaison Officer in the Communication Services unit within Mpumalanga’s Department of Agriculture, Rural Development, Land and Environmental Affairs (DARDLEA). That job title sounds administrative until you consider what it demands in practice: translating government processes into language communities can trust, correcting misinformation without inflaming tensions, and ensuring that public programmes do not remain invisible simply because they were poorly explained.

nnnn

What makes Nyathikazi notable is that he is not “just” a spokesperson. He is also a communications practitioner and former journalist, writing publicly in his personal capacity. That background matters. It suggests an understanding of how newsrooms work, how audiences receive information, and how quickly credibility can be lost when communication becomes defensive, vague, or overly polished.

nnnn

His writing and public commentary reflect a preoccupation with standards: what journalism should be, what public debate should look like, and what community life can become when neglect is normalised. On Mail & Guardian’s platform, he has tackled issues as practical as the condition of taxi ranks and as principled as interview ethics and fairness in the media. These are not “safe” topics; they are the kinds of conversations that force institutions, professionals and the public to look in the mirror.

nnnn

In a recent online exchange about the pressures facing newsrooms, Nyathikazi argued for deeper, more human storytelling—work that does not simply chase what is already trending. For community journalism in places like Bushbuckridge, that idea lands with weight. Our strongest stories are rarely the loudest. They are the ones that explain the “why”, elevate ordinary people, and hold power to account without reducing communities to crises.

nnnn

The challenge, of course, is that communication in government is only valuable when it is timely, transparent and measurable. A media liaison officer can open doors, but departments must keep those doors open with consistent information, accessible channels, and respect for the public’s right to know.

nnnn

Nyathikazi’s career arc—journalism into public-sector communications—suggests a belief that words can still improve the lived reality of communities. In a province that often battles with service-delivery frustrations and distrust, that belief is not sentimental. It is strategic.

n

post_title: Stricter Online Safety Measures for Children
post_content:
n

South Africa is considering tougher measures to safeguard children online, including the criminalisation of exposing minors to pornographic material.

nnnn

The proposals form part of the Draft White Paper on Audio and Audiovisual Media Services and Online Safety, currently under consideration by the Department of Communications and Digital Technologies. Departmental spokesperson Tlangelani Manganyi said the measures are aimed at strengthening protections for children in an increasingly digital world.

nnnn

According to Manganyi, the proposed interventions seek to shield children from harmful content that could negatively affect their physical, mental or moral development. “The intention is to ensure that children are not exposed to disturbing and harmful material, or prematurely introduced to adult experiences,” he said.

nnnn

The move comes amid a global push for stricter online safety regulations for children. Australia recently introduced the world’s first ban on social media use for children under the age of 16. In Europe, France has passed legislation restricting access to certain websites for children under 15.

nnnn

Social media platforms are also facing mounting pressure from regulators. TikTok has announced that it will begin rolling out new age-detection technology across Europe as part of efforts to identify and remove users under the age of 13. Meanwhile, the European Parliament is advocating for mandatory age limits on social media platforms, and Denmark has proposed a ban on social media use for children under 15.

nnnn

In the United Kingdom, a pilot programme aimed at enforcing age restrictions has already resulted in the removal of thousands of users found to be under the age of 13.

nnnn

Manganyi emphasised that South Africa’s approach would build on the existing mandate of the Film and Publication Board (FPB). “The FPB currently regulates the creation, production, possession and distribution of films, games and certain publications to provide consumer advice that enables people to make informed viewing, reading and gaming choices for themselves and for children in their care,” he said.

nnnn

The proposed changes signal a stronger stance by government to adapt legislation to the realities of digital media and online platforms, while placing the protection and wellbeing of children at the centre of policy development.

nnnn

Public consultations on the Draft White Paper are expected to guide the final shape of the proposed regulations.

nnnn

n

n

The Bushbuckridge community is in mourning following the passing of Councillor and ANC Branch Secretary for Ward 3, Comrade Mohammed Male, on 28 January 2026 after a brief illness.

nnnn

Cde Male served his community with dedication, integrity and compassion, holding both the role of Branch Secretary and Ward Councillor in the Bushbuckridge Local Municipality. Known for his calm nature and humility, he earned the respect of colleagues and residents alike, leaving a lasting legacy through his leadership and commitment to public service.

nnnn

The ANC in Ehlanzeni Region expressed its shock and sorrow, extending heartfelt condolences to his family, friends and comrades. “An uncompromised member of the movement of the people, Cde Male served with diligence and left a meaningful mark on the community,” the party said.

nnnn

Residents and colleagues have shared tributes online, remembering Cde Male as a devoted family man, a man of faith, and a leader who treated everyone with dignity. “His calm nature, kindness and willingness to serve will be remembered by all who worked with him,” one community member posted on social media. Many highlighted the positive impact he made in Ward 3 despite his term being cut short.

nnnn

The community is encouraged to keep his family and loved ones in their thoughts during this difficult time. Councillor Mohammed Male’s service and legacy in Ward 3 will not be forgotten.

nnnn

post_title: Road Safety Efforts Reduce Fatalities in Ehlanzeni
post_content:
n

Bushbuckridge, Ehlanzeni – Mpumalanga’s festive season road safety campaign has shown promising results in the Ehlanzeni District, which includes Bushbuckridge, even as the province mourns lives lost elsewhere.

nnnn

Addressing the province’s 2024/2025 festive season statistics at Protea Hotel in Mbombela, the MEC for Community Safety, Security and Liaison, Jackie Macie, MPL, highlighted the impact of coordinated law-enforcement efforts. Ehlanzeni was the only district in the province to record a reduction in road fatalities, with deaths declining from 39 to 33.

nnnn

The R40, Bushbuckridge’s main thoroughfare, was identified as one of the high-risk routes where eleven lives were lost province-wide, mostly due to speeding, reckless driving, and fatigue. To combat this, authorities increased visibility along key routes, established vehicle checkpoints, and conducted stop-and-search operations, particularly around border-linked areas.

nnnn

During the festive period, the focus in Ehlanzeni included border-related crime, illegal immigration, and road safety. The operations resulted in 506 arrests, including 43 for illegal immigration and numerous National Road Traffic Act violations.

nnnn

“Road safety is a shared responsibility,” MEC Macie stressed. “Motorists, passengers, and pedestrians all play a role. Every life lost is one too many.”

nnnn

The provincial government urges residents of Bushbuckridge and surrounding areas to respect traffic laws, avoid speeding, and speak out against reckless driving to ensure that the R40 and other roads become safer for all.

n

post_title: Reserve Bank Holds Interest Rates Steady at 6.75%
post_content:
n

The South African Reserve Bank’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has decided to keep the repo rate unchanged at 6.75%, meaning the prime lending rate remains at 10.25%.

nnnn

The decision was taken during this week’s MPC meeting, where four members voted to hold the rate steady, while two supported a 25-basis-point cut. The outcome comes after annual headline consumer inflation edged slightly higher to 3.6% in December.

nnnn

Reserve Bank Governor Lesetja Kganyago described 2025 as a “watershed year” for South Africa’s economy, despite ongoing global uncertainty.

nnnn

“Despite a volatile global backdrop, there was significant progress on domestic reforms, including a new inflation target,” Kganyago said. “These efforts have been rewarded with lower borrowing costs, a rapid decline in inflation expectations, and steadier growth.”

nnnn

For households and businesses carrying debt, the decision brings some relief, as monthly loan repayments will not increase. However, some economists believe there was room for a small interest rate cut to further support economic growth.

nnnn

Kganyago said the MPC remains focused on stabilising inflation at 3% over the next few years. He cautioned that in a less favourable scenario, inflation could peak at around 4%, with a slower return to the target.

nnnn

“In such a case, interest rates would remain largely unchanged in the near term, with the move towards a neutral level delayed by about a year,” he said.

nnnn

For local communities, the steady interest rate offers short-term certainty, while the broader focus remains on controlling inflation and supporting sustainable economic growth.

nnnn

n

post_title: KNP Access Improves After Severe Weather
post_content:
n

Some roads and tourism facilities in the Kruger National Park (KNP) have reopened following severe weather, but several restrictions remain in place as recovery and repair work continues.

nnnn

In an update issued on Friday, 30 January 2026, SANParks said conditions have improved and key assessments have been completed, allowing limited access to resume in some areas. However, closures and travel limits remain in place for safety reasons.

nnnn

Phalaborwa Gate will open to day visitors from Saturday, 31 January 2026, but travellers entering through this gate may only proceed as far as Satara Rest Camp. Pafuri Gate is open, although the Pafuri Border Post remains closed.

nnnn

In the northern region, Letaba and Olifants Rest Camps remain closed. Mopani Rest Camp is open, but SANParks said it can only be accessed via Punda Maria Gate, not Phalaborwa Gate. Visitors are advised to bring their own supplies as the restaurant at Mopani is closed.

nnnn

At Shingwedzi, only the shop and restaurant are open, while the rest camp remains closed until further notice. Bateleur is currently the only bush camp open in the north. Sirheni, Shimuwini and Tsendze remain closed.

nnnn

South of the park, the Sabie River and Sand River bridges are now accessible, improving travel routes between major camps. SANParks also confirmed that Tshokwane and Nkhuhlu picnic sites are open, but with limited menu options. Boulders Bush Camp is closed, and Orpen Gate remains closed until further notice

post_title: South Africa’s prisons under strain from overcrowding
post_content:
n

South Africa’s correctional facilities continue to face severe overcrowding, with more than 170,000 inmates detained nationwide during the recent festive season, far exceeding the system’s approved capacity.

nnnn

The Department of Correctional Services (DCS) has confirmed that prisons across the country are designed to accommodate just over 107,000 inmates. This means tens of thousands of offenders are being housed in facilities already stretched beyond their intended limits, placing immense pressure on infrastructure and staff.

nnnn

Addressing a media briefing on Monday, Correctional Services Commissioner Samuel Thobakgale said the current situation represents the highest prison population recorded in recent years.

nnnn

“This level of incarceration has placed immense pressure on infrastructure, staffing, security management and the department’s budget,” Thobakgale said. He added that the strain was worsened by reduced court activity during the festive season, which slows down the movement of cases and the release of eligible offenders.

nnnn

According to Thobakgale, overcrowding affects almost every aspect of the correctional system, from the safety of inmates and officials to the effective delivery of rehabilitation programmes.

nnnn

“The prisons are overburdened. The numbers continue to increase, and this reflects the effectiveness of the Justice, Crime Prevention and Security (JCPS) cluster — particularly the police, prosecution and the courts,” he said. “However, it also places additional weight on the correctional system in terms of managing the growing inmate population.”

nnnn

While the DCS has previously implemented measures such as parole placements, bail reviews and alternative sentencing to ease congestion, overcrowding remains a persistent challenge.

nnnn

Experts have long warned that overcrowded prisons can lead to increased violence, health risks and reduced opportunities for rehabilitation, ultimately undermining efforts to reduce reoffending.

nnnn

The department has reiterated its commitment to working with other justice stakeholders to find long-term solutions, including improved case flow management and the expansion of non-custodial sentencing where appropriate.

nnnn

As inmate numbers continue to rise, calls are growing for a more balanced approach that prioritises public safety while ensuring the correctional system remains humane, secure and sustainable.

nnnn

n

post_title: Fuel price relief as petrol dips
post_content:
n

Motorists will get another measure of relief at filling stations from Wednesday, 4 February 2026, after government confirmed a fresh round of fuel price cuts.

nnnn

The Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources said both grades of petrol will drop by 65 cents a litre, while diesel will decrease by between 50 cents and 57 cents a litre, depending on the grade.

nnnn

For many households, the biggest immediate benefit may be in transport and essential goods. Lower diesel costs can ease pressure on distribution, farming operations, and the taxi industry — although price changes in fares and deliveries are not always immediate and often depend on individual operators’ cost structures.

nnnn

The department also announced changes to other energy products used by households. Illuminating paraffin at the retail level will decrease by 70 cents a litre, offering some relief to families who rely on paraffin for cooking and heating. However, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) will increase by 31 cents per kilogramme nationally, and by 36 cents in the Western Cape, which could offset some of the gains for homes and small businesses that cook with gas.

nnnn

Department spokesperson Robert Maake said the latest adjustment follows shifts in both local and international market factors. A stronger South African rand against the United States dollar helped cushion prices, while average international refined product prices moved lower due to improved inventory availability — even as crude oil prices increased on average during the same period.

nnnn

With budgets still tight for many families, the reduction will be welcomed — especially for commuters and businesses that depend on road transport. The department urged consumers to note that the new prices apply from Wednesday and will reflect at the pumps once the official adjustment takes effect.

post_title: Mozambican National Jailed for Drug Trafficking
post_content:
n

A 39-year-old Mozambican national has been sentenced to ten years’ imprisonment for drug trafficking following his arrest at the Lebombo Port of Entry in Mpumalanga.

nnnn

According to the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation (the Hawks), the operation unfolded in June 2024 when members of the South African Police Service intercepted a minibus entering South Africa from Mozambique. The vehicle was found to be carrying 17 containers of crystal methamphetamine weighing a total of 17 kilograms, with an estimated street value of R4.25 million.

nnnn

The accused, Jorge Salomao Chimene, was the sole occupant of the minibus. The drugs were concealed in various compartments of the vehicle, including inside speakers, indicating an intention to smuggle the narcotics into the country.

nnnn

Following his arrest, the case was handed over to the Hawks’ Serious Organised Crime Investigation unit based in Nelspruit. Investigators successfully opposed bail after presenting evidence that the drugs were destined for distribution within South Africa.

nnnn

Chimene appeared in court on Thursday, 29 January 2026, where he pleaded guilty to possession of drugs. He was sentenced to ten years’ imprisonment, with seven years suspended for three years on condition that he is not convicted of a similar offence during that period. This means he will serve an effective three years behind bars.

nnnn

The Provincial Head of the Hawks in Mpumalanga, Major General Nico Gerber, welcomed the sentence, saying it sent a strong message to those involved in drug trafficking. He described the distribution of drugs as a serious crime that destroys lives and communities.

nnnn

Police have reiterated their commitment to combating cross-border drug trafficking and protecting communities from the harmful effects of illegal substances.

n

post_title: Parliament’s Ad Hoc Committee Moves on Ramaphosa
post_content:
n

Cape Town — South Africa’s Parliament is preparing to send written questions to President Cyril Ramaphosa amid ongoing controversy over allegations of political interference in the criminal justice system. The Ad Hoc Committee investigating testimony about the disbanded Political Killings Task Team (PKTT) agreed to commission its legal advisers to draft a set of questions for the President. 

nnnn

The decision follows a tense virtual meeting on Monday, during which committee members debated whether Mr Ramaphosa should be summoned to testify in person. Several witnesses during earlier hearings referenced the President in connection with decisions taken over the PKTT, which was established to investigate assassinations of political figures and community leaders in KwaZulu-Natal. 

nnnn

EFF leader Julius Malema, who sits on the committee, argued that Mr Ramaphosa should face the same scrutiny as any other witness. “Anything else that Madlanga was subjected to, the President can be subjected to,” Mr Malema said, emphasising that parliamentary processes, not party hierarchies, should determine proceedings. 

nnnn

Soviet Lekganyane, the committee chairperson, stressed that due process would guide the committee’s next steps. Members will have an opportunity to contribute to the list of written questions, and any further action — including whether the President might be asked to appear in person — will depend on the responses received. 

nnnn

The PKTT’s disbandment on 31 December 2024 has sparked deep controversy. Suspended Police Minister Senzo Mchunu testified that he briefed President Ramaphosa on the decision and that the President agreed with it, a claim that has fuelled calls for further clarification. Other witnesses, including KwaZulu-Natal Police Commissioner Lieutenant-General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi, suggested that Mr Ramaphosa may not have been fully informed before the task team was dissolved. 

nnnn

Other testimony has highlighted contradictions within the South African Police Service (SAPS) about whether the PKTT was formally disbanded at all, and concerns have been raised about delays in investigations into politically linked killings. 

nnnn

The committee’s work is part of a broader inquiry into allegations of corruption and political interference in law enforcement agencies. It has already questioned senior figures including Mr Mchunu and the head of the National Prosecuting Authority, Advocate Shamila Batohi, as part of a series of hearings that aim to restore public confidence in the justice system. 

nnnn

As the draft questions are finalised and sent to the Presidency, national attention will remain on how executive accountability and parliamentary oversight interact in one of South Africa’s most sensitive political investigations in recent years.

n

post_title: Flood repairs open key Kruger routes
post_content:
n

Visitors to Kruger National Park are beginning to see improved access after the severe January 2026 floods, which damaged roads, bridges, tourism facilities and staff accommodation across the park.

nnnn

In an update issued on Monday, 2 February 2026, SANParks confirmed that restoration work is continuing, with visitor safety remaining the top priority.

nnnn

The park’s H7 Route between Orpen Gate and Satara Rest Camp has now reopened to traffic. However, motorists have been cautioned to proceed with extreme care near the Nsemani Dam area, where flood damage has left only a single lane accessible. Heavy vehicles exceeding eight tonnes are not permitted through the affected section.

nnnn

To maintain movement while repairs and reconstruction continue, the parks authority said it is building a bypass using the S12 and S40 routes. This alternative route is expected to support accessibility during ongoing work at the dam area.

nnnn

Several visitor sites have also reopened as of Monday. These include Tsendze Rustic Camp near Mopani Rest Camp, the Masorini Ruins near Phalaborwa Gate, as well as the Mooiplaas Picnic Site and Babalala Picnic Site picnic sites.

nnnn

SANParks reminded visitors that gravel roads marked “No Entry” must not be used under any circumstances. Access at Orpen Gate has also been opened to Open Safari Vehicles, though a quota system will apply to manage traffic volumes and keep visitors safe.

n

n

Operation Shanela II has delivered significant law-enforcement gains across Mpumalanga, with hundreds of arrests and major confiscations recorded between 29 January and 1 February 2026.

nnnn

The multi-agency operation, coordinated by the South African Police Service (SAPS), brought together Traffic Police, law-enforcement agencies, the South African National Defence Force, the Department of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs, private security and Community Policing Forums.

nnnn

During the operation, officers searched 399 premises, stopped and searched more than 3,000 people and over 1,200 vehicles, and conducted extensive patrols, roadblocks and checkpoints across the province. Detectives also traced 11 wanted suspects, while specialised teams carried out tracking operations and hostel searches.

nnnn

Compliance inspections formed a key part of the operation. Police closed one unlicensed liquor outlet and inspected more than 220 licensed outlets. Inspections were also carried out at second-hand dealers, scrap yards, firearm-holding institutions, farms, mines and both formal and informal businesses to ensure compliance with labour and safety laws.

nnnn

Arrests were made for a wide range of serious offences, including murder, attempted murder, rape, armed robbery, carjacking, assault and burglary. Police also arrested suspects for drug-related crimes, illegal possession of firearms and ammunition, dealing in illicit liquor, driving under the influence, and immigration offences. In total, more than 100 undocumented immigrants were detained.

nnnn

Large quantities of drugs were seized, including over two tonnes of dagga, along with crack cocaine, crystal meth, nyaope and mandrax. Police also confiscated firearms, ammunition, dangerous weapons, fireworks, illegal cigarettes, contraband goods, copper cables and several vehicles.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner of SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, praised the operation’s outcomes, saying the results demonstrated the impact of integrated, intelligence-driven policing.

nnnn

“These outcomes send a strong message that crime will not be tolerated. We remain resolute in our mandate to protect the people of Mpumalanga and uphold the rule of law,” he said.

nnnn

Police have indicated that similar high-impact operations will continue as part of ongoing efforts to improve safety and restore order in communities across the province.

post_title: Families of Lily Mine Victims Renew Call for Justice
post_content:
n

Ten years after the Lily Mine collapse, the families of Pretty Nkambule, Yvonne Mnisi, and Solomon Nyirenda have lodged a formal complaint with the South African Human Rights Commission (SAHRC). They accuse the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) and the Department of Mineral Resources and Energy of failing to act on the findings of the 2017 Nelspruit Magistrate’s Court inquiry.

nnnn

Family spokesperson Harry Mazibuko said: “The tragedy was preventable and arose from negligence. The inquiry recommended criminal accountability, yet no decisive action has been taken.” The families are still waiting for the retrieval of their loved ones’ remains.

nnnn

ActionSA, led by Herman Mashaba, stood with the families on 5 February 2026, marking the tenth anniversary and renewing calls for justice. An inquest found that mine management failed in risk assessments, while authorities failed to curb illegal mining, contributing to the collapse.

nnnn

Mashaba said: “Three people vanished, and if we think it only happened to these families, it could happen to yours tomorrow. Lily Mine must remain top of mind.”

nnnn

The SAHRC is expected to investigate whether the NPA and Department of Mineral Resources have failed in their duties, while the families continue to demand accountability.

post_title: Tourism Sector Steps Up for Kruger Flood Recovery

“The park belongs to all South Africans, and it is our collective responsibility to protect this national treasure during its milestone year.”

nnnn

Members of the public and businesses wishing to assist can make donations directly to the SANParks Honorary Rangers Flood Disaster Relief Fund. Contributions of any size will help ensure that Kruger National Park continues to thrive for generations to come.

The South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) has suspended more than 70,000 social grant payments after beneficiaries were found to be non-compliant during a national eligibility review process.

nnnn

The agency confirmed that a total of 240,000 social grant payments were reviewed as part of efforts to ensure that all recipients still qualify for assistance based on their current financial and personal circumstances. The review process was conducted in cooperation with the National Student Financial Aid Scheme (NSFAS) and the South African Revenue Service (SARS), allowing for cross-checking of income, student funding and employment data.

nnnn

SASSA leadership briefed the media in Cape Town on Thursday, outlining the agency’s intensified campaign to protect the integrity of the social grant system and prevent fraud.

nnnn

SASSA Chief Executive Officer, Mr Themba Matlou, said the measures introduced were already producing results.

nnnn

“These measures go a long way in detecting and preventing fraud cases in the social grant system. We have also implemented life certification for identified beneficiaries, and the review of targeted beneficiary groups,” said Matlou.

nnnn

He added that for the current financial year, SASSA had planned to conduct 420,000 beneficiary reviews. By the third quarter, just under 400,000 beneficiaries had already been notified to present themselves for verification.

nnnn

As part of its anti-fraud strategy, SASSA last year introduced compulsory biometric enrolment for all new social grant applications. This system is aimed at preventing identity fraud and ensuring that grants are paid only to qualifying individuals.

nnnn

The Department of Social Development previously revealed that in 2024, SASSA had paid approximately R140 million to beneficiaries who were already deceased, highlighting the scale of irregularities within the system.

nnnn

SASSA has urged all beneficiaries who have been notified for review to cooperate fully, warning that failure to comply may result in the suspension or termination of grant payments. The agency says the process is necessary to protect public funds and ensure that social assistance reaches those who genuinely need it most.

post_title: Butsere Community Protests Eskom Over Power Crisis
post_content:
n

Residents of Butsere village in Bushbuckridge blocked the R40 near the Marongwane crossing on the morning of Thursday, 6 February, in protest against Eskom over a prolonged electricity outage and what they describe as unfair financial demands.

nnnn

According to community members, Eskom conducted an audit in the area and identified 63 households that had been illegally connected to the electricity network. Following the audit, Eskom reportedly required the installation of a new transformer, costing R68,000 in total. Each affected household was instructed to contribute R600 towards the installation. Residents say they managed to raise the funds, after which Eskom installed the transformer.

nnnn

However, the community claims that the transformer soon developed technical faults. When the matter was reported, Eskom technicians allegedly informed residents that the transformer was too small to supply electricity to all 63 households. The “links” were subsequently removed, leaving the community without electricity for over a month.

nnnn

Residents further allege that Eskom has now informed them that, in order to resolve the problem, the same households must pay an additional R48,800 on top of the original R68,000 already paid. Community members say this demand is unaffordable and unjust, particularly because Eskom had already audited the area and was aware that the transformer would serve 63 households at the time of installation.

nnnn

“The transformer they installed was meant for these same households. They knew how many homes it would supply, yet now we are being told to pay more for their mistake,” said one community member.

nnnn

The protest, which led to the temporary closure of the R40, disrupted traffic in the area as residents demanded a fair resolution to the crisis. Community leaders are calling on Eskom and relevant authorities to intervene urgently and restore electricity without placing further financial burdens on already struggling households.

nnnn

By the time of publication, Eskom had not issued an official response to the community’s claims.

The South African Police Service (SAPS) in Mpumalanga has launched a manhunt for three suspects following a violent carjacking incident in Bushbuckridge.

nnnn

The crime took place on Friday evening, 6 February 2026, at around 21:30 in Mandela Village. According to police, the victim was driving a white Toyota Quantum when he arrived at his home and stopped at the gate to open it. As he returned to the vehicle, he was confronted by two unknown men, one of whom was armed with a firearm.

nnnn

The armed suspect forced the complainant back into the vehicle, while the second suspect ordered him to lie down and stood on top of him while pointing the firearm at him. The suspects then drove off with the victim, later picking up a third suspect at an unknown location.

nnnn

After driving around for some time, the victim was dropped off at a nearby graveyard, where he was searched and robbed of a Samsung Galaxy A04 cellphone and R200 in cash. He was warned not to look back as the suspects fled the scene with the vehicle.

nnnn

The stolen items are estimated to be worth approximately:

nnnn

• Toyota Quantum: R500,000

nnnn

• Samsung Galaxy A04 cellphone: R1,500

nnnn

The suspects are described as three unknown men who were speaking different languages. At this stage, no arrests have been made, and investigations are ongoing.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, strongly condemned the incident and called on the community to assist police.

nnnn

“Carjacking remains a serious and violent crime that poses a threat to the safety of our communities. We urge residents to work closely with the police by sharing any information that may assist in bringing the perpetrators to justice. Communities are reminded to remain vigilant and to prioritise their personal safety at all times,” he said.

nnnn

Anyone with information that may assist the investigation is urged to contact Lieutenant Colonel Cindy Mkhabela on 082 469 1298, Crime Stop on 08600 10111, or report anonymously via the MySAPS App.

post_title: Kruger National Park boosts efforts to combat rhino poaching with enhanced security and community programs
Rangers intercept suspected poachers in KNP
post_content:
n

South African National Parks (SANParks) says its rangers have been involved in two recent anti-poaching incidents in the Kruger National Park, as authorities continue a sustained effort to disrupt rhino poaching and other wildlife crime.

nnnn

According to SANParks, the first incident happened on Thursday, 5 February 2026, in the Malelane section of the park, where rangers came into contact with suspected poachers during patrol operations. No arrests were made at the time, but rangers recovered a high-calibre rifle and bags believed to be linked to poaching activity.

nnnn

SANParks said the seizure of the weapon and equipment represents a meaningful disruption to criminal operations in the park, particularly at a time when rhino poaching remains one of the most persistent threats to conservation efforts.

nnnn

A second contact was reported on Friday, 6 February 2026, in the Stolznek section of the park. SANParks said rangers engaged suspected poachers and one suspect was fatally wounded during the confrontation.

nnnn

The incidents, SANParks said, reflect the dangers rangers face daily while protecting South Africa’s wildlife and natural heritage. The agency praised the commitment and bravery of ranger teams who continue to conduct patrols, track suspicious movement, and respond rapidly when threats are detected.

nnnn

“The recovery of weapons and equipment demonstrates the effectiveness of ranger patrols and the commitment to safeguarding rhinos from relentless poaching threats,” SANParks said in a statement.

nnnn

SANParks added that the fight against poaching remains a priority and that operations will continue to be intensified to protect rhinos for future generations.

nnnn

Both incidents have been handed over to the South African Police Service (SAPS) for further investigation and processing.

The victim, identified as Daniel Tehebo, an Ethiopian national, was reportedly followed by two armed men from another location before the attack. After parking his car and entering the restaurant, the suspects, driving a Volkswagen Polo, approached Tehebo and opened fire at close range.

nnnn

Mpumalanga police spokesperson Lieutenant Colonel Jabu Ndubane said Tehebo was shot in the hand and stomach but was saved by swift action from security guards, who returned fire and forced the suspects to flee. Fifteen spent cartridges were recovered at the scene.

nnnn

Tehebo was rushed to Nelspruit Mediclinic for urgent medical treatment. No members of the public were injured, and police continue to search for the suspects.

The incident occurred on Thursday afternoon as learners were preparing to board their scholar transport after school. According to the provincial Department of Education, the learner was accidentally run over by a reversing scholar transport bus. It is alleged that the child was positioned in the vehicle’s blind spot and could not be seen by the driver.

The South African Police Service (SAPS) is investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident.

A delegation from the Department of Education and the Department of Public Works, Roads and Transport paid their respects to the family, who expressed appreciation for the support, prayers and solidarity shown during this difficult time. The Department has extended its heartfelt condolences to the grieving family and the entire Thanda Primary School community.

May the soul of the departed rest in eternal peace.

nnnn

The department attributed the positive trend to sustained collaboration between government, private rhino owners and non-governmental organisations, highlighting the importance of partnerships in protecting the country’s wildlife heritage.

nnnn

Speaking on the progress, Aucamp said South Africa remains committed to an intelligence-driven and partnership-based approach to conservation, aimed at strengthening long-term rhino protection and disrupting wildlife trafficking networks.

nnnn

The country’s efforts have also gained international recognition. South Africa recently received the Asia Environmental Enforcement Recognition of Excellence Award for its work in combating transboundary environmental crimes.

“South Africa continues to strengthen its international collaboration to curb rhino poaching and wildlife trafficking. nnnn

Bondzeni Secondary School recorded a 100% matric pass rate in 2025, continuing a strong tradition of excellence. The school previously achieved a 100% pass rate in 2022, delivered an exceptional performance in 2023, recorded a commendable 98% in 2024, and has now returned to full success in 2025.

The celebratory visit formed part of the Department’s ongoing commitment to promoting motivation, academic excellence and learner development. Senior departmental officials engaged with the Class of 2026, encouraging them to draw inspiration from the achievements of previous learners and to remain disciplined, focused and determined in their academic journey.

Officials emphasised that every learner has the potential to succeed when provided with the right support, guidance and encouragement, highlighting that success is built through hard work, resilience and collective effort.

nnnn

In recognition of the achievement, the Department presented tokens of appreciation to the school’s top 10 Grade 12 achievers. The gesture was aimed at inspiring current learners to aim higher, dream bigger and strive for academic excellence.

nnnn

The Department reaffirmed its commitment to supporting schools in their pursuit of excellence and ensuring that every learner is equipped with the skills, knowledge and confidence needed to succeed in a rapidly changing world.

nnnn

Bondzeni Secondary School’s achievement stands as a powerful example of what is possible through dedication, teamwork and a shared vision for success.

post_title: Families Must Speak Up On Abuse
post_content:
n

South Africa will not defeat gender-based violence and femicide (GBVF) unless families speak openly with their children and report abuse without fear, Justice and Constitutional Development Minister Mmamoloko Kubayi has warned.

nnnn

Addressing residents at a Community Outreach Imbizo and Pre-State of the Nation Address (SONA) community activation at the Dulcie September Civic Hall in Athlone, Western Cape, Kubayi said incidents of sexual violence must never be hidden or treated as “private” matters.

nnnn

“When something like this happens, we don’t sit on it and hide it. There cannot be a debate when there is rape… it is a crime,” she said.

nnnn

Kubayi stressed that parents have both a legal and moral duty to report child sexual abuse, including teenage pregnancies involving minors. She emphasised that a child cannot legally consent to sex and that pregnancy involving an underage child amounts to statutory rape.

nnnn

“There is no 11-year-old who can give consent to sex. The age of consent is clear in the law. When a child becomes pregnant, it is statutory rape,” she said.

nnnn

The Minister urged families to act immediately by seeking medical care and reporting cases to the police. She added that teachers and community members share the same responsibility to protect children and report abuse.

nnnn

Kubayi also raised concerns about cases where families conceal teenage pregnancies after accepting financial settlements from perpetrators. She warned that such deals protect offenders and expose other children to harm.

nnnn

“You may spend that R50 000 and it will be finished, but you have a child who is destroyed for life. Once you do that, the perpetrator moves from this child to another,” she said.

nnnn

Kubayi said perpetrators must be held accountable regardless of their status in a household, including if they are breadwinners. She added that abuse affects both girls and boys, calling on civil society and community activists to help fight what she described as a growing pandemic.

nnnn

Government, she said, has amended legislation and is considering further reforms, including allowing the publication of convicted offenders’ names to prioritise victims over perpetrators

post_title: Operation Shanela II cracks down on crime
post_content:
n

Operation Shanela II has delivered a major blow against crime in Mpumalanga, following a province-wide law-enforcement operation conducted between 5 and 8 February 2026.

nnnn

The coordinated operation brought together multiple stakeholders, including the South African Police Service (SAPS), Traffic Police, various law-enforcement agencies, the Departments of Home Affairs, Health, Labour and Correctional Services, private security companies, and Community Policing Forums (CPFs).

nnnn

During the operation, law-enforcement teams carried out extensive activities across the province. A total of 275 premises were searched, while 4 285 people and 1 975 vehicles were stopped and searched. Police also conducted 1 106 stop-and-search operations, six specialised tracking operations, and 3 474 high-visibility patrols, which included 109 vehicle checkpoints, 26 roadblocks and 2 262 patrols. Detectives conducted 93 tracing operations for wanted suspects, and six hostels were searched.

nnnn

Significant compliance and inspection operations were also undertaken. Six unlicensed liquor outlets were closed, while 282 licensed liquor outlets were inspected. Police inspected 91 second-hand dealers, issuing two notices for non-compliance, and visited 25 scrap yards and recyclers. Firearm compliance inspections were conducted at both non-official and official institutions, including private security companies and state facilities.

nnnn

Labour-law compliance inspections were carried out at 132 informal businesses, including spaza shops, and 22 formal businesses in the hospitality and retail sectors. Joint operations with the Departments of Home Affairs and Labour saw 78 farms and one mine inspected, while enforcement actions were also conducted in terms of the SASREA and Regulation of Gatherings Act.

nnnn

Numerous arrests were made during the operation, including wanted suspects linked to serious crimes such as murder, rape, carjacking, assault GBH and illegal possession of firearms. Additional arrests were recorded for a wide range of offences, including drug dealing and possession, illegal liquor trading, possession of dangerous weapons, firearm and ammunition offences, serious violent crimes, burglary, driving under the influence, and human trafficking. A total of 70 illegal immigrants were also arrested.

nnnn

Large quantities of illegal items were confiscated, including drugs, firearms, ammunition, dangerous weapons, alcohol, copper cables, cash, contraband goods and vehicles. Drug seizures included dagga, crack cocaine, crystal meth (tik), nyaope, mandrax tablets and mandrax powder.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner of SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, praised all law-enforcement agencies and stakeholders for the successful execution of the operation.

nnnn

He said the sustained, integrated approach demonstrated SAPS’ unwavering commitment to decisively combat crime and restore safety and order across Mpumalanga.

nnnn

Operation Shanela II is expected to continue strengthening visible policing, community safety and coordinated crime prevention efforts throughout the province.

post_title: BMW Announces Global Recall Over Fire Risk
post_content:
n

German carmaker BMW has confirmed a global recall of hundreds of thousands of vehicles due to a potential fire risk linked to faulty engine starters.

nnnn

A company spokesperson told AFP on Wednesday that the recall would affect a “mid-six-figure number” of cars worldwide. BMW will contact affected vehicle owners directly and replace the potentially defective starters.

nnnn

According to a company statement, 16 BMW models fitted with starters produced between July 2020 and July 2022 may be affected. The issue is linked to excessive wear in the electromagnet over time, which could lead to technical failure.

nnnn

“BMW AG recommends that after starting the engine – especially after remote engine start – the vehicle should not be left unattended with the engine running,” the company said.

nnnn

BMW explained that, following customer complaints and vehicle inspections, it was established that the starters in the identified vehicles could become defective. The company also warned that a short circuit in the electromagnet cannot be ruled out, which could cause local overheating.

nnnn

“In the worst case, this can lead to a vehicle fire while driving,” the statement added.

nnnn

The recall was first reported by industry publication kfz-betrieb.

nnnn

This is not the first major recall for BMW in recent years. In 2024, the company was forced to cut its financial outlook after booking losses worth hundreds of millions of euros when it recalled around 1.5 million vehicles over faulty brakes supplied by Continental.

nnnn

However, BMW has indicated that the latest recall is unlikely to have any significant impact on its earnings.

nnnn

Motorists are advised to remain alert for official communication from BMW and to follow safety guidance while the recall process is underway.

nnnn

n

n

A major multi-agency operation targeting illegal mining activities in Mpumalanga has resulted in the seizure of illicit mining equipment and the arrest of four suspects at the Majax Informal Settlement in the Pilgrim’s Rest policing area.

nnnn

The operation was led by the Acting Provincial Commissioner of the South African Police Service (SAPS) in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, together with the Ehlanzeni District Commissioner, Major General D. Xaba, as part of an ongoing illegal mining stabilisation drive in the province.

nnnn

A multidisciplinary task team was deployed, comprising members of SAPS, the K9 Unit, Public Order Policing, the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation(DPCI), the Department of Mineral Resources and Energy (DMRE), the Department of Water and Sanitation, the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), the Inkomati-Usuthu Catchment Management Agency, the Mpumalanga Tourism and Parks Agency (MTPA), and the Thaba Chweu Local Municipality.

nnnn

During the operation, four suspects aged between 25 and 65 were arrested for various offences, including contravention of the Immigration Act, dealing in dagga, possession of illicit cigarettes, and possession of illicit liquor. An additional individual was also issued with a fine for selling liquor without a valid licence.

nnnnnnnn

Law enforcement agencies further confiscated a range of illegal mining equipment, including motors, phendukas, and other tools commonly used in unlawful mining activities.

nnnn

According to SAPS, the operation forms part of intensified, intelligence-driven efforts to combat illegal mining across Mpumalanga. Authorities say these stabilisation interventions are aimed at dismantling illegal mining networks, confiscating equipment used in criminal activities, enforcing compliance with relevant legislation, and restoring law and order in affected communities.

nnnn

The South African Police Service in Mpumalanga has reiterated its commitment to working closely with government departments and key stakeholders to ensure sustained action against illegal mining and related criminal activities across the province.

post_title: Mpumalanga Lekgotla adopts GBVF action pledge
post_content:
n

Municipal leaders and partners in Mpumalanga have adopted a bold declaration aimed at accelerating action against Gender-Based Violence and Femicide (GBVF) while strengthening women’s leadership in local government.

nnnn

The Mpumalanga SALGA Women’s Commission (SWC) Provincial Lekgotla concluded at Premier Hotel The Winkler after a two-day programme held on 10 and 11 February 2026 under the theme: “Letsema: Men, Women, Boys and Girls Working Together to End GBVF.” Delegates included councillors, provincial departments, Chapter 9 institutions, traditional leadership and civil society organisations, with discussions focused on prevention, protection, survivor support and accountability.

nnnn

Opening the gathering, Mpumalanga SWC Provincial Commissioner Cllr S. Makushe-Mazibuko described GBVF as a lived reality across communities and called for a whole-of-government and whole-of-society response. She said the Lekgotla was convened to reflect on SWC work, assess progress on previous resolutions, strengthen Multi-Party Women’s Commissions (MPWCs) as Section 79 committees, improve women’s representation and deepen gender mainstreaming across municipalities.

nnnn

Keynote speaker Cllr S.E. Mgcina, Gauteng SWC Provincial Commissioner, urged leaders to demonstrate courage and coordination, adding that the SWC must drive gender-responsive governance, influence implementation and hold institutions accountable for measurable change.

nnnn

Delegates heard a provincial update on GBVF from Major General D.G. Xaba, who emphasised the need to strengthen policing partnerships and community-based prevention structures working alongside municipalities and traditional leadership.

nnnn

The adopted SWC Declaration commits municipalities to time-bound measures, including stronger multi-sectoral partnerships with SAPS, the Office of the Premier, the Department of Social Development, the Commission for Gender Equality, traditional leadership and NGOs. It also calls for institutionalising the National Strategic Plan on GBVF within local government through gender-responsive planning, budgeting, monitoring and auditing in the 2026/27 municipal cycle.

nnnn

Other resolutions include implementing gender budget classification, prioritising women for senior management roles, expanding mentorship and leadership development, and improving survivor-centred support at first-contact points to reduce secondary victimisation. SALGA was also mandated to lobby for stronger GBVF integration in municipal planning frameworks and to support the establishment and monitoring of key services and structures, including Thuthuzela Care Centres and functional MPWCs across municipalities.

n

n

A spirit of unity, service and hope filled the grounds of Mathibela High School as a successful Back to School Campaign was hosted, bringing together learners, educators, community members and local organisations in a powerful community-driven initiative.

nnnn

The programme began with a short but impactful motivational session aimed at encouraging both learners and educators as they prepare for the new academic year. The message focused on discipline, commitment, and the importance of education in shaping a better future for the youth.

nnnn

This was followed by a well-organised cleaning campaign, which saw strong support from Bangwato Foundation and Makungu Security. The two organisations provided two grass cutters, cleaning equipment, and also ensured that food was available for volunteers, demonstrating practical commitment to community development.

nnnn

A total of 112 volunteers participated in the campaign, working tirelessly to clean the school premises. One of the major achievements of the day was the cutting of grass at the school’s soccer field, improving both the safety and appearance of the sporting facilities.

nnnn

The programme ran from 7:00am until 2:30pm, reflecting a full day of dedicated service and community involvement.

nnnn

Support for the initiative included Selby Matsane, the ANC Kaizer Mgiba Branch, Makungu Security, and Bangwato Foundation, with the entire programme facilitated by the Ward Councillor of Ward 5 in Alexandria.

nnnn

The campaign stands as a strong example of what can be achieved when communities, organisations and leadership work together for a common purpose. It not only improved the physical environment of the school but also strengthened community bonds and created a positive atmosphere for learning.

nnnn

This initiative sends a clear message: education is everyone’s responsibility, and collective action can make a meaningful difference in the lives of young people.

A provincial mass vaccination campaign against Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) has been launched in Mpumalanga, as authorities intensify efforts to curb the spread of the highly contagious livestock disease that has severely affected the cattle industry.

nnnn

The official launch took place at a communal livestock farm in Siyathemba Location, Balfour, within Dipaleseng Local Municipality, marking the beginning of a large-scale inoculation programme that will be rolled out to other districts across the province.

nnnn

The start of the vaccination drive follows President Cyril Ramaphosa’s announcement during the State of the Nation Address, where Foot and Mouth Disease was declared a national disaster due to its devastating impact on the cattle industry in several provinces.

nnnn

Dipaleseng has been identified as the epicentre of the outbreak in Mpumalanga, with approximately 35 confirmed cases, while the wider Gert Sibande District has recorded about 149 confirmed outbreaks across its local municipalities.

nnnn

More than 80 farmers from Balfour and surrounding areas, including Grootvlei, attended the launch. Farmers were urged to cooperate with government and veterinary services by preventing suspicious livestock movements, reporting any symptoms associated with FMD, and adhering strictly to animal movement restrictions and disease management measures.

nnnnnnnn

Authorities have emphasised that close cooperation between farmers, veterinary services and local communities is essential to prevent further spread of the disease and to protect livelihoods that depend on the livestock sector.

nnnn

The mass vaccination campaign will now be extended to other districts as more vaccine doses become available, forming part of a broader provincial strategy to contain and eventually eradicate Foot and Mouth Disease in Mpumalanga.

nnnn

n

A 56-year-old teacher has been arrested on charges of murder and attempted murder following a shooting incident in Elukwatini in the early hours of Saturday morning.

nnnn

Police responded to reports of a shooting at approximately 02:10 on 14 February 2026 in Elukwatini.

nnnn

On arrival, officers found a 22-year-old woman in the street with a gunshot wound to her foot. She informed police that she had been shot by her mother’s male friend and further stated that her mother had also been shot and was unable to escape.

nnnn

Inside the house, police discovered the 45-year-old mother lying on the floor with a gunshot wound to the head. Emergency Medical Services certified her dead at the scene. The injured daughter was transported to hospital for medical treatment.

nnnn

The suspect was found inside the house and was immediately arrested. A firearm believed to have been used in the commission of the crime was confiscated. He has been charged with murder and attempted murder and is expected to appear soon at the Albert Luthuli Magistrate’s Court.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of South African Police Service in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, condemned the incident and conveyed his condolences to the family of the deceased. He expressed deep concern over the continued incidents of Gender-Based Violence and Femicide (GBVF), calling on community members to seek help when facing personal challenges rather than resorting to violence.

nnnn

He added that communities cannot afford to continue losing loved ones in this manner and urged collective action to end violence against women and children.

nnnn

post_title: Gogo Nonyane ya Metsi: Week of 16–22 February 2026
post_content:
n

This week the sky stirs the water. An annular solar eclipse arrives on Tuesday, 17 February, a “ring of fire” moment of reset, and then the Sun slips into Pisces from Wednesday, 18 February, softening hearts and sharpening intuition.

nnnn

Aries

nnnnnnnn

My child of the first flame, you are closing a chapter with dignity. From midweek, rest is not laziness — it is medicine. The eclipse shakes your circles: choose allies who clap for you when you are not in the room. By weekend, your spirit wants quiet, not noise. Drink water before you answer messages; your “yes” must be clean and your “no” must be holy.

nnnn

Taurus

nnnnnnnn

Steady one, the week asks you to clear the air — in money matters and in love matters too. If you’ve been carrying an old worry, the eclipse exposes the root. Don’t chase comfort; renew it. Small changes in routine open big doors. Speak plainly, spend wisely, and let your body lead you back to balance.

nnnn

Gemini

nnnnnnnn

Quick mind, your voice is your bridge this week. The eclipse highlights reputation and direction — the path is there, but you must stop walking in two directions at once. Midweek Pisces energy makes you sensitive; protect your focus from gossip and scattered plans. Say less, do more, and watch how the right people find you.

nnnn

Cancer

nnnnnnnn

Moon-child, your waters feel deep, but they are not drowning you — they are cleansing you. The eclipse opens themes of trust, shared resources, and emotional honesty. If you need help, ask with maturity, not apology. By weekend, a gentle conversation repairs something you thought was broken. Light a candle, then forgive yourself.

nnnn

Leo

nnnnnnnn

Bright one, relationships stand in the spotlight. The eclipse can bring a turning point: a commitment, a boundary, or a truth that sets you free. Don’t roar to be heard — speak once, clearly. Pisces season then reminds you: love is not control, it is care. Choose partners, friends, and deals that respect your crown.

nnnn

Virgo

nnnnnnnn

Careful hands, the week asks you to soften your grip. The eclipse brings a reset in daily rhythms — health, work systems, and the way you manage stress. Midweek, your relationships require patience: stop fixing people, start listening. Organise your week like a prayer: simple, steady, and sincere.

nnnn

Libra

nnnnnnnn

Beautiful balancer, creativity and romance want your attention, but the eclipse demands honesty. If something feels one-sided, the scales will tip until you act. Pisces season sweetens your routines: do the small things that keep your spirit clean — sleep, water, movement, gratitude. A joyful opportunity arrives when you stop postponing your happiness.

nnnn

Scorpio

nnnnnnnn

Deep water, this week rewards straight talk. The eclipse stirs home and family matters — what must change in the space where you rest? Don’t hold secrets that are heavy; release them gently. Pisces season brings tenderness and desire: love can be safe when you stop testing it. Choose peace, even if you must disappoint someone.

nnnn

Sagittarius

nnnnnnnn

Traveller, your words travel before you do. The eclipse highlights communication, contracts, and decision-making. Read everything twice; promise only what you can deliver. Midweek Pisces energy turns your attention to home and roots — make your base stronger, and your future will run faster. The weekend favours learning, planning, and clean direction.

nnnn

Capricorn

nnnnnnnn

Mountain spirit, discipline is your blessing — but don’t become harsh with yourself. The eclipse brings a money-mind reset: budgets, debts, pricing, and self-worth. Midweek, focus improves when you stop multitasking. Choose one priority, finish it, then rest. Your success this week comes from structure that still leaves room for breath.

nnnn

Aquarius

nnnnnnnn

Star-child, the eclipse is in your territory — a powerful rebirth. You may feel exposed, emotional, or suddenly clear. Let it happen. This is a week to reintroduce yourself to yourself: new boundaries, new identity, new courage. Pisces season then turns your attention to value — know what you deserve and stop negotiating it down.

nnnn

Pisces

nnnnnnnn

My water-child, your season begins and the current carries you forward. The eclipse cleans out old fear so your intuition can speak louder. Midweek onwards, your energy rises — but don’t forget the body: eat well, rest well, pray well. This is a week for gentle confidence: you don’t need to force the river; you only need to follow its truth.

nnnn

Gogo’s Special Message for the Week

nnnn

“Ngwana wa metsi, do not fear the ripples. The sky is stirring you so you can return to yourself. Speak truth like clean water. Cut what drains you. Bless what feeds you. And remember: the river of your life moves forward — even when you are resting.”

post_title: Inclusive Employment Drive Welcomes 21 PLWD Employees
post_content:
n

A major step towards inclusive employment was marked as 21 new employees from the Persons Living with Disabilities (PLWD) community were officially welcomed through a transformative workplace inclusion initiative.

nnnn

The onboarding programme was hosted by the Human Resource Management (HRM) unit of the Mpumalanga Department of Health, demonstrating the department’s commitment to building a more representative and equitable workforce.

nnnn

The event was attended by representatives from the Office of the Premier, the local clinic and the transformation team, who participated in a meet-and-greet session with the new recruits. The programme was led by HRM Director Ms Mdluli, together with the HRM team, who addressed the employees and emphasised the importance of diversity, dignity and inclusion within the workplace.

nnnn

This initiative forms part of broader efforts to increase the representation of persons with disabilities in the workforce, aligning with the objectives of the Employment Equity Amendment Act, which proposes a target of at least 3% employment for persons with disabilities across all sectors.

nnnn

The 21 employees will undergo a comprehensive induction programme that includes structured training, orientation and continuous support to ensure their seamless integration into the working environment. The department highlighted that inclusion is not only about access to jobs, but also about creating supportive spaces where employees can grow, contribute meaningfully and thrive.

nnnn

Studies continue to show that inclusive workplaces benefit from diverse perspectives, increased innovation and improved employee morale — outcomes that strengthen institutional performance and service delivery.

nnnn

This initiative stands as a powerful example of practical inclusion in action, reinforcing the principle that development must leave no one behind.

n

n

Farmers in Bushbuckridge Local Municipality are rebuilding their livelihoods after recent floods caused widespread damage to crops, irrigation systems and farming infrastructure.

nnnn

An oversight visit to three key agricultural projects — the Dingledale Irrigation Scheme, Benica Farms in Acornhoek and Mariti Harvest — highlighted both the scale of the losses and the resilience of local producers. The visit was led by the Mpumalanga MEC for Agriculture, Rural Development, Land and Environmental Affairs, Khethiwe Moeketsi, alongside the municipal executive led by Executive Mayor Lydia Moroane, Council Speaker Ruth Raganya, Chief Whip Malandule, MMC for Economic Development, Environment and Planning Patricia Gubayi, ward councillors and community representatives.

nnnn

At the Dingledale Irrigation Scheme, farmers were assured that refurbishment of the canal, badly damaged by heavy rains and flooding, will begin soon. Crops were destroyed, while irrigation infrastructure, smart box systems and furrow irrigation channels were severely affected. The 1 748-hectare scheme, established in 1966, supports more than 300 families whose livelihoods depend on the canal. Farmers from the scheme supply produce to the Government Nutrition Programme and retailers including Boxer, Spar, Pick n Pay and Shoprite in Thulamahashe, Bushbuckridge and Acornhoek.

nnnnnnnn

In Acornhoek, the delegation visited Benica Farms, a multi-award-winning, SAP GAP-certified operation led by co-founders Bennedicter and Veronica Mhlongo. The farm supplies fresh vegetables, fruit and processed products to local retailers. Support was provided in the form of 15 000 spinach seedlings, 15 000 cabbage seedlings and five 50kg bags of fertiliser.

nnnnnnnn

In Mariti, the team visited Mariti Harvest, a mixed-farming project led by 28-year-old Makhutso Mnisi, which specialises in horticulture and the export of agricultural produce. The farm received 4 000 Raja chilli seedlings, 5 000 spinach seedlings, 1 500 tomato seedlings and five 50kg bags of fertiliser.

nnnn

Mnisi described the human and economic impact of the floods on her operation. “The recent floods devastated us in a sense that we lost about 2 000 tomatoes, which would have given us roughly 400 crates of tomatoes. Some of our workers who went for December holidays came back to no jobs because of this. The loss did not only affect workers, it also impacted our buyers,” she said.

nnnn

All the farms employ local workers, contribute to the local economy and support surrounding communities through food production and job creation. They also supply produce to government nutrition programmes and regional retailers.

nnnn

The visits underscored the resilience of Bushbuckridge’s farming community and the importance of coordinated support to restore production, rebuild infrastructure and secure sustainable livelihoods for rural families.

nnnn

nnnn

nnnn

nnnn

nnnn

nnnn

nnnnn

Learners at Mzinti Primary School are attending classes in buildings described as structurally unsafe, raising serious concerns about child safety and the state of school infrastructure in rural areas.

nnnn

The condition of the school was highlighted during an oversight visit by the Provincial Legislature’s Portfolio Committee on Education on Friday, 13 February 2026. The school, established in 1942, has ageing blocks, including one built by community members. It has 18 classrooms, with one converted into a staff room — but several structures are now reportedly unfit to safely accommodate learners and educators.

nnnnnnnn

According to a press statement issued by MPL Thoko Mashiane on 17 February 2026, teaching continues under the fear that ceilings or walls could collapse, especially during windy and rainy conditions. The School Governing Body (SGB) has attempted minor repairs using limited departmental maintenance funds, but the school’s condition remains a risk.

nnnn

While the circuit manager facilitated the installation of six mobile classrooms in November 2024 to ease overcrowding, the statement argues this has not addressed the underlying crisis.

nnnn

The situation worsened after January 2026 storms tore rooftops off four additional classrooms. Although the storm did not occur during school hours, the incident has intensified concerns about what could happen if severe weather strikes while learners are in class. Parts of the school are now said to be too unsafe for teaching and learning.

nnnn

Beyond the infrastructure decay, the school is reported to be battling overcrowding, a lack of ICT resources, crime including theft and burglary, insufficient parental support, and shortages of learning and teaching support materials such as desks and chairs.

nnnn

The SGB has formally appealed to the Mpumalanga Department of Education to demolish unsafe structures and replace them with permanent, modern classrooms that are safe, dignified and suitable for learning. Calls have also been made for urgent assessments, decommissioning of dangerous buildings, long-term planning to end overcrowding, and prioritisation of rural schools in infrastructure budgets.

nnnn

The matter has renewed debate about whether temporary solutions are enough when learners’ lives may be at risk.

post_title: ARV Tender Turmoil Raises Red Flags
post_content:
n

Health Minister Dr Aaron Motsoaledi has sought to reassure Parliament that disruptions linked to the national antiretroviral (ARV) tender will not derail South Africa’s HIV treatment programme, despite mounting concern over the financial stability of suppliers and a controversial takeover arrangement.

nnnn

The minister briefed MPs after it emerged that two companies awarded contracts to supply ARVs applied for business rescue in 2025. One of those suppliers is now linked to a proposed takeover by Hetero, an India-based pharmaceutical company that has also taken the Department of Health to court over the same tender amid suspicions of price-fixing.

nnnn

Parliamentarians from across parties questioned whether the department had done enough due diligence before awarding contracts, warning that any weakness in the supply chain could place patients at risk. The debate has been sharpened by lingering mistrust following the department’s widely criticised Digital Vibes tender saga, which has made MPs wary of decisions that appear rushed or insufficiently scrutinised.

nnnn

Barrs Pharmaceuticals and Innovata are among seven companies appointed to supply ARVs. MPs indicated discomfort that a supplier under business rescue could shift ownership or control while remaining tied to a key public-health contract — especially when the incoming entity has been involved in litigation linked to that very tender.

nnnn

Motsoaledi told the committee he is not directly involved in tender processes and said the department does not assess the financial statements of companies bidding for contracts. “We cannot examine balance sheets because, for us to do so, we do not have any skill whatsoever,” he said.

nnnn

However, Economic Freedom Fighters MP Naledi Chirwa argued that the minister’s position was misleading, saying the Public Finance Management Act requires the state to satisfy itself that bidders have the financial capacity to deliver. “There are too many red flags for us not to be suspicious with what is happening with this ARV tender,” she said.

nnnn

Health department officials responded that it is the role of National Treasury and the Department of Trade to flag risk indicators in companies’ financial standing and corporate status.

nnnn

Despite the friction, Motsoaledi insisted that medicine availability at state facilities has not been affected. He told MPs that clinics typically maintain a three-month buffer stock, which should cushion patients from short-term shocks while the tender issues are addressed.

nnnn

The committee’s scrutiny is expected to continue, with MPs demanding clearer accountability on vetting processes, supplier stability, and safeguards to protect uninterrupted ARV access.

n

n

Speaking in the National Assembly during the 2026 State of the Nation Address (SONA) debate, Mandla Ndlovu outlined major plans that could directly impact communities across the province, including Bushbuckridge.

nnnn

He told Parliament that Mpumalanga had reprioritised R288 million to repair infrastructure damaged by recent floods, with a further R100 million allocated through national departments. The floods claimed 20 lives in the province and displaced many families.

nnnn

Health services are set to expand, with new clinics planned, more doctors placed at community health centres, and major hospitals such as Mapulaneng and the Middelburg Regional Hospital nearing completion. Mpumalanga is also preparing for the implementation of National Health Insurance (NHI), supported by accredited health facilities and a digital patient record system.

nnnn

Education remains a priority, with 70,000 tablets set to be distributed to Grade 10 learners in 2026, following last year’s rollout to matric learners. New schools are under construction, pit latrine toilets are being eradicated, and more than 1,300 community ECD centres have been registered and funded. Boarding schools and specialised schools for learners with disabilities are also planned.

nnnn

Economic development initiatives include renewable energy projects, agricultural expansion, and large-scale hybrid rice production expected to create hundreds of thousands of jobs. Tourism developments, including projects in the Mariepskop area, were also highlighted.

nnnn

Addressing Parliament in Cape Town, Ndlovu praised the leadership of Cyril Ramaphosa, particularly his response to floods in Mpumalanga and Limpopo, and said cooperative governance was key to improving service delivery and economic growth.

nnnn

For communities such as Bushbuckridge, the focus on clinics, schools, disaster recovery, agriculture and job creation signals practical changes that could directly improve daily life and long-term opportunities across rural Mpumalanga.

nnnn
