post_title: Your Pad May Be Disrupting Your Flow
post_content:
n

A new University of the Free State (UFS) study is raising fresh questions about what South Africans may be exposed to during their monthly cycle. Researchers found that every sanitary pad and pantyliner tested contained at least two hormone-disrupting chemicals, including products marketed as “free from harmful chemicals”.

nnnn

Published in Science of the Total Environment, the study analysed 16 brands of sanitary pads and eight types of pantyliners sold in South African retail stores. The team screened for three groups of endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs): phthalates, bisphenols (including BPA), and parabens.

nnnn

The results showed widespread contamination across all products tested. Bisphenols were detected in 100% of pads and 75% of pantyliners, while parabens were found in over 81% of pads and 75% of liners. Phthalates appeared in all pantyliners tested and in 50% of sanitary pads. Researchers said these chemicals may not always be added on purpose, but could migrate into products through plastics, adhesives, inks, and manufacturing processes.

nnnn

What makes this issue especially personal is where these products are used. Menstrual pads and liners come into contact with mucosal tissue, which can absorb chemicals more directly than normal skin. While the amount in a single product might seem small, the study warns that repeated exposure over many years could add up. Long-term exposure to EDCs has been linked in research to hormonal disruption, fertility challenges, endometriosis, and certain cancers.

nnnn

The study also highlights gaps in regulation and transparency. In South Africa, standards focus largely on performance and hygiene, but researchers say there are limited chemical standards for the substances detected, and manufacturers are generally not required to disclose full ingredient lists.

nnnn

For consumers, the advice is practical rather than panic-driven: look for products with independent certification such as OEKO-TEX Standard 100, and consider reusable alternatives where suitable. The UFS team says it is also working on innovations, including reusable pads with antimicrobial properties.

nnnn

Ultimately, the research is a call for clearer labelling, stronger safety standards, and more honest “clean” marketing—so that shoppers can make informed choices about products used month after month, year after year.

n

post_title: Elderly Couple Released on Bail for Fraud Charges
post_content:
n

An elderly couple, Christopher Nkosi (65) and Sibongile Nkosi (59), co-directors of Ingcwenga Events Management cc, appeared in the Nelspruit Magistrate’s Court yesterday on fraud charges.

nnnn

The couple voluntarily handed themselves over to the Hawks’ Serious Commercial Crime Investigation in Nelspruit after warrants of arrest were issued. Their arrest follows that of their co-accused, Nhlanhla Mashaba (39), who was taken into custody on 11 February 2026 after being on the run.

nnnn

Investigations revealed that Mashaba allegedly collaborated with the Nkosis to manipulate e-filing during the 2013/2014 tax season, causing the South African Revenue Service (SARS) a loss of R212 469.85. The Hawks’ Nelspruit Serious Commercial Crime Investigation unit handled the case.

nnnn

The Nkosis were granted bail of R4 000 each, while Mashaba remains in custody pending a bail application on 26 February 2026.

n

post_title: Foreign National Arrested for R250k Drug Bust
post_content:
n

A 57-year-old foreign national, Patrick Izuchukwu Udeh (Nigerian), was arrested in Matafeni near Nelspruit on 18 February 2026 for dealing in drugs with an estimated street value of R250 000.

nnnn

The arrest followed an intelligence-driven operation involving the SAPS Provincial Organised Crime Investigation unit, Whiteriver K9, and the Pienaar Tactical Response Team (TRT). During the raid, cocaine was recovered and seized for forensic investigation.

nnnn

Udeh told police the drugs belonged to a friend who had left them for safekeeping in late January and had since fled to Johannesburg. Udeh appeared in the Nelspruit Magistrate’s Court and will return on 3 March 2026.

nnnn

n

n

Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) MP Sihle Lonzi used Wednesday’s State of the Nation Address (SONA) debate to slam government’s approach to youth unemployment, accusing leaders of blaming young people for a jobs crisis that is structural and deepening.

nnnn

In a passionate address in Parliament, Lonzi rejected what he called an attitude that suggests the youth are “lazy” or not trying hard enough to find work. He argued that the central problem is not a lack of effort by jobseekers, but a lack of jobs and a lack of urgency from the state.

nnnn

Lonzi told MPs the EFF would mobilise unemployed young people to physically deliver CVs to key state institutions — including the Union Buildings, Parliament and other government offices — as a visible reminder of the scale of joblessness. The party has framed the action as a protest against what it views as political “lip service” on employment, and a call for immediate, practical interventions.

nnnn

The MP also took aim at the Youth Employment Service (YES) programme, which government frequently highlights as part of its response to youth unemployment. Lonzi labelled it a “scam”, claiming the programme places young people in short-term roles without meaningful job security and, in some cases, without reliable payment. He pointed specifically to young people placed as education assistants and said some had allegedly not been paid since last year.

nnnn

Beyond criticising existing initiatives, Lonzi called for an economic shift that tackles unemployment at its roots. He argued that South Africa needs faster economic growth and a renewed focus on industrialisation, including bringing factories back to create sustainable employment at scale.

nnnn

His comments come at a time when youth unemployment remains one of the country’s most pressing challenges, with growing frustration among jobseekers who say they are applying repeatedly without success. Lonzi’s speech, and the EFF’s planned CV handovers, signal that the party intends to keep the issue in the public eye — and to pressure government to treat it as a national emergency.

n

post_title: Parliament Warns Colleges Over Foreign Hires
post_content:
n

Parliament has issued a stern warning to universities and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) colleges, cautioning institutions against using “internationalisation” as a loophole to sidestep South Africa’s immigration and labour laws when employing foreign nationals.

nnnn

The warning was delivered during a joint meeting of the Portfolio Committee on Higher Education and Training and the Portfolio Committee on Home Affairs, where MPs raised concerns about compliance failures, weak oversight and unreliable data on foreign academic appointments across the post-school education sector. Briefings by the Department of Higher Education and Training (DHET) and the Department of Home Affairs reportedly exposed serious gaps in data management and coordination, leaving Parliament unable to properly assess whether institutions are following legal requirements when hiring foreign staff.

nnnn

Higher Education and Training Minister Buti Manamela told the committees that the absence of credible data undermines effective oversight and makes it difficult to determine whether foreign nationals are being appointed to genuinely scarce and critical skills posts, or whether regulations are being bypassed.

nnnn

Committee members stressed that foreign appointments must align strictly with the country’s Critical Skills framework and should not displace suitably qualified South Africans. They warned that institutions must be able to demonstrate clear skills shortages before turning to international recruitment, particularly in roles that are not classified as scarce.

nnnn

Chairperson of the Portfolio Committee on Higher Education and Training, Tebogo Letsie, said compliance is non-negotiable. “When South African students go to other countries, they are expected to follow the laws of those countries. We expect the same from those who come here,” he said, adding that internationalisation must not be used as an excuse to ignore immigration laws.

nnnn

While emphasising that Parliament is not opposed to foreign academics and recognises their contributions in scarce disciplines, MPs expressed alarm over oversight findings that foreign nationals were occupying senior management and administrative posts, including principals and chief financial officers — positions not necessarily linked to critical skills.

nnnn

The Home Affairs committee further warned that employing undocumented foreign nationals is a criminal offence under Section 38 of the Immigration Act, which prohibits employers from hiring foreign nationals without valid work authorisation.

nnnn

The committees said they will intensify oversight, including engagement with the Department of Employment and Labour in the coming weeks, and increased scrutiny once proposed immigration-related legislation is tabled in Parliament.

post_title: SANRAL announces toll tariff hike from 1 March
post_content:
n

Motorists across South Africa will pay more at toll plazas from 1 March after the South African National Roads Agency (SANRAL) confirmed an annual tariff adjustment of 3.12%.

nnnn

The increase, which is lower than last year’s 4.85% rise, follows SANRAL’s yearly review of toll fees in line with the Consumer Price Index (CPI). The adjustment was published in the Government Gazette earlier this month and is based on inflation data provided by Statistics South Africa.

nnnn

SANRAL’s communications and marketing general manager, Vusi Mona, said the revenue collected at toll gates is essential to maintain, operate and improve toll roads, as well as to service debt incurred through toll road projects.

nnnn

“The funds go a long way towards ensuring that SANRAL fulfils its mandate of delivering quality road infrastructure that adds value to the lives of South African citizens,” Mona said.

nnnn

He added that the national road network plays a critical role in supporting basic services such as electricity, water, sanitation, telecommunications and public transport, and must meet industrial, commercial and household needs.

nnnn

Mona acknowledged the financial pressures facing South Africans, saying the agency is aware of the current economic challenges. However, he stressed that the annual adjustments are necessary to ensure the continued delivery of safe and reliable roads.

nnnn

“SANRAL is empathetic to the South African public, considering the current state of the economy. However, it is equally important to introduce the adjustments to ensure that the agency continues to deliver safe and quality roads to the benefit of all road users,” he said.

nnnn

The 3.12% increase will take effect nationwide at all SANRAL-managed toll plazas from 1 March.

nnnnn

n

27 officials from the Mpumalanga Department of Education were arrested on Sunday morning, 22 February, during a coordinated anti-corruption sting operation carried out across Mpumalanga, Gauteng, Limpopo and the Western Cape.

nnnn

The arrests form part of a major investigation into a R113 million corruption scheme being pursued by the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation(Hawks). In total, 41 individuals and companies are linked to the case, facing charges of fraud, theft, money laundering and contraventions of the Public Finance Management Act (PFMA).

nnnn

Those detained include nine departmental officials, 14 service providers and four other individuals connected to the alleged scheme. Among the high-profile suspects are the former acting Head of Department (HOD), the former acting Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and chief directors responsible for planning.

nnnnnnnn

Mpumalanga Hawks head, Major General Nico Gerber, said the alleged corruption dates back to 2018. The matter was reported during the 2019/2020 financial year, with a formal criminal case opened in 2020.

nnnn

According to Gerber, officials allegedly fabricated “emergency repair” and maintenance projects at 21 schools across the province. While some limited work may have been done, tenders and invoices were allegedly grossly inflated, procurement processes were bypassed, and service providers were unlawfully handpicked.

nnnn

Investigators further allege that false and inflated invoices were submitted for services purportedly rendered to the department, with financial irregularities stretching back more than five years. Contractors are accused of working in collusion with departmental officials to facilitate the scheme.

nnnn

Hawks spokesperson Magonseni Nkosi described the operation as a major breakthrough in tackling corruption in public institutions.

nnnn

“Following a lengthy investigation into irregularities within the Department of Education in Mpumalanga, we conducted a takedown operation in which 27 suspects were arrested. The operation is ongoing, and we are hopeful that the remaining suspects will be apprehended in due course,” said Nkosi.

nnnn

In a statement issued on 21 February 2026, the Mpumalanga Department of Education confirmed awareness of the Hawks’ operation. The department said the matter is now before the courts and is regarded as sub judice, and therefore declined to comment on the merits of the case.

nnnn

The department reiterated its commitment to ethical governance, transparency and accountability, maintaining a zero-tolerance stance on corruption and maladministration. It further stated that it will cooperate fully with law enforcement agencies to ensure due process is followed.

nnnn

The case is expected to continue in court as investigations expand, with further arrests anticipated as authorities pursue the remaining suspects linked to the corruption network.

post_title: New Eye Institute Opens in Lowveld
post_content:
n

The official opening of the Lowveld Eye Institute marked a major milestone for healthcare in Mpumalanga, as Premier Mandla Ndlovu, alongside Health MEC Sasekani Manzini, launched the state-of-the-art facility in the City of Mbombela on Friday, 20 February 2026.

nnnnnnnn

The purpose-built, fully digital ophthalmology hospital is expected to significantly expand access to quality eye care services, reduce preventable blindness and bring specialised healthcare closer to communities across the Lowveld region. The launch has been described as a vital boost to healthcare delivery, particularly for underserved communities who often struggle to access specialised medical services.

nnnn

The development of the institute reflects the importance of public–private partnerships in strengthening South Africa’s healthcare system, especially as the country prepares for the full rollout of the National Health Insurance. Such collaborations are seen as critical to ensuring that all citizens receive dignified, quality healthcare, regardless of socio-economic status.

nnnn

Speaking at the launch, Premier Ndlovu described the institute as more than just a building, calling it “a vision rooted in excellence, compassion, innovation and hope”. He highlighted that during construction, 250 part-time jobs were created, with 190 benefiting residents of Mpumalanga, contributing to local economic growth and job creation.

nnnn

Since beginning operations in January 2026, the institute has already created 30 permanent jobs, 28 of which have gone to local residents — a practical demonstration of the value of successful public–private partnerships in the province.

nnnn

The Premier also acknowledged the leadership and contribution of the institute’s clinical team and founders, praising their commitment to making world-class eye care accessible to the community. He expressed confidence that the facility would become a beacon of hope, restoring sight, preventing blindness, advancing research and mentoring future healthcare professionals.

nnnn

As part of broader healthcare reforms, the provincial government continues to prioritise access to services. Ndlovu revealed that 93.8% of public healthcare facilities in Mpumalanga are accredited by the Office of Health Standards Compliance, and that 25 doctors have recently been appointed to Community Health Centres across the province, bringing the total number of centres with permanent doctors to 36.

nnnn

The opening of the Lowveld Eye Institute represents a significant step forward in specialised healthcare in Mpumalanga, strengthening the province’s readiness for universal health coverage and ensuring that more residents can access life-changing eye care services closer to home.

post_title: Gogo Nonyane ya Metsi: Week of 23 February–1 March 2026
post_content:
n

This is a building week, ngwana wa metsi — not the week of “big thunder”, but the week of steady hands. The sky says: “Take what was revealed, and now shape it into a life you can live.”
You don’t need drama to transform. You need consistency, prayer, and one brave decision repeated daily.

nnnn

Aries

nnnnnnnn

nnnn

My fire-child, your spirit wants speed, but this week asks for precision. Choose one battle worth fighting and one habit worth keeping. Stop explaining yourself to people who already decided not to understand. Your power returns when you act quietly, then let results speak for you. Rest your body; it carries your destiny.

nnnn

Taurus

nnnnnnnn

Steady one, you are learning that comfort is not only softness — it is also boundaries. This week, protect your time and your money like sacred water. Spend where it grows you, not where it impresses others. Your heart is healing slowly; don’t rush it. A small home improvement or routine change brings big peace.

nnnn

Gemini

nnnnnnnn

Quick mind, this week your words must be clean and deliberate. Speak once, then follow through. Avoid gossip, shortcuts, and half-truths — they bounce back like stones in water. Your gift is connection, but not everyone deserves access. Choose your conversations carefully. A document, proposal, or message you finalise now sets your next month in order.

nnnn

Cancer

nnnnnnnn

Moon-child, you are sensitive, yes — but sensitivity is also wisdom. This week, listen to what your body is refusing: fatigue, tension, headaches, silence. You have carried too much for too long. Ask for help without guilt. Create peace at home: tidy one corner, light a candle, make one honest conversation. A family matter eases when you stop absorbing everyone’s emotions.

nnnn

Leo

nnnnnnnn

Bright one, this week wants mature confidence, not performance. Lead by doing, not by announcing. Your heart may feel tested — someone wants attention or control — but you must keep your dignity. Put love where it’s returned. Create something: write, design, organise, or plan a celebration. The weekend brings warmth if you stop chasing approval and start choosing what nourishes you.

nnnn

Virgo

nnnnnnnn

Careful hands, my child, you are being asked to simplify. Too many lists, too many worries, too many “what ifs”. This week, organise what is real: meals, sleep, schedule, and your workspace. Don’t over-fix people; fix your systems. A health improvement comes through routine, not panic. One practical decision midweek saves you money and stress before month-end.

nnnn

Libra

nnnnnnnn

Beautiful balancer, harmony is your gift, but this week says: peace without truth is a lie. Speak about what you need, not only what others want. Choose clarity in love, clarity in business, clarity in friendship. You may feel pulled between two options; pick the one that respects your values. A creative opportunity opens when you stop hesitating and commit to your own beauty.

nnnn

Scorpio

nnnnnnnn

Deep water, your intuition is sharp like a blade this week — use it with discipline, not suspicion. If something feels off, don’t fight immediately; observe, confirm, then move. This is a powerful week for planning, saving, and protecting your energy. Release an old resentment; it is poisoning your spirit slowly. The weekend favours intimacy and reconciliation if you soften your tone.

nnnn

Sagittarius

nnnnnnnn

Traveller, this week is not for running; it is for aiming. Your dreams are big, but your success will come from one focused direction. Reduce distractions, stop overpromising, and honour your deadlines. A conversation about travel, studies, or future plans becomes serious — treat it with respect. Your luck increases when you prepare properly. By Sunday, you’ll feel lighter if you choose truth over entertainment.

nnnn

Capricorn

nnnnnnnn

Mountain spirit, your discipline is strong, but this week asks you to add gentleness. You don’t need to carry everything alone. Delegate, ask, and allow support. Finances and long-term goals improve when you track details daily — not when you check once a month. Your relationships need time too; stop postponing connection. A small victory at work brings confidence, but don’t forget to celebrate yourself quietly.

nnnn

Aquarius

nnnnnnnn

Star-child, you are rebuilding your identity in a more grounded way. This week is for practical miracles: clean habits, cleaner finances, and stronger boundaries. Avoid people who drain you with endless drama; choose those who encourage growth. Your mind is busy — write your ideas down, don’t keep them spinning. A friendship shifts: either it deepens with honesty or fades with distance. Let it happen without forcing.

nnnn

Pisces

nnnnnnnn

My water-child, your season continues, and your spirit is open — but openness needs protection. Not every request is yours to carry. This week, choose self-care as a sacred duty: rest, prayer, water, and quiet. Your creativity rises like morning mist; use it to heal, not to escape. Love becomes clearer when you stop romanticising what hurts you. By weekend, a gentle yes brings blessing — but only if your boundaries remain firm.

nnnn

Gogo’s Special Message for the Week

nnnn

“Ngwana wa metsi, do not fear a slow week. Slow is where roots grow. Build your life like a clay pot: pressed carefully, shaped daily, fired with patience. Remove what leaks your energy. Keep what holds your spirit. And remember: the river does not rush — yet it reaches the ocean.”

The Special Investigating Unit (SIU) has uncovered a large-scale permit and visa racket within the Department of Home Affairs, estimated to have cost the state more than R180 million.

nnnn

Acting on a whistleblower tip-off, investigators discovered that four officials — each earning an estimated monthly salary of about R25,000 — allegedly made millions by selling permits and visas to foreign nationals. According to the SIU, the officials used their spouses to launder illicit funds into luxury properties and high-end vehicles.

nnnn

Acting SIU Head Leonard Lekgetho said the evidence points to serious weaknesses in border and immigration systems, warning that South Africa’s borders have effectively been compromised. He described the department’s operations as being treated “like a marketplace”.

nnnn

The investigation further revealed that organised syndicates were working with officials responsible for assessing asylum seeker applications. Following a 2024 raid on five refugee reception centres, during which laptops and mobile devices were seized, the SIU found evidence that favourable application outcomes were being sold for between R500 and R3,000.

nnnn

“The SIU investigation revealed that certain officials turned the permit system into a marketplace,” Lekgetho said. “Their modus operandi was simple: applications were sent via WhatsApp for expedited approval, and once approved, money flowed almost immediately.”

nnnn

The findings expose deep-rooted corruption within the immigration system and raise serious concerns about national security, border control and the integrity of asylum and permit processes in South Africa.

nnnn

n

n

The South African Police Service (SAPS), working in partnership with the Department of Correctional Services and private security companies, carried out successful search and seizure operations on 18 and 19 February 2026 in the Bushbuckridge area.

nnnn

The coordinated, intelligence-driven operation targeted a number of randomly selected schools, including Hobo, Tamajane, Masana, Letshele, Sekhukhusa and Dutau, within the Bushbuckridge Local Municipality.

nnnn

The operation formed part of SAPS’s ongoing efforts to combat drugs and other illicit activities in and around schools, with a focus on protecting learners and restoring safety within learning environments.

nnnn

During the raids, some learners found in possession of dagga cooperated with law enforcement officials, leading police to the premises of suspected suppliers. Most of the dagga shown in circulated images was seized directly from these suppliers, who have since been arrested.

nnnnnnnn

Police indicated that the operation was not only aimed at removing drugs from schools, but at dismantling the supply networks that target learners and operate within local communities.

nnnn

The raids reflect a broader strategy by SAPS to disrupt criminal syndicates, strengthen school safety, and prevent young people from being drawn into drug-related activities.

nnnn

Authorities have urged parents, educators and community members to work closely with law enforcement by reporting drug activity, supporting prevention programmes, and helping to create safer environments for children.

nnnn

The operation marks a significant step in strengthening security in schools and reinforcing the message that criminal activity targeting learners will be met with decisive law enforcement action.

n

Operation Shanela II has delivered a major crime breakthrough across Mpumalanga, with hundreds of suspects arrested and significant illegal items confiscated during province-wide operations conducted between 19 and 22 February 2026.

nnnn

The multi-agency operation was led by the South African Police Service (SAPS) and supported by Traffic Police, law enforcement agencies, the Departments of Home Affairs, Health, Labour, Social Development, Small Business Development and Correctional Services, as well as private security companies and Community Policing Forums (CPFs).

nnnn

Extensive operations across the province

nnnn

During the four-day operation:

nnnn

• 137 premises were searched

nnnn

• 7 132 people and 2 375 vehicles were searched

nnnn

• 844 stop-and-search operations were conducted

nnnn

• 6 specialised tracking operations took place

nnnn

• 3 556 high-visibility patrols were conducted, including vehicle checkpoints, roadblocks and tracing operations

nnnn

• 8 hostels, 155 farms, 6 mines and multiple businesses were inspected

nnnn

Compliance operations led to the closure of unlicensed liquor outlets, inspections of licensed liquor traders, scrap yards, second-hand dealers, firearm dealers, spaza shops, formal businesses, farms and informal traders.

nnnnnnnn

Arrests and serious crimes

nnnn

Dozens of wanted suspects were arrested during raids for serious offences including murder, attempted murder, rape, sexual offences, assault GBH, carjacking and illegal possession of firearms.

nnnn

In total, arrests were made for a wide range of offences, including:

nnnn

• Illegal possession of firearms and ammunition

nnnn

• Drug dealing and drug possession

nnnn

• Illegal liquor trading

nnnn

• Possession of counterfeit goods

nnnn

• Illegal cigarettes

nnnn

• Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs

nnnn

• Human trafficking

nnnn

• Business robbery, armed robbery, burglary and hijacking

nnnn

• Murder, rape and assault-related crimes

nnnn

More than 80 illegal immigrants were also arrested during the operation.

nnnn

Major seizures

nnnn

Large quantities of illegal items were confiscated, including:

nnnn

• Firearms (handguns, rifles and shotguns)

nnnn

• Ammunition and explosives

nnnn

• Drugs such as dagga, crack cocaine, crystal meth (tik) and nyaope

nnnn

• Counterfeit and contraband goods valued at over R1.1 million

nnnn

post_title: SAHRC to Investigate Lily Mine Families’ Complaint
post_content:
n

ActionSA has welcomed the decision by the South African Human Rights Commission (SAHRC) to accept for investigation the complaint lodged by the families of Pretty Nkambule, Solomon Nyirenda, and Yvonne Mnisi regarding the Lily Mine tragedy.

nnnn

The SAHRC confirmed that the complaint has been assessed and accepted for investigation, a development hailed by Herman Mashaba as an important step toward restoring dignity, accountability, and justice for families who have endured nearly a decade of uncertainty and neglect.

nnnn

ActionSA criticised the prolonged inaction by the National Prosecuting Authorityand the Department of Mineral Resources, noting that the failure to act decisively has compounded the suffering of victims’ families and undermined public confidence in the justice system.

nnnn

“For ten years, the families of the Lily Mine victims have been denied closure, the return of their loved ones’ remains, and meaningful communication from state institutions,” Mashaba said. “Justice delayed is justice denied. Human dignity does not end with death, and families have a fundamental right to truth, accountability, and closure.”

nnnn

ActionSA affirmed that it will continue to support the families throughout the investigation and monitor progress closely. The party stressed that the acceptance of the complaint must lead to concrete action, not further delays, and called for a thorough, independent investigation without undue delay.

nnnn

The SAHRC investigation now formally begins, marking a significant move toward addressing long-standing human rights concerns related to the Lily Mine tragedy and ensuring accountability within state institutions.

post_title: Two Decades of Visa Fraud Uncovered
post_content:
n

The Department of Home Affairs says a recent report exposes almost two decades of corruption in the country’s visa system. The Special Investigating Unit (SIU) revealed that permits and visas were allegedly sold, traded, and laundered, with the immigration system treated like a commodity.

nnnn

The probe, covering irregularities dating back to 2004, found the corruption to be organised, deliberate, and damaging to public trust. Minister Leon Schreiber said the investigation has exposed both the alleged perpetrators and systemic loopholes that enabled manipulation.

nnnn

Most of the wrongdoing was allegedly carried out by a small number of officials. Disciplinary action is underway, with 20 officials dismissed since April last year. Steps are being taken to ensure they are not re-employed elsewhere in the state.

nnnn

The investigation also identified over 2,000 study visas issued fraudulently, which are now being cancelled.

post_title: Police seize illegal guns in Bushbuckridge
post_content:
n

Illegal firearms and ammunition were seized during a coordinated crime prevention operation in the Ehlanzeni District, Mpumalanga, as part of Operation Shanela.

nnnn

The multidisciplinary team, working alongside local Farm Watch structures, conducted intelligence-driven operations between 23 and 24 February 2026 in Calcutta, Acornhoek and Bushbuckridge. The operation focused on crime prevention, tracing of wanted suspects and compliance inspections.

nnnn

Police conducted stop-and-searches, patrols and visits to liquor outlets in identified hotspots, including Saselani and Dwarsloop in Bushbuckridge. During the operation, a 30-year-old man was arrested for possession of unlicensed firearms and ammunition. Police seized two 9mm pistols, two magazines and approximately 16 live rounds.

nnnn

Further operational activities led to the recovery of two additional firearms, one of which is suspected to be a state-issued weapon. Crime Intelligence information later resulted in the recovery of another 9mm pistol with ammunition.

nnnn

Two suspects, aged 25 and 30, are expected to appear before the Bushbuckridge Magistrate’s Court and Acornhoek Magistrate’s Court respectively on Wednesday, 25 February 2026.

nnnnnnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of South African Police Service in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi emphasised that integrated, intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with community structures such as farm patrols remain critical in removing illegal firearms from communities.

nnnn

“These coordinated efforts enhance operational quality, strengthen cohesion among law enforcement partners, and significantly contribute to proactive policing and safer communities,” said Mkhwanazi.

post_title: A Beautiful Gateway to the Wild
post_content:
n

There is something truly special about landing inside the wilderness — and now the world is taking notice.

nnnn

Skukuza Airport, nestled deep within the heart of the Kruger National Park, has been named the most beautiful airport in the world by Forbes — a title that feels not just deserved, but inevitable.

nnnn

This is no ordinary airport terminal. With its distinctive thatched roof, warm wooden finishes, sweeping bushveld views and a striking life-sized rhino replica, Skukuza Airport feels less like a transport hub and more like the opening scene of a safari adventure. From the moment passengers step inside, the experience is immersive, calm and unmistakably African — a seamless blend of luxury and wilderness.

nnnn

Forbes captured the essence of the airport perfectly, describing it as a space that “ditches the classic airport look and embraces a luxury spa vibe instead”. Designed to feel warm, welcoming and tranquil, it offers the ideal farewell after days — or even weeks — spent surrounded by wildlife, and the perfect welcome for those just beginning their journey into the bush.

nnnn

Skukuza Airport operates as a small but vital gateway within the park. Airlink offers direct flights from Johannesburg, Durban and Cape Town, making access to the Kruger easier than ever before. While charter aircraft also operate from the airport, Airlink remains the only commercial airline servicing this unique destination.

nnnnnnnn

The airport is located close to Skukuza Main Camp — the administrative headquarters of the Kruger National Park — and lies near the adjoining Sabi Sand Conservancy, placing visitors within immediate reach of some of South Africa’s most renowned wildlife areas.

nnnn

Skukuza Airport’s history stretches back to 1959, but it was reopened just over a decade ago as part of a strategic move to improve access to the Kruger. The reopening aimed to reduce the long road journey from Nelspruit into the park, making travel safer, faster and more convenient for both local and international visitors.

nnnn

Today, the airport stands as a successful public-private partnership between SANParks and Skukuza Airport Management Company, jointly owned by Lion Sands and Airlink — a collaboration that has transformed a small regional airport into a globally recognised landmark.

nnnn

More than just a transport facility, Skukuza Airport has become a symbol of how infrastructure can harmonise with nature, rather than compete with it. Its global recognition is not only a win for tourism, but a proud moment for South Africa and for Mpumalanga in particular.

nnnn

In a world of glass terminals and concrete runways, Skukuza stands apart — a beautiful gateway to the wild, and now officially, the most beautiful airport on Earth.

n

The prosecution in a multimillion-rand tender fraud case at the Mpumalanga Department of Education has alleged that service providers were used to siphon off public funds.

nnnn

On Tuesday, several of the 36 suspects linked to the scandal appeared at the Mbombela Magistrates Court, where bail ranging from R5,000 to R50,000 was granted.

nnnn

The State claims more than 20 companies were involved in the irregular R113 million tender scheme. Investigations by the Hawks revealed that service providers were hand-picked with no official procedure followed. Some of the accused are directors of these entities.

nnnn

State prosecutor Prenishna Jagganath detailed the alleged irregularities, citing that “Accused 17 is a director of Makhayeni Sint; he was paid a total of 4.5 million from the department.” She added that more entities were involved than the number of accused: “When the State goes to trial with this, it will be 40 warm bodies, as I’ve indicated, and 69 corporate entities. These accused are sitting before you as service providers in their capacities as directors, and some of them will be personal capacities where they’ve received monies.”

nnnn

Bail proceedings are ongoing at the Nelspruit Magistrate’s Court for 38 accused facing charges linked to the R114 million Mpumalanga Education Department fraud case.

nnnn

Since the trial commenced on Monday, 15 of the accused have been granted bail, with the process expected to continue over the coming days.

nnnn

This case underscores growing concerns over tender irregularities and the use of service providers to allegedly exploit public funds in the province.

n

The Department of Basic Education (DBE) has revealed that repeating school grades is draining billions of rands from the education budget — funds that many experts say could be better spent on improving early literacy and learning.  

nnnn

According to the Funda Uphumelele National Survey, a major national study into reading outcomes for learners in grades 1 to 4, up to 8 % of the DBE’s budget — around R20 billion — is being used to fund the repetition of learners who fail to meet expected outcomes.  

nnnn

The same report highlights a troubling literacy picture in South African schools:

nnnn

• 15 % of Grade 3 learners scored zero on reading assessments, meaning they could not decode even a single word by the end of their third year of schooling.  

nnnn

• Only around 30 % to 31 % of learners in grades 1 to 3 are reading at the expected level in their home languages, according to the survey results.  

nnnn

These figures underline a foundational problem: many pupils enter schooling without strong reading skills, which affects their ability to succeed in later grades.

nnnn

Research in the report suggests that repeating learners in Grade 1 can lead to temporary learning gains. However, these improvements tend to fade as pupils move up through the system.  

nnnn

Experts argue that spending such large sums on repetition isn’t the most effective way to improve learning outcomes — especially when many of the problems begin in the earliest years of schooling.

nnnn

Educational researchers and advocates are calling for a shift in how the funds are used. They recommend:

nnnn

• Investing more in Early Childhood Development (ECD) so children start school better prepared.  

nnnn

• Introducing structured reading programmes in the early grades, which have been shown to deliver more lasting improvements than repeating learners.  

nnnn

The evidence suggests that focusing on early learning and literacy could reduce the need for repetition in the first place — breaking a costly cycle and giving learners a stronger start in their education.

nnnn

Redirecting funds from repetition toward ECD and structured reading programmes might help more children build essential skills from the beginning of their schooling journey.  

nnnn

Education experts warn that unless funding shifts towards effective early literacy support, the cycle of poor reading outcomes and expensive grade repetition may continue.  

n

n

A major partnership aimed at creating jobs and growing the economy was signed today, 25 February, between the Mpumalanga Provincial Government and the University of Mpumalanga.

nnnn

The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), signed at the university’s campus in Tfokomala, focuses on tackling unemployment, supporting small farmers, growing local businesses and creating real opportunities for ordinary people across the province.

nnnn

Premier Mandla Ndlovu said the agreement is about action, not speeches. The goal is to turn education, farming and business into practical job opportunities that improve daily life for communities.

nnnn

A key focus of the partnership is agriculture, which remains one of Mpumalanga’s strongest economic sectors. The plan includes expanding farming projects, improving access to markets, and supporting small-scale and emerging farmers so they can earn a stable income from their produce.

nnnn

One of the major developments linked to the agreement is the growth of a large fresh produce market, which will allow farmers to sell their crops more easily and access bigger local and international markets. This is expected to create jobs in farming, transport, trading, packaging and processing.

nnnn

The MoU also introduces a hybrid rice farming project, which will be piloted in the province. This project is expected to create large-scale employment over time and open doors for young people, small farmers and local entrepreneurs to enter commercial agriculture.

nnnn

For ordinary residents, the impact of the agreement is expected to be felt in everyday life:

nnnn
    n
  • More job opportunities in farming and agri-business
    • nnnn
  • Support for small and emerging farmers
    • nnnn
  • Growth of local small businesses (SMMEs)
    • nnnn
  • Training and skills development for young people
    • nnnn
  • Better access to markets for local produce
    • n
nnnn

The partnership also connects the university directly to communities, allowing students and researchers to work on real projects that solve real problems, instead of knowledge staying only in lecture halls.

nnnn

The MoU will run for five years, with the option to be renewed, and will be guided by a joint steering committee to ensure projects are implemented and monitored properly.

nnnn

For many families across Mpumalanga, today’s signing represents more than a formal agreement — it signals a serious effort to turn education, land and opportunity into jobs, income and a better future.

post_title: Businessmans holding poster with a smile. Business and happy concept.
4,000 ghost workers flagged in govt payroll
post_content:
n

National Treasury has revealed that a nationwide ghost worker audit has identified 4,323 suspicious cases within the government’s payroll system, with a verification process already under way.

nnnn

According to the department, employees who cannot be physically verified will face withheld salaries and suspension of their employment status, as government moves to clamp down on fraud and irregular payments in the public sector.

nnnn

Treasury highlighted that compensation of employees consumes nearly one-third of consolidated government spending, making payroll integrity a major priority in efforts to protect public funds and improve service delivery.

nnnn

As part of broader cost-cutting measures, the department also confirmed progress in its Early Retirement Programme, which allows qualifying government employees to retire early without financial penalties. The programme is expected to save R2.6 billion in the current financial year, following the approval of 7,687 applications in its first phase.

nnnn

To sustain the programme, Treasury has allocated R3.7 billion to departmental baselines for the 2025/26 and 2026/27 financial years, signalling a long-term commitment to reducing the wage bill while stabilising government finances.

nnnn

The measures form part of government’s wider strategy to clean up public administration, eliminate corruption risks, and ensure that public money is spent on services that directly benefit communities.

nnnn

n

n

Acorns to Oaks Secondary School in the Green Valley Circuit, Bohlabela District, hosted a vibrant World Read Aloud Day celebration on Wednesday, 25 February, bringing together learners, educators and partners in a shared commitment to literacy.

nnnn

The event was organised by the Department of Education in collaboration with Nal’ibali, Room to Read, and the National Education Collaboration Trust, reflecting a united effort to build a nation of readers and strengthen reading culture in schools.

nnnn

The celebration highlighted reading as the foundation of all learning and one of the most powerful tools for social and economic transformation. Speakers emphasised that promoting a culture of reading not only supports academic success, but also empowers learners to participate meaningfully in society.

nnnnnnnn

Book publishers Shuter & Shooter and Maskew Miller Learning also attended the event, reinforcing the importance of access to quality reading materials in schools.

nnnn

The keynote address was delivered on behalf of the MEC for Education, Lindi Masina, by the Chief Director for General Education and Training (GET), Elvis Siwela. In his message, he reaffirmed the department’s commitment to literacy development through the strengthening of school libraries, structured reading programmes and the promotion of a reading culture across all districts.

nnnn

He stressed that reading should not be limited to the Foundation Phase, but must become a sustained practice throughout a learner’s entire educational journey. He further called on educators, parents and learners to take collective responsibility in nurturing a lifelong love for books.

nnnn

World Read Aloud Day once again served as a powerful reminder that when communities read together, they grow together — turning the simple act of reading aloud into a lasting investment in education and development.

post_title: Snakes Keep Hazyview Residents on Alert
post_content:
n

Hazyview residents have reported a spike in snake sightings from last Friday through Wednesday, with encounters ranging from a massive python in a chicken coop to juvenile black mambas and cobras in homes.

nnnn

One local farmer shared how a three‑metre python had already eaten two of her chickens and was attacking a third when she discovered it. “We removed it and let it go on the other side of the farm,” she said. She warned fellow poultry owners to check their enclosures: “Secure the chicken hok better — even closed‑in chickens aren’t always safe.”

nnnn

Others reported snakes inside houses. One resident spotted what looked like a black mamba, while another called for help after finding a cobra indoors. Snake experts say such activity is not unusual.

nnnn

“Snakes are seeking shelter from the heat and actively hunting for food,” explained a local wildlife specialist. “In the Lowveld, they stop feeding during winter but will still come out to bask. Black mambas and puff adders also mate at the beginning of winter, causing a spike in movement. Come spring, they need to feed again after using up fat reserves over winter, so activity increases further.”

nnnn

Houses attract snakes because they provide perfect conditions for their prey. Watered gardens and ponds draw frogs, rodents are fond of walls and rockeries, and lizards find hiding spots in human environments. Experts advise residents to remember that snakes do not see houses as foreign — to them, it’s just another part of their habitat.

nnnn

Residents are urged to stay vigilant, secure poultry enclosures, and contact trained handlers when snakes appear indoors.

n

n

Masoganeng United battled to a 2–2 draw against Real Rangers FC in a Kruger Zone 2 away game at Welverdiend on Saturday, 21 February.

nnnn

The first half was evenly contested, with both sides finding the net once. Khutso put Masoganeng ahead after a precise assist from Puno Malahle, but Real Rangers quickly replied to make it 1–1 at half-time.

nnnn

Early in the second half, Real Rangers took the lead, leaving Masoganeng chasing the game. The visitors responded in the 65th minute when Khutso scored his second, this time assisted by Skhuliseni Mokoena, to level the score again.

nnnn

Masoganeng pressed hard in added time and created a clear chance to snatch a winner, but it went begging, leaving the game tied.

nnnn

Khutso’s brace earned him Player of the Match honours as Masoganeng United shared the spoils with Real Rangers.

post_title: Province Acts to Fix Daily Challenges
post_content:
n

The Mpumalanga Provincial Government officially opened its Executive Lekgotla on Thursday 26 February, setting out a roadmap to tackle jobs, water, and the rising cost of living. Premier Mandla Ndlovu addressed the gathering of government leaders, municipal managers, traditional authorities, and community partners, stressing that action — not talk — is needed to improve lives.

nnnn

Premier Ndlovu noted that while unemployment has decreased slightly to 32.3%, youth unemployment remains high at 44.7%, with over a quarter of young graduates still out of work. Rising costs and service delivery challenges mean ordinary households feel the pressure every day.

nnnn

To address these issues, the government has outlined what it calls “EDGE commitments”:

nnnn

• Execution Discipline – speeding up project delivery, stabilising critical vacancies, and strengthening accountability.

nnnn

• Delivery Through Partnerships – working with business, labour, and communities to grow agriculture, tourism, mining, logistics, and small businesses (SMMEs).

nnnn

• Governance That Restores Trust – improving municipal finances, transparent spending, and audit outcomes.

nnnn

• Equity and Resilience – long-term focus on reducing poverty, improving social protection, and strengthening climate and infrastructure resilience.

nnnn

Water security was highlighted as a top priority. The Premier acknowledged that having full dams is not enough: “Winning on water” means reliable household supply, functioning treatment works, and repaired infrastructure. Three municipalities — Thembisile Hani, Victor Khanye, and Govan Mbeki — will receive targeted interventions to stabilise supply and reduce outages.

nnnn

The Lekgotla also emphasised integrated planning through the District Development Model (DDM), ensuring that each district identifies key projects in water, roads, energy, housing, and local economic development, with clear funding, monitoring, and community involvement.

nnnn

Premier Ndlovu concluded that the province must focus on real impact, not activity, addressing the basics that affect daily life, while also improving domestic competitiveness amid global uncertainties. The message was clear: Mpumalanga aims to grow jobs, improve services, and ensure households see tangible improvements in their communities.

nnnn

n

n

Illegal firearms and ammunition were seized during a police operation in the Ehlanzeni District, Mpumalanga, as part of Operation Shanela.

nnnn

The intelligence-driven operation, conducted between 23 and 24 February 2026, involved a multidisciplinary police team working alongside local Farm Watch structures in Calcutta, Acornhoek and Bushbuckridge. Officers carried out stop-and-searches, patrols, and compliance inspections at hotspots including Saselani and Dwarsloop.

nnnn

During the operation, two men were arrested for possession of unlicensed firearms and ammunition. A 30-year-old suspect, Lucas Khosa, and 25-year-old Ripfumelo Kubayi were linked to firearms recovered by police, including multiple 9mm pistols and magazines. One of the seized firearms is suspected to be state-issued.

nnnnnnnn

Court updates:

nnnn

Ripfumelo Kubayi (25) was granted R1 000 bail by the Acornhoek Magistrate’s Court and is expected back in court on 17 March. Meanwhile, Lucas Khosa (30) remains in custody after being remanded and will appear before the Bushbuckridge Magistrate’s Court on 2 March for a formal bail application.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner of the South African Police Service in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, commended officers for their swift response and effective coordination. He emphasised that intelligence-led operations and cooperation with community structures such as farm patrols are vital to removing illegal firearms and ensuring safer communities.

nnnn

“These coordinated efforts strengthen cohesion among law enforcement partners and significantly contribute to proactive policing,” said Mkhwanazi.

nnnn

The case continues.

n

n

More than 200 leading scientists, researchers, conservationists and policymakers from around the world will converge at Skukuza in the Kruger National Park for the 23rd Savanna Science Network Meeting (SSNM), taking place from 2 to 5 March 2026.

nnnn

The international gathering will bring together experts from across the globe to discuss the growing challenges facing savanna ecosystems and the communities that depend on them. A total of 230 delegates have registered for the meeting, including 127 participants from across Africa, representing every continent except Antarctica.

nnnn

The conference is regarded as one of the world’s most significant scientific platforms for savanna research, focusing on biodiversity conservation, fire behaviour, vegetation monitoring, wildlife population studies, aerial counting strategies, technological innovation and governance challenges affecting conservation in Southern Africa and beyond.

nnnn

This year’s meeting coincides with the centenary celebrations of the Kruger National Park, marking 100 years of conservation in one of the world’s most iconic protected areas. A special presentation will also reflect on the January 2026 floods that affected parts of the park.

nnnn

Organisers say the meeting plays a critical role in strengthening cooperation between academics and park authorities, promoting evidence-based decision-making and ensuring research is aligned with priority conservation management needs. Capacity building remains a key focus, with students sharing the platform alongside world-renowned savanna scientists.

nnnn

For broader public access, all sessions will be live-streamed on YouTube, allowing communities, researchers and conservation supporters to participate online.

nnnn

The event is expected to further strengthen scientific collaboration and reinforce Kruger National Park’s role as a global centre for conservation research and environmental leadership.

n

n

The South African Police Service Commercial Crime Investigation Unit in Mpumalanga has arrested nine suspects linked to an alleged loan fraud syndicate operating in Hazyview and surrounding areas.

nnnn

The arrests were carried out during a coordinated operation between 24 and 25 February 2026, following a multidisciplinary investigation into suspected large-scale financial fraud. Police confirmed that the suspects were detained at various locations, including Acornhoek, Hazyview, Nelspruit and Schoemansdal.

nnnn

Preliminary investigations indicate that the group allegedly applied for loans and credit cards at a financial institution using fraudulent documentation. The estimated value of the alleged fraud exceeds R500 000.

nnnn

The suspects, aged between 26 and 55, appeared before the Masoyi Magistrate’s Court on Thursday, 26 February 2026. Each was granted bail of R1 000, and the case was postponed to 18 March 2026. Police have not ruled out further arrests as investigations continue.

nnnn

Authorities also suspect that the syndicate may have worked with an insider at the financial institution, a matter that remains under investigation.

nnnn

Acting Provincial Commissioner of the SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, praised officers for the operation, describing it as a significant step in dismantling organised crime networks in the province.

nnnn

“This operation demonstrates our firm commitment to dismantling organised crime syndicates. People must expect more decisive actions as we continue to deal firmly with crime in the province,” he said.

post_title: STATE OF THE PROVINCE ADDRESS 2026 – 05 MARCH 2026
post_content: nn

n

The Minister of Forestry and Fisheries has expressed strong confidence that the recovery fund established by South African National Parks will play a vital role in rebuilding Kruger National Park following the recent devastating floods.

nnnn

Speaking at a media briefing in the park on Friday, 27 February, the Minister reflected on key milestones achieved by the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) since his appointment on 17 November 2025, while also outlining the department’s ongoing commitment to environmental sustainability and conservation.

nnnnnnnn

“There’s a lot of people in this country that love the Kruger National Park and will be willing to help,” he said, emphasising the national and emotional significance of the iconic conservation area.

nnnn

He confirmed that the recovery fund is being managed by three independent auditing firms to ensure full transparency and accountability. According to the Minister, every cent donated will be strictly allocated to the recovery and rebuilding of the park, with no funds diverted to any other purpose.

nnnn

Just two months into his term of office, the Minister was confronted with the crisis caused by the floods. He praised the response of park management and emergency teams, highlighting the successful evacuation efforts.

nnnn

“We evacuated hundreds of people and not one single person lost their lives or even got injured. I think that testifies to the passion and the hard work that people in this park are putting in towards their love for this park,” he said.

nnnn

He described the floods as a major personal and professional challenge, but one that demonstrated the power of collective effort. “It tested me – obviously it was a huge challenge – but look at where we are now, showing that we can work together,” he added.

nnnn

Progress in recovery is already visible. Several camps affected by the floods have reopened, while others are still undergoing repairs. Letaba Camp, one of the hardest hit, is expected to reopen partially by the end of May this year, with full operations anticipated by November.

nnnn

The Minister reaffirmed his commitment to SANParks and the Kruger National Park, stating that his support would continue throughout the recovery process.

nnnn

The total confirmed damage currently stands at R490 million. However, some areas of the park remain inaccessible, and authorities estimate that the final cost could rise to between R500 million and R600 million.

nnnn

Through the Kruger Recovery Fund and the Honorary Rangers Fund, just over R3 million has already been raised — a figure the Minister described as “a drop in the ocean” compared to the scale of the destruction.

nnnn

Further support has been confirmed from the Minister of Tourism, who has committed R56 million to fund Expanded Public Works Programme (EPWP) workers. These workers will assist with large-scale cleaning and restoration operations within the park.

nnnn

As recovery efforts continue, government, conservation bodies and the public are being urged to work together to restore one of South Africa’s most treasured natural landmarks, ensuring that Kruger National Park remains protected for future generations.

n

post_title: Suspects in Court for Illegal Gold
post_content:
n

 Two undocumented foreign nationals have appeared in court following their arrest for the illegal possession of suspected illicit gold valued at approximately R3 million in the Pilgrim’s Rest policing area.

nnnn

The arrests were effected by members of the South African Police Service (SAPS) through Operation Shanela, during an intelligence-driven operation conducted by the Tactical Response Team (TRT) between 22:45 on 25 February and 07:00 on 26 February 2026 in the Ehlanzeni District.

nnnn

Police acted on information regarding foreign nationals allegedly involved in criminal activities in the Pilgrim’s Rest area. Upon arrival, officers conducted a search which led to the discovery of six bags containing approximately 90% processed gold. The items were immediately confiscated.

nnnn

Two Mozambican nationals, Gorge Sitho (25) and Alexdrie Solomon Zimbe (25), were arrested and charged with the illegal possession of precious metals, as well as contravention of the Immigration Act of South Africa. Detectives are working in collaboration with officials from the Department of Home Affairs to verify the immigration status of the suspects.

nnnnnnnn

The pair appeared in the Graskop Magistrate’s Court on Friday, 27 February 2026, and are expected to appear again at the Pilgrim’s Rest Periodical Court on 4 March 2026. Both suspects remain in police custody.

nnnn

The Acting Provincial Commissioner of SAPS in Mpumalanga, Major General (Dr) Zeph Mkhwanazi, commended officers for their swift response and dedication in combating illicit mining-related crimes.

nnnn

“This successful operation demonstrates our firm commitment to dismantling illegal mining networks and associated criminal activities in the province. We hope that this operation will send a strong message that criminality will find no refuge in society. We will continue to intensify our efforts,” he said.
